bib-exodus-006-p02.plain: Do not crave what belongs to your neighbour: not their house, their spouse, their workers, their animals, or anything else that is theirs.
bib-exodus-006-p02.core_idea: Do not crave what belongs to others

bib-exodus-007-p01.plain: Do not join a crowd in doing wrong. In court, do not go along with the majority to twist justice.
bib-exodus-007-p01.core_idea: Do not follow the crowd into wrongdoing

bib-exodus-007-p02.plain: If you find your enemy's animal wandering, take it back to him. If you see the donkey of someone who hates you collapsed under its load, do not walk away; help him with it.
bib-exodus-007-p02.core_idea: Help even your enemy when he is in trouble

bib-exodus-007-p03.plain: Do not take bribes: a bribe blinds people who can see and twists the words of honest people.
bib-exodus-007-p03.core_idea: Bribes blind and corrupt even the honest

bib-exodus-007-p04.plain: Do not mistreat a foreigner. You know how a foreigner feels, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
bib-exodus-007-p04.core_idea: Do not mistreat foreigners; you were one

bib-exodus-011-p01.plain: Yahweh passed by and proclaimed himself merciful and gracious, slow to anger, rich in loving kindness and truth, forgiving sin for thousands; yet he will not clear the guilty, but brings the parents' sins upon their children and grandchildren to the third and fourth generation.
bib-exodus-011-p01.core_idea: God is merciful and forgiving, yet holds guilt accountable
bib-exodus-011-p01.plain_v1: God proclaims his own name: merciful, gracious, slow to anger, full of steadfast love and truth, forgiving wrongdoing, yet not letting the guilty go unpunished, with consequences reaching to later generations.

judge_v1.issue: Softens visiting fathers' iniquity on children to third and fourth generation into vague 'consequences'.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Softens visiting the fathers' iniquity on children to vague 'consequences'.

bib-ezekiel-003-p01.plain: God promises to give his people one heart and a new spirit, replacing their hearts of stone with hearts of flesh, so they will follow his ways; they will be his people and he their God.
bib-ezekiel-003-p01.core_idea: God will replace hearts of stone with living hearts

bib-ezekiel-004-p01.plain: God says to Israel, pictured as an abandoned newborn: when I passed by and saw you lying in your blood, I told you to live, even there in your blood.
bib-ezekiel-004-p01.core_idea: God told the helpless one: live

judge.issue: Adds 'abandoned newborn' framing not in the passage; drops the repeated command.

bib-ezekiel-005-p01.plain: Sodom's wrongdoing was this: pride, too much food, and comfortable ease, while she did nothing to help the poor and needy.
bib-ezekiel-005-p01.core_idea: Comfort without helping the poor is wrongdoing

bib-ezekiel-005-p02.plain: The person who sins is the one who dies. A child will not carry a parent's guilt, nor a parent a child's; each person's goodness or wickedness is their own.
bib-ezekiel-005-p02.core_idea: Each person answers for their own deeds

bib-ezekiel-005-p03.plain: If a wicked person turns from their sins and does right, they will live; their past wrongs will not be held against them. God takes no pleasure in the wicked dying; he wants them to turn back and live.
bib-ezekiel-005-p03.core_idea: God wants the wrongdoer to turn back and live

judge.issue: Loosens 'turns from all his sins and keeps all my statutes' to 'does right'.

bib-ezekiel-005-p04.plain: Throw off all your wrongdoing and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why die? God says he takes no pleasure in anyone's death, so turn back and live.
bib-ezekiel-005-p04.core_idea: Turn from wrongdoing, make a new heart, and live

bib-ezekiel-009-p01.plain: Your beauty made you proud, and your splendour corrupted your wisdom.

bib-ezekiel-010-p01.plain: The people say their sins weigh on them and they are wasting away, so how can they live? God answers that he wants not the death of the wicked but their turning: turn back, why die?
bib-ezekiel-010-p01.core_idea: Weighed down by sin? God says turn and live

bib-ezekiel-010-p02.plain: People come and listen to you as if devoted, praising you with their mouths while their hearts chase profit. To them you are just a pleasant song: they hear your words but do not act on them.
bib-ezekiel-010-p02.core_idea: People enjoy hearing truth but do not act on it

bib-ezekiel-010-p03.plain: Shame on the leaders who look after only themselves. They take the best for themselves but neglect the weak, the sick, the injured, the strayed and the lost, and rule them harshly instead.
bib-ezekiel-010-p03.core_idea: Leaders who serve themselves neglect the vulnerable

judge.issue: Turns shepherds into 'leaders' and drops the rhetorical 'shouldn't shepherds feed the sheep?'.

bib-ezekiel-011-p01.plain: God says he will look for the lost, bring back the strays, bandage the injured and strengthen the sick, but destroy the fat and strong, and care for his flock with justice.
bib-ezekiel-011-p01.core_idea: God seeks the lost and heals the broken

bib-ezekiel-011-p02.plain: God promises a new heart and a new spirit: he will take away your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
bib-ezekiel-011-p02.core_idea: God will give you a new heart

bib-ezra-001-p01.plain: When the new temple's foundation was laid, the old who remembered the first temple wept aloud while many others shouted for joy, and no one could tell the joyful shouts from the weeping.
bib-ezra-001-p01.core_idea: Joy and grief can sound the same

bib-ezra-003-p01.plain: My God, I am too ashamed to lift my face to you; our wrongs have piled up over our heads and our guilt reaches the sky.
bib-ezra-003-p01.core_idea: Ashamed before God of guilt piled high

bib-ezra-003-p02.plain: Get up, because this task is yours, and we are with you. Be brave and do it.
bib-ezra-003-p02.core_idea: The task is yours; be brave, we're with you

bib-galatians-001-p01.plain: Am I trying to win people's approval, or God's? If I were still trying to please people, I would not be a servant of Christ.
bib-galatians-001-p01.core_idea: Seeking to please people conflicts with serving Christ

bib-galatians-001-p02.plain: In Christ Jesus there is no Jew or Greek, slave or free, male or female: you are all one.
bib-galatians-001-p02.core_idea: All are one in Christ Jesus

bib-galatians-001-p03.plain: You were called to freedom, but do not use it to indulge yourselves; serve one another in love. The whole law comes down to loving your neighbour as yourself. If you attack each other, you will destroy each other.
bib-galatians-001-p03.core_idea: Use freedom to serve one another in love

judge.issue: Turns 'be careful that you don't consume one another' warning into a flat prediction.

bib-galatians-001-p04.plain: What the Spirit produces is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. No law stands against these.
bib-galatians-001-p04.core_idea: The Spirit produces love, joy, peace and more

bib-galatians-001-p05.plain: If the Spirit gives us life, let us also live by the Spirit. Let us not become conceited, provoke one another, or envy one another.
bib-galatians-001-p05.core_idea: Live by the Spirit; avoid conceit and envy

bib-galatians-001-p06.plain: If someone slips into wrongdoing, the spiritual should gently restore them, watching their own temptation. Carry each other's burdens. Do not think yourself important; test your own work instead of comparing, since each carries their own load.
bib-galatians-001-p06.core_idea: Gently restore others; carry burdens; judge only yourself

judge.issue: Drops self-deception of thinking oneself something, and boasting in oneself.

bib-galatians-001-p07.plain: God is not mocked: you reap what you sow. Living for your appetites yields decay; living by the Spirit yields eternal life. So do not tire of doing good, because the harvest will come if you do not give up.
bib-galatians-001-p07.core_idea: You reap what you sow; don't tire of doing good

bib-genesis-001-p01.plain: God said it is not good for the man to be alone, and that he would make him a fitting partner.
bib-genesis-001-p01.core_idea: It is not good to be alone

bib-genesis-001-p02.plain: You will work hard for your food all your life until you go back to the ground you were made from, because you are dust and will return to dust.
bib-genesis-001-p02.core_idea: You are dust and will return to dust

bib-genesis-001-p03.plain: God asked Cain why he was angry and downcast. If he did right, he would be lifted up; if not, sin was lying in wait at his door, wanting him, but he must master it.
bib-genesis-001-p03.core_idea: Sin waits at the door; you must master it

bib-genesis-002-p01.plain: As long as the earth lasts, planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never stop.
bib-genesis-002-p01.core_idea: The seasons and days will keep coming

bib-genesis-003-p01.plain: God told Abram to leave his country, his relatives and his father's home, and go to a land God would show him.
bib-genesis-003-p01.core_idea: Leave the familiar for where God leads

bib-genesis-003-p02.plain: Abram asked Lot not to let any quarrel come between them or their workers, since they were family. The whole land was open: Lot could choose a direction, and Abram would take the other.
bib-genesis-003-p02.core_idea: Give way rather than quarrel with family

bib-genesis-004-p01.plain: God spoke to Abram in a vision: do not be afraid; I am your shield and your great reward.
bib-genesis-004-p01.core_idea: Do not be afraid; God is your shield

bib-genesis-008-p01.plain: Jacob woke and said that God was surely in this place and he had not known it. Filled with awe, he called it the house of God and the gate of heaven.
bib-genesis-008-p01.core_idea: God was here, and I did not know

bib-genesis-008-p02.plain: Jacob worked seven years to marry Rachel, and they felt like only a few days because he loved her so much.
bib-genesis-008-p02.core_idea: Love made seven years feel like days

bib-genesis-009-p01.plain: Jacob, alone, wrestled with a man until dawn. Unable to win, the man injured Jacob's hip and asked to be let go as day broke, but Jacob said he would not let go unless the man blessed him.
bib-genesis-009-p01.core_idea: Hold on until you are blessed

bib-genesis-009-p02.plain: Esau told his brother that he already had enough, and Jacob should keep what was his.
bib-genesis-009-p02.core_idea: I have enough; keep what is yours

bib-genesis-011-p01.plain: Jacob tore his clothes and mourned his son for many days. All his children tried to comfort him, but he refused, saying he would grieve until he joined his son in the grave.
bib-genesis-011-p01.core_idea: A father refuses comfort in his grief

judge.issue: Drops 'His father wept for him'.

bib-genesis-012-p01.plain: Joseph named his first son to say God had made him forget his hardship and his father's house, and his second to say God had made him fruitful in the land where he suffered.
bib-genesis-012-p01.core_idea: God made me fruitful in the land of my suffering

bib-genesis-012-p02.plain: The brothers admitted to one another that they were guilty: they had seen their brother's anguish when he begged them and would not listen, and now this trouble had come on them.
bib-genesis-012-p02.core_idea: Ignoring another's anguish brings guilt back on you

bib-genesis-013-p01.plain: Overcome with love for his brother, Joseph hurried away to find somewhere to cry. He wept in his room, washed his face, steadied himself, came back and ordered the meal served.
bib-genesis-013-p01.core_idea: Joseph wept privately, then composed himself

bib-genesis-013-p02.plain: Joseph told his brothers who he was, the brother they had sold into Egypt. He said not to be upset or angry with themselves, because God had sent him ahead to save lives.
bib-genesis-013-p02.core_idea: God used the wrong done to me to save lives

bib-genesis-014-p01.plain: Asked his age, Jacob told Pharaoh his life's journey had lasted 130 years, and that his days had been few and hard, shorter than the lives of his ancestors.
bib-genesis-014-p01.core_idea: My days have been few and hard

bib-genesis-014-p02.plain: Israel told Joseph he never expected to see his face again, and now God had let him see Joseph's children too.
bib-genesis-014-p02.core_idea: I never thought I'd see you; now your children too

bib-genesis-015-p01.plain: Joseph threw himself on his dead father's face, wept over him and kissed him.
bib-genesis-015-p01.core_idea: A son weeps over his dead father

judge.issue: Adds 'dead' father, context the passage itself does not state.

bib-genesis-015-p02.plain: Joseph told his brothers not to fear, since he was not God. They meant to harm him, but God meant it for good, to save many lives. He promised to provide for them, and spoke kindly to them.
bib-genesis-015-p02.core_idea: You meant harm, but God meant it for good

judge.issue: 'Am I in the place of God?' flattened to 'he was not God'; loses the point about judging.

bib-habakkuk-001-p01.plain: How long, God, must I cry out before you listen? I shout about violence and you do not save. Why make me watch wrongdoing, destruction and conflict all around?
bib-habakkuk-001-p01.core_idea: How long, God, must I cry unheard?

bib-habakkuk-001-p02.plain: God told the prophet to write the vision clearly so anyone could read it quickly. It is for a set time and will not fail; though it seems slow, wait for it, because it will surely come.
bib-habakkuk-001-p02.core_idea: Though it seems slow, wait; it will come

bib-habakkuk-001-p03.plain: Even if the fig trees, vines, olives and fields all fail, and the flocks and herds are gone, I will still rejoice in God my saviour. The Lord is my strength and makes me sure-footed on the heights.
bib-habakkuk-001-p03.core_idea: Even when everything fails, I will rejoice in God

bib-haggai-001-p01.plain: Think about how you are living. You plant much but harvest little; you eat and drink but are never satisfied; you dress but are never warm; and your wages vanish as if into a bag with holes.
bib-haggai-001-p01.core_idea: Look at your ways: much effort, little satisfaction

bib-hebrews-001-p01.plain: Our high priest understands our weaknesses, because he was tempted in every way as we are, yet did not sin. So let us come boldly to God's throne of grace to receive mercy and help when we need it.
bib-hebrews-001-p01.core_idea: Jesus understands our weakness; approach God boldly

bib-hebrews-002-p01.plain: So do not throw away your confidence; it will be richly rewarded. You need endurance, so that after doing God's will you receive what he promised.
bib-hebrews-002-p01.core_idea: Keep your confidence; endurance brings the promise

bib-hebrews-002-p02.plain: Faith is being sure of what we hope for and convinced of what we cannot see.
bib-hebrews-002-p02.core_idea: Faith is confidence in the hoped-for and unseen

bib-hebrews-002-p03.plain: By faith Abraham obeyed when God called him to go to the land he would inherit; he set out without knowing where he was going.
bib-hebrews-002-p03.core_idea: Faith sets out without knowing where

bib-hebrews-003-p01.plain: Since so many faithful witnesses surround us, let us drop every burden and the sin that trips us, and run our race with endurance, eyes on Jesus, who endured the cross for the joy ahead.
bib-hebrews-003-p01.core_idea: Drop every weight and run with endurance

judge.issue: Drops 'despising its shame', 'author and perfecter of faith', and Jesus seated at God's right hand.

bib-hebrews-003-p02.plain: Discipline feels painful, not pleasant, at the time, but later it brings the peace of right living to those trained by it. So strengthen your tired hands and weak knees, and walk straight paths so injuries can heal.

bib-hebrews-003-p03.plain: Keep loving each other as family. Welcome strangers, because some have hosted angels without knowing it. Remember prisoners as if you were in prison with them, and those who are mistreated, since you have a body too.
bib-hebrews-003-p03.core_idea: Love, welcome strangers, remember those who suffer

bib-hebrews-003-p04.plain: Do not love money; be content with what you have, because God has promised never to leave or abandon you. So we can say boldly that the Lord helps us and we will not fear what anyone can do.
bib-hebrews-003-p04.core_idea: Be content; God will never leave you

bib-hosea-001-p01.plain: Let us return to God. He has torn and wounded us, but he will heal us and soon raise us to live before him. Let us strive to know him; he will come as surely as sunrise, like spring rain.
bib-hosea-001-p01.core_idea: Return to God; he will heal what he wounded

judge.issue: Drops the 'two days... third day' revival and 'let us acknowledge Yahweh'.

bib-hosea-001-p02.plain: God wants mercy, not sacrifice; he wants people to know him more than he wants burnt offerings.
bib-hosea-001-p02.core_idea: God wants mercy more than ritual

bib-hosea-002-p01.plain: Sow what is right and you will reap kindness. Break up your hard, unplowed ground, because it is time to seek God until he comes and showers righteousness on you.
bib-hosea-002-p01.core_idea: Break up hard ground and seek God

bib-isaiah-001-p01.plain: Wash yourselves clean and put your evil deeds out of God's sight. Stop doing wrong and learn to do right: seek justice, help the oppressed, defend orphans and stand up for widows.
bib-isaiah-001-p01.core_idea: Stop doing wrong; learn to do right

bib-isaiah-001-p02.plain: God invites the people to talk things through: even if their sins are bright red like scarlet, they will become white as snow and wool.
bib-isaiah-001-p02.core_idea: Though sins are scarlet, they can be white as snow

bib-isaiah-001-p03.plain: Nations will no longer raise swords against one another, and they will not train for war any more.

bib-isaiah-001-p04.plain: Stop putting your trust in human beings; their life is only a breath, so what are they really worth?
bib-isaiah-001-p04.core_idea: Do not rely on mere mortals

bib-isaiah-001-p05.plain: Shame on those who keep buying up house after house and field after field until there is no room left for anyone, and they end up living alone in the land.

bib-isaiah-001-p06.plain: Shame on those who call evil good and good evil, who swap darkness for light and bitter for sweet. Shame on those who think themselves wise and clever.
bib-isaiah-001-p06.core_idea: Woe to those who call evil good

bib-isaiah-002-p01.plain: The prophet cried out that he was ruined, a man with unclean lips living among people with unclean lips, because he had seen God, the King.
bib-isaiah-002-p01.core_idea: Seeing God, I see my own unworthiness

bib-isaiah-002-p02.plain: I heard the Lord ask whom he should send and who would go. I answered: here I am, send me.

bib-isaiah-002-p03.plain: People who walked in darkness have seen a great light; light has shone on those living in the shadow of death.
bib-isaiah-002-p03.core_idea: Light has dawned on those in darkness

bib-isaiah-002-p04.plain: The people boasted: the brick buildings have fallen, but we will rebuild in cut stone; the fig trees are cut down, but we will plant cedars instead.
bib-isaiah-002-p04.core_idea: Proud boast: we will rebuild bigger

judge.issue: Adds 'the people boasted', a framing the passage itself does not state.

bib-isaiah-003-p01.plain: Can an axe boast against the one who swings it, or a saw against the one who uses it? That would be like a stick trying to lift the person holding it.
bib-isaiah-003-p01.core_idea: A tool cannot boast against its user

bib-isaiah-003-p02.plain: The wolf will live with the lamb and the leopard lie down with the young goat; calf and lion will be together, and a little child will lead them.
bib-isaiah-003-p02.core_idea: Enemies at peace, led by a child

bib-isaiah-003-p03.plain: God is my salvation; I will trust him and not be afraid, because the Lord is my strength and my song and has saved me.
bib-isaiah-003-p03.core_idea: I trust God and will not be afraid

bib-isaiah-003-p04.plain: The proud one who planned to climb above the stars and make himself like the Most High has fallen from heaven like the morning star, and will be brought down to the depths of the grave.
bib-isaiah-003-p04.core_idea: Pride that reaches for heaven falls to the pit

judge.issue: Shifts direct address to third person; drops 'who laid the nations low'.

bib-isaiah-004-p01.plain: Give advice and do justice. Shelter the outcasts like shade at midday; hide them, and do not betray those who are fleeing.
bib-isaiah-004-p01.core_idea: Shelter outcasts; do not betray the fugitive

bib-isaiah-004-p02.plain: My heart is racing and horror has seized me; the evening I longed for has turned to trembling.
bib-isaiah-004-p02.core_idea: The evening I longed for became dread

bib-isaiah-005-p01.plain: Someone calls to the watchman asking how much of the night is left. The watchman answers that morning is coming, but night too; ask again if you wish, and come back.

bib-isaiah-005-p02.plain: God will swallow up death for ever and wipe the tears from every face, and remove his people's disgrace from the whole earth, because God has said so.
bib-isaiah-005-p02.core_idea: God will end death and wipe away all tears

bib-isaiah-005-p03.plain: God keeps in perfect peace those whose minds stay fixed on him because they trust him. So trust God for ever; he is a rock that lasts for ever.
bib-isaiah-005-p03.core_idea: Trust in God keeps the mind in perfect peace

bib-isaiah-005-p04.plain: I long for you, God, through the night, and seek you with all my spirit, because when your judgements are seen on earth, people learn what is right.
bib-isaiah-005-p04.core_idea: I long for God in the night

bib-isaiah-006-p01.plain: Like a woman in labour crying out in pain, we have suffered before you, God, but have given birth only to wind; we have achieved no rescue on the earth.
bib-isaiah-006-p01.core_idea: We laboured in pain and produced only wind

judge.issue: Drops 'neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen'.

bib-isaiah-006-p02.plain: Go into your rooms, my people, and shut the doors. Hide for a little while until the anger has passed.
bib-isaiah-006-p02.core_idea: Shelter a little while until it passes

bib-isaiah-007-p01.plain: God says you will be saved by turning back and resting; your strength will come from quietness and trust.
bib-isaiah-007-p01.core_idea: Strength lies in quietness and trust

bib-isaiah-007-p02.plain: Even if God gives you hardship and suffering to live on, your teachers will no longer be hidden; whichever way you turn, you will hear a voice behind you saying, this is the way, walk in it.
bib-isaiah-007-p02.core_idea: Even in hardship you will hear: this is the way

bib-isaiah-007-p03.plain: Each person will be like a shelter from the wind and storm, like streams in a dry land, like the shade of a great rock in a weary country.
bib-isaiah-007-p03.core_idea: A person can be shelter for others

judge.issue: 'A man' generalised to 'each person', loosening who is meant.

bib-isaiah-007-p04.plain: Doing right will bring peace, and its result will be quiet and confidence for ever. God's people will live in peaceful homes, safe and quietly at rest.
bib-isaiah-007-p04.core_idea: Righteousness brings peace, quiet and safety

bib-isaiah-007-p05.plain: Lord, be kind to us; we have waited for you. Be our strength every morning and our rescue in times of trouble.
bib-isaiah-007-p05.core_idea: God, be our strength every morning

bib-isaiah-007-p06.plain: The wilderness and dry land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and bloom like a rose.

bib-isaiah-008-p01.plain: Strengthen weak hands and shaky knees. Tell the fearful: be strong, don't be afraid; your God is coming with vengeance and retribution, and he will come and save you.
bib-isaiah-008-p01.core_idea: Be strong, do not fear; God will save you
bib-isaiah-008-p01.plain_v1: Strengthen tired hands and weak knees. Tell the frightened to be strong and not afraid, because their God is coming to set things right and save them.

judge_v1.issue: Softens 'God will come with vengeance, God's retribution' to 'set things right'.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Softens 'vengeance' and 'God's retribution' to 'set things right'.

bib-isaiah-008-p02.plain: Gravely ill, King Hezekiah said he was going to the grave in mid-life, robbed of his remaining years, never again to see God or people among the living; his life was being cut off like cloth from a loom.
bib-isaiah-008-p02.core_idea: Lament at life cut off in its middle

judge.issue: Adds Hezekiah's illness as context; drops shepherd's tent and 'you will make an end of me'.

bib-isaiah-008-p03.plain: I suffered bitterly instead of having peace, but in your love you saved my life from the pit and threw all my sins behind your back.
bib-isaiah-008-p03.core_idea: God in love saved me and cast my sins away

bib-isaiah-009-p01.plain: God tells his messengers to comfort his people. Speak tenderly to Jerusalem: her hard service is over, her guilt is forgiven, and she has paid twice over for her sins.
bib-isaiah-009-p01.core_idea: Comfort my people: their hardship is over

bib-isaiah-009-p02.plain: A voice is told to cry out a message: all people are like grass, and their glory like wild flowers. The grass withers and the flower fades when God's breath blows, but God's word lasts for ever.
bib-isaiah-009-p02.core_idea: People fade like grass; God's word endures

bib-isaiah-009-p03.plain: God will come in power and rule. Yet he will care for his flock like a shepherd: he gathers the lambs in his arms, carries them close, and gently leads the mothers with young.
bib-isaiah-009-p03.core_idea: God carries his lambs like a gentle shepherd

judge.issue: Drops 'his reward is with him, and his recompense before him'.

bib-isaiah-009-p04.plain: The eternal God, creator of the earth, never tires, and his understanding has no limit. He strengthens the weak. Even the young grow tired and fall, but those who wait for God will renew their strength and soar like eagles.
bib-isaiah-009-p04.core_idea: Those who wait for God renew their strength

judge.issue: Drops 'run and not be weary, walk and not faint' and strength to the mightless.

bib-isaiah-009-p05.plain: Do not be afraid, because I am with you; do not lose heart, because I am your God. I will strengthen you, help you, and hold you up with my righteous right hand.
bib-isaiah-009-p05.core_idea: Do not fear; God is with you and upholds you

bib-isaiah-009-p06.plain: God presents his chosen servant, filled with his Spirit, who will bring justice to the nations. He will not shout or make a show; he will not break a bruised reed or snuff out a faint flame.
bib-isaiah-009-p06.core_idea: God's servant is gentle with the bruised and faint

judge.issue: Drops 'in whom my soul delights' and 'he will faithfully bring justice'.

bib-isaiah-009-p07.plain: God says he will lead the blind along roads and paths they do not know, turn their darkness into light and their crooked places straight, and never abandon them.
bib-isaiah-009-p07.core_idea: God leads the blind on unknown paths

bib-isaiah-009-p08.plain: God, who created and formed his people, says: do not be afraid, because I have rescued you. I have called you by name; you are mine.
bib-isaiah-009-p08.core_idea: Do not fear; God called you by name

bib-isaiah-010-p01.plain: When you go through deep waters, I will be with you, and the rivers will not sweep you away. When you walk through fire, you will not be burned, and the flames will not hurt you.
bib-isaiah-010-p01.core_idea: Through water and fire, God is with you

bib-isaiah-010-p02.plain: Do not dwell on the past or what happened long ago. God is doing something new; it is springing up now. He will make a road through the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
bib-isaiah-010-p02.core_idea: Forget the past; God is doing a new thing

bib-isaiah-010-p03.plain: God says he has wiped away your wrongdoings and sins like a thick cloud; come back to him, because he has rescued you.
bib-isaiah-010-p03.core_idea: Your sins are wiped away; return to God

bib-isaiah-010-p04.plain: God tells his people that he has carried them since birth, and he will go on carrying them into old age and grey hair. He made them, and he will bear them, carry them and rescue them.
bib-isaiah-010-p04.core_idea: God carries you from birth to old age

bib-isaiah-011-p01.plain: God says he has refined his people, though not the way silver is refined; he chose them in the furnace of suffering.
bib-isaiah-011-p01.core_idea: Chosen in the furnace of suffering

bib-isaiah-011-p02.plain: If only you had listened to my commands! Then your peace would have flowed like a river, and your goodness would have rolled on like the waves of the sea.
bib-isaiah-011-p02.core_idea: Heeding God brings peace like a river

bib-isaiah-011-p03.plain: I thought my work had been useless and my strength spent for nothing; yet what is due to me rests with God, and my reward is with him.
bib-isaiah-011-p03.core_idea: Though effort seems wasted, God holds my reward

bib-isaiah-011-p04.plain: Zion said God had abandoned and forgotten her. God answers: could a mother forget her nursing baby? Even if she could, I will not forget you. I have written you on the palms of my hands.

judge.issue: Drops "your walls are continually before me."

bib-isaiah-011-p05.plain: God has taught me how to speak so that my words can hold up someone who is weary. Every morning he wakes me to listen like a student.
bib-isaiah-011-p05.core_idea: God teaches words that sustain the weary

bib-isaiah-011-p06.plain: Because God helps me, I have not been put to shame. So I have set my face like stone, knowing I will not be let down.
bib-isaiah-011-p06.core_idea: With God's help, I set my face like flint

bib-isaiah-011-p07.plain: Whoever honours God but walks in darkness with no light should trust in God's name and lean on their God.
bib-isaiah-011-p07.core_idea: In darkness without light, trust God

judge.issue: Drops the condition of obeying the voice of God's servant.

bib-isaiah-012-p01.plain: Look at the sky and the earth: the heavens will vanish like smoke and the earth wear out like clothing, and its people will die too. But God's salvation lasts for ever, and his justice will never end.
bib-isaiah-012-p01.core_idea: All things pass; God's salvation lasts for ever

bib-isaiah-012-p02.plain: God tells those who hold his law in their hearts: do not fear people's scorn or be shaken by their insults. They will be eaten away like moth-eaten cloth, but God's justice and salvation last for ever.
bib-isaiah-012-p02.core_idea: Do not fear people's insults; they will pass

bib-isaiah-012-p03.plain: God says: I am the one who comforts you. Why fear mortals who wither like grass, and forget God your Maker who spread out the heavens? Why live in constant fear of the oppressor's fury? Where is that fury now?
bib-isaiah-012-p03.core_idea: Why fear mortals when God comforts you?

bib-isaiah-012-p04.plain: How beautiful is the arrival of the messenger crossing the mountains with good news of peace and salvation, telling Zion that its God reigns.
bib-isaiah-012-p04.core_idea: Beautiful are those who bring good news

bib-isaiah-012-p05.plain: God says he abandoned his people for a brief moment, but will gather them back with great mercy; in a flash of anger he hid his face, but his everlasting love will have mercy on them.

bib-isaiah-012-p06.plain: Even if the mountains are moved and the hills shaken, God's steadfast love will not leave you, and his promise of peace will not be taken away.

bib-isaiah-012-p07.plain: Come, all who are thirsty, come to the water; even with no money, come and eat for free. Why spend money on what is not food, and work for what never satisfies? Listen to God and feed your soul.
bib-isaiah-012-p07.core_idea: Why spend yourself on what does not satisfy?

bib-isaiah-012-p08.plain: God says his thoughts and ways are not like ours: as the heavens are higher than the earth, so his ways and thoughts are higher than ours.
bib-isaiah-012-p08.core_idea: God's ways are higher than our ways

bib-isaiah-012-p09.plain: You will go out with joy and be led in peace. The mountains and hills will burst into song before you, and all the trees will clap their hands.
bib-isaiah-012-p09.core_idea: You will go out in joy and peace

bib-isaiah-013-p01.plain: Good people die and no one takes it to heart; the kind are taken away and no one realises they are spared from coming evil. They enter peace and rest, those who lived upright lives.
bib-isaiah-013-p01.core_idea: The righteous who die enter peace

bib-isaiah-013-p02.plain: The high and holy God, who lives for ever, says he lives in the high and holy place, and also with those who are crushed and humble in spirit, to revive them.
bib-isaiah-013-p02.core_idea: God dwells with the humble and crushed in spirit

bib-isaiah-013-p03.plain: The fast God wants is this: break the chains of injustice and free the oppressed; feed the hungry, shelter the homeless poor, clothe the naked, and do not turn from your own. Then your light will break out like dawn.
bib-isaiah-013-p03.core_idea: True devotion is freeing the oppressed and feeding the hungry

judge.issue: Drops the promised healing, righteousness going before, and God's glory as rear guard.

bib-isaiah-013-p04.plain: We hope for light but find darkness, for brightness but walk in gloom. We feel along the wall like the blind and stumble at noon as if it were dusk; among the strong we are like the dead.
bib-isaiah-013-p04.core_idea: We look for light but walk in darkness

bib-isaiah-013-p05.plain: Get up and shine, because your light has come and God's glory has risen on you. Darkness will cover the earth and its peoples, but God will rise on you and his glory will be seen on you.
bib-isaiah-013-p05.core_idea: Arise, shine: your light has come

bib-isaiah-013-p06.plain: You will no longer need the sun or moon for light, because God will be your everlasting light and your glory. Your sun will never set again, and your days of mourning will be over.
bib-isaiah-013-p06.core_idea: God will be your light; mourning will end

bib-isaiah-013-p07.plain: The Lord's Spirit is on me: Yahweh anointed me to bring good news to the humble, heal the broken-hearted, free captives, proclaim his year of favour and our God's day of vengeance, and comfort mourners, giving joy for ashes, so they become his righteous planting, for his glory.
bib-isaiah-013-p07.core_idea: Sent to heal the broken-hearted and comfort mourners
bib-isaiah-013-p07.plain_v1: The speaker says God's Spirit has anointed him to bring good news to the humble, heal the broken-hearted, free captives, and comfort all who mourn, giving them beauty for ashes, joy for mourning and praise for despair.

judge_v1.issue: Drops "the day of vengeance of our God", softening the hard saying.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the 'day of vengeance' and the purpose that they be trees of righteousness.

bib-isaiah-014-p01.plain: I will rejoice greatly in God, and my soul will be glad, because he has dressed me in salvation and righteousness, like a groom in his garland or a bride in her jewels.
bib-isaiah-014-p01.core_idea: I rejoice: God has clothed me in salvation

bib-isaiah-014-p02.plain: You will no longer be called Forsaken, nor your land Desolate. You will be called My Delight, and your land Married, because God delights in you.
bib-isaiah-014-p02.core_idea: No longer forsaken: God delights in you

bib-isaiah-014-p03.plain: In all their suffering God suffered too, and his presence saved them. In love and pity he rescued them, and lifted and carried them through all the years of old.
bib-isaiah-014-p03.core_idea: God suffers with his people and carries them

bib-isaiah-014-p04.plain: We have all become unclean, and even our good deeds are like filthy rags. We all wither like leaves, and our sins sweep us away like the wind.
bib-isaiah-014-p04.core_idea: Our sins sweep us away like leaves

bib-isaiah-014-p05.plain: Yet, God, you are our Father. We are the clay and you are the potter; we are all the work of your hands.
bib-isaiah-014-p05.core_idea: We are clay; God is the potter

bib-isaiah-014-p06.plain: God says he is creating new heavens and a new earth, and the past will be forgotten. Rejoice for ever in what he creates. He will delight in his people, and weeping will never be heard in Jerusalem again.
bib-isaiah-014-p06.core_idea: God makes all things new; weeping will end

bib-isaiah-014-p07.plain: God says that before people call he will answer, and while they are still speaking he will hear.

bib-isaiah-014-p08.plain: God says he will comfort you as a mother comforts her child.

bib-james-001-p01.plain: When you face all kinds of trials, consider it pure joy, because testing your faith builds endurance. Let endurance finish its work, so that you become mature and complete, lacking nothing.
bib-james-001-p01.core_idea: Trials build endurance; welcome them with joy

bib-james-001-p02.plain: If you lack wisdom, ask God, who gives generously to all without scolding, and you will receive it. But ask in faith without doubting; a doubter is like a wind-tossed wave, unstable, and should expect nothing from the Lord.
bib-james-001-p02.core_idea: Ask God for wisdom, in faith without doubting

bib-james-001-p03.plain: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to get angry, because human anger does not produce the goodness God wants.
bib-james-001-p03.core_idea: Quick to listen, slow to speak and anger

bib-james-001-p04.plain: Do what God's word says; just listening fools you. A mere listener is like someone who sees their face in a mirror and forgets it at once. Whoever keeps to the law of freedom and acts will be blessed.
bib-james-001-p04.core_idea: Do what you hear, not only listen

bib-james-001-p05.plain: Pure religion in God's eyes is this: caring for orphans and widows in their distress, and keeping yourself from being corrupted by the world.
bib-james-001-p05.core_idea: True religion: care for the vulnerable, stay unstained

bib-james-001-p06.plain: What use is saying you have faith if you do nothing? If someone lacks clothes and food and you just wish them well without giving what they need, what good is that? Faith without action is dead.

bib-james-001-p07.plain: A small bit steers a horse, and a small rudder steers a huge ship through strong winds. The tongue is small too, yet it boasts of great things. Think how a tiny spark sets a whole forest on fire.
bib-james-001-p07.core_idea: The small tongue has huge power

bib-james-001-p08.plain: The wise show it by gentle good conduct. If bitter jealousy and selfish ambition fill your heart, don't boast or lie against the truth: that wisdom is earthly, sensual and demonic, breeding disorder and evil. Wisdom from above is pure, peaceful, gentle, merciful and sincere, and peacemakers sow righteousness.
bib-james-001-p08.core_idea: True wisdom is gentle and peaceful, not envious
bib-james-001-p08.plain_v1: If you are wise, show it by good deeds done gently. Bitter jealousy and selfish ambition are not wisdom from above; they bring disorder and evil. Wisdom from above is pure, peaceful, gentle, merciful and sincere, and peacemakers reap righteousness.

judge_v1.issue: Drops "earthly, sensual, and demonic" and the command not to boast or lie; softens.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the warning not to boast or lie against the truth.

bib-james-001-p09.plain: Your fights and wars come from the cravings battling inside you. You want and don't get, so you murder and covet, and fight. You don't have because you don't ask; and when you ask, you don't receive, because you want it only for your pleasures.
bib-james-001-p09.plain_v1: Fights come from the desires warring inside you. You want what you cannot have, so you fight. You do not have because you do not ask God, and when you ask, you ask only for your own pleasures.

judge_v1.issue: Drops "you murder and covet", softening the accusation.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops murder and covetousness; makes the asking explicitly of God.

bib-james-001-p10.plain: Don't run each other down, because judging a fellow believer sets you above God's law. There is only one lawgiver, who can save or destroy, so who are you to judge anyone?
bib-james-001-p10.core_idea: Only God may judge; we have no right to

bib-james-001-p11.plain: You plan next year's business as if sure of it, yet you don't know what tomorrow brings, for your life is a passing mist. Say instead, "If the Lord wills, we will live and do this."
bib-james-001-p11.core_idea: Life is brief; make plans subject to God's will

bib-james-001-p12.plain: Be patient until the Lord comes. A farmer waits patiently for the rains and the harvest; be patient like that too, and steady your hearts, because the Lord's coming is near.
bib-james-001-p12.core_idea: Wait patiently, like a farmer, for the Lord

bib-james-001-p13.plain: If you are suffering, pray. If you are happy, sing praise.
bib-james-001-p13.core_idea: Pray in suffering; sing praise in joy

bib-james-001-p14.plain: Admit your wrongs to each other and pray for each other so you can be healed. A good person's earnest prayer has great power.
bib-james-001-p14.core_idea: Confession and prayer for one another bring healing

bib-jeremiah-001-p01.plain: God tells Jeremiah he knew and chose him before birth. Jeremiah protests that he is too young to speak; God says not to plead youth, to go and speak, and not to fear, for God is with him.
bib-jeremiah-001-p01.core_idea: God chose you before birth and goes with you

judge.issue: Compresses God's command to say whatever he commands; drops promise to rescue.

bib-jeremiah-001-p02.plain: God says his people have done two wrongs: they left him, the source of living water, and dug their own cracked tanks that cannot hold water.
bib-jeremiah-001-p02.core_idea: Leaving God for empty substitutes that hold nothing

bib-jeremiah-002-p01.plain: I am in agony, my heart pounding and trembling inside me. I cannot stay quiet, because I have heard the trumpet and the alarm of war.
bib-jeremiah-002-p01.core_idea: Anguish of heart at the sound of war

bib-jeremiah-002-p02.plain: God says: stop at the crossroads and look; ask for the old, proven paths and which is the good way. Walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls.
bib-jeremiah-002-p02.core_idea: Seek the old good way and find rest

bib-jeremiah-003-p01.plain: If only I could find comfort in my sorrow! My heart is weak inside me.
bib-jeremiah-003-p01.core_idea: Longing for comfort in deep sorrow

bib-jeremiah-003-p02.plain: I am wounded by my people's wound and mourn: is there no healing balm, no doctor, so why aren't they healed? I wish my eyes were a spring of tears to weep day and night for the dead.
bib-jeremiah-003-p02.core_idea: Grieving for others' suffering, longing for healing

bib-jeremiah-003-p03.plain: God says the wise, the strong and the rich should not boast of what they have. If anyone boasts, let it be in knowing God, who acts with kindness, justice and right, which he delights in.
bib-jeremiah-003-p03.core_idea: Boast only in knowing God, not wisdom, strength, wealth

bib-jeremiah-004-p01.plain: My wound is grave, but I said, "This is my grief, and I must carry it." My home is torn down, my children are gone, and there is no one left to help me rebuild.
bib-jeremiah-004-p01.core_idea: Accepting a grief that must be carried

bib-jeremiah-004-p02.plain: Lord, I know people cannot steer their own lives. Correct me, God, but gently, not in anger, or you will crush me to nothing.
bib-jeremiah-004-p02.core_idea: We cannot direct our steps; correct me gently

bib-jeremiah-004-p03.plain: God, you are just, yet let me ask why the wicked prosper and traitors live at ease. You planted them and they flourish; they speak of you, but their hearts are far from you.

bib-jeremiah-004-p04.plain: If racing men on foot has worn you out, how will you race horses? If you only feel safe in peaceful country, how will you cope in the wild Jordan thickets?
bib-jeremiah-004-p04.core_idea: If small trials tire you, harder ones await

bib-jeremiah-005-p01.plain: I wish I had never been born, Mother: everyone fights with me. I have neither lent nor borrowed, yet everyone curses me.
bib-jeremiah-005-p01.core_idea: Cursed by all though I have wronged no one

bib-jeremiah-005-p02.plain: Your words were my joy, and because of you I sat alone, apart from the merrymakers. Why does my pain never end, and will you fail me like a stream that runs dry?
bib-jeremiah-005-p02.core_idea: Joy in God's word, yet lonely unending pain

judge.issue: Drops "filled me with indignation" and being called by God's name.

bib-jeremiah-005-p03.plain: Yahweh says: cursed is whoever trusts in people and turns from him; he will be like a desert shrub in parched salt land. Blessed is whoever trusts in Yahweh; he will be like a tree by water, green in heat, unworried in drought, always bearing fruit.
bib-jeremiah-005-p03.core_idea: Trust God and flourish like a well-watered tree
bib-jeremiah-005-p03.plain_v1: God says those who trust in people and turn from him are like a desert shrub that never sees good. Those who trust God are like a tree by a river: unafraid of heat, green, fruitful even in drought.

judge_v1.issue: Drops "cursed" and "blessed", softening the hard saying into a comparison.

bib-jeremiah-005-p04.plain: The human heart is more deceptive than anything, and deeply sick. Who can understand it?
bib-jeremiah-005-p04.core_idea: The human heart deceives and cannot be fathomed

bib-jeremiah-005-p05.plain: Someone who gets rich unjustly is like a partridge sitting on eggs it did not lay. The riches will leave him halfway through life, and at the end he will be shown a fool.
bib-jeremiah-005-p05.core_idea: Wealth gained wrongly is lost; the gainer proves a fool

bib-jeremiah-005-p06.plain: Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved, because you are the one I praise.

bib-jeremiah-006-p01.plain: At the potter's house I watched a pot go wrong in his hands, so he reshaped it into another, as he saw fit. God then says Israel is like that clay in his hands.
bib-jeremiah-006-p01.core_idea: God can reshape us as a potter reshapes clay

extension.text: Then I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was making something on the wheels. When the vessel that he made of the clay was marred in the hand of the potter, he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it. Then Yahweh’s word came to me, saying, “House of Israel, can’t I do with you as this potter?” says Yahweh. “Behold, as the clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.

bib-jeremiah-006-p02.plain: Lord, you persuaded me and overpowered me, and now everyone mocks me for your message. Yet if I try to stop speaking, it burns like fire in my bones and I cannot hold it in.
bib-jeremiah-006-p02.core_idea: God's word burns within and cannot be held in

bib-jeremiah-006-p03.plain: Why was I ever born, only to see trouble and sorrow, and spend my days in shame?
bib-jeremiah-006-p03.core_idea: Why was I born to sorrow and shame?

bib-jeremiah-007-p01.plain: God asks the king: does building with fine cedar make you a king? Your father ate and drank, yet did what was just and fair, and defended the poor and needy; that is what knowing God means.
bib-jeremiah-007-p01.core_idea: Knowing God means doing justice for the poor

bib-jeremiah-009-p01.plain: God says his plans for you are for peace, not harm, to give you hope and a future. Call and pray and he will listen; seek him with all your heart and you will find him.
bib-jeremiah-009-p01.core_idea: God plans hope for you; seek him and find

bib-jeremiah-009-p02.plain: God appeared to me long ago and said, "I have loved you with a love that lasts forever, so I have drawn you to me with kindness."
bib-jeremiah-009-p02.core_idea: God loves you with an everlasting love

bib-jeremiah-009-p03.plain: God says a cry is heard: Rachel weeping for her children, refusing comfort, because they are gone. Then God tells her to stop weeping; her work will be rewarded, there is hope, and her children will come home.
bib-jeremiah-009-p03.core_idea: Weeping mother told her children will return

bib-jeremiah-009-p04.plain: God says: I have given the weary soul its fill, and refreshed everyone who is sorrowful.
bib-jeremiah-009-p04.core_idea: God refreshes the weary and the sorrowful

bib-jeremiah-010-p01.plain: God says: I am the Lord, the God of every living being. Is anything too hard for me?
bib-jeremiah-010-p01.core_idea: Nothing is too hard for God

bib-jeremiah-010-p02.plain: God says: call to me and I will answer, and show you great, hidden things you do not know.
bib-jeremiah-010-p02.core_idea: Call to God and he will answer

bib-jeremiah-014-p01.plain: God repeats Baruch's complaint that God has added sorrow to his pain, and that he is worn out with groaning and finds no rest.
bib-jeremiah-014-p01.core_idea: Worn out by sorrow and finding no rest

bib-jeremiah-015-p01.plain: God says: leave your orphaned children with me; I will keep them alive. Let your widows trust in me.
bib-jeremiah-015-p01.core_idea: God will care for orphans and widows

bib-jeremiah-015-p02.plain: My people have been like lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray and sent them wandering over the hills, until they forgot where their place of rest was.
bib-jeremiah-015-p02.core_idea: Misled people lost and far from their rest

bib-jeremiah-016-p01.plain: Don't lose heart or be afraid of the news you hear. One year brings one report, the next year another, with violence and rulers fighting each other.
bib-jeremiah-016-p01.core_idea: Don't lose heart at alarming news

bib-job-001-p01.plain: Job says he was born with nothing and will die with nothing. The Lord gave and the Lord has taken away, and may the Lord's name be blessed.
bib-job-001-p01.core_idea: God gives and takes away; bless him still

bib-job-001-p02.plain: When Job's three friends heard of his disaster, they came to comfort him. Seeing him unrecognisable, they wept, tore their robes and sat on the ground with him seven days and nights, silent, because his grief was so great.
bib-job-001-p02.core_idea: Friends sat silently with Job in his grief

bib-job-001-p03.plain: Job asks why people in misery are kept alive, longing for a death that does not come. His groans pour out like water; what he feared has happened, and he has no ease, no quiet, no rest.
bib-job-001-p03.core_idea: Why is life given to those in misery?

judge.issue: Drops "whom God has hedged in" and the gladness at finding the grave.

bib-job-001-p04.plain: Job's friend says: you have taught many and strengthened weak, stumbling people with your words. But now trouble has come to you, and you lose heart and are shaken.
bib-job-001-p04.core_idea: The comforter falters when trouble reaches him

bib-job-001-p05.plain: Resentment kills the fool, and jealousy kills the naive.
bib-job-001-p05.core_idea: Resentment and jealousy destroy the foolish

bib-job-001-p06.plain: Trouble doesn't sprout from the soil like a weed; people are born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
bib-job-001-p06.core_idea: Trouble is part of being human

bib-job-001-p07.plain: Job asks what strength or future he has to make waiting worthwhile, since he is not made of stone or bronze. He has no help left in him, and good sense has been driven away.
bib-job-001-p07.core_idea: Too exhausted to wait any longer

bib-job-001-p08.plain: Someone who is about to collapse should be shown kindness by his friend, even if he has stopped fearing God.
bib-job-001-p08.core_idea: A friend owes kindness to one who is collapsing

bib-job-002-p01.plain: Job says human life is forced labour, like a hired worker's. He has been given months of misery and weary nights; lying down, he longs for morning and tosses and turns until dawn.
bib-job-002-p01.core_idea: Months of misery and sleepless nights

bib-job-002-p02.plain: Job says his days fly faster than a weaver's shuttle and pass without hope. He asks God to remember that his life is only a breath; he will never see good again.
bib-job-002-p02.core_idea: Life is a breath passing without hope

bib-job-002-p03.plain: Ask the generations before us and learn what their ancestors discovered, for we are newcomers who know nothing and our days are a shadow. Won't they teach you from their hearts?
bib-job-002-p03.core_idea: Learn from the wisdom of past generations

bib-job-002-p04.plain: Job says his days race by without good. If he tries to forget his complaint and cheer up, he still dreads his sorrows; he knows God won't clear him, so why struggle in vain?
bib-job-002-p04.core_idea: Trying to cheer up while dreading one's sorrows

bib-job-002-p05.plain: Job says: I am sick of my life. I will let my complaint pour out and speak from the bitterness of my soul.
bib-job-002-p05.core_idea: Weary of life, speaking out of bitterness

bib-job-002-p06.plain: Job's friend promises he will lift his face without shame and stand firm without fear. He will forget his misery like water that has flowed past; darkness will become morning, and hope will make him secure.
bib-job-002-p06.core_idea: Misery will pass like water; hope brings safety

bib-job-002-p07.plain: Those who are comfortable look down on people who suffer misfortune; they think disaster is meant for those already slipping.
bib-job-002-p07.core_idea: The comfortable scorn those who suffer

bib-job-002-p08.plain: Ask the animals and they will teach you; ask the birds and they will tell you. Speak to the earth and it will teach you, and the fish of the sea will explain.
bib-job-002-p08.core_idea: Creation itself teaches, if you ask

bib-job-003-p01.plain: If only you would keep completely quiet! That would be wisdom.
bib-job-003-p01.core_idea: Silence would be wiser than your words

bib-job-003-p02.plain: A human being lives only a few days, full of trouble. He blooms like a flower and is cut down; he slips away like a shadow and does not last.
bib-job-003-p02.core_idea: Human life is short and full of trouble

bib-job-003-p03.plain: There is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again. Even if its root grows old and its stump dies, at the scent of water it will bud and put out new shoots.
bib-job-003-p03.core_idea: A cut-down tree can sprout again

bib-job-003-p04.plain: Job calls his friends miserable comforters full of empty words; in their place he would strengthen them, not lecture. Yet whether he speaks or keeps silent, his grief does not ease.
bib-job-003-p04.core_idea: Miserable comforters; grief that will not ease

bib-job-003-p05.plain: Even so, the righteous keep to their path, and those with clean hands grow stronger and stronger.
bib-job-003-p05.core_idea: The righteous hold on and grow stronger

bib-job-003-p06.plain: My days are over, my plans broken off, and so are the hopes of my heart.
bib-job-003-p06.core_idea: My days are over and my plans broken

bib-job-003-p07.plain: My relatives have gone, and my close friends have forgotten me.

bib-job-004-p01.plain: Job says his closest friends loathe him and those he loved have turned against him. Wasted to skin and bone, he begs them to have pity on him, for God's hand has struck him.
bib-job-004-p01.core_idea: Abandoned by friends, begging for pity

bib-job-004-p02.plain: Job says: I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end he will stand upon the earth.
bib-job-004-p02.core_idea: My Redeemer lives and will stand at last

bib-job-004-p03.plain: Why do wicked people live long and grow powerful? Their children thrive around them, their homes are safe from fear, and God does not punish them.
bib-job-004-p03.core_idea: Why do the wicked live safe and prosper?

bib-job-004-p04.plain: One person dies strong, comfortable and well fed; another dies bitter, never having enjoyed good. Both lie down alike in the dust, covered by worms.
bib-job-004-p04.core_idea: Death levels the fortunate and the bitter alike

bib-job-004-p05.plain: Job says he looks east, west, north and south and cannot find God anywhere. But God knows the path he takes, and when God has tested him, he will come out like gold.
bib-job-004-p05.core_idea: God knows my way; testing will refine me

bib-job-005-p01.plain: As long as I live I will not give up my integrity. I will hold on to doing right and never let it go; my conscience will not accuse me.
bib-job-005-p01.core_idea: Holding on to integrity until death

bib-job-005-p02.plain: Where can wisdom be found? It is not in the deep or the sea, it cannot be bought with gold, silver or jewels, and it is worth more than rubies.
bib-job-005-p02.core_idea: Wisdom is priceless and cannot be bought

bib-job-005-p03.plain: God told humankind: reverence for the Lord is wisdom, and turning away from evil is understanding.
bib-job-005-p03.core_idea: Revering God is wisdom; shunning evil, understanding

bib-job-005-p04.plain: Job longs for the old days when God watched over him and lit his way through darkness, when God's friendship filled his home, his children were around him, life overflowed, and he was honoured in the city.
bib-job-005-p04.core_idea: Longing for past days of God's closeness

bib-job-005-p05.plain: I was eyes for the blind and feet for the lame. I was a father to the poor, and I looked into the case of strangers.
bib-job-005-p05.core_idea: I served the blind, the lame, the poor

bib-job-005-p06.plain: Job wept for people in trouble and grieved for the poor, yet when he hoped for good, evil came, and when he waited for light, darkness came. His heart is restless, and days of suffering have arrived.
bib-job-005-p06.core_idea: I hoped for light, and darkness came

bib-job-005-p07.plain: Job says he made a promise with his own eyes, so how could he look lustfully at a young woman?
bib-job-005-p07.core_idea: A covenant with my eyes against lust

bib-job-006-p01.plain: A young man says he held back from speaking to his elders, thinking age should teach wisdom. But understanding comes from God's breath in a person; greatness and age don't make someone wise or just.
bib-job-006-p01.core_idea: Wisdom comes from God's spirit, not age

bib-job-006-p02.plain: Has anyone ever said to God that they are guilty and won't do wrong again, and asked to be taught what they cannot see?
bib-job-006-p02.core_idea: Admit guilt, ask to see, and stop doing wrong

bib-job-006-p03.plain: No one asks, "Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night and makes us wiser than the animals and birds?"
bib-job-006-p03.core_idea: God gives songs in the night, yet none seek him

bib-job-006-p04.plain: Don't let wealth lure you into anger or a big bribe lead you astray. Would your riches or all your strength keep you safe when trouble comes?
bib-job-006-p04.core_idea: Wealth and strength won't save you in distress

bib-job-007-p01.plain: Stop, and think about the wonderful works of God.
bib-job-007-p01.core_idea: Pause and consider God's wondrous works

bib-job-007-p02.plain: God asks Job where he was when the earth's foundations were laid, and tells him to answer if he understands. Who set its measurements and its cornerstone, while the morning stars sang and the angels shouted for joy?
bib-job-007-p02.core_idea: Where were you when God made the earth?

bib-job-007-p03.plain: Job answers God that he is insignificant and has nothing to say, and puts his hand over his mouth. He has spoken once, even twice, and will say no more.
bib-job-007-p03.core_idea: Humbled before God, I fall silent

bib-joel-001-p01.plain: God says: even now, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning. Tear your hearts, not your clothes, and return to God, who is gracious, merciful, slow to anger and full of love.
bib-joel-001-p01.core_idea: Return to God with a torn heart

bib-joel-001-p02.plain: God says: I will repay you for the years the locusts ate, the swarms I sent among you.
bib-joel-001-p02.core_idea: God will restore the years that were lost

bib-john-001-p01.plain: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.

bib-john-001-p02.plain: The wind blows where it wants; you hear it but don't know where it comes from or goes. That is how it is with everyone born of the Spirit.
bib-john-001-p02.core_idea: Those born of the Spirit are like the wind

bib-john-001-p03.plain: God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that whoever believes in him will not perish but have eternal life. God sent him not to condemn the world but to save it.
bib-john-001-p03.core_idea: God gave his Son to save the world

bib-john-001-p04.plain: Everyone who does evil hates the light and avoids it, so their deeds won't be exposed. But whoever lives by the truth comes into the light, so it is clear their deeds were done in God.
bib-john-001-p04.core_idea: Evil hides from light; truth comes into it

bib-john-001-p05.plain: Jesus tells her that whoever drinks this water will be thirsty again, but whoever drinks the water he gives will never thirst; it becomes in them a spring welling up to eternal life.
bib-john-001-p05.core_idea: Jesus offers water that ends all thirst

bib-john-002-p01.plain: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth.
bib-john-002-p01.core_idea: Worship God in spirit and truth

bib-john-002-p02.plain: The saying is true: one person sows and another reaps. I sent you to harvest what you did not work for; others did the labour, and you have benefited from it.
bib-john-002-p02.core_idea: We reap what others have sown

bib-john-002-p03.plain: Jesus asked a man ill for thirty-eight years if he wanted to be well; the man said no one would help him into the pool. Jesus told him to take his mat and walk, and he was healed at once.
bib-john-002-p03.core_idea: Do you want to be made well?

extension.text: A certain man was there, who had been sick for thirty-eight years. When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had been sick for a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to be made well?” The sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, but while I’m coming, another steps down before me.” Jesus said to him, “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.” Immediately, the man was made well, and took up his mat and walked.

bib-john-002-p04.plain: How can you believe, when you seek praise from one another and not the honour that comes from the only God?
bib-john-002-p04.core_idea: Seeking human praise blocks faith in God

bib-john-003-p01.plain: Jesus says: whoever comes to me I will never turn away.

bib-john-003-p02.plain: Don't judge by appearances; judge fairly.

bib-john-003-p03.plain: Leaders brought Jesus a woman caught in adultery, and he told them whoever was without sin should throw the first stone, so they all left. He told her he did not condemn her, and to go and sin no more.
bib-john-003-p03.core_idea: Let the sinless throw the first stone

bib-john-003-p04.plain: You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
bib-john-003-p04.core_idea: The truth will set you free

bib-john-004-p01.plain: Seeing a man blind from birth, the disciples asked whose sin caused it, his or his parents'. Jesus said neither sinned; it happened so that God's works could be shown in him.
bib-john-004-p01.core_idea: Suffering is not always punishment for sin

bib-john-004-p02.plain: Jesus says: I am the good shepherd, who gives his life for the sheep. A hired hand who doesn't own them runs when the wolf comes and leaves them scattered, because he doesn't care for them.
bib-john-004-p02.core_idea: The good shepherd gives his life for the sheep

bib-john-005-p01.plain: Jesus tells her he is the resurrection and the life: whoever believes in him will live even after dying, and whoever lives and believes in him will never die. He asks if she believes this.
bib-john-005-p01.core_idea: Jesus is the resurrection and the life

bib-john-005-p02.plain: Mary fell at Jesus's feet weeping: if he had been there, her brother would not have died. Seeing her and the others weeping, Jesus was deeply moved and troubled, asked where they had laid him, and wept.
bib-john-005-p02.core_idea: Jesus wept with those who grieved

bib-john-005-p03.plain: Jesus says: unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it stays a single seed. But if it dies, it produces a great harvest.
bib-john-005-p03.core_idea: A seed must die to bear much fruit

bib-john-005-p04.plain: Jesus says his soul is troubled, and asks whether he should pray to be saved from this hour. But this hour is the very reason he came.
bib-john-005-p04.core_idea: Troubled, yet facing the hour he came for

bib-john-005-p05.plain: Jesus says that since he, their Lord and teacher, washed their feet, they should wash each other's feet, following his example. A servant is not above his master, and they are blessed if they act on this.
bib-john-005-p05.core_idea: Serve one another as Jesus served

bib-john-006-p01.plain: Jesus gives a new commandment: love one another as he has loved you. Everyone will know you are his disciples by your love for each other.
bib-john-006-p01.core_idea: Love one another as Jesus loved you

bib-john-006-p02.plain: Jesus says not to let your hearts be troubled, but to trust in God and in him. His Father's house has many rooms; he goes to prepare a place for you and will come back for you.
bib-john-006-p02.core_idea: Don't be troubled; a place is prepared for you

bib-john-006-p03.plain: Jesus says: I leave you peace, my own peace, not the kind the world gives. Don't let your hearts be troubled or afraid.
bib-john-006-p03.core_idea: Jesus gives a peace unlike the world's

bib-john-006-p04.plain: Jesus commands: love one another as I have loved you. There is no greater love than to give your life for your friends.
bib-john-006-p04.core_idea: No greater love than dying for friends

bib-john-006-p05.plain: Jesus says you will weep and grieve while the world rejoices, but your sorrow will turn to joy, like a mother who forgets her labour pains once her child is born. No one will take that joy away.
bib-john-006-p05.core_idea: Your sorrow will be turned into joy

judge.issue: Drops "I will see you again", the stated source of the coming joy.

bib-john-006-p06.plain: Jesus says they will scatter and leave him, yet he is not alone, because the Father is with him. In the world you will have trouble, but take heart: he has overcome the world.
bib-john-006-p06.core_idea: Take heart: Jesus has overcome the world

judge.issue: Drops "that in me you may have peace".

bib-john-007-p01.plain: From the cross, Jesus saw his mother beside the disciple he loved and told each of them to treat the other as mother and son. From then on, that disciple took her into his home.
bib-john-007-p01.core_idea: From the cross, Jesus gives his mother a son

bib-john-008-p01.plain: Jesus tells Thomas: you believe because you have seen me. Blessed are those who believe without having seen.
bib-john-008-p01.core_idea: Blessed are those who believe without seeing

bib-john-008-p02.plain: Jesus tells Peter: when you were young you dressed yourself and went where you liked. When you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and take you where you don't want to go.
bib-john-008-p02.core_idea: In old age others will lead you

bib-jonah-001-p01.plain: Jonah prays that the waters closed over him and he sank to the roots of the mountains, shut in forever, yet God brought his life up from the pit. When he was fainting, he remembered the Lord.
bib-jonah-001-p01.core_idea: From the depths, God brought my life up

bib-jonah-001-p02.plain: God asked Jonah, "Is it right for you to be angry?"

bib-joshua-001-p01.plain: God says: be strong and brave, as I have commanded you, and don't be afraid or discouraged. The Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
bib-joshua-001-p01.core_idea: Be strong and brave; God goes with you

bib-joshua-006-p01.plain: Not one of the good things God had promised Israel failed; every one came true.
bib-joshua-006-p01.core_idea: Every good promise God made came true

bib-joshua-007-p01.plain: Joshua says he is about to die. They know in their hearts that not one of the good things God promised them has failed; every one has come true.
bib-joshua-007-p01.core_idea: Not one of God's good promises has failed

bib-joshua-007-p02.plain: If you don't want to serve the Lord, choose today whom you will serve, your ancestors' gods or the gods of this land. But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.
bib-joshua-007-p02.core_idea: Choose today whom you will serve

bib-jude-001-p01.plain: But you, dear friends, keep building yourselves up in your holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit. Keep yourselves in God's love as you wait for the mercy of Jesus Christ that brings eternal life.
bib-jude-001-p01.core_idea: Build up your faith and stay in God's love

bib-judges-002-p01.plain: Deborah sings to herself: march on, my soul, and be strong.
bib-judges-002-p01.core_idea: March on, my soul, with strength

bib-judges-003-p01.plain: The trees wanted a king, but the olive, fig and vine each refused to give up their good gifts to rule. Only the bramble accepted, offering shade but threatening fire if refused.
bib-judges-003-p01.core_idea: The worthy decline power; the worthless seize it

bib-judges-006-p01.plain: Delilah asks Samson how he can say he loves her when his heart is not with her.
bib-judges-006-p01.core_idea: Love means the heart is truly with you

bib-judith-003-p01.plain: Judith prays to God: you help the oppressed, support the weak, protect the abandoned, and save those who have no hope.
bib-judith-003-p01.core_idea: God helps the oppressed and the hopeless

bib-lamentations-001-p01.plain: The once-crowded city sits alone like a widow, a princess turned slave, weeping all night with no one to comfort her. Her friends have betrayed her and become her enemies.
bib-lamentations-001-p01.core_idea: Desolate, betrayed and with no one to comfort

bib-lamentations-001-p02.plain: Does it mean nothing to you, all who pass by? Look and see if there is any sorrow like mine, which the Lord brought on me in his fierce anger.
bib-lamentations-001-p02.core_idea: Is there any sorrow like my sorrow?

bib-lamentations-001-p03.plain: Look, Lord, I am in distress, and my heart churns within me because I rebelled badly. Outside the sword kills, and at home there is only death.
bib-lamentations-001-p03.core_idea: In distress, heart churning over my wrongs

bib-lamentations-001-p04.plain: Get up and cry out in the night, pouring out your heart like water before the Lord. Lift your hands to him for the lives of your children, fainting from hunger in every street.
bib-lamentations-001-p04.core_idea: Pour out your heart before the Lord

bib-lamentations-001-p05.plain: I had lost all peace, strength and hope, but I call this to mind and so I have hope. God's love keeps us from ruin; his mercies are new every morning, and great is his faithfulness.
bib-lamentations-001-p05.core_idea: His mercies are new every morning

judge.issue: Drops "Yahweh is my portion; I will hope in him" and the remembered bitterness.

bib-lamentations-001-p06.plain: The Lord is good to those who wait for him and seek him. It is good to hope and wait quietly for the Lord to save.
bib-lamentations-001-p06.core_idea: Wait quietly in hope for the Lord

bib-lamentations-001-p07.plain: The Lord will not reject anyone forever. Though he brings grief, he will show compassion out of his great love, for he does not willingly cause suffering or grief.
bib-lamentations-001-p07.core_idea: God does not reject forever; compassion follows grief

bib-lamentations-001-p08.plain: Let us examine our ways and return to the Lord. Let us lift our hearts and our hands to God in heaven.
bib-lamentations-001-p08.core_idea: Examine our ways and return to God

bib-lamentations-001-p09.plain: Waters closed over my head and I thought I was finished, so I called your name, Lord, from the deepest pit. You heard me, came near, and said, "Don't be afraid."
bib-lamentations-001-p09.core_idea: From the depths I called, and God said: don't fear

bib-lamentations-002-p01.plain: Our hearts have lost their joy, and our dancing has turned to mourning. The crown has fallen from our head; how terrible for us, for we have sinned.
bib-lamentations-002-p01.core_idea: Our dancing has turned to mourning

bib-lamentations-002-p02.plain: You, Lord, reign forever, so why have you forgotten us for so long? Bring us back to you and we will return; make our days new as they were before.
bib-lamentations-002-p02.core_idea: Bring us back, Lord, and renew our days

bib-luke-001-p01.plain: Mary praises the Lord and rejoices in God her Saviour, who has noticed his humble servant. Every generation will call her blessed, for the Mighty One has done great things for her, and his name is holy.
bib-luke-001-p01.core_idea: My soul praises God, who lifted the humble

bib-luke-002-p01.plain: The crowds asked John what they should do. He answered: whoever has two coats should give one to someone with none, and whoever has food should do the same.
bib-luke-002-p01.core_idea: If you have two, share with one who has none

bib-luke-002-p02.plain: Soldiers asked John what they should do. He told them not to extort money by force or make false accusations, and to be content with their pay.
bib-luke-002-p02.core_idea: Take nothing by force; be content with your pay

bib-luke-002-p03.plain: Jesus answered that it is written: people don't live on bread alone, but on every word of God.
bib-luke-002-p03.core_idea: We do not live by bread alone

bib-luke-002-p04.plain: Jesus reads: the Spirit of the Lord is on me, sending me to bring good news to the poor, heal the broken-hearted, free captives, give sight to the blind, release the oppressed, and announce the Lord's year of favour.
bib-luke-002-p04.core_idea: Good news for the poor and broken-hearted

bib-luke-002-p05.plain: Simon had fished all night and caught nothing, but when Jesus told him to let down his nets in deep water, he did it at his word. They caught so many fish that the nets began to break.
bib-luke-002-p05.core_idea: After a fruitless night, trust brings a full net

bib-luke-003-p01.plain: Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
bib-luke-003-p01.core_idea: Those who weep now will laugh

bib-luke-003-p02.plain: Jesus says to those listening: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
bib-luke-003-p02.core_idea: Love your enemies and bless those who curse you

bib-luke-003-p03.plain: Treat others exactly as you would want them to treat you. Loving only those who love you earns no credit, because even sinners do that.
bib-luke-003-p03.core_idea: Treat others as you want to be treated

bib-luke-003-p04.plain: Don't judge, and you won't be judged; don't condemn, and you won't be condemned. Set others free, and you will be set free.
bib-luke-003-p04.core_idea: Don't judge or condemn; set free and be freed

bib-luke-003-p05.plain: Why notice the speck in your brother's eye and ignore the plank in your own, offering to fix his while blind to yours? You hypocrite: first remove your own plank, then you will see clearly to help him.
bib-luke-003-p05.core_idea: Fix your own faults before judging others

bib-luke-003-p06.plain: A good person brings good out of the good stored in their heart, and an evil person brings evil out of the evil stored there. What fills the heart comes out of the mouth.
bib-luke-003-p06.core_idea: The mouth speaks what fills the heart

bib-luke-003-p07.plain: Whoever hears Jesus's words and acts on them is like a man who built his house on rock, which the flood could not shake. Whoever hears but doesn't act built without foundation, and his house fell in ruins.
bib-luke-003-p07.core_idea: Build your life on hearing and doing

bib-luke-005-p01.plain: No one who puts a hand to the plough and keeps looking back is fit for God's Kingdom.
bib-luke-005-p01.core_idea: Don't look back once you've committed

bib-luke-005-p02.plain: A man was robbed and left half dead, and a priest and a Levite saw him and passed by on the other side. But a Samaritan felt compassion, bandaged his wounds and took him to an inn.
bib-luke-005-p02.core_idea: The Samaritan who stopped and showed compassion

bib-luke-005-p03.plain: Martha, busy serving, complained that her sister Mary sat listening at Jesus's feet instead of helping. Jesus said Martha was anxious about many things when only one is needed, and Mary had chosen the good part.
bib-luke-005-p03.core_idea: Anxious about many things when one is needed

bib-luke-005-p04.plain: Jesus teaches them to pray: Father in heaven, may your name be holy, your Kingdom come, your will be done. Give us our daily bread, forgive our sins as we forgive others, and keep us from temptation and from evil.
bib-luke-005-p04.core_idea: The Lord's Prayer: how Jesus taught us to pray

bib-luke-005-p05.plain: Keep asking and you will receive, keep seeking and you will find, keep knocking and the door will open. Everyone who asks, seeks and knocks will receive, find and be let in.
bib-luke-005-p05.core_idea: Ask, seek, knock, and it will be given

bib-luke-006-p01.plain: God forgets not even one cheap sparrow, and every hair on your head is counted. So don't be afraid: you are worth more than many sparrows.
bib-luke-006-p01.core_idea: God counts every hair; don't be afraid

bib-luke-006-p02.plain: Jesus warns: watch out and guard against greed, because a person's life is not made up of how much they own.
bib-luke-006-p02.core_idea: Life is not measured by possessions

bib-luke-006-p03.plain: Life is more than food and clothes; God feeds the ravens, who neither sow nor store, and you are worth far more. Worry can't add an inch to your height, so why worry about the rest?
bib-luke-006-p03.core_idea: Worry adds nothing; God feeds the ravens

bib-luke-006-p04.plain: Sell what you own, give to the poor, and store up treasure in heaven that no thief or moth can reach. Where your treasure is, your heart will be too.
bib-luke-006-p04.core_idea: Where your treasure is, your heart is

bib-luke-006-p05.plain: Much will be required of whoever has been given much, and even more will be asked of whoever has been trusted with much.

bib-luke-006-p06.plain: A man wanted to cut down a fig tree that had borne no fruit for three years. His gardener asked for one more year to tend and fertilise it, and to cut it down only if it still bore nothing.
bib-luke-006-p06.core_idea: One more year of care before giving up

bib-luke-006-p07.plain: At a wedding feast, take the lowest seat rather than the best, so your host may move you up with honour instead of down in shame. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
bib-luke-006-p07.core_idea: Take the lowest seat; the humble will be raised

bib-luke-007-p01.plain: Who builds a tower without first sitting down to count the cost? Otherwise, having laid the foundation and been unable to finish, people will mock: this man began building but couldn't finish.
bib-luke-007-p01.core_idea: Count the cost before you begin

bib-luke-007-p02.plain: Anyone who lost one sheep of a hundred would leave the ninety-nine, search until it was found, and carry it home rejoicing. Heaven rejoices more over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine who need no repentance.
