bib-romans-002-p01.plain: We even rejoice in our sufferings, because suffering builds endurance, endurance builds character, and character builds hope. That hope won't let us down, because God has poured his love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit.
bib-romans-002-p01.core_idea: Suffering builds endurance, character and hope

bib-romans-002-p02.plain: I don't understand my own actions. I don't do what I want to do; instead I do the very thing I hate.
bib-romans-002-p02.core_idea: Doing what I hate instead of what I want

bib-romans-002-p03.plain: I believe the sufferings we face now are nothing compared with the glory that will be revealed to us.
bib-romans-002-p03.core_idea: Present suffering is small beside coming glory

bib-romans-002-p04.plain: Our salvation rests on hope, and hope is for what we cannot yet see. If we already saw it, we would not need to hope; since we don't, we wait for it patiently.
bib-romans-002-p04.core_idea: Hope is for the unseen, so we wait patiently

bib-romans-002-p05.plain: For those who love God and are called by his purpose, everything that happens works together for good.
bib-romans-002-p05.core_idea: For those who love God, all works for good

bib-romans-002-p06.plain: Paul is certain that nothing at all, not death or life, angels or powers, present or future, high or low, or anything created, can cut us off from God's love in Christ Jesus.
bib-romans-002-p06.core_idea: Nothing can separate us from God's love in Christ

bib-romans-003-p01.plain: Don't shape yourself to fit this world; let your mind be renewed and changed, so you can discover and live out God's good, pleasing and perfect will.
bib-romans-003-p01.core_idea: A renewed mind, not conformity, reveals God's will

bib-romans-003-p02.plain: Love sincerely, without pretence. Hate what is evil and hold tight to what is good.
bib-romans-003-p02.core_idea: Love sincerely, hate evil, hold to good

bib-romans-003-p03.plain: Bless people who mistreat you instead of cursing them. Share others' joy and grief, live in harmony, spend time with humble people rather than chasing status, and don't think yourself wise.
bib-romans-003-p03.core_idea: Bless enemies, share feelings, stay humble

bib-romans-003-p04.plain: Don't repay evil for evil; live at peace with everyone as far as you can. Don't take revenge, but leave room for God's wrath, for vengeance is his. Feed your hungry enemy and give him drink; that will heap burning coals on his head. Overcome evil with good.
bib-romans-003-p04.core_idea: Overcome evil with good, not revenge
bib-romans-003-p04.plain_v1: Don't pay back wrong with wrong or take revenge; leave that to God. Live at peace with everyone as far as you can, feed your hungry enemy, and defeat evil by doing good.

judge_v1.issue: Softens 'give place to God's wrath' and drops 'heap coals of fire on his head'.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops respecting the honourable and heaping coals of fire.

bib-romans-004-p01.plain: The only debt you should carry is the duty to love each other. All the commandments come down to loving your neighbour as yourself, because love never harms anyone, and so love fulfils the law.
bib-romans-004-p01.core_idea: Love of neighbour fulfils the whole law

bib-romans-004-p02.plain: The night is nearly over and day is coming, so let's drop the deeds of darkness and put on light like armour.
bib-romans-004-p02.core_idea: Day is near; leave darkness, wear light

bib-romans-004-p03.plain: None of us lives or dies only for ourselves. Whether we live or die, we do it for the Lord, and we belong to him.
bib-romans-004-p03.core_idea: In life and death we belong to the Lord

bib-romans-004-p04.plain: Those of us who are strong should carry the weaknesses of the weak rather than pleasing ourselves. Each of us should please our neighbour in ways that do them good and build them up.
bib-romans-004-p04.core_idea: The strong should carry the weak

bib-romans-004-p05.plain: A prayer that the God of hope will fill you with joy and peace as you trust him, so that the Holy Spirit's power makes your hope overflow.
bib-romans-004-p05.core_idea: May God fill you with joy, peace, hope

bib-ruth-001-p01.plain: Ruth begs Naomi not to send her away: wherever Naomi goes or lives, Ruth will too; Naomi's people and God will be hers, and only death will part them.
bib-ruth-001-p01.core_idea: Loyal love that refuses to leave

judge.issue: Drops dying and burial where Naomi dies, and the oath invoking God.

bib-ruth-001-p02.plain: Naomi tells the townspeople not to call her Naomi, meaning pleasant, but Mara, meaning bitter: she left full and God has brought her home empty and afflicted.
bib-ruth-001-p02.core_idea: Grief renames you: I left full, came back empty

judge.issue: Softens 'the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me'; drops 'testified against me'.

bib-sirach-001-p01.plain: Unjust anger can never be excused; it brings a man down. A patient man holds on for a while, and joy comes to him later; he keeps quiet for a time, and many will praise his wisdom.
bib-sirach-001-p01.core_idea: Patience outlasts anger and brings joy later

bib-sirach-001-p02.plain: If you set out to serve the Lord, expect to be tested. Hold steady, don't panic in disaster, stay close to him and accept hardship patiently; gold is proved in fire, people in humiliation. Trust him and hope in him.
bib-sirach-001-p02.core_idea: Serving God means enduring testing with trust

judge.issue: Drops 'order your ways aright' and the promise of increase at the end.

bib-sirach-001-p03.plain: Look back through history: who ever trusted the Lord and was let down, stayed faithful and was abandoned, or called on him and was ignored? The Lord is compassionate and merciful; he forgives and rescues in trouble.
bib-sirach-001-p03.core_idea: No one who trusted the Lord was abandoned

bib-sirach-001-p04.plain: Look after your father in his old age and don't cause him grief. Be patient if his mind fails, and don't look down on him while you are strong; caring for him will be remembered and will build you up.
bib-sirach-001-p04.core_idea: Care patiently for your ageing father

judge.issue: Drops that relieving a father counts 'instead of sins'.

bib-sirach-001-p05.plain: Do your work humbly and good people will love you. The greater you become, the more you should humble yourself, and you will find favour with the Lord.
bib-sirach-001-p05.core_idea: The greater you are, the humbler be

bib-sirach-001-p06.plain: Don't chase things too hard or beyond your strength. Think about what you have been told to do; you don't need hidden things. Don't fuss over unnecessary matters, since you've been shown more than people can grasp.
bib-sirach-001-p06.core_idea: Attend to what's given, not what's beyond you

bib-sirach-001-p07.plain: Don't take away a poor person's living or keep the needy waiting. Don't add sorrow to the hungry or trouble to someone already distressed; give promptly, and don't turn away from a poor person who asks.
bib-sirach-001-p07.core_idea: Don't turn away from the poor and needy

bib-sirach-001-p08.plain: Watch for the right moment and beware of evil, and don't be ashamed about your own soul. For there is a shame that leads to sin, and a shame that brings honour and grace.
bib-sirach-001-p08.core_idea: There is a bad shame and a good shame
bib-sirach-001-p08.plain_v1: Watch for the right moment, avoid evil, and don't be ashamed to stand up for yourself. Some shame leads to sin, and some shame is honourable and gracious.

judge_v1.issue: Recasts 'not ashamed concerning your soul' as standing up for yourself; shifted frame.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Adds 'stand up for yourself'; the passage says not to be ashamed concerning your soul.

bib-sirach-001-p09.plain: Be quick to listen and slow to answer. If you understand, reply; if not, keep your hand over your mouth. Talk brings honour or disgrace, and a person's tongue can be their downfall.
bib-sirach-001-p09.core_idea: Listen quickly, answer slowly; the tongue can ruin you

bib-sirach-001-p10.plain: Test a friend before trusting them. Some friends stay only while it suits them, some turn hostile and expose your quarrels, and some share your table and good times but turn against you when you fall.
bib-sirach-001-p10.core_idea: Test friends; many vanish when trouble comes

bib-sirach-001-p11.plain: A faithful friend is strong protection and a real treasure; nothing can be traded for one, and their worth is beyond price. A faithful friend is like life-giving medicine, and those who fear the Lord will find one.
bib-sirach-001-p11.core_idea: A faithful friend is a priceless treasure

bib-sirach-002-p01.plain: Seek instruction from youth onward, and you will still be finding wisdom when your hair is grey. Approach wisdom like a farmer who ploughs, sows and waits; the work is small and you will soon enjoy the harvest.
bib-sirach-002-p01.core_idea: Cultivate wisdom early like a patient farmer

bib-sirach-002-p02.plain: Don't mock someone when they are in bitter pain, because there is One who brings people low and lifts them up.
bib-sirach-002-p02.core_idea: Never mock someone in their bitterness

bib-sirach-002-p03.plain: Honour your father wholeheartedly and don't forget your mother's labour pains. Remember they gave you life: how could you ever repay what they have done for you?
bib-sirach-002-p03.core_idea: Honour parents; you can never repay them

bib-sirach-002-p04.plain: Don't fail those who weep; mourn with those who mourn. Be quick to visit the sick, for this wins love. In everything, remember your death, and you will never go wrong.
bib-sirach-002-p04.core_idea: Comfort mourners, visit the sick, remember death

bib-sirach-002-p05.plain: Don't shame someone who turns away from sin, since we all deserve punishment. Don't dishonour the old, since we are ageing too. Don't gloat over the dead; remember that we all die.
bib-sirach-002-p05.core_idea: Don't scorn others; we share their fate

bib-sirach-002-p06.plain: Don't abandon an old friend, because a new one doesn't compare. A new friend is like new wine: once it has aged, you will enjoy it.
bib-sirach-002-p06.core_idea: Old friends, like aged wine, are best

bib-sirach-002-p07.plain: Don't envy the success of a wrongdoer; you don't know how he will fall.

bib-sirach-002-p08.plain: Don't be angry with your neighbour over every wrong, and never act through violence.

bib-sirach-002-p09.plain: Respect yourself humbly and give yourself the honour you deserve. Who will defend someone who sins against their own soul, or honour someone who disrespects their own life?

bib-sirach-002-p10.plain: Don't praise someone for their looks or despise them for their appearance. The bee is small among flying creatures, yet what it makes is the sweetest of all.
bib-sirach-002-p10.core_idea: Don't judge by appearances; the small bee makes honey

bib-sirach-003-p01.plain: Many kings have ended up sitting on the ground, while someone no one noticed has worn a crown. Many powerful men have been disgraced, and famous ones handed over to others.
bib-sirach-003-p01.core_idea: Fortune topples the great and raises the unknown

bib-sirach-003-p02.plain: Don't blame before you've looked into it; understand first, then correct. Don't answer before you've listened, and don't interrupt someone mid-speech.
bib-sirach-003-p02.core_idea: Understand and listen before you judge or answer

bib-sirach-003-p03.plain: Don't busy yourself with too many things: meddling brings trouble, and chasing or fleeing gets you nowhere. Some people toil, labour and rush, and fall further behind for it.
bib-sirach-003-p03.core_idea: Too much busyness leaves you further behind

fix.display_text: My son, be not busy about many matters: For if you meddle much, you will not be unpunished; And if you pursue, you will not overtake; And you will not escape by fleeing. There is one that toileth, and labors, and makes haste, And is so much the more behind.

bib-sirach-003-p04.plain: Some grow rich by scrimping and caution, and say, now I can rest and enjoy my goods. But he doesn't know how long he has; he will die and leave it all to others.
bib-sirach-003-p04.core_idea: Hoarded wealth is left to others at death

bib-sirach-003-p05.plain: In good times we forget the bad, and in bad times the good. The Lord can easily repay someone at death; an hour of pain erases pleasure, and a person's end reveals their deeds.
bib-sirach-003-p05.core_idea: A person's end reveals the truth of their life

bib-sirach-003-p06.plain: You can't really test a friend when things are going well, and an enemy can't stay hidden when things go badly. When you prosper your enemies are upset; when you struggle even a friend will pull away.
bib-sirach-003-p06.core_idea: Hard times reveal true friends and enemies

bib-sirach-003-p07.plain: When a rich man stumbles, friends hold him up and excuse his words; when a poor man falls, they push him away and ignore his wisdom. People praise the rich and ask of the poor, who is this?
bib-sirach-003-p07.core_idea: The world props up the rich and shuns the poor

bib-sirach-003-p08.plain: Happy is the person who hasn't slipped up in speech and isn't stung by regret for sins. Happy is the one whose own soul doesn't condemn them and who hasn't lost hope.
bib-sirach-003-p08.core_idea: Blessed is a clear conscience that keeps hope

bib-sirach-003-p09.plain: Treat yourself well with what you have, and give to the Lord properly. Death won't wait, so be generous to your friend while you live, and don't let a good day pass you by.
bib-sirach-003-p09.core_idea: Death won't wait; enjoy and give now

judge.issue: Drops 'the covenant of the grave is not shown to you' and giving by ability.

bib-sirach-003-p10.plain: All living things wear out like clothing; the oldest rule is that we die. Like leaves on a tree, some fall and some grow, so generations end and others are born. Every work decays, and its maker departs with it.
bib-sirach-003-p10.core_idea: Generations fall and grow like leaves

bib-sirach-003-p11.plain: God made humans from the start and left them free to choose. You can keep the commandments if you want to; fire and water, life and death are set before you, and whichever you reach for will be yours.
bib-sirach-003-p11.core_idea: God gave us free choice between life and death

bib-sirach-004-p01.plain: Don't tell yourself you can hide from the Lord, that no one up there will remember you, that you'll be lost among so many people, or that your soul counts for nothing in a boundless creation.
bib-sirach-004-p01.core_idea: Don't think you're too small for God to notice

bib-sirach-004-p02.plain: When a person thinks they've finished, they are only beginning. What is a human, and what is their good or evil? A hundred years at most: a drop from the sea against eternity.
bib-sirach-004-p02.core_idea: A lifetime is a drop against eternity

judge.issue: Drops 'when he ceases, he will be in perplexity' and the pebble image.

bib-sirach-004-p03.plain: A person's mercy reaches their neighbour, but the Lord's mercy reaches every living being; he corrects, disciplines and teaches, and brings people back like a shepherd with his flock.

bib-sirach-004-p04.plain: Don't spoil your good deeds or hurt people with words when you give. As dew cools scorching heat, a kind word is worth more than a gift, and a gracious person offers both.
bib-sirach-004-p04.core_idea: A kind word is better than a gift

bib-sirach-004-p05.plain: When you have plenty, remember hunger; when you are wealthy, remember poverty and need. Things change between morning and evening, and everything passes quickly before the Lord.
bib-sirach-004-p05.core_idea: In plenty, remember want; things change fast

bib-sirach-004-p06.plain: Have you heard something said? Let it die with you. Take heart: keeping it won't make you burst.
bib-sirach-004-p06.core_idea: Keep what you hear to yourself

bib-sirach-004-p07.plain: If you hear something against a friend, ask them: perhaps they didn't do or say it, and if they did, they may stop. Slander is common, so don't believe every word; who has never slipped with their tongue?
bib-sirach-004-p07.core_idea: Ask a friend before believing what you hear

judge.issue: 'Reprove' softened to 'ask'; adds a hearsay framing not in the passage.

bib-sirach-004-p08.plain: Some keep silent and are thought wise; others are disliked for talking too much. Some are silent for lack of an answer, others because they know their moment. The wise wait; the boaster and fool don't.
bib-sirach-004-p08.core_idea: The wise keep silent until the right time

bib-sirach-004-p09.plain: Some people find good fortune in misfortune, and some gains turn into losses. Some gifts bring no benefit, others pay back double. Some are brought low by glory, and some rise from a low place.

bib-sirach-004-p10.plain: Have you sinned? Don't add more to it, and pray to be forgiven for what you've already done.
bib-sirach-004-p10.core_idea: After sinning, stop and seek forgiveness

bib-sirach-005-p01.plain: When a thoughtful person hears a wise saying, they praise it and build on it. When a careless person hears it, they dislike it and toss it behind their back.
bib-sirach-005-p01.core_idea: The wise welcome wisdom; the careless discard it

bib-sirach-005-p02.plain: Fools have their heart in their mouth, but the wise keep their mouth in their heart.
bib-sirach-005-p02.core_idea: Fools blurt; the wise speak from the heart

bib-sirach-005-p03.plain: Weep for the dead, who have lost the light, and weep for a fool, who has lost understanding. Weep more gently for the dead, because they are at rest; a fool's life is worse than death.
bib-sirach-005-p03.core_idea: A fool's life is worse than death

bib-sirach-005-p04.plain: Timber bound into a building won't shake loose, and a heart settled on sound advice won't be afraid. But stakes on a hilltop fall in the wind, and a fool's fearful heart gives way to any fear.
bib-sirach-005-p04.core_idea: A heart grounded in good counsel stands firm

bib-sirach-005-p05.plain: Taunting a friend ends a friendship. Even after a drawn sword or harsh words there can be reconciliation, but not after insult, arrogance, a betrayed secret or a treacherous blow; those drive any friend away.

bib-sirach-005-p06.plain: Earn your neighbour's trust while they are poor, so you can share their gladness when they prosper. Stand by them in hard times, so you can share in their good fortune.
bib-sirach-005-p06.core_idea: Stand by people in hard times

bib-sirach-005-p07.plain: The speaker wishes someone would guard his mouth and seal his lips with good sense, so that he doesn't slip and his own tongue doesn't destroy him.
bib-sirach-005-p07.core_idea: A prayer to guard one's tongue

bib-sirach-005-p08.plain: The speaker names three things that made her beautiful before God and people: relatives who get along, neighbours who are friends, and a wife and husband who live in harmony.
bib-sirach-005-p08.core_idea: Harmony in family, neighbours and marriage is beautiful

judge.issue: Assigns the speaker a female gender, which the passage does not state.

bib-sirach-006-p01.plain: If you gathered nothing when young, how will you have anything when old? Good judgement and counsel are beautiful in the grey-haired. Long experience is the crown of the old, and their pride is the fear of the Lord.
bib-sirach-006-p01.core_idea: Experience is the crown of old age

bib-sirach-006-p02.plain: Rich or poor, a good heart always brings a cheerful face.
bib-sirach-006-p02.core_idea: A good heart gives a cheerful face

bib-sirach-006-p03.plain: The speaker was afraid of three things, and prayed about a fourth: a whole city's slander, a mob gathering, and a false accusation. All of these are worse than death.
bib-sirach-006-p03.core_idea: Slander and false accusation are worse than death

bib-sirach-006-p04.plain: A kiln tests a potter's pots, and a person is tested by how they reason. As fruit shows how a tree was tended, words show the heart. Don't praise anyone before you hear them reason.
bib-sirach-006-p04.core_idea: Words reveal the heart; judge by reasoning

bib-sirach-006-p05.plain: Love a friend and keep faith. If you reveal their secrets, don't chase them; the friendship is gone like a bird let loose. A wound can heal and insults be forgiven, but betraying secrets leaves no hope.
bib-sirach-006-p05.core_idea: Betraying a secret destroys a friendship for good

bib-sirach-006-p06.plain: Forgive your neighbour and your sins will be forgiven when you pray. How can someone nurse anger yet ask the Lord for healing, or refuse mercy yet beg it? Remember death, drop hostility, overlook others' faults.
bib-sirach-006-p06.core_idea: Forgive others to be forgiven yourself

judge.issue: Drops remembering the commandments and covenant; 'ignorance' broadened to 'faults'.

bib-sirach-006-p07.plain: A quarrel started in haste lights a fire, and a hasty fight sheds blood. Blow on a spark and it burns; spit on it and it goes out, and both come from the same mouth.
bib-sirach-006-p07.core_idea: Your mouth can fan or quench a quarrel

bib-sirach-006-p08.plain: A whip leaves a mark on the skin, but a tongue's blow breaks bones. Many have died by the sword, but not as many as have fallen because of the tongue.
bib-sirach-006-p08.core_idea: The tongue wounds more than the sword

bib-sirach-006-p09.plain: What life really needs is water, bread, clothing and a roof. A poor man's life under a log shelter is better than lavish food in someone else's house. Whether you have little or much, be content.
bib-sirach-006-p09.core_idea: Be content with little or much

bib-sirach-007-p01.plain: A poor man who is healthy is better off than a rich man plagued by illness. Health is worth more than all gold; no wealth beats a healthy body, and no gladness beats joy of heart.
bib-sirach-007-p01.core_idea: Health is worth more than wealth

bib-sirach-007-p02.plain: Don't give yourself over to sorrow or torment yourself with your thoughts. Gladness of heart is life and lengthens your days. Comfort your heart and push sorrow away; envy, anger and worry age you early.
bib-sirach-007-p02.core_idea: Don't give yourself to sorrow; gladness is life

judge.issue: Drops 'love your own soul' and 'sorrow has destroyed many'.

bib-sirach-007-p03.plain: Lying awake over wealth wears down the body, and its worries drive away sleep. Anxious wakefulness longs for sleep, and serious illness breaks it.

bib-sirach-007-p04.plain: Wine drunk in moderation is as good as life; it was made to gladden people. Taken at the right time and amount it brings joy, but drunk heavily it brings bitterness and fighting.
bib-sirach-007-p04.core_idea: Wine in measure gladdens; in excess embitters

bib-sirach-007-p05.plain: Young man, speak if you are needed, but hardly at all unless asked twice. Keep it short, say much in few words, and be like someone who knows but holds their tongue.
bib-sirach-007-p05.core_idea: Speak little; say much in few words

bib-sirach-007-p06.plain: Do nothing without taking advice, and once you have acted, don't regret it.
bib-sirach-007-p06.core_idea: Seek advice first, then don't regret

bib-sirach-007-p07.plain: Empty and false hopes belong to a person without sense, and dreams lift fools off the ground. Fixing your mind on dreams is like grabbing at a shadow or chasing the wind.
bib-sirach-007-p07.core_idea: Chasing dreams is grasping at shadows

bib-sirach-007-p08.plain: A well-taught, experienced person understands much; the inexperienced know little, but travel builds skill. The speaker has seen much in his wanderings, understands more than he can say, and survived deadly dangers because of it.

bib-sirach-008-p01.plain: Everyone says they are your friend, but some friends are friends only in name. Isn't it a grief close to death when a companion and friend turns into an enemy?
bib-sirach-008-p01.core_idea: A friend turned enemy is a deathly grief

bib-sirach-008-p02.plain: Don't forget a friend in your heart, and don't neglect them when you become rich.
bib-sirach-008-p02.core_idea: Don't forget friends when you prosper

bib-sirach-008-p03.plain: Hold firm to what your own heart advises, because nothing is more faithful to you. A person's soul can sometimes tell them more than seven watchmen sitting high on a tower.
bib-sirach-008-p03.core_idea: Trust the counsel of your own heart

bib-sirach-008-p04.plain: Let reasoning begin every task, and let advice come before every action.
bib-sirach-008-p04.core_idea: Think and take advice before acting

bib-sirach-008-p05.plain: Test your soul throughout your life, notice what is bad for it, and don't give it that. Not everything is good for everyone, and not everyone enjoys the same things.
bib-sirach-008-p05.core_idea: Learn what harms you and avoid it

bib-sirach-008-p06.plain: Let your tears fall for the dead and lament deeply; prepare the body and don't neglect the burial. Mourn bitterly as the person deserves, for a day or two, and then be comforted in your sorrow.
bib-sirach-008-p06.core_idea: Mourn fully, then let yourself be comforted

judge.issue: Drops the stated motive for mourning: so you are not evil spoken of.

bib-sirach-008-p07.plain: Don't give your heart to sorrow; remember your own end. The dead won't return, and grief harms you without helping them. Their fate will be yours: yesterday me, today you. Let their memory rest, and be comforted.
bib-sirach-008-p07.core_idea: Don't drown in grief; the dead are at rest

fix.display_text: Give not your heart to sorrow: Put it away, remembering the last end: Forget it not, for there is no returning again: Him you shall not profit, and you will hurt yourself. Remember the sentence upon him; for so also shall yours be; Yesterday for me, and today for you. When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest; And be comforted for him, when his spirit departs from him.

bib-sirach-009-p01.plain: People live with anger, jealousy, trouble, fear of death and strife. Even in bed their rest is short; in sleep they are troubled as if fleeing a battle, then wake amazed the fear was nothing.
bib-sirach-009-p01.core_idea: Anxiety haunts even our sleep, then proves empty

bib-sirach-009-p02.plain: The life of someone who works and is content will be sweet, but finding a treasure is better than both.

fix.display_text: The life of one that labors, and is contented, shall be made sweet; And he that finds a treasure is above both.

bib-sirach-009-p03.plain: Wine and music gladden the heart, but the love of wisdom is better than both.
bib-sirach-009-p03.core_idea: Love of wisdom beats wine and music

bib-sirach-009-p04.plain: Don't fear the sentence of death; it is the Lord's decree for everyone before and after you, so why resist it? Whether you live ten, a hundred or a thousand years, the grave doesn't ask.
bib-sirach-009-p04.core_idea: Death comes to all; don't fear it

judge.issue: Folds 'good pleasure of the Most High' into decree; 'grave doesn't ask' loosens the meaning.

bib-sirach-009-p05.plain: Take care of your reputation; it stays with you longer than a thousand fortunes in gold. A good life lasts a limited number of days, but a good name lasts forever.
bib-sirach-009-p05.core_idea: A good name outlasts life and gold

bib-sirach-009-p06.plain: Keep what you have been taught, but hidden wisdom and buried treasure are of no use to anyone. Better someone who hides their foolishness than someone who hides their wisdom.
bib-sirach-009-p06.core_idea: Hidden wisdom is useless; share it

judge.issue: Drops 'in peace' from keeping instruction.

bib-sirach-010-p01.plain: A mist that comes quickly heals everything, and dew that falls after the heat brings cheer.
bib-sirach-010-p01.core_idea: Relief after heat brings healing and cheer

bib-sirach-010-p02.plain: We can say many things and still fall short; the sum of all our words is that he, God, is everything.
bib-sirach-010-p02.core_idea: Words fall short; God is all

bib-sirach-011-p01.plain: The speaker was near death, surrounded, with no one to help and no human aid coming. Then he remembered the Lord's mercy and his age-old works, how he rescues those who wait for him.
bib-sirach-011-p01.core_idea: With no help left, remember God's mercy

bib-sirach-011-p02.plain: While still young, the speaker openly sought wisdom in prayer before the temple and will seek her to the end. He delighted in her, followed her uprightly from youth, listened a little and learned much.
bib-sirach-011-p02.core_idea: Seek wisdom from youth to the end

bib-sirach-011-p03.plain: Do your work before the time comes, and in his own time God will reward you.
bib-sirach-011-p03.core_idea: Do your work; reward comes in God's time

bib-songofsolomon-001-p01.plain: The speaker begs the women of Jerusalem, by the deer of the field, not to stir up or awaken love until love itself is ready.
bib-songofsolomon-001-p01.core_idea: Don't awaken love before its time

bib-songofsolomon-001-p02.plain: Her beloved calls her to rise and come away with him: winter and rain are over, flowers are out, birds are singing, figs are ripening and the vines are in fragrant blossom.
bib-songofsolomon-001-p02.core_idea: Winter is past; love calls you to come away

bib-songofsolomon-001-p03.plain: At night in bed she looked for the one she loves and couldn't find him. She resolves to get up and search the city's streets and squares for him, but still she doesn't find him.
bib-songofsolomon-001-p03.core_idea: Searching for a loved one and not finding

bib-songofsolomon-001-p04.plain: I belong to the one I love, and the one I love belongs to me.
bib-songofsolomon-001-p04.core_idea: Lovers belong wholly to each other

bib-songofsolomon-001-p05.plain: Keep me as a seal on your heart and arm, for love is as strong as death, its passion a blazing flame of God. No flood can drown love, and anyone trying to buy it with wealth would be scorned.
bib-songofsolomon-001-p05.core_idea: Love is strong as death and can't be bought

judge.issue: Drops 'jealousy is as cruel as Sheol'.

bib-songofthethreeyoungmen-001-p01.plain: A prayer to God: we follow you wholeheartedly, revere you and seek your face. Don't let us be shamed, but treat us with your kindness and your great mercy.
bib-songofthethreeyoungmen-001-p01.core_idea: We follow you; deal with us in mercy

bib-songofthethreeyoungmen-001-p02.plain: Give thanks to the Lord, because he is good and his mercy lasts forever.
bib-songofthethreeyoungmen-001-p02.core_idea: Give thanks; God's mercy lasts forever

bib-titus-001-p01.plain: To people who are pure, everything is pure; but to those who are corrupted and don't believe, nothing is pure, because their very minds and consciences are corrupted.
bib-titus-001-p01.core_idea: To the pure, all things are pure

bib-tobit-001-p01.plain: Tobit tells his child not to look down on their mother but to honour and please her and not grieve her all her life, remembering the dangers she went through for them while pregnant.
bib-tobit-001-p01.core_idea: Honour your mother all her days

bib-tobit-001-p02.plain: Give to the poor from what you own, without begrudging it, and God won't turn from you. Give much if you have much, and a little without fear if you have little; giving protects from death and darkness.
bib-tobit-001-p02.core_idea: Give to the poor from whatever you have

judge.issue: Drops giving as treasure laid up against the day of necessity.

bib-tobit-001-p03.plain: Don't do to anyone what you yourself hate.
bib-tobit-001-p03.core_idea: Don't do to others what you hate

bib-tobit-001-p04.plain: Ask advice from every wise person, and don't scorn any useful counsel.

bib-tobit-001-p05.plain: Tobit tells his child not to fear because they have become poor: you have great wealth if you revere God, turn away from all sin and do what pleases him.
bib-tobit-001-p05.core_idea: Fearing God is true wealth, even in poverty

bib-tobit-002-p01.plain: Don't be greedy to pile up money; let it be rubbish compared to our child. What the Lord has given us to live on is enough.
bib-tobit-002-p01.core_idea: What God gives is enough; people matter more

bib-tobit-003-p01.plain: Do good and evil won't find you. Prayer with fasting, giving and righteousness are good. A little gained honestly is better than much gained wrongly, and giving to the poor is better than hoarding gold.
bib-tobit-003-p01.core_idea: A little with goodness beats much without

bib-wisdomofsolomon-001-p01.plain: Beware of pointless grumbling and keep your tongue from backbiting, because no secret word goes without effect, and a lying mouth destroys the soul.
bib-wisdomofsolomon-001-p01.core_idea: Grumbling and lies harm your own soul

bib-wisdomofsolomon-001-p02.plain: The souls of the righteous are in God's hand and no torment will touch them. To foolish eyes they seemed to die, and their leaving looked like disaster and ruin, but they are at peace.
bib-wisdomofsolomon-001-p02.core_idea: The righteous dead are at peace in God's hand

bib-wisdomofsolomon-001-p03.plain: A righteous person who dies young will be at rest. Honourable old age isn't measured by length of time or number of years; understanding is a person's grey hair, and a blameless life is ripe old age.
bib-wisdomofsolomon-001-p03.core_idea: A good life, not long years, is true old age

bib-wisdomofsolomon-002-p01.plain: Wisdom is radiant and never fades; those who love and seek her find her easily, as she shows herself first. Whoever rises early finds her at the door; thinking of her frees you from worry.
bib-wisdomofsolomon-002-p01.core_idea: Wisdom is easily found by those who seek her

judge.issue: Drops 'thinking on her is perfect understanding'; merges it with being free from care.

bib-wisdomofsolomon-002-p02.plain: The king says he is mortal like everyone: formed in a womb, born breathing the same air, giving the same first cry, nursed with care. No king begins differently; all enter and leave life alike.
bib-wisdomofsolomon-002-p02.core_idea: Kings and all people share one birth and death

bib-wisdomofsolomon-002-p03.plain: Who can know God's plan or will? Human thoughts are timid and our plans fail; the body weighs down the soul and the worried mind. We barely grasp earthly things, so who has traced heavenly ones?
bib-wisdomofsolomon-002-p03.core_idea: Human minds can't fathom God's plan

bib-wisdomofsolomon-003-p01.plain: A prayer to God: you love everything that exists and hate nothing you made, or you wouldn't have made it. You spare all things because they are yours, Lord who loves life; your spirit is in everything.
bib-wisdomofsolomon-003-p01.core_idea: God loves everything he made; his spirit is in all

fix.display_text: For you love all things that are, And abhor none of the things which you did make; For never would you have formed anything if you did hate it. And how would anything have endured, except you had willed it? Or that which was not called by you, how would it have been preserved? But you spare all things, because they are yours, O Sovereign Lord, you lover of men’s lives; For your incorruptible spirit is in all things.

bib-wisdomofsolomon-004-p01.plain: Wickedness, condemned by its own conscience, is cowardly and always expects the worst. Fear is simply giving up the help reason offers, and the less help we expect within, the more frightening the unknown becomes.
bib-wisdomofsolomon-004-p01.core_idea: Fear is abandoning the help of reason

bib-zechariah-001-p01.plain: God's message to Zerubbabel: it will be done not by strength or power, but by my Spirit, says the Lord of Armies.
bib-zechariah-001-p01.core_idea: Not by might or power, but by God's Spirit

bib-zechariah-001-p02.plain: Who would look down on a day of small beginnings?

bib-zechariah-001-p03.plain: Judge fairly and show kindness and compassion to one another. Don't oppress widows, orphans, foreigners or the poor, and don't secretly plot harm against each other.
bib-zechariah-001-p03.core_idea: Be just and kind; don't oppress the vulnerable

fix.display_text: Execute true judgment, and show kindness and compassion every man to his brother. Don’t oppress the widow, nor the fatherless, the foreigner, nor the poor; and let none of you devise evil against his brother in your heart.
fix.reason: Unmatched closing quotation mark at end

bib-zechariah-002-p01.plain: God says: this is what you must do. Tell each other the truth, judge truly and make peace in your courts, don't plot harm against your neighbour, and don't love false oaths, for I hate all these things.
bib-zechariah-002-p01.core_idea: Speak truth, judge fairly, plot no harm

fix.display_text: These are the things that you shall do: speak every man the truth with his neighbor. Execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates, and let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his neighbor, and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, says Yahweh.

bib-zechariah-002-p02.plain: Come back to the stronghold, you prisoners of hope! God declares that even today he will give you back double.
bib-zechariah-002-p02.core_idea: Prisoners of hope will be restored double

bib-zephaniah-001-p01.plain: The Lord your God is with you, a mighty saviour. He delights in you with joy, quiets you with his love, and rejoices over you with singing.
bib-zephaniah-001-p01.core_idea: God rejoices over you with singing

chuang-tzu-giles-001-p01.plain: A small bird nesting in a huge forest uses only one twig, and a tapir drinking from a river takes only enough to fill its belly.

chuang-tzu-giles-001-p02.plain: If you have a big tree and don't know its use, plant it in the realm of nothingness and rest idly in its shade. No axe will touch it, because being useless to others keeps it safe from harm.
chuang-tzu-giles-001-p02.core_idea: Being useless to others can keep you safe

chuang-tzu-giles-001-p03.plain: Joy, anger, sorrow, happiness, caution and regret take turns in us, rising like music from hollows or mushrooms from damp. Day and night they change, and we can't tell where they come from, let alone their cause.
chuang-tzu-giles-001-p03.core_idea: Moods rise in us from unknown sources

chuang-tzu-giles-002-p01.plain: Isn't it pitiful to be worn down by life and rush through it unable to stop? Isn't it a real grief to toil endlessly, never enjoy the results, and then leave, exhausted, for who knows where?
chuang-tzu-giles-002-p01.core_idea: Endless toil without enjoying life is pitiful

chuang-tzu-giles-002-p02.plain: The perfect Tao doesn't announce itself. Perfect argument isn't put into words, perfect kindness doesn't show itself in deeds, perfect honesty isn't rigidly incorruptible, and perfect courage isn't rigidly unyielding.
chuang-tzu-giles-002-p02.core_idea: The highest things don't show themselves

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p01.plain: You're going too fast: you see an egg and expect to hear it crow, you look at your crossbow and expect roast duck already in front of you.
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p01.core_idea: Don't expect results before they can come

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p02.plain: How can I know that loving life isn't a delusion? How can I know that someone who dreads death isn't like a lost child who can't find the way home?
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p02.core_idea: Fearing death may be like a lost child

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p03.plain: Those who dream of feasts wake to grief; those who dream of grief wake to go hunting. While dreaming, they don't know it's a dream; only waking shows it. A Great Awakening will reveal this life as a great dream.
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p03.core_idea: Life itself may be a great dream

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p04.plain: Suppose you and I argue. If you win, are you necessarily right and I wrong, or the other way round? Or are we each partly right and partly wrong, or both entirely right or entirely wrong?
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p04.core_idea: Winning an argument doesn't prove you right

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p05.plain: Chuang Tzu dreamed he was a butterfly, fluttering about, unaware of being a man. He woke as himself, and now can't tell if he was a man dreaming he was a butterfly, or is a butterfly dreaming he's a man.
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p05.core_idea: Am I a man or a dreaming butterfly?

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p06.plain: My life is limited, but knowledge has no limit. Using what is limited to chase what is limitless is ruinous, and those who try it lose themselves.
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p06.core_idea: Chasing limitless knowledge with a limited life ruins you

judge.issue: Softens 'fatal' to 'ruinous'; 'knowledge fatally lost' becomes 'lose themselves'.

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p07.plain: When you work for others, don't chase fame; when you work for yourself, avoid shame. Keep to the middle way, and you will stay healthy in body and mind, do your duties, and live out your natural life.
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p07.core_idea: Keep to the middle way, avoiding fame and disgrace

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p08.plain: A good cook replaces his knife yearly because he slices; an ordinary cook monthly because he hacks. This cook has used one knife for nineteen years on thousands of oxen, and it is still as sharp as new.
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p08.core_idea: Skill that works with things wears nothing out

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p09.plain: Wild birds have to search hard for every bite and every drink, yet they don't want to be fed in a cage. In a cage they would have food on demand, but they would not be free.
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p09.core_idea: Freedom is worth more than easy comfort

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p10.plain: The Master was born when his time came and died when his time came. Accept birth and death like that, and grief has no place. The fuel burns out, but the fire may pass on endlessly.
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p10.core_idea: Accepting birth and death in their time ends grief

judge.issue: 'Pass on endlessly' overstates 'we know not that it comes to an end'.

chuang-tzu-giles-003-p11.plain: The wise people of old first found the Tao for themselves and only then shared it with others. Until you have it yourself, you have no time to spare for dealing with what wicked people do.
chuang-tzu-giles-003-p11.core_idea: Find the Tao yourself before trying to fix others

chuang-tzu-giles-004-p01.plain: Listen not with your ears or mind but with your soul. Let hearing and thinking stop, so the soul is empty and simply responds. Only the Tao lives in that emptiness; this is fasting of the heart.
chuang-tzu-giles-004-p01.core_idea: An empty, receptive heart is where the Tao lives

chuang-tzu-giles-004-p02.plain: The highest virtue is to tend your own heart so that neither joy nor sorrow takes hold of it, and to learn to accept what cannot be avoided.
chuang-tzu-giles-004-p02.core_idea: Highest virtue is calm acceptance of the inevitable

chuang-tzu-giles-004-p03.plain: An official often faces situations he cannot control. But if he simply sticks to his work and forgets himself completely, he has no time left to cling to life or dread death.
chuang-tzu-giles-004-p03.core_idea: Absorption in your work frees you from fear of death

chuang-tzu-giles-004-p04.plain: Contests start friendly and end hostile; parties start orderly and end in drunken chaos, because things are pushed too far. Everything is like this: it begins in good faith and ends in contempt. Small beginnings lead to big endings.
chuang-tzu-giles-004-p04.core_idea: Things pushed too far turn from good faith to contempt

chuang-tzu-giles-004-p05.plain: Words stir people up as wind stirs waves, and actions easily drift from their aim. So anger flares for no clear reason, and dishonest arguments follow. When you push someone too far into a corner, they will always fight back.
chuang-tzu-giles-004-p05.core_idea: Push someone into a corner and they will resist

judge.issue: Drops that both sides give way to passion; loses the dying-animal image.

chuang-tzu-giles-004-p06.plain: The praying mantis raised its arms to stop a chariot, not knowing it was far too weak, so proud was it of its energy. Be careful: if you keep offending people by acting superior, you will probably come to harm.
chuang-tzu-giles-004-p06.core_idea: Showing off your superiority leads to harm

chuang-tzu-giles-004-p07.plain: People who love horses pamper them. But when a groom suddenly swats a fly off a horse, the startled animal breaks its bridle and hurts itself. The intention is good, but real care for the horse is missing.
chuang-tzu-giles-004-p07.core_idea: Good intentions are not the same as real care

chuang-tzu-giles-004-p08.plain: Trees of every size are cut down for useful things: monkey cages, house beams, rich men's coffins. So they never live out their years. Being valuable brings this misfortune.
chuang-tzu-giles-004-p08.core_idea: Being useful can cut your life short

chuang-tzu-giles-005-p01.plain: The honours of this world weigh as little as feathers, yet nobody sees how little they are worth. The troubles of life weigh as much as the earth, yet nobody can escape them.
chuang-tzu-giles-005-p01.core_idea: Honours are light; misfortunes are heavy and unavoidable

chuang-tzu-giles-005-p02.plain: Many people with toes laughed at me for having none, and it used to make me angry. Since studying with our Master I no longer care; I have been with him nineteen years without even noticing the missing toes.
chuang-tzu-giles-005-p02.core_idea: Inner growth makes others' mockery stop mattering

judge.issue: Drops his suggestion that the Master has purified him.

chuang-tzu-giles-006-p01.plain: Whoever knows what God is and what Man is has arrived: he knows he came from God, rests in what is known, and waits for the unknown. Living out your full span is the fullness of knowledge.
chuang-tzu-giles-006-p01.core_idea: Knowing God and Man, rest and live your span

chuang-tzu-giles-006-p02.plain: The pure people of old acted without scheming and didn't chase results. They made no plans, so when they failed they had nothing to regret, and when they succeeded nothing to boast about.
chuang-tzu-giles-006-p02.core_idea: Acting without scheming leaves no regret or pride

chuang-tzu-giles-006-p03.plain: The pure people of old slept without dreams and woke without worry. They ate whatever came and breathed deeply, for the pure breathe from their very depths, while common people breathe only from their throats.
chuang-tzu-giles-006-p03.core_idea: The pure live calmly and breathe from deep within

chuang-tzu-giles-006-p04.plain: The pure people of old neither loved life nor hated death; they came and went. Not forgetting their origin, nor rushing back to it, they cheerfully played their parts and waited patiently for the end.
chuang-tzu-giles-006-p04.core_idea: Live your part cheerfully, neither clinging nor rushing

chuang-tzu-giles-006-p05.plain: Wetting stranded fish with breath or spit is nothing compared with leaving them in their rivers to begin with. Likewise, better than praising good rulers and blaming bad ones is to leave both and develop the Tao.
chuang-tzu-giles-006-p05.core_idea: Better to live naturally in the Tao than be rescued

extension.text: When the pond dries up, and the fishes are left upon dry ground, to moisten them with the breath or to damp them with spittle is not to be compared with leaving them in the first instance in their native rivers and lakes. And better than praising Yao and blaming Chieh would be leaving them both and attending to the development of TAO.

chuang-tzu-giles-006-p06.plain: The Tao gives me my body, my work as an adult, my rest in old age, and my rest in death. Whatever arranges my life so kindly is also the best judge of my death.
chuang-tzu-giles-006-p06.core_idea: Trust the Tao that shapes your life with your death

chuang-tzu-giles-006-p07.plain: Being born human is always a reason for joy. And then to go through countless changes, with only the infinite ahead of you, is a happiness beyond compare.
chuang-tzu-giles-006-p07.core_idea: Being human, and endlessly changing, is great joy

chuang-tzu-giles-007-p01.plain: Metal demanding to be made a famous sword would be rejected by the smith; so would I by God if I demanded to be a man again. The universe is the furnace, God the smith; I'll go wherever I'm sent.
chuang-tzu-giles-007-p01.core_idea: Accept whatever form God makes of you

judge.issue: Drops waking unconscious of the past, as from dreamless sleep, and \"a sinner like myself\".

chuang-tzu-giles-007-p02.plain: A lament sung over a dead friend: will you come back to us, Sang Hu? You have already returned to your God, while we remain here as men, alas.
chuang-tzu-giles-007-p02.core_idea: The dead friend has returned to God; we remain

chuang-tzu-giles-007-p03.plain: My parents wouldn't want me poor, and Heaven and Earth treat everyone equally, so why single me out? I searched for the cause and found none. So it must be Destiny that brought me here.
chuang-tzu-giles-007-p03.core_idea: Hardship no one chose must be Destiny

chuang-tzu-giles-008-p01.plain: The perfect person uses the mind like a mirror: it grabs at nothing and refuses nothing; it reflects but does not hold on. So he can deal with the world without being harmed by it.
chuang-tzu-giles-008-p01.core_idea: Use the mind like a mirror: reflect, don't hold

chuang-tzu-giles-008-p02.plain: Two rulers, treated kindly by their host Hun Tun, wanted to repay him. Seeing he had none of the seven openings people have for senses, they bored one hole a day; on the seventh day Hun Tun died.
chuang-tzu-giles-008-p02.core_idea: Forcing others into your mould can destroy them

chuang-tzu-giles-008-p03.plain: The one seeking perfection keeps to his own nature. A duck's short legs can't be stretched, nor a crane's long legs cut, without pain; so what is long or short in our moral nature shouldn't be altered.
chuang-tzu-giles-008-p03.core_idea: Don't force your nature to be other than it is

judge.issue: Drops the conclusion that all sorrow is thus avoided.

chuang-tzu-giles-008-p04.plain: True hearing is hearing yourself, not others; true seeing is seeing yourself, not others. Someone who watches others instead of himself takes hold of their lives rather than his own, and ends up becoming someone else instead of himself.
chuang-tzu-giles-008-p04.core_idea: Watch yourself, not others, to stay yourself

chuang-tzu-giles-009-p01.plain: Everyone strains to grasp what they don't know, but no one works on what they already know; and everyone runs down what they aren't good at, but no one questions what they are good at.
chuang-tzu-giles-009-p01.core_idea: People chase the unknown and dismiss what they lack

chuang-tzu-giles-009-p02.plain: Great joy pulls a person to one extreme, deep sorrow to the other, and when that balance is upset, nature and the body suffer. Swung between joy and sorrow, people lose their steadiness and fail in thought and action.
chuang-tzu-giles-009-p02.core_idea: Extremes of joy and sorrow throw you off balance

chuang-tzu-giles-010-p01.plain: Gentleness can soften the hardest heart, but try to cut and shape it and it blazes or freezes. In an instant it reaches the ends of the earth; nothing can lock or bind it. Such is the human heart.
chuang-tzu-giles-010-p01.core_idea: The human heart yields to gentleness, never to force

chuang-tzu-giles-010-p02.plain: See nothing and hear nothing; let your soul rest in quiet, and your body will take its proper shape. Keep total stillness and purity, don't tire your body or disturb your energy, and you will live for ever.
chuang-tzu-giles-010-p02.core_idea: Deep stillness and purity preserve body and soul

chuang-tzu-giles-010-p03.plain: Treasure what is inside you and shut out what is outside, because too much knowledge is a curse.
chuang-tzu-giles-010-p03.core_idea: Guard your inner life; much knowledge is a curse

chuang-tzu-giles-010-p04.plain: Rest in not-doing, and the world will become good by itself. Shed your old skin, spit out cleverness, ignore differences, become one with the infinite. Let your mind go, free your soul, be empty, be Nothing.
chuang-tzu-giles-010-p04.core_idea: Let go of doing and cleverness; become one with all

chuang-tzu-giles-010-p05.plain: People like those who resemble them and dislike those who don't. Befriending only your own kind comes from a wish to stand out from others. But driven that way, how can anyone actually stand out?
chuang-tzu-giles-010-p05.core_idea: Sticking to your own kind won't make you distinct

chuang-tzu-giles-011-p01.plain: Moving and resting, living and dying, rising and falling are not under a person's control. But working on yourself is in your own hands.
chuang-tzu-giles-011-p01.core_idea: Life's events aren't yours to control; self-cultivation is

chuang-tzu-giles-011-p02.plain: Don't you study to look like a sage, talk big to rise above others, and seek fame? Instead, forget yourself and drop the body's chains. If you can't govern yourself, how can you govern an empire?
chuang-tzu-giles-011-p02.core_idea: Govern yourself before presuming to govern others

judge.issue: Drops the promise \"and you will be near\".

chuang-tzu-giles-012-p01.plain: Call a man a flatterer and he's angry, yet he always is one. The world loves such pretence. To pose and agree with everyone to win favour, yet deny being a flatterer, is the height of folly.
chuang-tzu-giles-012-p01.core_idea: Pleasing the world while denying it is folly

judge.issue: Drops that people do not punish in others what they do themselves.

chuang-tzu-giles-012-p02.plain: A fool who knows he is a fool is not a great fool; someone who knows he is wrong is not badly wrong. Great error can never be shaken off, and a great fool never sees clearly.
chuang-tzu-giles-012-p02.core_idea: Knowing your folly means you're not a great fool

chuang-tzu-giles-012-p03.plain: If I know I can't succeed and still force it, that is just another mistake. So it is better to stop striving. But if I don't strive, who will?
chuang-tzu-giles-012-p03.core_idea: Forcing hopeless success is error, yet someone must try

chuang-tzu-giles-012-p04.plain: The sage's calm comes from his state of mind, which nothing can upset. Still water is a clear mirror; a still mind is clearer still. The sage's quiet mind becomes a mirror of the whole universe.
chuang-tzu-giles-012-p04.core_idea: A still mind mirrors the whole universe

chuang-tzu-giles-013-p01.plain: If people describe you truthfully and you reject it, you only double the blame. My humility is natural; it is not humility put on for its own sake.
chuang-tzu-giles-013-p01.core_idea: Accept true descriptions; real humility is natural

chuang-tzu-giles-013-p02.plain: You are too sure of yourself, too hasty, and you rate your own abilities too highly. People like that are not trusted.
chuang-tzu-giles-013-p02.core_idea: Overconfidence and haste make people distrust you

chuang-tzu-giles-013-p03.plain: Making a wheel, too slow and it's weak, too fast and the spokes won't fit; mind and hand must work as one. Words can't explain the knack, so I can't teach my son, and at seventy I'm still making wheels.
chuang-tzu-giles-013-p03.core_idea: Real skill cannot be put into words or taught

chuang-tzu-giles-014-p01.plain: A boat suits water and a cart suits land; push a boat on land and it won't move. Past and present are like water and land. Forcing old customs onto new times brings hard work, no result, and self-harm.
chuang-tzu-giles-014-p01.core_idea: Forcing old ways on new times only causes harm

chuang-tzu-giles-014-p02.plain: A great beauty frowned when she was upset. An ugly village woman, seeing how lovely she looked, copied the frown, and everyone fled from her. She saw that the frown was beautiful but not what made it beautiful.
chuang-tzu-giles-014-p02.core_idea: Copying the outward form misses its true source

chuang-tzu-giles-014-p03.plain: Those who live for wealth can't bear losing money; those who live for status can't bear losing fame; the power-hungry won't share authority. Anxious holding on, miserable losing, never learning from the past, such people are cursed by God.
chuang-tzu-giles-014-p03.core_idea: Living for wealth, fame or power brings endless anxiety

chuang-tzu-giles-014-p04.plain: The snow goose is white without washing, the raven black without dyeing; natural simplicity needs no argument, and fame isn't worth enlarging. Wetting stranded fish is nothing compared with leaving them in their rivers.
chuang-tzu-giles-014-p04.core_idea: Natural simplicity beats artificial effort and fame

chuang-tzu-giles-015-p01.plain: If the body works without rest, it dies. If the mind is used without a break, it gets tired, and once tired it loses its power.
chuang-tzu-giles-015-p01.core_idea: Body and mind both need rest to keep their power

chuang-tzu-giles-015-p02.plain: Getting what you want once meant complete happiness; now it means an office, which is outside you and comes and goes beyond your control. Don't treat office as fulfilment or fawn when poor; be equally happy always, and sorrow ends.
chuang-tzu-giles-015-p02.core_idea: Be equally content whatever position or poverty brings

chuang-tzu-giles-015-p03.plain: You can't talk about the ocean to a frog in a well, whose world is too small, or about ice to a summer insect, which lives one season. And you can't talk about the Tao to a narrow-minded schoolmaster.
chuang-tzu-giles-015-p03.core_idea: Narrow minds cannot grasp what lies beyond them

chuang-tzu-giles-015-p04.plain: Space and time are endless, and nothing is fixed. So the wise man is not elated by success or crushed by failure, does not grieve the far past, and neither celebrates life nor resents death.
chuang-tzu-giles-015-p04.core_idea: Seeing the endless whole frees you from elation and grief

judge.issue: Drops not regarding small as too little or great as too much, and the reasons given.

chuang-tzu-giles-016-p01.plain: What a person knows is nothing compared with what he doesn't, and his lifetime is nothing compared with the time he doesn't exist. When the small tries to take in the great, it only ends in confusion and failure.
chuang-tzu-giles-016-p01.core_idea: The small mind cannot exhaust the infinite

chuang-tzu-giles-016-p02.plain: The Tao has no beginning or end. Everything else is born, dies, and keeps changing for better or worse. The past can't return and time can't stop; every end is followed by a new beginning.
chuang-tzu-giles-016-p02.core_idea: Everything changes; every end begins something new

chuang-tzu-giles-016-p03.plain: Fishermen brave sea monsters, hunters brave tigers, and heroes face death in battle as calmly as life. But the sage's courage is knowing that failure is fate and success is opportunity, and staying fearless in great danger.
chuang-tzu-giles-016-p03.core_idea: True courage accepts fate and stays fearless

chuang-tzu-giles-017-p01.plain: Offered high office, Chuang Tzu asked whether a sacred tortoise would rather be dead and honoured in a temple or alive, wagging its tail in the mud. Alive, they said. Go, then: I'll wag my tail in the mud.
chuang-tzu-giles-017-p01.core_idea: Better a free, humble life than an honoured cage

chuang-tzu-giles-017-p02.plain: I don't know whether what the world calls happiness is real. Ordinary people's happiness seems to be blindly following the crowd as if they had no choice. Yet they all say they are happy.
chuang-tzu-giles-017-p02.core_idea: Following the crowd may not be real happiness

chuang-tzu-giles-017-p03.plain: After his wife died, Chuang Tzu sang and drummed on a bowl. He grieved at first, then remembered she had passed from formlessness to life to death like the seasons; wailing would show ignorance of nature's laws.
chuang-tzu-giles-017-p03.core_idea: Death is a natural change, like the seasons

chuang-tzu-giles-017-p04.plain: Life is a loan that only adds more dust to the world. Life and death are like day and night. Seeing death all around us, if it comes for me too, why should I hate it?
chuang-tzu-giles-017-p04.core_idea: Life and death are like day and night

chuang-tzu-giles-017-p05.plain: Those who understand life don't bother with what life cannot achieve. Those who understand destiny don't bother with what knowledge cannot control.
chuang-tzu-giles-017-p05.core_idea: Don't spend yourself on what you can't control

chuang-tzu-giles-018-p01.plain: Someone taking revenge doesn't break the weapon that did the killing, and even the most spiteful person doesn't hold a grudge against a tile that fell on his head.
chuang-tzu-giles-018-p01.core_idea: No one resents a thing that harms without intent

chuang-tzu-giles-018-p02.plain: A man betting for tokens plays well; bet his belt and he gets nervous; bet gold and he loses his head. His skill hasn't changed, but the stakes distract him. Anyone who values outside things becomes empty inside.
chuang-tzu-giles-018-p02.core_idea: Caring about external stakes ruins inner skill

chuang-tzu-giles-018-p03.plain: I go down with the whirlpool and come up with the current. I adapt myself to the water, not the water to me. That is how I can handle it.
chuang-tzu-giles-018-p03.core_idea: Adapt to the current instead of fighting it

chuang-tzu-giles-018-p04.plain: First I make my mind completely still. After three days I forget reward, after five fame, after seven my own body. Then, with no thought of the court, my skill is focused and all distraction is gone.
chuang-tzu-giles-018-p04.core_idea: Stilling the mind removes distraction and focuses skill

chuang-tzu-giles-019-p01.plain: Forgetting your feet means the shoes fit; forgetting right and wrong means the heart is at ease. No inner change and no yielding to outside pulls is ease in every situation, and true ease forgets it is easy.
chuang-tzu-giles-019-p01.core_idea: True ease is so complete you don't notice it

fix.display_text: To be unconscious of one's feet implies that the shoes are easy. To be unconscious of a waist implies that the girdle is easy. The intelligence being unconscious of positive and negative implies that the heart is at ease. No modifications within, no yielding to influences without,--this is ease under all conditions. And he who beginning with ease, is never not at ease, is unconscious of the ease of ease.

chuang-tzu-giles-019-p02.plain: Wherever there is union there is separation; completion, destruction; purity, oppression; honour, contempt; doing, undoing; openness, scheming; and wherever there is no pretence there is still deceit. So how can anything be fixed?
chuang-tzu-giles-019-p02.core_idea: Every condition carries its opposite; nothing is fixed

chuang-tzu-giles-019-p03.plain: The human part of us is what holds us back, and the human part of others is what causes us sorrow.
chuang-tzu-giles-019-p03.core_idea: Our humanness hinders us; others' humanness grieves us

chuang-tzu-giles-019-p04.plain: If an empty boat drifts into yours, even a hot-tempered man won't get angry; if someone is in it, he'll shout and curse. The difference is only the emptiness. If you drifted through life empty, who could hurt you?
chuang-tzu-giles-019-p04.core_idea: Be empty of self and no one can harm you

chuang-tzu-giles-019-p05.plain: Praising yourself proves nothing. Achievement brings decline, and fame brings loss. Who can let go of both achievement and fame and become one with everyone else?
chuang-tzu-giles-019-p05.core_idea: Let go of merit and fame; be one with all

chuang-tzu-giles-019-p06.plain: A good person's friendship is plain like water; a petty person's is rich like wine. The good one grows warmer; the petty one fades to nothing. Petty friendship starts for no real reason and ends the same way.
chuang-tzu-giles-019-p06.core_idea: Plain friendship deepens; showy friendship fades

chuang-tzu-giles-020-p01.plain: Chuang Tzu said he was poor, not miserable. Someone who has the Tao cannot be miserable; ragged clothes and worn-out boots are poverty, not misery.
chuang-tzu-giles-020-p01.core_idea: With the Tao, poverty is not misery

chuang-tzu-giles-020-p02.plain: Confucius said that hunger, thirst, cold and heat are only shackles on the road of life. They are part of the natural laws of the universe, and he follows his allotted course in obedience to them.
chuang-tzu-giles-020-p02.core_idea: Hardships are natural laws; follow your course

chuang-tzu-giles-020-p03.plain: Confucius said that the work of the world goes on and no one knows why. So how could anyone know its end or its beginning? All that is left to us is to wait.
chuang-tzu-giles-020-p03.core_idea: We cannot know the cause; we can only wait

chuang-tzu-giles-020-p04.plain: Chuang Tzu sighed at how creatures harm one another, and said that chasing gain leads to loss.

chuang-tzu-giles-020-p05.plain: Chuang Tzu said that while looking after his body, he lost sight of his real self; staring at muddy water, he lost sight of the clear depths.
chuang-tzu-giles-020-p05.core_idea: Caring for the body, he lost his true self

chuang-tzu-giles-020-p06.plain: An innkeeper loved his plain partner over his beautiful one: the beauty was so vain she seemed unattractive, the plain one so aware of it she didn't seem plain. Be good without being self-conscious, and you'll be loved everywhere.
chuang-tzu-giles-020-p06.core_idea: Be good without being conscious of it

chuang-tzu-giles-020-p07.plain: No sorrow compares with the death of the mind. The death of the body matters less.
chuang-tzu-giles-020-p07.core_idea: The mind's death is worse than the body's

chuang-tzu-giles-020-p08.plain: What you admire in me doesn't last. Still, why grieve? Though my old self is always passing away, something remains that does not pass away.
chuang-tzu-giles-020-p08.core_idea: Beneath the passing self, something endures

chuang-tzu-giles-020-p09.plain: Lao Tzu said that grazing animals don't mind new pasture and water creatures don't mind a new pond. Small changes are fine as long as the essential thing is left untouched.
chuang-tzu-giles-020-p09.core_idea: Small changes don't matter if the essence stays

chuang-tzu-giles-021-p01.plain: Asked how he stayed calm through being appointed and dismissed three times, Sun Shu Ao said office comes and can't be refused, goes and can't be kept. Gaining and losing it lie outside himself, so he feels no disappointment.
chuang-tzu-giles-021-p01.core_idea: Gain and loss of position lie outside yourself

judge.issue: Drops his insistence that he is no better than other people.

chuang-tzu-giles-021-p02.plain: Life follows death, and death begins life; who knows where the end is? Life is the gathering of the vital breath and death its scattering. If life and death simply follow each other, why should I complain?
chuang-tzu-giles-021-p02.core_idea: Life and death follow each other; why complain

chuang-tzu-giles-021-p03.plain: The universe is deeply beautiful yet says nothing. The seasons follow a fixed law yet make no sound. All creation rests on absolute principles, yet nothing speaks.
chuang-tzu-giles-021-p03.core_idea: The universe's beauty and order are silent

chuang-tzu-giles-021-p04.plain: Keep your body disciplined and your gaze fixed on the One, and the peace of God will come down on you. Hold back your knowledge and focus your thoughts on the One, and the holy spirit will live within you.
chuang-tzu-giles-021-p04.core_idea: Focus on the One and God's peace comes

chuang-tzu-giles-022-p01.plain: A human life passes like a white horse glimpsed through a crack: here, then gone. One change brings life, another death; creatures cry out and people grieve. Then the soul takes flight and the body follows on the journey home.
chuang-tzu-giles-022-p01.core_idea: Life flashes past; death is the journey home

chuang-tzu-giles-022-p02.plain: An eighty-year-old swordsmith never made a mistake. Asked whether it was skill or method, he said concentration: from age twenty he cared about nothing but swords, noticed nothing else, and put all his spare energy into that one craft.
chuang-tzu-giles-022-p02.core_idea: Mastery comes from total, lifelong concentration

chuang-tzu-giles-022-p03.plain: Let yourself change only on the outside. On the inside, stay constant and unchanged.

chuang-tzu-giles-022-p04.plain: Forests and fields fill me with joy, but sorrow soon returns, and I control neither. Life is a short stop at an inn. There is always more we can't know or do; struggling against that brings grief.
chuang-tzu-giles-022-p04.core_idea: Fighting life's limits only brings more grief

chuang-tzu-giles-023-p01.plain: Nan Yung said every choice harms either himself or others, and he sees no way out. Lao Tzu said: you are lost like a child without parents, trying to return to your natural self but unable to find the way.
chuang-tzu-giles-023-p01.core_idea: Lost in dilemmas, he can't find his natural self

judge.issue: Collapses the three specific dilemmas (knowledge, charity, duty) into a general statement.

chuang-tzu-giles-023-p02.plain: If the trouble comes from outside, don't keep fighting it; close the paths into your mind. If it comes from inside, don't struggle against it; shut out everything from outside.
chuang-tzu-giles-023-p02.core_idea: Don't fight disturbances; close the way in

chuang-tzu-giles-023-p03.plain: Lao Tzu said that preserving life means keeping all in the One, losing nothing, knowing when to stop and what is enough, minding your own affairs, being free of cares and cleverness: in fact, being like a child.
chuang-tzu-giles-023-p03.core_idea: To preserve life, be simple like a child

chuang-tzu-giles-023-p04.plain: People whose hearts are at rest give off a divine light, by which they see themselves as they really are. Only by cultivating that inner rest can anyone reach what is constant.
chuang-tzu-giles-023-p04.core_idea: A restful heart lets you see yourself truly

chuang-tzu-giles-023-p05.plain: Those devoted to inner life gain no reputation; those devoted to outward things compete for the top. Quiet practice makes even the humblest shine, while the status-seeker is like a peddler whose tiredness shows through his forced cheer.
chuang-tzu-giles-023-p05.core_idea: Quiet inner practice shines; chasing status shows strain

chuang-tzu-giles-023-p06.plain: No weapon is as deadly as human will, and no bandit as powerful as Nature, which nothing in the universe escapes. Yet it is not Nature that does the harm; it is a person's own heart.
chuang-tzu-giles-023-p06.core_idea: Harm comes from our own heart, not Nature

chuang-tzu-giles-023-p07.plain: Birth is not a beginning, and death is not an end. There is existence without limit and continuity without a starting point.
chuang-tzu-giles-023-p07.core_idea: Birth doesn't begin us; death doesn't end us

chuang-tzu-giles-024-p01.plain: If you want peace, calm your emotions. If you want spirituality, let your mind adapt. If you want to act rightly, go along with what is necessary, because necessity is the sage's Tao.
chuang-tzu-giles-024-p01.core_idea: Calm emotions, adapt, and accept necessity

chuang-tzu-giles-024-p02.plain: An exile is glad after days to meet anyone he knew from home, after a month anyone he'd seen there, after a year anyone resembling his countrymen. Being away from your own kind makes you long for them more.
chuang-tzu-giles-024-p02.core_idea: Absence from your own kind deepens the longing

chuang-tzu-giles-024-p03.plain: Being in a high position doesn't make you a great person, and being in a low one doesn't make you a lesser one.
chuang-tzu-giles-024-p03.core_idea: Rank does not make anyone high or low

chuang-tzu-giles-024-p04.plain: Schemers aren't happy without something to worry about, debaters without their arguments, critics without someone to attack. Such people are slaves to things outside themselves.
chuang-tzu-giles-024-p04.core_idea: Needing outside things to be happy is slavery

chuang-tzu-giles-024-p05.plain: Farmers, merchants, workers, the greedy, the boastful and the ambitious all depend on their activity; without it they are lost. People can never stop doing, and so they rush to ruin, scattering their life energy for good.
chuang-tzu-giles-024-p05.core_idea: Endless restless doing drains life away

chuang-tzu-giles-024-p06.plain: Anyone who wants to find a lost child but won't leave the house is likely to lose the child.
chuang-tzu-giles-024-p06.core_idea: You can't find what's lost without leaving home

chuang-tzu-giles-024-p07.plain: At his friend Hui Tzu's grave, Chuang Tzu told of a mason whose feat depended on a partner who never flinched; when the partner died, the feat ended. Since Hui Tzu died, Chuang Tzu has no one to talk with.
chuang-tzu-giles-024-p07.core_idea: Losing a true friend leaves no one to talk to

chuang-tzu-giles-025-p01.plain: Sharing your virtue with others is true wisdom; sharing your wealth is counted as merit. Showing off your superiority doesn't win people's hearts; showing yourself as lesser does.
chuang-tzu-giles-025-p01.core_idea: Humility, not displayed superiority, wins hearts

chuang-tzu-giles-025-p02.plain: On Monkey Mountain, one monkey showed off before a prince, even catching his arrow, and his guards shot it dead. The prince told his friend: it flaunted its skill in my face and died for it. Don't flaunt your superiority.

chuang-tzu-giles-025-p03.plain: A dog isn't good just because it barks well, nor a person good just because he talks well. Greatness needs even more than that; and if doing great things doesn't make you great, it certainly doesn't make you virtuous.
chuang-tzu-giles-025-p03.core_idea: Talking well or doing great things isn't virtue

chuang-tzu-giles-025-p04.plain: It is said that wind and sun make the river suffer. But though both act on it, the river is not really harmed: fed from its source, it keeps on flowing.
chuang-tzu-giles-025-p04.core_idea: Fed from its source, the river keeps flowing

chuang-tzu-giles-025-p05.plain: Your foot touches only a little ground, yet it is the untrodden ground around it that makes walking possible. Human knowledge is limited, but it is on what we don't know that we rely to reach an understanding of God.
chuang-tzu-giles-025-p05.core_idea: The unknown is what leads us toward God

chuang-tzu-giles-026-p01.plain: The old country and the old home delight a wanderer's eyes. Even if almost all of it has become a wilderness, his eyes are still glad to see it.
chuang-tzu-giles-026-p01.core_idea: Home gladdens the wanderer even in ruins

chuang-tzu-giles-026-p02.plain: The true sage pays no attention to God, to man, to beginnings or to matter. He moves in step with his times without suffering and takes things as they come without being overwhelmed. How can we become like him?
chuang-tzu-giles-026-p02.core_idea: The sage takes things as they come, untroubled

chuang-tzu-giles-026-p03.plain: The rulers of old gave their people credit for every success and took the blame for every failure. Whatever went right was the people's; whatever went wrong was theirs. So when anything fell short, they blamed themselves.
chuang-tzu-giles-026-p03.core_idea: Good leaders credit others and blame themselves

chuang-tzu-giles-026-p04.plain: At sixty, Chü Poh Yü changed his mind, calling wrong what he had called right. But who can say today's right won't turn out as wrong as the views of his previous fifty-nine years?
chuang-tzu-giles-026-p04.core_idea: Today's certainty may be tomorrow's mistake

chuang-tzu-giles-026-p05.plain: Seasons begin and end. Generations keep changing. Good and bad fortune take turns, bringing sorrow in one place and happiness in another.
chuang-tzu-giles-026-p05.core_idea: Fortune and seasons turn; nothing stays

chuang-tzu-giles-027-p01.plain: Someone who stubbornly sees things only from his own point of view may be right in one case and wrong in another.
chuang-tzu-giles-027-p01.core_idea: One fixed viewpoint is sometimes right, sometimes wrong

chuang-tzu-giles-027-p02.plain: Danger and safety take turns; good and bad fortune give rise to each other; gathering and scattering go together. You can see this happen. Movement runs forward and bends; exhaustion leads to renewal, and every end brings a new beginning.
chuang-tzu-giles-027-p02.core_idea: Opposites alternate; every end brings a beginning

chuang-tzu-giles-027-p03.plain: The cock crows and the dog barks; that much we know. But even the wisest person can't say why one crows and the other barks, or why they make any sound at all.
chuang-tzu-giles-027-p03.core_idea: We know what happens, not why

chuang-tzu-giles-027-p04.plain: Every parent wants devoted children, yet devotion to parents does not necessarily win their love.
chuang-tzu-giles-027-p04.core_idea: Filial devotion doesn't guarantee being loved

chuang-tzu-giles-027-p05.plain: As rubbed wood makes fire and clashing forces bring storms, the inner struggle between peace and unrest, good and evil, makes a fire that burns up a person's harmony. The mind can't withstand it, and with it the Tao ends.
chuang-tzu-giles-027-p05.core_idea: Inner conflict burns away harmony and the Tao

chuang-tzu-giles-027-p06.plain: Chuang Tzu, poor, asked a prince for grain and was promised silver later. He told of a stranded fish that begged for a pint of water, was promised a river later, and said: just put me in a dried-fish shop.
chuang-tzu-giles-027-p06.core_idea: Help promised later is no help to the desperate

chuang-tzu-giles-027-p07.plain: Lao Lai Tzu said: one generation's wounds are already too much, yet you would take on the sorrows of all time. Aren't you tired? Do you have the strength for that?
chuang-tzu-giles-027-p07.core_idea: Don't take on the sorrows of all time

chuang-tzu-giles-027-p08.plain: Even great wisdom faces countless traps; a fish safe from nets still has pelicans. Drop small cleverness and great wisdom will shine; put away goodness and you'll be naturally good. Children learn speech by living among speakers.
chuang-tzu-giles-027-p08.core_idea: Drop cleverness and effortful goodness; be natural

chuang-tzu-giles-028-p01.plain: Rest heals the sick, rubbing the eyelids smooths old wrinkles, and quiet clears away worry. But these remedies are only for those who need them; people free of these troubles pay them no attention.
chuang-tzu-giles-028-p01.core_idea: Remedies matter only to those who need them

chuang-tzu-giles-028-p02.plain: A trap is for the fish and a snare for the rabbit; once caught, the tool can be forgotten. Words are for ideas; once the idea arrives, the words can be forgotten. Where is someone beyond words to talk with?
chuang-tzu-giles-028-p02.core_idea: Words are tools; forget them once meaning arrives

chuang-tzu-giles-028-p03.plain: Tsêng Tzu held office twice and felt differently each time. While his parents were alive, he was happy on a small salary; later, with a large salary but his parents gone, he was sad.
chuang-tzu-giles-028-p03.core_idea: Loved ones matter more than money

chuang-tzu-giles-028-p04.plain: In life there are differences between people, but death makes us all equal.

chuang-tzu-giles-028-p05.plain: Lao Tzu said: you look arrogant; who would want to live with you? Someone truly pure behaves as if stained, and someone rich in virtue behaves as if he had too little.
chuang-tzu-giles-028-p05.core_idea: True virtue acts as if it lacks virtue

chuang-tzu-giles-028-p06.plain: Offered the empire, Shan Chüan said he is a small part of the universe: dressing for the seasons, farming, working dawn to dusk, resting after harvest, content and light-hearted. Why trouble with an empire? You don't know me.
chuang-tzu-giles-028-p06.core_idea: A contented simple life needs no empire

chuang-tzu-giles-028-p07.plain: A prince was wearing himself out fighting over land. His adviser showed him that he wouldn't trade a hand for the whole world, so his body matters far more than this land, yet he exhausts body and soul over it.
