chuang-tzu-giles-028-p07.core_idea: Don't wear out your life for lesser things

judge.issue: Compresses the chain of comparisons and drops the prince's fear and anxiety.

chuang-tzu-giles-029-p01.plain: The true sage weighs the reasons for all he does. Shooting at a bird with a priceless pearl makes the world laugh, because it gives up the greater for the lesser. Surely life is worth even more than that pearl.
chuang-tzu-giles-029-p01.core_idea: Life is worth more than any prize

chuang-tzu-giles-029-p02.plain: Lieh Tzu, poor and hungry, refused food sent by a minister, despite his wife's protest. The minister acted only on what others said about him, he explained; if others spoke ill of him, the minister would act on that too.
chuang-tzu-giles-029-p02.core_idea: Don't accept favours based only on others' opinions

chuang-tzu-giles-029-p03.plain: Yüan Hsien said that having no wealth is called being poor, while learning without being able to practise is called being sick. He is simply poor; there is nothing wrong with him.
chuang-tzu-giles-029-p03.core_idea: Poverty is not failure; unpractised learning is

chuang-tzu-giles-029-p04.plain: Poor Yen Hui declined office: his fields fed and clothed him, his lute and study made him happy. Confucius praised him: the contented don't chase gain, and those who cultivate the inner self feel no shame without position.
chuang-tzu-giles-029-p04.core_idea: Contentment frees you from chasing gain and status

judge.issue: Drops Confucius's line that those who have truly obtained do not fear loss.

chuang-tzu-giles-029-p05.plain: A prince's body was in the country but his heart in the city. Value life above all, he was told, and gain loses its pull. If you can't, follow your nature; forcing yourself beyond your ability doubles the harm.
chuang-tzu-giles-029-p05.core_idea: Forcing yourself beyond your nature doubles the harm

judge.issue: Drops the closing point that such double injury shortens life.

chuang-tzu-giles-029-p06.plain: Told they had failed, Confucius said failure means failing in the Tao, and holding to the Tao in a disordered age is no failure. Like pines thriving in frost and snow, he counts his hardship a blessing.
chuang-tzu-giles-029-p06.core_idea: Hardship, like winter, brings out true strength

judge.issue: Drops that inner cultivation keeps virtue intact when danger comes.

chuang-tzu-giles-029-p07.plain: The ancients who found the Tao were equally happy in success and failure; their happiness didn't depend on either. With the Tao, success and failure became just links in a chain, like cold, heat, wind and rain.
chuang-tzu-giles-029-p07.core_idea: With the Tao, success and failure don't decide happiness

chuang-tzu-giles-030-p01.plain: At most a person lives a hundred years. Remove the time lost to sickness, mourning and trouble, and only four or five days a month are left for laughter. Next to everlasting Heaven and Earth, a life is a flash.
chuang-tzu-giles-030-p01.core_idea: Life is brief, with few days for laughter

judge.issue: Drops the explicit 'every man has to die' and the swift-steed image.

chuang-tzu-giles-031-p01.plain: A ruler's power doesn't make him worthy, and poverty or low rank doesn't make someone unworthy. What separates the worthy from the unworthy is whether their actions are worthy.
chuang-tzu-giles-031-p01.core_idea: Worth is shown by actions, not rank

chuang-tzu-giles-031-p02.plain: Don't leave the path of virtue, and don't try to engineer your own good deeds, or your effort will be wasted. Don't chase wealth or aim at success, or you will throw away what connects you to God.
chuang-tzu-giles-031-p02.core_idea: Chasing wealth and success cuts your link to God

chuang-tzu-giles-031-p03.plain: The wise man acts for the common good without overstepping proper limits. So when he has enough, he doesn't try for more; he has no use for more, so he doesn't look for it.
chuang-tzu-giles-031-p03.core_idea: The wise stop seeking once they have enough

chuang-tzu-giles-031-p04.plain: Happiness is found in being content. Too much of anything is always a curse, and above all too much wealth.
chuang-tzu-giles-031-p04.core_idea: Happiness lies in contentment; excess is a curse

chuang-tzu-giles-032-p01.plain: Knowing your faults but not fixing them, and being warned but only going further wrong: that is stubbornness.
chuang-tzu-giles-032-p01.core_idea: Ignoring known faults and warnings is obstinacy

chuang-tzu-giles-032-p02.plain: A man afraid of his shadow and footsteps tried to outrun them, but they kept up. Thinking he was too slow, he ran until he died. He never realised that resting in the shade, keeping still, would have ended both.
chuang-tzu-giles-032-p02.core_idea: Running from yourself only exhausts you; be still

chuang-tzu-giles-032-p03.plain: Take careful care of your body, guard your natural purity, and leave outside matters to others; then you won't get entangled. But instead of improving yourself, you are trying to improve other people, and that is dealing with the external.
chuang-tzu-giles-032-p03.core_idea: Improve yourself instead of trying to fix others

chuang-tzu-giles-032-p04.plain: True grief mourns in silence. True anger commands respect without words. True friendship is harmony that needs no smiles.
chuang-tzu-giles-032-p04.core_idea: True feeling needs no outward show

chuang-tzu-giles-033-p01.plain: The true sage rests in what truly gives rest, not in what doesn't. The world rests in what doesn't give rest, and not in what does.
chuang-tzu-giles-033-p01.core_idea: Most people seek rest where none is found

chuang-tzu-giles-033-p02.plain: The sage treats certainties as uncertain, so he never takes up arms; most people treat uncertainties as certain, so they are always ready to fight. Getting used to fighting makes you fight at every provocation; relying on force, you perish.
chuang-tzu-giles-033-p02.core_idea: Holding certainties loosely keeps you from conflict

chuang-tzu-giles-033-p03.plain: Alas, human knowledge can split a hair, yet it cannot reach lasting peace.
chuang-tzu-giles-033-p03.core_idea: Knowledge is precise but cannot bring peace

chuang-tzu-giles-033-p04.plain: Outward punishments come from metal and wood; inner punishments come from anxiety and remorse. Fools are punished outwardly with chains and blades, while others are eaten up inside by warring emotions. Only the pure and perfect person escapes both.
chuang-tzu-giles-033-p04.core_idea: Anxiety and remorse are inner punishments

chuang-tzu-giles-033-p05.plain: Have you seen a sacrificial ox, decked in ribbons and fed richly? When it is led to slaughter at the temple, wouldn't it gladly trade places with some neglected calf?
chuang-tzu-giles-033-p05.core_idea: Pampered honour can lead to sacrifice

chuang-tzu-giles-033-p06.plain: As Chuang Tzu was dying, his disciples wanted a grand funeral. He said: with Heaven and Earth as my coffin, the sun, moon and stars as my ornaments, and all creation as my escort, isn't my funeral already prepared?

chuang-tzu-giles-034-p01.plain: Not craving fame after death, not trying to dazzle the world, not posing as humanity's benefactor, but being strict with yourself and forgiving of others' faults: that was the Tao of the ancients.
chuang-tzu-giles-034-p01.core_idea: Be strict with yourself, lenient with others

chuang-tzu-giles-034-p02.plain: Serving the public without faction or selfishness, moving freely, taking things as they come, with no regret for the past or worry about the future, favouring no one and friendly with all: that was the Tao of the ancients.
chuang-tzu-giles-034-p02.core_idea: No regret, no worry, taking things as they come

chuang-tzu-giles-034-p03.plain: Don't take a fixed position, and let outside things look after themselves. When moving, be like water; when still, like a mirror; when responding, like an echo.
chuang-tzu-giles-034-p03.core_idea: Move like water, rest like a mirror

chuang-tzu-giles-035-p01.plain: Being generous in sympathy toward all creation, and not aggressive toward other people, can be called perfection.
chuang-tzu-giles-035-p01.core_idea: Sympathy for all, aggression toward none, is perfection

chuang-tzu-giles-035-p02.plain: Silence, formlessness, change and impermanence; now life, now death; heaven and earth merged; the soul leaving for who knows where, as all things go in turn, never to return: this was the Tao of the ancients.
chuang-tzu-giles-035-p02.core_idea: All things change and pass, never returning

eckhart-sermons-field-001-p01.plain: My soul has room to take in God completely. I am certain that nothing is as near to me as God. God is nearer to me than I am to myself, and my existence depends on his presence.
eckhart-sermons-field-001-p01.core_idea: God is nearer to me than I am to myself

eckhart-sermons-field-001-p02.plain: Serving God from fear is good, from love better, from fear and love together best. A peaceful life in God is good, bearing pain patiently better, but peace in the middle of pain is best of all.
eckhart-sermons-field-001-p02.core_idea: Best of all is peace in the midst of pain

eckhart-sermons-field-002-p01.plain: You can be aware of God praying in a field or in church. If you feel him more in a quiet place, that is your shortcoming, not God's, for he is present everywhere. Whoever knows God everywhere knows him rightly.
eckhart-sermons-field-002-p01.core_idea: Knowing God rightly means finding him everywhere

eckhart-sermons-field-002-p02.plain: No one wants anything as eagerly as God wants people to know him. God is always ready; we are not. God is near, we are far; God is within, we are without; God is friendly, we are estranged.
eckhart-sermons-field-002-p02.core_idea: God is always near; we are the ones far away

eckhart-sermons-field-002-p03.plain: A wife who lost an eye feared her husband would love her less, so he put out one of his own to show his love. Likewise, people could hardly believe God loved them until God took on human nature.
eckhart-sermons-field-002-p03.core_idea: God became human to show his love

fix.display_text: There were a certain man and wife; the woman by accident lost an eye, and was sorely troubled thereat. Her husband then said to her, "Wife, why are you troubled?" She answered, "It is not the loss of my eye that troubles me, but the thought that you may love me less on account of that loss." He said, "I love you all the same." Not long after he put one of his own eyes out, and came to his wife and said, "Wife, that you may believe I love you, I have made myself like you: I, too, now, have only one eye." So men could hardly believe that God loved them till God put one of His eyes out, that is took upon Himself human nature, and was made man.
fix.reason: Misplaced space around closing quotation mark

eckhart-sermons-field-002-p04.plain: Whichever way the earth flees from heaven, it meets heaven, which makes it fruitful whether it wants this or not. So God does with people: whoever tries to escape him flies into his arms; every corner is open to him.
eckhart-sermons-field-002-p04.core_idea: No one can escape God; fleeing leads to him

eckhart-sermons-field-002-p05.plain: To hear the Father's wisdom you must live deep within, at home and at one with yourself. Bodily appetite, distraction and the illusion of time block the eternal Word; free of them, you would hear it.
eckhart-sermons-field-002-p05.core_idea: Inner unity frees us to hear God's eternal Word

judge.issue: Drops dwelling in eternity, spirit, solitude and desert as the outcome.

eckhart-sermons-field-002-p06.plain: If you truly love yourself, you love everyone as yourself; loving anyone less means you don't really love yourself. Loving only friends who are kind to you is a half-filled sail.
eckhart-sermons-field-002-p06.core_idea: True self-love means loving everyone equally

judge.issue: Drops the closing ideal of sharing another's joy, sorrow, life and death as one's own.

eckhart-sermons-field-003-p01.plain: To see colour the eye must have none itself. The eye that sees God is the same eye through which God sees me; God's sight and mine are one.
eckhart-sermons-field-003-p01.core_idea: God's seeing and mine are one sight

judge.issue: Drops 'one knowledge, and one love'; unity reduced to sight alone.

eckhart-sermons-field-003-p02.plain: Someone who gave up the self for twenty years but took it back for a moment would have given up nothing. Only one who never looks back at what was renounced has truly renounced the self.

eckhart-sermons-field-004-p01.plain: Real holiness means the spirit stays unmoved by love or hate, joy or sorrow, honour or shame, like a mountain in a light breeze. This stillness brings a person as close to God's likeness as possible.
eckhart-sermons-field-004-p01.core_idea: Unshaken stillness of spirit makes us most like God

eckhart-sermons-field-004-p02.plain: When God seems angry or kind, it is we who change, not God, just as the same sunshine hurts weak eyes and helps strong ones.
eckhart-sermons-field-004-p02.core_idea: God stays the same; our state changes

eckhart-sermons-field-004-p03.plain: A heart ready for the highest must be empty of everything else, like a blank tablet. If God is to write on your heart, all else must be cleared out first.
eckhart-sermons-field-004-p03.core_idea: God can write only on an emptied heart

judge.issue: Drops 'however noble' and that the sanctified heart has no outward object.

eckhart-sermons-field-004-p04.plain: Suffering is the fastest way to perfection, and those who share Christ's sharpest pain enjoy the greatest blessedness. Humility is its foundation, for love brings suffering and suffering brings love.
eckhart-sermons-field-004-p04.core_idea: Suffering and humility lead to perfection through love

judge.issue: Drops 'nothing sweeter than to have suffered' and the lowly being lifted to God.

eckhart-sermons-field-005-p01.plain: As wind makes fire grow, so the Holy Spirit makes the fire of love grow brighter in the soul, not all at once but gradually as the soul grows.
eckhart-sermons-field-005-p01.core_idea: The Holy Spirit gradually brightens the soul's love

eckhart-sermons-field-005-p02.plain: No saint was ever so great as to be completely unmoved. I can never reach a point where discord pleases me as much as harmony.
eckhart-sermons-field-005-p02.core_idea: Even saints are not wholly unmoved

eckhart-sermons-field-005-p03.plain: What makes an act moral is its inner source: the strength of will behind it and the nobility of its aim. Doing good frees a person and brings them nearer to their divine origin.
eckhart-sermons-field-005-p03.core_idea: Morality lies in inner will and noble aim

eckhart-sermons-field-005-p04.plain: All grief except grief for sin comes from loving the world. God holds no sorrow, so abide in God alone to be free of it; while we love created things, pain continues.
eckhart-sermons-field-005-p04.core_idea: Grief comes from attachment to the world

eckhart-sermons-field-005-p05.plain: Suffering endured only for yourself is grievous and hard to bear. Suffering endured for God alone is not heavy, because God carries the load.
eckhart-sermons-field-005-p05.core_idea: Suffering borne for God is lightened by God

emerson-essays-001-p01.plain: Beauty surrounds us, yet we do not see it clearly.
emerson-essays-001-p01.core_idea: We are surrounded by beauty we fail to see

emerson-essays-001-p02.plain: You may travel the whole world looking for beauty, but unless you carry it within you, you will not find it.
emerson-essays-001-p02.core_idea: Beauty must be carried within to be found

emerson-essays-002-p01.plain: Plain common sense and honest dealing astonish people more than anything. Every great action, and every great picture, is simple.

emerson-essays-002-p02.plain: The sweetest music is not in grand choral works but in a human voice speaking from the living moment with tenderness, truth or courage.
emerson-essays-002-p02.core_idea: A sincere living voice is the sweetest music

emerson-essays-002-p03.plain: When the sun set, his hope did not; his faith rose before the stars. His gaze seemed deep and ancient, and his patient endurance matched the silence of time.
emerson-essays-002-p03.core_idea: Steadfast hope and patient endurance outlast darkness

emerson-essays-003-p01.plain: No change in your situation can make up for a flaw in your character.

emerson-essays-003-p02.plain: If I am afraid, what I fear hardly matters; a fearful person will always find something to fear. The greed or malice I blame on society is really my own. I am always surrounded by myself.
emerson-essays-003-p02.core_idea: Our faults travel with us; we meet ourselves everywhere

judge.issue: Narrows 'our proper vice' taking many shapes to fear alone.

emerson-essays-004-p01.plain: Seeing the evils and their cure with the mind is not enough. We keep putting off really living while only a thought, not a spirit, moves us.
emerson-essays-004-p01.core_idea: Living requires spirit, not just understanding

emerson-essays-004-p02.plain: The only apology a noble person can bear to give or take for past actions is new action. If a friend displeases you, don't brood on it; he has already forgotten and is ready to do you good.
emerson-essays-004-p02.core_idea: New deeds are the best apology; don't brood

emerson-essays-004-p03.plain: People who live for the future will always look selfish to people who live for the present.
emerson-essays-004-p03.core_idea: Future-minded people seem selfish to the present-minded

emerson-essays-004-p04.plain: Where I thought I was poor, I found I was richest.
emerson-essays-004-p04.core_idea: Our apparent poverty can be our greatest wealth

emerson-essays-004-p05.plain: Nothing in life satisfies like the deep understanding between two good people who have helped each other long and trust both themselves and each other. It outranks every other pleasure and makes politics, trade and churches seem cheap.
emerson-essays-004-p05.core_idea: Deep friendship between good people is life's greatest satisfaction

emerson-essays-004-p06.plain: Could we honour a friend with truth, silence and patience instead of eagerly chasing him? If we truly belong together, we will meet.
emerson-essays-004-p06.core_idea: Real friends need not be chased; they will meet

emerson-essays-005-p01.plain: Life rushes on; we chase plans or flee fears. But meeting a friend makes us stop, and our hurry looks foolish; then we need presence and a full heart. In noble relationships, the moment is everything.
emerson-essays-005-p01.core_idea: In true relationships the present moment is everything

emerson-essays-005-p02.plain: Life teaches us that around every circle a larger one can be drawn: nature has no end, every end is a beginning, and beneath every depth lies a deeper one.
emerson-essays-005-p02.core_idea: Every end is a new beginning

emerson-essays-005-p03.plain: Nothing in nature is fixed. The universe is fluid and ever-changing, and permanence is only a matter of degree.

emerson-essays-005-p04.plain: People have no fixed limits. Everyone feels not fully understood, and if there is truth in him and he rests finally on the divine soul, that must be so: some inner room is never opened. So everyone believes he has greater possibilities.
emerson-essays-005-p04.core_idea: Everyone holds an unexplored greater possibility
emerson-essays-005-p04.plain_v1: Nothing in people is fixed either. Everyone feels not fully understood, sensing an unknown inner room never opened; that is, everyone believes they hold a greater possibility.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the condition 'if he rests at last on the divine soul', secularising the ground of the claim.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the condition about resting on the divine soul; 'either' is unexplained.

emerson-essays-005-p05.plain: Our moods don't trust each other. Today I write freely; yesterday I saw only emptiness, and next month I'll wonder who wrote this. Such shaky faith: I am God in nature; I am a weed by the wall.
emerson-essays-005-p05.core_idea: Our moods swing between greatness and smallness

emerson-essays-005-p06.plain: You can see a person's growth in each new circle of friends. For every friend lost by standing for truth, he gains a better one.
emerson-essays-005-p06.core_idea: Growth shows in better friendships gained through truth

emerson-essays-006-p01.plain: Courage is the power to recover yourself, so that wherever you are placed, you stand. It comes from preferring truth to your old idea of truth and being ready to let your beliefs be replaced.
emerson-essays-006-p01.core_idea: Courage is self-recovery through openness to new truth

judge.issue: Softens 'his Christianity, his world' to generic 'beliefs'; drops accepting truth from any quarter.

emerson-essays-006-p02.plain: Talk is good, but silence is better and puts talk to shame. The longer the talk, the further apart speaker and listener are; perfect understanding needs no words.
emerson-essays-006-p02.core_idea: Silence surpasses speech; understanding needs few words

judge.issue: Drops the stronger claim that full unity would not even tolerate words.

emerson-essays-006-p03.plain: In daily work I tend to repeat my old steps and doubt that change is possible. Then a bold poet's work jolts me out of my habits, and I see my own possibilities and can choose a straight path again.
emerson-essays-006-p03.core_idea: Inspired art breaks our habits and reveals our possibilities

emerson-essays-006-p04.plain: What is justice, beauty or wisdom to one person is injustice, ugliness or folly to another, as seen from a higher point of view.
emerson-essays-006-p04.core_idea: Values shift with one's point of view

emerson-essays-006-p05.plain: Divine moments even wipe away our regrets. I blame myself daily for laziness, but when God flows into me I stop counting lost time, for such moments see that the mind's energy matches the work, without need of time.
emerson-essays-006-p05.core_idea: Divine moments erase regret over lost time

emerson-essays-007-p01.plain: While we keep company with what is above us, we grow younger, not older. The young look up and learn from everything, but at seventy people think they know all and lose hope. Let them become vessels of the Holy Spirit, love and see truth, and hope and power return.
emerson-essays-007-p01.core_idea: Aspiring upward keeps the mind young
emerson-essays-007-p01.plain_v1: While we keep company with what is above us, we grow young, not old. The young look upward and learn; the old often think they know all and lose hope. Let them love and seek truth again.

judge_v1.issue: Drops 'organs of the Holy Ghost' and the renewal of hope and power; secularises the remedy.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops becoming organs of the Holy Ghost and the renewal of hope and power.

emerson-essays-007-p02.plain: In nature every moment is new; only what is coming is sacred, and nothing is secure but life and change. No oath protects a love from a higher love, nor any truth from new thought. People want to be settled, but only being unsettled gives them hope.
emerson-essays-007-p02.core_idea: Only change is secure; being unsettled brings hope
emerson-essays-007-p02.plain_v1: In nature every moment is new and only what is coming is sacred. Nothing is secure but life and change. People want to be settled, but there is hope for them only as far as they are unsettled.

judge_v1.issue: Drops that no love is bound against a higher love and no truth is safe from new thought.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops that no love or truth is secure against a higher one.

emerson-essays-007-p03.plain: Life is full of surprises. While we are building ourselves, we can't predict tomorrow's mood, joy or strength.
emerson-essays-007-p03.core_idea: Life is a series of surprises

emerson-essays-007-p04.plain: People boast of how cheerfully they have overcome dark events, but not if those events still come to mind. True victory is when the disaster fades into a small passing cloud in a large, moving life.
emerson-essays-007-p04.core_idea: True conquest lets past calamity fade into insignificance

emerson-essays-007-p05.plain: Nothing great was ever done without enthusiasm. Life's way is wonderful, and it works through letting go.

emerson-essays-007-p06.plain: Do not be afraid, weak child: no god would dare wrong even a worm. Rewards go to those who earn them; whatever nature made yours will cross hills and seas to follow you like your shadow.
emerson-essays-007-p06.core_idea: What is truly yours will find you

judge.issue: Drops 'power to him who power exerts' and that one's share rushes to meet one.

emerson-essays-007-p07.plain: Every excess brings a lack and every lack an excess; every sweet has its sour and every evil its good. For everything you miss you gain something else, and for everything you gain you lose something.
emerson-essays-007-p07.core_idea: Every gain has a loss, every loss a gain

judge.issue: Drops the penalty on abused faculties and the wit-for-folly balance.

emerson-essays-008-p01.plain: Wrongdoing and its punishment grow from the same root. Punishment ripens unnoticed inside the very pleasure that hid it.
emerson-essays-008-p01.core_idea: Punishment grows hidden inside wrongful pleasure

emerson-essays-008-p02.plain: People want to be great, seeking office, wealth, power and fame. They think greatness means having the sweet side of life without the bitter.
emerson-essays-008-p02.core_idea: People wrongly seek the sweet without the bitter

emerson-essays-008-p03.plain: As soon as we try to pull pleasure, profit or power away from the whole, it drains out of them. We can no more split off the good alone than have an inside without an outside, or light without shadow.
emerson-essays-008-p03.core_idea: Good cannot be split from its cost

emerson-essays-008-p04.plain: Everything God has made has a flaw in it.
emerson-essays-008-p04.core_idea: Everything God made has a crack

emerson-essays-008-p05.plain: Whenever you speak, you judge yourself; every word paints your portrait for others, whether you want it or not. Each opinion rebounds on the speaker, like a ball of thread thrown whose other end stays in the thrower's bag.
emerson-essays-008-p05.core_idea: Our words reveal and rebound on ourselves

emerson-essays-008-p06.plain: You cannot wrong others without being wronged yourself. The snob shuts himself out of enjoyment, and the religious exclusionist shuts heaven on himself. Treat people as pawns and you suffer too; leave out their heart and you lose your own.

emerson-essays-009-p01.plain: While I deal simply and fairly with others, meeting them is easy, like water meeting water. But once I seek good for me that isn't good for them, they pull back, and hate and fear grow between us.
emerson-essays-009-p01.core_idea: Unfairness breeds distance, hate and fear

judge.issue: Drops the mirror point that he shrinks exactly as far as I shrank.

emerson-essays-009-p02.plain: Nature exists to give benefit, but every benefit carries a debt. The one truly base thing is to take favours and give none back; we rarely repay the giver, so pass the good on to someone, and quickly.
emerson-essays-009-p02.core_idea: Pass on every benefit you receive

judge.issue: Drops 'he is great who confers the most benefits' and the warning that hoarded good corrupts.

emerson-essays-009-p03.plain: Love, and you will be loved. All love is as exactly balanced as the two sides of an equation.

emerson-essays-009-p04.plain: Even weaknesses serve good people; every defect proves useful somewhere, so everyone should thank their faults. A bad temper that makes someone unfit for company drives them to rely on themselves, like a wounded oyster mending its shell with pearl.
emerson-essays-009-p04.core_idea: Our faults can become our strengths

judge.issue: Drops the stag fable and the point about learning through contending and suffering.

emerson-essays-009-p05.plain: Our strength grows out of our weakness. Comfort puts a great person to sleep; being pushed, tormented and defeated teaches them, exposing their ignorance, curing their conceit, and giving them moderation and real skill.
emerson-essays-009-p05.core_idea: Strength grows from weakness and defeat

judge.issue: Drops 'a great man is always willing to be little'.

emerson-essays-009-p06.plain: No one can be cheated except by himself. The nature of things guarantees that honest service is never lost. If your master is ungrateful, serve him more; put God in your debt; every effort will be repaid.
emerson-essays-009-p06.core_idea: Honest service is never lost; only we cheat ourselves

emerson-essays-009-p07.plain: A martyr cannot be disgraced. Every lash spreads his fame, every burned book enlightens the world, every silenced word echoes across the earth. In time communities see the truth, and martyrs are vindicated.
emerson-essays-009-p07.core_idea: Persecution only amplifies the martyr's truth

emerson-essays-010-p01.plain: Virtue and wisdom carry no penalty; they add to who you are and to the world, pushing back darkness. Pure love, knowledge and beauty have no excess. The soul refuses limits and is always optimistic.
emerson-essays-010-p01.core_idea: Virtue and love have no penalty or limit

emerson-essays-010-p02.plain: Material goods have a cost, and unearned gain has no root and blows away. The soul's good comes through honest work. I no longer want unearned gain or more possessions: the gain only seems; the cost is certain.
emerson-essays-010-p02.core_idea: Unearned gain is fleeting; its cost is certain

emerson-essays-010-p03.plain: Even if great people around me overshadow me, I can still love and receive, and whoever loves makes the greatness he loves his own. Then I find that the one I envied is my guardian, and his riches are mine.
emerson-essays-010-p03.core_idea: Love makes others' greatness our own

emerson-essays-010-p04.plain: The upheavals that regularly break up our prosperity are signs that nature's law is growth. Every soul must leave its friends, home, laws and faith, as a shellfish leaves a shell it has outgrown, and slowly build a new one.
emerson-essays-010-p04.core_idea: Upheaval is the soul outgrowing its shell

emerson-essays-010-p05.plain: We cling to friends, not seeing they leave so better ones can come. We doubt today can match yesterday and weep in its ruins. God says, Up and onward forever, yet we walk looking backward.
emerson-essays-010-p05.core_idea: Clinging to the past blocks what comes next

judge.issue: Flattens angels and archangels to 'better ones'; drops faith that the spirit can feed us again.

emerson-essays-010-p06.plain: Illness, ruin, even a loved one's death seem at first pure loss. But the years reveal a healing force: such losses end old phases and open new paths, letting a sheltered person grow to shelter many.
emerson-essays-010-p06.core_idea: Loss, in time, reveals its power to grow us

judge.issue: Compresses the garden-flower-to-banyan image and the new influences that follow loss.

emerson-essays-010-p07.plain: We can't tell today whether we are busy or idle. Times we thought lazy later turned out to have achieved much and started much in us.
emerson-essays-010-p07.core_idea: Seemingly idle times can be quietly productive

emerson-essays-010-p08.plain: Every ship looks romantic except the one we are on; once aboard, the romance seems to belong to every other sail. Our own life looks trivial, and we avoid recording it.
emerson-essays-010-p08.core_idea: Other lives look romantic; ours seems trivial

emerson-essays-010-p09.plain: After my son's death, I seem to have lost only a beautiful estate. It does not touch me; what seemed part of me fell away without a scar. I grieve that grief can teach me nothing real.
emerson-essays-010-p09.core_idea: Grief, strangely, teaches nothing and leaves no mark

emerson-essays-011-p01.plain: Life is a string of moods, each a coloured lens showing only what is in its focus. We see only what we bring alive. Sunsets and genius are always there, but few hours are calm enough to enjoy them.
emerson-essays-011-p01.core_idea: Our moods colour and limit what we see

judge.issue: Drops that nature and books belong to the eyes that see them, depending on mood.

emerson-essays-011-p02.plain: I had imagined that life's value lay in its unknowable possibilities, in never knowing what might happen when I meet someone new.
emerson-essays-011-p02.core_idea: Life's value lies in its unknown possibilities

emerson-essays-011-p03.plain: Every mind has a door that never closes, through which the Creator enters.
emerson-essays-011-p03.core_idea: The Creator can always enter the mind

emerson-essays-011-p04.plain: We love what is real and lasting, yet a healthy body needs circulation and a sane mind needs variety. We need a change of objects; devotion to a single thought soon becomes hateful.

emerson-essays-011-p05.plain: A person is like a stone that looks dull until you turn it to just the right angle, and then it shows deep, beautiful colours.
emerson-essays-011-p05.core_idea: Everyone shines from the right angle

emerson-essays-011-p06.plain: We gain something even from dealing with so much foolishness and fault. Whoever loses, we end up on the winning side; the divine stands behind our failures and follies too.
emerson-essays-011-p06.core_idea: God is behind even our failures

emerson-essays-012-p01.plain: Don't drive yourself mad with thinking; just get on with your work wherever you are. Life is sturdy, not intellectual, and its best is for balanced people who enjoy what they find without questioning.
emerson-essays-012-p01.core_idea: Stop overthinking; live and enjoy what you find

emerson-essays-012-p02.plain: Happiness is filling the hour fully, leaving no gap for regret or self-approval. We live among surfaces, and the art of life is to skate well on them.
emerson-essays-012-p02.core_idea: Happiness is filling the present hour

emerson-essays-012-p03.plain: Life is lived in moments, so use them well; five minutes today are worth five minutes in a thousand years. Be balanced, wise and your own today, and treat people as if they were real; perhaps they are.
emerson-essays-012-p03.core_idea: Use today's moments well and treat people as real

emerson-essays-012-p04.plain: I am thankful for small mercies. A friend expects the best from the universe and is disappointed by less; I expect nothing and am always grateful for modest good things.
emerson-essays-012-p04.core_idea: Expect little and be grateful for modest goods

emerson-essays-012-p05.plain: You are told your illness demands this or that, but your life is a tent for one night; sick or well, finish your task. You will not worsen, and the universe, which holds you dear, will be better.
emerson-essays-012-p05.core_idea: Sick or well, finish your work; you are held dear

emerson-essays-013-p01.plain: Life is a string of surprises and would not be worth living otherwise. Daily God hides the past and future behind a clear screen of sky, as if saying: you will not remember, and you will not expect.
emerson-essays-013-p01.core_idea: God hides past and future to keep life surprising

judge.issue: 'Clear screen' loses 'impenetrable'; drops that God delights to isolate us.

emerson-essays-013-p02.plain: Every person is impossible until born; everything is impossible until we see it succeed.
emerson-essays-013-p02.core_idea: Everything seems impossible until it happens

emerson-essays-013-p03.plain: Life's results can't be calculated; the years teach what days never know. A person plans, recruits others, quarrels and blunders, and something gets done, but never what he intended; the individual is always mistaken.
emerson-essays-013-p03.core_idea: Life's outcomes always differ from our plans

emerson-essays-013-p04.plain: Why fret when something stops me being where I was expected? Wherever I am, my presence can serve friendship and wisdom just as well, for I bring the same power to every place.
emerson-essays-013-p04.core_idea: Wherever you are, your presence matters equally

emerson-essays-013-p05.plain: All personal sympathy is partial. Two people are like globes that touch at only one point; their other parts stay idle and grow restless the longer the union lasts.
emerson-essays-013-p05.core_idea: People connect only partially, like touching spheres

emerson-essays-014-p01.plain: A key lesson of wisdom is to tell what is yours from what is another's. I cannot settle other people's lives, but holding the key to my own convinces me they hold the key to theirs.
emerson-essays-014-p01.core_idea: Know your own business from others'

emerson-essays-014-p02.plain: A sympathetic person is like a swimmer among drowning men who will pull him under. They want rescue from the harm of their vices, not from the vices. A wise healer first says: get out of that.
emerson-essays-014-p02.core_idea: Help people quit their vices, not just the consequences

judge.issue: Drops that charity is wasted tending symptoms.

emerson-essays-014-p03.plain: Our good nature and listening to everyone ruin us; such compliance robs us of real usefulness. The only answer to others' pestering trivia is focused attention on an aim that makes their wants trivial, leaving no grievance.
emerson-essays-014-p03.core_idea: Focused purpose answers others' trivial demands

judge.issue: Drops calling focused attention 'a divine answer' and looking directly forthright.

emerson-essays-014-p04.plain: I don't claim this picture is complete. I am a fragment, and this is a fragment of me.
emerson-essays-014-p04.core_idea: I am a fragment, offering a fragment

emerson-essays-014-p05.plain: Be patient; we will win in the end. Daily chores are soon forgotten, but in solitude a person finds sanity and insight that last. Ignore ridicule and defeat and rise again: justice will yet win, and the world exists to turn genius into practical power.
emerson-essays-014-p05.core_idea: Be patient; rise after defeat, victory remains

judge.issue: Drops the deception of time and the quick insight that lights a life.

emerson-essays-014-p05.plain_v1: With patience we will win. Chores take long and are forgotten, while a life-guiding insight takes a moment; in solitude we find clarity. Never mind ridicule or defeat; get up again, old heart, victory remains.

judge_v1.issue: Drops closing thesis: victory for justice and genius transformed into practical power.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops time's deceptions and the closing on genius becoming practical power.

emerson-essays-014-p06.plain: My heart was free again: friend, through you alone the sky and rose seem beautiful and all things look nobler. Your goodness has taught me to master my despair, and my hidden life is made fair by your friendship.
emerson-essays-014-p06.core_idea: A friend's nobleness helps us master despair

emerson-essays-014-p07.plain: We feel far more kindness than we ever say. Despite chilling selfishness, all people are bathed in love. Think how many we barely speak to yet honour, or silently rejoice to be near. Read those passing glances; the heart knows.
emerson-essays-014-p07.core_idea: Far more unspoken kindness exists than we say

emerson-essays-014-p08.plain: Our minds and energies grow with our affection. A scholar may sit for hours without one good thought, yet when he writes to a friend, gentle thoughts arrive at once in well-chosen words.
emerson-essays-014-p08.core_idea: Affection quickens our thinking and expression

emerson-essays-015-p01.plain: The moment we give in to affection, the world is transformed: no winter, no night, no tragedy or boredom. If the soul knew it would someday rejoin its friend, it could be content alone for a thousand years.
emerson-essays-015-p01.core_idea: Love transforms the world and sustains the soul

judge.issue: Drops that even duties vanish and the radiant forms of the beloved.

emerson-essays-015-p02.plain: I woke deeply grateful for my friends, old and new, and wondered whether to call God the Beautiful, shown daily in such gifts. I prefer solitude, yet whoever understands me becomes mine forever.
emerson-essays-015-p02.core_idea: Gratitude for friends as God's gifts

judge.issue: Softens 'I chide society' to preferring solitude; drops noticing the noble who pass.

emerson-essays-015-p03.plain: The soul grows friends like a tree grows leaves, pushing out old ones as new buds form. Nature's law is alternation: the soul gathers friends to know itself better, then goes alone a while to enrich its company.
emerson-essays-015-p03.core_idea: The soul alternates between friendship and solitude

emerson-essays-015-p04.plain: Friendships end quickly and poorly because we build them of wine and dreams, not the heart's tough fibre. We grab quick sweetness from the slowest fruit in God's garden, which takes many seasons to ripen.
emerson-essays-015-p04.core_idea: True friendship ripens slowly; don't rush it

judge.issue: Drops that friendship's laws are austere, eternal and one with nature and morals.

emerson-essays-015-p05.plain: I want to treat friendship not delicately but with rough courage. Real friendships are not fragile like glass or frost; they are the most solid thing we know.
emerson-essays-015-p05.core_idea: Real friendship is solid, not fragile

emerson-essays-015-p06.plain: A friend is someone with whom I can be sincere and think aloud. With such a real equal I can drop even my deepest layers of pretence, politeness and second thought, and meet him whole and simply.
emerson-essays-015-p06.core_idea: A friend is someone you can be fully sincere with

emerson-essays-015-p07.plain: Everyone is sincere when alone. When a second person enters, hypocrisy begins: we hold others off with compliments, gossip, amusements and business, hiding our thoughts under a hundred folds.
emerson-essays-015-p07.core_idea: Hypocrisy begins when another person enters

emerson-essays-016-p01.plain: Friendship aims at the closest, most homely partnership, for help and comfort through all of life and death. It suits calm days and pleasant walks, but also rough roads, shipwreck, poverty and persecution.
emerson-essays-016-p01.core_idea: Friendship is for hard times as well as good

emerson-essays-016-p02.plain: Friendship needs a rare balance of likeness and difference. I'd rather be alone than have my friend fake sympathy or merely agree. Let him stay himself. Better be a nettle in your friend's side than his echo.
emerson-essays-016-p02.core_idea: A true friend is not your echo

judge.issue: Drops 'the not mine is mine' and being balked by antagonism as much as compliance.

emerson-essays-016-p03.plain: Friendship calls for reverence. Friends choose themselves. Your friend has merits you lack, which you cannot honour if you cling to him; stand back and let them grow. Are you a friend to his buttons or to his thought?
emerson-essays-016-p03.core_idea: Revere your friend; give their gifts room

judge.issue: Drops 'treat your friend as a spectacle'; 'religious treatment' reduced to reverence.

emerson-essays-016-p04.plain: Virtue's only reward is virtue; the only way to have a friend is to be one. You get no closer to someone just by getting into his house.
emerson-essays-016-p04.core_idea: To have a friend, be one

emerson-essays-016-p05.plain: The higher our ideal of friendship, the harder it is to find. We walk alone, and ideal friends are dreams. Yet the faithful heart hopes that elsewhere souls exist who can love us and whom we can love.
emerson-essays-016-p05.core_idea: Hope sustains us though ideal friends are rare

emerson-essays-017-p01.plain: Loving without being loved back is thought shameful, but true love cannot go unreturned. It looks past the unworthy person to the eternal, and when that mask falls, it is not sad but freer and surer of itself.

emerson-essays-017-p02.plain: Rings and jewels are not gifts but excuses for gifts. The only true gift is a part of yourself; you must bleed for me.
emerson-essays-017-p02.core_idea: The only true gift is a part of yourself

emerson-essays-017-p03.plain: Services are worth nothing; only kinship of spirit counts. Trying to bond with people through favours is just a trick: they consume your service and leave you out. But love them, and they feel you and delight in you always.
emerson-essays-017-p03.core_idea: Love, not service, truly connects people

emerson-essays-017-p04.plain: Fine wine, sugar and flowers go to rogues, slaves and clowns, while storm clouds crown the god. The hero is not fed on sweets but daily eats his own heart; great men's rooms are prisons, and headwinds suit royal sails.
emerson-essays-017-p04.core_idea: Heroes are shaped by hardship, not comfort

emerson-essays-018-p01.plain: Heroism obeys a private impulse, against the crowd and, for a time, the wise. Only the hero sees its wisdom, so the just disapprove until time shows it matches their ideals. It spurns comfort but finally succeeds.
emerson-essays-018-p01.core_idea: Heroism defies opinion until time vindicates it

judge.issue: Drops that the prudent come to extol the act once it succeeds.

emerson-essays-018-p02.plain: Heroism is at heart self-trust: the soul at war, defying falsehood and wrong to the last and able to endure any evil. It is truthful, just, generous and temperate, scorns petty calculation and scorn, and persists with untiring courage.
emerson-essays-018-p02.core_idea: Self-trust is the essence of heroism

emerson-essays-018-p03.plain: A heroic soul won't sell its justice or nobility and doesn't ask for good meals or a warm bed. Greatness means seeing that virtue is enough. Poverty adorns it; it needs no abundance and bears its loss well.

emerson-essays-019-p01.plain: The muses and gods live where the heart is, not in famous places. Our own towns seem dull, but if we stay, we may learn here is best. Be truly present, and hope, friends and God will be with you.
emerson-essays-019-p01.core_idea: Be present where you are; the divine is here

judge.issue: Drops art, nature, fate and angels from what attends the present self.

emerson-essays-019-p02.plain: Heroism's mark is persistence. Once you've chosen your part, stick to it and don't seek the world's approval or take back what prudent people disapprove of. As one youth was advised: always do what you are afraid to do.
emerson-essays-019-p02.core_idea: Persist in your chosen course; do what you fear

judge.issue: Drops the 'serve your brother' condition and congratulating oneself on breaking decorum.

emerson-essays-019-p03.plain: For any weakness or embarrassment we can find comfort in thinking it is part of who we are and our role among others. Nature never promised we'd never look foolish. Be generous with your dignity; greatness is done with opinion.
emerson-essays-019-p03.core_idea: Greatness doesn't depend on appearing dignified

emerson-essays-019-p04.plain: The only road to peace is following your own heart. Keep less company, stay home often, settle in ways you approve. Holding high ideals in humble duties hardens character to act honourably, even on the scaffold.
emerson-essays-019-p04.core_idea: Peace comes from following your own heart

emerson-essays-019-p05.plain: In dark times we may envy those who have safely finished their brave work and died, beyond life's turmoil. Yet love that would perish rather than betray has already made death impossible and is eternal.

judge.issue: Drops envy of the dead such as Washington and awaiting one's own end.

emerson-essays-019-p06.plain: One mind is shared by all people, and each person opens onto all of it. Whoever can reason may think what Plato thought, feel what a saint felt, and understand whatever has happened to anyone.
emerson-essays-019-p06.core_idea: All people share one universal mind

emerson-essays-020-p01.plain: Every mind must learn the whole lesson for itself and cover all the ground. What it does not see and live, it will not know.
emerson-essays-020-p01.core_idea: We only truly know what we live ourselves

emerson-essays-020-p02.plain: To the poet, the philosopher and the saint, all things are friendly and sacred, every event useful, every day holy, every person divine, because they look at life itself, not circumstances.
emerson-essays-020-p02.core_idea: Seeing life itself makes every day holy

emerson-essays-021-p01.plain: When Plato's thought becomes mine, or a truth that inspired an ancient poet inspires me, time vanishes. When our souls meet in one perception, why measure distance or count the years between us?
emerson-essays-021-p01.core_idea: Shared insight abolishes time and distance

emerson-essays-021-p02.plain: A rigid, harsh adult crushes a child's spirit and courage, breeding fear, obedience and even sympathy with the tyranny. Only as an adult does the child see that his oppressor was himself a child ruled by names, words and forms.

emerson-essays-022-p01.plain: Brother, stop your soul from ebbing away into the habits you have slid into for so many years.

emerson-essays-022-p02.plain: Love can teach a mind more about itself in a day than ages of thinking. We don't know ourselves until moved by outrage, eloquence or a nation's shared emotion; no one can predict what a new experience will awaken.
emerson-essays-022-p02.core_idea: Experience, not thought, reveals who we are

emerson-essays-023-p01.plain: Everyone views the human condition with some sadness: like a grounded ship battered by waves, we lie exposed to coming events. But a truth grasped by the mind is beyond fate, raised like a god above care and fear.
emerson-essays-023-p01.core_idea: Truth grasped by the mind rises above fate

emerson-essays-023-p02.plain: What am I, and what has my will done to make me so? Nothing. Hidden currents of power and mind carried me to this thought and moment; my cleverness and stubbornness barely helped or hindered.
emerson-essays-023-p02.core_idea: Hidden currents, not our will, shape us

emerson-essays-023-p03.plain: Spontaneous action is always best. Careful deliberation never gets as close to a question as the sudden insight that comes on waking or a morning walk, after mulling it over the night before.

emerson-essays-023-p04.plain: All progress unfolds like a bud: first instinct, then opinion, then knowledge, as a plant has root, bud and fruit. Trust your instinct to the end even without reasons; don't hurry it, and it will ripen into truth you understand.
emerson-essays-023-p04.core_idea: Trust instinct; it ripens into knowledge

emerson-essays-023-p05.plain: We expect a truth to come clear on a walk or in the quiet library, but it doesn't. Then suddenly, unannounced, it appears. Yet the insight comes only because we had already laid siege to it.
emerson-essays-023-p05.core_idea: Insight arrives unbidden after sustained effort

emerson-essays-023-p06.plain: It takes long to see how rich we are. We think our lives dull, yet in later years we keep finding treasures in childhood memories, until we suspect our own foolish life is a miniature of all human history.
emerson-essays-023-p06.core_idea: Our ordinary lives mirror all of history

emerson-essays-024-p01.plain: Every thought is also a prison. I can't see what you see because I'm swept so far in one direction that I'm outside the circle of your view.

emerson-essays-024-p02.plain: We crave new thoughts, but each new one is only the old in a new face; we make it ours and instantly want another, never really richer.
emerson-essays-024-p02.core_idea: Craving new thoughts never truly enriches us

emerson-essays-024-p03.plain: God offers every mind a choice between truth and rest; you can't have both. Lovers of rest take the first creed they meet and shut out truth. Lovers of truth stay unmoored, bearing uncertainty, and honour their highest law.
emerson-essays-024-p03.core_idea: Choose truth or comfort; you cannot have both

judge.issue: Drops abstaining from dogmatism and the rest, commodity and reputation the other gains.

emerson-essays-024-p04.plain: Listeners are happy; talkers are not. While I hear truth I feel bathed in beauty, without limits, open to the deep. But when I speak, I define, confine, and become less.
emerson-essays-024-p04.core_idea: Listening enlarges us; speaking confines us

emerson-essays-025-p01.plain: We see our own past as flawed and others' as ideal; recalling our dearest relationships, we wince with regret. Seen as truth, all is beautiful; seen as experience, all is sour. Details are sad; the plan is noble.
emerson-essays-025-p01.core_idea: Life's details are sad; its larger plan is noble

emerson-essays-026-p01.plain: Hence the saying, If I love you, what is that to you? What we love is beyond your will: not you, but your radiance, something in you that you don't know and never can.
emerson-essays-026-p01.core_idea: We love a radiance beyond the beloved's knowing

emerson-essays-026-p02.plain: We are by nature watchers and learners, but our affections are tents for a night that slowly change, at times tying our happiness to certain people. In health the mind returns, and those loves blend with God.
emerson-essays-026-p02.core_idea: Changing affections ultimately find their perfection in God

extension.text: We are by nature observers, and thereby learners. That is our permanent state. But we are often made to feel that our affections are but tents of a night. Though slowly and with pain, the objects of the affections change, as the objects of thought do. There are moments when the affections rule and absorb the man and make his happiness dependent on a person or persons. But in health the mind is presently seen again⁠—its overarching vault, bright with galaxies of immutable lights, and the warm loves and fears that swept over us as clouds must lose their finite character and blend with God, to attain their own perfection.

judge.issue: Drops the mind's vault of immutable lights and loves reaching perfection in God.

emerson-essays-026-p03.plain: We need not fear losing anything as the soul grows. The soul can be trusted to the end: relationships so beautiful can only be replaced by something more beautiful, and so on forever.
emerson-essays-026-p03.core_idea: The soul's growth only brings greater beauty

emerson-essays-027-p01.plain: A gentleman is truthful and master of his own actions, showing it in behaviour that bows to no person, opinion or possession. Beyond that truth and strength, he is kind: manhood first, then gentleness.
emerson-essays-027-p01.core_idea: True gentility is honest self-mastery, then kindness

emerson-essays-028-p01.plain: Newcomers think every social act follows strict ritual. Later they learn good sense and character make their own forms, even sprawling on the floor with children; strong will is always in fashion. Fashion asks only composure and self-content.
emerson-essays-028-p01.core_idea: Character and composure outrank social ritual

emerson-essays-028-p02.plain: What do we really seek in all our visits and hospitality? Is it the curtains, pictures and decorations? Or do we keep asking: was there a real person in the house?
emerson-essays-028-p02.core_idea: We seek real people, not fine surroundings

emerson-essays-028-p03.plain: Nature's mysteries and our deep separateness should teach us independence; let us not be too familiar. We should meet each morning as if from foreign lands and part at night the same way. Keep each person's island untouched.
emerson-essays-028-p03.core_idea: Preserve each person's independence, even among friends

judge.issue: Drops the hall of heroic and sacred sculptures as a hint of self-poise.

emerson-essays-029-p01.plain: The secret of social success is warmth and sympathy. Someone unhappy in company can't find a fitting word. Someone happy there finds every turn of conversation a lucky chance to say what he has to say.
emerson-essays-029-p01.core_idea: Warmth, not information, makes us good company

emerson-essays-029-p02.plain: Heroes have not died out. There's still the plain stranger who jumps in to save a drowning man, the helper of runaway slaves, the planter of orchards for future generations, the just person content with a bad name.
emerson-essays-029-p02.core_idea: Quiet heroes still live among us

emerson-essays-029-p03.plain: A beautiful form beats a beautiful face, and beautiful behaviour beats both; it is the finest of the fine arts. Small amid nature, a person can, through the goodness shining in his face and manners, match the world's majesty.
emerson-essays-029-p03.core_idea: Beautiful behaviour is the finest art

emerson-essays-030-p01.plain: Are you rich enough to help the odd, the foreign, the poor, the outcast, making them feel welcomed and hopeful? Refusing them with clever reasons is vulgar; welcoming them is gentle. Without a rich heart, wealth is an ugly beggar.
emerson-essays-030-p01.core_idea: True wealth is a generous heart

emerson-essays-030-p02.plain: At the forest's edge, the worldly person must drop city ideas of great and small, wise and foolish. Custom falls away at the first step. Here is a holiness that shames our religions and a reality that discredits our heroes.
emerson-essays-030-p02.core_idea: Nature strips away our worldly measures

emerson-essays-030-p03.plain: Cities don't give our senses enough room. Day and night we go out to feast our eyes on the horizon; we need that open space as we need water to bathe.
emerson-essays-030-p03.core_idea: We need open horizons as we need water

emerson-essays-031-p01.plain: My house sits low on the village edge. But paddling the river with a friend, one stroke leaves village gossip and the world behind, entering a realm of sunset and moonlight almost too bright for flawed people.
emerson-essays-031-p01.core_idea: Nature lifts us out of petty concerns

judge.issue: Drops that entering the realm requires novitiate and probation.

emerson-essays-031-p02.plain: We overpraise famous scenery. The wonder of any landscape is where sky meets earth, visible from any hill; the stars shine as grandly over a plain common as over Egypt. Landscapes differ little; beholders differ greatly. Beauty breaks in everywhere.
emerson-essays-031-p02.core_idea: Beauty is everywhere; what differs is the beholder

judge.issue: Drops the necessity of beauty every landscape lies under; nature never caught in undress.

emerson-essays-031-p03.plain: We watch a foaming brook with a pang: if our lives flowed with real energy, we would put the brook to shame. True zeal sparkles with its own fire, not reflected light.
emerson-essays-031-p03.core_idea: Our zeal should outshine the lively brook

emerson-essays-032-p01.plain: Our bodies' excessive fear, flinching at cold, a snake or a sudden noise, protects us through countless false alarms from the one real danger that comes at last.
emerson-essays-032-p01.core_idea: Many false alarms guard against one real danger

emerson-essays-032-p02.plain: No one can write without believing, for the moment, that it is the history of the world, or do anything well without thinking it matters. My work may not matter, but I mustn't think so.
emerson-essays-032-p02.core_idea: Believe your work matters to do it well

judge.issue: Drops the consequence: thinking it worthless means not doing it with impunity.

emerson-essays-032-p03.plain: Promise always outruns delivery. We live among approximations; every goal leads to another, never a final success. We camp in nature rather than settle; however we prepare food and drink, they leave us hungry and thirsty even when full.
emerson-essays-032-p03.core_idea: No success fully satisfies; every end points beyond

emerson-essays-033-p01.plain: Spiritual guides surround us, and a kindly purpose awaits us. Pitted against nature, we feel doomed. But if we feel the Maker's soul streaming through us, we find morning peace and nature's deepest powers within us.
emerson-essays-033-p01.core_idea: Let the Maker's soul flow through you for peace

judge.issue: Drops 'instead of identifying ourselves with the work'; 'workman' rendered as 'Maker'.

emerson-essays-033-p02.plain: Every moment and every object teaches, for wisdom fills every form. It has entered us as blood, as pain, as pleasure, in dull sad days and cheerful working days; only after long time did we grasp what it was.
emerson-essays-033-p02.core_idea: Every experience teaches, though we learn slowly

emerson-essays-033-p03.plain: Am I too sheltered? My lot differs so much from yours, my poor brother and sister. I miss what labour and poverty teach. Amid polite courtesy and luxury I suspect I'm a prisoner, paying a ruinous tax for conforming.
emerson-essays-033-p03.core_idea: Comfort and conformity can imprison us

emerson-essays-034-p01.plain: Attacks on institutions have shown that society gains nothing when someone tries to reform things around him without reforming himself; he becomes tiresomely good in one thing and narrow in the rest, often ending in hypocrisy and vanity.
emerson-essays-034-p01.core_idea: Reform yourself before reforming the world

emerson-essays-034-p02.plain: I can't spend my time irritably attacking. If I left church at every false sentiment, I'd never stay five minutes. But why leave? The street is just as false, and in my own manners and speech the lie remains.
emerson-essays-034-p02.core_idea: Falsehood is everywhere, even in ourselves

emerson-essays-034-p03.plain: Friendship and grand alliances are fine, but no society can be as large as one person. In natural friendships a person multiplies himself; once he pledges himself to a group, he shrinks below the size of one.
emerson-essays-034-p03.core_idea: No society is larger than one whole person

emerson-essays-034-p04.plain: Two people cannot be in harmony when one person is not in harmony with himself: when thoughts and actions, faith and habits, reason and senses pull apart, like rowing forward with one hand and backward with the other.
emerson-essays-034-p04.core_idea: Inner harmony must come before harmony with others

emerson-essays-035-p01.plain: People are better than they seem. They enjoy flattery for a moment but know the truth. It is foolish cowardice not to trust them with blunt truth; they'll resent your honesty briefly and thank you forever.
emerson-essays-035-p01.core_idea: Tell people the truth; they will thank you

emerson-essays-035-p02.plain: What do we truly want from each other? Not flattery, but to be exposed and shamed out of our nonsense, made real instead of ghosts. Tired of drifting through an unreal world, we crave reality, even through pain.
emerson-essays-035-p02.core_idea: We crave reality and truth, even if painful

emerson-essays-035-p03.plain: We cherish those who love us, and time with them makes up for much misery. But those who reject us as unworthy matter even more: they show us a higher life and stir new powers to attempt new things.
emerson-essays-035-p03.core_idea: Those who reject us push us to grow

judge.issue: Drops 'build a heaven we had not dreamed' and powers from the spirit's recesses.

emerson-essays-035-p04.plain: We are frozen by fear, clinging to house, land, job and money because they have fed us, though we admit our real life does not flow through them. We long to be set on fire and made useful.
emerson-essays-035-p04.core_idea: Fear makes us cling to possessions instead of greatness

judge.issue: Drops 'we desire to be made great'; fire image flattened.

emerson-essays-036-p01.plain: The best people believe that, in sum, one person is worth about the same as another. Each excels in something, and each weakness is compensated, since every limitation concentrates a person's strength.
emerson-essays-036-p01.core_idea: Every weakness concentrates strength somewhere else

judge.issue: Loses that lack of skill elsewhere increases fitness for one's own work.

emerson-essays-036-p02.plain: Once you see that a higher will governs everything without exception, you grow calm. The earth carries us safely without our help; our own path is our only job, and we needn't manage the universe.
emerson-essays-036-p02.core_idea: Tend your own orbit; the universe runs itself

emerson-essays-036-p03.plain: Don't rush to expose the false reputations of prominent people. They are working harder at revealing themselves and will succeed. Hold back your criticism for a few days, and their inadequacy will be plain to everyone.
emerson-essays-036-p03.core_idea: Pretenders expose themselves without your help

emerson-essays-036-p04.plain: Living amid wonder, we owe cheer, courage and aspiration. The wise marvel at the ordinary. Having received so much, the heart can trust the Power and the Soul that guide it, sure the future will match the past.
emerson-essays-036-p04.core_idea: Wonder at the ordinary and trust the guiding Soul

judge.issue: Drops wise-versus-unwise contrast detail and 'quit other leadings'; question made assertion.

emerson-essays-037-p01.plain: Everywhere we are close to the best. We put off our hopes, and that delay is the root of idleness and crime; while waiting, we kill time with jokes, sleep, eating and wrongdoing.
emerson-essays-037-p01.core_idea: Deferring our hopes breeds idleness and wrongdoing

judge.issue: Drops point that laboured feats seem pointless before bursting into universal power.

emerson-essays-037-p02.plain: A person who prizes his own talent finds, out in the wider world, that others have different gifts and he is useless in their places. Every gift gets its turn, and we all take turns at the top.
emerson-essays-037-p02.core_idea: Every talent has its turn; we all rotate

judge.issue: Drops the arc of early modesty turning to self-flattery.

emerson-essays-038-p01.plain: If one person were perfect, there would be no need for the rest of us. As long as anyone exists, he is needed for something, so let him stand up for his own part.
emerson-essays-038-p01.core_idea: Everyone alive is needed for something

emerson-essays-038-p02.plain: When you criticise a great mind, you are probably attacking your own caricature of it. Every person has something infinite in them, a channel of heaven, so criticising them can amount to cutting off your own soul.
emerson-essays-038-p02.core_idea: Criticising others often wounds your own soul

judge.issue: Drops the infinite in genius sporting with the critic's limitations.

emerson-essays-038-p03.plain: The world's secret is that nothing truly dies; things only step out of sight for a while and then come back.
emerson-essays-038-p03.core_idea: Nothing dies; things withdraw and return

emerson-essays-038-p04.plain: Love reveals nature's riches by showing hidden worth in a friend, suggesting equal good everywhere. As a good fruit costs no more effort than a poor one, I want only the best in work, speech, thought and friends.
emerson-essays-038-p04.core_idea: Love reveals hidden worth; settle only for the best

emerson-essays-038-p05.plain: If only we were safe from moods! Even sincere teachers soon disown what they passionately preached, and we keep shifting our viewpoint. Knowing there are always other moods, I am never wholly sincere.
emerson-essays-038-p05.core_idea: Shifting moods make every conviction unstable

judge.issue: Compresses the prophets-recanting image heavily; core kept.

emerson-essays-038-p06.plain: We can speak frankly and fully yet leave feeling nothing was said, because people cannot truly know each other. When a companion assumes he knows my mind, endless explanation leaves us exactly where we began.
emerson-essays-038-p06.core_idea: Assuming we understand each other blocks real understanding

emerson-essays-039-p01.plain: The daydreams of sincere people foretell the future. What a sensitive young person privately imagines but fears to say becomes public resolutions, then a cause fought over, then established law for a century, until new dreams replace it.
emerson-essays-039-p01.core_idea: Today's private dreams become tomorrow's laws

emerson-essays-040-p01.plain: While I govern myself, my neighbour and I can often work together. But when I try to direct him too, I overstep and the relationship becomes false; even if he cannot protest, it is a lie that hurts us both.
emerson-essays-040-p01.core_idea: Controlling others creates false, harmful relationships

emerson-essays-040-p02.plain: If I put myself in my child's place and we see things together, that shared understanding guides us both. But if I guess at his situation from outside and give orders, he will never obey me.
emerson-essays-040-p02.core_idea: Shared understanding guides; outside orders fail

emerson-essays-040-p03.plain: Knowing we fall short of the great character we owe, we show off some small talent as a substitute. It may impress others, but it doesn't calm us or give us real strength; we carry a quiet penance.
emerson-essays-040-p03.core_idea: Showing off talent cannot replace real character

emerson-essays-040-p04.plain: No one would choose to be a fraud if they could afford to be honest.
emerson-essays-040-p04.core_idea: People fake it only when honesty feels unaffordable

emerson-essays-041-p01.plain: Every person has a right to work, to be trusted, loved and honoured. A state founded on the power of love has never yet been attempted.
emerson-essays-041-p01.core_idea: A state built on love has never been tried

emerson-essays-041-p02.plain: Time arrives feeling open and sacred, then gets chopped into trivial chores, errands, headaches, taxes, tiresome dealings and the sting of awkward words. Whatever we do, life brings its petty annoyances, like flies in summer.
emerson-essays-041-p02.core_idea: Petty chores and annoyances eat up our time

emerson-essays-041-p03.plain: Every simple, innocent act yields some wisdom. A homebody who loves the ticking clock and the crackle of logs on the fire has comforts others never imagine.
emerson-essays-041-p03.core_idea: Simple domestic life holds quiet wisdom and comfort

emerson-essays-041-p04.plain: If you keep a law, any law, your path will be full of satisfactions. Pleasures differ more in quality than in quantity.
emerson-essays-041-p04.core_idea: Living by a law brings satisfaction

emerson-essays-042-p01.plain: To be good, words and actions must come at the right time. Sharpening a scythe sounds cheerful in June, but the same sound is lonely and sad when it is too late to make hay.
emerson-essays-042-p01.core_idea: Good words and deeds must be timely

emerson-essays-042-p02.plain: Every lie harms the liar and the health of society; even a profitable lie is later heavily taxed by events. Frankness invites frankness. Trust people and they will be true to you; treat them greatly and they will show greatness.
emerson-essays-042-p02.core_idea: Honesty and trust bring out the best in others

judge.issue: Softens 'suicide in the liar'; drops frankness making business a friendship.

emerson-essays-042-p03.plain: Anyone who wants peace of mind must steel his resolve. Face the thing you fear most, and your firmness will usually show the fear was groundless. As the Latin proverb says, the eye is beaten first in battle.
emerson-essays-042-p03.core_idea: Face your worst fear and it shrinks

emerson-essays-042-p04.plain: In quarrels with neighbours, fear exaggerates the other side, and it gives bad advice. Everyone feels weak inside and looks strong to others. You fear him, and he fears you; up close, bullies are timid.
emerson-essays-042-p04.core_idea: Those you fear are just as afraid of you

judge.issue: Drops peace kept because one is afraid and the other dares not.

emerson-essays-043-p01.plain: Love is said to be blind, but kindness actually helps us see. When you meet an opponent, ignore the dividing lines and meet on whatever common ground remains; it will widen fast until the barriers dissolve.
emerson-essays-043-p01.core_idea: Meet opponents on common ground and barriers melt

emerson-essays-043-p02.plain: We hold back from closeness with the people around us, as if waiting for something better. But tomorrow will be like today, and life slips away while we prepare to live. Let us enjoy the affections near us.
emerson-essays-043-p02.core_idea: Life wastes while we wait; cherish nearby affections

judge.issue: Drops friends dying off and being too old for new patronage.

emerson-essays-043-p03.plain: A person is his own guiding star; an honest, complete soul commands all light and fate, and nothing comes to him too early or too late. Our deeds, good or bad, are our angels and shadows that stay with us.
emerson-essays-043-p03.core_idea: Our own acts shape our fate

emerson-essays-043-p04.plain: Watch the flashes of insight in your own mind more than famous poets and sages. We dismiss our thoughts because they're ours, then meet them in great works. Hold to your own impressions, or a stranger will voice them first.
emerson-essays-043-p04.core_idea: Trust your own insights before others voice them

judge.issue: Drops holding impressions with good-humoured inflexibility against the crowd, and the shame.

emerson-essays-043-p05.plain: In time everyone learns that envy is ignorance and imitation is suicide; you must accept yourself as you are, and good comes only through work on your own plot. Your power is new, and you only discover it by trying.
emerson-essays-043-p05.core_idea: Accept yourself; your power is found by trying

emerson-essays-043-p06.plain: We only half express ourselves, ashamed of the divine idea each of us embodies, but God won't have his work shown by cowards. You feel relieved and glad after putting your heart into your work; anything less gives no peace.
emerson-essays-043-p06.core_idea: Wholehearted effort brings peace; half-effort does not

judge.issue: Drops the idea trusted if faithfully imparted, and genius deserting the half-hearted.

emerson-essays-043-p07.plain: Trust yourself. Accept the place divine providence has given you, as great men did, sensing that what is fully trustworthy works within them. We must accept that same high destiny, not as cowards or invalids but as guides, redeemers and benefactors, obeying the Almighty and advancing on chaos.
emerson-essays-043-p07.core_idea: Trust yourself and accept your providential place
emerson-essays-043-p07.plain_v1: Trust yourself; every heart responds to that. Accept the place, people and times divine providence has given you, as great men did, trusting what works within them. We must take up that destiny boldly, not as cowards hiding.

judge_v1.issue: Drops 'obeying the Almighty effort' and the call to be guides, redeemers, benefactors.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the call to be guides, redeemers and benefactors advancing on chaos.

emerson-essays-043-p08.plain: Society everywhere conspires against the independence of its members. It is like a company where people trade their freedom for security. Its favourite virtue is conformity; it hates self-reliance and prefers names and customs to real creators.
emerson-essays-043-p08.core_idea: Society demands conformity and resists self-reliance

emerson-essays-043-p09.plain: To be truly a person you must be a nonconformist and test whether what is called good really is. Nothing is finally sacred except the integrity of your own mind. Clear yourself with yourself, and the world will agree.
emerson-essays-043-p09.core_idea: Nothing is sacred but your mind's integrity

emerson-essays-043-p10.plain: I'm ashamed of how easily we give in to titles, big organisations and dead institutions. Any polite, well-spoken person sways me more than they should. I ought to stand upright and speak the plain truth in every way.
emerson-essays-043-p10.core_idea: Stop deferring to titles; speak plain truth

emerson-essays-043-p11.plain: Goodness needs some sharpness to it; otherwise it isn't goodness at all.

emerson-essays-044-p01.plain: I want to live, not to atone or put on a show. I'd rather my life be modest and genuine than dazzling and unsteady. However small my gifts, I exist and need no outside proof of my worth.
emerson-essays-044-p01.core_idea: Live genuinely, not for show or approval

judge.issue: Drops refusing to judge the man by actions and paying for an intrinsic right.

emerson-essays-044-p02.plain: Only what I must do concerns me, not what people think. It's hard because others always think they know your duty better. The great person keeps, sweetly, the independence of solitude while in the middle of the crowd.
emerson-essays-044-p02.core_idea: Keep your independence even amid the crowd

judge.issue: Drops greatness/meanness distinction and the easy-in-world, easy-in-solitude contrast.

emerson-essays-044-p03.plain: Keeping up customs that mean nothing to you scatters your strength, wastes time and blurs who you are. Behind such screens I can't see the real you. Do your own work and I'll know you, and you'll strengthen yourself.
emerson-essays-044-p03.core_idea: Dead conformity scatters you; your own work reveals you

emerson-essays-044-p04.plain: One humiliating experience is the forced smile we wear among people we're uneasy with, answering talk that bores us. The face muscles, moved not naturally but by a cheap act of will, tighten unpleasantly.
emerson-essays-044-p04.core_idea: Forced smiles in company feel false and painful

emerson-essays-044-p05.plain: The world punishes nonconformity with disapproval, so you must judge a sour face rightly. The crowd's frowns, like its smiles, have no deep cause; they come and go with the wind and the newspapers.
emerson-essays-044-p05.core_idea: The crowd's disapproval is shallow and passing

judge.issue: Drops the condition: frowns rooted in real contempt would justify sadness.

emerson-essays-044-p06.plain: Another fear that stops self-trust is wanting to stay consistent with past words so others aren't disappointed. Why drag that corpse of memory around? If you contradict yourself, so what? Live in a new day.
emerson-essays-044-p06.core_idea: Don't let past words chain your present self

judge.issue: Drops bringing the past to judgment in the present rather than trusting memory.

emerson-essays-044-p07.plain: Foolish consistency is a bugbear of small minds; a great soul ignores it. Say plainly what you think today, and tomorrow say what you think then, even if it contradicts today. Being misunderstood is the lot of the great.
emerson-essays-044-p07.core_idea: To be great is to be misunderstood

judge.issue: 'To be great is to be misunderstood' loosened; drops named misunderstood figures.

emerson-essays-044-p08.plain: People see us as we truly are. Character speaks louder than our intentions. We think our virtues or vices show only in deeds, but they give off a breath every moment.
emerson-essays-044-p08.core_idea: Character shows constantly, not only in actions

emerson-essays-044-p09.plain: Even the best ship sails a zigzag course, yet from far enough away the line looks straight. Your genuine actions will explain one another; conformity explains nothing. Act sincerely, and your past sincere acts will back you up.
emerson-essays-044-p09.core_idea: Genuine actions add up to a straight course

judge.issue: 'Act singly' rendered 'act sincerely', losing the sense of acting alone and independently.

emerson-essays-044-p10.plain: If I can do right today and ignore who's watching, it's because past right actions now support me. Whatever happens, do right now. Character builds up over time; all the good days before add their strength to this one.
emerson-essays-044-p10.core_idea: Character is cumulative; do right now

judge.issue: Drops 'always scorn appearances and you always may'.

emerson-essays-044-p11.plain: Let us stop bowing and apologising. When an important man comes to dinner, I don't want to please him; I want him to want to please me. I'll stand for humanity, kindly if I can, but truthfully.
emerson-essays-044-p11.core_idea: Stop apologising; stand kind but true
