emerson-essays-044-p12.plain: So a person should know his worth and keep things in their place. He shouldn't sneak around like an outsider or an unwanted guest in a world that exists for him.
emerson-essays-044-p12.core_idea: Know your worth; you belong here

judge.issue: 'Keep things under his feet' softened to 'keep things in their place'.

emerson-essays-044-p13.plain: Kings and lords sound grander than ordinary people doing a day's work, but the substance of life is the same for both. Why revere famous rulers so much? Your private act today carries stakes as great as theirs.
emerson-essays-044-p13.core_idea: Ordinary acts matter as much as famous deeds

judge.issue: Drops 'did they wear out virtue?', the challenge to hero-worship.

emerson-essays-045-p02.plain: If we live truly, we will see truly. Being strong comes as naturally to the strong as weakness does to the weak.

emerson-essays-045-p03.plain: A soul lifted above passion sees the oneness and eternal cause of things, sees that Truth and Right exist in themselves, and grows calm knowing all things go well.
emerson-essays-045-p03.core_idea: Rising above passion brings calm trust

emerson-essays-045-p04.plain: Only living counts, not having lived. Power stops the moment we rest; it exists in the moment of moving from an old state to a new one, in leaping the gap, in darting at a goal.
emerson-essays-045-p04.core_idea: Power lives in transition, not rest

emerson-essays-045-p05.plain: Why take on the faults of friend, spouse, parent or child just because they share my home or blood? All people share my blood. That's no reason to adopt their bad temper or folly, or feel ashamed of it.
emerson-essays-045-p05.core_idea: Family ties don't oblige you to share faults

emerson-essays-045-p06.plain: Sometimes the whole world seems to pester you with urgent trifles: friends, clients, children, illness, fear, need all knock at once. Keep your composure and don't enter their confusion. Others can annoy me only through my own weak curiosity.
emerson-essays-045-p06.core_idea: Others disturb you only as you allow

judge.issue: Drops 'no man can come near me but through my act'.

emerson-essays-045-p07.plain: I appeal against your customs: I must be myself and can't keep breaking myself for others. If you can love me as I am, we'll be happier; if not, I'll still try to deserve it. I won't hide my tastes.
emerson-essays-045-p07.core_idea: Be yourself and let others love you as you are

emerson-essays-046-p01.plain: Our strength and courage seem drained away, and we have become timid, gloomy whiners. We fear truth, fortune, death and each other.
emerson-essays-046-p01.core_idea: We have become timid and afraid of everything

emerson-essays-046-p02.plain: Young people lose heart at their first failure. But a sturdy youth who tries trade after trade and always lands on his feet is worth a hundred pampered ones. He doesn't postpone life; he has a hundred chances, not one.
emerson-essays-046-p02.core_idea: Don't postpone life; failure leaves a hundred chances

judge.issue: Drops the disheartened graduate and living without shame at lacking a profession.

emerson-essays-046-p03.plain: Prayer that asks for a particular thing, anything less than all good, is corrupt. True prayer is viewing life's facts from the highest point of view, the joyful speech of a seeing soul, God's spirit declaring his works good.
emerson-essays-046-p03.core_idea: True prayer contemplates, it doesn't beg

emerson-essays-046-p04.plain: Discontent is a lack of self-reliance, a weakness of will. Grieve over disasters only if it helps the sufferer; otherwise get on with your own work, and the damage already begins to be repaired.
emerson-essays-046-p04.core_idea: Discontent is weak will; do your own work

emerson-essays-046-p05.plain: Travel is a fool's paradise. I imagine Naples or Rome will dazzle me and lift my sadness, but when I wake up there, the same sad self I fled is beside me. My giant goes with me wherever I go.
emerson-essays-046-p05.core_idea: You cannot travel away from yourself

judge.issue: Drops 'first journeys discover the indifference of places' and feigned enchantment.

emerson-essays-046-p06.plain: Insist on being yourself and never imitate. Your own gift carries a lifetime's development; a borrowed talent you only half own. What each person does best, only their Maker can teach them.
emerson-essays-046-p06.core_idea: Develop your own gift; never imitate

emerson-essays-047-p01.plain: The Caliph Ali said your share in life is already looking for you, so you can stop chasing after it and be at rest.
emerson-essays-047-p01.core_idea: Your lot is seeking you; rest

emerson-essays-047-p02.plain: Whoever sees that power is inborn, and that he was weak only from seeking good outside himself, and then trusts his own thought, instantly stands upright and works wonders, like a man on his feet rather than his head.
emerson-essays-047-p02.core_idea: Power is within; stop seeking it outside

emerson-essays-047-p03.plain: Good news, like a political win, more income, a sick person's recovery or a friend's return, lifts your spirits and you think good days are coming. Don't believe it. Only you, and the triumph of principles, can bring you peace.
emerson-essays-047-p03.core_idea: Nothing brings you peace but yourself

emerson-essays-047-p04.plain: When we reflect on our lives, we find them wrapped in beauty. Looking back, everything takes on a pleasing shape, like distant clouds; even tragic and dreadful things, and ordinary neglected ones, gain grace in memory.
emerson-essays-047-p04.core_idea: In memory, even hard things become beautiful

emerson-essays-047-p05.plain: Every loss and pain is particular; to the heart the universe stays unharmed. Troubles and disasters don't lessen our trust. No one has ever described his griefs as lightly as he could have.
emerson-essays-047-p05.core_idea: Pain is particular; the whole remains unhurt

emerson-essays-047-p06.plain: Nature doesn't want us to fret and fume. She cares little more for our good works and learning than for our frauds and wars. When we leave our busy meetings for the woods, she says, "So worked up, little sir?"
emerson-essays-047-p06.core_idea: Nature gently mocks our frantic busyness

emerson-essays-048-p01.plain: Everything teaches us faith; we need only obey. There is guidance for each of us, and by listening humbly we will hear the right word. Why agonise over choices? There is a right place and fitting work for you.
emerson-essays-048-p01.core_idea: Listen humbly; guidance and your place exist

emerson-essays-048-p02.plain: Everyone has a calling, and talent is the call. There is one direction open to each person, where obstacles fall away, like a ship in a river that finds its channel and sweeps calmly out to an endless sea.

emerson-essays-048-p03.plain: What a person does is what he truly has; why hope or fear? His strength is within. He should count as solid only the good that grows from his nature; fortune's gifts come and go like summer leaves.
emerson-essays-048-p03.core_idea: Only inner good is solid; fortune passes

judge.issue: Drops scattering fortune's goods as signs of one's infinite productiveness.

emerson-essays-048-p04.plain: Certain small memories of people and events stay with you far beyond their apparent importance. They relate to your gift, so give them weight instead of reaching for more usual examples. What your heart thinks great is great.
emerson-essays-048-p04.core_idea: What your heart finds great is great

emerson-essays-048-p05.plain: No one can learn what they aren't ready for, however close it is. God shields us from ideas that come too early. We can't see what's before us until the mind ripens; then the old blindness seems a dream.
emerson-essays-048-p05.core_idea: We learn only when we're ready

emerson-essays-049-p01.plain: In the Alps a traveller may see his own shadow swollen into a frightening giant. An old man told his sons, frightened by a shape in the dark, that they would never see anything worse than themselves.
emerson-essays-049-p01.core_idea: What frightens us is often our own shadow

emerson-essays-049-p02.plain: We wrongly think we must win friends by conforming to society's dress, manners and values. My only true friend is the soul I meet on my own path, neither of us bowing to the other, who shares my experience.
emerson-essays-049-p02.core_idea: True friends are met on your own path

judge.issue: Drops 'native of the same celestial latitude'; spiritual kinship flattened.

emerson-essays-049-p03.plain: A person gets the standing he claims. Take the place that is yours and everyone goes along. The world lets each of us set our own value, hero or fool, and accepts whatever measure we take of ourselves.
emerson-essays-049-p03.core_idea: The world accepts the value you set on yourself

judge.issue: Drops the closing contrast of sneaking versus work one with the stars.

emerson-essays-049-p04.plain: Michelangelo told a young sculptor not to worry much about the lighting on his statue; the light of the public square would show its worth.
emerson-essays-049-p04.core_idea: Real worth is tested in the open

emerson-essays-049-p05.plain: A person is taken for what he is worth. It's pointless to wonder what others think of us, and just as pointless to fear staying unknown.
emerson-essays-049-p05.core_idea: Don't worry about others' opinion or obscurity

emerson-essays-050-p01.plain: No sincere word is ever completely lost. No generous act falls to the ground without some heart unexpectedly welcoming it.
emerson-essays-050-p01.core_idea: Sincere words and generosity always find a home

emerson-essays-050-p02.plain: When you visit a friend, don't waste it apologising for not coming sooner; just visit, letting the highest love reach him through you. Don't torment yourself over gifts not given. Be a gift yourself, shining with real light.
emerson-essays-050-p02.core_idea: Skip apologies; be a gift yourself

emerson-essays-050-p03.plain: Real action happens in quiet moments. Life's turning points aren't career, marriage or office, but a silent thought on a walk that revises how we live: you did this, but that would be better. Later years serve that thought.
emerson-essays-050-p03.core_idea: Life's turning points are quiet thoughts

emerson-essays-050-p04.plain: Why belittle who we are out of false modesty? A good person is content. I admire a great hero but don't wish to be him; being told he acted while I sit still won't trouble me. Both are good.
emerson-essays-050-p04.core_idea: Be content with who you are

judge.issue: Drops 'when the need is' condition and loving this hour's world over his.

emerson-essays-050-p05.plain: Let us find peace by being faithful to our duties. Why wander into history before answering my benefactors, or read of great campaigns before replying to my own letters? Much reading is a timid escape from our work.
emerson-essays-050-p05.core_idea: Do your own duties before gazing elsewhere

emerson-essays-050-p06.plain: Some hours of life carry more weight and lasting effect than others. Our faith comes in moments, while our faults are habits. Yet those brief moments have a depth that makes them feel more real than everything else.
emerson-essays-050-p06.core_idea: Brief moments of faith outweigh habitual faults

emerson-essays-050-p07.plain: A person is a stream with a hidden source; our being flows into us from somewhere unknown. No one can foresee the next moment. Every moment I must admit events come from something higher than my own will.
emerson-essays-050-p07.core_idea: Our lives flow from a source beyond our will

emerson-essays-051-p01.plain: We live in sequences, divisions and fragments. Yet within each person is the soul of the whole: the wise silence, the universal beauty to which every part is equally related, the eternal One.
emerson-essays-051-p01.core_idea: Within us lives the soul of the whole

emerson-essays-051-p02.plain: A light shines through us onto things and shows us we are nothing, the light is everything. A person is the front of a temple in which all wisdom and goodness live.
emerson-essays-051-p02.core_idea: A light within us is everything

emerson-essays-051-p03.plain: Our true youth and age aren't measured from birth. Some thoughts, like love of eternal beauty, always find us young and keep us so. In sickness or weariness, a line of poetry or a deep sentence refreshes us beyond time.
emerson-essays-051-p03.core_idea: Great thoughts keep us young beyond time

judge.issue: Drops the intellect redeeming us from time and Plato/Shakespeare bringing longevity.

emerson-essays-051-p04.plain: We know better than we act. We don't yet fully own ourselves, yet we know we are much more than we seem.
emerson-essays-051-p04.core_idea: We are more than we yet live

emerson-essays-051-p05.plain: With my child, learning and money are useless; only soul counts. If I'm wilful, he resists and I win only by force. If the soul judges between us, the same soul looks from his eyes, and he loves with me.
emerson-essays-051-p05.core_idea: Lead a child by soul, not will

judge.issue: Drops renouncing my will; 'reveres and loves' reduced to 'loves'.

emerson-essays-052-p01.plain: We are wiser than we know. If we don't interfere with our thinking and see how things stand in God, we know each thing and every person, because the Maker of all stands behind us and sees through us.
emerson-essays-052-p01.core_idea: We are wiser than we know

judge.issue: 'Dread omniscience' softened to 'sees through us'; drops 'act entirely'.

emerson-essays-052-p02.plain: Don't demand a description of the lands you're sailing to. A description can't really show them; tomorrow you'll arrive and know them by living there.
emerson-essays-052-p02.core_idea: You'll know the future by living it

emerson-essays-052-p03.plain: Our craving to know the future confesses sin, and God gives no answer. The veil over tomorrow comes not from God's decree but from human nature: the soul lets us read only cause and effect, teaching us to live today. Drop idle curiosity, work and live, and the answer comes.
emerson-essays-052-p03.core_idea: The future is veiled so we live today

judge.issue: Flattens 'question and answer are one' into 'the answer comes'.

emerson-essays-052-p03.plain_v1: Our hungry questions about the future betray a fault; God gives them no answer. Our nature veils tomorrow so we learn to live today. Drop idle curiosity, work and live, and the growing soul makes question and answer one.

judge_v1.issue: Softens 'confession of sin' to 'fault'; drops cause-and-effect veil and not God's decree.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Softens 'confession of sin' to 'a fault'; drops that the veil is not an arbitrary decree.

emerson-essays-052-p04.plain: We teach what we are, without meaning to. Thoughts enter and leave our minds by paths we never deliberately opened. Character teaches over our heads.
emerson-essays-052-p04.core_idea: We teach what we are, involuntarily

emerson-essays-053-p01.plain: Deal so plainly with people that they must be completely sincere with you and can't hope to trifle with you. That is the highest compliment you can give.
emerson-essays-053-p01.core_idea: Plain dealing is the highest compliment

emerson-essays-053-p02.plain: How dear and soothing the thought of God is to us, filling lonely places and wiping away the scars of our mistakes and disappointments.
emerson-essays-053-p02.core_idea: The thought of God comforts and heals

emerson-essays-053-p03.plain: What is truly yours comes to you. Seeking a friend, let your feet run, not your mind. If you miss him, accept it's for the best; the power in you is in him too, and would unite you if right.
emerson-essays-053-p03.core_idea: What is truly yours will come to you

emerson-essays-053-p04.plain: Believe that every word in the world you should hear will reach you. Every proverb or book meant to help or comfort you will find its way home, and every friend your tender heart truly longs for will embrace you.
emerson-essays-053-p04.core_idea: What you truly need will find you

emerson-essays-053-p05.plain: Faith that rests on authority isn't faith. Leaning on authority shows how far religion has declined and the soul has withdrawn.
emerson-essays-053-p05.core_idea: Faith based on authority is not faith

emerson-essays-053-p06.plain: Everyone lives by truth and needs to express it. In love, art, greed, politics, work and play, we try to voice our painful secret. A person is only half himself; the other half is his expression.
emerson-essays-053-p06.core_idea: We are only half ourselves without expression

emerson-essays-054-p01.plain: However often deceived, a person still waits for a companion who can hold him steady to a truth until he has made it his own.
emerson-essays-054-p01.core_idea: We long for someone to steady us in truth

emerson-essays-055-p01.plain: Even the plainest life gives enough experience to express any thought. Why crave new facts? Day and night, home and garden, a few books and actions serve as well as every trade and spectacle.

emerson-essays-056-p01.plain: A lost traveller drops the reins and trusts his horse's instinct to find the road; we should do the same with the divine instinct that carries us through this world.
emerson-essays-056-p01.core_idea: Trust the divine instinct that carries you

emerson-essays-056-p02.plain: You can never cheat nature with a trick. The Creator's calm presence doesn't answer to opium or wine; the great vision comes to a pure, simple soul in a clean body. Drug-made excitement is counterfeit, not inspiration.
emerson-essays-056-p02.core_idea: True inspiration comes to the pure, not intoxicated

emerson-essays-056-p03.plain: The spirit that satisfies quiet hearts, rising from dry grass and stones in the March sun, comes to the poor and simple. Fill your head with city fashion, greed and stimulants, and you'll find no wisdom in the lonely woods.
emerson-essays-056-p03.core_idea: Wisdom comes to quiet, simple hearts

emerson-essays-056-p04.plain: Like a lost shepherd dying in snow a few feet from his door, we are dying beside the waters of life and truth. We can't reach any thought but our present one; every thought, every heaven, is a prison.
emerson-essays-056-p04.core_idea: We perish within reach of truth

emerson-essays-057-p01.plain: Poet, don't doubt; persist. Say: it's in me and it will come out. Stand there, stuck and stammering, jeered at, and keep striving until that dream-power you glimpse each night breaks out, a power beyond all limits.
emerson-essays-057-p01.core_idea: Persist until what is in you comes out

judge.issue: Drops man as conductor of the whole river of electricity; power 'transcending privacy' lost.

emerson-essays-057-p02.plain: Wherever snow falls, water flows, birds fly, twilight comes, clouds or stars fill the sky, wherever there is danger, awe and love, there is Beauty, plentiful as rain, poured out for you. No place on earth is unfit for it.
emerson-essays-057-p02.core_idea: Beauty is everywhere, poured out for you

epictetus-discourses-long-001-p01.plain: I must die, but must I die complaining? I must be chained, but must I also lament? I must go into exile, but can anyone stop me going with smiles, cheer and contentment?
epictetus-discourses-long-001-p01.core_idea: No one can force you to meet fate lamenting

epictetus-discourses-long-001-p02.plain: Since I'm naturally slow, should I not bother trying? Of course not. I'll never be the strongest or richest man, yet I still care for my body and property; we don't neglect anything just because we can't reach the top.
epictetus-discourses-long-001-p02.core_idea: Don't neglect effort because you can't be the best

judge.issue: Drops the Socrates comparison: not inferior to him is enough.

epictetus-discourses-long-001-p03.plain: You call yourself a poor wretch with a miserable bit of flesh. Wretched, yes, but you have something better than your flesh. Why neglect the better part and cling to this?
epictetus-discourses-long-001-p03.core_idea: You have something better than your body

epictetus-discourses-long-002-p01.plain: Haven't you been given greatness of soul, courage and endurance? If I have greatness of soul, why worry about anything that might happen? What could disturb me? Shall I not use these powers as intended, instead of grieving over events?
epictetus-discourses-long-002-p01.core_idea: Use your inner powers instead of lamenting

epictetus-discourses-long-002-p02.plain: You won't endure and you're discontent: alone, you call it loneliness; with people, you call them crooks; you blame family and neighbours. Instead, call solitude peace and freedom, like the gods, and call company a festival, and accept everything contentedly.
epictetus-discourses-long-002-p02.core_idea: Rename your situation and accept it contentedly

epictetus-discourses-long-003-p01.plain: Epictetus said nothing great happens suddenly, not even a grape or a fig. A fig must flower, fruit, then ripen. If a fig takes time, how could you expect the fruit of a person's mind to come quickly and easily?

epictetus-discourses-long-003-p02.plain: Why do we get angry? Because we value so much what people take from us. Don't prize your clothes, and you won't be angry at the thief.
epictetus-discourses-long-003-p02.core_idea: Value things less and anger fades

epictetus-discourses-long-003-p03.plain: When a thief stole the iron lamp beside my household gods, I reflected that he had done nothing strange. Tomorrow I'll have a clay lamp instead; you can only lose what you have.
epictetus-discourses-long-003-p03.core_idea: We can only lose what we have

epictetus-discourses-long-003-p04.plain: When your head or ear hurts, don't cry 'alas'. You may groan aloud, but don't groan inwardly. If help is slow, don't torment yourself saying everyone hates you; who wouldn't dislike someone who behaves like that?
epictetus-discourses-long-003-p04.core_idea: Bear pain without inner complaint or self-pity

epictetus-discourses-long-003-p05.plain: What is free by nature can't be disturbed or hindered by anything except itself. It is a person's own opinions that disturb him.
epictetus-discourses-long-003-p05.core_idea: Our own opinions are what disturb us

epictetus-discourses-long-004-p01.plain: Difficulties show what people are. When one comes, remember God, like a wrestling trainer, has matched you with a tough opponent so you can become a champion, which takes sweat. No difficulty is more useful, if you use it.
epictetus-discourses-long-004-p01.core_idea: Difficulties are God's training for your strength

judge.issue: Generalises 'no man had a more profitable difficulty than you' to all difficulties.

epictetus-discourses-long-004-p02.plain: Keep what is yours and don't crave what is others'. Your integrity and sense of shame are your own; who but you can take them or stop you using them? Yet chasing what isn't yours, you lose what is.
epictetus-discourses-long-004-p02.core_idea: Chasing others' things costs you your own

epictetus-discourses-long-004-p03.plain: Prizing my body or possessions makes me a slave, showing where I can be caught. Like a snake guarding its head, whatever you guard is where your master will strike. Knowing this, whom will you flatter or fear?
epictetus-discourses-long-004-p03.core_idea: What you cling to becomes your weak point

epictetus-discourses-long-004-p04.plain: It is we, or rather our opinions, that squeeze and trap us. What does insulting a stone achieve? If a person listens like a stone, the insulter gains nothing; he only succeeds by using the weakness of the one insulted.
epictetus-discourses-long-004-p04.core_idea: Insults only work through our own weakness

epictetus-discourses-long-004-p05.plain: Show me a place death never visits, or a charm against it. If there is none, what then? I can't escape death, but can't I escape fearing it, rather than die lamenting and trembling?
epictetus-discourses-long-004-p05.core_idea: You can't escape death, but you can escape fearing it

epictetus-discourses-long-005-p01.plain: God has set this law: if you want anything good, get it from yourself. You insist on getting it from someone else. Don't; get it from yourself.
epictetus-discourses-long-005-p01.core_idea: All good must come from yourself

epictetus-discourses-long-006-p01.plain: Freedom is simply the power to live as we choose. No one wants to live in error, fear, sorrow or turmoil, so no one living that way is free; whoever is rid of them is rid of slavery too.
epictetus-discourses-long-006-p01.core_idea: Freedom means release from fear and sorrow

epictetus-discourses-long-006-p02.plain: Things themselves don't matter, but how we use them does. To stay calm yet careful, act like a dice player: the dice and counters don't matter and I can't know the throw, but using the throw skilfully is my job.
epictetus-discourses-long-006-p02.core_idea: You can't control the throw, only its use

epictetus-discourses-long-006-p03.plain: Treat life like a voyage: I choose the captain, crew and day. In a storm, my part is done; the rest is the captain's. If the ship sinks, I won't drown fearful or blame God; I pass like an hour.
epictetus-discourses-long-006-p03.core_idea: Do your part, then accept what follows

extension.text: But we should act as we do in the case of a voyage. What can I do? I can choose the master of the ship, the sailors, the day, the opportunity. Then comes a storm. What more have I to care for? for my part is done. The business belongs to another, the master. But the ship is sinking--what then have I to do? I do the only thing that I can, not to be drowned full of fear, nor screaming nor blaming God, but knowing that what has been produced must also perish: for I am not an immortal being, but a man, a part of the whole, as an hour is a part of the day: I must be present like the hour, and past like the hour.

judge.issue: Drops knowing what is produced must perish, being mortal and part of the whole.

epictetus-discourses-long-007-p01.plain: Always remember what is yours and what belongs to someone else, and nothing will disturb you.
epictetus-discourses-long-007-p01.core_idea: Know what is yours and stay undisturbed

epictetus-discourses-long-007-p02.plain: You are something higher: a fragment of God, carrying a portion of him within you. Why then are you unaware of your noble origin? Why don't you know where you came from?
epictetus-discourses-long-007-p02.core_idea: You carry a portion of God within

epictetus-discourses-long-007-p03.plain: Each skill is kept up by practising it, and ruined by its opposite. Likewise modest, faithful acts preserve the modest and faithful person, while shameless, faithless, abusive, angry or greedy acts strengthen those very traits.
epictetus-discourses-long-007-p03.core_idea: What we repeatedly do shapes our character

epictetus-discourses-long-008-p01.plain: Storing bread and wine is different from eating them. What is eaten becomes muscle, flesh, blood and health. What is merely stored can be shown off when you like, but its only benefit is looking as if you have it.
epictetus-discourses-long-008-p01.core_idea: Knowledge must be digested, not just stored

epictetus-discourses-long-008-p02.plain: As a brother, give way, be easily persuaded, speak well of him, never fight him over things outside your will, and so gain more of what is within it. Trading a lettuce or seat for good character is a bargain.
epictetus-discourses-long-008-p02.core_idea: Yield outward things to gain good character

epictetus-discourses-long-008-p03.plain: Shall I not hurt someone who hurt me? First consider what hurt is. If good and evil lie in our will, then you are saying: since he harmed himself by wronging me, shall I harm myself by wronging him?

epictetus-discourses-long-009-p01.plain: When someone is anxious, ask what he wants; only wanting what's beyond his control makes him anxious. A lute player alone is calm, but in the theatre he is anxious, because he wants applause, which isn't in his power.
epictetus-discourses-long-009-p01.core_idea: Anxiety comes from wanting what we can't control

epictetus-discourses-long-009-p02.plain: Socrates' first and chief trait was never to get irritated in argument or say anything abusive or insulting, but to bear with abusive people and end the quarrel.
epictetus-discourses-long-009-p02.core_idea: Never be provoked; end the quarrel

epictetus-discourses-long-009-p03.plain: A guide who finds someone lost leads him to the right road; he doesn't mock him and walk off. Show the ignorant person the truth and he will follow. Until you can, don't ridicule him; recognise your own inability instead.
epictetus-discourses-long-009-p03.core_idea: Guide the mistaken; don't mock them

epictetus-discourses-long-010-p01.plain: What do we admire and busy ourselves with? External things. So why wonder that we are afraid and anxious? When we think what's coming is bad, we cannot help being fearful and anxious.
epictetus-discourses-long-010-p01.core_idea: Valuing externals breeds fear and anxiety

epictetus-discourses-long-010-p02.plain: The divine law: keep to your own, don't claim others' things, use what is given, don't crave what isn't, give back readily what is taken, and be thankful for the time you had it, rather than cry like a child.
epictetus-discourses-long-010-p02.core_idea: Use what is given; release it with thanks

epictetus-discourses-long-010-p03.plain: You long to see Athens and the Acropolis again? Aren't you content with what you see every day: sun, moon, stars, earth and sea? If you understand Him who governs everything and carry him within, why crave pretty stones?
epictetus-discourses-long-010-p03.core_idea: The daily world is wonder enough

epictetus-discourses-long-010-p04.plain: Every habit grows by matching actions: walking by walking, reading by reading. Stop for a month, or lie in bed ten days, and you feel the weakening. To build a habit, do it; to break one, do something else instead.
epictetus-discourses-long-010-p04.core_idea: Habits grow by doing and fade by stopping

epictetus-discourses-long-010-p05.plain: If you don't want to be quick-tempered, don't feed the habit. Stay calm and count the days without anger: every day, then every second, third, fourth. After thirty days, give thanks to God. The habit weakens, then disappears.
epictetus-discourses-long-010-p05.core_idea: Starve anger and count the calm days

judge.issue: 'Make a sacrifice to God' softened to 'give thanks to God'.

epictetus-discourses-long-011-p01.plain: Don't be swept away by a sudden impression; tell it to wait while you test it. Don't let it paint vivid pictures of what follows; replace it with a noble impression. Practise this and you'll find real strength.
epictetus-discourses-long-011-p01.core_idea: Test impressions before letting them carry you

epictetus-discourses-long-011-p02.plain: The struggle is great and the work divine: it is for self-mastery, freedom, happiness and calm. Call on God for help, as sailors pray in a storm; no storm is worse than violent impressions that drive out reason.
epictetus-discourses-long-011-p02.core_idea: Call on God against storms of impression

judge.issue: 'Kingship' rendered 'self-mastery'; Dioscuri invocation generalised to praying.

epictetus-discourses-long-011-p03.plain: Friendship exists only where there is faithfulness, modesty and a sharing of honest things, and nothing else.
epictetus-discourses-long-011-p03.core_idea: Friendship rests on fidelity and honesty

epictetus-discourses-long-012-p01.plain: People act like a traveller heading home who stops at a pleasant inn and stays there. You've forgotten your purpose: you were passing through, not travelling to it. Many inns and meadows are pleasant, but only to pass through.
epictetus-discourses-long-012-p01.core_idea: Don't mistake a pleasant stop for the goal

epictetus-discourses-long-012-p02.plain: Thank God for sight, hearing, life itself and what sustains it, food, wine and oil. But remember he has given you something better than all these: the power to use them, test them and judge the worth of each.
epictetus-discourses-long-012-p02.core_idea: The power to judge things is God's best gift

epictetus-discourses-long-013-p02.plain: What are weeping and lamenting, bad luck, strife, blame and accusation? Opinions, nothing more: opinions that treat things outside our will as if they were good or bad.
epictetus-discourses-long-013-p02.core_idea: Our troubles are opinions about externals

epictetus-discourses-long-014-p01.plain: Your ship is lost; that is what happened. A man was taken to prison; that is what happened. That it went badly for him is something each person adds from his own opinion.
epictetus-discourses-long-014-p01.core_idea: Events are neutral; we add the misfortune

epictetus-discourses-long-014-p02.plain: Before you sleep, review each of the day's actions: what went wrong, what you did, what you left undone. Go through all of it, then blame what was wrong and rejoice in what was right.

epictetus-discourses-long-014-p03.plain: Now it's time for fever, thirst or hunger: bear each well. Isn't that in your power? A doctor can stop you drinking or eating, but no one can stop you bearing thirst and hunger well.
epictetus-discourses-long-014-p03.core_idea: No one can stop you bearing hardship well

epictetus-discourses-long-014-p04.plain: My brother shouldn't have treated me like this. True, but that's his concern; however he behaves, I will act toward him as I should. My conduct is my business and no one can prevent it; his can be hindered.
epictetus-discourses-long-014-p04.core_idea: Others' conduct is theirs; yours is yours

epictetus-discourses-long-015-p01.plain: Loneliness is the state of feeling helpless. Being alone doesn't make you lonely, and being among many doesn't prevent it. When we lose a brother, son or friend we leaned on, we feel left alone even in a crowded city.
epictetus-discourses-long-015-p01.core_idea: Loneliness is helplessness, not being alone

epictetus-discourses-long-015-p02.plain: Still, a person should be ready for being alone too, able to be enough for himself and to be his own companion.
epictetus-discourses-long-015-p02.core_idea: Learn to be your own companion

epictetus-discourses-long-015-p03.plain: Like bad actors who can only sing in a chorus, some people can't walk alone. If you're anything, walk alone and talk to yourself; don't hide in the crowd. Look around, rouse yourself, and find out who you are.
epictetus-discourses-long-015-p03.core_idea: Step out of the crowd and know yourself

epictetus-discourses-long-015-p04.plain: Before any act, consider what comes before and after it, then proceed. If you don't, you'll start eagerly without thinking ahead, and when the consequences appear you'll give up shamefully.
epictetus-discourses-long-015-p04.core_idea: Consider the consequences before you begin

epictetus-discourses-long-015-p05.plain: If you often socialise with others, you will either become like them or change them. Put a dead coal beside a burning one: either the dead one puts out the other, or the live one lights it.
epictetus-discourses-long-015-p05.core_idea: Company either shapes you or is shaped by you

epictetus-discourses-long-015-p06.plain: My wife treats me badly, my father gives me nothing: that is all that happened. Calling it evil is a false addition. So rid yourself not of poverty but of your opinion of it, and you will be happy.
epictetus-discourses-long-015-p06.core_idea: Drop the opinion, not the hardship

epictetus-discourses-long-016-p01.plain: Who can force you to agree with what seems false? No one. Who can force you to deny what seems true? No one. So you can see there is something in you that is free by nature.

epictetus-discourses-long-016-p02.plain: Don't let what goes against nature in someone else become an evil for you. You were made by nature not to be downcast or unhappy along with others, but to be happy with them.
epictetus-discourses-long-016-p02.core_idea: Others' wrongs need not make you unhappy

epictetus-discourses-long-016-p03.plain: If friends die far away, they have only met the common fate of mortals. You cannot wish to live to old age and also never see anyone you love die.
epictetus-discourses-long-016-p03.core_idea: Living long means seeing loved ones die

epictetus-discourses-long-017-p01.plain: Remind yourself that anyone you love is mortal and not truly yours; they are given for a season, like a fig. Wanting your child or friend when that is not allowed is wanting a fig in winter.
epictetus-discourses-long-017-p01.core_idea: Loved ones are lent for a season, not owned

epictetus-discourses-long-017-p02.plain: Calling death a bad omen is like calling falling leaves or ripening grapes one. These are changes, not destruction; death is a larger change, into something that does not yet exist.
epictetus-discourses-long-017-p02.core_idea: Death is a change of state, not destruction

judge.issue: Drops change as a 'fixed economy and administration'; leaving home as small change.

epictetus-discourses-long-017-p03.plain: It is a strong thing to be able to say: I knew my son was mortal. Likewise say: I knew I am mortal, and could lose my home or be imprisoned.
epictetus-discourses-long-017-p03.core_idea: Expect loss, and it will not surprise you

epictetus-discourses-long-017-p04.plain: If you have given up the struggle for a good life, you can start again at once, without waiting. Each time you give up you can renew it, and one victory makes you like one who never quit.
epictetus-discourses-long-017-p04.core_idea: You can always begin the struggle again

epictetus-discourses-long-018-p01.plain: Can something be shameful to you that you did not do or cause, like a fever? If your parents were poor or left their property to others, is that your shame?
epictetus-discourses-long-018-p01.core_idea: You are not shamed by what you did not do

epictetus-discourses-long-018-p02.plain: Why grieve? Fear comes from what you expect, and grief from what is already present.
epictetus-discourses-long-018-p02.core_idea: Fear looks ahead; grief comes from the present

epictetus-discourses-long-019-p01.plain: Do not stay so close to old friends that you sink to their habits, or you will ruin yourself. Changing has a cost: you must choose between being loved as before and being better but not treated the same.
epictetus-discourses-long-019-p01.core_idea: Growing may cost you old friendships

epictetus-discourses-long-019-p02.plain: When you lose something external, ask what you gained in its place. If it is worth more, such as calm or modesty instead of money or idle talk, do not call it a loss.
epictetus-discourses-long-019-p02.core_idea: Count what you gain, not only what you lose

epictetus-discourses-long-019-p03.plain: Not only the desire for power and riches makes us servile, but also the desire for calm, leisure, travel or learning. Whatever outside thing we prize puts us under others' control.
epictetus-discourses-long-019-p03.core_idea: Valuing any external thing makes you dependent

epictetus-discourses-long-020-p01.plain: If you have lessened your bad temper, harsh words, haste or laziness, you can celebrate every day for each good act. That is a greater reason for celebration than high office.

judge.issue: 'Making sacrifices' rendered as celebration; drops no longer being moved as before.

epictetus-discourses-long-020-p02.plain: A neighbour throws stones and breaks your things; you did nothing wrong, and you are not an object but a free will. Only a wolf bites back; look at the human faculties you were given instead of revenge.
epictetus-discourses-long-020-p02.core_idea: Answer injury as a human, not a beast

epictetus-discourses-long-020-p03.plain: Afraid of being despised? Those who know you will not despise someone gentle and modest. As for those who do not know you, why care? No craftsman minds the opinion of people ignorant of his craft.
epictetus-discourses-long-020-p03.core_idea: Ignore the opinion of those who don't know you

epictetus-discourses-long-021-p01.plain: Another person's opinion of you is outside your will, so it is nothing to you. If it still upsets you, you have not really grasped what is good and evil.
epictetus-discourses-long-021-p01.core_idea: Others' opinions of you are not your concern

epictetus-discourses-long-021-p02.plain: Poverty, power or exile: I can bear any of them well. I was well not because of a place but because of my opinions, which no one can take from me, and with them I am content anywhere.
epictetus-discourses-long-021-p02.core_idea: Contentment comes from your opinions, not your place

judge.issue: Drops acting the poor man's part well and taking power with its trouble.

epictetus-discourses-long-021-p03.plain: When you see someone powerful or rich, consider what you have instead. If you do not crave power or riches, you possess more than they do and something worth far more.
epictetus-discourses-long-021-p03.core_idea: Not wanting riches is worth more than riches

judge.issue: Drops the condition: possessing nothing in place of riches makes you miserable.

epictetus-discourses-long-021-p04.plain: All human troubles are about external things. What shall I do? How will it turn out? These are the words of people fixed on things outside the power of their will.
epictetus-discourses-long-021-p04.core_idea: Anxiety comes from fixing on what you can't control

epictetus-discourses-long-022-p01.plain: What would you like to be doing when death finds you? I would want to be doing something worthy of a human being: kind, useful to all, noble.
epictetus-discourses-long-022-p01.core_idea: Be found doing something good when death comes

epictetus-discourses-long-022-p02.plain: A prayer to God: thank you for the life you gave; I am content to have used what is yours. Take it back and place it where you choose, for everything was yours.
epictetus-discourses-long-022-p02.core_idea: Give back your life to God with thanks

epictetus-discourses-long-022-p03.plain: If you relax your attention for a while, do not think you can recover it at will. Each lapse builds a habit of inattention and of putting it off, and so you keep pushing away a good life.

epictetus-discourses-long-022-p04.plain: Saying 'Tomorrow I will pay attention' means 'Today I will be shameless, petty and passionate.' If attention is good tomorrow, it is better today, so you can keep it tomorrow too.
epictetus-discourses-long-022-p04.core_idea: Don't put off self-attention until tomorrow

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p01.plain: Some things are in our power, such as opinion, desire and aversion; others are not, such as body, property and reputation. Treat only what is yours as yours, and no one can compel or harm you.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p01.core_idea: Control only what is yours; let the rest go

judge.issue: Drops listed consequences: lamenting, blaming gods and men, having no enemy.

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p02.plain: Practise saying to every harsh impression: you are only an impression, not what you seem. Test it: if it concerns something not in your power, be ready to say it does not concern you.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p02.core_idea: Test harsh impressions; ignore what you can't control

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p03.plain: With anything you love, remember what it really is. If you love a jug, know it is a jug, and its breaking won't upset you; when you kiss your child or wife, know you kiss a mortal.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p03.core_idea: Remember the nature of what you love

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p04.plain: We are upset not by events but by our opinions about them; death isn't terrible, or Socrates would have thought so. So when troubled, blame our own opinions, not others. The untaught blame others, the beginner blames himself, and the fully taught blames neither.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p04.plain_v1: People are disturbed not by events but by their opinions about them; death is not terrible, the opinion that it is terrible is. So blame neither others nor ultimately yourself, but your opinions.

judge_v1.issue: Conflates the three stages: blame others, blame yourself, blame neither.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the three stages of instruction; muddles whom the passage says to blame.

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p05.plain: Like a passenger ashore gathering shells, you may take up a wife and child, but keep listening for the captain. When he calls, leave everything and run to the ship; if you are old, stay close to it.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p05.core_idea: Hold life's gifts loosely; be ready to leave

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p06.plain: Do not try to make things happen as you wish; wish them to happen as they do, and your life will flow calmly.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p06.core_idea: Want things as they are, and find peace

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p07.plain: Illness hinders the body but not the will, unless the will chooses. Lameness hinders the leg, not the will. Whatever happens hinders something else, not you yourself.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p07.core_idea: Hardship hinders the body, not the will

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p08.plain: Whenever something happens, ask what power you have to use it. Against attraction you have self-control, against pain endurance, against insults patience. Trained this way, impressions will not sweep you along.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p08.core_idea: Every event calls on a strength you have

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p09.plain: Never say you lost something; say you gave it back, even a child, wife or estate. It doesn't matter through whom the giver took it back. While you have it, care for it like a traveller at an inn.

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p10.plain: To improve, accept being thought foolish about external things, and distrust yourself if people think you important. You cannot both keep your will in line with nature and secure externals; caring for one neglects the other.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p10.core_idea: Progress means letting others think you foolish

judge.issue: Drops 'wish to be considered to know nothing'.

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p11.plain: If you want your children, wife and friends to live forever, you are foolish: you want what is not in your power to be in your power, and what belongs to others to be yours.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p11.core_idea: Wanting loved ones to live forever is folly

epictetus-discourses-long-023-p12.plain: Act in life as at a banquet: take your share politely when a dish reaches you, do not hold it back as it passes, and do not reach for it early. Treat children, wife, office and wealth this way.
epictetus-discourses-long-023-p12.core_idea: Take life's gifts like dishes at a banquet

judge.issue: Drops the promise of becoming a worthy partner at the gods' banquets.

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p01.plain: When you see someone grieving a loss, do not be swept along as if outside things truly hurt him; it is his opinion that afflicts him. Show sympathy in words, even lament with him, but do not grieve inwardly.

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p02.plain: You are an actor in a play the author chooses, short or long. Whether you play a poor man, a lame man or a ruler, your job is to play it well; choosing the part belongs to another.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p02.core_idea: Play well the part you are given

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p03.plain: You can be unbeatable if you enter only contests you can win. Do not assume the powerful or honoured are happy; if the good lies in our power, there is no room for envy.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p03.core_idea: Enter only contests you control, and envy fades

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p04.plain: It is not the person who insults or strikes you who wrongs you, but your opinion that it is insulting. When someone irritates you, your own opinion did it; pause, and you will master yourself more easily.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p04.core_idea: Your opinion, not the insult, upsets you

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p05.plain: Keep death, exile and every dreadful thing, above all death, daily before your eyes, and you will never think meanly or crave anything too much.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p05.core_idea: Remembering death keeps desires in check

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p06.plain: If you want philosophy, expect mockery. Don't look down on people, but hold to what seems best, as if posted there by God. Stay firm and mockers will later admire you; give in and be mocked twice.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p06.core_idea: Expect ridicule, hold your principles, stay humble

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p07.plain: If you ever turn to outward things to please someone, you have lost your purpose. Be content to be a philosopher; if you want to seem one, seem so to yourself.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p07.core_idea: Seek your own approval, not others'

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p08.plain: Do not worry about living without honour as a nobody. Office and invitations are not your business, so lacking them is no dishonour; be somebody in what is in your power, where you can be of great worth.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p08.core_idea: Be somebody in what is in your power

judge.issue: Drops the argument that dishonour cannot come through another's fault.

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p09.plain: If someone is preferred over you at a dinner or in greetings, rejoice for him if these things are good; if they are bad, do not grieve at missing them.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p09.core_idea: Don't grieve when others are preferred

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p10.plain: When a neighbour's cup breaks, we say such things happen; think the same when yours breaks. We call another's bereavement part of life, yet cry out at our own; remember how we view others' losses.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p10.core_idea: Judge your losses as you judge others'

judge.issue: Drops the framing of learning nature's will and extending it to greater things.

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p11.plain: You would be angry if someone handed your body over to any passer-by. Aren't you ashamed to hand your mind to anyone you meet, so that their insults disturb it?
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p11.core_idea: Don't let others' insults control your mind

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p12.plain: Before any act, consider what comes before it and what follows. Otherwise you will start eagerly without thinking ahead, and later, when ugly consequences appear, you will be ashamed.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p12.core_idea: Think through consequences before you act

epictetus-discourses-long-024-p13.plain: If a brother wrongs you, keep your own stance towards him; ask not what he does but what you must do to keep your will in line with nature. No one damages you unless you think you are damaged.
epictetus-discourses-long-024-p13.core_idea: You are harmed only if you think so

epictetus-discourses-long-025-p01.plain: Set yourself at once a character and a way of being, and keep to it both when you are alone and when you are with people.
epictetus-discourses-long-025-p01.core_idea: Decide who you are, alone and in company

epictetus-discourses-long-025-p02.plain: If you hear someone speaks ill of you, do not defend yourself; reply that he did not know your other faults, or he would have mentioned more than these.
epictetus-discourses-long-025-p02.core_idea: Answer criticism by admitting more faults

epictetus-discourses-long-025-p03.plain: When visiting powerful people, expect to be turned away or ignored. If it is your duty to go anyway, bear what happens and never say it was not worth it; that is the mark of someone upset by externals.
epictetus-discourses-long-025-p03.core_idea: Expect rejection, do your duty anyway

epictetus-discourses-long-025-p04.plain: When a pleasure tempts you, pause and let it wait. Picture both the enjoyment and the regret afterwards, and how glad you will be if you abstain. If you do go ahead, don't let its charm conquer you.
epictetus-discourses-long-025-p04.core_idea: Pause before pleasure and weigh the aftermath

judge.issue: Drops the closing weighing of the victory gained by not being conquered.

epictetus-discourses-long-025-p05.plain: Once you have decided something should be done, do not hide while doing it, even if many will disapprove. If it is wrong, don't do it; if it is right, why fear those who wrongly criticise?
epictetus-discourses-long-025-p05.core_idea: Do what is right openly, despite critics

epictetus-discourses-long-025-p06.plain: If you take on a role beyond your strength, you act badly in it and neglect the role you could have filled.
epictetus-discourses-long-025-p06.core_idea: Take on only the roles you can fulfil

epictetus-discourses-long-025-p07.plain: The body is the measure of what you should own, as the foot is of the shoe. Keep to it and you stay within limits; pass it and there is no stopping, as a shoe becomes gilded, dyed, embroidered.
epictetus-discourses-long-025-p07.core_idea: Your needs set the limit for possessions

epictetus-discourses-long-025-p08.plain: Someone who treats you badly or speaks ill of you does what seems right to him. If he is mistaken, he is the one harmed, because he is deceived. So be gentle, and say: it seemed so to him.
epictetus-discourses-long-025-p08.core_idea: Those who wrong you hurt themselves; be gentle

epictetus-discourses-long-025-p09.plain: Everything has two handles, one you can carry it by and one you cannot. If your brother wrongs you, do not grab the wrong; grab the fact that he is your brother, raised with you, and you can bear it.
epictetus-discourses-long-025-p09.core_idea: Hold hard things by the handle you can bear

epictetus-discourses-long-025-p10.plain: Being richer or more eloquent than you does not make me better than you; it only means I have more property or better speech. But a person is neither property nor speech.
epictetus-discourses-long-025-p10.core_idea: Wealth or eloquence doesn't make you better

epictetus-discourses-long-026-p01.plain: If someone bathes quickly, say he bathes quickly, not badly; if he drinks a lot, say he drinks a lot. Until you know his reasons, how can you know he is doing wrong?
epictetus-discourses-long-026-p01.core_idea: Describe what people do; don't judge it

judge.issue: "His reasons" loosens "determined his opinion" (judgement behind the act).

epictetus-discourses-long-026-p02.plain: Never call yourself a philosopher or lecture ordinary people on principles; act on them instead. At a dinner, do not say how people should eat; eat as you should.
epictetus-discourses-long-026-p02.core_idea: Live your principles instead of preaching them

epictetus-discourses-long-026-p03.plain: The untaught expect help and harm from outside; the philosopher expects them from himself. One making progress blames and praises no one, claims nothing, ignores praise and criticism, curbs desire, and watches himself like an enemy.
epictetus-discourses-long-026-p03.core_idea: Progress means looking to yourself, not outside

judge.issue: Compresses list of signs; drops blaming himself when hindered and moving carefully.

epictetus-discourses-long-026-p04.plain: You are an adult now. Keep postponing self-improvement and you will stay ignorant until you die. Live now as someone making progress; every trial is the contest, it cannot wait, and one surrender can undo progress.
epictetus-discourses-long-026-p04.core_idea: The time to improve is now, not later

judge.issue: Drops making what seems best an unbreakable law.

epictetus-discourses-long-026-p05.plain: A prayer to Zeus and Destiny: lead me where I must go, and I will follow willingly; if I refuse, I make myself miserable and must follow anyway. Whoever yields nobly to necessity is wise in divine things.
epictetus-discourses-long-026-p05.core_idea: Follow fate willingly rather than be dragged

enchiridion-001-p01.plain: Some things are in our power, like opinion, aim, desire and aversion; others are not, like body, property and reputation. Treat only what is yours as yours, and no one can compel or hurt you.
enchiridion-001-p01.core_idea: Control only what is yours; let the rest go

judge.issue: Drops freedom of what is ours and the full list of consequences.

enchiridion-001-p02.plain: People are disturbed not by things but by their views of them; death is not terrible, the notion that it is terrible is. So blame not others but your own views; the wise blame neither others nor themselves.
enchiridion-001-p02.core_idea: Our views, not things, disturb us

judge.issue: Drops the middle stage of reproaching oneself; "wise" for perfectly instructed.

enchiridion-001-p03.plain: Do not demand that events happen as you wish; wish them to happen as they do, and you will do well.
enchiridion-001-p03.core_idea: Want things as they happen, and fare well

enchiridion-001-p04.plain: Sickness hinders the body, but not the will unless it chooses. Lameness hinders the leg, not the will. Say this about everything that happens: it hinders something else, not truly you.
enchiridion-001-p04.core_idea: Hardship hinders the body, not the will

enchiridion-001-p05.plain: Whenever something happens, ask yourself what strength you have to use for it: self-control for attraction, endurance for pain, patience for insult. With this habit, events will not overwhelm you.
enchiridion-001-p05.core_idea: Every event calls on a strength you have

enchiridion-001-p06.plain: Never say you lost something; say you gave it back, even a child, wife or estate. It doesn't matter through whom the giver took it back. While you have it, treat it as not yours, like travellers at an inn.

enchiridion-001-p07.plain: To improve, be willing to be thought foolish about external things, and do not want to seem knowledgeable. If others think you important, distrust yourself; you cannot both keep your will in harmony with nature and secure externals.
enchiridion-001-p07.core_idea: Progress means letting others think you foolish

enchiridion-001-p08.plain: Behave in life as at a banquet: take a modest share when a dish reaches you, don't stop it as it passes, and don't long for it before it comes. Treat children, spouse, office and riches this way.
enchiridion-001-p08.core_idea: Take life's gifts like dishes at a banquet

judge.issue: Drops the promise of becoming worthy to feast with the gods.

enchiridion-001-p09.plain: When you see someone weeping over a loss, do not be overcome; what hurts him is not the event but the view he takes of it. Talk with him kindly, even groan with him, but do not groan inwardly.

enchiridion-001-p10.plain: You are an actor in a play the Author chooses, short or long. Whether you play a poor man, a cripple or a ruler, act it well; that is your job, but choosing the part belongs to another.
enchiridion-001-p10.core_idea: Play well the part you are given

enchiridion-001-p11.plain: You can be unconquerable if you fight only battles you can win. Do not assume the honoured or powerful are happy; if good lies in what is in our power, there is no room for envy. Seek freedom, not rank.
enchiridion-001-p11.core_idea: Fight only battles you control; seek freedom

enchiridion-001-p12.plain: It is not the person who abuses or strikes you who insults you, but your view that it is insulting. When provoked, know that your own opinion provokes you; take time before reacting and you will control yourself.
enchiridion-001-p12.core_idea: Your view, not the insult, provokes you

enchiridion-001-p13.plain: If you want philosophy, expect to be laughed at. Don't look superior, but hold to what seems best as one placed there by God. Persist, and the mockers will later admire you; give in, and you will be mocked twice.
enchiridion-001-p13.core_idea: Expect ridicule, hold your principles, stay humble

enchiridion-002-p01.plain: Do not worry that you will live in discredit and be nobody. Power and invitations are not your business, so missing them is no disgrace; be somebody in what lies in your power, where you can matter most.
enchiridion-002-p01.core_idea: Be somebody in what is in your power

judge.issue: Drops the argument that discredit cannot come through another.

enchiridion-002-p02.plain: If someone is preferred before you at a party or in courtesies, rejoice for him if these things are good; if they are bad, do not grieve that you lack them.
enchiridion-002-p02.core_idea: Don't grieve when others are preferred

enchiridion-002-p03.plain: You would be angry if someone handed your body over to a stranger. Aren't you ashamed to hand your mind to anyone who insults you, to be upset and confused?
enchiridion-002-p03.core_idea: Don't let insults take over your mind

enchiridion-002-p04.plain: In everything, consider what comes before and after, then begin. Otherwise you will start with energy, careless of consequences, and quit in shame when they appear.
enchiridion-002-p04.core_idea: Think through consequences before you begin

enchiridion-002-p05.plain: If a brother is unjust, keep your own just stance towards him. Think not of what he does but of keeping your will in line with nature; you are hurt only when you consent to be hurt.
enchiridion-002-p05.core_idea: You are hurt only if you consent

enchiridion-002-p06.plain: If someone tells you a person speaks ill of you, do not make excuses; say he must not know your other faults, or he would have mentioned more.
enchiridion-002-p06.core_idea: Answer criticism by admitting more faults

enchiridion-003-p01.plain: When a promised pleasure dazzles you, don't be swept away; make it wait. Picture both the enjoyment and the regret afterwards, against the pride of abstaining. Even if it seems fitting, don't let its lure conquer you.
enchiridion-003-p01.core_idea: Pause before pleasure and weigh the aftermath

judge.issue: Drops the closing weighing of the victory gained over the pleasure.

enchiridion-003-p02.plain: When you have clearly judged something should be done, never shrink from being seen doing it, even if people misunderstand. If it is wrong, don't do it; if it is right, why fear unfair critics?
enchiridion-003-p02.core_idea: Do what is right openly, despite critics

enchiridion-003-p03.plain: If you take on a role beyond your strength, you handle it badly and give up a role you could have carried.
enchiridion-003-p03.core_idea: Take on only the roles you can carry

enchiridion-003-p04.plain: Someone who harms you or speaks ill of you follows what seems right to him, not to you. If he is mistaken, he is the one hurt, since he is deceived. So bear him gently: it seemed so to him.
enchiridion-003-p04.core_idea: Those who wrong you hurt themselves; be gentle

enchiridion-003-p05.plain: Everything has two handles: one you can carry it by and one you cannot. If your brother wrongs you, don't take hold of his wrong; take hold of the fact that he is your brother, raised with you.
enchiridion-003-p05.core_idea: Hold hard things by the handle you can bear

judge.issue: Omits the conclusion that this handle lets you bear it.

enchiridion-003-p06.plain: Being richer or more eloquent does not make me your superior; it only means my possessions or style exceed yours. And you are neither your property nor your style.
enchiridion-003-p06.core_idea: Wealth or eloquence doesn't make you superior

enchiridion-003-p07.plain: How long will you put off demanding the best of yourself? You know the principles and are no longer a boy. Keep postponing and you will stay ordinary until death. From now on, live as a mature, progressing person.
enchiridion-003-p07.core_idea: Stop delaying; start living wisely now

judge.issue: Drops the rhetorical "what master do you wait for" and judgments of reason.

enchiridion-003-p08.plain: A prayer to Zeus and Destiny: lead me wherever my lot is fixed, and I follow cheerfully. If I refused, I would be wicked and miserable and still have to follow.
enchiridion-003-p08.core_idea: Follow fate cheerfully; you must follow anyway

gibran-forerunner-001-p01.plain: You go ahead of yourself: everything you have built is only the base for a greater self, and that self in turn will be a base for more.
gibran-forerunner-001-p01.core_idea: You are always building toward a larger self

gibran-forerunner-001-p02.plain: We have always gone ahead of ourselves and always will. All we gather is only seed for fields not yet ploughed; we are both the fields and the ploughmen, the harvesters and the harvest.
gibran-forerunner-001-p02.core_idea: We are both the sowers and the harvest

gibran-forerunner-001-p03.plain: A prayer to love, which has given my desires dignity: let my stronger self not take what tempts my weaker self. I would rather starve and die than reach for a cup love did not fill or bless.
gibran-forerunner-001-p03.core_idea: Take only what love has blessed

gibran-forerunner-001-p04.plain: Many give up a kingdom for solitude, and eagles come down among moles to learn the earth's secrets. Some give up dreams to stay near the dreamless, or cover their souls so others aren't shamed by naked truth.
gibran-forerunner-001-p04.core_idea: People give up great things to stay close to others

gibran-forerunner-002-p01.plain: On an island I saw a monster endlessly eating earth and drinking sea. I asked if he was never satisfied. He said he was full, even weary of it, but afraid there would be nothing left tomorrow.
gibran-forerunner-002-p01.core_idea: Fear of tomorrow drives endless craving

gibran-forerunner-002-p02.plain: Two eagles circling over a lamb began fighting each other. The astonished sheep told her lamb the sky was large enough for both, and to pray that God make peace between his winged brothers. The lamb prayed.
gibran-forerunner-002-p02.core_idea: The innocent pray even for their predators

gibran-forerunner-002-p03.plain: The astonished traveller cried that since his horse was stolen, everyone had rushed to list his faults, yet no one said a word against the thief.
gibran-forerunner-002-p03.core_idea: People blame the victim, not the wrongdoer

gibran-forerunner-002-p04.plain: The weather-cock complained to the wind that it was dull and always blew in its face, disturbing the stability God gave it. The wind did not answer; it only laughed in space.
gibran-forerunner-002-p04.core_idea: The vain blame the world for their own position

gibran-forerunner-002-p05.plain: A bird rose from deep in my heart and flew upward, growing as it rose, from a swallow to something that filled the heavens. Yet it never left my heart.
gibran-forerunner-002-p05.core_idea: What rises from the heart still stays within it

gibran-forerunner-002-p06.plain: My faith, how can I rise to your height? I am chained like a prisoner who cannot see the temple's domes, and cannot fly with you. Yet you rise from my heart, my heart holds you, and I am content.
gibran-forerunner-002-p06.core_idea: Faith soars beyond me, yet lives in my heart

judge.issue: Drops the sea-to-mist and fruit-heart images of the self's limits.

gibran-forerunner-002-p07.plain: A white sheet of paper vowed to stay pure forever and never let ink or dark touch it. The ink and the coloured pencils kept away. The paper did stay pure and chaste forever, and empty.
gibran-forerunner-002-p07.core_idea: Purity kept at all costs can leave life empty

gibran-forerunner-003-p01.plain: A man sold a beautiful statue he had dug up to a collector. Walking home, he wondered how anyone could pay so much for dead stone. The collector wondered how anyone could trade such life for dead money.
gibran-forerunner-003-p01.core_idea: Each values what the other thinks is dead

gibran-forerunner-003-p02.plain: One fish told another there is a sea above theirs where creatures live as they do. The other scoffed: anything that leaves our sea dies, so what proof is there of life in other seas?
gibran-forerunner-003-p02.core_idea: We doubt any life beyond what we know

gibran-forerunner-003-p03.plain: On a dark night a man stole his neighbour's biggest melon. When he opened it at home and found it unripe, his conscience suddenly woke, and he regretted the theft.
gibran-forerunner-003-p03.core_idea: Conscience often wakes only when the gain fails

gibran-forerunner-003-p04.plain: The wish to die, though stronger than anything, is held back by a wish to live that is weaker than anything.
gibran-forerunner-003-p04.core_idea: A faint will to live can hold back despair

gibran-forerunner-003-p05.plain: Memory holds my spirit here: a line of distant days, a youth spent dreaming, a face, a voice that lingers, a hand touching mine.
gibran-forerunner-003-p05.core_idea: Memories of love hold the spirit back

judge.issue: Flattens "a face that bids my eyelids not to sleep" to "a face".

gibran-forerunner-003-p06.plain: Beyond my solitude is a deeper one, to whose dweller my aloneness seems a crowded market and my silence noise. I am too young and restless to seek it; the world's voices and shadows still hold me back.
gibran-forerunner-003-p06.core_idea: There is always a deeper solitude beyond yours

judge.issue: "The world's voices" interprets "yonder valley" rather than rendering it.

gibran-forerunner-003-p07.plain: Beyond my burdened self lives a freer self, but I am too young and angry to be it. How can I be free unless my burdened selves die, or all people are free, or my roots wither and fledglings leave?
gibran-forerunner-003-p07.core_idea: Freedom requires letting go of what holds you

judge.issue: Compresses roots, leaves and eagle images into a list; drops their logic.

gibran-forerunner-003-p08.plain: You want love in a cup, not as a rushing river. You listen to its faint murmur, but when love shouts you cover your ears.
gibran-forerunner-003-p08.core_idea: We want love only in small, safe amounts

gibran-forerunner-003-p09.plain: Night is ending, and we children of night must die at dawn; from our ashes a stronger love will rise, laughing in the sun and never dying.
gibran-forerunner-003-p09.core_idea: From our ending a deathless love will rise

gibran-madman-001-p01.plain: In my madness I found freedom and safety: the freedom of being alone, and safety from being understood, since those who understand us enslave part of us. Yet a jailed thief is also safe from thieves.
gibran-madman-001-p01.core_idea: Being understood can enslave part of you

gibran-madman-001-p02.plain: For thousands of years I called myself God's slave, creation and son, and God passed by in silence. When I said we grow together, his root and his flower, God enfolded me, and was in the valleys too.
gibran-madman-001-p02.core_idea: God answers when we see ourselves as one with him

judge.issue: Drops the final address ("my aim and my fulfillment") and God's whispered words.

gibran-madman-001-p03.plain: Friend, I am not what I seem; appearance is a garment that shields me from your questions and you from my neglect. My true self lives in silence, forever unseen and unreachable.
gibran-madman-001-p03.core_idea: The true self stays hidden behind appearances

gibran-madman-001-p04.plain: Friend, you are not my friend, but how can I make you understand? My path is not yours, yet we walk together hand in hand.
gibran-madman-001-p04.core_idea: We walk together on different paths

gibran-madman-001-p05.plain: A scarecrow said he never tired of the joy of scaring; I said I knew it too. He replied only those stuffed with straw know it; praise or insult? A year later, crows nested under his hat.
gibran-madman-001-p05.core_idea: Those who frighten others are hollow in the end

judge.issue: Drops the scarecrow having "turned philosopher", which sets up the ending.

gibran-madman-001-p06.plain: A mother and daughter, sleepwalking, met in their garden and poured out their hatred: each blamed the other for ruining her life. A cock crowed, they woke, and spoke to each other gently.
gibran-madman-001-p06.core_idea: Hidden resentments lie beneath polite affection

judge.issue: Softens the mutual death wishes to "blamed the other".

gibran-madman-001-p07.plain: A wise dog passed cats being told that if they prayed with faith it would rain mice. He laughed inwardly at the foolish cats: surely what rains down for prayer and faith is not mice but bones.
gibran-madman-001-p07.core_idea: Everyone imagines heaven serves their own appetite

gibran-madman-001-p08.plain: A man with a valley full of needles was asked by Jesus's mother for one, to mend her son's torn garment. He gave her no needle, only a learned lecture on giving and taking to take to her son.
gibran-madman-001-p08.core_idea: Talk about generosity is no substitute for giving

gibran-madman-001-p09.plain: Seeing his long shadow at sunrise, a fox decided he would eat a camel for lunch and hunted camels all morning. At noon he saw his shadow again and said a mouse will do.
gibran-madman-001-p09.core_idea: Ambitions shrink as the day goes on

gibran-madman-001-p10.plain: A witch poisoned the city well so all who drank went mad. Everyone drank except the king and his chamberlain, and the people said the king was mad. So he drank too, and the city rejoiced at his recovered reason.
gibran-madman-001-p10.core_idea: To the mad crowd, sanity looks like madness

gibran-madman-002-p01.plain: I invented a new pleasure, and as I tried it an angel and a devil rushed to my door and fought over it, one crying sin, the other virtue.
gibran-madman-002-p01.core_idea: The same pleasure is called sin and virtue

gibran-madman-002-p02.plain: In my father's garden are two cages, one with a lion from the desert and one with a sparrow that does not sing. Each dawn the sparrow greets the lion as a fellow prisoner.
gibran-madman-002-p02.core_idea: Great and small alike can be prisoners

gibran-madman-002-p03.plain: Three ants on a sleeping man's nose complained the land was barren. The third said they stood on the Supreme Ant, too vast to see or hear. The others laughed. Then the man scratched his nose and crushed them.
gibran-madman-002-p03.core_idea: We mock what is too vast for us to perceive

gibran-madman-002-p04.plain: As I buried one of my dead selves, the grave-digger said he liked only me: everyone else came and went weeping, while I came laughing and went laughing.
gibran-madman-002-p04.core_idea: Bury your old selves with laughter, not tears

gibran-madman-002-p05.plain: The Evil God complained to the Good God that people kept mistaking him for the Good God. The Good God said people mistook him for the Evil God too. The Evil God walked off cursing human stupidity.

gibran-madman-002-p06.plain: My defeat is dearer to me than a thousand triumphs. Through it I know myself and find joy in being scorned. It taught me that being enthroned is enslavement, and being understood is being levelled down.
gibran-madman-002-p06.core_idea: Defeat teaches more and frees more than triumph

judge.issue: Drops defeat as sword and shield and the ripe-fruit warning about being grasped.

gibran-madman-002-p07.plain: My defeat, my undying courage: together we will laugh with the storm, bury all that dies in us, stand firmly in the sun, and be dangerous.

gibran-madman-002-p08.plain: I have seen faces with many expressions and one fixed one, shine hiding ugliness and shine hiding beauty, old faces lined with nothing and smooth ones engraved with everything. I know faces because I look beneath appearances.
gibran-madman-002-p08.core_idea: See past appearances to what lies beneath

gibran-madman-003-p01.plain: A friend called a blind man the wisest in the land. I asked the man, blind from birth, what wisdom he followed. He said he was an astronomer, and touching his chest, said he watches all these suns and stars.
gibran-madman-003-p01.core_idea: The universe can be seen within

gibran-madman-003-p02.plain: I sit between my brother the mountain and my sister the sea. We three are one in our loneliness, bound by a deep, strong and strange love.
gibran-madman-003-p02.core_idea: Loneliness can be a shared bond

gibran-madman-003-p03.plain: A blade of grass complained that a falling leaf was noisy; the leaf scorned it as lowly. The leaf fell asleep, came back in spring as grass, and in autumn grumbled that the falling leaves were so noisy.
gibran-madman-003-p03.core_idea: We condemn others, then become them

gibran-madman-003-p04.plain: The Eye saw a beautiful mountain in the mist. The Ear could not hear it, the Hand could not touch it, the Nose could not smell it. So they all agreed something must be wrong with the Eye.
gibran-madman-003-p04.core_idea: People dismiss what their own senses cannot perceive

gibran-madman-003-p05.plain: Two scholars, one an unbeliever and one a believer, argued for hours about the gods. That evening the unbeliever went to the temple and begged forgiveness, and the believer burned his sacred books, having become an unbeliever.
gibran-madman-003-p05.core_idea: Arguments can convert each side to the other

gibran-madman-003-p06.plain: My Sorrow died like all living things, leaving me alone to think. Now my words feel heavy, no one hears my songs or looks at me, and in sleep voices pity the man whose Sorrow is dead.
gibran-madman-003-p06.core_idea: Losing your sorrow can leave you unseen

gibran-madman-003-p07.plain: My Joy grew pale because no other heart shared it, and it died of isolation. Now I remember my dead Joy only with my dead Sorrow, but memory is an autumn leaf that murmurs briefly and falls silent.

gibran-madman-003-p08.plain: I live among a perfect race, the most imperfect one, a human chaos moving among finished worlds whose people have complete laws, pure order, and thoughts, dreams and visions all sorted and recorded.
gibran-madman-003-p08.core_idea: Feeling chaotic among people who seem perfect

gibran-madman-003-p09.plain: This is a perfect world, God's ripest fruit. So why am I here, O God, a green seed of unfulfilled passion, a directionless storm, a fragment of a burnt planet? Why, God of lost souls, yourself lost among gods?
gibran-madman-003-p09.core_idea: Asking God why a restless soul belongs here

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p01.plain: I walk forever along these shores between the sand and the foam. The tide will erase my footprints and the wind will blow the foam away, but the sea and shore will remain forever.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p01.core_idea: Our traces fade; the sea and shore remain

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p02.plain: Only yesterday I thought I was a fragment trembling out of rhythm in life. Now I know I am the whole sphere, and all life moves within me in rhythmic fragments.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p02.core_idea: You are not a fragment; life moves within you

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p03.plain: Awake, people tell me I and my world are a grain of sand on an infinite shore. In my dream I tell them I am the infinite sea, and all worlds are grains of sand on my shore.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p03.core_idea: You are the sea, not the grain of sand

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p04.plain: Only once have I been left speechless: when someone asked me who I am.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p04.core_idea: The hardest question is who you are

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p05.plain: A pearl is a temple that pain builds around a grain of sand. What longing built our bodies, and around what grains?
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p05.core_idea: Pain and longing build beautiful things

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p06.plain: When God threw me like a pebble into this wonderful lake, I stirred its surface with countless circles. But when I reached the depths, I became very still.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p06.core_idea: Depth brings stillness after surface turmoil
