gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p07.plain: Give me silence, and I will be bolder than the night.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p07.core_idea: Silence gives courage to face the dark

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p08.plain: I was born a second time when my soul and my body loved each other and became one.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p08.core_idea: Soul and body united bring rebirth

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p09.plain: Remembering is a kind of meeting. Forgetting is a kind of freedom.

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p10.plain: Don't the spirits living in the sky envy humans their pain?
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p10.core_idea: Pain may be a gift even spirits envy

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p11.plain: A pilgrim told me to follow him to the Holy City in a day and a night. We walked many days and nights without reaching it, and to my surprise he grew angry with me because he had misled me.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p11.core_idea: Those who mislead us often blame us for it

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p12.plain: God, let me be the lion's prey before you let the rabbit be mine.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p12.core_idea: Better to be prey than prey on the weak

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p13.plain: You can reach the dawn only by going through the night.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p13.core_idea: Only through darkness do we reach the dawn

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p14.plain: My house begs me to stay with my past; the road calls me to my future. I tell them I have neither: in staying there is going, in going there is staying. Only love and death change everything.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p14.core_idea: Only love and death truly change things

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p15.plain: How can I lose faith in life's fairness, when those who sleep on feathers dream no more beautifully than those who sleep on the bare ground?
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p15.core_idea: Dreams are equal for rich and poor

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p16.plain: Strangely, wanting certain pleasures is part of my pain.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p16.core_idea: Desire itself can be a source of pain

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p17.plain: I have despised my soul seven times: when it was meek to rise, limped before the lame, chose the easy, excused its wrong by others', called weakness patience, scorned a face that was its own mask, and prized its praise-song.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p17.core_idea: Seven ways the soul betrays itself

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p18.plain: I do not know absolute truth, but I am humble about my ignorance, and that humility is my honour and reward.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p18.core_idea: Humility before ignorance is its own honour

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p19.plain: Between what we imagine and what we achieve lies a gap that only our longing can cross.

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p20.plain: Paradise is just behind that door, in the next room, but I have lost the key. Maybe I have only misplaced it.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p20.core_idea: Paradise is near; we've only mislaid the key

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p21.plain: You are blind and I cannot hear or speak, so let us touch hands and understand each other.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p21.core_idea: Understanding can pass beyond words and sight

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p22.plain: A person's meaning lies not in what they achieve but in what they long to achieve.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p22.core_idea: We are defined by our longings, not achievements

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p23.plain: Some of us are like ink and some like paper. Without the dark ones, some would have no voice; without the light ones, some could not see.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p23.core_idea: We need each other's differences to be seen and heard

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p24.plain: If you listen to me, I will give you a voice.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p24.core_idea: Listening is repaid with a voice

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p25.plain: Our mind is like a sponge and our heart like a stream. Isn't it strange that most of us choose to soak things up rather than to flow?
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p25.core_idea: Choose to flow like the heart, not absorb

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p26.plain: When you yearn for good things you cannot name, and feel sad without knowing why, you are growing along with everything that grows and rising toward a larger self.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p26.core_idea: Nameless longing and sorrow are signs of growth

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p27.plain: When my cup is empty I accept it, but when it is only half full I resent that it is not full.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p27.core_idea: Partial having breeds more resentment than having nothing

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p28.plain: What is real in another person lies in what they cannot show you, so to understand them, listen to what they leave unsaid.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p28.core_idea: Understand people by what they cannot say

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p29.plain: Half of what I say means nothing, but I say it so the other half can get through to you.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p29.core_idea: Some words exist to carry the meaningful ones

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p30.plain: Having a sense of humour means seeing things in their right proportion.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p30.core_idea: Humour is a sense of proportion

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p31.plain: My loneliness began when people praised my chatty faults and criticised my quiet virtues.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p31.core_idea: Being praised for faults and blamed for virtues isolates

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p32.plain: A truth should always be known, but only sometimes spoken.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p32.core_idea: Know truth always; speak it only sometimes

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p33.plain: The real part of us is quiet; the part we have picked up from outside is the part that talks.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p33.core_idea: Our true self is silent, the acquired self talks

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p34.plain: The life in me cannot truly reach the life in you, but let us talk anyway so we do not feel alone.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p34.core_idea: We talk to ease loneliness, though words cannot fully connect

judge.issue: "Cannot truly reach" softens the flat "cannot reach".

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p35.plain: Only those who cannot speak are jealous of those who talk a lot.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p35.core_idea: Only the voiceless envy the talkative

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p36.plain: If winter claimed to have spring in its heart, who would believe it?
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p36.core_idea: Claims that contradict appearances are hard to believe

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p37.plain: If you truly looked, you would see yourself in everything you see, and if you truly listened, you would hear your own voice in every voice.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p37.core_idea: You can find yourself in everyone and everything

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p38.plain: Finding truth takes two people: one to say it and one to understand it.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p38.core_idea: Truth needs a speaker and a listener

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p39.plain: Many beliefs are like a window: you see the truth through them, but they also keep you apart from it.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p39.core_idea: Doctrines reveal truth yet separate us from it

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p40.plain: Let us play hide and seek: if you hid in my heart you would be easy to find, but if you hide inside your own shell, no one can find you.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p40.core_idea: Hiding behind your defences makes you unreachable

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p41.plain: How noble is a sad heart that will join happy hearts in singing a happy song.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p41.core_idea: It is noble to share joy while sad

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p42.plain: I want to walk along with everyone who is walking, not stand still and watch the procession go past.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p42.core_idea: Join life rather than watch it pass

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p43.plain: You owe the person who serves you more than money: give them your heart, or serve them in return.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p43.core_idea: Those who serve us deserve heart, not just pay

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p44.plain: Trees are poems the earth writes on the sky, and we cut them down to make paper so we can write down our emptiness.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p44.core_idea: We destroy natural poetry to record our emptiness

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p45.plain: Given the choice between the power to write a poem and the joy of a poem never written, I would choose the joy, because it is the better poetry.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p45.core_idea: The unwritten poem's ecstasy is better poetry

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p46.plain: Poetry is not stating an opinion; it is a song that comes from a painful wound or a smiling mouth.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p46.core_idea: Poetry is song born of pain or joy

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p47.plain: If you sing about beauty, even all alone in the middle of a desert, someone will hear you.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p47.core_idea: Singing of beauty always finds an audience

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p48.plain: Poetry is wisdom that delights the heart, and wisdom is poetry that sings in the mind.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p48.core_idea: Poetry and wisdom are two faces of one thing

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p49.plain: We often sing lullabies to our children so that we ourselves can get to sleep.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p49.core_idea: What we do for others often soothes ourselves

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p50.plain: A great singer is one who gives voice to what we keep silent.

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p51.plain: How can you sing with a mouth full of food, or raise your hand to bless when it is full of gold?
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p51.core_idea: Fullness and greed block song and blessing

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p52.plain: People say the nightingale presses a thorn into its breast when it sings its love song; we all do the same, for how else could we sing?
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p52.core_idea: All true song comes from pain

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p53.plain: Even the most free and soaring spirit still has bodily needs it cannot escape.

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p54.plain: A mad person is just as much a musician as you or I; only their instrument is a little out of tune.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p54.core_idea: The mad share our music, slightly out of tune

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p55.plain: The song a mother keeps silent in her heart is sung out loud by her child.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p55.core_idea: A mother's hidden song lives in her child

judge.issue: Adds "eventually", a timing the passage does not state.

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p57.plain: I have never fully agreed with my other self; the truth seems to lie somewhere between us.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p57.core_idea: Truth lies between our inner selves

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p58.plain: Your other self always feels sorry for you, but it grows by sorrow, so all is well.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p58.core_idea: Your other self grows through sorrow

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p59.plain: Soul and body only seem to fight in people whose souls are asleep and whose bodies are out of tune.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p59.core_idea: Soul and body conflict only when out of balance

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p60.plain: When you reach the heart of life you will find beauty in everything, even in eyes that cannot see beauty.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p60.core_idea: At life's heart, everything holds beauty

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p61.plain: We live only to discover beauty; everything else is a kind of waiting.

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p62.plain: Plant a seed and the earth will give you a flower; dream your dream to the sky and it will bring you the one you love.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p62.core_idea: What you sow and dream returns to you

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p63.plain: The devil died the day you were born, so now you do not have to pass through hell to meet an angel.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p63.core_idea: You need not go through hell to find goodness

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p64.plain: If you want to possess something, you must not lay claim to it.

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p65.plain: When a man and a woman touch hands, they both touch the heart of eternity.

gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p66.plain: Love itself is the veil that hangs between two lovers.
gibran-sand-and-foam-001-p66.core_idea: Love both joins and veils lovers

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p01.plain: Men who will not forgive women their small faults will never get to enjoy their great virtues.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p01.core_idea: Forgive small faults to enjoy great virtues

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p02.plain: Love that is not made new every day turns into a habit, and then into a kind of slavery.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p02.core_idea: Love must be renewed daily or it enslaves

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p03.plain: Lovers embrace what lies between them rather than each other.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p03.core_idea: Lovers embrace their bond, not each other

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p04.plain: Love and doubt have never been on speaking terms with each other.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p05.plain: Friendship is always a sweet duty, never a chance to gain something.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p06.plain: If you do not understand your friend in every kind of situation, you will never understand them.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p06.core_idea: Truly knowing a friend means knowing them in all conditions

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p07.plain: Your finest clothes are woven by others, your tastiest meal is at another's table, your most comfortable bed is in another's house; so how can you separate yourself from other people?
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p07.core_idea: We cannot separate ourselves from others

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p08.plain: Your mind and my heart will never agree until your mind stops living in numbers and my heart stops living in fog.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p08.core_idea: Mind and heart agree only when both leave extremes

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p09.plain: How can my heart be opened unless it is broken?
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p09.core_idea: A heart opens only when broken

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p10.plain: Only great sorrow or great joy can show who you really are.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p10.core_idea: Great sorrow or joy reveals your truth

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p11.plain: If you want to be truly seen, you must either dance freely and openly in the sun or carry your cross.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p11.core_idea: You are revealed through joy or suffering

judge.issue: "Dance freely and openly" softens "dance naked", losing the full exposure.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p12.plain: If nature listened to our talk of contentment, no river would seek the sea and no winter would become spring; if it listened to our talk of thrift, how many of us would even be alive?
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p12.core_idea: Nature ignores our talk of contentment and thrift

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p13.plain: When you turn your back on the sun, all you see is your own shadow.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p13.core_idea: Turning from the light shows only your shadow

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p14.plain: You are free under the sun, the stars, and even in total darkness or with your eyes shut; but you are a slave to the one you love, and to the one who loves you.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p14.core_idea: Love is the one bond that limits our freedom

judge.issue: Drops "because you love him", the reason for the bondage.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p15.plain: We are all beggars at the temple gate, each receiving a share of the King's gifts as he comes and goes; yet we envy one another, which belittles the King.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p15.core_idea: Envying each other belittles the giver of all

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p16.plain: You cannot eat more than your hunger allows; the other half of the loaf belongs to someone else, and a little should be left for an unexpected guest.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p16.core_idea: Take only what you need and share the rest

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p17.plain: Without guests, every house would be like a grave.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p18.plain: I stopped my guest at the door and said, do not wipe your feet when you come in, but when you leave.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p18.core_idea: A guest should take nothing away from the house

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p19.plain: Real generosity is not giving me what I need more than you, but giving me what you need more than I do.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p19.core_idea: Generosity means giving what you yourself need

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p20.plain: You are truly charitable when you give while looking away, so you do not see the receiver's embarrassment.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p20.core_idea: True charity spares the receiver's shame

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p21.plain: The difference between the richest and the poorest person is only a day of hunger and an hour of thirst.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p21.core_idea: Rich and poor are separated by very little

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p22.plain: We often borrow from our future to pay off debts from our past.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p22.core_idea: We spend our future paying for our past

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p23.plain: Angels and devils visit me too, but I get rid of them: I bore the angel with an old prayer, and the devil passes me by when I commit an old sin.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p23.core_idea: Stale prayer and stale sin both drive visitors away

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p24.plain: This life is not a bad prison, though I dislike the wall between my cell and my neighbour's; yet I do not blame the guard or the Builder of the prison.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p24.core_idea: Life is a fair prison, but walls divide us

judge.issue: Adds the explicit "this life" reading of the prison.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p25.plain: People who give you a snake when you asked for a fish may have nothing but snakes to give; for them, that is generosity.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p25.core_idea: People can only give what they have

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p26.plain: Trickery sometimes works, but it always ends up destroying itself.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p27.plain: You truly forgive when you forgive murderers who never shed blood, thieves who never steal, and liars who never say anything false.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p27.core_idea: True forgiveness reaches hidden, unspoken wrongs

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p28.plain: Whoever can point to the line between good and evil can touch the hem of God's garment.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p28.core_idea: Knowing good from evil brings one near God

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p29.plain: If your heart is a volcano, how can you expect flowers to grow in your hands?
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p29.core_idea: An angry heart cannot produce gentle deeds

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p30.plain: A strange kind of indulgence: sometimes I would let myself be wronged and cheated so I can laugh at those who think I do not know it.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p30.core_idea: Letting yourself be cheated can hold secret amusement

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p31.plain: If someone wipes their dirty hands on your coat, let them keep the coat; they may need it again, and you surely will not.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p31.core_idea: Let go of what others have soiled

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p32.plain: Please do not cover up your natural faults with virtues you have acquired; I would rather have the faults, since they are like my own.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p32.core_idea: Honest faults are better than borrowed virtues

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p33.plain: How often I have claimed crimes I never committed so that another person could feel at ease with me.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p33.core_idea: Admitting imagined faults can put others at ease

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p34.plain: Even the masks life wears hide a deeper mystery.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p35.plain: You can judge others only by what you know of yourself; so who is guilty and who is innocent? The truly just person feels half guilty for your wrongdoing.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p35.core_idea: Judge others by yourself and share their guilt

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p36.plain: Only when something is chasing you do you become fast.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p37.plain: O God, I have no enemies, but if I must have one, let him be as strong as I am, so that only truth wins.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p37.core_idea: Wish for an equal opponent so truth prevails

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p38.plain: You and your enemy will get along well once you are both dead.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p39.plain: A Man crucified long ago for being too loving was seen three times yesterday: asking police to spare a prostitute, drinking wine with an outcast, and fighting a promoter inside a church.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p39.core_idea: Christ's love still sides with the outcast against the profiteer

judge.issue: "Was seen" drops the narrator's own strange meeting with him.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p40.plain: If everything people say about good and evil were true, my whole life would be one long crime.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p40.core_idea: Conventional morality would condemn every life

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p41.plain: Pity is only half of justice.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p42.plain: The only person who has wronged me is the one whose brother I wronged first.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p42.core_idea: The wrongs done to us echo the wrongs we did

judge.issue: Adds 'first', implying the speaker wronged first; the original sets no order.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p43.plain: When you see someone taken to prison, think that perhaps they are escaping a narrower prison; when you see someone drunk, think that perhaps they were fleeing something even uglier.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p43.core_idea: Assume hidden suffering behind others' failings

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p44.plain: I have often hated to protect myself, but if I were stronger I would not have needed that weapon.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p44.core_idea: Hatred is a weapon of the weak

judge.issue: 'Would not have needed' replaces 'would not have used'; shifts from choice to necessity.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p45.plain: How foolish is the person who tries to cover the hatred in their eyes with a smile.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p45.core_idea: A smile cannot hide hatred in the eyes

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p46.plain: Only those beneath me can envy or hate me, and only those above me can praise or belittle me; since none of this happens to me, I am above and below no one.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p46.core_idea: I stand equal to everyone, neither above nor below

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p47.plain: When you tell me you do not understand me, it is both more praise than I deserve and an insult you do not deserve.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p47.core_idea: Not being understood is both praise and insult

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p48.plain: How petty I am when life gives me gold and I give you silver, yet I think of myself as generous.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p48.core_idea: We give less than we receive yet feel generous

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p49.plain: When you reach the heart of life, you will find you are no higher than a criminal and no lower than a prophet.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p49.core_idea: At life's heart all people are equal

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p50.plain: How strange that you pity the slow of foot but not the slow of mind, and the blind in eye rather than the blind in heart.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p50.core_idea: We pity the wrong kinds of disability
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p50.plain_v1: It is strange that we pity people who are slow on their feet but not those slow in mind, and the blind in eye rather than the blind in heart.

judge_v1.issue: Shifts the reproach from 'you' to 'we', softening the address to the reader.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p51.plain: It is wiser for a lame person not to break their crutches over their enemy's head.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p51.core_idea: Do not destroy your own support in anger

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p52.plain: How blind is someone who gives to you from their pocket in order to take from your heart.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p52.core_idea: Giving in order to take is blindness

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p53.plain: Life is a procession: the slow find it too fast and drop out, and the fast find it too slow and drop out too.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p53.core_idea: Both the slow and the fast leave life's procession

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p54.plain: If sin exists, some of us commit it backwards by following our ancestors' footsteps, and some commit it forwards by overruling our children.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p54.core_idea: Sin lies in blindly following elders or dominating children

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p55.plain: The truly good person is one with all those who are thought of as bad.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p55.core_idea: True goodness stands with the condemned

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p56.plain: We are all prisoners, but some of us have cells with windows and some do not.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p56.core_idea: All are prisoners, some with windows

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p57.plain: It is strange that we all defend our wrongs more fiercely than our rights.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p57.core_idea: We defend our wrongs harder than our rights

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p58.plain: If we all confessed our sins to one another, we would laugh at how unoriginal we are; and if we revealed our virtues, we would laugh for the same reason.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p58.core_idea: Our sins and virtues are equally unoriginal

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p59.plain: Government is an agreement between you and me, and you and I are often wrong.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p59.core_idea: Government is as fallible as the people behind it

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p60.plain: Crime is either another word for need or a symptom of illness.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p60.core_idea: Crime springs from need or sickness

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p61.plain: Is there any greater fault than being aware of other people's faults?
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p61.core_idea: Noticing others' faults is itself a fault

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p62.plain: If someone laughs at you, you can pity them, but if you laugh at them you may never forgive yourself; if someone hurts you, you may forget it, but if you hurt them you will always remember.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p62.core_idea: Harm we do outweighs harm done to us

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p63.plain: In truth, the other person is your own most sensitive self in another body.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p63.core_idea: Others are your tender self in another body

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p64.plain: How careless you are to want others to fly with your wings when you cannot even give them a feather.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p64.core_idea: You cannot make others share gifts you cannot give

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p65.plain: A man once ate my bread and drank my wine and left laughing at me; when he came back for more I turned him away, and the angels laughed at me.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p65.core_idea: Refusing the ungrateful makes us the fools

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p66.plain: Hate is a dead thing, so who among you would want to be its tomb?
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p66.core_idea: Holding hate makes you a tomb

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p67.plain: The murdered person's honour is that they are not the murderer.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p67.core_idea: Better to suffer wrong than to commit it

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p68.plain: Humanity's true voice is in its quiet heart, never in its chattering mind.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p68.core_idea: Humanity speaks truly through its silent heart

judge.issue: 'Tribune' (champion, advocate) rendered as 'true voice'; slight loss of meaning.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p69.plain: They call me mad because I will not sell my days for gold, and I call them mad because they think my days have a price.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p69.core_idea: Your time is not for sale

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p70.plain: They lay out their gold, silver, ivory and ebony, and we lay out our hearts and spirits; yet they think they are the hosts and we the guests.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p70.core_idea: Those who give their hearts are the true hosts

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p71.plain: I would rather be the least of people, with dreams and the will to fulfil them, than the greatest with no dreams and no desires.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p71.core_idea: Better small with dreams than great without them

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p72.plain: The most pitiful person is the one who turns their dreams into money.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p72.core_idea: Selling your dreams for money is pitiful

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p73.plain: We all climb toward our heart's desire. If another climber steals your sack and purse and grows fat and loaded, pity him: his climb will be harder and longer. And if, lean as you are, you see him heaving himself upward, help him a step; it will speed you.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p73.core_idea: Pity and help those who rob you on the climb
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p73.plain_v1: We are all climbing toward what our hearts desire; if another climber steals your pack and purse and grows fat and heavy, pity him, since his climb will be harder, and help him a step, which will speed you too.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the condition of seeing the thief struggle upward before helping him a step.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p74.plain: You cannot judge anyone beyond what you know of them, and you know very little.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p74.core_idea: Our knowledge is too small to judge others

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p75.plain: The truly free person is the one who patiently carries the burden of the enslaved.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p75.core_idea: Freedom means patiently bearing others' burdens

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p76.plain: A thousand years ago my neighbour told me he hated life because it was nothing but pain; yesterday I passed a cemetery and saw life dancing on his grave.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p76.core_idea: Life goes on joyfully past those who reject it

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p77.plain: Conflict in nature is just disorder longing to become order.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p78.plain: Solitude is a silent storm that breaks off our dead branches, yet it sends our living roots deeper into the living earth.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p78.core_idea: Solitude clears the dead and deepens the living

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p79.plain: When I described the sea to a brook, it thought I was exaggerating; when I described a brook to the sea, it thought I was belittling.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p79.core_idea: Each judges truth by its own scale

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p80.plain: How narrow is a view that values the ant's busy work above the grasshopper's singing.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p80.core_idea: Song matters as much as industry

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p81.plain: What counts as the highest virtue here might count as the least in another world.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p81.core_idea: Virtue is relative to the world we are in

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p82.plain: If we did not measure and weigh things, we would be as amazed by a firefly as we are by the sun.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p83.plain: Death is no closer to the old than to the newborn, and neither is life.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p83.core_idea: Death and life are equally near at every age

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p84.plain: If you really must be frank, be frank in a beautiful way; otherwise stay quiet, for a man in our neighbourhood is dying.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p84.core_idea: Speak honestly with grace, or keep silent

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p85.plain: Perhaps a funeral on earth is a wedding feast among the angels.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p85.core_idea: Death here may be celebration beyond

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p86.plain: In truth we only ever talk to ourselves, but sometimes loudly enough for others to hear.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p86.core_idea: All speech is really talking to oneself

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p87.plain: The obvious is something nobody sees until someone puts it simply.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p87.core_idea: The obvious is unseen until simply said

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p88.plain: If the Milky Way were not inside me, how could I ever have seen or known it?
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p88.core_idea: We can know only what is already within us

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p89.plain: Perhaps to the sea a shell means its pearl, and perhaps to time coal means the diamond it becomes.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p89.core_idea: Things are defined by what they can become

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p90.plain: Fame is the shadow that passion casts when it stands in the light.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p91.plain: A root is a flower that wants nothing to do with fame.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p92.plain: Beyond beauty there is neither religion nor science.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p92.core_idea: Beauty underlies both religion and science

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p93.plain: Every great man I have known had something small in his nature, and that small thing kept him from idleness, madness or suicide.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p93.core_idea: A small flaw keeps the great grounded

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p94.plain: The truly great person is one who would rule no one and be ruled by no one.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p94.core_idea: Greatness is neither mastering nor being mastered

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p95.plain: Tolerance is love that has caught the disease of arrogance.
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p95.core_idea: Tolerance is love tainted by superiority

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p96.plain: A disagreement can be the quickest route between two minds.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p97.plain: I am both the flame and the dry brush, and one part of me burns up the other.

gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p98.plain: We are all seeking the top of the holy mountain, but would our road not be shorter if we treated the past as a map rather than a guide?
gibran-sand-and-foam-002-p98.core_idea: Use the past as a map, not a guide

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p01.plain: Wisdom stops being wisdom when it becomes too proud to cry, too serious to laugh, and too self-absorbed to look beyond itself.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p01.core_idea: Wisdom dies in pride, gravity and self-absorption

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p02.plain: If I had filled myself with everything you know, where would I have room for everything you do not know?
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p02.core_idea: Leave room for what is unknown

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p03.plain: I learned silence from talkers, tolerance from the intolerant, and kindness from the unkind; yet oddly I feel no gratitude to these teachers.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p03.core_idea: We learn virtues from people who lack them

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p04.plain: The silence of envious people is far too loud.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p04.core_idea: Envy is loud even in silence

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p05.plain: When you come to the end of what you should know, you will be at the beginning of what you should sense.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p06.plain: An exaggeration is a truth that has lost its temper.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p07.plain: If you can see only what light shows and hear only what sound announces, then you do not truly see or hear.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p07.core_idea: True perception goes beyond the senses

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p08.plain: You cannot laugh and be unkind at the same moment.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p09.plain: Closest to my heart are a king without a kingdom and a poor man who does not know how to beg.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p09.core_idea: Dignity in loss and poverty moves the heart

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p10.plain: A modest failure is nobler than a boastful success.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p11.plain: Dig anywhere in the earth and you will find treasure, but you must dig with a peasant's faith.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p12.plain: A fox chased by twenty riders and twenty hounds said they would surely kill it, but how poor and stupid they must be, since twenty foxes on asses with twenty wolves would never bother hunting one man.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p12.core_idea: Overwhelming force against the weak is foolish

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p13.plain: It is the mind in us that obeys the laws we make, never the spirit.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p13.core_idea: Man-made laws bind the mind, not the spirit

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p14.plain: I am a traveller and a navigator, and every day I discover a new region in my own soul.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p14.core_idea: Each day reveals new regions of the soul

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p15.plain: A woman protested that of course the war was righteous, because her son died in it.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p15.core_idea: Grief makes us call our losses righteous

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p16.plain: I told Life I wanted to hear Death speak, and Life simply raised her voice a little and said that I was hearing him now.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p17.plain: When you have solved every mystery of life, you long for death, since it is just one more mystery of life.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p18.plain: Birth and death are the two noblest acts of courage.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p18.core_idea: Birth and death are supreme acts of bravery

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p19.plain: My friend, we will stay strangers to life, to each other and to ourselves until you speak and I listen as if your voice were mine, and I stand before you as if before a mirror.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p19.core_idea: We become known only by seeing ourselves in each other

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p20.plain: People tell me that knowing myself would let me know everyone; I reply that only by seeking everyone will I know myself.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p21.plain: Each person is two people: one awake in the dark, the other asleep in the light.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p21.core_idea: We are awake in darkness and asleep in light

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p22.plain: A hermit gives up a broken-up, piecemeal world so that he can enjoy the whole world fully and without interruption.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p22.core_idea: The hermit leaves fragments to enjoy the whole

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p23.plain: Between the scholar and the poet lies open ground. A scholar who crosses it becomes wise; a poet who crosses it becomes a prophet.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p23.core_idea: Scholar and poet each grow by crossing toward the other

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p24.plain: I saw philosophers in the market carrying their heads in baskets and shouting that wisdom was for sale. Poor things: they have to sell their minds to feed their hearts.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p24.core_idea: Philosophers sell their minds to feed their hearts

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p25.plain: A philosopher pitied a street sweeper for his hard, dirty work. When the philosopher said his own job was studying human minds, deeds and desires, the sweeper smiled and pitied him too.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p25.core_idea: Studying human nature can be the dirtier job

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p26.plain: The person who listens to the truth is no less than the person who speaks it.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p26.core_idea: Hearing truth matters as much as speaking it

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p27.plain: No person can mark the line between what we need and what is luxury. Only angels can, and angels are both wise and a little sad.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p27.core_idea: Only angels can separate needs from luxuries

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p28.plain: Generosity means giving more than you can afford, and pride means taking less than you need.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p28.core_idea: Generosity gives beyond means; pride takes below need

judge.issue: 'More than you can afford' narrows 'more than you can' to money.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p29.plain: Really you owe nothing to any one person. You owe everything to everyone.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p29.core_idea: We owe everything to everyone, not to anyone

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p30.plain: Everyone who lived before us still lives with us now. None of us would want to be a rude host to them.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p30.core_idea: The dead live among us as our guests

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p31.plain: Whoever longs the most lives the longest.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p32.plain: People say a bird in the hand is worth more than many in the bush. But a bird and a feather still out of reach are worth more; chasing that feather is life itself.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p32.core_idea: Chasing what is out of reach is life itself

judge.issue: Drops the comparison with 'ten birds in the hand'; the reversal is blurred.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p33.plain: Great beauty holds me captive, but an even greater beauty sets me free, even from itself.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p33.core_idea: The greatest beauty frees rather than captures

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p34.plain: Beauty glows more brightly in the heart of someone who longs for it than in the eyes of someone who sees it.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p34.core_idea: Longing for beauty outshines seeing it

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p35.plain: I admire people who show me their minds and honour those who show me their dreams. So why do I feel shy, even a little ashamed, before someone who serves me?
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p35.core_idea: Being served brings an odd shame

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p36.plain: Talented people once took pride in serving princes. Now they take pride in serving the poor.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p36.core_idea: The gifted now find honour serving the poor

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p37.plain: The angels know that too many practical people live off the hard work of dreamers.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p37.core_idea: Practical people often live off dreamers' labour

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p38.plain: Wit is often a mask. Pull it off and you will find either an annoyed genius or mere cleverness showing off.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p38.core_idea: Wit often masks irritation or showing off

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p39.plain: Only people who carry secrets in their own hearts can guess the secrets in ours.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p39.core_idea: It takes secrets to sense secrets

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p40.plain: Anyone who will share your joy but not your pain loses the key to one of the seven gates of Paradise.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p40.core_idea: Friends must share pain as well as joy

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p41.plain: Yes, Nirvana exists: it is in leading your sheep to green grass, putting your child to sleep, and writing the last line of your poem.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p41.core_idea: Nirvana is found in ordinary fulfilled tasks

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p42.plain: We choose our joys and our sorrows long before we live through them.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p42.core_idea: We choose our joys and sorrows in advance

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p43.plain: Sadness is only a wall standing between two gardens.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p44.plain: When your joy or your sorrow grows great, the world around you shrinks.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p44.core_idea: Great joy or sorrow shrinks the world

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p45.plain: Desire is half of being alive; not caring is half of being dead.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p45.core_idea: Desire is life; indifference is death

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p46.plain: The bitterest part of today's sorrow is remembering yesterday's joy.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p46.core_idea: Past joy makes present sorrow bitterest

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p47.plain: People tell me I must choose between this world's pleasures and the next world's peace. I have chosen both, because I know the Supreme Poet wrote only one poem, and it fits together perfectly.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p47.core_idea: This world and the next are one poem

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p48.plain: Faith is an oasis in the heart that the caravan of thinking will never reach.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p49.plain: When you reach your highest point, you will desire only for the sake of desiring, hunger for hunger itself, and thirst for a greater thirst.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p49.core_idea: At our height, longing becomes its own aim

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p50.plain: If you tell your secrets to the wind, do not blame the wind for passing them on to the trees.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p50.core_idea: Do not blame others for secrets you spread

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p51.plain: Turtles can tell you more about the roads than hares can.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p51.core_idea: The slow traveller knows the road best

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p52.plain: It is strange that creatures without backbones have the hardest shells.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p52.core_idea: The spineless often wear the hardest shells

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p53.plain: Be thankful you do not have to live down a famous father or a rich uncle. Above all, be thankful no one will have to live down your fame or your wealth.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p53.core_idea: Be glad no fame or wealth burdens anyone

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p54.plain: A person who envies me is praising me without knowing it.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p55.plain: For a long time you were a dream in your mother's sleep, and then she woke up to give birth to you.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p55.core_idea: Each child begins as a mother's dream

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p56.plain: Some of our children justify our lives, and some are only our regrets.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p56.core_idea: Children can be justifications or regrets

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p57.plain: When night comes and you feel dark too, lie down and be dark on purpose. If you are still dark in the morning, get up and tell the day so. Pretending to night and day is foolish; they would laugh.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p57.core_idea: Own your darkness openly instead of pretending

judge.issue: Drops 'with a will' from the morning: the deliberate declaration 'I am still dark' is weakened.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p58.plain: A mountain hidden in mist is still not a hill, and an oak in the rain is still not a weeping willow.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p58.core_idea: Passing conditions do not change true nature

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p59.plain: When I stood before you like a clear mirror, you saw your own image in me and said you loved me. But really you loved yourself, seen in me.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p59.core_idea: Some love is self-love seen in another

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p60.plain: When you enjoy loving your neighbour, it stops being a virtue.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p60.core_idea: Love that is enjoyed is no longer virtue

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p61.plain: Love that is not always welling up fresh is always dying.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p61.core_idea: Love must keep renewing or it dies

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p62.plain: You cannot be young and understand youth at the same time. Youth is too busy living to know, and knowledge is too busy searching for itself to live.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p62.core_idea: Youth lives without knowing; knowledge knows without living

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p63.plain: Watching from a window, you might call a nun noble and a prostitute shameful. But listen quietly and a voice says one seeks it in prayer, the other in pain, and both have room for its spirit.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p63.core_idea: The saint and the sinner both seek the divine

judge.issue: The voice speaking as 'me' becomes 'it'; drops 'in your innocence'.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p64.plain: A great person has two hearts: one that bleeds and one that holds back and endures.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p64.core_idea: Greatness both feels pain and patiently endures

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p65.plain: If someone tells a lie that hurts no one, why not think of it kindly: their facts were too small a house for their imagination, so they moved somewhere roomier?
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p65.core_idea: Harmless lies are imagination outgrowing facts

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p66.plain: Behind every closed door lies a deeply sealed mystery.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p66.core_idea: Every closed door hides a mystery

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p67.plain: Waiting is the sound of time's hoofbeats.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p67.core_idea: In waiting we feel time passing

judge.issue: 'Sound of time's hoofbeats' adds an interpretation to 'the hoofs of time'.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p68.plain: What if trouble were a new window opened in the eastern wall of your house, where the sun rises?
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p68.core_idea: Trouble may open a new window of light

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p69.plain: You may forget someone you laughed with, but you will never forget someone you cried with.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p69.core_idea: Shared tears bind us more than shared laughter

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p70.plain: Salt must be strangely holy, since it is found both in our tears and in the sea.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p70.core_idea: Salt links our tears to the sea

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p71.plain: You are only a small piece of your huge true self: a mouth looking for bread, and a hand that blindly holds a cup for a thirsty mouth.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p71.core_idea: We are fragments of a far greater self

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p72.plain: If you could rise even a little above race, nation and self, you would truly become like God.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p72.core_idea: Rising above race, nation and self is godlike

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p73.plain: I would not complain about the sea at low tide. The ship is sound and our Captain capable; it is only your stomach that is upset.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p73.core_idea: Our unease is not the voyage's fault

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p74.plain: What we long for and cannot reach is dearer to us than what we already have.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p74.core_idea: The unattained is dearer than the attained

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p75.plain: From a cloud you would see no borders between countries and no markers between farms. It is a pity you cannot sit on a cloud.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p76.plain: Long ago seven white doves flew up a mountain, and one watcher noticed a black spot on one wing. Now the valley's people tell of seven black doves.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p76.core_idea: A small flaw grows into the whole story

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p77.plain: In autumn I buried my sorrows in my garden. In spring they grew into flowers unlike any others, and my neighbours asked me for their seeds for their own gardens.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p77.core_idea: Buried sorrows can bloom into beauty others want

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p78.plain: It is misery to hold out an empty hand and receive nothing. But it is hopelessness to hold out a full hand and find no one to take what you offer.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p78.core_idea: Worse than receiving nothing is having none receive

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p79.plain: I long for eternity because there I will meet the poems I never wrote and the pictures I never painted.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p80.plain: Art is a step from nature toward the Infinite.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p80.core_idea: Art moves from nature toward the Infinite

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p81.plain: Even hands that make crowns of thorns are better than hands that do nothing.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p82.plain: Our holiest tears never look for our eyes.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p82.core_idea: The deepest grief is not wept outwardly

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p83.plain: Every person descends from every king and every slave who ever lived.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p83.core_idea: All of us share every ancestor

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p84.plain: Did Judas's mother love her son any less than Mary loved Jesus?
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p84.core_idea: A mother's love does not depend on the child

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p85.plain: Three miracles of Jesus are missing from the Bible: he was a man like us, he had a sense of humour, and he knew he was a conqueror even while defeated.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p85.core_idea: Jesus's humanity and humour were miracles too

judge.issue: Drops 'our Brother', which carries the passage's intimate stance toward Jesus.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p86.plain: Crucified One, you are crucified on my heart, and the nails through your hands pierce my heart too. A stranger passing this place tomorrow will not know two bled here; he will think it one man's blood.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p86.core_idea: The believer bleeds with the crucified Christ

judge.issue: 'This Golgotha' becomes 'this place', losing the identification of the heart with Golgotha.

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p87.plain: The Blessed Mountain is the highest in the world. Whoever reaches its top wants only to come down and be with those in the deepest valley; that is why it is called blessed.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p87.core_idea: True height makes us want to serve the lowest

gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p88.plain: Every thought I have locked up in words, I must set free through my actions.
gibran-sand-and-foam-003-p88.core_idea: Words must be freed through deeds

gita-arnold-001-p01.plain: Krishna tells the prince that the senses' heat and cold, sorrow and joy, are brief and changing; bear them as the wise do. The soul that stays calm through sorrow and joy alike lives the undying life.
gita-arnold-001-p01.core_idea: A calm soul through joy and sorrow is undying

gita-arnold-001-p02.plain: The spirit was never born and will never end; beginnings and endings are dreams. It stays birthless, deathless and unchanging forever, untouched by death even when its body seems dead.
gita-arnold-001-p02.core_idea: The spirit is never born and never dies

gita-arnold-001-p03.plain: Just as a person takes off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the spirit lightly sets aside its body and moves on to a new home.
gita-arnold-001-p03.core_idea: The spirit changes bodies like clothes

gita-arnold-001-p04.plain: Krishna tells the prince that living things come from the unseen and return to the unseen at death; only the in-between is seen. So what is there to grieve?
gita-arnold-001-p04.core_idea: Birth and death are unseen; why grieve?

gita-arnold-001-p05.plain: Krishna says: do not crave. Do right for its own sake, not for its results. Keep working, make your work your devotion, set self aside, and stay even in good or bad; that evenness is Yoga.
gita-arnold-001-p05.core_idea: Act rightly without attachment to results

judge.issue: Drops 'contemning gain and merit'; scorn of reward is only partly carried by 'set self aside'.

gita-arnold-001-p06.plain: Krishna says a right action is worth far less than a rightly thinking mind. Take refuge in your soul and make your heaven there, and scorn those who are good only for the rewards.
gita-arnold-001-p06.core_idea: A right mind matters more than right acts

gita-arnold-002-p01.plain: Someone who is not crushed by sorrow or carried away by joy, who lives beyond passion, fear and anger, and rests in calm, deep contemplation, is the true sage.
gita-arnold-002-p01.core_idea: The sage stays steady in sorrow and joy

gita-arnold-002-p02.plain: Dwelling on sense objects breeds attraction, then desire, passion and recklessness, until memory, purpose and mind are lost. But handling them without love or hate, with a free soul in charge, brings tranquillity, an end to earthly pain, and peace.
gita-arnold-002-p02.core_idea: Dwelling on desires ruins; mastering them brings peace

gita-arnold-002-p03.plain: Like the ocean, which takes in rivers from every land yet never overflows, the perfected person takes in the world's tempting streams without being stirred and remains the same sea.
gita-arnold-002-p03.core_idea: The perfected person absorbs desire unmoved, like the sea

gita-arnold-002-p04.plain: It is better to do your own task as best you can, even failing, than to take up another's, however good it looks. Dying in your own duty is no harm; seekers of other paths keep wandering.
gita-arnold-002-p04.core_idea: Better your own duty, imperfectly, than another's

gita-arnold-003-p01.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that even if he were the worst of all wrongdoers, the ship of Truth would carry him safely across the sea of his wrongs.
gita-arnold-003-p01.core_idea: Truth carries even the worst sinner across

gita-arnold-003-p02.plain: Do not be too happy when joy comes or too sad when grief comes; stay steady and fixed on Brahma.
gita-arnold-003-p02.core_idea: Stay steady in Brahma through joy and grief

gita-arnold-003-p03.plain: Sense pleasures are wombs that breed certain grief; they begin and end, and the wise take no delight in them. But whoever learns, while still in the body, to master lust and anger is blessed.
gita-arnold-003-p03.core_idea: Mastering lust and anger brings blessing

gita-arnold-003-p04.plain: Krishna says true religion is not for those who fast or feast too much, oversleep, or exhaust themselves with vigils. True piety is moderation in eating, rest, play, wishes and deeds, with timely sleep and waking.
gita-arnold-003-p04.core_idea: True piety is moderation in all things

gita-arnold-003-p05.plain: The Yogi's mind is like a lamp burning steadily out of the wind: shut away from the storms of the senses and burning brightly toward Heaven.
gita-arnold-003-p05.core_idea: A yogi's mind is a sheltered, steady flame

gita-arnold-003-p06.plain: Each time the heart breaks loose, wild and wavering, rein it back under the soul's control. Perfect bliss grows only in a calm heart, a spirit free of passion and wrong, given to the Infinite.
gita-arnold-003-p06.core_idea: Keep bringing the wandering heart back

gita-arnold-003-p07.plain: Krishna admits to Arjuna that the human heart is truly hard to restrain and always wavering. Yet it can be tamed through habit, by practising self-command.
gita-arnold-003-p07.core_idea: The restless heart is tamed by practice

gita-arnold-004-p01.plain: Krishna says he is the freshness of water, the light of moon and sun, the sacred word, the scent of wet earth, the breath in all that moves, the root of everything, and the wisdom of the wise.
gita-arnold-004-p01.core_idea: God is the essence within all things

judge.issue: Drops several attributes (taste of water, fire's light, holiness, strength of seed, greatness).

gita-arnold-004-p02.plain: Krishna says that whoever offers him, with faith and love, even a leaf, a flower, a fruit or some water, he accepts that offering made with a loving heart.
gita-arnold-004-p02.core_idea: God accepts the humblest gift given in love

gita-arnold-004-p03.plain: Krishna says that if someone living an evil life turns their mind straight to him, count them among the good: they have chosen the high road, will soon be righteous, and will reach unchanging peace.
gita-arnold-004-p03.core_idea: Turning to God makes even the wicked good

gita-arnold-005-p01.plain: Krishna says that intellect, skill, endurance, self-control, truthfulness, calm, joy and grief, birth and death, fear and courage, shame and honour, gentleness, peace, laughter, tears, devotion, generosity and the will to help all come as his gifts.
gita-arnold-005-p01.core_idea: Every human quality is God's gift

gita-arnold-005-p02.plain: Krishna says the wise, knowing him as the source of all, fix their hearts on him and find happiness and peace. To those who love him he gives a clear mind, and dwells within to dispel their ignorance.
gita-arnold-005-p02.core_idea: God lights the minds of those who love him

judge.issue: Drops 'whereby they draw to Me' and 'all for love of them'; the gift's purpose and motive lost.

gita-arnold-005-p03.plain: Krishna says he is the Spirit seated deep in every creature's heart: they come from him, live by him, and leave at his word.
gita-arnold-005-p03.core_idea: God is the Spirit in every heart

gita-arnold-006-p01.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna he can be known, seen and entered only through full service, perfect faith and total surrender. Whoever does everything for him, finds him in all things, worships always and loves all he has made comes to him.
gita-arnold-006-p01.core_idea: God is reached through total love and surrender

judge.issue: Drops 'for Love's sole end', the motive of love behind the devotee's acts.

gita-arnold-006-p02.plain: If you are too weak to fix yourself on Me always, don't despair: worship Me steadily; if not, work for Me; if even that fails, take refuge in Me and give up the fruits of your work. Worship beats knowledge, renunciation beats both, and peace lies very near renunciation.
gita-arnold-006-p02.core_idea: Whatever your weakness, God offers a lower step
gita-arnold-006-p02.plain_v1: Krishna says: if you cannot keep your mind on him, do not despair. Worship him; failing that, work for him; failing that, bring him your failure and let go of results. Eternal peace lies very near renunciation.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the closing ranking: worship above knowing, renunciation above all; secondary teaching lost.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the ranking: worship above knowing, renunciation above both.

gita-arnold-006-p03.plain: Krishna says he loves the person who neither troubles others nor is troubled by them, is free of anger, beyond gladness, grief and fear, calm, pure and balanced, working with him yet detached from all work.
gita-arnold-006-p03.core_idea: God loves the calm, detached, untroubled person

gita-arnold-006-p04.plain: Krishna loves the person who treats friend and foe alike, meets shame and glory, pleasure and pain with equal peace, is free of desire, unmoved by praise or slander, and steadfast in him.
gita-arnold-006-p04.core_idea: God loves the one who stays even in all things

gita-arnold-007-p01.plain: Krishna lists the signs of someone on the path to heavenly birth: fearlessness, striving for wisdom, generosity, self-restraint, humility, truthfulness, harmlessness, slowness to anger, letting go easily, kindness to sufferers, contentment, patience, purity and no thirst for revenge or self-importance.
gita-arnold-007-p01.core_idea: The virtues that mark the path to heaven

judge.issue: List condensed; drops love of study, charity that sees no faults, tenderness, mild bearing.

gita-arnold-007-p02.plain: Krishna says the doors to Hell, through which people go to ruin, are three: lust, anger and greed. Avoid all three.
gita-arnold-007-p02.core_idea: Lust, anger and greed are hell's doors

gita-arnold-007-p03.plain: Words that hurt no one, that are always true, gentle and kind, and the words spoken in reading sacred scripture: these make up true religion in speech.
gita-arnold-007-p03.core_idea: Kind, true speech is a form of worship

gita-arnold-007-p04.plain: Krishna says true action is doing your duty faithfully because it is right, not clinging to the work or its reward, untroubled by failure or success. No one embodied can stop acting; giving up the profit is true renunciation.
gita-arnold-007-p04.core_idea: True renunciation is acting without wanting rewards

fix.display_text:
But, Arjun!
Abstaining from attachment to the work,
Abstaining from rewardment in the work,
While yet one doeth it full faithfully,
Saying, "'Tis right to do!" that is "true" act
And abstinence! Who doeth duties so,
Unvexed if his work fail, if it succeed
Unflattered, in his own heart justified,
Quit of debates and doubts, his is "true" act:
For, being in the body, none may stand
Wholly aloof from act; yet, who abstains
From profit of his acts is abstinent.
fix.reason: stray space inside quote; missing apostrophe in 'Tis

gita-arnold-008-p01.plain: Krishna says the rightful doer acts without self-seeking, humble, determined and steady, the same in good or bad fortune, content simply to do right; that person truly acts.
gita-arnold-008-p01.core_idea: The true doer acts humbly, without self-seeking

fix.display_text:
There is the "rightful" doer. He who acts
Free from self-seeking, humble, resolute,
Steadfast, in good or evil hap the same,
Content to do aright--he "truly" acts.
fix.reason: missing space after quote; hyphen should be dash

gita-arnold-008-p02.plain: Good pleasure lasts and banishes pain for ever. It tastes bitter as poison at first but later sweet as the nectar of immortality. Drink it; it rises from the spirit's deep contentment.
gita-arnold-008-p02.core_idea: True pleasure is bitter first, sweet later

gita-arnold-008-p03.plain: Better your own duty done imperfectly than another's done well. Whoever does his nature-given task does not sin; don't abandon it, Prince, though it bears blame, for all work has fault as fire has smoke. Only one working with free mind, subdued soul, dead desires and renounced results is released.
gita-arnold-008-p03.core_idea: Do your own duty though it is imperfect
gita-arnold-008-p03.plain_v1: Krishna says your own work done with faults beats another's done well. Do not drop your natural duty because it carries blame; every work has some, as every flame has smoke. Perfection comes through renouncing results.

judge_v1.issue: Drops conditions for release (unfettered mind, subdued soul, dead desires) and 'shall not fall in sin'.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops 'not fall in sin' and the full conditions of release; 'perfection' is loose.

gita-arnold-008-p04.plain: Krishna tells Arjuna that he is precious and well loved. Give him your heart, worship him, serve him and cling to him in faith and love, and you will come to him; he promises, because Arjuna is dear to him.
gita-arnold-008-p04.core_idea: God promises to receive those who love him

judge.issue: Shifts between addressing the reader as 'you' and speaking of Arjuna in the third person.

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p01.plain: It is empty to follow bodily desires that end in misery, to want a long life but not a good one, to think only of this life, and to love what quickly passes instead of hurrying toward eternal joy.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p01.core_idea: Living only for passing things is vanity

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p02.plain: However much you know, there is far more you do not. Do not be proud; admit your ignorance, since many know Scripture better than you. To learn anything worthwhile, love being unknown and counted as nothing.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p02.core_idea: Admit your ignorance and love being unknown

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p03.plain: The best lesson is to judge yourself humbly and others kindly. Even if your neighbour sins openly, do not think yourself better; you cannot know how long you will stay good. We are all weak; count no one weaker.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p03.core_idea: Think humbly of yourself and kindly of others

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p04.plain: Nothing troubles you more than your own undisciplined heart. A good person plans inwardly and submits all to right reason. The hardest battle is self-mastery, and that should be our aim: growing daily stronger than self.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p04.core_idea: The hardest battle is mastering yourself

judge.issue: Compresses inner ordering of outward works and resisting the evil will into vague "plans inwardly".

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p05.plain: In this life every perfection has some flaw. Humbly knowing yourself leads to God more surely than deep learning. Learning is not wrong, but a good conscience and a holy life are better than everything.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p05.core_idea: Humble self-knowledge leads to God better than learning

judge.issue: Drops the line that all our sight has some darkness in this life.

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p06.plain: Only someone with great love is truly great. The truly great think themselves small; the truly wise count earthly things as rubbish to gain Christ; the truly learned do God's will instead of their own.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p06.core_idea: True greatness is love, humility and doing God's will

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p07.plain: Wisdom means not acting hastily, not clinging to your opinions, and not believing or repeating all you hear. Seek advice from a wise, conscientious person and learn from your betters. A good life makes one wise before God; the humbler and more obedient to God, the wiser and more peaceful.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p07.core_idea: Wisdom is humility, caution and good counsel
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p07.plain_v1: Wisdom means not rushing to act, not clinging to your opinions, not believing or repeating all you hear, and taking advice from wise, good people. The humbler you are and the more obedient to God, the wiser and calmer.

judge_v1.issue: Drops that a good life makes one wise toward God and the call to seek instruction from betters.

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p08.plain: Wanting anything too much makes you restless. The proud and greedy never rest; the humble live in peace. Someone not yet dead to self is easily tempted by small things, and sad and irritable when giving up pleasures.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p08.core_idea: Excessive desire breeds restlessness; humility brings peace

judge.issue: Drops that the weak and carnal find withdrawing from desires hard; anger at opposition softened.

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p09.plain: Trusting in people or created things is futile. Don't be ashamed to serve others for Christ's love or to seem poor. Hope in God, not yourself: do what you can and God will help. Trust not learning or cleverness but God's favour; he resists the proud and helps the humble.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p09.core_idea: Trust God, not yourself or other people
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p09.plain_v1: Life is empty if you trust people or created things. Do not be ashamed to serve others for love of Jesus Christ. Hope in God, do what you can, and God will help; he resists the proud, favours the humble.

judge_v1.issue: Drops warnings not to trust learning or cleverness and to accept being reckoned poor.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops being reckoned poor and not trusting in learning or cleverness.

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p10.plain: Don't take pride in wealth, powerful friends, strength, looks or skill; illness can take the body's gifts quickly, and every good gift comes from God, who wants to give even Himself.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p10.core_idea: Boast only in God, the giver of every gift

judge.issue: Drops the positive command to boast in God instead.

imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p11.plain: Don't think yourself better than others; God sees differently than people do. Assume others have more good than you. Putting yourself below everyone does no harm; the humble have peace, the proud have envy and anger.
imitation-of-christ-benham-001-p11.core_idea: Humility brings peace; pride brings envy and anger

judge.issue: Drops not being proud of good works and risk of appearing worse before God.

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p01.plain: We should love everyone but not be close with everyone. Someone admired from a distance may disappoint in person, and getting too familiar can make others see our faults and like us less.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p01.core_idea: Love all, but keep close friendship for few

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p02.plain: People naturally favour those who agree with them, but with Christ among us we must sometimes give up our opinion for peace. No one knows everything, so listen to others; yielding for God's sake does you more good.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p02.core_idea: Yield your opinion sometimes, for peace and God

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p03.plain: I often wish I had stayed quiet and kept away from people. We chatter because we hope for comfort and distraction, talking of what we love or hate, yet we seldom return to silence with a clear conscience.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p03.core_idea: Much talk seldom leaves the conscience unharmed

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p04.plain: You can have great peace if you stop busying yourself with what others say and do. Someone absorbed in other people's affairs and neglecting their inner self cannot stay at peace; the single-hearted are blessed with peace.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p04.core_idea: Mind your own inner life to find peace

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p05.plain: Breaking a habit is hard, opposing your own will harder. But if you can't overcome small obstacles, how will you overcome great ones? Resist your will early and unlearn bad habits before they lead to worse. If you knew the peace and joy holy living brings, you'd be more zealous.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p05.core_idea: Resist bad habits early, while they are small
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p05.plain_v1: Breaking a habit is hard, and going against your own will is harder. If you can't beat small obstacles, how will you beat big ones? Resist bad habits early, before they drag you into worse.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the closing idea: peace and joy a holy life brings, and the call to spiritual zeal.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the closing point about the peace and joy a holy life brings.

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p06.plain: Sorrows and unfair criticism are good for us sometimes. They remind us we are only passing through this world, keep us humble, and make us look harder for God's approval when people misjudge us.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p06.core_idea: Adversity and unfair judgment teach humility

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p07.plain: No one is free of temptation while alive, because its root is inside us. One trouble passes and another comes. Running away from temptation doesn't work; we overcome it by endurance and true humility.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p07.core_idea: Temptation is overcome by endurance, not flight

judge.issue: Drops being born in concupiscence, the Fall, and that fleeing temptation can deepen it.

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p08.plain: Temptation starts with an unsteady mind and little trust in God; a careless person is tossed like a ship without a rudder. As fire tests iron, temptation tests a good person and shows us what we really are.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p08.core_idea: Temptation reveals what we truly are

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p09.plain: Trials show how far a person has grown. Being devout is easy when nothing hurts; patience in hardship is real progress. Some resist big temptations but fall to small ones, which humbles them out of self-reliance.

judge.issue: "Kept safe from great temptations" becomes "resist" them; drops the greater reward in trials.

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p10.plain: Look to yourself and don't judge what others do. Judging others is wasted effort and leads to error and sin; examining yourself is always worthwhile. Our feelings skew our judgment, less so when we desire only God.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p10.core_idea: Examine yourself instead of judging others

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p11.plain: Many people seek their own ends without realising it. They seem calm while things go their way, but as soon as their wishes are thwarted they are shaken and upset.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p11.core_idea: Hidden self-interest shows when wishes are thwarted

imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p12.plain: Without love no deed is worth anything, but anything done in love, however small, bears good fruit, because God looks at how much a person is able to do more than at the size of the deed.
imitation-of-christ-benham-002-p12.core_idea: Small deeds done in love bear fruit

imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p01.plain: Whoever loves much does much, and whoever does well does much. Doing well means serving the common good over your own. Much that looks like love is really self-will or hope of reward.
imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p01.core_idea: Loving much and serving others is doing much

judge.issue: Drops that false charity is "carnality" springing from natural inclination.

imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p02.plain: What you can't fix in yourself or others, bear patiently until God changes it; it may be good for testing your patience. Meanwhile ask God to help you bear these things willingly.
imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p02.core_idea: Bear patiently what you cannot change

judge.issue: Drops that without patience our merits are worth little.

imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p03.plain: Be patient with other people's faults, since you have many that others must put up with. If you can't make yourself what you want, how can you remake someone else? We want others perfect but don't fix ourselves.
imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p03.core_idea: Bear others' faults; you have your own

imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p04.plain: We want others corrected and restricted but refuse it for ourselves, so we rarely judge our neighbour by the same standard as ourselves. And if everyone were perfect, what would we have to bear from others for God's sake?
imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p04.core_idea: We rarely judge others by our own standard

imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p05.plain: Each day we should renew our commitment and stir up our zeal as though it were the first day of our turning to God, asking Him to help us make a good start, since so far we have done nothing.
imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p05.core_idea: Begin again each day as if for the first time

imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p06.plain: If you can't examine yourself constantly, do it at least twice a day: set your intentions in the morning, and in the evening review how you did in word, deed and thought, where you may have wronged God and others.
imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p06.core_idea: Set intentions each morning, review each evening

imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p07.plain: Make time for meditation and think often of God's mercies. Drop idle curiosity, gossip and wandering about, and you will find enough time for reflection. The greatest saints avoided company and lived hidden with God.
imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p07.core_idea: Cut idle talk to make time for God

judge.issue: Drops studying what brings sorrow for sin rather than amusement.

imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p08.plain: Long talk with people often leaves us less than we were; silence is easier than measured speech. So whoever seeks the spiritual must go apart from the crowd with Jesus. Only one who loves staying home goes out safely, who loves silence speaks safely, who loves obeying commands safely.
imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p08.core_idea: Only lovers of silence speak safely
imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p08.plain_v1: Someone said that each time he went among people he came back less of a man. Silence is easier than talking without excess. Only those who love quiet and obedience can safely speak, lead and command.

judge_v1.issue: Drops going apart with Jesus and the home/abroad sayings; the spiritual frame is lost.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the call to go apart from the crowd with Jesus to seek the spiritual.

imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p09.plain: Those most admired often fall hardest through overconfidence, so inner temptation is good for many, keeping them from pride. How clear a conscience and how much peace belong to the one who drops vain worries and hopes only in God.
imitation-of-christ-benham-003-p09.core_idea: Temptation guards against pride; hope in God brings peace

judge.issue: Drops not entangling with the world or seeking passing joys, and thinking only of divine things.

imitation-of-christ-benham-004-p01.plain: In solitude you find what you often lose out in the world. Kept up, solitude grows sweet; neglected, it becomes tiresome. Stay with it from the start and it becomes a dear friend and comfort.
