judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the brief fundamental principles that cleanse and send you back content.

meditations-004-p05.plain: Death, like birth, is a mystery of nature: a coming together of elements and a coming apart into them. It is nothing to be ashamed of, since it is not against the nature or reason of a thinking being.
meditations-004-p05.core_idea: Death is as natural as birth

meditations-004-p06.plain: Drop your judgment, and the complaint "I have been harmed" goes with it. Drop that complaint, and the harm is gone.
meditations-004-p06.core_idea: Harm lies in your judgment of it

meditations-004-p07.plain: Don't see things the way the person who wrongs you sees them, or the way they want you to; see them as they truly are.
meditations-004-p07.core_idea: See things as they are, not as wrongdoers would

meditations-004-p08.plain: Keep two rules ready: do only what reason suggests for the good of others, and change your mind when someone corrects you, but only when convinced it is just or useful, not because it is pleasant or flattering.
meditations-004-p08.core_idea: Act by reason; change your mind for good reasons

meditations-004-p09.plain: Don't live as if you had ten thousand years. Death hangs over you. While you live and still can, be good.
meditations-004-p09.core_idea: Death is near; be good now

meditations-005-p01.plain: You avoid much trouble by not watching what your neighbour says, does or thinks, and attending only to whether your own actions are just and pure. Don't look around at others' bad conduct; run straight along your line.
meditations-005-p01.core_idea: Mind your own conduct, not others'

meditations-005-p02.plain: Whatever is beautiful is beautiful in itself; praise adds nothing and blame takes nothing away. Truly beautiful things, like truth, kindness or modesty, need nothing more. Is an emerald worse for not being praised?
meditations-005-p02.core_idea: Beauty does not depend on praise

meditations-005-p03.plain: Speaking to the Universe: whatever suits you suits me; nothing is too early or too late if it is on time for you. All your seasons bring is fruit to me, Nature: all comes from you and returns to you.
meditations-005-p03.core_idea: Accept whatever nature brings, in its time

meditations-005-p04.plain: Rather than merely doing few things, do what is necessary and what reason asks of a social being. Most of what we say and do is needless; cut it and gain peace. Ask: is this necessary? Cut needless thoughts too.
meditations-005-p04.core_idea: Cut the unnecessary from acts and thoughts

meditations-005-p05.plain: Love the craft you have learned, however humble, and be content with it. Live the rest of your life as one who has entrusted everything to the gods with his whole soul, being neither tyrant nor slave to anyone.
meditations-005-p05.core_idea: Love your work; be no one's master or slave

meditations-005-p06.plain: Even lasting fame is nothing. What deserves our serious effort is just one thing: fair thoughts, actions for the common good, honest words, and a willingness to accept everything that happens as necessary and natural.
meditations-005-p06.core_idea: Fame is nothing; live justly and accept what comes

meditations-005-p07.plain: Everything lasts only a day, both the one who remembers and the one who is remembered.
meditations-005-p07.core_idea: All, remembered or remembering, is brief

meditations-005-p08.plain: You will die soon, and you are still not simple, not calm, still fearing harm from outside, not kind to everyone, and not yet placing wisdom only in acting justly.
meditations-005-p08.core_idea: Death is near and you still have work to do

meditations-005-p09.plain: Time is like a fast-flowing river of events: as soon as something appears it is swept away, another takes its place, and that too is swept away.
meditations-005-p09.core_idea: Time sweeps everything away like a river

meditations-005-p10.plain: Everything that happens is as ordinary and familiar as roses in spring and fruit in summer, including illness, death, slander, betrayal, and whatever else pleases or upsets fools.
meditations-005-p10.core_idea: Even hardship is as ordinary as the seasons

meditations-005-p11.plain: If a god told you that you would die tomorrow or the day after, you would hardly care which, since the difference is tiny. So think it no great matter whether you die many years from now or tomorrow.
meditations-005-p11.core_idea: A long life or short, the difference is small

meditations-005-p12.plain: See how brief and worthless human things are: yesterday a speck, tomorrow ashes. Pass this short time in line with nature and end content, like a ripe olive falling, blessing nature and thanking the tree it grew on.
meditations-005-p12.core_idea: Live by nature and depart content

judge.issue: "A little mucus" softened to "a speck".

meditations-005-p13.plain: Be like a headland that the waves keep crashing against: it stands firm and calms the raging water around it.
meditations-005-p13.core_idea: Stand firm like a rock against waves

meditations-006-p01.plain: Don't say "I'm unhappy because this happened." Say "I'm fortunate, because though this happened I stay free from pain, not crushed by the present or afraid of the future." It could happen to anyone, but not everyone would stay untroubled.
meditations-006-p01.core_idea: Bearing misfortune well is good fortune

meditations-006-p02.plain: When you don't want to get up in the morning, remember: I am rising to do a human being's work. Why resent doing what I exist for? Was I made to lie under the blankets and keep warm?
meditations-006-p02.core_idea: You were made for work, not for bed

meditations-006-p03.plain: How easy it is to push away and wipe out every troubling or unsuitable impression, and at once be completely calm.
meditations-006-p03.core_idea: You can dismiss troubling thoughts and be calm

meditations-006-p04.plain: Treat every word and act that accords with nature as fitting for you, and don't be put off by others' blame. If something is good to do or say, do it. Ignore others' ways; follow your own and nature's.
meditations-006-p04.core_idea: Do what is right; ignore others' blame

judge.issue: Drops "the way of both is one", the unity of one's own and common nature.

meditations-006-p05.plain: You say people can't admire your cleverness. Fine, but you can show qualities fully in your power: sincerity, seriousness, endurance, contentment, kindness, frankness, simplicity, generosity of spirit. No natural lack excuses you, yet you choose to fall short.
meditations-006-p05.core_idea: Show the virtues already within your power

fix.display_text: Thou sayest, Men cannot admire the sharpness of thy wits.⁠—Be it so: but there are many other things of which thou canst not say, I am not formed for them by nature. Show those qualities then which are altogether in thy power, sincerity, gravity, endurance of labour, aversion to pleasure, contentment with thy portion and with few things, benevolence, frankness, no love of superfluity, freedom from trifling, magnanimity. Dost thou not see how many qualities thou art immediately able to exhibit, in which there is no excuse of natural incapacity and unfitness, and yet thou still remainest voluntarily below the mark?

judge.issue: List loses "aversion to pleasure" and "no love of superfluity".

meditations-006-p06.plain: Some who do a good turn count it as a favour owed; others silently treat the person as in their debt. A third kind hardly notices, like a vine that bears grapes, asks nothing, and goes on bearing.
meditations-006-p06.core_idea: Do good without seeking credit, like a vine

judge.issue: Drops the horse, dog and bee images and not calling others to come and see.

meditations-006-p07.plain: Don't be disgusted or discouraged when you fail to live by right principles. Come back, be content if most of what you do fits human nature, and treat philosophy not as a harsh master but as a soothing remedy.
meditations-006-p07.core_idea: When you fail, return gently and keep going

judge.issue: Drops "love this to which thou returnest" and reposing in reason.

meditations-007-p01.plain: Your mind takes on the character of your habitual thoughts, because the soul is dyed by them. So dye it with thoughts like this: wherever a person can live, they can also live well.
meditations-007-p01.core_idea: Your thoughts shape the character of your mind

meditations-007-p02.plain: Nothing happens to anyone that they are not made by nature to bear. Others face the same things and stay firm, from ignorance or wanting to look brave. It is shameful that ignorance and vanity should outdo wisdom.
meditations-007-p02.core_idea: You are made to bear what happens to you

meditations-007-p03.plain: Things themselves cannot touch, enter or move the soul at all. The soul moves itself, and whatever judgments it chooses to make shape how things appear to it.
meditations-007-p03.core_idea: Only your judgments move your soul

meditations-007-p04.plain: I must do good to people and bear with them. But when they block my proper actions, they are as neutral as sun or wind. They can hinder my acts, not my mind, which turns obstacles into help.
meditations-007-p04.core_idea: The mind turns obstacles into help

meditations-007-p05.plain: Think often how quickly everything passes: all flows like a river, hardly anything stands still, and the endless past and future swallow everything. Isn't it foolish, then, to be puffed up or tormented by things that trouble you so briefly?
meditations-007-p05.core_idea: All passes quickly; don't be tormented by it

meditations-007-p06.plain: Does someone wrong me? That's their concern; they have their own character and actions. I have what universal nature wants me to have now, and I do what my nature wants me to do now.

meditations-007-p07.plain: Are you angry at someone's body odour or bad breath? Anger does no good; it comes naturally. He could see his fault? You have reason too: use it to show him his error. If he listens, anger is needless.
meditations-007-p07.core_idea: Correct others with reason, not anger

fix.display_text: Art thou angry with him whose armpits stink? Art thou angry with him whose mouth smells foul? What good will this anger do thee? He has such a mouth, he has such armpits: it is necessary that such an emanation must come from such things⁠—but the man has reason, it will be said, and he is able, if he takes pain, to discover wherein he offends⁠—I wish thee well of thy discovery. Well then, and thou hast reason: by thy rational faculty stir up his rational faculty; show him his error, admonish him. For if he listens, thou wilt cure him, and there is no need of anger.

meditations-007-p08.plain: Remember how much you have endured; that your life's story is complete and your service done; how many beautiful things you have seen, how many pleasures and pains you have spurned, and how kind you have been to ill-minded people.
meditations-007-p08.core_idea: Recall all you have endured and done well

meditations-007-p09.plain: Very soon you will be ashes or bones, a name or not even that, and a name is only an echo. What life prizes is empty and petty, like puppies biting each other or children quarrelling, laughing, then crying.
meditations-007-p09.core_idea: What we prize in life is empty and brief

meditations-007-p10.plain: You can live in a steady flow of happiness if you go the right way and think and act rightly.
meditations-007-p10.core_idea: Right thought and action bring steady happiness

meditations-008-p01.plain: If you are doing your duty, let it not matter whether you are cold or warm, tired or rested, criticised or praised, dying or doing something else. Dying is also an act of life; there too, just do it well.
meditations-008-p01.core_idea: Do your duty whatever your condition, even dying

meditations-008-p02.plain: The best revenge is not to become like the person who wronged you.
meditations-008-p02.core_idea: The best revenge is not to be like them

meditations-008-p03.plain: When circumstances force you to lose your composure, return to yourself quickly and don't stay out of tune longer than you must. The more often you return to your inner harmony, the better you will master it.
meditations-008-p03.core_idea: Return quickly to inner harmony when shaken

meditations-008-p04.plain: How strange people are: they won't praise those living alongside them, yet they badly want praise from future people they will never see. That is like being upset that people who lived before you didn't praise you.

meditations-008-p05.plain: If something is hard for you, don't assume it is impossible for people. If it is possible for people and fits human nature, believe you can achieve it too.
meditations-008-p05.core_idea: What others can do, you can do too

meditations-008-p06.plain: In the gym, if a sparring partner scratches you or butts your head, you don't get upset or call him treacherous; you quietly keep out of his way. Do the same in life: overlook much, step aside, hold no hatred.
meditations-008-p06.core_idea: Overlook offences; step aside without hatred

meditations-008-p07.plain: If anyone can show me that I think or act wrongly, I will gladly change, because I seek the truth, and truth never harmed anyone. The one harmed is whoever stays in error and ignorance.
meditations-008-p07.core_idea: Gladly accept correction; truth harms no one

meditations-008-p08.plain: Asked to spell a name, you wouldn't shout each letter or get angry back at angry listeners; you'd calmly go letter by letter. So every duty has parts. Attend to them and, without anger at angry people, finish the task.
meditations-008-p08.core_idea: Calmly finish your duty, step by step

meditations-008-p09.plain: How cruel to stop people pursuing what seems good to them, yet you do so when angry at their wrongdoing, since they pursue what they think is good for them. They are mistaken? Then teach them, without anger.
meditations-008-p09.core_idea: Teach wrongdoers instead of being angry

meditations-008-p10.plain: It is shameful for your soul to give up in this life while your body is still holding on.
meditations-008-p10.core_idea: Don't let your spirit quit before your body

meditations-008-p11.plain: Come back to your senses and wake yourself up. Just as on waking you see that only dreams troubled you, now look at the things around you the same way you looked at those dreams.
meditations-008-p11.core_idea: See waking troubles as you see dreams

meditations-009-p01.plain: Adapt yourself to the circumstances your life has given you, and love the people you have been placed among, truly and sincerely.
meditations-009-p01.core_idea: Accept your lot and love those around you

meditations-009-p02.plain: If you think things outside your control are good or bad for you, misfortune or loss will make you blame the gods and hate people. Count only what is in your power as good or bad, and that blame disappears.
meditations-009-p02.core_idea: Judge only what you control as good or bad

judge.issue: Drops "we do much injustice" by not treating these as indifferent; fault-finding with God folded into blame.

meditations-009-p03.plain: One thing here is worth a great deal: to live in truth and justice, with goodwill even toward liars and unjust people.
meditations-009-p03.core_idea: Live truly and justly, kind even to the unjust

meditations-009-p04.plain: To cheer yourself up, think of the good qualities of the people around you: one's energy, another's modesty, a third's generosity. Nothing delights like seeing virtue in those we live with, so keep it in mind.
meditations-009-p04.core_idea: Delight in the virtues of those around you

meditations-009-p05.plain: You aren't unhappy that you weigh only so much and not three hundred pounds. So don't be unhappy that you will live only so many years and no more; be content with your time as you are with your size.

meditations-009-p06.plain: We have the power to form no opinion about a thing and so stay undisturbed, because things themselves cannot force our judgments.

meditations-009-p07.plain: Train yourself to listen closely to what others say, and as far as possible, enter into the speaker's mind.
meditations-009-p07.core_idea: Listen closely and understand the speaker

meditations-009-p08.plain: To someone with jaundice honey tastes bitter; someone bitten by a mad dog fears water; children love a ball. So why am I angry? Does a false belief have less power over someone than bile or poison?
meditations-009-p08.core_idea: People's errors work like illness; why be angry

meditations-009-p09.plain: Your principles die only if the thoughts behind them go out, and you can keep fanning those into flame. Outside things have no hold on your mind. You can recover your life by seeing things again as you once did.
meditations-009-p09.core_idea: Rekindle your principles to recover your life

judge.issue: Drops "I can have the opinion I ought to have; why then am I disturbed?"

meditations-009-p10.plain: Am I capable of this? If so, I use my mind as a tool given by nature. If not, I step aside for someone better, unless there's reason not to, or do my best with a helper. Whatever I do, alone or with others, should serve the common good.
meditations-009-p10.core_idea: Do what you can, with help, for the common good
meditations-009-p10.plain_v1: Is my understanding enough for this? If so, I use it as nature's tool. If not, I step aside for someone abler, or do my best with help. Whatever I do, alone or with others, should serve the common good.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the condition "unless there be some reason why I ought not" to step aside.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the condition 'unless there be some reason why I ought not'.

meditations-009-p11.plain: How many once famous people are now forgotten, and how many who praised the famous are long dead.
meditations-009-p11.core_idea: Fame and its admirers both fade

meditations-009-p12.plain: Don't be ashamed to accept help. Your job is to do your duty, like a soldier storming a city wall. If you are lame and can't climb the wall alone, but can with someone's help, what then?
meditations-009-p12.core_idea: Don't be ashamed to accept help

meditations-010-p01.plain: Don't let the future trouble you. If you must face it, you will meet it with the same reason you use now for the present.
meditations-010-p01.core_idea: Face the future with the reason you have now

meditations-010-p02.plain: Let whatever happens fall on the parts that can feel it; they may complain if they like. But I am not harmed unless I judge what happened to be bad, and it is in my power not to judge so.
meditations-010-p02.core_idea: No harm unless you judge it harm

meditations-010-p03.plain: Whatever anyone does or says, I must be good, as gold or an emerald might say. Whatever anyone does or says, I must be an emerald and keep my colour.

meditations-010-p04.plain: Happiness means a good inner spirit. So, imagination, what are you doing here? Go away, as you came; I don't want you. You came in your old habitual way. I'm not angry with you; just go.

judge.issue: Drops "I entreat thee by the gods"; daemon rendered as inner spirit.

meditations-010-p05.plain: Are you afraid of change? Nothing happens without it, and nothing suits nature better. You can't have a hot bath unless wood changes, or be fed unless food changes. Your own change is just as natural and necessary.
meditations-010-p05.core_idea: Change is natural and necessary, including yours

meditations-010-p06.plain: Soon you will forget everything, and soon everyone will forget you.
meditations-010-p06.core_idea: All forgetting and being forgotten is near

meditations-010-p07.plain: It is distinctly human to love even wrongdoers. You can, if you remember they are your kin, that they err from ignorance and not on purpose, that you will both soon die, and that they have not harmed your mind.
meditations-010-p07.core_idea: Love wrongdoers; they cannot harm your mind

meditations-010-p08.plain: When someone wrongs you, consider what they believed was good or bad. Then you will pity them, not be angry. If you share that belief, forgive them; if not, you will more easily be kind to someone mistaken.
meditations-010-p08.core_idea: Understand a wrongdoer's beliefs, then forgive

meditations-010-p09.plain: Think less of what you lack than of what you have. Pick the best of it and imagine how eagerly you would seek it if you didn't have it. But don't grow so attached that losing it would upset you.
meditations-010-p09.core_idea: Value what you have without clinging

meditations-010-p10.plain: Wipe out imaginings. Stop being pulled like a puppet. Stay in the present. Understand what happens to you and others. Separate cause from matter. Think of your last hour. Leave a wrong where it was done.
meditations-010-p10.core_idea: Stay present; leave wrongs where they happened

meditations-010-p11.plain: On pain: unbearable pain ends us, and lasting pain is bearable. The mind keeps its calm by withdrawing into itself, and its ruling part is not made worse. Let the parts hurt by pain speak for themselves if they can.
meditations-010-p11.core_idea: Pain is bearable; the mind stays whole

meditations-010-p12.plain: On fame: look at the minds of people who chase it, what they avoid and what they pursue. And remember that as new sand piles over old sand, so in life earlier events are quickly buried by later ones.
meditations-010-p12.core_idea: Fame is soon buried like sand

meditations-010-p13.plain: It is not right to be upset with things, because they don't care about it at all.
meditations-010-p13.core_idea: Things don't care about your anger

meditations-010-p14.plain: Everywhere and always, you can reverently accept your present situation, treat the people around you justly, and carefully examine your present thoughts so that nothing slips in unchecked.
meditations-010-p14.core_idea: Accept the present, act justly, watch your thoughts

meditations-010-p15.plain: Think of yourself as already dead, your life finished up to now, and live the rest you are given in line with nature.
meditations-010-p15.core_idea: Live the remaining time as a bonus, by nature

meditations-011-p01.plain: Look within. The source of good is inside you, and it will keep bubbling up if you keep digging.
meditations-011-p01.core_idea: The source of good is within you

meditations-011-p02.plain: Living well is more like wrestling than dancing: you must stand ready and steady to meet sudden, unexpected attacks.

meditations-011-p03.plain: Keep looking at whose approval you want and what principles guide them. Then you won't blame those who offend unintentionally, and you won't crave their approval once you see where their opinions and desires come from.

meditations-011-p04.plain: The philosopher says every soul is deprived of truth against its will, and so likewise of justice, self-control, kindness and the rest. Keep this in mind constantly, and you will be gentler with everyone.
meditations-011-p04.core_idea: No one errs willingly; be gentle with all

meditations-011-p05.plain: Pain is no disgrace and does not harm your mind. As Epicurus said, pain is neither unbearable nor endless if you recall its limits and add nothing to it. Drowsiness, heat and lost appetite are pain too.
meditations-011-p05.core_idea: Pain has limits; don't add to it

judge.issue: Drops "say to thyself that thou art yielding to pain" and the rational and social aspects.

meditations-011-p06.plain: Nature lets you govern what is yours; you can be godlike yet known to no one. Little is needed for a happy life. If you've abandoned hope of great learning, still be free, modest, sociable and obedient to God.
meditations-011-p06.core_idea: Little is needed to live well and nobly

judge.issue: "Do not renounce the hope" of being free becomes a flat command; drops self-circumscription.

meditations-011-p07.plain: Moral perfection is living each day as your last, without frantic excitement, laziness or pretence.
meditations-011-p07.core_idea: Live each day as the last, calmly and honestly

meditations-011-p08.plain: It is absurd to try to escape other people's wrongdoing, which you cannot do, instead of escaping your own, which you can.
meditations-011-p08.core_idea: Flee your own faults, not other people's

meditations-011-p09.plain: Once you have done a good deed and someone has benefited, why want anything more, like a reputation for goodness or something in return? Only fools do that.
meditations-011-p09.core_idea: A good deed needs no reward or recognition

meditations-011-p10.plain: Before each action, ask whether you will regret it. Soon you will be dead and everything gone; if you are acting as a thinking, social being under God's law, what more could you want?
meditations-011-p10.core_idea: Act well now; death makes regret pointless

judge.issue: "Under the same law with God" narrowed to "under God's law"; drops "How is this with respect to me?"

meditations-011-p11.plain: You may not have time to read, but you do have time to curb arrogance, rise above pleasure, pain and fame, and not be annoyed by foolish, ungrateful people, even to care for them.
meditations-011-p11.core_idea: There is always time to improve your character

meditations-011-p12.plain: When you don't want to get up, remember that you are made to do useful work with others; animals sleep too. What fits your own nature is more truly yours and more pleasant.
meditations-011-p12.core_idea: Get up: you were made for work, not sleep

meditations-011-p13.plain: Changing your mind when someone corrects you is just as free as sticking to your mistake, because the choice still comes from your own judgement and understanding.
meditations-011-p13.core_idea: Accepting correction is an act of freedom

meditations-012-p01.plain: If something is up to you, why do it badly? If it is up to others, blaming chance or the gods is foolish. Blame nobody: fix the cause or the thing if you can; otherwise complaining is pointless.
meditations-012-p01.core_idea: Blame no one; fix what you can

judge.issue: Adds "badly"; drops "nothing should be done without a purpose".

meditations-012-p02.plain: You deserve what you are suffering, because you would rather become good tomorrow than be good today.
meditations-012-p02.core_idea: Putting off goodness brings its own suffering

meditations-012-p03.plain: Accept wealth and success without arrogance, and be ready to give them up.

meditations-012-p04.plain: Someone who resents what happens or cuts himself off from others is like a severed limb. Yet God has given people alone the power to rejoin the whole after breaking away, and to take their place again.
meditations-012-p04.core_idea: You can always rejoin the whole you broke from

judge.issue: Drops God's kindness in letting man never be separated at all.

meditations-012-p05.plain: Don't trouble yourself by picturing your whole life's troubles at once. Ask what in this moment is truly unbearable. Only the present can hurt you, and taken alone it is small enough to bear.
meditations-012-p05.core_idea: Face only the present moment's trouble

judge.issue: Drops "you will be ashamed to confess" and chiding the mind that cannot hold out.

meditations-012-p06.plain: I should not cause myself pain, since I have never deliberately caused pain even to anyone else.
meditations-012-p06.core_idea: Don't hurt yourself more than you'd hurt others

meditations-012-p07.plain: When something outside you causes you pain, it is not the thing that disturbs you but your judgement of it, and you can erase that judgement right now.
meditations-012-p07.core_idea: Your judgement, not events, causes your distress

meditations-012-p08.plain: The mind that keeps its own counsel cannot be conquered. A mind free of passions is a fortress, the safest refuge a person has. Not seeing this is ignorance; seeing it and not using it is misery.
meditations-012-p08.core_idea: A calm mind is an unconquerable fortress

fix.display_text: Remember that the ruling faculty is invincible, when self-collected it is satisfied with itself, if it does nothing which it does not choose to do, even if it resist from mere obstinacy. What then will it be when it forms a judgement about anything aided by reason and deliberately? Therefore the mind which is free from passions is a citadel, for man has nothing more secure to which he can fly for refuge and for the future be inexpugnable. He then who has not seen this is an ignorant man; but he who has seen it and does not fly to this refuge is unhappy.

judge.issue: Drops even obstinate resistance and the stronger case of judgement aided by reason.

meditations-012-p09.plain: Tell yourself only what you actually observe. If someone speaks ill of you, that is the fact; that you were harmed is not. Add nothing from inside, and nothing has happened to you.
meditations-012-p09.core_idea: Stick to the facts; add no story

judge.issue: Drops the sick-child example.

meditations-013-p01.plain: If a cucumber is bitter, throw it away. If there are thorns on the path, step around them. That is enough; don't ask why such things exist in the world.
meditations-013-p01.core_idea: Deal with annoyances; don't ask why they exist

meditations-013-p02.plain: Don't be sluggish in what you do, muddled in what you say, or scattered in what you think; don't let your soul be torn inside or spill outward, and don't be too busy for leisure.
meditations-013-p02.core_idea: Live with focus, order and calm

meditations-013-p03.plain: Even if people kill or curse you, they cannot stop your mind being pure and just, as a spring stays clean when cursed or dirtied. Become such a fountain by daily practising freedom, contentment, simplicity and modesty.
meditations-013-p03.core_idea: No one can pollute a mind that renews itself

meditations-013-p04.plain: Why would you want praise from someone who curses himself constantly, or to please someone who isn't pleased with himself and regrets almost everything he does?
meditations-013-p04.core_idea: Don't seek approval from the self-dissatisfied

meditations-013-p05.plain: My neighbour's will matters as little to my own will as his body does. We exist for one another, but each mind has its own work; God did not let my happiness depend on someone else's wickedness.
meditations-013-p05.core_idea: Another's wrongdoing cannot harm your mind

meditations-013-p06.plain: Fearing death means fearing either no sensation or a different kind. If you feel nothing, nothing can hurt you; if you feel something different, you become another kind of living being and keep living.
meditations-013-p06.core_idea: Death, either way, is nothing to fear

meditations-013-p07.plain: People exist for each other, so either teach them or put up with them.
meditations-013-p07.core_idea: Teach others or bear with them

meditations-013-p08.plain: Whoever does wrong wrongs himself, because by acting unjustly he makes himself a worse person.

meditations-013-p09.plain: Right now, a judgement based on understanding, actions aimed at the common good, and contentment with whatever happens: that is enough.
meditations-013-p09.core_idea: Good judgement, good acts, contentment suffice

meditations-013-p10.plain: If you can, teach those who do wrong; if you can't, remember you were given patience for this. Even the gods are kind to such people and help them. You can be kind too; who stops you?
meditations-013-p10.core_idea: Correct wrongdoers or be patient with them

meditations-014-p01.plain: Don't work like someone miserable, or like someone wanting pity or admiration. Aim at one thing only: to act or hold back as reason and the common good require.
meditations-014-p01.core_idea: Work for the common good, not for show

meditations-014-p02.plain: Today I escaped all my troubles, or rather threw them out, because they were never outside me; they were in my own opinions.

meditations-014-p03.plain: Look closely at what drives the people whose judgement you fear, and you will see what sort of judges they are, even of themselves.
meditations-014-p03.core_idea: Those you fear judging you judge poorly

meditations-014-p04.plain: Your job is to leave someone else's wrongdoing where it belongs, with them.

meditations-014-p05.plain: Endings are not evil. Childhood, youth and adulthood each ended like a small death, as did each stage of family life, and none was to be feared. So the end of your whole life is nothing to fear either.
meditations-014-p05.core_idea: Life is full of endings; death is one more

meditations-014-p06.plain: When people blame, hate or slander you, look into their souls; their opinion of you is not worth worrying about. Still, be kind to them: by nature they are your friends, and the gods help them too.
meditations-014-p06.core_idea: Understand critics, ignore their opinion, stay kind

meditations-014-p07.plain: Act if you can, without looking around to see who notices, and don't expect a perfect society. Be content when even the smallest thing goes well, and count that as no small thing.
meditations-014-p07.core_idea: Do good quietly; value small progress

meditations-014-p08.plain: Many things that trouble you exist only in your opinion, so you can clear them away. Then you gain room by picturing the whole universe, endless time, and how brief each life is between two eternities.
meditations-014-p08.core_idea: See the vastness of time to shrink worries

meditations-014-p09.plain: Loss is simply change. Nature delights in change, and through it everything is done well, as it always has been and always will be.
meditations-014-p09.core_idea: Loss is only change, and change is natural

meditations-014-p10.plain: If someone has done wrong, the harm is theirs. And maybe they haven't done wrong at all.
meditations-014-p10.core_idea: Wrongdoing harms the doer, if wrong was done

meditations-014-p11.plain: If the gods have power, why pray for events to happen or not, instead of praying to be free of fear, desire and pain about them? Better to use what is in your power freely than crave what isn't.
meditations-014-p11.core_idea: Pray for inner freedom, not outcomes

judge.issue: Drops the first horn (if gods lack power, why pray) and the objection about what is in our power.

meditations-015-p01.plain: When someone's shameless behaviour offends you, ask whether a world without shameless people is possible. It isn't, so don't demand the impossible. Remembering this makes you kinder to each person.
meditations-015-p01.core_idea: Wrongdoers must exist; don't demand otherwise

meditations-015-p02.plain: When you call someone faithless or ungrateful, look at yourself: you trusted them, or gave expecting return. Isn't doing good, as your nature calls for, enough? The eye asks no payment for seeing.

judge.issue: "The fault is manifestly thy own" softened to "look at yourself".

meditations-015-p03.plain: My soul, will you never be good, simple and whole, content and loving, full and wanting nothing more: no more pleasure, time, places, climate or company?
meditations-015-p03.core_idea: Longing for a soul content and wanting nothing

meditations-015-p04.plain: Whatever happens, either you are built to bear it, so bear it without complaint, or you are not, and it will end once it has consumed you. But you can bear anything your opinion can make tolerable.
meditations-015-p04.core_idea: You can bear what your judgement makes bearable

judge.issue: Drops making things bearable by thinking it your interest or duty.

meditations-015-p05.plain: If someone is wrong, kindly teach them and show them the mistake. If you can't, blame yourself, or not even yourself.

meditations-015-p06.plain: Learn to see how everything turns into everything else; nothing builds greatness of mind more. Such a person, knowing he must soon leave all behind, simply acts justly, accepts what nature gives, ignores others' opinions, and follows God.
meditations-015-p06.core_idea: Seeing constant change frees you to act justly

judge.issue: Drops laying aside busy pursuits and being content with one's present lot.

meditations-016-p01.plain: Why worry anxiously when you can work out what to do? If the way is clear, take it calmly; if not, pause and seek good advice. If you fail, fail trying to do right. Reason brings calm and energy.
meditations-016-p01.core_idea: Reason brings calm, clear and steady action

judge.issue: Drops pressing on justly against opposition, and cheerfulness of the reasoned life.

meditations-016-p02.plain: A wise and humble person says to nature, which gives and takes away everything: give what you want, take back what you want. He says it not proudly, but willingly and gladly.
meditations-016-p02.core_idea: Let nature give and take, gladly

meditations-016-p03.plain: Stop talking about what a good person should be like, and be one.

meditations-016-p04.plain: When someone's fault offends you, think how you go wrong yourself, for instance by prizing money, pleasure or reputation. That quickly cools anger, especially if you remember he is compelled; or, if you can, free him from it.
meditations-016-p04.core_idea: Recall your own faults to ease anger at others

meditations-016-p05.plain: A healthy eye sees everything, not only green things; a healthy stomach takes all food. So a healthy mind is ready for anything. Demanding that your children live and everyone praise you is a sick eye wanting green.
meditations-016-p05.core_idea: A healthy mind accepts whatever happens

meditations-016-p06.plain: Whenever someone does something, get used to asking yourself what their aim is. But start with yourself: examine yourself first.
meditations-016-p06.core_idea: Question motives, starting with your own

meditations-017-p01.plain: If I have done something for the common good, I already have my reward. Keep this in mind always, and never stop doing such good.
meditations-017-p01.core_idea: Doing good is its own reward

meditations-017-p02.plain: A branch cut from its neighbour is cut from the whole tree. Whoever hates and turns from another cuts himself off from all society, by his own act. Yet Zeus lets us grow back and rejoin the whole.
meditations-017-p02.core_idea: Hating others cuts you off from everyone

judge.issue: Drops that the person does not realise he has cut himself off.

meditations-017-p03.plain: Just as obstructive people shouldn't turn you from right action, don't let them turn you from goodwill toward them either. Being angry at them is as weak as giving way through fear; both desert their post.
meditations-017-p03.core_idea: Stay firm and stay kind toward opponents

judge.issue: Drops the ground that the obstructor is by nature a kinsman and friend.

meditations-017-p04.plain: If someone despises me, that's their concern; mine is to do nothing contemptible. If someone hates me, that's their concern; I will be gentle and kind to all, and honestly show even them their mistake, without reproach or show.
meditations-017-p04.core_idea: Others' contempt is theirs; your conduct is yours

meditations-018-p01.plain: In anger, remember that being swept away by passion is not strong. Gentleness is more human and more courageous. The nearer the mind is to freedom from passion, the stronger it is; anger, like pain, is weakness and defeat.
meditations-018-p01.core_idea: Gentleness is strength; anger is weakness

meditations-018-p02.plain: Without one constant aim, you can't be the same person throughout life. And that aim should be the common good, since only on such things do people agree. Whoever directs everything to it will act consistently and stay himself.
meditations-018-p02.core_idea: One aim, the common good, makes a steady life

meditations-018-p03.plain: You can't set rules for others in writing or reading until you have learned to follow rules yourself. This is even truer in life.
meditations-018-p03.core_idea: Learn to obey before you lead

meditations-018-p04.plain: Everything you are trying to reach by a long route you can have now, if you stop denying it to yourself: let go of the past, trust the future to providence, and guide the present with piety and justice.
meditations-018-p04.core_idea: Drop the past, trust the future, live rightly now

meditations-018-p05.plain: Strangely, each of us loves ourselves most, yet values others' opinion of us more than our own. No one could bear, even for a day, to have every thought exposed; we care more what neighbours think than what we think.
meditations-018-p05.core_idea: We value others' opinion over our own

meditations-018-p06.plain: Practise even the things you despair of ever doing. The left hand is clumsy at most tasks for lack of practice, yet it holds the reins more firmly than the right, because it has practised that.
meditations-018-p06.core_idea: Practice builds skill even where you despair

meditations-019-p01.plain: Either fate rules everything, or a kind Providence, or only chaos. If fate, why resist? If Providence, make yourself worthy of help. If chaos, be glad you have a guiding mind; no storm can carry that away.
meditations-019-p01.core_idea: Whatever rules the world, your mind stays yours

meditations-019-p02.plain: If it isn't right, don't do it; if it isn't true, don't say it.
meditations-019-p02.core_idea: Do only what's right; say only what's true

meditations-019-p03.plain: Realise at last that you have something within you better and more divine than the feelings that pull you about like a puppet. What is in my mind now: fear, suspicion, desire?
meditations-019-p03.core_idea: You are more than the feelings that pull you

meditations-019-p04.plain: Everything is opinion, and your opinion is in your power. Drop it when you choose, and like a sailor who has rounded the headland, you will find calm, stillness and a waveless bay.
meditations-019-p04.core_idea: Let go of opinion and find calm

meditations-019-p05.plain: When troubled, you have forgotten: all happens by universal nature; another's wrong is nothing to you; all things always happen so; humans are kin through mind; each mind is divine; child, body and soul come from the deity; all is opinion; and you live and lose only the present.
meditations-019-p05.core_idea: Trouble comes from forgetting basic truths
meditations-019-p05.plain_v1: When troubled, you've forgotten that all happens by nature; that others' wrongs are nothing to you; that all people are kin; that each mind is divine; that nothing is yours; that all is opinion; that you lose only now.

judge_v1.issue: Drops recurrence item and that body, child and soul came from the deity.

meditations-019-p06.plain: Security in life lies in seeing each thing fully for what it is, and with your whole soul doing justice and speaking truth. What remains but to enjoy life, linking one good act to the next without gaps?
meditations-019-p06.core_idea: See clearly, act justly, link good to good

meditations-019-p07.plain: How tiny your share of endless time, of all matter, of the universal soul, of the earth you crawl on! Seeing this, count nothing great except acting as your nature leads and bearing what nature brings.
meditations-019-p07.core_idea: In a vast universe, only right action is great

avot-001-p01.plain: Antigonus of Socho, who received the tradition from Shimon the Righteous, taught: don't serve the master for a reward, like hired servants; serve without expecting reward, and let the fear of Heaven be upon you.

avot-001-p02.plain: Joshua ben Perahiah taught: find yourself a teacher, get yourself a companion, and give everyone the benefit of the doubt.
avot-001-p02.core_idea: Find a teacher and friend; judge others generously

avot-001-p03.plain: If I don't stand up for myself, who will? But if I care only for myself, what am I? And if not now, when?
avot-001-p03.core_idea: Care for yourself and others, and act now

avot-001-p04.plain: Shimon, son of Gamaliel, said that growing up among sages he found nothing better than silence. Action matters more than study, and too much talk leads to sin.

avot-001-p05.plain: Hillel taught: don't cut yourself off from the community; don't trust yourself until you die; don't judge others until you stand in their place; speak clearly; and don't put off study for spare time, which may never come.
avot-001-p05.core_idea: Stay humble, connected, and don't delay

avot-001-p06.plain: Where no one is acting with decency and courage, be the one who does.
avot-001-p06.core_idea: Be decent when no one else is

judge.issue: Interprets 'be a man' as decency and courage; a narrower reading.

avot-001-p07.plain: Rabbi Eliezer taught: value your friend's honour as your own, don't be quick to anger, and repent one day before you die.
avot-001-p07.core_idea: Honour friends, avoid anger, repent daily

avot-001-p08.plain: Rabbi Tarfon said the day is short, the work great, the workers lazy, the reward great and the Master insistent. You needn't finish the work, but you aren't free to abandon it; much Torah study brings much reward.
avot-001-p08.core_idea: You needn't finish the work, but must not quit

avot-002-p01.plain: Someone whose wisdom outweighs their deeds is like a tree with many branches and few roots, which wind uproots. Someone whose deeds outweigh their wisdom is like a tree with deep roots, which no wind can move, as Jeremiah says.
avot-002-p01.core_idea: Deeds root you more firmly than knowledge

avot-002-p02.plain: Ben Zoma taught, citing scripture: the wise learn from everyone; the strong master their own impulses; the rich are happy with what they have; and the honoured are those who honour others.
avot-002-p02.core_idea: Wisdom, strength, wealth and honour redefined

judge.issue: Drops the this-world and world-to-come distinction in the gloss.

avot-002-p03.plain: Don't look down on anyone or dismiss anything, because every person has their moment and every thing has its place.
avot-002-p03.core_idea: Everyone has their hour, everything its place

avot-002-p04.plain: Rabbi Yannai said we cannot explain why the wicked are at ease or why the righteous suffer.
avot-002-p04.core_idea: Why the good suffer is beyond us

avot-002-p05.plain: Rabbi Mathia ben Harash taught: greet people first, and better to follow among lions than to lead among foxes.

avot-002-p06.plain: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar taught: don't try to calm your friend while he is angry, comfort him while his dead lies before him, question him as he makes a vow, or try to see him in his disgrace.
avot-002-p06.core_idea: Know when to leave a friend be

avot-002-p07.plain: Shmuel Hakatan quoted Proverbs: don't rejoice when your enemy falls or stumbles, or the Lord may see it, be displeased, and turn his anger away from him.
avot-002-p07.core_idea: Don't gloat when your enemy falls

avot-002-p08.plain: Rabbi taught: look not at the jug but at what is in it. A new jug can hold old wine, and an old jug may not even hold new wine.
avot-002-p08.core_idea: Judge what's inside, not the outside

avot-002-p09.plain: Rabbi Elazar Ha-kappar said that envy, lust and the craving for honour drive a person out of the world.
avot-002-p09.core_idea: Envy, lust and vanity destroy a person

avot-003-p01.plain: A wise person defers to those wiser, doesn't interrupt, doesn't answer hastily, asks and answers to the point, takes things in order, admits what he hasn't heard, and accepts the truth. A fool does the opposite.
avot-003-p01.core_idea: Seven habits separate the wise from fools

avot-003-p02.plain: Four temperaments: quick to anger, quick to calm, the loss cancels the gain; slow to anger, slow to calm, the gain cancels the loss; slow to anger, quick to calm is pious; quick to anger, slow to calm is wicked.
avot-003-p02.core_idea: Be slow to anger and quick to forgive

avot-003-p03.plain: Love that depends on something ends when that thing ends; love that depends on nothing never ends. Amnon's love for Tamar was the first kind; David and Jonathan's love was the second.

avot-003-p04.plain: A dispute for the sake of Heaven will endure in the end; one that isn't will not. Hillel and Shammai's debates were for Heaven's sake; Korah's rebellion was not.
avot-003-p04.core_idea: Only disputes for a higher purpose endure

avot-003-p05.plain: Ben He He said that the reward matches the effort.

avot-004-p01.plain: Don't seek greatness or crave honour. Do more than you learn. Don't long for the tables of kings, for your table and crown are greater, and your Employer can be trusted to reward your work.
avot-004-p01.core_idea: Seek deeds, not honour; your reward is sure

plato-apology-jowett-001-p01.plain: Socrates questioned a politician thought wise and found he was not; when told so, the man and others came to hate him. Socrates concluded he was slightly wiser: neither knew anything truly good, but he alone didn't think he knew.
plato-apology-jowett-001-p01.core_idea: Wisdom begins with knowing you don't know

plato-apology-jowett-003-p01.plain: Asked whether he is ashamed of a life that may get him killed, Socrates says no: a worthwhile person doesn't weigh the odds of living or dying, only whether he is acting rightly or wrongly.
plato-apology-jowett-003-p01.core_idea: Ask only whether you act rightly

plato-apology-jowett-003-p02.plain: Fearing death is pretending to know what we don't. No one knows whether death, which people dread as the worst evil, might be the greatest good. Thinking you know what you don't is shameful ignorance.
plato-apology-jowett-003-p02.core_idea: Fearing death claims knowledge we lack

plato-apology-jowett-003-p03.plain: Socrates says all he does is urge young and old to care first not for their bodies or wealth but for improving their souls. Virtue doesn't come from money; money and every other good come from virtue.
plato-apology-jowett-003-p03.core_idea: Care for your soul before body or wealth

plato-apology-jowett-004-p01.plain: Asked why he can't simply keep quiet in exile, Socrates says that would disobey the god. Daily discussion of virtue and self-examination is the greatest human good, and the unexamined life is not worth living.
plato-apology-jowett-004-p01.core_idea: The unexamined life is not worth living

plato-apology-jowett-005-p01.plain: The hard thing, friends, is not escaping death but escaping wrongdoing, because wrongdoing runs faster than death.
plato-apology-jowett-005-p01.core_idea: Avoiding wrongdoing is harder than avoiding death

plato-apology-jowett-005-p02.plain: If you think killing people will stop others criticising your bad lives, you are wrong; that escape is neither possible nor honourable. The easiest and noblest way is not to silence others but to improve yourselves.
plato-apology-jowett-005-p02.core_idea: Improve yourself rather than silence critics

plato-apology-jowett-005-p03.plain: If death is no consciousness at all, like a dreamless sleep, it is a wonderful gain. Few days or nights, even for a great king, are better than such a night, and then all eternity is only one night.
plato-apology-jowett-005-p03.core_idea: If death is dreamless sleep, it is gain

plato-apology-jowett-005-p04.plain: So, judges, be hopeful about death, and know for certain that no evil can happen to a good person, in life or after death.
plato-apology-jowett-005-p04.core_idea: No evil can befall a good person

plato-apology-jowett-005-p05.plain: It is time to leave: I go to die, and you to live. Which is better, only God knows.
plato-apology-jowett-005-p05.core_idea: Only God knows if death or life is better

plato-phaedo-jowett-001-p01.plain: Pleasure is strange, and oddly tied to pain, its apparent opposite. They never come at the same moment, yet whoever chases one usually gets the other, like two bodies joined at one head.
plato-phaedo-jowett-001-p01.core_idea: Pleasure and pain are bound together

plato-phaedo-jowett-002-p01.plain: Socrates says he would grieve at death if he did not believe he was going to wise, good gods, and perhaps better people. He hopes something remains for the dead, far better for the good than the evil.
plato-phaedo-jowett-002-p01.core_idea: Hope in an afterlife eases grief at death

plato-phaedo-jowett-002-p02.plain: The body causes endless trouble: it needs food, falls ill, and hinders our search for true being. It fills us with loves, lusts, fears, fantasies and foolishness, and takes away our very power to think.
plato-phaedo-jowett-002-p02.core_idea: Bodily needs distract the mind from truth

plato-phaedo-jowett-003-p01.plain: Isn't wisdom the one true currency for which everything should be exchanged? Only with wisdom is anything truly gained, whether courage, self-control or justice.
plato-phaedo-jowett-003-p01.core_idea: Wisdom is the only true currency

plato-phaedo-jowett-003-p02.plain: When lovers see a lyre, a garment or anything their beloved used, don't they picture the beloved in their mind? That, Socrates says, is recollection.
plato-phaedo-jowett-003-p02.core_idea: Objects call up the people we love

extension.text: And yet what is the feeling of lovers when they recognize a lyre, or a garment, or anything else which the beloved has been in the habit of using? Do not they, from knowing the lyre, form in the mind's eye an image of the youth to whom the lyre belongs? And this is recollection.

plato-phaedo-jowett-004-p01.plain: Talk us out of our fears, Socrates, or rather the child inside us who sees death as a bogeyman and is afraid alone in the dark. Socrates replied: sing charms to him daily until the fear is charmed away.
plato-phaedo-jowett-004-p01.core_idea: Soothe the inner child's fear of death daily

plato-phaedo-jowett-004-p02.plain: Asked who will calm their fears once he is gone, Socrates says to search far and wide among Greeks and foreigners, sparing no effort or money, for nothing is better spent. And search among yourselves too.
plato-phaedo-jowett-004-p02.core_idea: Seek wise guides everywhere, including yourselves

plato-phaedo-jowett-005-p01.plain: A philosopher's soul doesn't ask to be freed only to give itself back to pleasures and pains, undoing its own work like Penelope's weaving. It calms passion, follows reason, and feeds on contemplating what is true and divine.
plato-phaedo-jowett-005-p01.core_idea: Freed by reason, don't return to passion

plato-phaedo-jowett-006-p01.plain: Certainty here may be impossible in this life, yet it is cowardly not to examine these questions fully. Find the truth, or else take the best human theory as your raft through life, unless God's word carries you more safely.
plato-phaedo-jowett-006-p01.core_idea: Without certainty, sail on the best reasoning

plato-phaedo-jowett-006-p02.plain: Having been so convinced before, seeing our belief shaken threw confusion over that argument and any future one: either we can't judge, or there is no basis for belief at all.
plato-phaedo-jowett-006-p02.core_idea: Shaken faith makes all belief seem doubtful

plato-phaedo-jowett-006-p03.plain: Hatred of people comes from trusting too readily without experience. You trust someone completely, they prove false, then another, especially close friends, until finally you hate everyone and believe no one has any good in them.
plato-phaedo-jowett-006-p03.core_idea: Naive trust, betrayed, turns into misanthropy

plato-phaedo-jowett-007-p01.plain: Let us not believe that no argument is ever sound. Rather, say that we ourselves are not yet sound, and must strive bravely for health of mind: you for the rest of your lives, and I as I face death.
plato-phaedo-jowett-007-p01.core_idea: The fault lies in our thinking, not reason

plato-phaedo-jowett-007-p02.plain: Quoting Homer: he struck his chest and scolded his heart, telling it to endure, for it had endured far worse before.

plato-phaedo-jowett-010-p01.plain: If the soul is immortal, it needs care for eternity, not just this life. If death ended all, the wicked would escape their evil. As it is, only virtue and wisdom save us; the soul takes only its upbringing along.
plato-phaedo-jowett-010-p01.core_idea: An immortal soul needs care for eternity

judge.issue: Drops the awful danger of neglect and education's great effect at the journey's start.

plato-phaedo-jowett-011-p01.plain: A person can be hopeful about his soul if he has put aside bodily pleasures and adornments, sought the pleasures of knowledge, and dressed his soul in its own jewels: self-control, justice, courage, nobility and truth.
plato-phaedo-jowett-011-p01.core_idea: Adorn the soul with virtue, not finery

judge.issue: Drops that the adorned soul is ready for its journey to the world below.

plato-phaedo-jowett-011-p02.plain: Asked for final wishes, Socrates tells Crito only what he always said: take care of yourselves, and that serves him and everyone. Without that, and without living by his teaching, promises made now are worthless.
plato-phaedo-jowett-011-p02.core_idea: The best service is caring for yourself

prophet-001-p01.plain: How can I leave in peace, without sorrow? I cannot leave this city unwounded. I spent long days of pain and long lonely nights here, and who can leave his pain and loneliness behind without regret?
prophet-001-p01.core_idea: Even places of pain are hard to leave

prophet-001-p02.plain: Love never knows how deep it is until the moment of parting.
prophet-001-p02.core_idea: Parting reveals the depth of love

prophet-001-p03.plain: When love calls, follow, even though its path is hard and it may wound you and shatter your dreams. Love crowns you and also crucifies you; it helps you grow and also cuts you back.
prophet-001-p03.core_idea: Follow love, though it both crowns and wounds

prophet-001-p04.plain: Love gives only itself and takes only from itself; it neither owns nor is owned. Don't say God is in your heart; say you are in God's heart. You can't steer love; if you are worthy, it steers you.
prophet-001-p04.core_idea: Love is complete in itself and guides you

prophet-001-p05.plain: Love each other without binding each other. Share, rejoice and give your hearts, but let each of you stay separate, like lute strings sounding one song, or temple pillars and trees that stand apart.

judge.issue: Drops 'not into each other's keeping' and that only Life can hold your hearts.

prophet-001-p06.plain: Your children are not your own; they are Life longing for itself, coming through you, not from you. Give them love, not your thoughts; house their bodies, not their souls, which live in a tomorrow you can't visit. Strive to be like them, not to make them like you.
prophet-001-p06.core_idea: Children belong to life, not to their parents
prophet-001-p06.plain_v1: Your children are not yours; they come from Life's longing for itself, through you but not from you. Give them love but not your thoughts; house their bodies, not their souls, which live in a tomorrow you can't visit.

judge_v1.issue: Drops striving to be like children, not making them like you; life does not go backward.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the conclusion: be like them, not make them like you; life goes forward.

prophet-001-p07.plain: Giving possessions is giving little; giving yourself is true giving. Possessions are things hoarded for fear of tomorrow, yet fear of need is itself need, like dreading thirst beside a full well.

prophet-002-p01.plain: You have heard, and wearily repeat, that life is darkness. It is, unless there is drive; drive is blind without knowledge, knowledge useless without work, work empty without love. Working with love binds you to yourself, others and God.
prophet-002-p01.core_idea: Work done with love gives life meaning

fix.display_text: You have been told also that life is darkness, and in your weariness you echo what was said by the weary. And I say that life is indeed darkness save when there is urge, And all urge is blind save when there is knowledge, And all knowledge is vain save when there is work, And all work is empty save when there is love; And when you work with love you bind yourself to yourself, and to one another, and to God.

prophet-002-p02.plain: Work is love made visible. If you can only work with distaste, better to stop and beg from those who work joyfully, for bread baked without care is bitter and only half satisfies hunger.

prophet-002-p03.plain: Joy is sorrow unmasked; the well that holds your laughter was filled with your tears. The deeper sorrow carves into you, the more joy you can hold. Look deep in joy or sorrow: both spring from the same thing.
prophet-002-p03.core_idea: Sorrow carves the space that joy fills

judge.issue: Generalises the closing: what gave sorrow gives joy, and sorrow weeps for former delight.

prophet-002-p04.plain: You speak of wrongdoers as strangers, not one of you. But just as the holiest cannot rise above the highest in each of you, the wicked cannot fall below the lowest that is also in you.
prophet-002-p04.core_idea: The wrongdoer's darkness is in us all

prophet-003-p01.plain: How can you punish people whose remorse already outweighs their wrongs? Remorse is itself justice. You can't impose it on the innocent or remove it from the guilty; it comes unasked at night, making people face themselves.
prophet-003-p01.core_idea: Remorse is justice working from within

prophet-003-p02.plain: You will be truly free not when your days are carefree and your nights without need or grief, but when these surround your life and you still rise above them, unbound.
prophet-003-p02.core_idea: Freedom is rising above cares, not escaping them

prophet-003-p03.plain: If you want to get rid of a fear, know that it lives in your own heart, not in the hand of what you fear.

prophet-003-p04.plain: Your soul is often a battlefield of reason against passion. You must make peace, even love, between them. Reason and passion are your soul's rudder and sails; reason alone confines, and passion alone burns itself out.
prophet-003-p04.core_idea: Reason and passion must work together

prophet-003-p05.plain: Pain breaks the shell around your understanding, as a fruit's stone must break for its heart to reach the sun. If you marvelled at life's daily miracles, pain would seem as wondrous as joy, and you'd calmly accept grief's winters.
prophet-003-p05.core_idea: Pain opens the way to understanding

prophet-003-p06.plain: Don't say you have found the truth or the soul's path; say you have found a truth, and met the soul on your path. The soul walks every path, and unfolds like a lotus with countless petals.
prophet-003-p06.core_idea: No one owns the whole truth

prophet-003-p07.plain: A friend is your needs answered: a field you sow with love and reap with thanks, a table and a hearth. With a friend you speak freely, and even in silence your hearts listen and share everything with quiet joy.
prophet-003-p07.core_idea: A true friend meets your deepest needs

prophet-003-p08.plain: When you part from a friend, don't grieve, for what you love most in them may be clearer when they're gone, as a mountain is clearer to the climber from the plain.
prophet-003-p08.core_idea: Absence clarifies what we love in a friend

prophet-003-p09.plain: You talk when you are no longer at peace with your thoughts or alone with your heart; then talk becomes a pastime that half kills thinking. Some seek talkers because silence and solitude show them their naked selves.
prophet-003-p09.core_idea: Much talk is an escape from oneself

prophet-004-p01.plain: You try to measure time, which can't be measured, and let hours and seasons rule you. Yet the timeless part of you knows life is timeless, that yesterday is only today's memory and tomorrow today's dream.
prophet-004-p01.core_idea: Yesterday is memory, tomorrow a dream

prophet-004-p02.plain: You are good when you are at one with yourself. But when you are divided, you are not evil: a divided house is not a den of thieves, only a divided house.
prophet-004-p02.core_idea: Being divided inside does not make you evil

prophet-004-p03.plain: You are good when you walk boldly toward your goal. But you are not evil when you limp there; even those who limp are not going backwards.

prophet-004-p04.plain: Some elders remember past pleasures with regret, like wrongs done while drunk. But regret clouds the mind rather than correcting it; they should remember their pleasures with gratitude, like a summer harvest.
prophet-004-p04.core_idea: Remember past pleasures with gratitude, not regret

prophet-004-p05.plain: Your everyday life is your temple and your religion. Whenever you enter it, bring all of yourself.

prophet-004-p06.plain: To know death's secret, look into the heart of life; an owl blind by day can't reveal light. Life and death are one, like river and sea. Your hopes quietly know the beyond, as seeds under snow dream of spring.

prophet-005-p01.plain: Dying is standing naked in the wind and melting into the sun; ceasing to breathe frees the breath to rise and seek God. Only after drinking silence will you sing, after the summit begin to climb, after burial truly dance.
prophet-005-p01.core_idea: Death is a release into fuller life

prophet-005-p02.plain: You've heard you are only as strong as your weakest link. That's half true; you are also as strong as your strongest. Judging you by your smallest deed or your failures is like judging the ocean by its foam.
prophet-005-p02.core_idea: You are also your strongest link

prophet-005-p03.plain: You are like the ocean, which cannot rush its tides even for waiting ships. And you are like the seasons: even when your winter denies your spring, spring rests inside you, smiling and unoffended.
prophet-005-p03.core_idea: Your spring waits patiently within your winter

prophet-005-p04.plain: You give a great deal without knowing you give. Kindness that admires itself in a mirror turns to stone, and a good deed that praises itself gives birth to a curse.

prophet-005-p05.plain: You are not confined to your body, house or fields. What you truly are lives above the mountains and roams with the wind, not crawling for warmth or hiding for safety, but a free spirit that surrounds the earth.
prophet-005-p05.core_idea: Your true self is a free spirit

prophet-005-p06.plain: The part of you that seems weakest and most confused is in fact the strongest and most determined.
prophet-005-p06.core_idea: Your seeming weakness is your strength

prophet-005-p07.plain: The hands that made the veil over your eyes and the clay in your ears will remove them, and you will see and hear. You won't regret your blindness, knowing all things' hidden purpose, and will bless darkness like light.
prophet-005-p07.core_idea: One day you'll bless darkness as well as light

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p01.plain: Listen to the reed flute grieve its exile: since it was cut from the reed bed, its sad notes have made people weep as it pours out its longing. Whoever lives far from home always longs to return.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p01.core_idea: The soul longs for the home it came from

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p02.plain: My days are toil and sorrow, walking hand in hand with anguish. But it doesn't matter if my days vanish so, as long as you remain, O incomparable Pure One.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p02.core_idea: Sorrow matters little if God remains

fix.display_text:
Through grief my days are as labor and sorrow,
My days move on, hand in hand with anguish. Yet, though my days vanish thus, 'tis no matter,
Do thou abide, O Incomparable Pure One!

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p03.plain: Rise up, break your chains and be free; how long will money enslave you? A pitcher holds only a day's worth, even of an ocean. Greed never fills; only one torn open by love is free of greed and sin.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p03.core_idea: Love frees us from endless greed

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p04.plain: Do you know why your mirror shows nothing? Its face hasn't been scrubbed of rust. Cleaned of all rust and dirt, it would reflect the shining Sun of God.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p04.core_idea: A purified heart reflects God's light

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p05.plain: A true lover is proven by heartache; no sickness is like the sickness of the heart.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p06.plain: However much we describe and explain love, once we are in love our words embarrass us. Speech makes most things clear, but love is clearer left unexplained.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p07.plain: O God, there are countless traps and baits, and we are like greedy, foolish birds, caught in a new trap every moment, even the mightiest of us. You free us each moment, and we fly straight back in.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p07.core_idea: God keeps freeing us from our own traps

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p08.plain: Each night, spirits are freed from the body's cage, neither ruling nor ruled. Asleep, prisoners forget their prison and kings their power; there is no worry about loss or gain, or about anyone at all.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p08.core_idea: Sleep frees every spirit from its cage

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p09.plain: Being awake chains our spirits to whims, worries over loss and gain, and fear of misery, so they lose their purity, dignity and longing for heaven. The one truly asleep is the one who chases every whim and fancy.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-001-p09.core_idea: Chasing every whim is the real sleep

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-002-p01.plain: Many run from one danger into a worse one, fleeing a snake to meet a dragon. People scheme and trap themselves; what they think will save them turns out to destroy them.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-002-p01.core_idea: Our schemes to escape can trap us

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-002-p02.plain: We must climb to the roof step by step; fatalism has no place here. You have feet, so why pretend to be lame? You have hands, so why hide your claws?
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-002-p02.core_idea: Use the abilities you have; don't play helpless

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-002-p03.plain: Effort is how we thank God for His blessings; fatalism gives no such thanks. Thanks for blessings brings more blessings, while fatalism snatches them out of your hands.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-002-p03.core_idea: Effort is thanks for God's blessings

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-002-p04.plain: Until the heart sees the Giver of the secret, it thinks its horse is lost while riding it. It runs door to door asking who stole its horse; people tell it to look at itself: the horse is beneath it.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-002-p04.core_idea: What you seek is already carrying you

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-002-p05.plain: We know light by its opposite and colours by their contrasts. God made pain and grief so that happiness could be known through them.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-002-p05.core_idea: Pain exists so joy can be known

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p01.plain: We and the world are made new every moment, though we never notice it. Life is like a stream, always renewed, even though it looks continuous.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p01.core_idea: Life is renewed every moment, unnoticed

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p02.plain: If you can't swim or sail, don't throw yourself into the sea out of vanity. A real swimmer brings pearls up from the deep and wins gain from danger.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p02.core_idea: Take risks only where you have skill

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p03.plain: I use my grief as a healing salve for my eyes, so they fill with pearls. Tears shed under God's correction are pearls, though people think they are only tears.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p03.core_idea: Tears from God's chastening are precious

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p04.plain: Love's garden has no limits and bears more than joy and sorrow. The true lover rises above both and stays fresh whatever the season.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p04.core_idea: True love rises above joy and sorrow

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p05.plain: Why do you run from our cries here on earth, God? Why do you pour more sorrow on hearts already sorrowful?
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p05.core_idea: A cry to God about sorrow

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p06.plain: Don't judge by how ordinary people fare, and don't be thrown by harshness or kindness. Mercy and severity, joy and sorrow all pass away; only God remains.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p06.core_idea: Joy and sorrow pass; God remains

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p07.plain: One fault among a hundred good qualities is like one dry stick in a green garden.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p07.core_idea: One flaw is small among many virtues

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p08.plain: Sober thinking clings to memory, and past and future hide God from us, so burn them both away. How long will you stay divided into segments, like a reed?
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-003-p08.core_idea: Past and future veil God from us

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-004-p01.plain: You want to repent for the past, but how will you repent for that repenting? One moment you love the lute's music, the next you embrace weeping.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-004-p01.core_idea: Regret for the past is another trap

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-004-p02.plain: Love and tenderness belong to our humanity; passion and lust belong to our animal side.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-004-p02.core_idea: Love is human; lust is animal

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-004-p03.plain: Gifts friends give each other are only signs, outward proof of the love hidden in their hearts.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-004-p03.core_idea: Gifts are signs of hidden love

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-004-p04.plain: God says: nothing above or below, not earth, sky or highest heaven, can contain me, yet I am contained in the believer's heart. Look for me in such hearts.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-004-p04.core_idea: God dwells in the believer's heart

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-004-p05.plain: Hold back from idle, wandering thoughts, for there are lions in that desert. Restraint is the best medicine, just as scratching only worsens an itch; practise it and your soul grows strong.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-004-p05.core_idea: Restraint from idle thoughts strengthens the soul

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-005-p01.plain: Fruit appears only when the blossoms fall. Bread must be broken to feed, grapes crushed to make wine, and citrons pounded to heal the sick.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-005-p02.plain: You need a friend; don't walk this road alone or go your own way through the desert.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-005-p03.plain: If every rub offends you, how will you ever be polished into a mirror?

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-005-p04.plain: Whoever sees and admits their own faults is moving fast toward perfection. Whoever thinks they are already perfect makes no progress toward God; no sickness of the soul is worse.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-005-p05.plain: If you want to go beyond mere names and words, free yourself from self at once. Scour off the rust with contrition, like polishing a steel mirror, and you will see your own pure, bright essence.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-005-p05.core_idea: Free yourself from self to see your essence

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-006-p01.plain: Darkness brings sleep and quiet, yet the water of life is found in darkness, spirits are refreshed there, and silence is when heavenly voices speak. Opposites come from opposites; light was made out of darkness.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-006-p01.core_idea: Light is born out of darkness

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-006-p02.plain: Before God's commands, bow your pride. Don't mock or scold even those who go astray.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-006-p02.core_idea: Humble yourself; don't scorn the lost

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-006-p03.plain: Nothing is more bitter than being cut off from you, God, and without your shelter there is only confusion. Our goods rob our souls and our bodies tear at them; without relying on you, how can we live?

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-006-p04.plain: See how delicate the heart is: one speck of dust was enough to cloud its moonlight.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-006-p05.plain: Patience, not haste, will get you what you want. Be patient; God knows what is best.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-006-p06.plain: It takes time for blood to turn into milk. Until your good fortune is born like a new baby, the blood does not become sweet milk.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-006-p06.core_idea: Good things take time to ripen

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-006-p07.plain: If greed clouded a mirror, it would lie as we humans do. If scales were greedy for money, would they ever weigh anything truly?

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-007-p01.plain: Give up loving outward forms, for love doesn't depend on a face; if it did, why turn from the form when life leaves it? Lover, think hard about what you really love.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-007-p01.core_idea: Love is for the soul, not the form

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-007-p02.plain: Learn to tell true dawn from false, the wine from the cup, so that instead of many restless eyes, one eye opens through patience and steadiness. Then you will see true colours, and jewels instead of stones.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-007-p02.core_idea: Patience lets you see what is true

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-007-p03.plain: Love makes bitter things sweet, copper into gold, pain into healing, thorns into roses, a prison into a garden and grief into joy. Without love, soft wax turns to hard iron.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-007-p04.plain: Even when harm comes to you, look carefully at the one who does it. Seeing how good and ill rise and fall opens a way from misfortune to happiness, since each state gives birth to its opposite.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-007-p04.core_idea: Each hardship turns into its opposite

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-008-p01.plain: God says he looks not at words but at whether the heart is humble, since the heart is what matters. He wants a burning heart: light the flame of love and burn away fine phrases.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-008-p01.core_idea: God looks at the heart, not words

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-008-p02.plain: Good people seek out pain to heal, and wherever there is pain or poverty, help goes there. Don't seek water; just show you are thirsty, and water will spring up around you.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-008-p02.core_idea: Show your need, and help comes

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-008-p03.plain: If you can't reach the Ka'ba yourself, show your helplessness to God, for crying out is powerful. As a mother waits for her child's cry, God sends his love's milk when you call, so keep crying to him.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-008-p03.core_idea: Cry out to God in your need

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-008-p04.plain: Pain is a treasure full of mercies: the fountain of life lies in darkness and cold, and spring hides inside autumn. Keep company with grief and seek life in your own death.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-009-p01.plain: Someone who believes everything is a fool, but someone who calls everything false is a scoundrel.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-009-p01.core_idea: Neither believe all nor doubt all

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-009-p02.plain: I am master of my thoughts, not ruled by them, as a builder is master of the building. All creatures are slaves to thought, and that is why they are sad; I go into thought and leave it at will.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-009-p02.core_idea: Master your thoughts; don't be ruled by them

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-010-p01.plain: Look past names to qualities, so the qualities can lead you to the essence. Sects quarrel over God's names; when they reach his essence, they find his peace.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-010-p01.core_idea: Look beyond God's names to his essence

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-010-p02.plain: Angels don't walk on land and animals know nothing of the sea. You are an animal in body and an angel in soul, so you move on both earth and heaven.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-010-p02.core_idea: You are both animal and angel
