rumi-masnavi-whinfield-010-p03.plain: God says: your calling 'Allah' was my answer 'Here I am'; your pain and longing were my messengers. Your struggles were my pull that started your prayer; each 'O Lord' of yours holds many answers from me.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-010-p03.core_idea: Your prayer is already God's answer

fix.display_text:
That calling 'Allah' of thine was my 'Here am I,'
And that pain and longing and ardour of thine my messenger;
Thy struggles and strivings for assistance
Were my attractions, and originated thy prayer.
Thy fear and thy love are the covert of my mercy,
Each 'O Lord!' of thine contains many 'Here am I's.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-010-p04.plain: Pain is better than ruling the world, because it makes you call on God in secret. The cries of people without pain are dull and cold; the cries of the sorrowful come from burning hearts.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-011-p01.plain: Brave friend, hold on to God, who is beyond the worlds above and below. He stays with you when you have no home, brings peace out of turmoil, and keeps his promise when you suffer.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-011-p01.core_idea: Hold on to God, who never leaves

fix.display_text:
O brave friend, grasp His skirt,
Who is removed alike from the world above and below;
Who neither, like Jesus, ascends to heaven,
Nor, like Korah, sinks into the earth;
Who will abide with thee in the house and abroad
When thou lackest house and home.
He will bring forth peace out of perturbations,
And when thou art afflicted will keep His promise.
fix.reason: Stray full stop and scan error 'afllicted'

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-011-p02.plain: The sea is not its foam, yet we watch the foam and miss the sea, tossed like blind boats on a bright ocean. You see the water; see the Water moving it, the Spirit within your spirit.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-011-p02.core_idea: Look past the foam to the sea

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-011-p03.plain: You are rooted like grass, your head shaken by every wind. Your foot won't be free until you pull it out of the mud; the way out is hard, but when God frees you, you can go your way.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-011-p03.core_idea: Pull yourself free from the mire

fix.display_text:
You are footbound like the grass in the ground,
And your head is shaken by the wind uncertainly.
Your foot stands not firmly till you move it,
Nay, till you pluck it not up from the mire.
When you pluck up your foot you escape from the mire,
The way to this salvation is very difficult.
When you obtain salvation at God's hands, O wanderer,
You are free from the mire, and go your way.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-011-p04.plain: Be silent so you can hear God speak words no tongue can say, and things no book or talk can express.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-011-p05.plain: Don't stare at your own image, beautiful or ugly, or at your weakness and baseness. Look at the one you love and long for.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-011-p05.core_idea: Look at your love, not yourself

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-011-p06.plain: Knowledge has two wings; opinion has only one and flies lopsided, rising and falling as it tries to reach home. Once it leaves opinion behind and sees true knowledge, it spreads both wings.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-012-p01.plain: The heart is like a feather blown about by the wind, or water boiling in a kettle; its purposes change every moment with its circumstances. So why trust its plans, and why make vows you'll be ashamed to break?

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-012-p02.plain: The strange thing isn't that birds fall into traps they can't see, but that they see the trap and still fly into it on their own wings.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-012-p02.core_idea: We walk into traps we can see

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-012-p03.plain: Sensations and thoughts are like weeds covering pure water. Reason clears them aside, and the wise then see the clear water.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-012-p03.core_idea: Reason clears thoughts to reveal clarity

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-012-p04.plain: A part cut off from its whole is useless, like a limb torn from the body. Until it is joined again, it is dead and a stranger to life.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-012-p04.core_idea: Cut off from the whole, we die

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-012-p05.plain: Don't think my feet walked the earth, for a lover travels with the heart, which, drunk with love, knows nothing of roads or distance. Near and far belong to bodies; spirits travel another way.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-012-p06.plain: All prophets' praises flow into one stream because the One praised is One, so in this sense all religions are one. People always mean to praise the One; they err only in their ideas of him.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-012-p06.core_idea: All religions praise the same One

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-013-p01.plain: Never despair of God's grace; hold on to him, for many hard situations later ease. Hope often follows hopelessness, as sunlight follows darkness.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-013-p01.core_idea: Hard times ease; hope follows despair

fix.display_text:
One must not despair of the grace of such a Benefactor,
One must cling to the stirrup-straps of God.
Ah! many are the conditions which at first are hard,
But, are afterwards relieved and lose their harshness.
Oftentimes hope succeeds to hopelessness,
Many times does sunlight succeed to darkness.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-013-p02.plain: You load a ship without knowing whether you'll drown or arrive; if you waited to know, you would never trade. A timid heart gains nothing, for only the lamp that catches fire gives light.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-013-p02.core_idea: Nothing is gained without risking uncertainty

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-013-p03.plain: Let others pale at bad luck; smile like the rose at loss and gain, for it smiles even when torn, and what God's decree takes is gain. Sufism is finding joy in the heart when trouble strikes.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-013-p03.core_idea: Find joy in the heart amid distress

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-013-p04.plain: It is said: don't mourn your cattle if a wolf has raided your flock, because that disaster may prevent a bigger one, and that loss may spare you a worse loss.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-013-p04.core_idea: A loss may spare a greater loss

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-014-p01.plain: With you, my love, hell would be heaven and a prison a rose garden. Without you, lilies and roses would be like flames of fire.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-014-p01.core_idea: With the beloved, hell becomes heaven

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-014-p02.plain: I died as matter and became a plant, as a plant and became an animal, as an animal and became human. Why fear death will make me less, when I'll rise an angel, then something beyond imagining?

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-014-p03.plain: Pour water from a pitcher into a stream: it doesn't flee the stream but becomes it. Its separate self is lost, but its essence remains, and it is not made less.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-014-p03.core_idea: Merging into the whole loses nothing essential

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-014-p04.plain: Every heart has a window to other hearts, so they are not shut off from each other like bodies. Two lamps may stand apart, yet their light joins in one ray.

fix.display_text:
Since in each heart there is a window to other hearts,
They are not separated and shut off like two bodies.
Thus, even though two lamp-dishes be not joined,
Yet their light is united in a single ray.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-014-p05.plain: When love sparks in one heart it is returned in the other, and if you love God, God loves you, for one hand can't clap alone. The thirsty seek water, and water seeks the drinker.

judge.issue: Drops 'thirst is the water's attraction; I am the water's and the water is mine'.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-015-p01.plain: Vegetables boiling in a pot leap up and ask why they are burned. The cook pushes them down: she boils them not from dislike but to give them flavour and make them part of life.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-015-p01.core_idea: Trials are meant to ripen us

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-015-p02.plain: Nothing is absolutely bad; evil is relative, and every poison or cure helps one creature and hinders another. Venom is life to the snake and death to us; the sea is a garden to fish and fatal to land creatures.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-015-p03.plain: Am I worth less than a lamb or a deer, to have no shepherd? No, I have a Guardian fit to rule, who knows every wind that blows on me, cold or mild, and is never unaware or absent.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-015-p04.plain: What you call a throne is a prison; you think you rule, but you are shut outside. You can't even master your own passions, so how can you govern good and evil?
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-015-p04.core_idea: Who can't rule himself rules nothing

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p01.plain: As children of Adam we heard heaven's melodies in Paradise, and beneath our earthly veil we faintly remember them. That is why music feeds lovers: it reminds them of their first union with God.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p01.core_idea: Music recalls our union with God

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p02.plain: When you have become your own fortune, you can never lose it. How could you lose yourself, when your true self is your treasure and your kingdom?
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p02.core_idea: Your true self is a treasure never lost

fix.display_text:
When, O spiritual one, thou hast become thy own fortune,
Then, being thyself thy fortune, thou wilt never lose it.
How, O fortunate one, canst thou ever lose thyself,
When thy real self is thy treasure and thy kingdom?
fix.reason: Full stop scanned for comma after 'How'

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p03.plain: People are like demons chained by love of money, dragged off to toil in shops and fields. The chain is made of their fears and worries; don't think they wear no chain.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p03.core_idea: Greed and fear chain us to toil

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p04.plain: Seek help from God, not from anyone else. Look for water in the ocean, not in a dried-up channel.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p05.plain: Don't be afraid to admit your ignorance and guilt, so the heavenly Teacher won't hold back his teaching. Saying 'I don't know; teach me' openly is better than false pride.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p05.core_idea: Admit ignorance so you can learn

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p06.plain: How long will you hide behind 'I was compelled' and ignore your free will, blaming God for your sins as Iblis did? You took pleasure and pride in those sins; no one feels such pleasure in acting under compulsion.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p06.core_idea: Don't blame God for your own choices

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-016-p07.plain: Trade your cleverness for wonder. Cleverness is only opinion; bewilderment is real insight.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-017-p01.plain: Age is a matter of mature wisdom, son, not white hair and beard.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-017-p01.core_idea: Age is wisdom, not grey hair

fix.display_text:
Age consists in maturity of wisdom, O son,
Not in whiteness of the beard and hair.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-017-p02.plain: To someone who sees only surfaces, real and fake coins look alike: gold can be blackened with smoke, and copper gilded to fool the simple. We look at the heart, not the outside.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-017-p02.core_idea: Look at the heart, not the surface

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-017-p03.plain: Don't grieve over what is past; once something is done, don't torment yourself about it.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-018-p01.plain: Your real treasure is hidden under a false one, like butter hidden in milk. The false one is your passing body; the true one is your divine soul, long unseen and overlooked.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-018-p01.core_idea: The soul lies hidden in the body

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-018-p02.plain: I see the world full of blessings, fresh springs always welling up, branches dancing and leaves clapping like singers. All this glory is a mirror seen through a veil; what would it be if the veil were lifted?
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-018-p02.core_idea: The world's beauty veils a greater glory

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-018-p03.plain: It's true our bodily senses are weak, but within us is a mighty power. The body is like flint and steel: plain, yet able to strike fire.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-018-p03.core_idea: A frail body holds great power

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-019-p01.plain: When my spirit recognises yours, we remember that we share one origin and are one at heart.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-019-p02.plain: Words bear witness by being true, and actions by keeping promises, and a false witness of either is rejected. Your words and actions must not contradict each other if they are to be trusted.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-019-p03.plain: Don't you know how beautiful your own face is? Stop warring with yourself: it is your own foolish thoughts, like poisoned claws, that wound your quiet soul.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-019-p03.core_idea: Our own thoughts wound the soul

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-019-p04.plain: God, you turn earth into gold and made the first human from earth; your work is transforming, mine is mistakes and forgetting. Turn my errors into knowledge, and make me, who am wholly base, gentle and meek.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-019-p04.core_idea: A prayer to be transformed by God

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-019-p05.plain: You began as fire, earth or air, and had you stayed so you would never have become human. Through change God gave you a better existence, and he will give you thousands more, each better than the last.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-019-p05.core_idea: Change carries us to better existence

fix.display_text:
On the day that you entered upon existence,
You were first fire, or earth, or air.
If you had continued in that, your original state,
How could you have arrived at this dignity of humanity?
But through change your first existence remained not
In lieu thereof God gave you a better existence
In like manner He will give you thousands of existences,
One after another, the succeeding ones better than the former.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-020-p01.plain: Don't foolishly beg the spear for mercy; beg the King who holds it. Why cry to spear and sword when they are only captives in his hand?
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-020-p01.core_idea: Appeal to God, not his instruments

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-020-p02.plain: God, I turn to your free grace and not to my own deeds. I set my hope on it, because you gave me my existence first, unasked, so I firmly trust your grace.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-020-p02.core_idea: Trust God's grace, not your deeds

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-020-p03.plain: When a preacher has no light or life himself, how can his words bear fruit? He tells others to walk straight while he sways like a reed in the wind; however eloquent, his preaching hides a wavering faith.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-020-p03.core_idea: Words without inner life bear no fruit

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-021-p01.plain: Think well of true friends even when they are harsh with you, because suspicion cuts you off from hundreds of friends. If a loving friend treats you roughly to test you, it makes no sense to distrust them.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-021-p01.core_idea: Don't let suspicion cost you friends

judge.issue: Renders 'Brothers of purity' loosely as 'true friends', losing the spiritual-brotherhood sense.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-021-p02.plain: God told Job he had given a grain of patience to every hair on his head. So don't dwell on your own patience; look beyond it to the One who gives it.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-021-p03.plain: God, you are hidden in yourself but seen in your gifts. You are the water and we the millstone, the wind and we the dust, the spring and we the garden: the cause unseen, its effects visible to all.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-021-p03.core_idea: God is unseen but known by his gifts

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-021-p04.plain: Prince, even a kingdom from east to west is as brief as lightning, and any kingdom that doesn't last forever is only a dream. How long will you cling to an illusion that grips you like an executioner?
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-021-p04.core_idea: Passing power is only a dream

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p01.plain: The moon shines and the dogs howl; everyone acts according to their nature.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p01.core_idea: Everyone acts according to their nature

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p02.plain: A person's wings are their aims, so look at what a lover aspires to, not the good and evil on him. A fine falcon hunting mice is worthless; an owl devoted to the king is a true falcon.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p03.plain: God, my shifting resolves come from you, so by the same command mercifully free me from indecision. You are testing me, so help me, and give me one guiding principle, not ten.

judge.issue: Drops the plea 'how long is this trial to last' and the trial's unmanning force.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p04.plain: The whole world runs from its own will and self toward forgetting and intoxication. People turn to drink to escape self-awareness for a while, knowing that this existence of thought, memory and will is a trap and a hell.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p04.core_idea: People drink to escape the self

judge.issue: Drops the closing broadening: fleeing self via intoxication or preoccupation alike.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p05.plain: Bodies are like sealed jars, one holding the water of life and another deadly poison. Look at the contents and you are wise; look only at the jar and you are misled.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p05.core_idea: Judge by what's inside, not the vessel

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p06.plain: God, you are as close as my own face, and such nearness is itself a veil. You are nearer to me than my neck vein, so how can I call to you as if you were far away?
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p06.core_idea: God is too near to be seen

judge.issue: Drops 'Thou art my reason', unseen through intervening obstacles.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p07.plain: It may seem like midnight to you, but to me the dawn of a joyful morning seems near. To ordinary people the world looks dead, but to God every part of it is alive with feeling and love.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-022-p07.core_idea: Dawn is near; the world is alive

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-023-p01.plain: No buyer is more generous than God: he takes your worthless goods and pays with light for your heart. For a few tears he gives a sweet divine spring, and for each sad sigh a place in heaven.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-023-p02.plain: Cook your pot slowly and skilfully, for food boiled in a rush is ruined. God could have made the universe in a moment, yet took six days, and a baby takes nine months: God works by slow degrees.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-023-p03.plain: The Prophet said it well: whoever leaves this world doesn't grieve over dying, but over the opportunities they lost.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-023-p04.plain: Any misfortune or trouble is better than being cut off from God and forgetting him, because troubles pass and that separation remains. Happy is the one who keeps a watchful heart before God.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-023-p04.core_idea: Troubles pass; distance from God remains

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-023-p05.plain: God lowers and raises, and nothing comes to be without both: the seasons, day and night, health and sickness, peace and war. The world flies on these two wings, so every soul lives in hope and fear, trembling like leaves.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-023-p05.core_idea: Life moves through lows and highs

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-023-p06.plain: God is nearer to you than your neck vein, yet you shoot the arrow of speculation far away. You have readied your bow, but the game is right beside you and you aim too far.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-023-p06.core_idea: God is near; you look too far

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-024-p01.plain: Strip off your proud intellect so that grace can always pour down on you. Cleverness is the opposite of humility; give it up and keep company with simplicity.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-024-p01.core_idea: Humility receives grace; cleverness blocks it

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-024-p02.plain: Justice is putting each thing in its proper place, and injustice is misplacing it. Nothing God made is useless or wholly good or bad, not even vengeance or mercy; each helps or harms according to its place.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-024-p02.core_idea: Justice is everything in its place

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-024-p03.plain: How can one prisoner caught in a trap free another? Everyone in the world is a prisoner awaiting death, except one or two rare people whose bodies are in prison but whose souls are in heaven.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-024-p03.core_idea: A prisoner cannot free a prisoner

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-024-p04.plain: Don't get drunk on cups of outward forms, or you'll end up worshipping idols; the wine is in the cups but doesn't come from them. Look to the Giver of the wine, which no cup can hold.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-024-p04.core_idea: Look past forms to their Giver

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-024-p05.plain: The Truth is your real self, not your body; it is higher than 'you' and 'me' and has no limits. Don't tremble in your shell, pearl: you are the sugar, not the cane, so hold to your real self.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-024-p05.core_idea: Your real self is beyond the body

fix.display_text:
The Truth is yourself, but not your mere bodily self,
Your real self is higher than 'you' and 'me.'
This visible 'you' which you fancy to be yourself
Is limited in place, the real 'you' is not limited.
Why, O pearl, linger you trembling in your shell?
Esteem not yourself mere sugar-cane, but real sugar.
This outward 'you' is foreign to your real 'you;'
Cling to your real self, quit this dual self.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-025-p01.plain: A guide's shadow is better than directions to God, and contentment is better than a hundred fine dishes. A seeing eye is better than a hundred walking sticks; the eye can tell jewels from pebbles.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-025-p01.core_idea: A guide is better than directions

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-025-p02.plain: When the devout wail and the angels plead for them, God says the delay is for their good. Their need draws them to him; if he removed it at once, they would wander off and be lost.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-025-p02.core_idea: Delayed answers draw us to God

judge.issue: Compresses away the sinners' groans and angels' plea; 'devout' loses the sinner framing.

rumi-masnavi-whinfield-025-p03.plain: Parrots and nightingales are caged because of their sweet voices; ugly owls and crows never are. In the same way, the disappointments of the devout serve a wise purpose.
rumi-masnavi-whinfield-025-p03.core_idea: The devout are tried for their worth

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-001-p01.plain: One sore spot in a healthy body takes all our attention and spoils our comfort. Likewise, when all goes well but one trivial thing, that failure keeps bothering us while we hardly think of our successes.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-001-p02.plain: When we're free of pain, our wishes show us a mirage of happiness that doesn't exist. Chasing it brings real pain, and afterwards we look back with regret at the painless state we gambled away and can't get back.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-001-p02.core_idea: Chasing imagined happiness brings real pain

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-001-p03.plain: The best the world offers is a life free from pain, quiet and bearable, so we limit our hopes to that. The safest way not to be very miserable is not to expect to be very happy.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-001-p03.core_idea: Expect little happiness to avoid misery

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-001-p04.plain: If all worldly things slip from your grasp, don't grieve, for they are worthless; if you owned a world, don't rejoice. Since you are meant to pass to a better world, hurry on, for this one is worth nothing.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p01.plain: Joy is like gold in the mines: found only now and then, by chance and without rule, mostly in tiny grains and rarely in heaps.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p01.core_idea: Joy comes rarely, in small grains

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p02.plain: To judge how happy someone is, ask what troubles them, not what pleases them; the more trivial the troubles, the happier they are. Only the well-off are irritated by trifles, since real misfortune makes them unnoticeable.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p02.core_idea: Trivial troubles show a happy life

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p03.plain: Don't build happiness on needing many things, because such a broad foundation is the easiest to undermine by accident. Keeping your demands as low as possible relative to your means is the surest way to avoid great misfortune.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p03.core_idea: Need little to be safely happy

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p04.plain: Life is like a journey where the view keeps changing, and so do our wishes; we often find something better than we sought, by another path. Instead of pleasure we gain experience and insight, a lasting blessing.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p04.core_idea: We seek pleasure but gain wisdom

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p05.plain: Searching for gold, the alchemists found other things: gunpowder, china, medicines, natural laws. In a sense, we are all alchemists.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p05.core_idea: Searching, we find something else of value

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p06.plain: While doing something great, we don't see it as great; we just do what seems right at the moment. Only looking back on our whole life do we see how some inspiration led us down the one right path.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p06.core_idea: Life's pattern shows only in hindsight

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p07.plain: Frivolous people live too much in the present, anxious people too much in the future; few strike the balance. Those always chasing future happiness are like donkeys following hay tied in front of them, living provisionally until they die.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-002-p07.core_idea: Living for the future wastes life

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-003-p01.plain: Only the present is real and our existence lies wholly in it, so we should welcome every bearable, pain-free hour. It is the height of folly to spoil it with regret for the past or worry about the future.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-003-p01.core_idea: Only the present is real; enjoy it

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-003-p02.plain: Only evils certain to come on a known date have a right to trouble us, and there are very few; most are merely possible, and even certain ones come at uncertain times. Always preparing for both leaves no peace.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-003-p02.core_idea: Don't let possible evils steal your peace

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-003-p03.plain: Today comes only once and never returns; tomorrow is another day that also comes only once. Each day is an irreplaceable part of life, yet we treat life as a general idea that loses nothing if one day is wasted.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-003-p04.plain: We'd enjoy the present more if, while well, we remembered how every pain-free hour looked like lost paradise when we were sick. Instead we waste happy hours in bad moods and long for them only when trouble comes.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-003-p04.core_idea: We notice good days only once lost

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-003-p05.plain: A person can only be themselves when alone. If you don't love solitude, you won't love freedom, because only alone are you truly free.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-003-p05.core_idea: Only in solitude are we free

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-004-p01.plain: No one is in perfect harmony with anyone but themselves, not even a friend or partner. Deep peace of mind, the greatest blessing after health, comes only in solitude, and for someone rich within it is the happiest life.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-004-p01.core_idea: Deep peace is found in solitude

judge.issue: Drops that lasting peace needs complete retirement, and the 'wretched world' framing.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-004-p02.plain: Just as people huddle together for warmth on cold days, you can warm your mind by contact with others. But someone with plenty of inner warmth doesn't need to.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-004-p02.core_idea: A rich inner life needs little company

extension.text: On cold days people manage to get some warmth by crowding together; and you can warm your mind in the same way--by bringing it into contact with others. But a man who has a great deal of intellectual warmth in himself will stand in no need of such resources.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-004-p03.plain: Becoming friends with solitude early is like striking a gold mine, but not everyone can do it.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-004-p03.core_idea: Befriending solitude is a rare treasure

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-005-p01.plain: One hidden drawback of seclusion: just as staying indoors makes the body sensitive to every draught, long solitude makes our temper so sensitive that trivial words or looks upset us, things busy people never notice.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-005-p01.core_idea: Too much solitude makes us touchy

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-005-p02.plain: If you need solitude but can't bear too much of it, take some into company: say less than you think, expect little, and care little for others' opinion. Society is like a fire; the wise warm themselves at a distance.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-005-p02.core_idea: Keep a wise distance from society

judge.issue: Drops the objective-relation rationale and the fool who gets scorched and flees to solitude.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-005-p03.plain: Envy is natural but is a vice and a misery, so stifle it as an enemy of your happiness. As Seneca says, stop comparing and you'll enjoy what you have; when many seem better off, think of those worse off.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p01.plain: Think a plan over carefully, allowing for the unforeseen that can upset everything. But once you've decided and begun, let it run without reworrying; as Goethe put it, see well to your girths, then ride on boldly.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p01.core_idea: Deliberate carefully, then act without second-guessing

judge.issue: Drops the warning to refrain from unnecessary action in important matters.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p02.plain: When a misfortune has already happened and can't be changed, don't let yourself think it might have gone otherwise or been avoided. Such thoughts only make your distress unbearable and turn you into your own tormentor.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p03.plain: When we've made obvious mistakes, we shouldn't gloss over or excuse them. We should admit them, see them in their full size, and firmly resolve to avoid them in future.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p04.plain: Once we give in to gloom, dark visions arise that don't easily fade, because they might just come true. We can't judge how likely they are, so possibility slides into probability and we hand ourselves over to torment.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p05.plain: Night makes everything look black, so thoughts before sleep or in sleepless hours are as distorted as dreams, and darkest about our own affairs. By morning these nightmares vanish: night is coloured, day is white.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p05.core_idea: Night thoughts darken; morning clears them

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p06.plain: Each day is a small life: waking is a little birth, morning a little youth, and going to sleep a little death.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p06.core_idea: Each day is a little life

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p07.plain: The smallest annoyance can swell into a monster when we brood over it and paint it in glaring colours. It's much better to take a calm, matter-of-fact view of what is unpleasant; that is the easiest way to bear it.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p08.plain: Hold small things close to your eyes and they block out the world. Likewise, the nearest people and things, however unimportant, take more attention than they deserve and crowd out what matters, and we should resist this.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p08.core_idea: Small near things crowd out what matters

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p09.plain: Instead of thinking 'if only that were mine', ask 'what if this were not mine?' Picture your possessions, health, friends and loved ones as lost, since we usually learn their value only after losing them.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p09.core_idea: Value what you have before losing it

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-006-p10.plain: We often try to escape present gloom by imagining future success, inventing many fanciful hopes. Each one holds an illusion, and disappointment is certain when hard facts shatter them.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-007-p01.plain: It is comforting to look back on the great misfortunes that never happened.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-007-p02.plain: Our thoughts should be kept in little drawers, so we can open one without disturbing the rest.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-007-p03.plain: We must limit our wishes, curb our desires and temper our anger, remembering we get only a tiny share of what's worth having and must suffer many ills. Bear and forbear, or no wealth or power will spare us misery.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-007-p03.core_idea: Bear and forbear, or be wretched

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-007-p04.plain: People want to use their strength and see its effect, and they are most satisfied when they make something, whether a book or a basket. There is direct pleasure in watching work grow daily until it is finished.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-007-p05.plain: Struggling with difficulties comes as naturally to people as digging to a mole, and having every want met brings unbearable stagnation. Overcoming obstacles, in work or thought, is the full delight of existence.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-007-p05.core_idea: Struggle is the delight of life

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-007-p06.plain: If thinking can't shake off an outside influence, counter it with an opposite one. Get over an insult by seeing people who think well of you, and ease the dread of danger by focusing on how to prevent it.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-007-p06.core_idea: Counter a bad influence with its opposite

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-008-p01.plain: To toughen the body, work and exercise it hard while healthy and accustom it to hardship. But when illness strikes, do the opposite: nurse and rest the affected body, because what is sick and weak can't be hardened.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-008-p01.core_idea: Train when healthy; rest when ill

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-008-p02.plain: Give the brain all the sleep it needs to recover, because sleep is to a person what winding is to a clock.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-008-p02.core_idea: Sleep restores us like winding a clock

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-008-p03.plain: In life it helps to be able to do two things: look ahead and overlook. The first protects you from loss and harm; the second from quarrels.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-008-p04.plain: Learn patience with people by practising it on stubborn objects, seeing their opposition as fixed by their nature. Being angry at people is as foolish as being angry at a stone that rolls into your path.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-008-p04.core_idea: Don't rage at people's fixed nature

judge.issue: Drops the closing counsel to make use of those you cannot alter.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-008-p05.plain: Two people are hardly ever in exactly the same mood, since it depends on their circumstances, work, health and passing thoughts. These differences cause friction even between the most compatible people.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-008-p05.core_idea: Differing moods cause friction between friends

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-009-p01.plain: When a false claim is accepted, don't despair or think that's the end of it. Over time it will be examined and discussed, and usually everyone comes to see what a clear mind saw at once.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-009-p02.plain: Seeing clearly amid general delusion is like having the only correct watch in a town of wrong clocks. You alone know the time, but it does you no good, since everyone goes by the clocks.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-009-p02.core_idea: Being right alone is of little use

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-009-p03.plain: You won't lose a friend by refusing a loan, but very likely will by granting one. Likewise, being a little proud rarely alienates people, while being too kind and obliging often makes them arrogant until there is a break.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-009-p03.core_idea: Too much kindness can spoil friendships

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p01.plain: Be careful not to form a very high opinion of someone you've only just met, or you'll probably be disappointed, then ashamed of yourself, and perhaps even harmed.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p01.core_idea: Don't judge new acquaintances too highly

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p02.plain: If someone shows annoying traits, ask whether they're worth putting up with those traits again, even worse. If so, let it pass, knowing it will recur; if not, break with them at once and for good.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p02.core_idea: Decide if someone's worth their faults

extension.text: If any person with whom we are associated or have to do, exhibits unpleasant or annoying qualities, we have only to ask ourselves whether or not this person is of so much value to us that we can put up with frequent and repeated exhibitions of the same qualities in a somewhat aggravated form. In case of an affirmative answer to this question, there will not be much to be said, because talking is very little use. We must let the matter pass, with or without some notice; but we should nevertheless remember that we are thereby exposing ourselves to a repetition of the offence. If the answer is in the negative, we must break with our worthy friend at once and forever; or in the case of a servant, dismiss him.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p03.plain: When you come across meanness or stupidity, in life or in books, don't let it upset you. Treat it as new knowledge about human nature, like a mineralogist finding a perfect specimen.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p03.core_idea: Study human folly instead of resenting it

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p04.plain: Grasping a rule for dealing with people is easy, yet you may break it soon after. Don't despair or give up on rules: first understand the rule, then learn its practice, which takes time.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p04.core_idea: Understanding a rule is quick; practising it takes time.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p05.plain: Showing off a quality is admitting you lack it. Whatever a man boasts of is where he is weak; someone who truly has a gift is content to know it and feels no need to display it.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p05.core_idea: People boast most about what they lack.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p06.plain: Just as we don't feel our own body's weight, we see others' faults but not our own. The upside: others become a mirror showing our own flaws, though we usually think we see someone else.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-010-p06.core_idea: Others' faults are a mirror of our own.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-011-p01.plain: Short of a friend making a big sacrifice for you, the best test of his feelings is how he reacts when he hears of a misfortune that has just struck you.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-011-p01.core_idea: A friend's reaction to your misfortune reveals his feelings.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-011-p02.plain: Distance and long absence wear down friendship. Over the years even dear friends we never see become abstract ideas, kept up by habit, while we stay warmly attached to whoever is in front of us, even pets.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-011-p03.plain: Friends say they are sincere; enemies actually are. Take your enemies' criticism like bitter medicine that helps you know yourself.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-011-p04.plain: We often trust others out of laziness, self-interest and vanity, yet expect them to keep faith. And we shouldn't be angry when people don't trust us: they simply think honesty is very rare.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-011-p04.core_idea: Trust often springs from laziness, selfishness and vanity.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-011-p05.plain: Being polite is wise and being rude is stupid; making enemies through needless rudeness is like setting your own house on fire. Politeness is token money, openly false, so spend it generously.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-011-p05.core_idea: Politeness costs nothing, so be generous with it.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p01.plain: We'd be far slower to take offence at an insult if we didn't think so highly of ourselves, and if we understood what people privately think of one another.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p01.core_idea: Pride makes insults sting more than they should.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p02.plain: Never copy another person's conduct, since no two situations or characters are alike; two people doing the same thing get different results. Think carefully, then act according to your own character.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p02.core_idea: Act from your own character, not another's example.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p03.plain: If two people's silly talk that you overhear irritates you, imagine you're listening to two fools in a comic play.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p04.plain: If you want people to accept your judgment, state it calmly and without passion.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p04.core_idea: Calm statements persuade better than passionate ones.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p05.plain: It is usually wiser to show your intelligence by staying silent than by speaking; silence is prudence, speech has a touch of vanity. Yet people prefer speech's brief pleasure to silence's lasting gain.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p05.core_idea: Silence shows wisdom better than speech.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p06.plain: Money is never better spent than when someone cheats you of it, because in one stroke you have bought caution.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p07.plain: Show anger and hatred only through what you do, never otherwise; feelings work best in action when you avoid displaying them.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p07.core_idea: Let anger show only in deeds.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p08.plain: Whatever form a life takes, it is made of the same elements, in a cottage or a palace. Success and failure differ less than they seem, like a kaleidoscope showing new patterns from the same bits of glass.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p08.core_idea: All lives are made of the same stuff.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p09.plain: A life is like a ship's voyage with luck as the wind, speeding it or driving it off course. A person's own effort is like the rudder: it helps a little, but a sudden squall can undo it all.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-012-p09.core_idea: Luck steers life more than effort does.

judge.issue: Drops that with a favourable wind the ship needs no steering at all.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p01.plain: Looking back on life, a man sees where luck failed him and easily blames himself too much. But a life isn't wholly self-made; it comes from events and his own choices, constantly shaping each other.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p01.core_idea: Life is shaped by events and choices together.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p02.plain: Life is a card game dealt by fate, or better, a chess game where fate is the opponent. We keep adjusting our tactics until our original plan is barely recognisable.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p02.core_idea: Fate forces us to keep changing our plans.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p03.plain: Our brains are not the wisest part of us. In life's big moments, a person acts less from clear knowledge than from a deep inner impulse, almost an instinct, rising from the core of their being.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p03.core_idea: Big decisions come from deep instinct, not reasoning.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p04.plain: Everyone has inborn principles, part of their very blood, that they usually can't name. Only looking back on life do they see these principles have guided them all along, like an invisible thread.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p04.core_idea: Hidden inborn principles guide a whole life.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p05.plain: Never forget that time changes everything and nothing lasts. In any situation, picture its opposite: misfortune in good times, betrayal in trust, and in hard times, happier days. That is lasting worldly wisdom.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p05.core_idea: Always imagine the opposite of your present state.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p06.plain: Only experience truly teaches that everything in this world is unstable and passing. Each moment's circumstances seem as if they should last forever, but in a world where all is fleeting, only change endures.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p07.plain: You can force a tree to bloom in days, but then it withers. Likewise a young man who overworks his strength borrows from time, and repays the debt out of his later years and his very life.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p07.core_idea: Forcing youth's strength costs you later life.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p08.plain: Whatever happens to you, don't rejoice or grieve too much: fortune can turn at any moment, and we often misjudge what is good for us. Many have mourned what proved their best luck, or celebrated their ruin.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-013-p08.core_idea: Don't overreact; we misjudge what's good for us.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p01.plain: Misfortune weighs less if we've thought about it beforehand: we know its size and it feels no heavier than it is. Unexpected, it terrifies us and seems limitless, just as darkness and uncertainty magnify danger.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p01.core_idea: Preparing for misfortune keeps it in proportion.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p03.plain: Life's small daily irritations can be seen as practice for bearing great misfortunes. Treat petty quarrels, gossip and rudeness like stones in the road: push them aside and don't brood on them at all.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p03.core_idea: Push small annoyances aside without brooding.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p04.plain: The most accomplished person would be one who is never undecided and never in a hurry.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p04.core_idea: Never irresolute, never in a hurry.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p05.plain: It is a cowardly soul that loses heart and gives up as soon as a storm starts gathering, or even at the first cloud on the horizon.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p05.core_idea: Losing heart at the first sign of trouble is cowardly.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p06.plain: As long as a risky outcome is still undecided and things might yet turn out well, no one should tremble but only resist, just as you shouldn't despair of the weather while any blue sky shows.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p06.core_idea: While hope remains, resist rather than despair.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p07.plain: All our lives, the present is the only thing we really possess. The young look ahead to a long future and the old look back on a long past, while shifting temperament colours the present differently at each age.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p07.core_idea: The present is all we ever possess.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p08.plain: When young, we were absorbed in what was around us as if nothing else existed. Later, discovering how much the world holds, we lose that early state of mind, and with it our patience.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-014-p08.core_idea: Knowing more of the world costs us patience.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p01.plain: In youth, life's poetry shows us a dazzling vision, and we torment ourselves wanting it to come true, like trying to grab a rainbow. Expecting life to be a romance is the seed of disappointment.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p02.plain: The second half of life has less longing and more rest. The young think great happiness exists but is hard to reach; the old know it doesn't, so they relax, enjoy the present and take pleasure in small things.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p02.core_idea: Age brings rest by dropping the hunt for happiness.

fix.display_text: The consequence of this is that, as compared with the earlier, the later half of life, like the second part of a musical period, has less of passionate longing and more restfulness about it. And why is this the case? Simply because, in youth, a man fancies that there is a prodigious amount of happiness and pleasure to be had in the world, only that it is difficult to come by it; whereas, when he becomes old, he knows that there is nothing of the kind; he makes his mind completely at ease on the matter, enjoys the present hour as well as he can, and even takes a pleasure in trifles.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p03.plain: Life's experience mainly gives clear sight. The mature person sees things as they really are, while in youth he saw a phantom world built from his own whims, inherited prejudice and delusion.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p03.core_idea: Experience brings clear sight of reality.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p04.plain: When young, we expect the big events and important people of our life to arrive with drums and trumpets; in old age we see they all slipped in quietly, almost unnoticed, by the side door.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p05.plain: Life is like embroidery: in the first half you see the right side, in the second the back. The back is less pretty but more instructive, because it shows how the threads were worked together.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p05.core_idea: Later life shows how life was woven together.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p06.plain: Being surprised by how people behave, and handling them awkwardly and crossly, is a sign of a nobler kind of character.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p06.core_idea: Awkwardness with people can signal a noble character.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p07.plain: From youth, life seems to stretch endlessly ahead; from old age, it looks a short way back, like looking through a reversed telescope. To see how short life is, you must have lived a long time.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p07.core_idea: Only the old see how short life is.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p08.plain: Time moves slower when we are young, so life's first quarter is both the happiest and the longest, leaving the most memories. Spring days drag; autumn days are short but gentler and more even.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-015-p08.core_idea: Youth feels longest; later days are short but mellow.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p01.plain: We don't like dwelling on unpleasant things that happened to us, especially when they hurt our pride, since we're rarely blameless. So people readily forget much that was unpleasant, along with much that didn't matter.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p01.core_idea: We forget what wounds our pride.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p02.plain: Why do the years ahead seem endless in youth? Because we must make room for everything we hope to achieve; we pack them with so many plans that even a vast lifespan couldn't carry them all out.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p02.core_idea: Youth's crowded plans make life seem endless.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p03.plain: Sometimes we think we long for a faraway place when really we long for the time we spent there, when we were younger and fresher. Time disguises itself as place, and going back shows how we were fooled.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p03.core_idea: Longing for a place is often longing for lost time.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p04.plain: Even when young, a person should save and pace his strength.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p04.core_idea: Conserve your strength even in youth.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p05.plain: Some people are charming only while young; others shine in their prime and fade with age; many look their best in old age, when experience softens their character and they take life easily.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p05.core_idea: Different people flourish at different ages.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p06.plain: A sailor sees his progress only as the coast shrinks behind him. In the same way, a man realises he is getting old when people older than him start to seem young.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p06.core_idea: You notice ageing when older people seem young.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p07.plain: As time speeds up with age, boredom mostly fades, and with the passions quieted, life's burden is lighter than in youth, if health holds. So the years just before old age's troubles are called one's best.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-016-p07.core_idea: Life grows lighter as passions quiet with age.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p01.plain: Later life and old age bring intellectual rewards. Only then is a person truly rich in experience, able to see life from every side and grasp how things connect; what he thought he knew in youth, he now really knows.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p01.core_idea: Old age turns knowledge into real understanding.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p02.plain: The tree of knowledge must grow to full height before it bears fruit, but its roots are in youth.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p02.core_idea: Knowledge ripens late but is rooted in youth.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p03.plain: While our minds are growing, we get used to scorning yesterday from today. The habit persists even after our powers decline, when we should respect the past instead, so we often undervalue what we did and thought when young.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p03.core_idea: We wrongly look down on our younger selves.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p04.plain: The first forty years of life provide the text and the remaining thirty the commentary; without the commentary we cannot properly grasp the text's meaning, its moral and its finer applications.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p04.core_idea: Later life explains the meaning of earlier life.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p05.plain: Near life's end it's like the close of a masked ball: the masks come off. You see who people really were; characters are revealed, deeds have borne fruit, and every sham has collapsed. Only time could do this.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p05.core_idea: Time unmasks everyone by life's end.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p06.plain: As life goes on, it shows a person what he is made of.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p06.core_idea: Life reveals what we are made of.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p07.plain: Youth is called happy and age sad, which would be true if passions made us happy. But passions toss the young about, bringing much pain and little joy; in age they cool, and the freed mind turns contemplative.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p07.core_idea: Age frees the mind as the passions cool.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p08.plain: Youth is restless and age is calm, which shows how pleasure is shared between them. Like a child grabbing at pretty things, the young imagine delights the world can't deliver, and longing for them makes happiness impossible.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-017-p08.core_idea: Youth's restless longing makes happiness impossible.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-018-p01.plain: The mind does weaken with age, but a strong one keeps enough to fight boredom. Experience and reflection sharpen an old man's judgment and widen his view, and his continuing self-education gives the mind work and satisfaction.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-018-p01.core_idea: Experience and self-education reward the ageing mind.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-018-p02.plain: It's lucky if an old person keeps some love of study, music or theatre and stays responsive to the world. In old age, what a person has within himself matters more than ever.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-018-p02.core_idea: In old age, inner resources matter most.

fix.display_text: It is a piece of good fortune if the old man retains some of his love of study or of music or of the theatre,--if, in general, he is still somewhat susceptible to the things about him; as is, indeed, the case with some people to a very late age. At that time of life, what a man has in himself is of greater advantage to him than ever it was before.

schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-018-p03.plain: It is sad that all our faculties waste away faster and faster as we age, yet this is necessary and even good: it prepares us for death, which would otherwise be too hard to bear.
schopenhauer-counsels-maxims-018-p03.core_idea: Decline in age prepares us for death.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-001-p01.plain: The same events affect no two people alike; each lives in a world of his own. How a person looks at the world shapes it: dull and empty to one, rich and meaningful to another.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-001-p01.core_idea: How we see the world shapes our world.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-001-p02.plain: People who hear of someone's interesting experiences wish the same had happened to them, forgetting they should envy the mind that made those events meaningful. To a dull person, the same events would have been ordinary.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-001-p02.core_idea: The mind, not the event, makes experience rich.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-001-p03.plain: On stage, one actor plays a prince and another a servant, but underneath each is the same anxious player. Life is the same: rank and wealth assign roles, but beneath them is the same poor mortal with his troubles.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-001-p03.core_idea: Beneath every role is the same struggling human.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-001-p04.plain: Health outweighs every other blessing; a healthy beggar is happier than a sick king. A cheerful temper, clear mind and good conscience can't be bought. What you are within matters more than what you own or your reputation.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-001-p04.core_idea: What you are matters more than what you have.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-001-p05.plain: A good, moderate, gentle person can be happy while poor, while a greedy, envious, spiteful man is miserable even if he is the richest in the world.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-002-p01.plain: All that is truly in our power is to make the best use of our own qualities: pursue what calls on them, aim for the perfection they allow, and choose the work and life that develop them.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-002-p01.core_idea: Choose a life that uses your own gifts.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-002-p02.plain: A very strong man forced into fine desk work, or a brilliant mind stuck in bodily labour, will be unhappy all his life. Still, especially when young, beware of conceit and imagining you have powers you lack.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-002-p03.plain: Great wealth adds little to happiness beyond real needs, and its upkeep brings worry. Many rich people are unhappy for lack of inner culture. Yet people chase riches over culture, though what we are matters more than what we have.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-002-p03.core_idea: What you are outweighs what you own.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-002-p04.plain: To a sour, ill-tempered person every pleasure tastes like fine wine in a bitter mouth. So in good and bad alike, what happens to us matters less than how we meet it.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-002-p04.core_idea: How we meet events matters more than events.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-002-p05.plain: When cheerfulness knocks, fling the door open; it is never untimely, yet we hesitate. Cheerfulness is happiness in ready cash: it makes us happy now, and the present is all such brief beings as we have.

judge.issue: Loosens the claim: present happiness as highest blessing becomes the present being all we have.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-003-p01.plain: What makes us happy or unhappy isn't what things are in themselves but how we see them. As Epictetus said, people are moved not by things but by their thoughts about them.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-003-p01.core_idea: Our view of things, not things, moves us.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-003-p02.plain: With health, everything gives pleasure; without it, nothing can be enjoyed, and even a great mind or a happy temperament is diminished.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-003-p02.core_idea: Without health, nothing can be enjoyed.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-003-p03.plain: Human happiness has two enemies, pain and boredom. The further we get from one, the nearer we come to the other, and life swings more or less violently between them.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-003-p03.core_idea: Life swings between pain and boredom.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-003-p04.plain: A wise man seeks freedom from pain, quiet, leisure and a modest life; after some experience of people he chooses retirement, or even solitude if very gifted. The more one has within, the less one needs from others.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-003-p04.core_idea: The richer within, the less we need others.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-004-p01.plain: Ordinary people think only about how to pass their time; a person of any talent tries to use it.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-004-p01.core_idea: Use time rather than merely pass it.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-004-p02.plain: Don't expect much from other people or the outside world. One person can't be a great deal to another; in the end everyone stands alone, and what matters is who it is that stands alone.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-004-p02.core_idea: Everyone stands alone; what matters is who.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-004-p03.plain: Wherever we are, we are left to ourselves, and we either make or find our own happiness.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-004-p03.core_idea: We make our own happiness wherever we are.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-004-p04.plain: The world offers little: it is full of misery and pain, with boredom lurking beyond them; evil usually wins and folly is loudest. Here, a person rich within is like a warm, bright room on a freezing December night.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-004-p04.core_idea: Inner richness is warmth in a cold world.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-004-p05.plain: It is great foolishness to trade your inner life, giving up most of your peace, leisure and independence, for show, rank, titles and honours.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-004-p05.core_idea: Don't trade inner peace for outward status.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-005-p01.plain: A life of the mind guards against boredom and its harms: bad company, dangers, losses and extravagance that hit those who seek happiness only outside. Schopenhauer notes his philosophy never earned him sixpence but saved him many expenses.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-005-p01.core_idea: The life of the mind protects against boredom's harms.

fix.display_text: The life of the mind is not only a protection against boredom; it also wards off the pernicious effects of boredom; it keeps us from bad company, from the many dangers, misfortunes, losses and extravagances which the man who places his happiness entirely in the objective world is sure to encounter. My philosophy, for instance, has never brought me in a six-pence; but it has spared me many an expense.
fix.reason: Comma should be full stop before new sentence

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-005-p02.plain: The ordinary person bases happiness on outside things like property, rank, family and friends, so when he loses them or they disappoint, his happiness collapses. His centre of gravity lies outside himself, shifting with every wish.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-005-p02.core_idea: Happiness built on externals easily collapses.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-005-p03.plain: A person rich within needs nothing from outside except undisturbed leisure to develop his mind and enjoy that wealth; in short, permission to be himself every day of his life.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-005-p03.core_idea: The inwardly rich need only freedom to be themselves.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-005-p04.plain: The more wisdom you have, the more grief you have; whoever adds to knowledge adds to sorrow.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-006-p01.plain: A person never misses things it never occurs to him to want and is just as happy without them, while someone with a hundred times more is miserable for lacking the one thing he desires.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-006-p01.core_idea: We only miss what we expect to have.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-006-p02.plain: Riches, like sea-water, make you thirstier the more you drink; so does fame. After losing wealth, once the first grief passes, we return to our usual mood by lowering our demands, which hurts and then heals like an old wound.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-006-p02.core_idea: Wealth breeds thirst; loss heals as demands shrink.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-006-p03.plain: Discontent comes from constantly raising our demands while being unable to increase what would satisfy them.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-007-p01.plain: Wife and children are not counted among a man's possessions; rather, he belongs to them. Friends might sooner count, but a man's friends are no more his than he is theirs.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-007-p01.core_idea: We belong to our family more than it to us.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-007-p02.plain: People care far too much about others' opinions, though these aren't essential to happiness. Yet praise a man and he lights up as surely as a stroked cat purrs, even at an obvious lie, if it touches his pride.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-007-p02.core_idea: We crave praise like a cat craves stroking.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-007-p03.plain: Once we've seen even the greatest people treated with contempt by a handful of fools, we understand that valuing what others say is giving them too much honour.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-007-p03.core_idea: Others' opinions deserve less weight than we give.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-008-p01.plain: We'd be far happier recognising early that our real life is in our own skin, not in others' opinions. Health, temperament, abilities, income, family and home matter a hundred times more than what people think of us.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-008-p01.core_idea: Real life is in your own skin, not others' opinions.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-008-p02.plain: In nearly everything we do, we first ask what people will say, and almost half of life's troubles come from this worry. It lies beneath our touchy self-importance, our vanity and pretension, and all our showing off.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-008-p02.core_idea: Worry about others' opinions causes half our troubles.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-008-p03.plain: A quiet, retired life does wonders for peace of mind, mainly because we escape living constantly under others' eyes and minding their passing opinions; we can return to ourselves.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-008-p03.core_idea: Withdrawing from others' gaze brings peace of mind.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-009-p01.plain: Whoever breaks a trust has lost trust for ever, whatever he does and whoever he is, and the bitter results of that loss can never be avoided.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-009-p01.core_idea: Broken trust is lost for ever.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-011-p01.plain: Socrates was often roughly treated after his debates and bore it mildly. When kicked, he asked whether he should resent a donkey's kick; when told a man had insulted him, he said the words weren't addressed to him.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-011-p01.core_idea: Insults need not be taken personally.

fix.display_text: Socrates' frequent discussions were often followed by his being severely handled, and he bore it all mildly. Once, for instance, when somebody kicked him, the patience with which he took the insult surprised one of his friends. Do you think, said Socrates, that if an ass happened to kick me, I should resent it? On another occasion, when he was asked, Has not that fellow abused and insulted you? No, was his answer, what he says is not addressed to me.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-012-p01.plain: The truer the charge, the more it stings; a hint of a real fault offends more than a terrible accusation that is baseless. So someone sure he has done nothing to deserve blame can safely treat it with contempt.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-012-p01.core_idea: Baseless accusations can be met with contempt.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-012-p02.plain: Truly knowing your own worth makes you indifferent to insults; but if you can't help resenting one, a little shrewdness and good breeding will let you keep up appearances and hide your anger.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-012-p02.core_idea: Knowing your worth makes insults powerless.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-014-p01.plain: Seneca said, finely, that fame follows merit as surely as a body casts a shadow, sometimes going ahead of it and sometimes behind.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-014-p01.core_idea: Fame follows merit like a shadow.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-014-p02.plain: Fame that will last usually comes late, since excellent work takes time. Lasting fame grows slowly like an oak, brief fame like a yearly plant, and false fame springs up overnight like a fungus and dies as fast.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-014-p02.core_idea: Lasting fame grows slowly, like an oak.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-015-p01.plain: Whoever pursues the good and genuine must avoid the bad and defy, even despise, the crowd. So fame flees those who chase it and seeks those who shun it: the first pander to current taste, the second defy it.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-015-p01.core_idea: Fame flees those who chase it.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-015-p02.plain: Making your worth depend on others' opinions is a wretched way to live. Each person lives mainly in and for himself; what he is matters most to him. Others' heads are a poor home for real happiness.
schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-015-p02.core_idea: Your worth can't live in other people's heads.

judge.issue: Drops that worthlessness in oneself means worthlessness otherwise, and the hero/genius fame point.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-015-p03.plain: It's not fame that makes a person happy but what earns it: his merits and the character and ability behind them. Others' opinion matters little by comparison, so someone who deserves fame but lacks it has the more important part.

schopenhauer-wisdom-of-life-015-p04.plain: In old age there is no greater comfort than knowing you poured all your youthful strength into works that still remain young.

seneca-001-p01.plain: Some of our time is snatched away, some slips off, some drifts out of reach; the most shameful loss is through carelessness. Most of life passes doing wrong, much doing nothing, and all of it doing what doesn't matter.
seneca-001-p01.core_idea: Most of our time is lost through carelessness.

seneca-001-p02.plain: Who truly values his time, weighs each day, and understands that he is dying daily? We wrongly look ahead to death, but most of it is already past: all the years behind us belong to death.
seneca-001-p02.core_idea: We are dying daily; past years belong to death.

seneca-001-p03.plain: Take hold of today's work and you won't need to lean so much on tomorrow. While we put things off, life rushes past.
seneca-001-p03.core_idea: While we postpone, life speeds by.

seneca-001-p04.plain: Nothing is truly ours except time, the one thing nature gave us, and it slips away easily. People count cheap, replaceable things as debts, yet never feel indebted for time, the one loan no one can repay.
seneca-001-p04.core_idea: Time is our only true possession.

seneca-001-p05.plain: You don't rush around changing where you live, since such restlessness shows a disordered spirit. The first sign of a well-ordered mind is being able to stay in one place and spend time in your own company.
seneca-001-p05.core_idea: A settled mind can stay put and be alone.

seneca-001-p06.plain: Stay with a small number of great thinkers and digest their work if you want ideas that take firm root. Being everywhere means being nowhere: someone always travelling ends up with many acquaintances but no friends.
seneca-001-p06.core_idea: Everywhere means nowhere; go deep, not wide.

seneca-001-p07.plain: The poor man isn't the one with too little but the one who craves more. However much you own, coveting your neighbour's goods and future gains makes you poor. The right limit: first what's needed, then what's enough.
seneca-001-p07.core_idea: Poverty is craving more, not having little.

seneca-001-p08.plain: If you don't trust a friend as you trust yourself, you misunderstand friendship. Judge a person before befriending him, not after. Think long before admitting someone; once you do, welcome him wholeheartedly and speak as freely as to yourself.
seneca-001-p08.core_idea: Judge before befriending; then trust completely.

seneca-001-p09.plain: Some people pour out private matters to anyone they meet; others won't confide even in their closest friends. Both are wrong: trusting everyone and trusting no one are equal faults, though the first is more innocent and the second safer.
seneca-001-p09.core_idea: Trusting everyone and trusting no one are both faults.

seneca-001-p10.plain: Love of busyness is not hard work; it is only the restlessness of a hunted mind. And true rest isn't rejecting all activity as a nuisance; that kind of rest is just laziness.
seneca-001-p10.core_idea: Busyness is restlessness; idleness isn't rest.

seneca-001-p11.plain: No evil is great if it is the last one. Death would be worth dreading if it stayed with you, but it either doesn't come at all or comes and passes.
seneca-001-p11.core_idea: Death, the last evil, cannot stay with you.

seneca-001-p12.plain: Most people drift miserably between fear of death and the hardships of life: they don't want to live, and yet they don't know how to die.
seneca-001-p12.core_idea: People fear death yet dislike living.

seneca-001-p13.plain: No good thing makes its owner happy unless his mind has accepted that he might lose it; and nothing is lost more easily than what, once lost, isn't missed.
seneca-001-p13.core_idea: Accept possible loss to enjoy what you have.

judge.issue: Renders lost with less discomfort as lost more easily, blurring the meaning.

seneca-001-p14.plain: No one has been raised so high by Fortune that she didn't threaten him as much as she favoured him. Don't trust her calm: the sea can churn in a moment, and proud ships can sink the same day.
seneca-001-p14.core_idea: Fortune's calm can turn in a moment.

seneca-002-p01.plain: People toil for unnecessary things, which wear out their clothes, keep them in army camps till old age and wreck them on foreign shores. What is enough is close at hand. Whoever has made peace with poverty is rich.
seneca-002-p01.core_idea: Whoever makes peace with poverty is rich.

seneca-002-p02.plain: Just as one chain binds a prisoner to the soldier guarding him, hope and fear, though unlike, march together: fear follows hope.
seneca-002-p02.core_idea: Hope and fear are chained together.

seneca-002-p03.plain: Animals flee dangers they see and then stop worrying, but humans torment themselves over the future and the past. Memory brings back fear and foresight anticipates it. The present alone can make no one miserable.
seneca-002-p03.core_idea: Only past and future torment us; the present doesn't.

seneca-002-p04.plain: Seneca feels not just improved but transformed, though much in him still needs changing. Seeing faults he never noticed proves his spirit is better, just as a sick man who knows he is sick is congratulated.
seneca-002-p04.core_idea: Seeing your faults is a sign of progress.

judge.issue: Recasts first-person confession to Lucilius as third-person report about Seneca.

seneca-002-p05.plain: Many have lacked not a friend but a friendship. That can't happen when souls are joined by shared, honourable aims, because then people know they hold everything in common, especially their troubles.
seneca-002-p05.core_idea: True friends share everything, especially troubles.

seneca-002-p06.plain: Nothing pleases me, however good, if I must keep it to myself. If wisdom were offered on condition that I hide it, I'd refuse it. No good thing is pleasant to have without friends to share it.
seneca-002-p06.core_idea: No good is pleasant without friends to share it.

seneca-002-p07.plain: Asked what progress he had made, a man answered that he had begun to be a friend to himself. That is a great gain: such a person is never alone, and is surely a friend to all humankind.
seneca-002-p07.core_idea: Befriend yourself and you are never alone.

seneca-002-p08.plain: Seneca admits his weakness: he never comes home with the same character he took out. Something he had calmed inside is stirred up again, and some enemies he had beaten come back.
seneca-002-p08.core_idea: Going among crowds unsettles the calm we've built.

seneca-002-p09.plain: One example of indulgence or greed does great harm; companions rub off on us. Don't copy the bad because they're many, nor hate the many. Withdraw into yourself; keep company with those who improve you and whom you can improve.
seneca-002-p09.core_idea: Keep company that makes you better; we learn by teaching.

judge.issue: Drops the closing point that the process is mutual: people learn while they teach.

seneca-002-p10.plain: You may ask why you learned all these things. Don't worry that the effort was wasted: you learned them for yourself.
seneca-002-p10.core_idea: Learning for yourself is never wasted.

seneca-003-p01.plain: Many people praise you, but should you be pleased with yourself if the crowd can understand you? Your good qualities should face inward.
seneca-003-p01.core_idea: Let your good qualities face inward.

seneca-003-p02.plain: Fortune's so-called gifts are traps. Anyone who wants a safe life will avoid her sticky lures as far as he can; we think we hold these things, but they hold us.
seneca-003-p02.core_idea: Fortune's gifts are traps that hold us.

seneca-003-p03.plain: Eat to end hunger, drink to quench thirst, dress against cold, house yourself against discomfort; thatch shelters as well as gold. Scorn useless ornament. Only the soul deserves wonder, and to a great soul nothing is great.
seneca-003-p03.core_idea: Meet only real needs; only the soul deserves wonder.

seneca-003-p04.plain: Those who seem to be doing nothing are often doing the greater work, dealing with things both mortal and immortal at once.
seneca-003-p04.core_idea: Quiet reflection can be the greatest work.

judge.issue: Adds 'often', softening the claim that the seemingly idle are busied with greater tasks.

seneca-003-p05.plain: Hecato offers a love potion that needs no drugs, herbs or spells: if you want to be loved, love. There is great pleasure both in keeping old friendships and in making new ones.
seneca-003-p05.core_idea: If you would be loved, love.

fix.display_text: Hecato says: “I can show you a philtre, compounded without drugs, herbs, or any witch’s incantation: ‘If you would be loved, love.’” Now there is great pleasure, not only in maintaining old and established friendships, but also in beginning and acquiring new ones.
