seneca-003-p06.plain: Winning a friend differs from having won one as sowing from reaping. Making a friend pleases more than keeping one, as painting pleases an artist more than the finished picture; so too children's infancy is sweeter than their youth.
seneca-003-p06.core_idea: Making a friend delights more than keeping one.

judge.issue: Drops delight of absorption and that youth yields more fruit; compresses the contrast.

seneca-003-p07.plain: Friends chosen for usefulness last only while useful: the prosperous are crowded with friends, while those who fail stand alone. Whoever becomes your friend because it pays will stop when it no longer pays. Real friendship seeks nothing but friendship.
seneca-003-p07.core_idea: Friends made for profit leave when profit ends.

judge.issue: Drops those who desert or betray through fear.

seneca-004-p01.plain: Whoever thinks himself unlucky is unlucky. What does your situation matter if it looks bad to you?
seneca-004-p01.core_idea: Thinking yourself wretched makes you wretched.

seneca-004-p02.plain: What counts is not what you say but what you feel, and not how you feel on one particular day but how you feel all the time.
seneca-004-p02.core_idea: Lasting feeling, not words, shows contentment.

seneca-004-p03.plain: Crates saw a young man walking alone and asked what he was doing. The youth said he was talking with himself. Crates told him to be careful, because he was keeping company with a bad man.
seneca-004-p03.core_idea: Solitude is only good with good company inside.

seneca-004-p04.plain: Release the gods from your old prayers and pray anew for a sound mind and good health, first of soul, then of body. Pray often, and call boldly on God; you aren't asking for what belongs to another.
seneca-004-p04.core_idea: Pray for a sound mind and health.

seneca-004-p05.plain: You are free of desire when you ask God only for what you could pray aloud. People tell God what they hide from others. So live among people as if God saw you; speak with God as if people heard.
seneca-004-p05.core_idea: Live as if God sees; pray as if people hear.

seneca-004-p06.plain: Even the steadiest speakers sweat, tremble, or stammer before an audience. Training and experience never remove this; nature uses such weakness to make her power felt even in the strongest.
seneca-004-p06.core_idea: Even the strong cannot train away nature's nerves.

seneca-004-p07.plain: We avoid most wrongdoing if someone we respect is near when we're tempted. Happy is the one who improves others even in their thoughts, and the one who steadies himself by recalling someone he reveres; he'll soon deserve reverence.
seneca-004-p07.core_idea: Keep someone you revere in mind to stay good.

judge.issue: Drops the soul needing someone it respects to hallow its inner shrine.

seneca-004-p08.plain: Choose a mentor whose life, talk and face satisfy you, and always picture him as your guardian or model. We need someone to measure our character against; you can't straighten what's crooked without a ruler.
seneca-004-p08.core_idea: You need a model, as a ruler straightens lines.

seneca-004-p09.plain: Let's cherish and love old age; it is full of pleasure if you know how to use it. Fruit tastes best at the season's end, youth is most charming as it closes, and the drinker enjoys the last glass most.
seneca-004-p09.core_idea: Old age is full of pleasure if used well.

seneca-005-p01.plain: Life is most delightful on the downward slope before the steep drop, and even the very edge has pleasures, or not wanting pleasures replaces them. How comforting to have worn out your appetites and be done with them.
seneca-005-p01.core_idea: Late life brings the relief of spent appetites.

seneca-005-p02.plain: Young and old alike should look death in the face; we aren't called in order of age. Yet no one is too old to hope for one more day, and one day is a stage on life's journey.
seneca-005-p02.core_idea: Face death at any age; each day still counts.

seneca-005-p03.plain: If God grants another day, welcome it gladly. The happiest person, secure in himself, awaits tomorrow without fear. Whoever can say he has truly lived receives each new morning as a bonus.
seneca-005-p03.core_idea: Having lived, each new day is a bonus.

seneca-005-p05.plain: We only gain full faith in our strength after facing many difficulties, some at close range. A fighter enters the ring confidently only after being bloodied and knocked down in body but not spirit, rising each time more defiant.
seneca-005-p05.core_idea: Confidence comes from rising after many falls.

judge.issue: Drops the spirit that refuses to be ruled by external things.

seneca-005-p06.plain: More things frighten us than harm us; we suffer more in imagination than in reality. Don't be unhappy before the crisis comes; it may never come. We exaggerate, imagine or anticipate sorrow, suffering more, sooner or needlessly.
seneca-005-p06.core_idea: We suffer more in imagination than reality.

seneca-005-p07.plain: When people try to convince you that you are unhappy, attend to what you feel, not what you hear; you know your affairs best. Ask whether there is real harm or just talk, and whether you're inventing an evil.
seneca-005-p07.core_idea: Trust your own sense of your troubles, not others'.

seneca-005-p08.plain: First check whether your evidence of future trouble is solid. We're usually troubled by fears and rumour and believe talk too quickly. We don't test our fears; we flee like soldiers panicked by dust from stampeding cattle.
seneca-005-p08.core_idea: Test your fears before running from them.

seneca-005-p09.plain: Some trouble may come, but it isn't here now. How often the unexpected happens and the expected never does! Even if it is certain, why rush to meet suffering? It will come soon enough; meanwhile, look forward to better things.
seneca-005-p09.core_idea: Don't rush out to meet future suffering.

seneca-005-p10.plain: The mind invents evils without evidence, reads the worst into vague words and inflates grudges. Indulge every fear and life is unbearable. Resist with resolve, or balance fear with hope: dreaded things often vanish and hoped-for ones disappoint.

judge.issue: 'Often vanish' softens the claim that it is more certain dreaded things come to nothing.

seneca-005-p11.plain: Among his faults, the fool is always getting ready to live. Think how repellent it is that people lay new foundations for their lives every day and start fresh hopes even at the edge of the grave.
seneca-005-p11.core_idea: The fool is always getting ready to live.

seneca-006-p01.plain: The body may be indulged but not made a master. Live not for the body, but as if you couldn't live without it. Loving it too much brings fear, worry and insult, and makes virtue seem cheap.
seneca-006-p01.core_idea: Care for the body, but don't be its slave.

seneca-006-p02.plain: The wise man looks to the reasons for his actions, not their results. The beginning is in our power; fortune decides the outcome, but I don't let her pass judgment on me.
seneca-006-p02.core_idea: Own your intentions; leave outcomes to fortune.

seneca-006-p03.plain: Whoever craves riches fears for them, and no one enjoys a blessing that brings anxiety; he always wants a little more. Busy increasing his wealth, he forgets how to use it, and from master he becomes a mere steward.
seneca-006-p03.core_idea: Craving wealth turns its master into its servant.

seneca-006-p04.plain: Exercise the mind day and night; moderate work nourishes it, and no weather or old age need stop this training. Cultivate the good that gets better with the years.
seneca-006-p04.core_idea: Cultivate the good that improves with age.

seneca-006-p05.plain: You don't need to bend over your books constantly; the mind needs a change, but one that relaxes it without weakening it.
seneca-006-p05.core_idea: Rest the mind without letting it go slack.

seneca-007-p01.plain: When you see many people ahead of you, think how many are behind. To be grateful for your life, consider how many you have passed. But why bother with others? You have surpassed yourself.
seneca-007-p01.core_idea: Measure progress against yourself, not others.

judge.issue: Drops thanking the gods; gratitude rendered without its religious frame.

seneca-007-p02.plain: Set a limit you won't even want to pass. Away with deceptive goods: they look better to those hoping for them than to those who have them. If they had substance they'd satisfy; instead they make the drinker thirstier.
seneca-007-p02.core_idea: Set a limit; worldly goods never satisfy.

seneca-007-p03.plain: No one can live happily, or even bearably, without studying wisdom; completed wisdom brings happiness, begun wisdom makes life bearable. Keeping the resolutions you've made matters more than making grand new ones; persevere until good inclination becomes settled purpose.
seneca-007-p03.core_idea: Keep your resolutions until they become character.

seneca-007-p04.plain: Philosophy isn't a show or a pastime; it is deeds, not words. It shapes the soul, orders life, guides conduct and steers us through uncertainty. Without it no one lives fearlessly or at peace.
seneca-007-p04.core_idea: Philosophy shapes the soul and steers life.

seneca-007-p05.plain: Natural desires have limits; desires born of false opinion have none. A road ends, but wandering doesn't. To tell natural desire from misleading desire, ask whether it can stop somewhere; if the goal keeps receding, it is against nature.
seneca-007-p05.core_idea: Natural desires have limits; false ones never end.

seneca-007-p06.plain: Whatever made poverty hard also makes wealth hard. A sick man is sick on any bed, and a troubled mind stays troubled whether it is rich or poor; the illness travels with the person.
seneca-007-p06.core_idea: A troubled mind stays troubled, rich or poor.

seneca-008-p01.plain: It takes courage to stay sober while the crowd gets drunk, but more self-control to join in the festival in your own restrained way, neither standing out nor losing yourself in the crowd.
seneca-008-p01.core_idea: Join in with the crowd, but on your own terms.

seneca-008-p02.plain: Use calm, easy times to toughen your mind for hard ones, as soldiers drill in peacetime. If you don't want someone to flinch in a crisis, train them before it arrives.
seneca-008-p02.core_idea: Prepare for hardship while times are good.

seneca-008-p03.plain: A fire's damage depends on what it lands on: solid wood resists, dry tinder blazes. Anger works the same way; great anger ends in madness, so avoid anger altogether to keep your mind healthy.
seneca-008-p03.core_idea: Avoid anger to keep a healthy mind.

seneca-008-p05.plain: In a quieter, private life you would have less but feel full; now you have plenty and are never satisfied. Would you rather be poor and content, or rich and hungry? Wealth is greedy and draws others' greed.
seneca-008-p05.core_idea: Better poor and content than rich and hungry.

judge.issue: Drops that while nothing satisfies you, you cannot satisfy others.

seneca-008-p06.plain: Think harder about who you will eat and drink with than about what you will eat. A meal without a friend is the life of a lion or a wolf.
seneca-008-p06.core_idea: Choose your companions more carefully than your food.

seneca-008-p07.plain: Don't pick friends among those who come to flatter you. A busy, wealthy man thinks people are his friends when he is no friend to them; a small debt makes someone owe you, a large one makes them hate you.
seneca-008-p07.core_idea: Big favours can turn people into enemies.

judge.issue: Recasts reception-hall choice as flatterers; drops the belief that favours win friends.

seneca-009-p01.plain: The highest mark of wisdom is that your actions match your words and you stay the same person in every situation. Few manage it, and no philosopher keeps the same pace always, but he can always walk the same path.
seneca-009-p01.core_idea: Wisdom means your actions match your words.

seneca-009-p02.plain: Choose one standard to live by and run your whole life by it. People who live modestly at home but show off in public reveal an unsteady mind that hasn't found its balance.
seneca-009-p02.core_idea: Live by one consistent standard everywhere.

seneca-009-p03.plain: Poverty keeps your true friends and clears away those who wanted what you had. You might love it for that alone, since it shows who really loves you. When will no one flatter you with lies?
seneca-009-p03.core_idea: Poverty reveals who truly loves you.

seneca-009-p04.plain: Nobody is born rich. Every baby must make do with milk and rags; that is how we all start, and yet later whole kingdoms feel too small for us.
seneca-009-p04.core_idea: We start with little, then want everything.

seneca-009-p05.plain: Your biggest obstacle is yourself. You don't know what you want; you approve the right path more readily than you follow it; you see where real happiness lies but lack the courage to reach it.
seneca-009-p05.core_idea: You are your own biggest obstacle.

seneca-009-p06.plain: Time will sweep over us all like a flood. A few great people will keep their heads above it for a long while, fighting oblivion, though in the end they too will go into silence.
seneca-009-p06.core_idea: Time buries all; a few resist longer.

seneca-009-p07.plain: Epicurus said that to make Pythocles rich, you shouldn't give him more money but take away some of his desires.
seneca-009-p07.core_idea: Wealth comes from wanting less, not having more.

seneca-010-p01.plain: People complain about their ambitions the way lovers complain about each other: it is squabbling, not real hatred. They stay by choice in what they call unbearable. A few are held by slavery; many more cling to it.
seneca-010-p01.core_idea: Many people cling to what they claim enslaves them.

seneca-010-p02.plain: If you keep looking back to see how much wealth you can take with you into a quieter life, you will never get out. No one can swim to shore carrying their luggage.
seneca-010-p02.core_idea: You can't escape while clutching your possessions.

seneca-010-p03.plain: Catch anyone unawares, young or old, and you will find them equally afraid of death and equally ignorant of how to live. No one has finished anything, because we keep postponing everything to the future.
seneca-010-p03.core_idea: Postponing life leaves us afraid of death.

seneca-010-p04.plain: A person has understood wisdom if they can die as free of worry as when they were born. Instead we panic as the end nears, turning pale and weeping uselessly. What is worse than fretting at the doorway of peace?
seneca-010-p04.core_idea: Wisdom is dying as calmly as you were born.

seneca-010-p05.plain: People care how long they live, not how well, though anyone can choose to live nobly and no one can choose to live long.
seneca-010-p05.core_idea: Living nobly is in our power; living long isn't.

seneca-010-p06.plain: The foundation, and really the summit, of a sound mind is not taking joy in useless things and not letting outside things control your happiness. Anyone driven by hope for something, however attainable, stays troubled and unsure.
seneca-010-p06.core_idea: Don't let external things control your happiness.

seneca-010-p07.plain: I want you never to lack gladness, and for it to be born at home, inside you. Other pleasures only smooth the brow for a while; laughing isn't joy. The soul itself must be happy and confident, above every circumstance.
seneca-010-p07.core_idea: Real gladness is born inside you.

seneca-010-p08.plain: Real good comes from a clear conscience, honourable aims, right actions, indifference to luck, and a calm, steady life on one path. People who jump from one goal to another, or drift by chance, cannot hold any lasting good.
seneca-010-p08.core_idea: Lasting good comes from a steady, honest life.

seneca-010-p09.plain: Few steer their lives by a clear purpose; the rest drift like things in a river, some gently, some violently, some stranded, some swept out to sea. So decide what you want and stick to it.
seneca-010-p09.core_idea: Decide what you want and stick to it.

seneca-011-p01.plain: Some people only start living when it's time to stop. More surprising still, some have stopped living before they ever began.
seneca-011-p01.core_idea: Some stop living before they ever begin.

seneca-011-p02.plain: Why invite trouble early and spoil today by fearing tomorrow? It is foolish to be unhappy now over what might come. Instead, assume what you fear will happen, size it up, and you'll see it is either small or brief.
seneca-011-p02.core_idea: Measure your fear; it is smaller than you think.

seneca-011-p03.plain: Death is so little to be feared that, thanks to it, there is nothing left to fear at all.
seneca-011-p03.core_idea: Because of death, nothing need be feared.

seneca-011-p04.plain: Strip things of everything that disturbs and confuses, and see what they really are; you'll find nothing fearful in them but the fear. Like children scared of loved ones in masks, we must take the masks off things.
seneca-011-p04.core_idea: Unmask things; often only the fear is frightening.

seneca-011-p05.plain: Have you only just realised that death, exile and grief hang over you? You were born into these dangers. Let us treat everything that could happen as something that will happen.
seneca-011-p05.core_idea: Expect that whatever can happen will happen.

seneca-011-p06.plain: If I become poor, I'll be one of many; if exiled, I'll treat my new place as home; if chained, I'm already bound to a body. Saying 'I shall die' really means I'll no longer risk sickness, prison, or death.
seneca-011-p06.core_idea: Feared misfortunes lose their power when examined.

seneca-011-p07.plain: We lose childhood, then youth; all past time is gone, and even today is shared with death. As the last drop doesn't empty the water-clock alone, our final hour only completes a dying we've long been doing.
seneca-011-p07.core_idea: We are dying a little every day.

seneca-011-p08.plain: Epicurus says it is absurd to rush toward death because you're tired of life, when it was your way of living that drove you toward death.
seneca-011-p08.core_idea: Weariness of life comes from how we live.

seneca-012-p01.plain: I don't know if I'll succeed, but I'd rather lack success than lack faith. Don't give up on curing the sick even when the illness is long-standing, if you resist excess and make them do hard things.
seneca-012-p01.core_idea: Better to lack success than lack faith.

seneca-012-p02.plain: Act as if Epicurus were watching you. It helps to have someone to look up to as a witness of your thoughts; live as if a good person were beside you, since solitude tempts us to wrongdoing.
seneca-012-p02.core_idea: Live as if a good person were watching.

judge.issue: Drops the fallback standard: act as if anyone at all were looking on.

seneca-012-p03.plain: Only my vices and what fed them have grown old; my mind is strong and glad to be loosely tied to the body. It has set down most of its load and calls old age its time to bloom.
seneca-012-p03.core_idea: In old age, the mind can bloom.

seneca-012-p04.plain: Ignore public opinion, which always wavers, and set aside your learning; death will give the final verdict. Your clever talk and gathered maxims prove nothing about your soul's strength. What you truly are shows only at your last breath.
seneca-012-p04.core_idea: Your last breath shows your soul's true strength.

seneca-012-p05.plain: You are younger, but so what? Our years are not counted out in advance. You don't know where death is waiting for you, so be ready for it everywhere.
seneca-012-p05.core_idea: Death may come anywhere; be ready.

seneca-012-p06.plain: I'm not so shameless as to try to cure others while I am sick myself. I am discussing troubles we share and passing on the remedy, as if we lay ill in the same hospital.
seneca-012-p06.core_idea: We share our troubles as fellow patients.

seneca-012-p07.plain: Before you die, make sure your faults die first. Disordered pleasures cost dearly and leave regret. Seek a good that lasts, which the soul can find only within itself; virtue alone gives lasting, peaceful joy, untouched by passing troubles.
seneca-012-p07.core_idea: Let your faults die before you do.

judge.issue: Drops that guilty pleasures are insubstantial and fleeting even when harmless.

seneca-013-p01.plain: Do you think you're the only one this has happened to, that all your travel hasn't lifted the heaviness from your mind? What you need is a change of soul, not a change of climate.
seneca-013-p01.core_idea: You need a change of soul, not scenery.

seneca-013-p02.plain: Socrates asked why travel would help when you always take yourself along. New places are useless if you flee with yourself in tow. Until you put down the burdens of your mind, no place will satisfy you.
seneca-013-p02.core_idea: Wherever you go, you take yourself with you.

seneca-013-p03.plain: Who you are matters more than where you go, so don't tie your mind to any one place. Live by this: I wasn't born for one corner of the universe; the whole world is my country.
seneca-013-p03.core_idea: The whole world is my country.

seneca-013-p04.plain: I disagree with those who seek a stormy life and wrestle with problems daily. The wise person endures all that but doesn't choose it, preferring peace to war. Casting out your faults helps little if you then fight others'.
seneca-013-p04.core_idea: The wise endure storms but prefer peace.

seneca-013-p05.plain: Epicurus said knowing your wrongdoing begins salvation; you can't want correction until you see you're wrong. Rather than boasting of faults, find yourself guilty: be accuser, then judge, then advocate, and sometimes be hard on yourself.
seneca-013-p05.core_idea: Admitting your faults is the start of reform.

seneca-013-p06.plain: Don't count how many people frighten you. Many may threaten your life, but only one at a time can reach you. Nature has arranged it so that as only one gave you life, only one will take it away.
seneca-013-p06.core_idea: Many may threaten, but only one can strike.

seneca-013-p07.plain: Winning popular approval takes trickery and making yourself like the crowd. But what you think of yourself matters far more than what others think. The favour of low people can only be won by low means.
seneca-013-p07.core_idea: Your own judgment of yourself matters most.

seneca-013-p08.plain: Philosophy makes us joyful even facing death, strong and cheerful whatever state the body is in. A great pilot can still sail with torn sails, and keep even a wrecked hull on course.
seneca-013-p08.core_idea: A strong mind sails on when the body fails.

seneca-014-p01.plain: Leaving calmly when your hour comes takes long practice. Other dangers leave hope: illnesses end, fires go out, people survive. But old age leading toward death grants no reprieve; no ending is gentler, yet none lingers longer.
seneca-014-p01.core_idea: Departing calmly in old age takes long practice.

seneca-014-p02.plain: Whoever doesn't want to die never truly wanted to live, since life is given on condition of death. It is foolish to fear what is certain. Death's rule is fair and binds everyone; equality is the heart of fairness.
seneca-014-p02.core_idea: Life is given on condition of death.

seneca-014-p03.plain: An enemy threatens death, but indigestion gets there first. Some fears are real, others only seem so. We fear not death but the thought of it. Death is always equally near, so no time of life is free of it.
seneca-014-p03.core_idea: We fear the thought of death, not death.

judge.issue: Drops the reasoning that if death is to be feared, it must be feared always.

seneca-014-p04.plain: Don't listen to those who love you most; they wish bad things for you with good intentions. If you want to be happy, ask the gods that none of their fond wishes for you come true.
seneca-014-p04.core_idea: Loved ones often wish us the wrong things.

seneca-015-p01.plain: What are 'Roman knight', 'freedman's son' or 'slave'? Just titles born of ambition or injustice. A person can leap to heaven from the slums.
seneca-015-p01.core_idea: Anyone can rise to greatness from any origin.

seneca-015-p02.plain: Anyone who holds you back does real harm, since life is short, and we shorten it further by being unsteady, always making fresh starts. We break life into little pieces and fritter it away.
seneca-015-p02.core_idea: Constant fresh starts fritter life away.

seneca-015-p03.plain: When will you reach the point where time means nothing to you, calm and unconcerned about tomorrow because you are fully enjoying your life? People crave the future because no one has yet found himself.
seneca-015-p03.core_idea: We crave the future because we haven't found ourselves.

seneca-015-p04.plain: I'll use the old road, but take a shorter, smoother one if I find it. Earlier discoverers are guides, not masters. Truth is open to all, owned by no one, and much remains for future generations.
seneca-015-p04.core_idea: Past thinkers are guides, not masters.

seneca-015-p05.plain: A friend loves you, but not everyone who loves you is a friend. Friendship always helps; love can sometimes do harm. Work on improving yourself, if only so you learn how to love.
seneca-015-p05.core_idea: Not everyone who loves you is your friend.

seneca-015-p06.plain: We feel joy about loved ones even when apart, but it is light and brief. Seeing someone, being with them and talking together gives a living pleasure, especially when they are the kind of person you hoped for.
seneca-015-p06.core_idea: Being together brings a living joy.

judge.issue: 'Especially when' loosens the condition that living pleasure needs the sort of man desired.

seneca-016-p01.plain: Hurry to find me, but find yourself first. Above all, be consistent with yourself. To test your progress, ask whether you want the same things today as yesterday. A shifting will means a mind adrift; what is settled stays put.
seneca-016-p01.core_idea: Progress means wanting the same things consistently.

seneca-016-p02.plain: Look how the universe repeats its cycle: no star goes out; they set and rise in turn. Summer leaves but returns next year, winter comes back in its months, and night overwhelms the sun only for day to return.
seneca-016-p02.core_idea: Everything that sets will rise again.

seneca-016-p03.plain: You ask how to free yourself. You can't escape what is necessary, but you can overcome it.
seneca-016-p03.core_idea: You can't escape necessity, but you can overcome it.

seneca-016-p04.plain: No one knows how they started craving what they crave; impulse, not thought, drove them there. It is shameful to drift instead of moving forward, then suddenly ask, dazed, in the middle of the whirlpool, how you got here.
seneca-016-p04.core_idea: Don't drift, then wonder how you got here.

judge.issue: Drops 'Fortune attacks us as often as we attack Fortune'.

seneca-016-p05.plain: Words should be scattered like seed: however small, in good ground they grow great. Reason grows the same way, increasing as it works. Few words are needed; if the mind truly takes them in, they gain strength and spring up.
seneca-016-p05.core_idea: A few good words can grow great in the mind.

seneca-016-p06.plain: Like a flame, the soul is always moving, and the more eager, the more active. Happy is the one who turns it toward better things: he rises above chance, handles good fortune wisely, eases hardship, and scorns what others admire.
seneca-016-p06.core_idea: Direct the soul's restless energy toward better things.

seneca-016-p07.plain: A great soul scorns great things and prefers the ordinary to the excessive. Too-rich soil flattens grain and heavy loads break branches; likewise the soul is ruined by unchecked prosperity, which harms both others and itself.

seneca-017-p01.plain: Need sets a limit, but nothing limits luxuries. So people sink into pleasures until what was extra becomes essential, and they become slaves to them. Worst of all is loving your own ills, when vices have become habits beyond cure.
seneca-017-p01.core_idea: Luxuries become needs, and then we're enslaved.

seneca-017-p02.plain: Thank you for writing so often; your letters show me your real self and bring me straight into your company. If pictures of absent friends please us, a letter, carrying real traces of a friend's hand, pleases far more.
seneca-017-p02.core_idea: A friend's letter brings their real presence.

judge.issue: Drops that a letter gives what is sweetest in meeting: recognition of the friend.

seneca-017-p03.plain: No need to raise hands to heaven or beg at temples. God is near you, with you, within you. A holy spirit dwells in us, watching our deeds; as we treat it, it treats us. None is good without God.
seneca-017-p03.core_idea: God is near you, with you, within you.

judge.issue: Drops that none rises above fortune without God's help, and that God gives upright counsel.

seneca-017-p04.plain: If you saw someone fearless in danger, free of cravings, happy in hardship, calm in a storm, wouldn't you feel reverence? You'd say such greatness is too lofty for a small body; a divine power has come upon them.
seneca-017-p04.core_idea: A calm, fearless soul seems touched by the divine.

judge.issue: Drops looking down on men and viewing the gods as equals.

seneca-017-p05.plain: Take pride only in what is truly yours. We praise a vine for its fruit, not golden leaves. Slaves, houses and income are outside a person. Praise what can't be given or taken: the soul, and reason perfected in it.

seneca-018-p01.plain: We think we only 'buy' what we pay cash for, yet we spend our very selves, through anxiety, danger, honour, freedom and time, as if nothing were cheaper than ourselves. Check the true price; often what costs nothing costs most.
seneca-018-p01.core_idea: What costs nothing often costs us most.

judge.issue: Drops the close: we would belong to ourselves if these things did not own us.

seneca-018-p02.plain: This thing will perish? It was an extra; you'll live without it as before. Whether you had it long or briefly, losing it is bearable. Less money means less trouble; less influence, less envy.
seneca-018-p02.core_idea: Every loss also removes a burden.

seneca-018-p03.plain: Look at the losses we weep over: what troubles us is not the loss but the idea of loss. Our mind tells us something is gone. Whoever owns himself has lost nothing, but few are blessed with owning themselves.
seneca-018-p03.core_idea: Whoever owns himself has lost nothing.

seneca-018-p04.plain: A good conscience is happy among crowds; a bad one is troubled even alone. If your deeds are honourable, let everyone know; if shameful, what does secrecy matter when you know? How wretched to scorn that witness.
seneca-018-p04.core_idea: You yourself always witness your own deeds.

seneca-018-p05.plain: The well-born are those naturally fitted for virtue. Trace any family far enough and its origins are mixed. Ancestral busts don't make a noble; the past isn't ours. Only the soul ennobles us, and it can rise from any condition.
seneca-018-p05.core_idea: Only the soul makes a person noble.

seneca-018-p06.plain: Everyone wants a happy life but mistakes the means for happiness, fleeing it while seeking it. Happiness is freedom from care, yet people pile up worries. As in a maze, the faster you hurry, the worse you're tangled.
seneca-018-p06.core_idea: Chasing happiness's trappings drives it away.

seneca-018-p07.plain: Things lead us astray, so we must learn to tell them apart. We embrace bad instead of good and pray for the opposite of what we once prayed for. Our prayers clash with our prayers, our plans with our plans.

seneca-019-p01.plain: Flattery looks so like friendship that it outdoes it, welcomed deep into the heart and pleasing exactly where it harms. Enemies come as friends; vices pass for virtues, rashness for bravery, cowardice for prudence. Mistaking them is dangerous.

seneca-019-p02.plain: Everyone lives for tomorrow, and that does great harm: such people don't live, they prepare to live, postponing everything. As it is, life passes us by as if it were someone else's, perishing a little each day.
seneca-019-p02.core_idea: Living for tomorrow means never truly living.

seneca-019-p03.plain: Treat those below you as you would want those above you to treat you. Whenever you think how much power you have over a slave, remember your master has just as much over you.
seneca-019-p03.core_idea: Treat inferiors as you'd want superiors to treat you.

seneca-019-p04.plain: Don't seek friends only in public life; look carefully and you'll find them at home. Good material often waits for an artist. Judging a horse by its saddle is foolish; judging a person by clothes or rank is doubly so.
seneca-019-p04.core_idea: Don't judge people by their clothes or rank.

seneca-020-p01.plain: Show me someone who isn't a slave: to lust, greed, ambition, and all to fear. Ex-consuls, millionaires and nobles are enslaved to others. No slavery is more shameful than the kind we choose for ourselves.
seneca-020-p01.core_idea: Self-imposed slavery is the most shameful.

seneca-020-p02.plain: What annoys us doesn't necessarily harm us. Our luxurious lives make us fly into rage at anything that doesn't suit our whims.
seneca-020-p02.core_idea: Luxury makes small annoyances feel like injuries.

seneca-020-p03.plain: One sign of good character is that it forms its own judgments and sticks to them; badness is fickle, always changing, not for the better but just for something different.
seneca-020-p03.core_idea: Good character holds steady; badness keeps shifting.

seneca-020-p04.plain: Friendship makes all our interests shared; no one's fortune is theirs alone, since we live in common. No one who thinks only of his own advantage can be happy; live for your neighbour if you would live for yourself.
seneca-020-p04.core_idea: Live for your neighbour to live for yourself.

seneca-020-p05.plain: It is careless to remember a friend only when a landscape reminds you. Yet familiar places can stir a stored-away sense of loss, waking old memories, just as a lost friend's cloak or house renews grief that time had softened.
seneca-020-p05.core_idea: Familiar places reawaken grief softened by time.

seneca-020-p06.plain: It seems only a moment since I was a schoolboy, a moment since I began pleading in court, then lost the wish and the ability. Time flies incredibly fast, as those looking back see; in the present we barely notice.
seneca-020-p06.core_idea: Time flies; we only see it looking back.

seneca-020-p07.plain: All past time lies together in one abyss. Life is a point, even less, yet nature makes it seem longer by dividing it into infancy, childhood, youth, middle years and old age. So many steps for so short a climb.
seneca-020-p07.core_idea: Life is brief, though its stages make it seem long.

seneca-021-p01.plain: Death trails me and life slips away; teach me to face this. Help me stop fleeing death and keep life from fleeing me. Show me life's good lies in its use, not length; many who live long live too little.
seneca-021-p01.core_idea: Life's worth lies in its use, not length.

seneca-021-p02.plain: Don't think the gap between life and death is narrow only at sea. It is just as narrow everywhere. Death doesn't show itself as close everywhere, but everywhere it is just as close.

seneca-021-p03.plain: Why fool ourselves? Our trouble is not outside us but deep within, and healing is harder because we don't even know we are sick.
seneca-021-p03.core_idea: Our trouble is within, and we don't see it.

seneca-021-p04.plain: Everything yields to steady, careful treatment; bent timber can be straightened, and heat reshapes curved beams. How much more easily the soul can be shaped, since it is more pliable than any liquid.
seneca-021-p04.core_idea: With patient effort, the soul can be reshaped.

seneca-021-p05.plain: Don't lose hope for us because we're caught in evil, even for a long time. No one gets a good mind before a bad one; the bad takes hold of us first. Learning virtue means unlearning vice.

seneca-022-p01.plain: What force drags us one way while we aim another, toward what we want to leave? Something fights our spirit and won't let us want anything for good. We swerve between plans; no wish is free, whole, or lasting.
seneca-022-p01.core_idea: We swerve between plans; no wish lasts.

seneca-022-p02.plain: Some natures, like buildings on firm ground, rise easily; others must first sink foundations through soft soil, hidden work that is the larger part. Luckier is one never troubled by himself; worthier is one who wrestled his way to wisdom.
seneca-022-p02.core_idea: Wisdom won through struggle deserves more credit.

seneca-022-p03.plain: Choose as your guide someone you admire more when you watch them act than when you hear them speak.
seneca-022-p03.core_idea: Choose guides whose actions outshine their words.

seneca-022-p04.plain: How foolish to leave a lecture happy just because ignorant people applauded. Why enjoy praise from people you yourself can't praise?
seneca-022-p04.core_idea: Don't value praise from those you don't respect.

seneca-022-p05.plain: Why won't anyone admit their faults? Because they are still in their grip. Only someone awake can tell their dream, so confessing your wrongs shows a sound mind.
seneca-022-p05.core_idea: Admitting faults shows you've woken from them.

seneca-023-p01.plain: What a privilege, to have a human's weaknesses and a god's calm. Philosophy's power to soften the blows of chance is beyond belief.
seneca-023-p01.core_idea: Philosophy softens the blows of chance.

seneca-023-p02.plain: Death is non-existence, which I already know from before my birth, when I felt nothing. A lamp is no worse off put out than before it was lit; we too are lit and put out, with peace on either side.
seneca-023-p02.core_idea: Death is like the peace before birth.

judge.issue: Omits that suffering comes in the period between being lit and extinguished.

seneca-023-p03.plain: I won't be frightened at the last hour; I'm prepared. Admire someone who enjoys living yet doesn't mind dying. The wise man is never thrust out, because he willingly does what necessity is about to force on him.
seneca-023-p03.core_idea: Willingly accept what necessity will force anyway.

judge.issue: Drops the point that even being thrust out can be met as if leaving willingly.

seneca-023-p04.plain: Where you live adds little to peace of mind; the mind must make everything agreeable to itself. I have seen people gloomy in a lovely villa, and others busy and engaged in complete solitude.
seneca-023-p04.core_idea: Peace of mind comes from the mind, not the place.

seneca-023-p05.plain: You can talk with absent friends whenever you like, and enjoy it more for the absence; presence makes us take them for granted. We're often apart even when together. Keep a friend in your spirit, and they're never absent.
seneca-023-p05.core_idea: A friend held in the spirit is never absent.

judge.issue: Drops that absence should be borne cheerfully and that travel robs us of little.

seneca-024-p01.plain: Night doesn't chase our troubles away; it brings them into view and only changes the shape of our worries. Sleepless hours can be as harrowing as the day. Real calm is what a healthy mind reaches when it relaxes.
seneca-024-p01.core_idea: Real calm comes from a healthy mind, not silence.

seneca-024-p02.plain: Picture a man who silences his whole house to sleep, yet tosses and turns, hearing sounds that aren't there. His soul is in uproar and needs soothing. A still body doesn't mean a peaceful soul; sometimes quiet means disquiet.
seneca-024-p02.core_idea: Outer quiet can hide inner turmoil.

seneca-024-p03.plain: You can be sure you're at peace with yourself when no noise reaches you, and no words, whether flattery, threats, or empty buzzing, shake you out of yourself.
seneca-024-p03.core_idea: Inner peace is not being shaken by words.

seneca-025-p01.plain: No one stays the same from youth to age, or even day to day; like Heraclitus's river, we keep flowing. It is madness to cling to the fleeting body and fear dying once, when our former selves die every moment.
seneca-025-p01.core_idea: We change every day; why fear one final change?

seneca-025-p02.plain: We are weak, watery creatures standing among unreal things, so let us turn our minds to what is everlasting.
seneca-025-p02.core_idea: Turn your mind to what is everlasting.

seneca-025-p03.plain: Simple living can carry you to old age, which should be neither refused nor craved. There is pleasure in keeping your own company as long as possible, once you have made yourself worth enjoying.
seneca-025-p03.core_idea: Make yourself good company for your old age.

seneca-026-p02.plain: We are chained by vices we've long wallowed in, not just stained but dyed by them. Folly grips us because we don't fight hard enough for salvation or take the words of the wise to heart; we treat it lightly.
seneca-026-p02.core_idea: Folly grips us because we fight it half-heartedly.

seneca-026-p03.plain: What hinders us most is being too pleased with ourselves. We accept any flattery as our due, even praise for virtues we plainly lack, like a torturer called 'most gentle'. Thinking ourselves the best, we refuse to be reformed.

seneca-026-p04.plain: The wise are joyful and calm, living like the gods. If you're never downcast or anxious about the future and your soul stays even and content, you have the greatest good. Seeking joy through riches and titles brings only grief.
seneca-026-p04.core_idea: Seeking joy in riches and titles brings grief.

judge.issue: Drops that seeking pleasures everywhere leaves you as far from wisdom as from joy.

seneca-026-p05.plain: Such people chase joy without knowing where lasting joy lies: in feasting, honours, lovers, or showy learning. All are misled by brief, deceptive delights, like drunkenness, which buys one wild hour with days of sickness, or costly applause.
seneca-026-p05.core_idea: Brief pleasures deceive us and cost dearly.

seneca-027-p01.plain: How little nature needs to be satisfied! A very small amount sends her away content. It isn't our stomach's real hunger that costs so much, but our anxious cravings.
seneca-027-p01.core_idea: Nature needs little; cravings cost us dearly.

seneca-027-p02.plain: Let us stop wanting what we have long wanted; in old age I no longer desire what I did as a boy. My one task is ending my chronic faults. I live each day as complete, perhaps my last.
seneca-027-p02.core_idea: Live each day as a complete life.

seneca-027-p03.plain: Before I was old, I tried to live well; now that I'm old, I'll try to die well, and dying well means dying gladly. Make sure you never do anything unwillingly.
seneca-027-p03.core_idea: Live well, then die well and gladly.

seneca-027-p04.plain: What is forced on you if you resist isn't forced if you want it. Acting against your will, not under orders, makes us unhappy. So train your mind to want what circumstances demand, and to face your end without sadness.
seneca-027-p04.core_idea: Want what circumstances demand, and you're free.

seneca-027-p05.plain: Prepare for death before preparing for life. Life has enough, but we always feel something missing. Whether you've lived long enough depends on your mind, not your years. I have lived long enough, had my fill, and await death.
seneca-027-p05.core_idea: Living long enough depends on the mind, not years.

seneca-027-p06.plain: People who claim business keeps them from study are fooling us; their appointments are mostly with themselves. My time is free and I'm my own master anywhere, because I lend myself to my affairs rather than surrendering to them.
seneca-027-p06.core_idea: Lend yourself to your affairs; don't surrender.

seneca-027-p07.plain: Anyone can despise everything, but no one can own everything. The shortest road to riches is to despise riches.
seneca-027-p07.core_idea: The shortest road to riches is despising them.

seneca-027-p08.plain: I'm sorry your friend has died, but don't grieve more than is fitting. Not mourning at all is better but fits only someone far above fortune, and even he feels a sting. Moderate tears are forgivable. Weep, but don't wail.
seneca-027-p08.core_idea: We may weep, but we must not wail.

judge.issue: Drops that tears must be checked by our own effort, and that eyes should not stay dry.

seneca-027-p09.plain: Will you forget your friend? If your memory lasts only as long as your grief, it's short-lived; soon something will make you laugh. Once you stop watching yourself suffer, sorrow fades, and the sharper it is, the sooner it ends.
seneca-027-p09.core_idea: Grief fades once you stop watching it.

seneca-027-p10.plain: Let us make the memory of those we have lost a pleasant one. Names of loved ones we've lost will always return with a sting, but there is pleasure even in that sting.
seneca-027-p10.core_idea: Remembering the lost stings, yet brings pleasure.

seneca-027-p11.plain: Thinking of my dead friends is sweet to me. I had them knowing I would one day lose them, and I have lost them as if I still have them.
seneca-027-p11.core_idea: Love friends knowing you'll lose them; keep them after.

seneca-027-p12.plain: Let us enjoy our friends eagerly, since we don't know how long we'll have them. Think how often we're apart on journeys, or fail to meet even when nearby; we lose too much of their time while they live.
seneca-027-p12.core_idea: Enjoy friends now; time with them is short.

seneca-027-p13.plain: If other friends can't console us for losing one, we wrong them. If we have no others, we've hurt ourselves more than Fortune has: she took one friend, but we robbed ourselves of every friend we never made.
seneca-027-p13.core_idea: Unmade friendships are a loss we cause ourselves.

seneca-027-p14.plain: You have buried someone you loved; look around for someone to love. It is better to replace your friend than to weep for him.
seneca-027-p14.core_idea: After loss, look for someone new to love.

seneca-027-p15.plain: Time ends grief even if we don't. But for a sensible person, the most shameful cure for sorrow is growing tired of it. Better to leave grief than have grief leave you; stop soon, since no one can grieve long.
seneca-027-p15.core_idea: Leave grief before grief leaves you.

seneca-027-p16.plain: Reflect now not only that everything is mortal, but that death follows no fixed schedule. Whatever can happen at any time can happen today.
seneca-027-p16.core_idea: Whatever can happen any day can happen today.

seneca-028-p01.plain: Much remains to be done and always will, and someone born a thousand ages from now will still have the chance to add something.
seneca-028-p01.core_idea: There will always be more to discover.

seneca-028-p02.plain: Craftsmen straining their eyes in poor light step outside to rest them in daylight. So the soul, shut up in the dark house of the body, seeks the open sky whenever it can and finds rest in contemplating the universe.
seneca-028-p02.core_idea: The soul rests by contemplating the universe.

seneca-028-p03.plain: The wise person is tied to the body but lives by his better self, thinking of lofty things. He treats life as a term of service, neither loving nor hating it, enduring a mortal lot, knowing a greater one awaits.
seneca-028-p03.core_idea: Treat life as service, neither loved nor hated.

judge.issue: 'Lives by his better self' loses the sense that his better self is absent from the body.

seneca-029-p01.plain: Let us be brave in danger and not fear wrongs, wounds, chains or poverty. Death is either an end or a change. Ceasing to exist is like never beginning; and if I change state, I'll never be this cramped again.
seneca-029-p01.core_idea: Death is an end or a change; neither is fearful.

seneca-029-p02.plain: A great person can come from a hovel, and a beautiful, great soul from an ugly, frail body. Nature seems to make such people to prove virtue can be born anywhere, letting them break through their bodily limits.
seneca-029-p02.core_idea: A great soul can live in any body.

seneca-029-p03.plain: Every honourable act is done willingly. Mix in reluctance, complaint, cowardice or fear and it loses its best quality, self-approval. What isn't free can't be honourable, because fear is slavery.
seneca-029-p03.core_idea: Honour must be free; fear is slavery.

seneca-030-p01.plain: Annoyance, pain and hardship don't matter, because virtue overcomes them. As the sun outshines lesser lights, virtue's greatness overwhelms pains and wrongs, making them no more than a storm-cloud at sea.
seneca-030-p01.core_idea: Virtue outshines every pain and wrong.

seneca-030-p02.plain: The good that true reason approves is solid and lasting, lifting the spirit high. What the crowd praises only puffs us up with empty joy, and what it fears only startles us, as animals startle at the look of danger.
seneca-030-p02.core_idea: Reason's good lasts; the crowd's goods are empty.

seneca-030-p03.plain: One dies young, another old, another as an infant with barely a glimpse of life. All were equally subject to death; it simply let one go further, cut another off in his prime, and stopped the third at the start.
seneca-030-p03.core_idea: All are equally subject to death, at any age.

seneca-030-p04.plain: As perfectly clear weather can't get clearer, someone who cares for body and soul, with no turmoil in the soul and no pain in the body, has reached perfection. Extra delights only add spice; peace of body and soul suffices.
seneca-030-p04.core_idea: Peace in body and soul is the highest good.

seneca-031-p01.plain: Let me say something bolder: if some goods could be greater, I'd rank the harsh ones above the mild and pleasant, because breaking through difficulties is a greater achievement than keeping joy within limits.

seneca-031-p02.plain: I'd rather not suffer torture, war or illness, but if I must, I want to bear them with courage, honour and restraint. So hardship isn't desirable; what is desirable is the virtue that lets us endure it patiently.
seneca-031-p02.core_idea: Not hardship, but virtue to endure it, is desirable.

seneca-031-p03.plain: Put on a hero's courage and step away from common opinion for a while. Picture virtue as something of great beauty and grandeur, worshipped not with incense or garlands but with sweat and blood.
seneca-031-p03.core_idea: Virtue is honoured with sweat and blood.

seneca-031-p04.plain: Demetrius calls an easy life, untroubled by Fortune, a 'Dead Sea'. If nothing stirs you, tests you or threatens your resolve, and you lie in unshaken comfort, that isn't tranquillity, only a flat calm.
seneca-031-p04.core_idea: A life without challenge is a flat calm.

seneca-032-p01.plain: When you withdraw from the world, talk with yourself rather than be talked about. Speak ill of yourself in private, as people do of neighbours, to get used to speaking and hearing truth. Above all, study your greatest weakness.
seneca-032-p01.core_idea: In solitude, honestly examine your own faults.

seneca-032-p02.plain: With my leisure I'm trying to heal my own sores. My trouble is worse than a swollen foot, and hidden: an ulcer deep in my chest. Don't praise me as one who has escaped life's madness; I've condemned only myself.
seneca-032-p02.core_idea: I have condemned nothing except myself.

seneca-032-p03.plain: Others will outdo me in public influence, pay, rank or followers, and that's worth accepting as long as I can outdo Fortune. In the crowd I'm no match for her; she has more backing.
seneca-032-p03.core_idea: Let others win status; aim to outdo Fortune.

seneca-032-p04.plain: Like travellers who set out late and hurry to make up time, let us spur ourselves on. Our age suits this: youth's boiling is past, and faults that raged then are weakened and need little effort to put out.
seneca-032-p04.core_idea: Starting late, speed up; later life suits growth.

seneca-032-p05.plain: I don't like you rushing from place to place. Constant moving shows an unsteady spirit, which can't become whole in retirement until it stops its restless curiosity and wandering. To steady your spirit, first stop your body from running about.
seneca-032-p05.core_idea: To steady the spirit, stop restless wandering.

seneca-032-p06.plain: Someone getting over an old love must avoid every reminder, since nothing regrows as easily as love. Likewise, to let go of things you once craved passionately, turn your eyes and ears away from them.
seneca-032-p06.core_idea: Avoid reminders of what you're trying to leave.

seneca-032-p07.plain: We sail past life, leaving boyhood, youth and our best years astern, until we sight the common end. Fools think it a dangerous reef, but it is the harbour we must all enter; arriving early is like a quick voyage.
seneca-032-p07.core_idea: Death is a harbour, not a reef.

judge.issue: Drops that the early arrival has no right to complain and none may refuse the harbour.

seneca-033-p02.plain: Want to be free of the body's hold? Live in it as if about to leave it. Remembering you'll lose it makes you braver about departing. But how can someone think of their end while craving things without end?
seneca-033-p02.core_idea: Live in the body as if about to leave it.

seneca-033-p03.plain: To decide what to avoid or pursue, ask how it serves your life's whole purpose. A painter can't paint a likeness without knowing his subject; you can't arrange details without a chief aim. We see life's parts, never the whole.
seneca-033-p03.core_idea: Judge every choice by your life's whole purpose.

seneca-033-p04.plain: An archer must know his target before he aims. Our plans fail because they have no aim. If you don't know your harbour, no wind is the right wind. Chance rules our lives because we live by chance.
seneca-033-p04.core_idea: Without a destination, no wind is right.

seneca-033-p05.plain: Devoted to virtue, you'll find everything it touches a blessing, whatever others think. Torture, if you're calmer than your torturer; illness, if you don't curse Fortune: all supposed ills become manageable and end in good if you rise above them.
seneca-033-p05.core_idea: Virtue turns supposed ills into goods.

judge.issue: Drops 'yield not to the disease' and that mere loving of virtue is not enough.

seneca-033-p06.plain: Socrates, who said the highest wisdom is telling good from evil, advised: to be happy, follow these rules and let some think you a fool. Let anyone insult or wrong you; if virtue lives with you, you'll suffer nothing.
seneca-033-p06.core_idea: With virtue, insults and contempt can't harm you.

seneca-034-p01.plain: Everything has its time to be born, grow and be destroyed; even the stars and the earth will end. All things age, at different paces, toward one goal; whatever exists will cease, yet not perish, but return to its elements.
seneca-034-p01.core_idea: Everything ends, returning to its elements.

seneca-034-p02.plain: To the luxurious, simple living is a penalty; to the lazy, work is punishment; to the idle, study is torture. We call things unbearable where we ourselves are weak. These things aren't hard in themselves; we are soft and flabby.
seneca-034-p02.core_idea: Things seem hard because we are soft.

seneca-034-p03.plain: What matters is not only what you see but the eyes you see it with; our souls are too dim-sighted to see the truth.
seneca-034-p03.core_idea: How you see matters as much as what.

seneca-034-p04.plain: It's no wonder that someone stays steady in calm weather. Save your wonder for the person who rises when everyone else sinks and keeps standing when all others have fallen.
seneca-034-p04.core_idea: True strength shows when everyone else falls.

seneca-034-p05.plain: The evil in torture and hardship is the mind sagging and collapsing. That can't happen to the sage; he stands upright under any load and doesn't complain at what can strike anyone. He knows he was born to carry burdens.
seneca-034-p05.core_idea: The wise know they were born to carry burdens.

seneca-034-p06.plain: The wise man is still human and feels pain; he isn't a rock. His irrational part can be hurt; his rational part holds firm, brave and unconquerable. There lies the highest good; until it's reached, the mind wavers.
seneca-034-p06.core_idea: The wise feel pain, but reason stays unconquered.

seneca-034-p07.plain: The wise man overcomes Fortune by virtue, but many who claim wisdom are scared by flimsy threats; we shouldn't demand the same of learners. I still urge myself to do what I recommend, and don't yet follow my own advice.
seneca-034-p07.core_idea: Learners shouldn't be judged like the fully wise.

judge.issue: Drops that his principles are not yet trained to come to his aid in every crisis.

seneca-035-p01.plain: Anything imperfect either advances or slips back, and if you ease off, you lose ground you can't simply resume. So keep going: most of the road lies ahead, but wanting to progress is most of progress.
seneca-035-p01.core_idea: Wanting to progress is the greater part of progress

seneca-035-p02.plain: We should make all our time our own, but that can only happen once we first belong to ourselves.
seneca-035-p02.core_idea: To own your time, first own yourself

seneca-035-p03.plain: When will we master our passions and be able to say we have won? The victory is not over foreign armies but over greed, ambition, and the fear of death, which have beaten even world conquerors.
seneca-035-p03.core_idea: True conquest is over greed, ambition and fear of death

seneca-035-p04.plain: Busy affairs that eat our time should be pushed aside, not patiently sorted out. Any time is right for useful study, yet many people neglect it in exactly the situations that make it necessary.
seneca-035-p04.core_idea: Busyness is no excuse to neglect wisdom

seneca-035-p05.plain: Those still short of wisdom can have their happiness broken, but the wise person's joy is like woven cloth no chance can tear. It depends on nothing outside; it is born within and stays there.
seneca-035-p05.core_idea: The wise person's joy comes from within

seneca-035-p06.plain: A healthy mind is content with itself, trusts itself, and sees that everything people pray for doesn't matter to a happy life. What can be added to or lost is not lasting; Fortune gives us nothing we truly own.
seneca-035-p06.core_idea: Lasting happiness rests only on what is truly yours

judge.issue: Drops 'let the man rejoice in what is truly his own'.

seneca-035-p07.plain: Like a dog snapping at scraps and gulping each one while waiting for more, we bolt whatever Fortune throws us without real pleasure. The wise person is satisfied and sets aside whatever comes to him.
seneca-035-p07.core_idea: Greedy grasping brings no pleasure; the wise are satisfied

seneca-035-p08.plain: Ambitious people never think of all those they have passed, only of those still ahead, and that bothers them more. Every craving is like this: it starts exactly where it ought to stop.
seneca-035-p08.core_idea: Craving always begins where it should end

seneca-035-p09.plain: I owe a great deal to the sun, the moon, the seasons and the god who rules them, even though none of them exists for me alone.
seneca-035-p09.core_idea: We owe thanks even for gifts shared by all

seneca-036-p01.plain: God comes not only near people but into them; no mind without God is good. Divine seeds are scattered in our bodies: a good cultivator grows them into something like their source, a bad one lets weeds take over.
seneca-036-p01.core_idea: Divine seeds in us grow or die by our care

judge.issue: Bad cultivator 'lets weeds take over' rather than killing the divine seeds.

seneca-036-p02.plain: People suffer over children, love and elections, but the largest crowd of the unhappy despair at the expectation of death, which can come from anywhere. Until you lose that fear, you live with a pounding heart.
seneca-036-p02.core_idea: Fear of death makes the most people miserable

seneca-036-p03.plain: We flinch at our neighbours' troubles like birds at the whirr of an empty sling. No one who yields to such fancies can be happy, for happiness needs calm, and a life of dread is poor.
seneca-036-p03.core_idea: Happiness requires calm, not constant dread

seneca-036-p04.plain: Whoever hands himself to Fortune is caught in a web of worry. The only way out is to scorn outside things and be content with what is honourable; whoever values anything above virtue waits anxiously on Fortune.
seneca-036-p04.core_idea: Only valuing virtue frees you from Fortune's web

seneca-036-p05.plain: Virtue needs nothing because it is pleased with what it has and does not crave what it lacks. To virtue, whatever is enough is plenty.

seneca-036-p06.plain: Trust fleeting goods and you soon lose them, and you suffer trying not to. Few people get to set prosperity down gently; most fall along with the things that raised them, crushed by what once lifted them up.
seneca-036-p06.core_idea: What lifts us up can also crush us

seneca-036-p07.plain: No wall can keep Fortune out, so let us strengthen our defences within. If the inner self is safe, a person can be attacked but never captured.
seneca-036-p07.core_idea: A secure inner self can't be captured

seneca-037-p01.plain: Virtue fills the whole soul and is enough on its own. Losing children or friends makes no one less just or wise; while your virtue is unharmed, you will not feel the loss of what is taken.
seneca-037-p01.core_idea: With virtue intact, no loss truly diminishes you

judge.issue: Compressed; drops that losses make one neither happier nor more wretched.

seneca-037-p02.plain: A circle's size doesn't change its shape, and what is straight isn't judged by length or duration. Cut an honourable life down from a hundred years to a single day, and it is just as honourable.
seneca-037-p02.core_idea: An honourable life is honourable at any length

seneca-037-p03.plain: Virtue may rule kingdoms or be hemmed in by poverty, exile or bereavement, yet it is no smaller in a tiny corner. Happiness lives only in the mind, and needs knowledge of things divine and human.
seneca-037-p03.core_idea: Virtue and happiness stay whole in narrow circumstances

judge.issue: Drops explicit conclusion that confined virtue is equally happy.

seneca-037-p04.plain: As the body shows signs before illness, a weak spirit trembles at troubles long before they come. It is madness to be tortured by the future instead of saving strength; if you can't escape suffering, at least postpone it.
seneca-037-p04.core_idea: Don't suffer in advance from troubles not yet here

seneca-037-p05.plain: No one should be tormented by the future, or by sorrows long past. Past and future are both absent; we feel neither of them, and there can be no pain except from what you actually feel.
seneca-037-p05.core_idea: Past and future are absent; we feel neither

seneca-037-p06.plain: Say what you feel and feel what you say; let your speech match your life. A person keeps his promise when he is the same whether you see him or hear him.
seneca-037-p06.core_idea: Let your words match your life

seneca-037-p07.plain: When will you learn it all, fix it in mind, and practise it? Memorising these truths is not enough; they must be tested. The happy person is not the one who knows them but the one who does them.
seneca-037-p07.core_idea: Happiness comes from doing, not merely knowing

seneca-038-p01.plain: We hurry toward virtue while weighed down by vices, and, shamefully, give what is honourable only our spare time. Yet what a reward awaits us if we break away from the distractions and evils that cling to us.
seneca-038-p01.core_idea: We give virtue only our spare time

seneca-038-p02.plain: If we climb out of these low depths, peace of mind and complete freedom await. That freedom means fearing neither people nor gods, craving neither wickedness nor excess, and having full power over yourself; being your own master is priceless.
seneca-038-p02.core_idea: True freedom is mastery over oneself

seneca-038-p03.plain: You should keep learning as long as you don't know, even to the end of your life; as the proverb says, as long as you live, keep learning how to live. Even an old man should keep learning.
seneca-038-p03.core_idea: Keep learning how to live as long as you live

seneca-038-p04.plain: You will make as much progress as you try to make, so why wait? Money, titles and influence may come by chance, but wisdom and virtue never do; they take real effort, and the effort is worth it.
seneca-038-p04.core_idea: Virtue never comes by chance; it takes effort

judge.issue: Drops that the toil wins all goods at a single stroke.

seneca-039-p01.plain: Every action in life turns on whether it is honourable or shameful. A good person does what is honourable even if it brings toil, harm or danger, and refuses what is shameful even if it brings money, pleasure or power.
seneca-039-p01.core_idea: A good person chooses honour over gain or safety

seneca-039-p02.plain: Riches and honours don't make anyone great; you are measuring the pedestal along with the man. To learn someone's true worth, strip away wealth, titles and even the body, and look at the soul itself.
seneca-039-p02.core_idea: Judge a person by the soul, not the pedestal

seneca-039-p03.plain: A trouble thought about in advance strikes gently; for the unprepared, much of the pain is surprise. So the wise person gets used to future hardships by reflecting on them, knowing that anything may come.

seneca-040-p01.plain: Everyone knows they must die, yet they tremble when death nears. Weeping because you won't be alive a thousand years from now is as foolish as weeping because you weren't alive a thousand years ago.
seneca-040-p01.core_idea: Not existing after death is like not existing before birth

seneca-040-p03.plain: During a long illness I was often tempted to end my life, but thinking of my kind old father held me back: he could not bear to lose me. So I ordered myself to live. Sometimes even living takes courage.
seneca-040-p03.core_idea: Sometimes it takes courage simply to live

judge.issue: Adds 'during a long illness', context not in the passage.

seneca-040-p04.plain: Honourable comfort heals, and whatever lifts the soul also helps the body. My studies saved me; I credit philosophy with my recovery and owe it my life, which is the least of what I owe it.
seneca-040-p04.core_idea: Philosophy lifted the soul and healed the body

seneca-040-p05.plain: My friends helped me recover with cheering words and hours at my bedside. Nothing helps the sick or removes the fear of death like friends' affection; I felt I would live on through them.
seneca-040-p05.core_idea: Friends' love eases illness and the fear of death

seneca-040-p06.plain: Illness has often put off death, and facing death has saved many. You will die not because you are sick but because you are alive; when you recover, you have escaped illness, not death.
seneca-040-p06.core_idea: We die because we live, not because we are ill

seneca-040-p07.plain: No one can suffer both severely and for long; Nature, who loves us tenderly, has made pain either bearable or short.
seneca-040-p07.core_idea: Pain is either bearable or brief

seneca-040-p08.plain: People say giving up usual pleasures, fasting and going hungry, is hard. It is at first, but then desire fades and the appetite tires. There is no bitterness in going without what you no longer want.
seneca-040-p08.core_idea: Doing without is painless once desire fades

seneca-041-p01.plain: Don't make your troubles heavier by complaining. Pain is slight if opinion adds nothing to it; tell yourself it is small and will pass, and you make it small. Everything depends on opinion; we suffer according to what we think.
seneca-041-p01.core_idea: We suffer according to our opinion of things

seneca-041-p02.plain: A person is as wretched as he convinces himself he is. Past sufferings, even if real, are over; what was bitter to bear is pleasant to have borne. Root out both fear of future pain and memory of past pain.
seneca-041-p02.core_idea: Let go of past pain and fear of future pain

seneca-041-p03.plain: In the middle of troubles, tell yourself that some day the memory of this sorrow may even bring you pleasure.
seneca-041-p03.core_idea: Today's sorrow may one day be a pleasant memory

seneca-041-p04.plain: Remember the honourable or brave things you have done and look at the good side of your own life. Go over in your mind the things you have most admired.
seneca-041-p04.core_idea: Recall your good deeds and what you admire

seneca-041-p05.plain: There is room for virtue even on a sickbed; you can be brave in your blankets, not only in battle. Your task is to wrestle bravely with illness. Be your own spectator and give yourself the applause.
seneca-041-p05.core_idea: Bravery is possible even on a sickbed

seneca-041-p06.plain: Hold this thought tightly: don't give in to hard times, don't trust good times, and keep in view everything Fortune could do, as if she surely will. What you have long expected arrives more gently.
seneca-041-p06.core_idea: What is long expected arrives more gently

seneca-042-p01.plain: Fame is the shadow of virtue and follows it even unwanted. Like a shadow, it sometimes goes ahead and sometimes lags behind, and when it comes late, after envy has retreated, it is all the greater.
seneca-042-p01.core_idea: Fame follows virtue like a shadow, sometimes late

seneca-042-p02.plain: Virtue is never lost for good; a day will reveal it. Whoever thinks only of his own generation lives for a few. Look to the countless people to come, who will judge you fairly, even if you never know it.
seneca-042-p02.core_idea: Live for the fair judgement of future generations

judge.issue: Loses nuance that being hidden is no loss; posterity's praise unfelt.

seneca-042-p03.plain: Virtue always rewards those who follow it faithfully and stay the same whether watched or caught unprepared. Pretence achieves nothing; masks are easily seen through, and lies are thin and transparent.
seneca-042-p03.core_idea: Pretence fails; lies are thin and transparent

seneca-042-p04.plain: If the body can be trained to take blows and scorching heat, how much more easily can the mind be toughened to take Fortune's blows and rise again? Virtue costs nothing; all that makes you good lies within you.
seneca-042-p04.core_idea: Everything needed to be good lies within you

seneca-042-p05.plain: Compare the faces of the poor and the rich to see how little evil poverty holds. The poor smile more often and more truly, their worries passing like clouds; the rich fake cheer while hiding festering sorrows.
seneca-042-p05.core_idea: The poor often smile more truly than the rich

seneca-042-p06.plain: To judge your own worth, set aside your money, property and honours, and look into your soul. Right now you are taking other people's word for who you are.
seneca-042-p06.core_idea: Judge yourself by your soul, not others' opinion

seneca-042-p07.plain: You complain of meeting an ungrateful person. Being wary only makes you stingy, so the good you might do is lost to you. Better to get nothing back than give nothing; after a poor crop, sow again.
seneca-042-p07.core_idea: Better no return than never giving at all

seneca-042-p08.plain: Finding one grateful person is worth risking many ungrateful ones; givers are often deceived, yet sailors return to sea after shipwreck. Dropping everything troublesome would make life dull; when the outcome is uncertain, keep trying until you succeed.
seneca-042-p08.core_idea: Keep giving and trying despite disappointments

seneca-043-p01.plain: A modest sum given at the right moment can do more than a fortune spent on a palace. It matters greatly whether a gift merely helps or truly rescues someone; often the gift is small but its effects are great.
seneca-043-p01.core_idea: A small timely gift can matter greatly

judge.issue: Recasts the give-outright vs assist, save vs set-up contrast loosely.

seneca-043-p02.plain: We should be as grateful as we can, because gratitude benefits ourselves. Whoever helps another helps himself, not because of any return, but because every virtue is its own reward. The payment for a good deed is having done it.
seneca-043-p02.core_idea: The reward of a good deed is doing it

seneca-043-p03.plain: When we do wrong, the worst of it stays with us; as Attalus said, evil drinks most of its own poison. The ungrateful person torments himself, forgetting kindnesses and clinging to injuries, and nothing is more wretched.
seneca-043-p03.core_idea: Evil drinks most of its own poison

seneca-043-p04.plain: Bad people enjoy a gift only while receiving it, but the wise person delights in having received it, a joy that never fades. He looks down on wrongs done to him and forgets them, not by accident but by choice.
seneca-043-p04.core_idea: Remember kindnesses; choose to forget wrongs

seneca-044-p01.plain: We value a favour most while seeking it and least once we have it, because greed for more makes us forget. Riches, titles and power are not praised because they're worth wanting, but wanted because they're praised.
seneca-044-p01.core_idea: Things are wanted because praised, not praised because worthy

judge.issue: Drops judging by nature not reputation, and the public-individual error cycle.

seneca-044-p02.plain: Both frantic busyness and idleness are to be avoided. Someone lounging on a perfumed couch is as good as dead; leisure without study is death, a tomb for the living.
seneca-044-p02.core_idea: Leisure without study is a living tomb

seneca-044-p03.plain: What good is retreating from the world when the real causes of worry follow you across the sea? No hiding place keeps out fear of death or pain; troubles press in from outside, and fret within even in solitude.
seneca-044-p03.core_idea: Our anxieties follow us wherever we hide

seneca-044-p04.plain: We don't praise poverty, exile, pain or death; we praise the person whom poverty can't humble, who goes into exile with dignity, whom pain can't force, and whose soul death takes before it can be thrown into confusion.
seneca-044-p04.core_idea: We praise those hardship cannot break, not hardship

judge.issue: 'With dignity' loses the point: exile borne as if he were the one sentencing.

seneca-044-p05.plain: Death is not truly an evil, but it looks like one. We are made to love our existence, death seems to rob us of familiar goods, and we shrink from an unknown future and the world of shades.
seneca-044-p05.core_idea: Death only seems evil because we fear the unknown

seneca-045-p01.plain: No act is honourable unless you give yourself to it wholeheartedly. If you act from fear of worse or hope of gain, you are torn two ways and the glory is gone; virtue acts with an undivided, fearless spirit.
seneca-045-p01.core_idea: Honourable action needs a wholehearted, undivided spirit

seneca-045-p02.plain: Live as if everyone could see you, and think as if someone could look into your soul, because someone can. Nothing is hidden from God; he witnesses our souls and enters our thoughts.
seneca-045-p02.core_idea: Live as if God sees into your soul

judge.issue: Drops that God enters our thoughts as one who may at any time depart.

seneca-045-p03.plain: I will watch myself and review each day, a most useful habit. What makes us bad is that none of us looks back over our lives; we think only of what's next, yet our plans always depend on the past.
seneca-045-p03.core_idea: Review each day; the future depends on the past

seneca-045-p04.plain: A gap opens quickly between two people going different ways. My young slave is climbing up while I am coming down, and coming down is much faster. In fact, my life isn't descending now; it is falling.
seneca-045-p04.core_idea: In old age, life falls faster than it rose

seneca-045-p05.plain: The roar and cheering from the races surround me, but they don't break my train of thought. I bear the uproar calmly; the mass of voices sounds like crashing waves or wind in treetops, noise without meaning.
seneca-045-p05.core_idea: A settled mind hears uproar as meaningless noise

seneca-046-p01.plain: Drunkenness doesn't create vice; it reveals it by stripping away the shame that holds people back. Once wine takes over the mind, every hidden evil comes out: the lustful, arrogant, cruel and spiteful all give their vices free rein.
seneca-046-p01.core_idea: Drunkenness doesn't create vice; it reveals it

seneca-046-p02.plain: What glory is there in out-drinking everyone? When the others are asleep or vomiting and you alone are left standing as champion, you have still been beaten by the barrel.
seneca-046-p02.core_idea: Winning at drinking means being beaten by drink

seneca-046-p03.plain: If you come to resemble someone you admire deeply, resemble him as a child resembles a father, not as a painting resembles its subject, for a painting is lifeless.
seneca-046-p03.core_idea: Imitate like a living child, not a lifeless copy

seneca-047-p01.plain: Whatever stands out in human affairs, however petty, is reached by a hard, steep road. But the peak of true greatness, far above Fortune, from which you look down on all that seems loftiest, is reached over level ground.
seneca-047-p01.core_idea: True greatness lies above Fortune, along a level road

seneca-047-p02.plain: Animals, wild or tame, don't obey reason, and neither do passions, however mild. Tigers and lions only soften their wildness for a while, then turn savage when you least expect it. Vices are never truly tamed.

seneca-047-p03.plain: It's foolish to think you can control how something ends when you couldn't control how it started. It is easier to keep a thing out than to hold it down once you've let it in.
seneca-047-p03.core_idea: Easier to keep out than to control once in

seneca-047-p04.plain: Being full is the limit of eating and drinking: one eats more, another less, but both are satisfied. So too, one lives many years and another few; it doesn't matter, if the many held as much happiness as the few.
seneca-047-p04.core_idea: A short happy life equals a long one

seneca-048-p01.plain: Evil is giving in to so-called evils and handing them your freedom. Bravery is not recklessness or love of danger; it is knowing what is truly evil and what isn't, and patiently bearing what only seems evil.
seneca-048-p01.core_idea: Bravery is knowing what is truly evil

judge.issue: Drops that we should suffer all things to keep our liberty.

seneca-048-p02.plain: A pilot promises not a smooth voyage but skilled steering, and storms show his skill all the more. If the sea sinks him only on an even keel, he has done his job; storms affect his success, not his work.
seneca-048-p02.core_idea: Storms affect your success, not your skill

seneca-048-p03.plain: Phidias could make the best possible statue from ivory, bronze, marble or cheaper stuff. So the wise person practises virtue in wealth or poverty, home or exile, health or frailty, making something worthwhile of whatever fortune brings.
seneca-048-p03.core_idea: Make something worthwhile of whatever fortune gives

seneca-049-p01.plain: If I have bread, figs are a treat; if not, figs are my bread, so every day is a feast. The soul is greatest when it drops all outside things, finding peace by fearing nothing and riches by craving none.
seneca-049-p01.core_idea: Riches come from craving no riches
