seneca-049-p02.plain: I ride a shabby farm cart and can hardly bear others thinking it mine; I blush when grander travellers pass. So the simplicity I praise hasn't fully taken root. Whoever blushes at a rattletrap will boast in a fine carriage.
seneca-049-p02.core_idea: Shame at simplicity reveals hidden vanity

seneca-049-p03.plain: You call a man rich for his gold plate, his lands everywhere and his huge account books. But he is poor, because he is in debt for everything he has, whether he borrowed from a person or from Fortune.
seneca-049-p03.core_idea: Everything we own is borrowed from Fortune

seneca-050-p01.plain: The highest good lives in the soul, and unless the soul is pure and holy, there is no room in it for God.
seneca-050-p01.core_idea: Only a pure soul has room for God

seneca-050-p02.plain: The worst punishment for a crime lies in the crime itself. Don't think punishment waits for the hangman or prison; it comes the moment the crime is committed.
seneca-050-p02.core_idea: Wrongdoing is its own immediate punishment

seneca-050-p03.plain: True goods give confidence and greatness of soul, but riches give shamelessness and arrogance, and arrogance is only a fake show of greatness.
seneca-050-p03.core_idea: Arrogance is a false show of greatness

seneca-051-p01.plain: Why study where Ulysses wandered instead of how to keep ourselves from going astray? We face storms of the spirit daily. Show me instead how to love my country, wife and father, and sail toward them even after shipwreck.
seneca-051-p01.core_idea: Study to live well, not for idle trivia

seneca-051-p02.plain: You teach me how high and low notes make harmony; instead, bring my soul into harmony with itself. You show me the mournful keys; show me rather how to avoid a mournful note in hard times.
seneca-051-p02.core_idea: Seek harmony in the soul, not just in music

seneca-051-p03.plain: What use is dividing land if I can't share it with my brother, or am bitter when a neighbour takes a scrap? The mathematician teaches me to lose none of my boundaries; I want to lose them all lightly.
seneca-051-p03.core_idea: Learn to lose possessions with a light heart

seneca-051-p04.plain: I don't know what will happen, but I know what could, so I await the whole future without misgiving. Knowing anything can happen but not everything will, I am ready for good and prepared for bad.
seneca-051-p04.core_idea: Be ready for good, prepared for bad

seneca-052-p01.plain: Temperance governs our desires, driving some out and bringing others back to a healthy level. It knows the right measure of appetite is not what you want to take, but what you ought to take.
seneca-052-p01.core_idea: Take what you ought, not what you want

seneca-052-p02.plain: Kindness forbids being overbearing or grasping, and is gentle and courteous to everyone in word, deed and feeling. It treats no misfortune as only someone else's, and values its own good because one day it will be another's.
seneca-052-p02.core_idea: Kindness treats no one's trouble as only theirs

seneca-052-p03.plain: We spend huge amounts of time and bore others to earn the praise "What a learned man you are!" Let us be content with a plainer compliment: "What a good man you are!"
seneca-052-p03.core_idea: Better to be called good than learned

seneca-053-p01.plain: Knowing the worth of things, knowing when to act, and restraining impulse are three different skills. Life is in harmony only when action follows impulse, and impulse is as strong as its object is truly worth seeking.
seneca-053-p01.core_idea: Let impulse match the true worth of things

seneca-053-p02.plain: Medicine starts helping when its touch makes the sick body sting. I will say things that help people against their will. Let words other than compliments reach you; if you won't hear the truth alone, hear it together.
seneca-053-p02.core_idea: Helpful truth may sting like medicine

seneca-053-p03.plain: What good are your many bedrooms? You sleep in only one. No place is truly yours where you yourself are not.
seneca-053-p03.core_idea: You can only be in one place at once

seneca-053-p04.plain: Study not to add to what you know, but to make what you know better.
seneca-053-p04.core_idea: Study to improve knowledge, not just add to it

seneca-054-p01.plain: How can you admire both Daedalus, who invented the saw, and Diogenes, who, seeing a boy drink from his hand, smashed his own cup as needless baggage and curled up in his tub? Which one is wise?
seneca-054-p01.core_idea: Wisdom lies in needing less, not inventing more

seneca-054-p02.plain: Nature didn't make humans alone unable to live without contrivances; shelter and food were ready, free and easily got. We made life hard by scorning what is easy and making things precious and admired.
seneca-054-p02.core_idea: Nature gave enough; we made life difficult

seneca-055-p01.plain: The wise person has discovered truth and nature, seeing the divine in it, and taught us to follow the gods and accept chance as their command. He showed that the happiest need no happiness, and the most powerful rule themselves.
seneca-055-p01.core_idea: Most powerful is the one who rules himself

judge.issue: Drops condemning false opinions and remorseful pleasures; compressed.

seneca-055-p02.plain: Greed brought poverty into the world, and by craving much it lost everything.
seneca-055-p02.core_idea: Greed creates poverty by craving too much

seneca-055-p03.plain: Nature does not hand out virtue; becoming good is a skill you have to learn.
seneca-055-p03.core_idea: Goodness is learned, not given by nature

seneca-056-p01.plain: A soul gets virtue only by being trained, taught and perfected through constant practice. We are born to pursue it, not already holding it; even the best people, before instruction, have only the raw material of virtue, not virtue itself.
seneca-056-p01.core_idea: We are born able to gain virtue, not with it

seneca-056-p02.plain: Surprise makes disasters heavier, and everyone hurts more from what catches them off guard. So nothing should be unexpected: send your mind ahead to meet every problem, thinking not of what usually happens but of what can happen.
seneca-056-p02.core_idea: Expect what can happen, not just what usually does

seneca-056-p03.plain: What long years, great toil and the gods' kindness built can be scattered in a day, even an instant. It would comfort us if things perished as slowly as they grow, but growth is slow and ruin is fast.
seneca-056-p03.core_idea: Growth is slow, but ruin is swift

seneca-056-p04.plain: A setback has often made room for better fortune, and many buildings have fallen only to rise higher.
seneca-056-p04.core_idea: Setbacks often make room for something better

seneca-056-p06.plain: Don't judge people's worth by their graves or the monuments of different sizes along the road; their ashes make everyone level. We are unequal at birth but equal in death.
seneca-056-p06.core_idea: Unequal at birth, equal in death

seneca-056-p07.plain: Nature says the hardships you complain of are the same for all; she can make nothing easier, but anyone can make things easier for himself through equanimity. You must suffer pain, hunger, old age, sickness, loss and death.
seneca-056-p07.core_idea: Equanimity eases the hardships everyone must face

seneca-056-p08.plain: How crazy it is to fear a bad reputation among people who themselves have bad reputations.
seneca-056-p08.core_idea: Don't fear the judgement of the disreputable

seneca-057-p02.plain: The happy person is the one nothing can weaken; he stays on the heights relying on no one but himself, because anyone who leans on a prop may fall.
seneca-057-p02.core_idea: Lean on no prop and you cannot fall

seneca-057-p03.plain: The happy life is peace of mind and lasting calm, which come from greatness of soul and firm good judgement. You reach it by seeing the whole truth and acting always with order, measure, fitness and a kindly, reasonable will.
seneca-057-p03.core_idea: The happy life is lasting peace of mind

seneca-057-p04.plain: Nature has wrapped the soul in the body like a cloak. But no one judges clothes by the wardrobe that holds them, and the scabbard doesn't make the sword good or bad.
seneca-057-p04.core_idea: The body is only the soul's cloak

seneca-057-p05.plain: Clouds don't shrink the sun; it keeps its course and shines out undiminished. Likewise, obstacles take nothing from virtue, though it may look dimmer to us. Disasters, losses and wrongs affect virtue only as a cloud affects the sun.
seneca-057-p05.core_idea: Hardships hide virtue like clouds hide the sun

seneca-058-p01.plain: The heart of virtue is needing no day beyond today and not counting the days you have; in the briefest moment, virtue completes an eternity of good.
seneca-058-p01.core_idea: Virtue needs nothing beyond the present moment

seneca-058-p02.plain: The soul knows that true riches are kept somewhere other than piled-up treasure houses: it is the soul, not the strongbox, that should be filled.
seneca-058-p02.core_idea: Fill the soul, not the strongbox

seneca-058-p03.plain: Why does it matter how soon you leave a place you must leave anyway? Aim to live rightly, not long: long life needs only Fate, right living needs the soul. A life is long if it is full, through self-mastery.

seneca-058-p04.plain: Let our lives be like precious jewels, valued not for their size but for their weight. Measure them by what they achieve, not by how long they last.
seneca-058-p04.core_idea: Measure life by its weight, not its length

seneca-058-p05.plain: A short life can be a complete life, as a short person can be a complete person. How long I exist isn't mine to decide, but how I live is. I must stop drifting in darkness and truly live.
seneca-058-p05.core_idea: How long you live isn't yours; how you live is

seneca-059-p01.plain: Death comes to everyone; the killer soon follows the killed. It is a small thing that people worry about so much. And what does it matter how long you avoid what you cannot escape?
seneca-059-p01.core_idea: Death comes to all; delay matters little

seneca-059-p02.plain: Remember that pain has an excellent quality: if it lasts long it can't be severe, and if it is severe it can't last long. We should bravely accept whatever the unchanging laws of the universe demand of us.
seneca-059-p02.core_idea: Severe pain is short; long pain is mild

seneca-060-p01.plain: The soul holds the seed of everything honourable, and advice stirs it to grow, as a gentle breeze fans a spark into flame. A touch, a jolt, is enough to rouse virtue.
seneca-060-p01.core_idea: Good advice fans the seed of virtue within

seneca-060-p02.plain: Nothing improves the mind or steadies a wavering spirit like spending time with good people. Seeing and hearing them gradually sinks into the heart; meeting wise people lifts us, and a great person can help even in silence.
seneca-060-p02.core_idea: Good company slowly shapes the heart

seneca-061-p01.plain: Virtue comes partly from training and partly from practice: first learn, then strengthen what you've learned by acting on it.
seneca-061-p01.core_idea: Learn first, then strengthen learning by action

seneca-061-p02.plain: Every word we hear does some harm, whether curses or good wishes. Enemies' prayers plant false fears, and friends' kind wishes spoil us, sending us after distant, uncertain goods when happiness is in store at home.
seneca-061-p02.core_idea: Happiness is found at home, not in distant goods

seneca-061-p03.plain: Don't envy those the crowd calls great, or let applause or a magistrate in purple disturb your calm; he is no happier than you. For a command that helps you and harms no one, clear away your own faults.
seneca-061-p03.core_idea: Master your own faults rather than envy power

seneca-061-p04.plain: Never believe that anyone can become happy through someone else's unhappiness.
seneca-061-p04.core_idea: No one gains happiness from another's misery

seneca-061-p05.plain: A large part of health is having left behind those who advise madness and having fled far from company that harms everyone in it.
seneca-061-p05.core_idea: Leaving harmful company is part of health

seneca-061-p06.plain: Stop showing off and you'll stop craving. Ambition, luxury and self-indulgence need a stage to perform on; withdraw from the crowd and you cure them all.

seneca-062-p01.plain: Good fortune and good sense sit at opposite poles, which is why we are wiser in hard times. It is prosperity that takes away our goodness.
seneca-062-p01.core_idea: Adversity makes us wiser; prosperity corrupts

seneca-062-p02.plain: We often want one thing and pray for another, not telling the truth even to the gods, who either don't listen or take pity on us.
seneca-062-p02.core_idea: We aren't honest even in our prayers

seneca-063-p01.plain: We honour those who sit by a sick friend's bed, but those hoping for an inheritance are vultures waiting for carrion. The same act can be shameful or honourable; purpose and manner make all the difference.
seneca-063-p01.core_idea: Purpose makes the same act honourable or shameful

seneca-063-p02.plain: As our beliefs are, so will our actions and thoughts be; and as our actions and thoughts are, so will our lives be.
seneca-063-p02.core_idea: Beliefs shape actions, and actions shape lives

seneca-063-p03.plain: Life without ideals wanders aimlessly, and setting up an ideal requires principles. Nothing is more shameful than uncertain, wavering conduct and the habit of timidly backing away.

seneca-063-p04.plain: Do you want to win the gods' favour? Then be a good person. Whoever imitates the gods worships them enough.
seneca-063-p04.core_idea: Be good: imitating the gods is worship

seneca-063-p05.plain: How small a thing it is merely not to harm someone you ought to help! What truly deserves praise is when people treat each other with kindness.
seneca-063-p05.core_idea: Not harming is little; kindness deserves praise

seneca-064-p01.plain: Nature made us kin, from one source for one end, and gave us affection and a bent for friendship. By her law, doing wrong is worse than suffering it. Let our hands be ready to help wherever help is needed.
seneca-064-p01.core_idea: We are kin; doing wrong is worse than suffering it

seneca-064-p02.plain: Keep this in your heart: I am human, and nothing human is foreign to me. Let us share things, since we share birth. We are like the stones of an arch, which would fall without each other's support.
seneca-064-p02.core_idea: We hold each other up like stones in an arch

seneca-064-p03.plain: Let us ignore gossip and value each thing by asking what it actually is, not what it is called.
seneca-064-p03.core_idea: Judge things by what they are, not their name

seneca-064-p04.plain: Only those with a fixed standard of judgement have peace of mind; others drift back and forth, rejecting then seeking the same things, because they judge by rumour. If you want to desire the same things always, desire the truth.
seneca-064-p04.core_idea: To want steadily, want the truth

seneca-064-p05.plain: Of all the evils you complain about, the only real one is your complaining. There is no misery for a person unless he thinks something miserable. The day I find anything unbearable, I won't be able to bear myself.
seneca-064-p05.core_idea: Complaining is the only real evil

seneca-064-p06.plain: I am ill, but that is part of my lot. My slaves are sick, my income is gone, my house is falling apart, and I have faced losses, accidents, work and fear. This is common; in fact, it is unavoidable.
seneca-064-p06.core_idea: Troubles are a common, unavoidable part of life

seneca-064-p07.plain: When things go hard, I have trained myself not just to obey God but to agree with Him, willingly. Everything that makes us groan is part of the tax of life, which you should never hope to escape.
seneca-064-p07.core_idea: Hardships are life's tax; pay it willingly

judge.issue: Drops resolve to meet nothing with ill humour and never seek to escape.

seneca-064-p08.plain: A long life includes all these troubles, just as a long journey includes dust, mud and rain.
seneca-064-p08.core_idea: Long lives bring troubles, like mud on journeys

seneca-065-p01.plain: Life is a battle. Those who brave the sea, steep crags and dangerous campaigns are heroes in the front ranks; those in rotten luxury while others toil are turtle-doves, safe only because people despise them.
seneca-065-p01.core_idea: Life is a battle; idle luxury is contemptible

seneca-065-p02.plain: You are wrong to think luxury, bad manners and other vices each generation blames on its age are special to our time. They are the vices of humanity, not of the era; no age has been free of blame.
seneca-065-p02.core_idea: Vices belong to humanity, not to any age

seneca-065-p03.plain: We slide into wrongdoing easily, with or without guides and companions. The road to vice is downhill and steep, and many become incurable because, unlike mistakes in a craft, the mistakes of life bring pleasure.
seneca-065-p03.core_idea: The road to vice is steep and pleasant

seneca-065-p04.plain: A good conscience wants to come out and be seen, but wickedness is afraid even of shadows.
seneca-065-p04.core_idea: A good conscience seeks light; guilt fears shadows

seneca-065-p05.plain: Good luck saves many from punishment, but no one from fear, because we loathe what Nature condemns. Those who hide their wrongs can never be sure of staying hidden; their conscience convicts them. Guilt always lives in fear.
seneca-065-p05.core_idea: Guilt may escape punishment but never fear

seneca-065-p06.plain: No one who depends on good fortune is happy; joy from outside will leave, but joy springing from yourself is sound and lasts. Outside things can please and serve, but only if they depend on us, not we on them.
seneca-065-p06.core_idea: Joy from within lasts; joy from outside leaves

seneca-065-p07.plain: Fortune's gifts are good only if their owner masters himself, not his possessions him. Fortune gives no good or evil, only raw material; the soul, stronger than any fortune, shapes it into a happy or wretched life.
seneca-065-p07.core_idea: The soul, not Fortune, makes life happy or wretched

seneca-065-p08.plain: A bad person makes everything bad, even what arrived looking best. A good and honest person corrects Fortune's wrongs, softens hardship by knowing how to bear it, enjoys prosperity gratefully and moderately, and faces trouble steadily and bravely.
seneca-065-p08.core_idea: A good person turns hardship to good

seneca-065-p09.plain: Whenever things go against your expectations, say to yourself, as a braver and truer phrase to steady your spirit, that heaven decided on something better.
seneca-065-p09.core_idea: When plans fail, trust that heaven chose better

seneca-065-p10.plain: It is tragic for the soul to dread the future, anxious to keep its pleasures to the end. Such a soul never rests and loses the present. Fearing to lose something is no different from grieving its loss.
seneca-065-p10.core_idea: Fearing loss is as painful as loss itself

seneca-065-p11.plain: Foresee and avoid the harm you can, helped by confidence and a mind resolved to endure anything. Whoever can bear Fortune can guard against it. Nothing is more foolish than fearing trouble before it comes.
seneca-065-p11.core_idea: Prepare for trouble, but don't fear it early

seneca-066-p01.plain: What you are called owner of is in your hands but not truly yours. We must lose our lives as surely as our property, and knowing this is a comfort. Lose things calmly, since you must lose life too.
seneca-066-p01.core_idea: Lose things calmly; even life must be lost

seneca-066-p02.plain: Facing loss, remember what you've lost and don't let its enjoyment vanish with it. Having can be taken away; having had, never. Chance takes the thing but leaves its enjoyment, unless we throw that away by regretting.
seneca-066-p02.core_idea: Having can be taken, but having had cannot

seneca-066-p03.plain: Why lose heart? What could be done can be done, if we purify our souls and follow Nature; straying from it enslaves us to chance. Return to our true state, and we can endure pain and defy Fortune.
seneca-066-p03.core_idea: Follow Nature and Fortune cannot conquer you

seneca-066-p04.plain: If you had lost a friend, the greatest blow of all, you should have tried to rejoice that you had him rather than mourn that you lost him.
seneca-066-p04.core_idea: Rejoice in having had a friend, not only mourn

seneca-066-p05.plain: Do you bury the friendship with the friend? Were those years of closeness for nothing? Much of those we loved stays with us after they are gone. The past is ours, and nothing is more secure than what has been.
seneca-066-p05.core_idea: The past we shared with loved ones stays ours

seneca-066-p06.plain: We are ungrateful for past joys because we hope for the future, which soon becomes past anyway. Enjoying only the present limits us; the future delights by anticipation and the past by memory, but only the past is certain.
seneca-066-p06.core_idea: Past joys are certain; cherish them

seneca-066-p07.plain: See how swiftly time runs, with all humanity rushing to the same point only moments apart. The one you think has passed away has only gone on ahead. Why mourn the one before you when you travel the same road?
seneca-066-p07.core_idea: The dead have only gone ahead on our road

seneca-066-p08.plain: Whoever complains that someone died is complaining that he was human. Everyone shares the same terms: whoever is given birth is bound to die.
seneca-066-p08.core_idea: To be born is to be bound to die

seneca-066-p09.plain: Time separates us, but death makes us equal. Life's span is uncertain and everything shifts at Fortune's command; only death is sure. Yet everyone complains about the one thing in which no one is deceived.
seneca-066-p09.core_idea: Amid all uncertainty, only death is sure

seneca-066-p10.plain: Life itself is neither good nor bad; it is simply the place where good and bad happen.
seneca-066-p10.core_idea: Life is the place where good and evil happen

seneca-066-p11.plain: Some feelings claim their rights: tears fall despite us, and shedding them eases the soul. Let them fall, but don't force them; weep as feeling moves you, not as imitation demands, and add nothing to natural grief.
seneca-066-p11.core_idea: Let tears fall naturally, without adding to grief

seneca-067-p01.plain: Don't hold back or force out your tears because other people are watching; tears are most shameful when they are faked. Let them come naturally.
seneca-067-p01.core_idea: Let tears flow naturally, never feigned for an audience

seneca-067-p02.plain: You can follow nature in grief and still keep your dignity. Grief can have a grace of its own; the wise keep a measure even in tears, while the unwise let sorrow and joy overflow.
seneca-067-p02.core_idea: Grief can be genuine and still dignified

seneca-067-p03.plain: Accept calmly what cannot be avoided. Nothing that happens is truly unheard of or new; right now countless people are arranging funerals and mourning, while you have already finished your mourning.
seneca-067-p03.core_idea: Death is common; accept the inevitable calmly

seneca-067-p04.plain: You may talk often about the one who died and treasure his memory. That memory will come back more often if you greet it without bitterness, since no one wants to keep company with sorrow.
seneca-067-p04.core_idea: Welcome memories of the dead without bitterness

seneca-067-p05.plain: Mourning wildly and then forgetting the dead is how animals love their young, fiercely and then not at all. A sensible person should keep remembering the dead but stop mourning them.
seneca-067-p05.core_idea: Keep remembering the dead, but stop mourning

seneca-067-p06.plain: To someone grieving an early death, say this: compared with eternity, young and old alike live almost no time at all, yet we foolishly treat our tiny lives as if they were vast.
seneca-067-p06.core_idea: Against eternity, every life is equally brief

seneca-068-p01.plain: Every day and hour shows how small and fragile we are, reminding us of the weakness we forget; while we plan as if we will live forever, they make us glance back at death.
seneca-068-p01.core_idea: Daily life reminds us of our fragility and death

seneca-068-p02.plain: It is foolish to map out your whole life when you don't even own tomorrow. Planning to get rich and then retire assumes too much; everything is uncertain, and chance cuts into even the hour you are living.
seneca-068-p02.core_idea: Don't count on the future; tomorrow isn't yours

seneca-068-p03.plain: Fate has set a limit to each life, but no one knows how close theirs is. So live as if you had reached the end: put nothing off, and settle life's accounts every day.
seneca-068-p03.core_idea: Live each day as if it were your last

seneca-068-p04.plain: Life's great flaw is that part of it is always put off. Someone who completes their life each day never lacks time; postponing breeds fear and craving for the future, and worry about what's coming is the most miserable thing.
seneca-068-p04.core_idea: Postponing life breeds anxiety about the future

seneca-068-p05.plain: Begin living right now, and treat each day as a whole life. Whoever lives that way is at ease, while those who live only on hope find the future slipping away, replaced by greed and fear of death.
seneca-068-p05.core_idea: Treat each day as a complete life

seneca-068-p06.plain: We must drop our craving for more life; suffering will come at some point anyway. What matters is not how long you live but how nobly, and living nobly often means not living long.
seneca-068-p06.core_idea: How nobly you live matters, not how long

seneca-069-p01.plain: The human soul is great and noble; it accepts no limits except those it shares with the gods.
seneca-069-p01.core_idea: The soul is great and accepts no small limits

seneca-069-p02.plain: As the womb readies us for life outside it, life readies us for another birth. So await your last hour without fear, the body's end but not the soul's; treat your things like luggage, since you must move on.
seneca-069-p02.core_idea: Life prepares the soul for another birth

seneca-069-p03.plain: The day you dread as the end of everything is really the day your eternal life begins.
seneca-069-p03.core_idea: Death is the birthday of eternity

seneca-069-p04.plain: Why look for disasters that may never come, like fires or collapsing buildings? Accidents are rare; the danger you face every day comes from other people. Guard against that, because no harm is more common or more sly.
seneca-069-p04.core_idea: Everyday danger comes from people, not accidents

seneca-070-p01.plain: In dealing with others, do no harm so that you are not harmed. Share in everyone's joys and sympathize with their troubles, while remembering what to give and what to hold back.
seneca-070-p01.core_idea: Harm no one; share others' joys and troubles

seneca-070-p02.plain: Coming back to life for others' sake shows a great heart. The highest kindness is to guard your health in old age more carefully because someone you love wants you to.
seneca-070-p02.core_idea: Caring for yourself for a loved one's sake

judge.issue: Drops the contrast that old age otherwise permits less care for self-preservation.

seneca-070-p03.plain: Told that a man's travels did him no good, Socrates said he had taken himself along. To escape your troubles you need a new self, not a new place; wherever you go, you bring your own character.
seneca-070-p03.core_idea: You can't escape your troubles by travelling

seneca-070-p04.plain: If you count wealth as a good, you will feel poor whenever a neighbor is richer. If you prize status, others' promotions will torment you, and your ambition will make you feel last if anyone is ahead.
seneca-070-p04.core_idea: Valuing wealth and status breeds endless envy

seneca-070-p05.plain: Once your mind has learned blind panic, you won't feel safe even when you are, and it can't protect itself. It flees danger instead of avoiding it, and we are most exposed when we turn our backs.
seneca-070-p05.core_idea: Panic makes us more vulnerable, not safer

seneca-070-p06.plain: New friends won't be the same, but neither will you; you change every hour, though you notice it less in yourself. Swinging between hope and despair breeds trouble; if you are wise, mix the two.
seneca-070-p06.core_idea: Everyone changes; balance hope with despair

seneca-070-p07.plain: Rushing from place to place won't help, because you carry your emotions and troubles with you, and they press on you from every side. A sick person needs medicine, not a change of scenery.
seneca-070-p07.core_idea: Troubles need a cure, not a change of scenery

seneca-070-p08.plain: The only safe harbor from life's storms is to stop fearing the future, stand firm, and be ready to take whatever fortune throws at you head-on, without hiding or turning away.
seneca-070-p08.core_idea: Stand firm and face fortune head-on

seneca-071-p01.plain: Many things that seem terrifying at night look laughable in daylight.
seneca-071-p01.core_idea: Night fears look ridiculous by day

seneca-071-p02.plain: We don't lack confidence because things are hard; things are hard because we lack confidence.
seneca-071-p02.core_idea: Difficulty comes from lack of confidence

seneca-071-p03.plain: Give up the gold, silver and possessions that weigh down a wealthy home; freedom has a price. If you value freedom highly, you must value everything else little.

seneca-071-p04.plain: Whoever is feared is also afraid; no one has spread terror and still lived with peace of mind.
seneca-071-p04.core_idea: Those who are feared live in fear

seneca-071-p05.plain: Nothing helps more than staying quiet, talking little with others and much with yourself. Conversation coaxes secrets out of us, and no one keeps what they hear to themselves, so a secret soon becomes common talk.
seneca-071-p05.core_idea: Talk little; secrets never stay secret

seneca-071-p06.plain: The surest path to peace of mind is never to do wrong. Wrongdoers live in fear and restlessness; their conscience gives them no ease, and even if they escape notice, they never feel sure they have.
seneca-071-p06.core_idea: A clear conscience is the basis of peace

seneca-071-p07.plain: No one is truly at the mercy of their affairs. People tangle themselves up in them by choice, then tell themselves that being busy proves they are happy.
seneca-071-p07.core_idea: Busyness is chosen, and it isn't happiness

seneca-072-p01.plain: We overdo everything, even reading and study, so we end up learning to perform in the classroom rather than to live.
seneca-072-p01.core_idea: Learn for life, not for show

seneca-072-p02.plain: Life is like a public bath, a crowd or a journey: things get thrown at you or hit you by accident. On this rough road you will slip, fall, tire, lose companions and bury people, and must keep going.
seneca-072-p02.core_idea: Life is a rough journey; keep going

seneca-072-p03.plain: People face dangers bravely when they have prepared for them long in advance, while the unprepared panic over trifles. So make sure nothing catches you off guard; constant reflection lets you meet any trouble like an adult, not a novice.
seneca-072-p03.core_idea: Prepare in advance so nothing catches you off guard

seneca-072-p04.plain: Winter brings cold, summer heat, bad weather illness, and floods or fires bring losses. We cannot change this order of things, but we can build brave hearts that endure chance and live in harmony with nature.
seneca-072-p04.core_idea: We can't change nature, only our courage

seneca-072-p05.plain: Whatever happens, assume it had to happen, and don't rail against nature. Endure what you cannot change and follow without complaint the God who guides all things; only a bad soldier grumbles at his commander.
seneca-072-p05.core_idea: Endure what you cannot change without complaint

seneca-072-p06.plain: A prayer to the Master of the heavens: lead me wherever you wish and I will follow quickly. Even if unwilling, I will go and suffer anyway; fate leads the willing soul and drags the unwilling.
seneca-072-p06.core_idea: Fate leads the willing and drags the unwilling

judge.issue: Drops 'My Father' and suffering in sin what could be done in virtue.

seneca-072-p07.plain: Don't grab at knowledge randomly or all at once; you know the whole by studying its parts. Take on only what you can handle and absorb what you can hold; a sound mind grows as it takes in more.
seneca-072-p07.core_idea: Learn in parts, at a pace you can handle

seneca-072-p08.plain: It is easy to stir someone to want goodness, because nature has planted the seeds of virtue in all of us. When something prompts it, the good spirit wakes as if freed from chains.
seneca-072-p08.core_idea: The seeds of virtue are in everyone

seneca-072-p09.plain: The poor lack many things; the greedy lack everything. A greedy person helps no one and harms himself most.
seneca-072-p09.core_idea: Greed impoverishes and harms the greedy most

seneca-072-p10.plain: Someone who wants little needs little.
seneca-072-p10.core_idea: Want little and you need little

seneca-073-p01.plain: The best days of our unhappy human life go by first; then come sickness, bitter old age and toil, until harsh death takes everything away.

seneca-073-p02.plain: Just as the best wine pours from the top of the jar and the dregs sink to the bottom, the best part of life comes first. Should we let others drink the best and keep the dregs for ourselves?
seneca-073-p02.core_idea: Life's best part comes first; don't waste it

seneca-073-p03.plain: So let us work with courage and single purpose, skipping distractions, so we don't realise too late how fast time flies. Welcome each day as it comes as the best one, and make it truly yours.
seneca-073-p03.core_idea: Welcome each day as the best and use it

judge.issue: Drops 'when we are left behind' and that time's course cannot be stayed.

seneca-073-p04.plain: People prove their words are truly their own by doing what they talk about.
seneca-073-p04.core_idea: Your words are yours when you act on them

seneca-074-p01.plain: Good people help each other, because each gives the other's virtues exercise and keeps wisdom sharp. Everyone needs someone to compare notes and think things through with.
seneca-074-p01.core_idea: Good people sharpen each other's virtues

seneca-074-p02.plain: It is natural to love our friends and rejoice in their success as our own; without this, even virtue fades. Virtue asks us to plan and think carefully, and that is easier with a friend.
seneca-074-p02.core_idea: Friendship strengthens virtue and clear thinking

judge.issue: Compresses virtue's tasks; drops that virtue grows only through exercise.

seneca-074-p03.plain: People see others' affairs more clearly than their own, because self-love blinds them and fear in danger clouds their judgment. Wisdom begins when a person is calm and free of fear.
seneca-074-p03.core_idea: Wisdom begins when fear and self-love fall away

judge.issue: Drops 'they say' framing and 'defect of character'; states as plain fact.

seneca-074-p04.plain: Look at how things really are, not how people describe them, and you'll see that misfortunes help us more than they harm us. Hardship has often started happiness, while welcomed privileges have often led people to a cliff edge.
seneca-074-p04.core_idea: Misfortune often helps more than it harms

judge.issue: 'More likely to help' firmed to 'help more'; precipice image thinned.

seneca-074-p05.plain: If you are wise, measure everything by the human condition and limit both your joys and your fears. Don't rejoice in anything for long, so you won't fear anything for long.
seneca-074-p05.core_idea: Limit joy so you limit fear

seneca-074-p06.plain: There is no reason to think anything is truly fearful; the things that unsettle us are empty. We pass fear to each other without ever examining what we dread, so falsehood survives because no one challenges it.
seneca-074-p06.core_idea: Our fears are empty because we never examine them

judge.issue: Drops 'the good behind it' and that no one has sifted out the truth.

seneca-074-p07.plain: Just as children cower in fear in the dark, grown adults feel afraid even in broad daylight.
seneca-074-p07.core_idea: Adults fear in daylight as children fear the dark

seneca-075-p01.plain: What you truly need is found everywhere; what you don't need always has to be hunted down with great effort.
seneca-075-p01.core_idea: Necessities are easy; luxuries take effort

seneca-075-p02.plain: Turn to true riches: learn to be content with little, and boldly say that with water and porridge you could rival Jupiter in happiness. Better still, need not even those, since happiness shouldn't depend on gold or on porridge.
seneca-075-p02.core_idea: Happiness should depend on nothing external

judge.issue: 'Base' softened to 'shouldn't'; challenge rendered as command.

seneca-075-p03.plain: If you think on these things often, you will try not to look happy but to be happy, and to seem happy to yourself rather than to others.
seneca-075-p03.core_idea: Be happy, not merely seem happy

seneca-075-p04.plain: People love and hate their own vices at the same time.
seneca-075-p04.core_idea: We love and hate our vices at once

seneca-076-p01.plain: Bravery is an unbreakable fortress for our human weakness. Someone protected by it can endure life's siege without anxiety, because they rely on their own strength and their own weapons.
seneca-076-p01.core_idea: Bravery is a fortress for human weakness

seneca-076-p02.plain: Posidonius said you are never safe relying on weapons fortune gave you; fight with your own. Fortune never arms you against herself, so those armed against enemies are defenseless against fortune.
seneca-076-p02.core_idea: Rely on inner strength, not fortune's gifts

seneca-076-p03.plain: Alexander conquered nation after nation, yet he lay in the dark lamenting a friend he killed or lost, beaten by anger and grief. He aimed to control everything except his own emotions.
seneca-076-p03.core_idea: Conquering the world isn't conquering yourself

seneca-076-p04.plain: People are badly mistaken who think they prosper by conquering ever more territory. They know nothing of the kingdom as great as the heavens: command over yourself is the greatest command of all.

seneca-076-p05.plain: Everyone should first be convinced that they must be just without reward, and should even take pleasure in freely upholding justice. Don't look for a reward for doing right; the just act itself pays more.
seneca-076-p05.core_idea: A just act is its own reward

judge.issue: Drops turning thoughts away from personal interest.

seneca-076-p06.plain: Those who want their virtue noticed are after fame, not virtue. You must be willing to be just without praise, often even while disgraced; if you are wise, take delight in a bad name earned by doing right.

seneca-077-p01.plain: We'd want less if we saw how little we can consume and for how short a time. Nothing helps moderation more than remembering that life is short and uncertain; whatever you do, keep death in mind.

seneca-078-p01.plain: Money costs us tears and toil. Greed is miserable both in craving and in getting; owning wealth brings more anguish than gaining it, losses hurt more than they should, and whatever we fail to add feels like loss.
seneca-078-p01.core_idea: Wealth brings more misery than it relieves

judge.issue: Drops 'though Fortune leave our property intact'.

seneca-078-p02.plain: If those who crave wealth or office could talk with people who have them, they'd change their prayers: the successful always chase more and scorn what they've got. No one is content; everyone prefers what they missed.
seneca-078-p02.core_idea: No one is satisfied by what they win

judge.issue: Drops complaints about plans and outcomes; 'even if it comes on the run'.

seneca-078-p03.plain: Every vice has its excuse and starts small and easy to manage, then spreads; once begun, you can't be sure it will stop. Every emotion starts weak and grows, so it's easier to prevent than to give up.
seneca-078-p03.core_idea: Stop vices and passions before they start

seneca-078-p04.plain: Love stirs us whether returned or rejected, and easy love troubles us as much as hard love. Knowing our weakness, let us stay calm and keep our unsteady spirit away from drink, beauty, flattery and other temptations.
seneca-078-p04.core_idea: Know your weakness and avoid temptation

judge.issue: Drops pride as what scorned love kindles.

seneca-078-p05.plain: As far as we can, let us step back from slippery places; even on dry ground it is hard enough to stand firm.
seneca-078-p05.core_idea: Avoid temptation; standing firm is hard enough

seneca-079-p01.plain: Nature has given us enough strength, if only we use it and gather our powers to help us rather than hinder us. The real reason is unwillingness; the excuse is inability.

seneca-080-p03.plain: Life has handed you so many unsolved problems, and you are still splitting hairs? Stop practising with toy weapons; you need real armour. Teach me how to keep sadness and fear from my soul and shed hidden cravings. Do something!
seneca-080-p03.core_idea: Stop theorising and deal with real troubles

judge.issue: 'Fortune' rendered as 'life'.

seneca-080-p04.plain: Nature hasn't given us so much time that we can waste any. Illness, family troubles, business and sleep already take much of it. With so short and swift a life, why spend most of it on useless things?
seneca-080-p04.core_idea: Life is too short to waste on trivia

seneca-080-p05.plain: How much happier is the person who watches the scramble for office, power, wealth and family without caring, asking nothing of anyone and telling Fortune, I want no favours from you. That cuts Fortune down to size.
seneca-080-p05.core_idea: Asking nothing of Fortune makes you free

judge.issue: Drops Cato/Vatinius point that Fortune spurns the good; 'great-souled' lost.

seneca-080-p06.plain: Happiness is lowly, not greedy, so it never gluts desire. What you think lofty seems small to those who reach it, and they climb higher. Ignorant of truth and led by common talk, people chase things as good, then find them bad, empty or lesser. Crowds mistake big for good.
seneca-080-p06.core_idea: What we chase looks great only from afar
seneca-080-p06.plain_v1: What we chase looks grand only because we are far below it; to those who reach it, it is just a rung on the ladder. Misled by the crowd, people win their wish and find it bad, empty or disappointing.

judge_v1.issue: Drops opening claim that happiness is lowly, not greedy; and the urge to climb higher.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the opening claim that happiness is lowly, not greedy.

seneca-081-p01.plain: Would you rather have much, or enough? Whoever has much wants more, proof they don't have enough yet; whoever has enough has what the rich never get: a place to stop.
seneca-081-p01.core_idea: Enough gives what wealth never does: a stopping-point

seneca-081-p02.plain: Money has never made anyone rich; it only makes people crave more of it, because having more lets them reach for still more.
seneca-081-p02.core_idea: Money only breeds a craving for more

seneca-081-p03.plain: The Builder of the universe, who set the laws of life, meant us to live well but not in luxury. All we need for well-being lies close at hand; luxury can only be gathered with misery and anxiety.
seneca-081-p03.core_idea: Needs are easy; luxury brings misery

seneca-082-p01.plain: Nothing satisfies us, though we are already dying, nearer the edge every hour. It is a mistake to fear only the last day, since every day counts toward death; the last hour arrives, but every hour approaches it.
seneca-082-p01.core_idea: We are dying every day, not just the last

judge.issue: Drops 'death wears us away, does not whirl us away' and blindness of mind.

seneca-082-p02.plain: Being one consistent person is a great role, but only the wise manage it; the rest of us keep changing masks, thrifty one day, wasteful the next. Keep the character you began with, so people at least recognise you.
seneca-082-p02.core_idea: Be one consistent person throughout life

judge.issue: Drops 'see that men can praise you'; keeps only recognition.

seneca-083-p01.plain: Infancy, boyhood, youth and old age are different stages, but I, who have lived through each, am still the same person.
seneca-083-p01.core_idea: Through every stage of life, I remain myself

seneca-083-p02.plain: We work harder and are better people when we rise early and greet the dawn; it is shameful to lie dozing when the sun is high, or wake only at noon, which still feels like dawn to many.
seneca-083-p02.core_idea: Rising early makes us better and more diligent

seneca-084-p01.plain: Arriving tired at my villa late at night to find nothing ready, I use the delay to reflect: nothing is heavy if you accept it lightly, and nothing need anger you unless you add to your troubles by getting angry.
seneca-084-p01.core_idea: Accept things lightly and they weigh little

seneca-084-p02.plain: Get used to plain food, since circumstances catch out even the rich. No one can have whatever they wish, but anyone can stop wishing for what they lack and cheerfully use what comes. An uncomplaining stomach brings independence.
seneca-084-p02.core_idea: Freedom lies in not wanting what you lack

seneca-084-p03.plain: We don't notice how much is unnecessary until it's gone; we used things because we had them and bought them because others did. We follow convention instead of reason, as if being common made something right.
seneca-084-p03.core_idea: Live by reason, not by what others do

judge.issue: Wrong views becoming the standard of right only loosely kept.

seneca-084-p04.plain: Like a catchy tune after a concert, flatterers' praise of wrong things sticks in our minds and keeps returning. So shut your ears to bad talk from the start, before the words settle in and grow bolder.
seneca-084-p04.core_idea: Shut out bad talk before it takes root

seneca-085-p01.plain: No one is good by accident; virtue must be learned. Pleasure is petty and shared with animals, and glory is empty. Poverty harms only those who fight it, and death is no evil but something all people share equally.
seneca-085-p01.core_idea: Virtue must be learned; death is shared by all

seneca-085-p02.plain: Why work so hard on strength, beauty, hair or speed, when cattle are stronger, lions have finer manes and hares are faster? Stop competing where you must lose and return to the good that really is yours.
seneca-085-p02.core_idea: Seek the good that is truly your own

seneca-085-p03.plain: Count yourself happy only when your joys come from reason and nothing people grasp or pray for makes you desire it. You come into your own when you see that the world's fortunate are the most unfortunate of all.
seneca-085-p03.core_idea: The world's fortunate are truly the least fortunate

judge.issue: Drops 'I do not say prefer' distinction between desire and preference.

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-001-p01.plain: We too have a religion, given to our ancestors and handed down to us. It teaches us to be thankful, to stay united and to love one another, and we never quarrel about religion.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-001-p01.core_idea: Our religion teaches thanks, unity and love

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-001-p02.plain: My ancestors worshipped the Great Mystery in silence and alone, without seeking anything for themselves. Silent, because words are always weak; alone, because God is nearer in solitude, and no priest stood between a person and the Maker.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-001-p02.core_idea: Worship of the Great Mystery is silent and solitary

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-001-p03.plain: People who live outdoors know that solitude builds a kind of inner force that crowds quickly drain. Even their enemies admit the American Indian has an unmatched inner power and composure, independent of circumstances.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-001-p03.core_idea: Solitude builds inner strength that crowds drain

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-001-p04.plain: Even if you admire natural law, science hasn't explained everything. The origin of life is the supreme mystery at the heart of worship, and before it we, like the naturalist, can only see the Divine in creation with awe.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-001-p04.core_idea: Life's origin remains a mystery that calls for awe

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-002-p01.plain: Among our people, old age was in some ways the happiest time of life. It brought freedom from hard and dangerous work and from the rules of custom and manners everyone else had to follow.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-002-p01.core_idea: Old age brings freedom and happiness

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-002-p02.plain: For the Indian, the one unavoidable duty was prayer, the daily recognition of the Unseen and Eternal, needed more than food. At dawn he bathes and faces the rising sun in silent prayer; each soul meets the Great Silence alone.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-002-p02.core_idea: Daily silent prayer at dawn, alone

judge.issue: Drops that each soul worships apart, the mate never accompanying.

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-002-p03.plain: Whenever a hunter comes upon a beautiful or awe-inspiring sight, like a rainbow over a mountain or a red prairie sunset, he pauses to worship. He needs no weekly holy day, because to him every day is God's.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-002-p03.core_idea: Every day is holy; worship where beauty appears

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-003-p01.plain: Friendship is the hardest test of character. Loyalty to family is easy, and love between man and woman is mixed with desire and self-interest. To have a friend and stay true through every trial is the mark of a man.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-003-p01.core_idea: True friendship is the hardest test of character

judge.issue: 'Is held to be' and 'we think' dropped; cultural belief stated as fact.

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-004-p01.plain: Long before I heard of Christ or met a white man, an unschooled woman, with Nature's help, taught me the heart of morality. I knew God, understood goodness and loved true beauty; civilization has taught me nothing better.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-004-p01.core_idea: Nature taught me goodness; civilization added nothing better

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-004-p02.plain: As a child I knew how to give, but I lost that grace once civilized. Then any pretty pebble was precious and every tree sacred; now I worship with the white man before a painted landscape priced in dollars.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-004-p02.core_idea: Civilization traded natural reverence for price tags

judge.issue: Drops the natural versus artificial life contrast.

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-004-p03.plain: The first Americans joined pride with humility and saw speech as a dangerous gift, not proof of superiority. They held silence to be perfect balance of body, mind and spirit; the ideal was a self unshaken by life's storms.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-004-p03.core_idea: Silence is perfect balance of body, mind, spirit

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-004-p04.plain: The old chief Wabashaw said: hold your tongue when young, and in old age you may develop a thought that will help your people.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-004-p04.core_idea: Silence in youth ripens wisdom for age

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-005-p01.plain: We believed love of possessions is a weakness to overcome, because it upsets the spirit's balance. So children learned generosity early, giving away what they valued most and handing out the family's gifts, and heard stories shaming the stingy.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-005-p01.core_idea: Love of possessions upsets the spirit; teach generosity

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-005-p02.plain: The true Indian puts no price on his property or work; only his strength limits his generosity. He counts a hard or dangerous task an honour and would be ashamed to ask a reward, leaving thanks to the one served.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-005-p02.core_idea: Give generously and ask no reward

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-005-p03.plain: A truly brave person gives in to neither fear nor anger, desire nor pain, and is always master of themselves; such courage rises to chivalry, patriotism and real heroism.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-005-p03.core_idea: True bravery is mastery of yourself

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-005-p04.plain: An old chief told a scout setting out in midwinter to hunt for a starving people: let no cold, hunger, pain, danger, nor even death, or the fear of them, stop you from doing a good deed.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-005-p04.core_idea: Let nothing stop you from doing good

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-006-p01.plain: The Indian's attitude to death, the test and backdrop of life, fits his whole outlook: it holds no terror for him. He meets it simply and calmly, seeking only an honourable end as a last gift to his family.

soul-of-the-indian-eastman-007-p01.plain: The Indian never doubted the soul is immortal but didn't speculate about the afterlife. He believed the spirit the Great Mystery breathed into us returns to Him, pervades nature, and may linger near the grave, hearing prayers.
soul-of-the-indian-eastman-007-p01.core_idea: The spirit returns to the Great Mystery and pervades nature

judge.issue: Drops that 'happy hunting-ground' is borrowed and the custom of not naming the dead.

an-001-p01.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that nothing prevents ill will or removes it like the heart's release through love. When you focus your mind wisely on loving-kindness, ill will doesn't arise, or if it has, it fades.
an-001-p01.core_idea: Loving-kindness prevents and dissolves ill will

an-001-p02.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that nothing prevents restlessness and remorse or removes them like a settled mind. When the mind is settled, they don't arise, or if they have, they go.
an-001-p02.core_idea: A settled mind dissolves restlessness and remorse

an-001-p03.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that nothing brings as much happiness as a developed and cultivated mind. A trained mind brings happiness.

an-001-p04.plain: Just as you can't see the bottom of a muddy lake, a mendicant whose mind is clouded can't know what is good for themselves or others, or reach the noble ones' higher knowledge, because their mind is clouded.
an-001-p04.core_idea: A clouded mind cannot see what is good

an-001-p05.plain: The Buddha says he sees nothing that changes as quickly as the mind, so quickly that it's hard even to find a comparison for it.
an-001-p05.core_idea: Nothing changes faster than the mind

an-001-p06.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that the mind is radiant by nature, but it gets stained by defilements that come and visit it.
an-001-p06.core_idea: The mind is radiant but stained by visiting defilements

judge.issue: Adds 'by nature', an interpretive claim the passage leaves unstated.

an-002-p01.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that nothing grows good qualities and weakens bad ones like contentment. When you are content, the skillful grows and the unskillful fades.

an-002-p02.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that nothing grows good qualities and weakens bad ones like having good friends. With good friends, the skillful grows and the unskillful fades.

an-002-p03.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that losing wealth is a small thing; losing wisdom is the worst loss.
an-002-p03.core_idea: Losing wisdom is worse than losing wealth

an-002-p04.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that losing fame is a small thing; losing wisdom is the worst loss.
an-002-p04.core_idea: Losing wisdom is worse than losing fame

an-004-p01.plain: The Buddha says that when someone has right view, all their deeds, intentions and choices lead to good, pleasant results, just as a good seed of sugarcane or grape makes everything it absorbs taste sweet.
an-004-p01.core_idea: Right view makes every action bear good fruit

an-006-p01.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that developing one thing calms body and mind, settles thinking, and fully develops every quality needed for realization: mindfulness of the body.
an-006-p01.core_idea: Mindfulness of the body calms and awakens

an-006-p02.plain: The Buddha says two things cause remorse: having done bad things and having failed to do good things, in body, speech and mind. Thinking of either, a person feels mortified.
an-006-p02.core_idea: Bad done and good undone both cause remorse

an-006-p03.plain: The Buddha says he learned two things: never be satisfied with good qualities, and never stop trying. Even if only skin and bones remained, he kept striving to reach what human effort can achieve; it was by diligence he awakened.

an-007-p01.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants to give up what is unskillful. It is possible, or he wouldn't say so; and since doing it leads to welfare and happiness rather than harm, he urges it.
an-007-p01.core_idea: Giving up the unskillful is possible and brings happiness

an-007-p02.plain: Two kinds of people are wise: one who recognizes their own mistake, and one who properly accepts another person's confession of a mistake.
an-007-p02.core_idea: Wise people admit mistakes and accept apologies

an-007-p03.plain: Two things lead to realization: serenity and discernment. Serenity develops the mind, which lets go of greed; discernment develops wisdom, which lets go of ignorance. A mind stained by greed isn't free, and wisdom clouded by ignorance can't grow.
an-007-p03.core_idea: Serenity frees from greed; discernment frees from ignorance

an-008-p01.plain: The Buddha says you could never repay your parents, even by carrying them for a hundred years or making them rulers of the earth, for they raised you. But helping them grow in faith, ethics, generosity or wisdom repays them.
an-008-p01.core_idea: Parents can be repaid only by helping them grow spiritually

extension.text: Mendicants, I say that these two individuals cannot easily be repaid. What two? Mother and father. You would not have done enough to repay your mother and father even if you were to carry your mother around on one shoulder and your father on the other, and if you lived like this for a hundred years, and if you were to anoint, massage, bathe, and rub them; and even if they were to defecate and urinate right there. Even if you were to establish your mother and father as supreme monarchs of this great earth, abounding in the seven treasures, you would still not have done enough to repay them. Why is that? Parents are very helpful to their children: they raise them, nurture them, and show them the world. But you have done enough, more than enough, to repay them if you encourage, settle, and ground unfaithful parents in faith, unethical parents in ethical conduct, stingy parents in generosity, or ignorant parents in wisdom.

judge.issue: Drops that this applies to parents lacking faith, ethics, generosity or wisdom.

an-008-p02.plain: An untrue person is ungrateful and thankless, for that is all the wicked know how to be. A true person is grateful and thankful, for that is the nature of the good.

an-008-p03.plain: An elder of eighty, ninety or a hundred who still burns for sensual pleasures counts as a child, not a senior. A young person in their prime who doesn't live for sensual pleasures counts as wise, a true senior.
an-008-p03.core_idea: Maturity is freedom from craving, not age

an-008-p04.plain: Train yourselves to have peaceful senses and a peaceful mind. Then what you do, say and think will be peaceful, and you can offer the gift of peace to your spiritual companions.
an-008-p04.core_idea: A peaceful mind lets you give peace to others

an-010-p01.plain: Good people live together this way: a senior mendicant thinks anyone, of any rank, should correct him and he should correct them. If corrected, he'd see it as kindness, say thank you, and fix what he did wrong.
an-010-p01.core_idea: Welcome correction from anyone with thanks

an-010-p02.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants there are two kinds of fools: one who carries the burden of what hasn't happened, and one who doesn't take up the burden of what has.
an-010-p02.core_idea: Fools carry imagined burdens and drop real ones

an-010-p03.plain: Defilements grow in two kinds of people: one who feels remorse over what they shouldn't, and one who feels no remorse over what they should.

an-010-p04.plain: Two hopes are hard to let go of: the hope for wealth and the hope for a long life.
an-010-p04.core_idea: Hopes for wealth and long life are hard to drop

an-010-p05.plain: Two kinds of people are rare in the world: one who takes the initiative to help, and one who is grateful and thankful.

an-011-p01.plain: There are two things: cleansing your own mind, and not clinging to anything in the world.
an-011-p01.core_idea: Cleanse your mind and cling to nothing

an-011-p02.plain: A wise, capable good person keeps themselves healthy and whole, beyond reproach and full of merit, by two qualities: after careful examination, they criticize what deserves criticism and praise what deserves praise.
an-011-p02.core_idea: Praise and criticize only after careful examination

an-012-p01.plain: Fools and wise people alike are known by what they do, for wisdom shows itself in the traces it leaves.
an-012-p01.core_idea: People are known by their deeds

an-012-p02.plain: A wise person is known by three things: they recognize their own mistake, they deal with it properly, and they properly accept it when someone else confesses a mistake to them.
an-012-p02.core_idea: Wisdom shows in how we handle mistakes

an-013-p01.plain: A mendicant eats in moderation by reflecting that food is not for fun, indulgence or looks, but only to sustain the body, avoid harm and support spiritual practice, ending old discomfort without creating new, and living blamelessly and at ease.
an-013-p01.core_idea: Eat to sustain the body, not for indulgence

an-013-p02.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that bad conduct in body, speech and mind leads to hurting yourself, hurting others, and hurting both.
an-013-p02.core_idea: Bad conduct hurts you and others

an-014-p01.plain: A shopkeeper can gain more wealth or grow what they have by focusing carefully on their work in the morning, at midday and in the afternoon.
an-014-p01.core_idea: Steady attention to work builds wealth

an-014-p02.plain: There are three kinds of people: minds like an open sore, like lightning, and like diamond. The open-sore mind is irritable; even mild criticism makes them angry and bitter, like a festering sore that oozes more when struck.
an-014-p02.core_idea: An irritable mind flares like a struck sore

an-015-p01.plain: Spend time with people similar to you in ethics, meditation and wisdom. Because you share these, you can talk about them, the conversation flows, and you're both at ease.
an-015-p01.core_idea: Keep company with those who share your values

an-015-p02.plain: A person with speech like honey has given up harsh words; they speak gently, pleasantly and politely, in a way that reaches the heart and pleases people.
an-015-p02.core_idea: Gentle speech that reaches the heart

an-016-p01.plain: The Buddha says a family whose children honor their parents lives with divinity, with its first teachers, and with those worthy of offerings to the gods. These are all names for parents, who raise children and show them the world.
an-016-p01.core_idea: Parents are divinity and first teachers

an-017-p01.plain: Amid wealth and comfort, the Buddha reflected that ordinary people recoil at the old, forgetting they will age too. Since he would also grow old, recoiling made no sense, and he gave up the vanity of youth.
an-017-p01.core_idea: We too will age, so drop the vanity of youth

an-017-p02.plain: Sickness, old age and death are natural for everyone, yet ordinary people are disgusted by them in others. It would not be right for me to feel disgust, since my life is just the same.
an-017-p02.core_idea: Sickness, age and death are shared by all

an-018-p01.plain: There is no hiding place in the world for someone who does wrong. You yourself will know whether you lied or told the truth.
an-018-p01.core_idea: You can't hide wrongdoing from yourself

an-018-p02.plain: Life is very short and moves steadily on; for someone carried into old age there is no shelter. Seeing the danger in death, do good deeds that bring you joy.
an-018-p02.core_idea: Life is short; do good while you can

an-018-p04.plain: A person overcome by hate intends harm to themselves, others, or both, and suffers mental pain and sadness. Once hate is given up, they no longer intend harm and no longer suffer that pain.
an-018-p04.core_idea: Hate harms everyone; giving it up ends the pain

an-019-p01.plain: A deluded person doesn't truly know what is good for themselves, for others, or for both. Once delusion is given up, they truly understand it.
an-019-p01.core_idea: Without delusion, we see what is truly good

an-021-p01.plain: The noble truth of suffering: rebirth, old age, death, sorrow, pain and distress are suffering; so are meeting the disliked, losing the loved, and not getting what you want. In short, the five grasping aggregates are suffering.
an-021-p01.core_idea: The noble truth: life as grasped is suffering

an-021-p02.plain: Old age, sickness and death are three perils that tear mothers and children apart. Neither can take the other's place: a mother cannot age, sicken or die instead of her child, nor a child instead of their mother.
an-021-p02.core_idea: No one can age, sicken or die for another

judge.issue: The wish of each to suffer in the other's place is flattened.

an-022-p01.plain: The Buddha says he meditates by spreading a heart full of love in every direction, above, below and all around, to the whole world, abundant, boundless and free of hostility and ill will.
an-022-p01.core_idea: Spread boundless love to the whole world

an-022-p02.plain: The Buddha tells the Kālāmas not to accept things because of tradition, scripture, logic, a speaker's skill, or respect for a teacher. When you know for yourselves that something is unskillful and leads to harm and suffering, give it up.
an-022-p02.core_idea: Test teachings by your own experience

judge.issue: Compresses the list; drops 'criticized by sensible people'.

an-023-p01.plain: A noble disciple whose mind is free of ill will gains four comforts now: if there is an afterlife, a good rebirth; if not, a happy life; if wrongdoers suffer, no harm to them; if not, they know themselves pure.
an-023-p01.core_idea: A pure heart is safe whatever the truth

an-024-p01.plain: People who argue with hostility and arrogance hunt for each other's flaws and gloat when an opponent slips up and is beaten, but the noble ones don't discuss things like this.
an-024-p01.core_idea: The noble don't argue to win

an-024-p02.plain: Greed is mildly blameworthy but slow to fade. Hate is very blameworthy but quick to fade. Delusion is very blameworthy and slow to fade.
an-024-p02.core_idea: Greed, hate and delusion differ in harm and persistence

an-025-p01.plain: Perfected ones give up lying for life; they speak the truth, are honest and reliable, and don't deceive the world with words. For this day and night, I too will give up lying and be honest and dependable.
an-025-p01.core_idea: Give up lying and speak the truth

an-026-p01.plain: Greed destroys sight, vision and understanding. It blocks wisdom, sides with distress, and doesn't lead to extinguishment.

an-027-p01.plain: If someone follows rules, a lifestyle and a spiritual path as the core of life, it bears fruit only if bad qualities decline and good ones grow; if the reverse happens, it bears no fruit.
an-027-p01.core_idea: A practice is fruitful only if it makes you better

an-028-p01.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that if you practice partly, you succeed partly; if you practice fully, you succeed fully. Either way, the training rules are not fruitless.

an-028-p02.plain: The Buddha tells Kassapa he did make a mistake, but since he has recognized it and dealt with it properly, the Buddha accepts it. Growth in the training means recognizing a mistake, handling it properly and restraining yourself in future.
an-028-p02.core_idea: Owning and correcting a mistake is growth

an-028-p03.plain: A farmer must plough, plant and water the field promptly, but has no power to make the crops sprout, flower and ripen on command; that happens in its own time as the seasons turn.
an-028-p03.core_idea: Do your work, then let results come in time

an-029-p01.plain: A divided community is one where mendicants quarrel and wound each other with cutting words; a harmonious one is where they live in agreement, valuing each other, blending like milk and water, and looking at each other kindly.
an-029-p01.core_idea: Harmony means mutual kindness; division means wounding words

an-030-p01.plain: A mendicant training the mind should balance three things: stillness, effort and calm detachment. Too much stillness brings laziness, too much effort brings restlessness, and detachment alone keeps the mind from settling deeply.
an-030-p01.core_idea: Balance stillness, effort and equanimity in meditation

judge.issue: Drops 'from time to time' and that immersion is for ending defilements.

an-030-p02.plain: Before awakening, the Buddha asked what attracts us to the world, what is wrong with it, and how to escape. Its pleasure attracts, its impermanence and suffering are the drawback, and letting go of desire is the escape.
an-030-p02.core_idea: The world pleases, disappoints, and is escaped by letting go

an-031-p01.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that three indulgences never satisfy: sleep, alcohol and sex.
an-031-p01.core_idea: Sleep, drink and sex never truly satisfy

an-031-p02.plain: When the mind is guarded, your actions in body, speech and thought are guarded too, and they do not rot; a person whose actions have not gone rotten will die well.
an-031-p02.core_idea: A guarded mind keeps actions sound and death good

an-031-p03.plain: Actions born of greed, hate and delusion are harmful, bring suffering and lead to more such actions. Actions born of contentment, love and understanding are good, bring happiness and lead to an end of action.
an-031-p03.core_idea: Greed breeds harmful deeds; love and understanding breed good ones

an-031-p04.plain: Three kinds of people rarely appear in the world: a fully awakened Buddha, someone who teaches what the Buddha taught, and a person who is truly grateful.
an-031-p04.core_idea: Buddhas, true teachers and grateful people are rare

an-032-p01.plain: Desire is bitterness, ill will is rot, and bad thoughts are the flies. If you are bitter and rotting inside, those flies will surely swarm and plague you.
an-032-p01.core_idea: Desire and ill will draw bad thoughts like flies

an-033-p01.plain: Some people are like a line carved in stone: they get angry often and their anger lasts a long time, the way such a line resists wind and water.
an-033-p01.core_idea: Some people's anger lasts like a line in stone

an-033-p02.plain: Some people are like a line drawn in water: even when someone speaks to them roughly and harshly, they stay in touch, keep dealing with them and greet them, and the offence vanishes at once.
an-033-p02.core_idea: Some let harsh words vanish like a line in water

an-033-p03.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants to keep company with a friend who gives what is hard to give, does what is hard to do, and bears what is hard to bear.
an-033-p03.core_idea: A true friend gives, does and endures the hard things

an-034-p01.plain: Beings who do good in body, speech and mind in the morning have a good morning; at midday, a good midday; in the evening, a good evening.
an-034-p01.core_idea: Doing good at any hour makes that hour good

an-035-p02.plain: If you learn little and lack ethics, you're criticised for both; learn little but are ethical, you're praised for ethics; learn much but lack ethics, you're criticised for ethics, as your learning failed; learn much and are ethical, you're praised for both.
an-035-p02.core_idea: Learning and ethics together earn full praise
an-035-p02.plain_v1: People will blame you if you lack learning and ethics, and praise you for whichever you have. If you both learn much and live ethically, they will praise you for both.

judge_v1.issue: 'Praise you for whichever you have' is wrong: learning without ethics earns criticism, not praise.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Loses the point that learning succeeds only through ethics; overgeneralises the praise.

an-035-p03.plain: Craving goes with a person from life to life, and they never escape the round of rebirth. Seeing that craving causes suffering, a mendicant lets go of it and of grasping, and lives mindfully.
an-035-p03.core_idea: Craving causes suffering and binds us to rebirth

an-036-p01.plain: Whatever your posture, if you dwell on worldly thoughts, you have gone astray and cannot reach the highest awakening. A mendicant who has calmed their thoughts and loves peace of mind can reach it.
an-036-p01.core_idea: Calm thoughts open the way to awakening

an-036-p02.plain: There are four ways decisions get biased: by favouritism, hostility, foolishness and fear. If you act against what is right for these reasons, your good name fades like the waning moon.
an-036-p02.core_idea: Biased decisions make your reputation wane

an-037-p01.plain: Even at eighty or a hundred, if your speech is untimely, false and pointless, you are a childish elder. Even if you are young, if your speech is timely, true and useful, you are a wise elder.
an-037-p01.core_idea: Wise speech, not age, makes someone a true elder

an-037-p02.plain: If you are content with simple things that are blameless, cheap and easy to get, you will not fret about shelter, clothes, food or drink, and nothing will hold you back anywhere.
an-037-p02.core_idea: Contentment with little frees you everywhere

an-037-p03.plain: Discontent cannot overpower the attentive; attentive people are exactly those who overcome discontent.

an-037-p04.plain: You should live content, with a kind heart, mindful, your mind focused and calm within.
an-037-p04.core_idea: Live content, kind, mindful and calm

an-038-p01.plain: Someone who has goodwill, stays mindful, is calm within, and trains to let go of desire is called diligent.
an-038-p01.core_idea: Goodwill, mindfulness and letting go make one diligent

an-038-p02.plain: There are four ways of drawing people together: giving, kind words, caring for others, and treating people as equals. These hold the world together like the linchpin of a moving chariot.
an-038-p02.core_idea: Giving, kindness, care and equality hold society together

judge.issue: Drops 'as they deserve in each case' qualifying equal treatment.

an-039-p03.plain: One way of deepening meditation is to know feelings, perceptions and thoughts as they arise, as they stay, and as they pass away; this leads to mindfulness and clear awareness.
an-039-p03.core_idea: Watch feelings and thoughts arise, stay and pass

an-040-p01.plain: The Buddha says you cannot reach the end of the world by travelling, yet there is no end of suffering without reaching it, because the world, its origin and its ending are found within this body and mind.
an-040-p01.core_idea: The end of suffering lies within, not far away

an-040-p02.plain: The sky is far from the earth and sunrise far from sunset, but farther still is the way of good people from the wicked. The company of the good stays steady; the company of the wicked is fickle.
an-040-p02.core_idea: The good and the wicked are worlds apart

an-040-p03.plain: When wife and husband are both faithful, generous, disciplined and living rightly, they speak kindly to each other, live at ease with their needs met, and their enemies lose heart.
an-040-p03.core_idea: A couple equal in goodness lives in ease and kindness

an-041-p01.plain: An old couple each tell the Buddha they have never betrayed each other even in thought and want to be together in the next life too. He says they should be equal in faith, ethics, generosity and wisdom.
an-041-p01.core_idea: Lasting couples match in faith, ethics, generosity and wisdom

an-041-p02.plain: When covetous greed, ill will, dullness, restlessness or doubt rules your heart, you do what you shouldn't and leave undone what you should, and your reputation and happiness crumble.
an-041-p02.core_idea: A heart ruled by hindrances wrecks happiness

an-041-p03.plain: One kind of happiness is being free of debt: a man who owes nothing, large or small, to anyone feels pleasure and happiness when he thinks of it.
an-041-p03.core_idea: Owing nothing brings its own happiness

an-041-p04.plain: Someone who knows the happiness of owing nothing, owning things and using wealth, and then looks wisely, sees that all of it is not worth a sixteenth of the happiness of blameless living.
an-041-p04.core_idea: Blamelessness far outweighs the happiness of wealth

an-041-p05.plain: Your parents are called Divinity, first teachers and elder gods, worthy of offerings. That is because parents do so much for their children: they raise them, nurture them and show them the world.
an-041-p05.core_idea: Parents deserve reverence for raising and guiding us

an-041-p06.plain: Those who judge by looks or are swayed by a voice are full of desire and do not understand. The fool, seeing neither what is inside nor outside, is carried away by a voice.
an-041-p06.core_idea: Judging by looks and voices is foolish

an-042-p01.plain: A wish for all living beings, every one of them: may they see only good things, and may no harm come to anyone.
an-042-p01.core_idea: May all beings see only good and meet no harm

an-042-p03.plain: When cattle cross a river, they all follow the bull, straight or astray. People are the same: when the leader behaves badly the whole country sleeps badly, and when the king is just the whole country sleeps at ease.
an-042-p03.core_idea: As the leader goes, so go the people

an-042-p04.plain: A new bride at first shows careful respect to her in-laws, husband and servants, but with familiarity she ends up telling them to go away. Mendicants slip the same way, so they should keep the heart of a new bride.

extension.text: It’s like a bride on the day or night she’s first brought to her husband’s home. Right away she sets up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for her mother and father in law, her husband, and even the bondservants, workers, and staff. But after some time, because of living together and familiarity, she’ll even say to her mother and father in law, or to her husband: ‘Go away! What would you know?’ In the same way, on the day or night a mendicant first goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, right away they set up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, and even the monastery workers and novices. But after some time, because of living together and familiarity, they’ll even say to their tutor or mentor: ‘Go away! What would you know?’ So you should train like this: ‘We will live with hearts like that of a newly wedded bride.’

an-044-p01.plain: The Buddha tells Potaliya that the finest person criticizes those who deserve criticism and praises those who deserve praise, truthfully and at the right time, because knowing the right time and context is best.
an-044-p01.core_idea: Praise and criticize truthfully, at the right time
