an-044-p02.plain: A person who talks but does not act is like a cloud that thunders but brings no rain.
an-044-p02.core_idea: Talk without action is thunder without rain

an-046-p01.plain: A mendicant endures cold, heat, hunger, thirst, insects, weather, rude criticism, and even severe, life-threatening pain.
an-046-p01.core_idea: Endure hardship, insult and pain patiently

an-046-p02.plain: The Buddha names four kinds of things: unpleasant and harmful, unpleasant but beneficial, pleasant but harmful, and pleasant and beneficial.
an-046-p02.core_idea: Pleasantness and benefit are separate questions

an-046-p03.plain: A mendicant whose mind is no longer swayed by greed, hate, delusion or intoxication, having got rid of them, does not shake or grow nervous, and is not won over by other teachers' doctrines.
an-046-p03.core_idea: A mind free of greed and hate stays unshaken

an-046-p04.plain: Fear of guilt is when you think, 'If I did wrong in body, speech or mind, wouldn't I blame myself?' Afraid of that, you give up bad conduct, develop good conduct and keep yourself pure.
an-046-p04.core_idea: Fear of self-blame keeps conduct pure

an-048-p01.plain: A person can be in retreat in mind but not in body: they don't go off to the forest or wilderness, yet their thoughts are of letting go, goodwill and harmlessness.
an-048-p01.core_idea: Retreat can happen in the mind, not just the place

an-048-p02.plain: The Buddha names four kinds of brightness: the moon, the sun, fire and wisdom. The best of them is the brightness of wisdom.

an-048-p03.plain: The Buddha names four kinds of good speech: speech that is true, brings people together, is gentle, and is thoughtful.
an-048-p03.core_idea: Good speech is true, harmonious, gentle and thoughtful

an-048-p04.plain: There are two kinds of illness, mental and physical. Some beings stay free of physical illness for years, even a century, but almost no one is free of mental illness for an hour, except those who have ended the defilements.
an-048-p04.core_idea: Almost no one is free of mental affliction

an-049-p01.plain: The Buddha tells a nun her act was a foolish mistake, but since she has seen it and made amends, he accepts it. Recognising a mistake, dealing with it and resolving to restrain yourself is growth.
an-049-p01.core_idea: Owning and correcting a mistake is growth

an-050-p01.plain: The impatient way is to abuse, annoy or argue back when someone does that to you. The patient way is not to hit back when someone abuses, annoys or argues with you.

an-052-p01.plain: No one in the world, human or divine, can guarantee four things: that what ages won't age, what sickens won't sicken, what dies won't die, or that past bad deeds won't bear their painful fruit.
an-052-p01.core_idea: No one can stop aging, sickness, death or karma

an-052-p02.plain: The Buddha tells a brahmin not to speak of everything he has seen, heard, thought or known, nor of nothing. Speak of things that make good qualities grow and bad ones fade; don't speak of things that do the opposite.
an-052-p02.core_idea: Speak only of what makes goodness grow

an-052-p03.plain: People who fear death are those still craving sensual pleasures. When they fall gravely ill, they think the pleasures they love will leave them, and they grieve, wail and fall into confusion.
an-052-p03.core_idea: Craving for pleasure makes us fear death

an-053-p01.plain: The Buddha tells a mendicant that the mind leads the world and drags it around; whatever arises in the mind takes control.
an-053-p01.core_idea: The mind leads and controls the world

judge.issue: Shifts "when the mind arises, it takes control" to whatever arises in the mind.

an-053-p02.plain: A truly wise person never intends harm to themselves, to others, or to both. When they think, they think only of what benefits themselves, others, both and the whole world.
an-053-p02.core_idea: Wisdom means intending only benefit, never harm

an-054-p01.plain: You learn a person's ethics by living with them, their honesty by dealing with them, their resilience in hard times, and their wisdom by talking with them, but only over time, with attention, and if you are wise.
an-054-p01.core_idea: Character is known over long, attentive acquaintance

an-054-p02.plain: Someone who loses family, wealth or health may reflect that this is how worldly life is: everyone meets gain and loss, fame and disgrace, blame and praise, pleasure and pain. So they do not grieve and fall apart.
an-054-p02.core_idea: Accept life's ups and downs without falling apart

an-055-p01.plain: Good and true people encourage their followers to live free of greed, hate, delusion and aggression, so that they will not act from these in body, speech or mind.
an-055-p01.core_idea: Live free of greed and hate to act well

an-056-p01.plain: Queen Mallikā promises the Buddha that from now on she will not be irritable, even under heavy criticism, will give generously to spiritual seekers, and will not envy the possessions and honour others receive.
an-056-p01.core_idea: Resolving to drop temper and envy and give

an-057-p01.plain: The Buddha describes craving as a weaver that clings and creeps, choking the world and tangling it like yarn and matted reeds, so that it cannot escape bad rebirths and the round of rebirth.
an-057-p01.core_idea: Craving tangles the world and traps it

an-057-p02.plain: Hate can be born of fondness: when you love someone and others dislike them, you think, 'They dislike the person I like,' and hate for those others springs up.
an-057-p02.core_idea: Love for one person can breed hate for others

an-060-p01.plain: The Buddha names four things that greatly help a person: keeping company with good people, hearing the true teaching, thinking wisely, and practising in line with the teaching.
an-060-p01.core_idea: Good company, true teaching, wise thought and practice help

an-060-p02.plain: There are four ignoble searches: someone who will age, sicken, die and become corrupted searches only for things that also age, sicken, die and are corrupted.
an-060-p02.core_idea: Mortal beings chase only what is also mortal

an-061-p01.plain: Families lose their wealth because they don't look for what is lost, don't repair old things, eat and drink too much, or put an unethical person in charge. They keep it by doing the opposite.
an-061-p01.core_idea: Wealth lasts through care, repair, moderation and honesty

an-062-p01.plain: If a baby puts a stone in his mouth, a caring nurse will pull it out even if it draws blood and upsets him, out of kindness. Once the boy is grown and sensible, she stops worrying about him.
an-062-p01.core_idea: Real care sometimes hurts, until the person can stand alone

an-064-p01.plain: The Buddha tells Nāgita he wants no fame. Those who cannot easily enjoy the peace of renunciation, solitude and awakening as he does can have the filthy, lazy pleasure of possessions, honour and popularity.
an-064-p01.core_idea: The peace of renunciation beats fame and possessions

an-064-p02.plain: As the spotless moon outshines all the stars, a person of faith and good ethics outshines all the stingy people of the world with their generosity.
an-064-p02.core_idea: Generosity outshines stinginess like the moon outshines stars

an-065-p01.plain: When you give, many people love and befriend you, your good name spreads, and a generous person can walk into any gathering confident.
an-065-p01.core_idea: Generosity brings love, good name and confidence

an-065-p02.plain: Good people, grateful and thankful, look after their parents, remembering what they did, and do for their parents what their parents once did for them.
an-065-p02.core_idea: Care for parents as they cared for you

an-065-p03.plain: Like a great banyan tree at a crossroads that shelters birds from all around, a person of faith becomes a refuge for many people.
an-065-p03.core_idea: A person of faith shelters many, like a great tree

an-066-p01.plain: A follower of the Buddha who wants happiness should not pray, hope or pine for it, but practise the way that leads to it; by practising it they gain happiness.
an-066-p01.core_idea: Happiness comes from practice, not from wishing

judge.issue: Drops "as a god or a human being" from the happiness gained.

an-066-p02.plain: When someone close grows old, a wise disciple reflects that this happens to all beings, and that grieving would only harm their health, work and friends. So they don't grieve, and have drawn out sorrow's poisoned arrow.
an-066-p02.core_idea: Everyone ages; grieving it only wounds you

judge.issue: Drops contrast with ordinary people and the closing "sorrowless, free of thorns".

an-066-p03.plain: Grieving and lamenting does not do even a little good, and when your enemies see you are sad, they take heart.

an-067-p01.plain: If chants, recitations, fine words or charity actually help, keep doing them. But if something good simply cannot be had, by you or anyone, accept it without grief: past deeds are powerful, and nothing more can be done.
an-067-p01.core_idea: Accept what cannot be changed without grieving

an-068-p01.plain: Everyone, lay or ordained, should often reflect: I will grow old, I will get sick, I will die, I will be parted from all I love, and I own my deeds and will inherit their results, good or bad.
an-068-p01.core_idea: Reflect often on aging, sickness, death, loss and karma

an-068-p02.plain: It isn't only me who must be parted from everyone and everything I love; all beings must be, as long as they keep being born and dying.
an-068-p02.core_idea: Everyone must lose what they love

an-070-p01.plain: The Buddha points to tree roots and empty huts and tells the mendicant to meditate, not to be negligent, so as not to regret it later. That is his instruction.
an-070-p01.core_idea: Meditate now, so you won't regret it later

an-071-p01.plain: A young mendicant reflects that old age will come and make practice in the forest hard, so they had better make the effort now to reach what they haven't yet reached, and so live at ease when old.
an-071-p01.core_idea: Make your effort while you are young

an-073-p01.plain: The lion strikes every prey with care, never carelessly, whether an elephant or a hare or a cat, so that he does not lose his way.
an-073-p01.core_idea: Do even small things with full care

an-074-p01.plain: A mendicant can live at ease in a community by keeping their own ethics without urging others to, watching themselves instead of others, and not being bothered by being unknown.
an-074-p01.core_idea: Mind your own conduct, not others'

an-075-p01.plain: A good carer can prepare medicine, knows what helps and what harms the patient, cares out of love rather than for gain, is not disgusted by bodily waste, and can encourage the patient with talk of the Dhamma.
an-075-p01.core_idea: Good caregiving comes from skill and love

an-076-p01.plain: The Buddha names five who sleep little at night: a woman longing for a man, a man longing for a woman, a thief longing for loot, a king busy with duties, and a mendicant longing for freedom.
an-076-p01.core_idea: Longing and duty keep people awake

an-077-p01.plain: A mendicant endures cold, heat, hunger, thirst, insects, weather, rude criticism, and even severe, life-threatening pain.
an-077-p01.core_idea: Endure hardship, insult and pain patiently

an-077-p02.plain: One kind of person gives someone robes, food, shelter or medicine, thinking, 'I give, this one receives,' and then looks down on the person they gave to.
an-077-p02.core_idea: Giving can turn into contempt for the receiver

an-078-p01.plain: A good person gives in five ways: out of faith, with care, at the right time, with no strings attached, and without harming themselves or others.
an-078-p01.core_idea: Give with faith, care, timing, freedom and no harm

an-079-p01.plain: There are five ways to get rid of resentment toward someone: develop love, compassion or equanimity for them, stop paying attention to them, or reflect that they own their deeds and will inherit the results.
an-079-p01.core_idea: Love, compassion, equanimity or letting go dissolve resentment

an-079-p02.plain: If someone's speech is bad but their actions are good, ignore their speech and focus on their actions, like a thirsty traveller who sweeps aside the moss on a pond to drink the clear water.
an-079-p02.core_idea: Look past someone's faults to the good in them

an-080-p02.plain: Sāriputta says that when accused, rightly or wrongly, gently or harshly, he will rely on truth and an even temper, saying plainly whether the fault is in him or not.
an-080-p02.core_idea: Meet accusations with truth and an even temper

judge.issue: Names Sāriputta as speaker, which the passage does not; condenses the range of accusations.

an-082-p01.plain: You should not harm living beings, lie, steal, take others' partners or drink alcohol, which clouds the mind. Recollect the Buddha, reflect on the teaching, and develop a harmless, caring mind that leads to the heavens.
an-082-p01.core_idea: Keep the precepts and cultivate a caring mind

judge.issue: Drops the qualifier 'so long as strength is found'.

an-084-p01.plain: The Buddha says well-spoken words have five qualities: they are timely, true, gentle, beneficial and loving. Such speech is blameless and sensible people do not criticize it.
an-084-p01.core_idea: Speak in time, truly, gently, helpfully and lovingly

an-085-p01.plain: Tolerance has five benefits: most people like you, you are neither cruel nor full of regret, you die without confusion, and after death you are reborn in a heavenly realm.
an-085-p01.core_idea: Tolerance brings goodwill, peace and a good rebirth

an-086-p01.plain: Good conduct has five benefits: you don't blame yourself, sensible people praise you, you gain a good name, and you move away from false teachings and settle on true ones.
an-086-p01.core_idea: Good conduct brings self-respect and a good name

an-088-p01.plain: When you are joyful, rapture arises; rapture calms the body; a calm body feels bliss; and in bliss the mind becomes deeply still in meditation.
an-088-p01.core_idea: Joy leads step by step to deep stillness

an-089-p01.plain: Nakula's mother tells her dying husband not to die worrying, since worry is suffering. If he fears she cannot provide for the children and home, he need not: she can spin and card wool and will manage.
an-089-p01.core_idea: Don't die worrying; those left behind will cope

an-090-p01.plain: As night falls, a mendicant reflects that they could die tonight from a snakebite, a fall or an illness, and asks whether any bad qualities remain unabandoned that would stand in their way if they died.
an-090-p01.core_idea: Ask each night what you would regret if you died

an-091-p01.plain: A mendicant goes out, returns, stands, sits, lies down and works, all mindfully; practised this way, it leads to mindfulness and awareness of the situation.

an-092-p01.plain: Being glad before giving, confident while giving and uplifted afterwards: that is the perfect offering.
an-092-p01.core_idea: Give gladly before, during and after

an-093-p01.plain: Greed does not lead to contentment, only to more greed. Hate does not lead to love, only to more hate. Delusion does not lead to understanding, only to more delusion.
an-093-p01.core_idea: Greed, hate and delusion only breed more of themselves

an-093-p02.plain: A white lotus grows in water but water does not cling to it. In the same way, the Buddha is born and lives in the world, but the world does not cling to him.
an-093-p02.core_idea: Live in the world without the world clinging to you

an-094-p01.plain: The Buddha tells Ānanda not to be judgmental or pass judgment on people, because those who judge others harm themselves.

an-095-p01.plain: As the moon's light outshines all the stars put together, diligence is the one quality that, when developed, secures benefits in this life and in lives to come.
an-095-p01.core_idea: Diligence secures good in this life and the next

an-096-p01.plain: When someone abuses, annoys or argues with an ascetic, the ascetic does not do the same back; that is how an ascetic keeps to their duty.

an-096-p02.plain: The Buddha reminds Soṇa that a harp plays well only when its strings are neither too tight nor too loose. Likewise, too much energy brings restlessness and too little brings laziness, so Soṇa should find balance.
an-096-p02.core_idea: Effort works best balanced, like a well-tuned string

judge.issue: Drops 'focus on energy and serenity' and 'learn the character of this situation'.

an-096-p03.plain: As wind cannot move a solid rock, sights, sounds, tastes, smells, touches and ideas, liked or disliked, do not disturb someone who is unaffected; their mind stays steady and free as they watch things pass.
an-096-p03.core_idea: An unmoved mind is like a rock in the wind

an-098-p01.plain: A calm mountain lake without a wave cannot be called forever still; a storm from any direction could stir it up again.
an-098-p01.core_idea: Calm today does not guarantee calm forever

an-099-p01.plain: Sensual pleasure is not the pretty things in the world but the greedy intention in a person. The pretty things stay as they are; the attentive remove their desire for them.
an-099-p01.core_idea: Desire, not the world's beauty, is the problem

an-100-p01.plain: The Buddha says that intention is what he calls action, because after choosing, one acts by body, speech and mind.
an-100-p01.core_idea: Intention is what makes an action

an-100-p02.plain: Birth, aging, illness and death are suffering; so are sorrow, grief, pain, sadness and distress, and not getting what you wish for.
an-100-p02.core_idea: Life's losses and unmet wishes are suffering

an-100-p03.plain: Overwhelmed by suffering, a person either grieves and falls into confusion, or searches outside for someone who knows a word or two that might end it. Suffering leads to confusion or a search.
an-100-p03.core_idea: Suffering leads to confusion or a search for help

an-100-p04.plain: A mendicant who loves company and groups cannot take pleasure in being alone in seclusion, and without that they cannot learn the patterns of the mind.
an-100-p04.core_idea: Knowing your mind requires time alone

an-101-p01.plain: The Buddha says you cannot reach perfection without giving up six things: conceit, feeling inferior, feeling superior, overrating yourself, stubbornness and grovelling.
an-101-p01.core_idea: Perfection requires dropping conceit in all its forms

an-101-p02.plain: A mendicant who enjoys the teaching, meditation, letting go, solitude, kindness and freedom from mental proliferation is full of joy here and now and has prepared the ground for ending the defilements.
an-101-p02.core_idea: Joy comes from teaching, meditation, letting go and kindness

an-102-p01.plain: Three bad qualities are discontent, cruelty and unprincipled conduct. To give them up, develop rejoicing, harmlessness and principled conduct.
an-102-p01.core_idea: Rejoicing, harmlessness and principle replace their opposites

an-102-p02.plain: Three bad qualities are discontent, lack of awareness and wanting too much. To give them up, develop contentment, awareness and having few wishes.
an-102-p02.core_idea: Contentment, awareness and few wishes cure their opposites

an-102-p03.plain: Three bad qualities are restlessness, lack of restraint and negligence. To give them up, develop calm, restraint and diligence.
an-102-p03.core_idea: Calm, restraint and diligence cure restlessness and negligence

an-103-p01.plain: The Buddha tells Ugga that fire, floods, rulers, thieves and heirs can take ordinary wealth, but not seven kinds: faith, ethics, conscience, prudence, learning, generosity and wisdom. Whoever has these is truly rich.
an-103-p01.core_idea: Inner qualities are wealth no one can take

judge.issue: Drops 'unloved' heirs and 'invincible among gods and humans'.

an-105-p01.plain: A true friend gives and does what is hard, bears your harsh words, shares and keeps secrets, and never abandons you or looks down on you in trouble or loss. If you want a friend, keep company with such people.
an-105-p01.core_idea: A true friend stays loyal through hardship

an-105-p02.plain: Stay close to a friend with seven qualities, even if they push you away: they are liked and respected, they correct you and accept correction, they speak of deep things, and they don't urge you to do wrong.
an-105-p02.core_idea: Keep friends who correct you and lead you right

an-108-p01.plain: Nanda's mother tells of her only, dearly loved son being seized and executed by the rulers, yet she cannot recall becoming upset at any stage. The listener marvels that she keeps even her thoughts pure.
an-108-p01.core_idea: Even in terrible loss, the mind can stay unshaken

an-110-p01.plain: Arguments lead to lots of talking, talking makes people restless, restlessness loses restraint, and without restraint the mind is far from stillness.
an-110-p01.core_idea: Arguments lead the mind away from stillness

an-110-p02.plain: A mendicant who hears that nothing is worth clinging to comes to understand all things, watches every feeling as impermanent and lets it go, grasps at nothing, and so is free of anxiety and reaches nirvana.
an-110-p02.core_idea: Grasp at nothing and anxiety ends

an-110-p03.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants not to fear good deeds, because 'good deeds' is another word for happiness.
an-110-p03.core_idea: Good deeds mean happiness; don't fear them

an-110-p04.plain: An irritable person overwhelmed by anger is ugly, however well bathed, groomed and dressed in fine clothes they may be.

an-110-p05.plain: A person overwhelmed by anger takes what they don't need for what they need, and what they need for what they don't, and getting things so backwards brings them lasting harm and suffering.
an-110-p05.core_idea: Anger makes you mistake harm for good

an-111-p01.plain: An irritable person looks ugly and sleeps badly, mistakes what they need, may kill in word or deed, loses wealth and good name, and is avoided by family, friends and loved ones.
an-111-p01.core_idea: Anger costs you sleep, wealth, name and loved ones

an-111-p02.plain: Anger causes harm and disturbs the mind without the person seeing the danger. In anger you cannot see the good or the truth; you wreck easily what was hard to build, and afterwards you burn with remorse.
an-111-p02.core_idea: Anger blinds you and destroys what you built

an-111-p03.plain: Anger is a hidden snare of death in the heart. Cut it out with self-control, wisdom, energy and right views.
an-111-p03.core_idea: Cut out anger with self-control and wisdom

an-111-p04.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants that all conditioned things are impermanent, unstable and unreliable, and that this alone is reason enough to grow disenchanted with them, let go of desire and be free.
an-111-p04.core_idea: All conditions are unreliable, so let go of them

an-112-p01.plain: Like a wise gatekeeper who keeps strangers out and lets friends in, a noble disciple guards the mind with mindfulness, giving up what is harmful and blameworthy, developing what is good, and keeping pure.
an-112-p01.core_idea: Mindfulness guards the mind like a gatekeeper

an-114-p01.plain: Thinking of your own good is reason enough to keep going diligently; so is thinking of others' good, or the good of both.
an-114-p01.core_idea: Your good and others' good both justify diligence

an-114-p02.plain: Human life is like a dewdrop on a blade of grass, gone as soon as the sun rises: brief, fleeting and full of suffering. So wake up, do good and live the spiritual life, for no one born escapes death.
an-114-p02.core_idea: Life is a dewdrop; wake up and do good

an-115-p01.plain: It is right to say today that human life is short, fleeting and full of suffering, so wake up, do good and live the spiritual life, since no one born escapes death. A long life now is about a century.
an-115-p01.core_idea: Life is short; do good before death comes

an-116-p01.plain: Loving even one creature with a heart free of hate makes you a good person; a noble one who feels for all creatures creates great merit.
an-116-p01.core_idea: Love for even one being makes you good

an-116-p02.plain: Do not kill or have others kill, do not conquer or urge others to conquer; with love for all beings you will have no enemy.
an-116-p02.core_idea: Love for all beings leaves no enemies

an-116-p03.plain: Gain and loss, fame and disgrace, blame and praise, pleasure and pain are all impermanent. A wise, mindful person sees this, so the pleasant does not sway their mind and the unpleasant does not repel them.
an-116-p03.core_idea: Life's ups and downs pass; stay unmoved by them

an-116-p04.plain: It is good for a mendicant to look from time to time at their own failings and others', and at their own successes and others'.
an-116-p04.core_idea: Review failings and successes, yours and others'

an-120-p01.plain: The ocean floor slopes gradually with no sudden drop. In the same way, in the Buddha's teaching, awakening comes through gradual training and practice, not all at once.
an-120-p01.core_idea: Awakening comes gradually, like a sloping shore

an-120-p02.plain: As the ocean has only one taste, salt, the Buddha's teaching and training has only one taste, freedom.
an-120-p02.core_idea: The whole teaching tastes of freedom

an-122-p02.plain: Now that you have a human life and the true teaching has been so well taught, if you don't seize the moment you are wasting your time.
an-122-p02.core_idea: Seize this rare chance; don't waste it

an-123-p01.plain: A mendicant who has few wishes, contentment, solitude, energy, mindfulness, stillness or wisdom does not wish for others to know they have these qualities.

an-124-p01.plain: A good person is born into a family for the welfare and happiness of many: parents, children, partners, workers, friends, ancestors, rulers, gods and spiritual seekers, just as a great rain cloud nourishes all crops.
an-124-p01.core_idea: A good person benefits everyone, like rain

an-125-p01.plain: All the treasure in the world, pearls, gems and gold, is not worth a sixteenth part of a mind developed in love, just as starlight cannot rival the moon.
an-125-p01.core_idea: A loving mind outweighs all treasure

an-127-p01.plain: The Buddha tells Gotamī that whatever leads to passion, attachment, accumulating, more desire, discontent, crowding, laziness and being a burden is not his teaching; whatever leads to the opposite is.
an-127-p01.core_idea: Test any teaching by where it leads

an-127-p02.plain: Good friendship means spending time with people, young or old, who are mature in faith, ethics, generosity and wisdom, talking with them, and following their example.
an-127-p02.core_idea: Befriend good people and follow their example

an-127-p03.plain: Balanced finances means knowing your income and spending, being neither extravagant nor stingy, so that what comes in exceeds what goes out.
an-127-p03.core_idea: Spend less than you earn, neither lavish nor stingy

an-129-p01.plain: The Buddha tells a mendicant to train his mind to be steady and settled within, untouched by bad qualities. Then he should develop the heart's release through love, practising it fully until it becomes his foundation.
an-129-p01.core_idea: Settle the mind, then build it on love

an-130-p01.plain: The Buddha names eight noble ways of speaking: saying you haven't seen, heard, thought or known something when you haven't, and saying you have when you have.
an-130-p01.core_idea: Say only what you truly saw, heard or knew

an-131-p01.plain: As night falls, a mendicant reflects that they could die tonight from a snakebite, a fall, an illness or an attack, and asks whether any bad qualities remain unabandoned that would stand in their way if they died.
an-131-p01.core_idea: Ask each night what you would regret if you died

an-132-p01.plain: One ground for laziness: a mendicant has work to do and thinks it will tire the body, so they lie down instead of making the effort to attain what they have not yet attained.
an-132-p01.core_idea: Avoiding tiredness becomes an excuse for laziness

an-133-p01.plain: All things are rooted in desire and produced by attention. Contact is their origin, feeling where they meet, stillness their chief, mindfulness their ruler, wisdom their overseer, and freedom their core.
an-133-p01.core_idea: Freedom is the core of all things

an-134-p01.plain: One should see the body's unattractiveness to give up greed, develop love to give up hate, use breath meditation to quiet thinking, and see impermanence to uproot the sense of 'I am', reaching nirvana in this life.
an-134-p01.core_idea: Specific practices uproot greed, hate and self-conceit

judge.issue: Drops the step that perceiving impermanence stabilises perception of not-self.

an-135-p01.plain: Four things draw people together: giving, kind words, care and equality. The best gift is the teaching, the best kind words are teaching an eager listener, and the best care is helping others grow in faith, ethics, generosity and wisdom.
an-135-p01.core_idea: The best giving and care is sharing the teaching

an-136-p01.plain: The earth is not disgusted when clean and filthy things are thrown on it. In the same way, Sāriputta says, he lives with a heart like the earth: vast, limitless, and free of enmity and ill will.
an-136-p01.core_idea: Keep a heart as accepting as the earth

judge.issue: Names Sāriputta as speaker, which the passage does not.

an-139-p01.plain: There are nine ways to get rid of resentment. One is to think, 'They harmed me, but what can I possibly do about it?'
an-139-p01.core_idea: Letting go of what can't be undone ends resentment

an-140-p01.plain: A foolish mountain cow, eager to try new pastures, lifts her back hoof before her front one is set down, so she never reaches the new place and never gets safely back to where she started.
an-140-p01.core_idea: Rushing ahead without footing gets you nowhere

an-141-p01.plain: Ānanda tells a nun of a meditative stillness that neither strains forward nor pulls back and isn't forced. Being free, it is stable; stable, it is content; content, one is not anxious. Its fruit is enlightenment.
an-141-p01.core_idea: Unforced stillness is stable, content and free of anxiety

judge.issue: Adds Ānanda as speaker; drops that the Buddha is the one who declared the fruit.

an-142-p01.plain: A wild bull elephant who once lived crowded by the herd, eating trampled grass and drinking muddy water, now lives alone, free of all that, and happily scratches his itches with a branch.
an-142-p01.core_idea: Solitude brings relief from crowded life

an-142-p02.plain: Before his awakening the Buddha thought renunciation was good, yet his mind did not embrace it or find it peaceful. He realised it was because he had not seen the drawbacks of sensual pleasures or experienced the benefits of renunciation.
an-142-p02.core_idea: Seeing pleasure's drawbacks makes renunciation feel peaceful

an-149-p01.plain: Mean jealousy is given up not by body or speech but by seeing it clearly with wisdom again and again. It is wishing that someone else not prosper or not receive what they are given.
an-149-p01.core_idea: Jealousy is overcome by repeated wise seeing

an-149-p02.plain: Corrupt wishes are given up not by body or speech but by seeing them clearly with wisdom again and again. They are wanting to be known for faith, ethics, learning, solitude or energy that you do not have.
an-149-p02.core_idea: Wanting credit for virtues you lack is corrupt

an-150-p01.plain: King Pasenadi is said to be the greatest in his realm, yet even he decays and dies. Seeing this, a wise disciple loses their desire even for the highest, let alone for lesser things.
an-150-p01.core_idea: Even the greatest decay, so desire fades

an-152-p01.plain: A mendicant who wants to accuse someone should first check whether their own conduct is pure and blameless; if not, people will tell them to train their own behaviour first.
an-152-p01.core_idea: Check your own conduct before accusing others

judge.issue: Generalises 'bodily behavior' to conduct in general.

an-153-p03.plain: I own my actions and inherit their results; they are where I come from, my family and my shelter, good or bad. As each day and night passes, what kind of person am I turning into?
an-153-p03.core_idea: You inherit your deeds; ask who you are becoming

an-154-p01.plain: Just as a young person checks their face in a mirror to remove any dirt, and is glad when there is none, a mendicant should check their own mind; this checking helps their good qualities.
an-154-p01.core_idea: Check your mind as you check a mirror

an-154-p02.plain: The Buddha says he does not praise standing still in good qualities, let alone slipping back; he praises growing in them.
an-154-p02.core_idea: Praise growth in goodness, not standing still

an-155-p01.plain: Giving up means a mendicant does not put up with sensual, hostile or cruel thoughts, or any other unwholesome quality, once it arises, but lets it go and gets rid of it entirely.
an-155-p01.core_idea: Do not tolerate harmful thoughts; let them go

an-155-p02.plain: Fading away is when a mendicant, alone in the wilderness or an empty hut, reflects that the stilling of all activity, letting go of attachments and ending craving is peaceful and sublime.
an-155-p02.core_idea: Letting go of all craving is peaceful

an-157-p01.plain: In this teaching, being dissatisfied is suffering and being satisfied is happiness. When you are dissatisfied you find no ease anywhere, whatever you do; when satisfied, you find happiness wherever you are.
an-157-p01.core_idea: Dissatisfaction is suffering; contentment brings happiness everywhere

an-158-p01.plain: Ten rare, desirable things each have a cause: effort brings wealth, good friends support ethics, honesty wins friends, eager listening and questioning bring wisdom, right practice leads to heaven, and so on.
an-158-p01.core_idea: Each good thing in life is fed by something

judge.issue: Lists only some of the ten pairs; beauty, health, learning and others omitted.

an-159-p01.plain: The Buddha gives ten ways to let go of resentment: whenever someone has harmed, is harming or will harm you or those you love, or helps those you dislike, think: what can I possibly do? And don't get angry needlessly.
an-159-p01.core_idea: Drop resentment: think, what can I possibly do?

fix.display_text: “Mendicants, there are these ten ways to get rid of resentment. What ten? Thinking: ‘They harmed me, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment. Thinking: ‘They are harming me …’ … ‘They will harm me …’ … ‘They harmed someone I love …’ … ‘They are harming someone I love …’ ‘They will harm someone I love …’ … ‘They helped someone I dislike …’ … ‘They are helping someone I dislike …’ … Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment. And you don’t get angry for no reason. These are the ten ways of getting rid of resentment.”

an-162-p01.plain: The Buddha says not to make efforts that make bad qualities grow and good ones shrink, but to make efforts that shrink the bad and grow the good.
an-162-p01.core_idea: Pursue efforts that grow good qualities, not bad

an-163-p01.plain: The Buddha tells Uttiya he teaches from his own insight to purify beings, help them get past sorrow and grief, end pain and the cycle of suffering, and reach extinguishment.
an-163-p01.core_idea: The Buddha teaches to end suffering and sorrow

an-164-p01.plain: A good person stops lying and stays truthful and trustworthy. They stop gossip that divides people; instead they bring together those who are split and support those who are united, loving harmony and speaking for it.
an-164-p01.core_idea: Speak truthfully and use words to create harmony

an-166-p01.plain: Few people cross to the far shore; most just run up and down this side. But those who practise a well-explained teaching will cross the realm of death, so hard to get beyond.
an-166-p01.core_idea: Few cross over; those who practise the teaching will

an-170-p01.plain: They have a kind heart and wish all beings well: may they be free of hatred and ill will, untroubled and happy.
an-170-p01.core_idea: Wish all beings freedom from hatred, and happiness

an-171-p01.plain: All beings own their actions and inherit what comes of them. Their deeds are their origin, their family and their refuge, and they will receive the results of whatever they do, good or bad.
an-171-p01.core_idea: Beings inherit the results of their own deeds

an-172-p01.plain: A good person avoids gossip that divides people and works for harmony. They avoid harsh words and speak gently and kindly. They avoid idle chatter, saying only what is true, timely, sensible, brief and useful.
an-172-p01.core_idea: Speak kindly, truthfully, timely, and for harmony

an-172-p02.plain: They meditate spreading love in every direction until it fills the whole world, boundless and free of hatred. They see their mind has grown from narrow to limitless, and their limited past deeds no longer hold there.
an-172-p02.core_idea: Boundless love makes the mind limitless

an-172-p03.plain: Neither women nor men can take this body with them when they die. What lies inside mortal beings is the mind.
an-172-p03.core_idea: We leave the body behind; the mind is within

an-173-p01.plain: A person living ethically need not wish to be free of regret; it comes naturally. With no regret, joy arises by itself, and from joy comes rapture, without any need to wish for it.
an-173-p01.core_idea: Ethical living naturally leads to joy, without wishing

an-175-p01.plain: Those with faith, energy, mindfulness, meditative immersion and wisdom succeed; those lacking them do not.
an-175-p01.core_idea: Faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion and wisdom bring success

an-176-p01.plain: Remember your good friends and think how very fortunate you are to have friends who advise and guide you out of kindness and care.
an-176-p01.core_idea: Be grateful for friends who guide you kindly

an-176-p02.plain: Mendicants, fully cultivating the heart's release by love brings eleven benefits: easy sleep, happy waking, no bad dreams, love of humans and non-humans, protection by deities, safety from fire, poison and blade, quick immersion, a bright face, dying unconfused, and, if you go no higher, rebirth in a divine realm.
an-176-p02.core_idea: Cultivating love brings many blessings, in life and death
an-176-p02.plain_v1: Developing love fully brings eleven benefits: you sleep and wake easily, have no nightmares, are loved by humans and others, protected by gods, settle quickly in meditation, look bright, die unconfused, and may be reborn divinely.

judge_v1.issue: Drops immunity to fire, poison and blade and the condition 'if you don't penetrate higher'.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops safety from fire, poison and blade, and the condition on divine rebirth.

dhp-001-p01.plain: Intention leads everything we do. If you speak or act with a corrupt mind, suffering follows you like a cart wheel behind the ox; act with a pure mind, and happiness follows like your own shadow.
dhp-001-p01.core_idea: Suffering or happiness follows the intention behind actions

dhp-001-p02.plain: Those who keep repeating how others abused, struck, beat or robbed them never put their hatred to rest; those who do not hold on to such grudges let it rest.

dhp-001-p04.plain: Through hard work, care, restraint and self-control, a wise person builds an island for themselves that no flood can wash over.
dhp-001-p04.core_idea: Self-discipline builds an island floods cannot reach

dhp-001-p05.plain: The mind trembles and shakes and is hard to guard and control, but the wise straighten it, like an arrow-maker straightening an arrow.
dhp-001-p05.core_idea: The wise straighten the restless mind

dhp-001-p06.plain: The mind is hard to restrain, flighty, landing wherever it wants. It is good to tame it, because a tamed mind brings bliss.
dhp-001-p06.core_idea: A tamed mind leads to bliss

dhp-001-p07.plain: Very soon this body will lie on the ground, lifeless and unconscious, thrown aside like a useless log.
dhp-001-p07.core_idea: The body will soon lie lifeless

dhp-001-p08.plain: A mind aimed the wrong way will do you more harm than any enemy or hater could do.
dhp-001-p08.core_idea: Your own misdirected mind harms you most

dhp-001-p09.plain: Don't look for faults in others, in what they have or haven't done. Watch only yourself, and what you have or haven't done.
dhp-001-p09.core_idea: Examine your own conduct, not others' faults

dhp-001-p10.plain: Just as a fragrant, lovely lotus can bloom from a heap of roadside trash, so a disciple of the Buddha, among those thought worthless, outshines blind ordinary people with wisdom.
dhp-001-p10.core_idea: Beauty and wisdom can rise from what is despised

extension.text:
From a heap of trash
discarded on the highway,
a lotus might blossom,
fragrant and delightful.
So too, among those thought of as trash, a disciple of the perfect Buddha outshines with their wisdom the blind ordinary folk.

dhp-001-p10.plain_v1: A fragrant, lovely lotus can bloom from a pile of rubbish thrown by the roadside. In the same way, a disciple of the Buddha shines with wisdom among people looked down on as worthless.

judge_v1.issue: Loses that the disciple, from among the despised, outshines 'blind ordinary folk'.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops that the disciple outshines the blind ordinary folk.

dhp-001-p11.plain: If on your travels you find no companion equal to or better than you, go on firmly alone; there is no companionship with fools.
dhp-001-p11.core_idea: Better alone than in the company of fools

dhp-001-p12.plain: A fool who knows they are a fool is at least that much wise. The real fool is the one who thinks they are wise.
dhp-001-p12.core_idea: The true fool thinks they are wise

dhp-001-p14.plain: Treat someone who points out your faults as a guide to buried treasure. Keep close to such a wise person who corrects you when needed; with them, life improves.
dhp-001-p14.core_idea: Value those who point out your faults

dhp-001-p15.plain: Just as wind cannot move solid rock, blame and praise do not shake the wise.
dhp-001-p15.core_idea: Blame and praise do not move the wise

dhp-001-p16.plain: Good people let go of everything and do not beg for what they want. Whether touched by sorrow or happiness, the wise are neither cast down nor carried away.
dhp-001-p16.core_idea: The wise stay steady through joy and sorrow

dhp-001-p17.plain: Never wish to succeed by unfair means, for yourself or anyone else, whether for children, money or country; instead be good, wise and fair.
dhp-001-p17.core_idea: Never seek success by unjust means

dhp-001-p18.plain: One meaningful saying that brings you peace is worth more than a thousand empty ones.
dhp-001-p18.core_idea: One meaningful word outweighs a thousand empty ones

dhp-001-p19.plain: The greatest victor is not someone who defeats a million men in battle, but someone who conquers just one: himself.
dhp-001-p19.core_idea: Conquering yourself is the greatest victory

dhp-002-p01.plain: It is better to live one day full of energy and strength than a hundred years lazy and listless.
dhp-002-p01.core_idea: One energetic day beats a hundred idle years

dhp-002-p02.plain: If you do something wrong, don't keep repeating it or set your heart on it, because building up wrongdoing brings suffering.
dhp-002-p02.core_idea: Don't repeat wrongdoing; piling it up brings suffering

dhp-002-p03.plain: Don't think of wrongdoing as minor, as though it won't come back to you. A pot fills drop by drop, and a fool fills with wickedness bit by bit.
dhp-002-p03.core_idea: Small wrongs add up, drop by drop

dhp-002-p04.plain: Don't speak harshly, or people may answer harshly. Aggressive words cause pain, and the stick may strike back at you.
dhp-002-p04.core_idea: Harsh words come back at you

dhp-002-p05.plain: If you make yourself as still as a broken gong that no longer rings, you reach extinguishment and are free of conflict.
dhp-002-p05.core_idea: Stillness brings peace and ends conflict

dhp-002-p06.plain: How can there be joy or laughter when the world is always burning? Wrapped in darkness, wouldn't you look for a light?
dhp-002-p06.core_idea: In a burning world, seek the light

dhp-002-p07.plain: Even the splendid chariots of kings wear out, and this body grows old too. But the teaching of the good never ages, as the good tell one another.
dhp-002-p07.core_idea: Bodies age, but the truth of the good does not

dhp-002-p08.plain: Someone who learns little grows old like an ox: their body gets bigger, but their wisdom does not.
dhp-002-p08.core_idea: Ageing without learning grows the body, not wisdom

dhp-002-p09.plain: Those who rejected the spiritual life when young and earned no wealth either now lie like used-up arrows, mourning the past.
dhp-002-p09.core_idea: Neglecting youth leaves you lamenting in old age

dhp-002-p10.plain: If you treated yourself the way you teach others, you would be well tamed and able to tame; for the self, it seems, is hard to tame.
dhp-002-p10.core_idea: Practise on yourself what you teach others

dhp-002-p11.plain: You are your own master; who else could be? With a well-trained self, you gain a master that is truly rare.

dhp-002-p12.plain: Doing bad things that harm yourself is easy, but doing good, helpful things is the hardest of all.
dhp-002-p12.core_idea: Harm is easy; doing good is hardest

dhp-002-p13.plain: You do wrong by yourself and are corrupted by yourself; you avoid wrong by yourself and are purified by yourself. Purity is personal; no one can purify someone else.
dhp-002-p13.core_idea: No one can purify another; it's up to you

dhp-002-p14.plain: Never neglect your own true good for the sake of someone else's, however important. Knowing what is truly good for you, stay devoted to your heart's goal.
dhp-002-p14.core_idea: Stay devoted to your own true goal

dhp-002-p15.plain: Get up, don't be careless; live by principle and act well. Someone who acts well sleeps easily, in this world and the next.
dhp-002-p15.core_idea: Live well and you sleep at ease

dhp-002-p17.plain: Even if it rained money, sensual pleasures would never satisfy you. A wise person knows they give little satisfaction and much suffering.
dhp-002-p17.core_idea: Sensual pleasures never satisfy and bring suffering

dhp-002-p18.plain: Let us live very happily, loving among those who are hostile; among hostile people, let us live with love.
dhp-002-p18.core_idea: Live happily, with love among the hostile

dhp-002-p19.plain: Winning breeds hatred, and the defeated sleep badly. The peaceful sleep easily, having left both winning and losing behind.
dhp-002-p19.core_idea: Peace lies beyond victory and defeat

dhp-002-p20.plain: Health is the greatest blessing, contentment the greatest wealth, trust the best family, and extinguishment the highest happiness.
dhp-002-p20.core_idea: Health, contentment, trust and nirvana are life's best

dhp-002-p21.plain: Don't get too attached to what you like or dislike, because missing what you like is painful, and so is facing what you dislike.
dhp-002-p21.core_idea: Attachment to likes and dislikes brings pain

judge.issue: Passage is about people you like or dislike; plain shifts it to things.

dhp-002-p22.plain: Sorrow and fear both come from what we hold dear. Someone who holds nothing dear has no sorrow, let alone fear.
dhp-002-p22.core_idea: Sorrow and fear come from holding things dear

dhp-003-p01.plain: Sorrow and fear both come from desire. Someone free of desire has no sorrow, let alone fear.
dhp-003-p01.core_idea: Freedom from desire means freedom from sorrow

dhp-003-p02.plain: When anger lurches forward like a runaway chariot, hold it back. That person is a true charioteer; everyone else is just holding the reins.
dhp-003-p02.core_idea: Truly controlling anger is real mastery

dhp-003-p03.plain: Overcome anger with kindness, wickedness with goodness, stinginess with generosity and lies with truth.
dhp-003-p03.core_idea: Meet anger with kindness, lies with truth

dhp-003-p04.plain: It has always been this way, Atula: people blame you when you are silent, when you talk a lot, even when you speak just right. No one has ever been, or will be, wholly praised or wholly blamed.
dhp-003-p04.core_idea: No one escapes blame; no one is wholly praised

dhp-003-p05.plain: A wise person clears away their own impurities gradually, little by little, moment by moment, the way a smith refines silver.
dhp-003-p05.core_idea: Purify yourself gradually, bit by bit

dhp-003-p06.plain: Life is easy for the shameless, who are bold as crows, pushy, rude and corrupt. Life is hard for those with a conscience, who seek purity, do not cling, are humble, honest in their living and discerning.
dhp-003-p06.core_idea: Life is easy for the shameless, hard for the conscientious

dhp-003-p07.plain: No fire burns like greed, no crime is like hatred, no net traps like delusion, and no river sweeps away like craving.
dhp-003-p07.core_idea: Greed, hate, delusion and craving are the worst traps

dhp-003-p08.plain: Others' faults are easy to see, your own hard. You toss others' faults up high like hay, while hiding your own as a cheat hides a bad hand of cards.
dhp-003-p08.core_idea: We see others' faults, but hide our own

dhp-003-p09.plain: If you keep searching for other people's flaws, your own impurities only grow, and you are far from ending them.
dhp-003-p09.core_idea: Fault-finding in others makes your own flaws grow

dhp-003-p10.plain: Making quick judgments does not make you just. A wise person weighs both what matters and what does not.
dhp-003-p10.core_idea: Justice needs careful judgment, not haste

dhp-003-p11.plain: Talking a lot does not make you wise. The one who is secure, free of hostility and fear, is called wise.
dhp-003-p11.core_idea: Wisdom is security and fearlessness, not much talk

dhp-003-p12.plain: Grey hair does not make you an elder. Someone who has matured only in years has grown old for nothing.
dhp-003-p12.core_idea: Age alone does not make you wise

dhp-003-p13.plain: You have to do the work yourselves; the Buddhas only point out the way.
dhp-003-p13.core_idea: You must do the work yourself

dhp-003-p14.plain: Everything conditioned is impermanent. When you see this with wisdom, you grow weary of suffering, and that is the path to purity.
dhp-003-p14.core_idea: Seeing impermanence clearly is the path to purity

dhp-003-p15.plain: Some don't act when it is time to begin; though young and strong, they are lazy. Their minds sunk in gloomy thoughts, idle and sluggish, they cannot see the path.
dhp-003-p15.core_idea: Laziness keeps you from finding the path

dhp-003-p16.plain: Wisdom grows from meditation and fades without it. Knowing these two roads, of growth and decline, live in a way that lets wisdom grow.

dhp-003-p17.plain: If giving up small, worldly pleasures lets you see a far greater happiness, the wise will give them up for that greater happiness.
dhp-003-p17.core_idea: Give up small pleasures for greater happiness

dhp-003-p18.plain: Those who seek their own happiness by causing others to suffer stay entangled in hatred and never get free of it.
dhp-003-p18.core_idea: Happiness bought with others' pain breeds enmity

dhp-003-p19.plain: Good people shine from far away like the Himalayan peaks, but the wicked go unseen, like arrows shot into the night.
dhp-003-p19.core_idea: The good shine far; the wicked go unseen

dhp-003-p20.plain: Sitting alone, sleeping alone, wandering tirelessly alone, someone who trains themselves alone will find delight in the forest.

dhp-003-p21.plain: It is better not to do a bad deed, because it will torment you later. It is better to do a good deed, which brings no torment.
dhp-003-p21.core_idea: Bad deeds haunt you; good deeds do not

dhp-003-p22.plain: Like a war elephant hit by arrows in battle, I will put up with abuse, because so many people behave badly.
dhp-003-p22.core_idea: Endure abuse patiently, like an elephant in battle

dhp-004-p01.plain: My mind used to wander wherever it wanted, however it pleased. Now I will guide it carefully, as a trainer with a hook guides an elephant in heat.
dhp-004-p01.core_idea: Train the wandering mind with care

dhp-004-p02.plain: Take joy in being diligent and guard your mind well. Pull yourself out of this pit, like an elephant stuck in mud.
dhp-004-p02.core_idea: Pull yourself out of the mire with diligence

dhp-004-p04.plain: It is a blessing to have a friend when you need one, to be content with whatever you have, to have done good by the end of life, and to let go of all suffering.
dhp-004-p04.core_idea: Friendship, contentment, good deeds and freedom are blessings

dhp-004-p05.plain: Whoever is overcome by craving and attachment to the world sees their sorrows grow like grass in the rain. Whoever overcomes it finds their sorrows fall away like water off a lotus leaf.
dhp-004-p05.core_idea: Overcoming craving makes sorrow slide away

dhp-004-p06.plain: A tree cut down grows back while its roots are strong; in the same way, suffering keeps returning as long as the tendency to crave has not been uprooted.
dhp-004-p06.core_idea: Suffering returns until craving is uprooted

dhp-004-p07.plain: Let go of the past, the future and the present, and go beyond rebirth. With your heart free in every way, you won't return to birth and old age.
dhp-004-p07.core_idea: Let go of past, present and future

dhp-004-p08.plain: Wealth ruins a fool, but not someone seeking the far shore. Craving money, the fool destroys themselves and others.
dhp-004-p08.core_idea: Craving wealth ruins fools and those around them

dhp-004-p09.plain: Spend time with spiritual friends who are tireless and earn their living honestly. Share what you have, act skilfully, and when you are full of joy you will end suffering.
dhp-004-p09.core_idea: Good friends, sharing and joy end suffering

dhp-004-p10.plain: Encourage and examine yourself; a mendicant who is self-controlled and mindful always lives happily. You are your own master and your own home, so restrain yourself as a merchant manages a fine horse.
dhp-004-p10.core_idea: You are your own master; restrain yourself

dhp-004-p11.plain: For a brahmin nothing is better than holding the mind back from attachment. Wherever the wish to harm falls away, suffering subsides right there.
dhp-004-p11.core_idea: Where the wish to harm stops, suffering eases

dhp-004-p12.plain: Why the matted hair and deerskin, you fool? The tangle is inside you, yet you only clean up your outside.
dhp-004-p12.core_idea: Outer show cannot fix an inner tangle

dhp-004-p13.plain: Someone who bears abuse, violence and imprisonment without anger, whose strength is patience, is who the Buddha calls a true brahmin.

dhp-004-p14.plain: Someone who does not fight among fighters, stays calm among the armed and does not grasp among the grasping is who the Buddha calls a true brahmin.
dhp-004-p14.core_idea: Stay peaceful among the hostile and grasping

dn-002-p01.plain: The Buddha tells the mendicants not to become resentful or angry when others criticise him, his teaching or the Sangha. Anger only harms you, and it stops you judging whether the criticism is fair.
dn-002-p01.core_idea: Anger at criticism blinds you and harms you

dn-007-p01.plain: A content mendicant needs only robes for the body and alms food for the stomach, and carries nothing else wherever they go, like a bird whose only load is its wings.
dn-007-p01.core_idea: Contentment travels light, like a bird

dn-009-p01.plain: The Buddha tells the king that killing his just father for power was a foolish wrong. But because he sees it as wrong and confesses it, the Buddha accepts it; recognising, admitting and restraining future wrongs is growth.
dn-009-p01.core_idea: Owning a wrong and resolving to change is growth

dn-010-p01.plain: Among those who value family lineage, the noble class is highest. But someone accomplished in knowledge and conduct is highest among gods and humans.
dn-010-p01.core_idea: Knowledge and good conduct outrank birth

dn-011-p01.plain: Anyone tied to concerns of ancestry, clan, pride or arranging marriages is far from supreme knowledge and conduct. You realise it only once you give such things up.
dn-011-p01.core_idea: Pride in lineage blocks true knowledge

dn-013-p01.plain: Ethics and wisdom always go together and are the best things in the world. As one hand washes the other, ethics purifies wisdom and wisdom purifies ethics.
dn-013-p01.core_idea: Ethics and wisdom purify each other

dn-015-p01.plain: Whatever can come into being can also come to an end.
dn-015-p01.core_idea: Everything that arises will pass away

dn-016-p01.plain: Let us set aside the things we disagree on; there are some things we agree on.
dn-016-p01.core_idea: Start from common ground, not disagreement

dn-019-p01.plain: Harmful qualities will be given up and purifying ones will grow. You will realise abundant wisdom for yourself in this life, with only joy, happiness, calm, mindfulness and awareness. Such a life is blissful.
dn-019-p01.core_idea: Giving up corruption leads to a joyful life

dn-020-p01.plain: Home life is cramped and dusty, while the life of one who has gone forth is wide open. Living at home, it is hard to lead the spiritual life fully and purely, polished like a shell.
dn-020-p01.core_idea: Leaving home life opens the way to purity

dn-021-p02.plain: Someone gravely ill loses appetite and strength, but in time recovers both, and thinking of this they are filled with joy and happiness.
dn-021-p02.core_idea: Recovering from illness brings deep joy

dn-024-p01.plain: They meditate spreading boundless love in every direction to the whole world. Like a strong horn blower heard in all four directions, love developed this way leaves no room for their limited past deeds.
dn-024-p01.core_idea: Boundless love outweighs limited past deeds

dn-025-p01.plain: For me now, life is short, brief and passing; a long life is a hundred years or a little more.
dn-025-p01.core_idea: Human life is short and fleeting

dn-026-p01.plain: Everyone must die, Your Majesty, you too; no one is spared. Your family will see you no more, and you will never see them again.
dn-026-p01.core_idea: Everyone dies, and leaves their loved ones

dn-026-p02.plain: This world is in trouble: it is born, ages, dies and is reborn, yet does not know how to escape this suffering of old age and death. When will a way out be found?
dn-026-p02.core_idea: The world seeks escape from ageing and death

dn-027-p01.plain: Patience is the highest discipline and extinguishment the highest goal, say the Buddhas. A true renunciate never harms others. Do no evil, do what is good and purify your mind: this is the Buddhas' teaching.
dn-027-p01.core_idea: Avoid evil, do good, purify your mind

dn-028-p01.plain: The Buddha explains to Ananda a chain: feeling leads to craving, craving to seeking and gaining, then desire, attachment, ownership, stinginess and guarding possessions, and from guarding come violence, quarrels, slander and lies.
dn-028-p01.core_idea: Craving leads step by step to conflict and lies

judge.issue: Drops the 'evaluation' and 'desire and lust' links from the chain.

dn-029-p01.plain: Pleasant, painful and neutral feelings are all impermanent and conditioned, arising from causes, and bound to end, fade and cease.
dn-029-p01.core_idea: All feelings are impermanent and pass away

dn-031-p01.plain: The Buddha says he is now old, eighty, at the last stage of life. Like a worn-out cart held together by a rope, his body is kept going as if by a rope.
dn-031-p01.core_idea: Even the Buddha's body grows old and frail

dn-031-p02.plain: Ananda, be your own island and your own refuge, with no other. Let the teaching be your island and refuge, with no other.
dn-031-p02.core_idea: Be your own refuge, with the teaching

dn-032-p02.plain: The Buddha says he is very old with little life left; he will depart, having made himself a refuge. He urges the mendicants to be diligent, mindful and virtuous, and to guard their minds well.
dn-032-p02.core_idea: Be diligent, mindful and guard your mind

dn-033-p01.plain: The merit of a giver grows, and hatred does not build up in someone with self-control.
dn-033-p01.core_idea: Giving grows merit; self-control prevents hatred

dn-034-p01.plain: Enough, Ananda, don't grieve or lament. I taught that we must be parted from all we love. How could anything born and conditioned not wear away, even the Buddha's body?
dn-034-p01.core_idea: All that is born must pass, so don't grieve

dn-035-p01.plain: Conditions are impermanent; it is their nature to rise and fall. Having arisen, they cease, and their stilling is bliss.
dn-035-p01.core_idea: Everything rises and falls; stillness is bliss

dn-037-p01.plain: Conditions are so impermanent, so unstable, so unreliable; that alone is reason enough to become disenchanted with them, let go of desire and be free.
dn-037-p01.core_idea: Impermanence is reason enough to let go

dn-038-p01.plain: Someone caught up in sensual pleasures and bad qualities hears the noble ones' teaching, reflects on it and practises. Living apart from those pleasures, they find pleasure, then happiness greater still, like joy born of gladness.
dn-038-p01.core_idea: Leaving sensual pleasures brings deeper happiness

dn-041-p01.plain: Who knows what will happen to the living? We are heading towards future lives. We must be wise and wake up, do good and live the spiritual life, because no one born escapes death.
dn-041-p01.core_idea: Wake up and do good; death is certain

dn-044-p01.plain: The Buddha tells the lord of gods that jealousy and stinginess come from liking and disliking. Where there is liking and disliking, they exist; where there is none, they do not.
dn-044-p01.core_idea: Jealousy and stinginess grow from likes and dislikes

dn-044-p02.plain: If a kind of sadness makes bad qualities grow and good ones decline, don't cultivate it. If a kind of sadness makes bad qualities decline and good ones grow, cultivate it.
dn-044-p02.core_idea: Some sadness helps you grow; cultivate only that

dn-044-p03.plain: The world contains many different elements, and whatever one beings fix on, they cling to it stubbornly, insisting that it alone is true and everything else is worthless.
dn-044-p03.core_idea: People cling stubbornly to their own truth

dn-045-p02.plain: A meditator knows when restlessness and remorse are present in them and when they are not. They understand how these arise, how they are given up once arisen, and how they are kept from arising again.
dn-045-p02.core_idea: Notice restlessness and remorse, and how they end

dn-046-p02.plain: The noble truth of suffering's origin is craving, which leads to rebirth and seeks pleasure wherever it lands: craving for sensual pleasure, for existence and for non-existence. It arises wherever something in the world seems pleasant.
dn-046-p02.core_idea: Craving for the pleasant is the origin of suffering

judge.issue: Drops 'mixed up with relishing and greed' and where craving settles.

dn-046-p03.plain: Right effort means a mendicant works with enthusiasm and determination to prevent bad qualities arising, to give up those that have arisen, to bring good qualities into being, and to keep and fully develop those that have arisen.
dn-046-p03.core_idea: Right effort: prevent and drop bad, grow good

dn-048-p01.plain: Good ascetics and brahmins don't force what is unripe to ripen; they wait for it to ripen.
dn-048-p01.core_idea: Don't force what is unripe; wait

dn-054-p01.plain: They meditate giving up covetousness, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt, cleansing the mind of each, so it becomes kind to all beings, alert, settled and sure about what is good.
dn-054-p01.core_idea: Meditation cleanses the mind of the five hindrances

judge.issue: Compresses five hindrances; loses 'perceiving light, mindful and aware' detail.

dn-054-p02.plain: The Buddha tells Nigrodha his words were a foolish mistake. But because he recognises and confesses it, the Buddha accepts it; seeing a mistake for what it is, admitting it and resolving to restrain yourself is growth.
dn-054-p02.core_idea: Admitting a mistake and changing is growth

judge.issue: Softens 'foolish, stupid, and unskillful' to just 'foolish mistake'.

dn-061-p01.plain: The Buddha does not answer questions about the past that are false and pointless, or true but pointless. When a question is true, correct and beneficial, he knows the right time to answer.
dn-061-p01.core_idea: Answer only what is true and useful, when timely

dn-065-p01.plain: You don't get your work done because you think it's too cold, too hot, too late, too early, you're too hungry or too full. Dwelling on excuses, you earn nothing more and lose what you have.
dn-065-p01.core_idea: Excuses for not working cost you everything

dn-065-p02.plain: Some are just drinking companions, and some call you their dearest friend, but a true friend is one who stands by you when you need them.
dn-065-p02.core_idea: A friend in need is a true friend

dn-065-p03.plain: When the young neglect work saying it is too cold, too hot, too late, wealth slips past them. But one who treats heat and cold like blades of grass does his duties, and his happiness lasts.
dn-065-p03.core_idea: Ignore discomfort and do your work

dn-065-p04.plain: You can spot a flattering fake friend by four signs: they back you equally in doing bad and good, and praise you to your face while running you down behind your back.
dn-065-p04.core_idea: Flatterers praise you to your face, then betray you

dn-065-p05.plain: A good friend who stays the same in good times and bad shows four signs: they share their secrets, keep yours, don't abandon you in trouble, and would even give their life for you.
dn-065-p05.core_idea: A true friend stays loyal in good times and bad

dn-065-p06.plain: A sympathetic true friend shows four signs: they are not glad at your misfortune, they rejoice in your good fortune, they stop others criticising you and they encourage others to praise you.
dn-065-p06.core_idea: A true friend rejoices in your good fortune

dn-065-p07.plain: A friend who helps, one who stays the same in pleasure and pain, one who gives good advice and one who cares: a wise person recognises these four and looks after them like a mother her nursing child.
dn-065-p07.core_idea: Cherish true friends as a mother cherishes her child

dn-066-p01.plain: Those who win glory are wise, virtuous, gentle, well spoken, calm and agreeable; diligent, steady in trouble, consistent and intelligent; inclusive, friendly, generous, free of stinginess, and able to lead, teach and persuade.
dn-066-p01.core_idea: Virtue, diligence and generosity win honour

dn-067-p02.plain: Some ways of practice are painful now and painful later; some painful now but pleasant later; some pleasant now but painful later; and some pleasant now and pleasant later.
dn-067-p02.core_idea: Practices differ in present and future pain or pleasure

dn-068-p01.plain: I will speak at the right time, truthfully, gently, helpfully and with love, not at the wrong time, falsely, harshly, harmfully or out of hidden hatred.
dn-068-p01.core_idea: Speak timely, truthful, gentle, helpful and loving words

dn-068-p02.plain: Inspiration brings joy, and joy brings rapture. When the mind is full of rapture, the body calms; a calm body feels bliss, and a blissful mind becomes deeply absorbed in meditation.
dn-068-p02.core_idea: Joy leads step by step to deep meditation

dn-069-p01.plain: When someone has wronged you, you can let go of resentment by thinking: what can I possibly do?
dn-069-p01.core_idea: Let go of resentment: what can I do?

dn-069-p02.plain: People give gifts for many reasons: after insulting the recipient, out of fear, to repay or expect a gift, because giving is good, out of fairness, for reputation, or to adorn and equip the mind.
dn-069-p02.core_idea: People give for many different motives

judge.issue: 'Out of fairness' loosely renders 'I cook, they don't' obligation.

dn-071-p01.plain: Craving leads to seeking, seeking to gaining things, then judging, desire, attachment, ownership, stinginess and guarding possessions. From guarding come violence, quarrels, disputes, accusations, slander and lies.
dn-071-p01.core_idea: Craving leads step by step to violence and lies

dn-071-p02.plain: Reflecting wisely brings joy, then rapture, a calm body, bliss and deep meditation. A settled mind truly sees; seeing truly, you become disenchanted, desire fades, and you are freed.
dn-071-p02.core_idea: Wise reflection leads step by step to freedom

mn-002-p01.plain: Paying attention unwisely makes defilements arise and grow. Paying attention wisely keeps them from arising and gets rid of those already there.
mn-002-p01.core_idea: Wise attention prevents and removes mental defilements

mn-002-p02.plain: A mendicant who reflects wisely does not put up with sensual, hostile or cruel thoughts, or any bad quality, once it arises, but drops it and gets rid of it completely.
mn-002-p02.core_idea: Don't tolerate harmful thoughts; drive them out

mn-003-p01.plain: The Buddha recalls staying alone in eerie shrines on special nights to face fear. When a deer passed or leaves rustled, he wondered if fear was coming, then resolved to deal with fear as it came, staying as he was.
mn-003-p01.core_idea: Face fear as it comes, just as you are

judge.issue: Loses his self-questioning about always expecting fear to come.

mn-004-p01.plain: Someone who understands they have a flaw will make an effort to remove it, and die with a pure mind, free of greed, hate and delusion, just as a dirty bronze cup grows brighter when it is used and cleaned.
mn-004-p01.core_idea: Knowing your flaws lets you remove them

judge.issue: Drops enthusiasm and energy, and keeping the cup out of dirty places.

mn-005-p01.plain: A dirty cloth looks badly dyed whatever colour is used, while a clean cloth takes dye well. In the same way, a corrupted mind can expect a bad destiny, and an uncorrupted mind a good one.
mn-005-p01.core_idea: A pure mind, like clean cloth, leads to good

mn-005-p03.plain: For the pure in heart every day is holy, and their vows are fulfilled. Bathe here, brahmin, by sheltering all beings: if you don't lie, harm, steal or hoard, why go to holy Gaya? Any well will do.
mn-005-p03.core_idea: Purity of heart, not holy rivers, cleanses you

judge.issue: Drops 'faithful'; 'hoard' only loosely renders 'not stingy'.

mn-006-p01.plain: Others may cling tightly to their views and refuse to let go, but we will not cling to our views; we will let them go easily.
mn-006-p01.core_idea: Hold your views lightly and let them go

mn-006-p02.plain: The Buddha tells Cunda that even having the thought of good qualities is very helpful, let alone acting on them in body and speech.

mn-006-p03.plain: If you are stuck in mud yourself, you cannot pull out someone else who is stuck. Only if you are tamed, trained and at peace yourself can you help others become so.
mn-006-p03.core_idea: You can't rescue others while you're sinking

mn-006-p04.plain: Here are the roots of trees and empty huts. Meditate, Cunda! Don't be careless, or you will regret it later.
mn-006-p04.core_idea: Meditate now, so you won't regret it later

mn-011-p01.plain: The Buddha recalls sleeping in a burial ground with bones for a pillow while village louts spat, urinated and threw mud on him, yet he never had a bad thought about them. That was his equanimity.
mn-011-p01.core_idea: Equanimity holds no ill will even under abuse

mn-012-p01.plain: Sensual pleasures bring little satisfaction and much suffering. Even someone who sees this clearly can return to them until they find the rapture and bliss beyond sensual pleasure, or greater peace; then they do not return.
mn-012-p01.core_idea: Only a deeper joy frees you from sensual pleasures

mn-013-p01.plain: Suppose a mendicant asks others to correct them, but they are impatient and don't accept instruction respectfully. Then their companions think them not worth advising, and they lose their trust.
mn-013-p01.core_idea: Those who resist correction lose others' trust

judge.issue: 'Lose their trust' shifts 'doesn't gain their trust'.

mn-013-p02.plain: As a young person checks their face in a mirror and cleans away any dirt, a mendicant should check themselves. If bad qualities remain, they should work to drop them; if not, they should train joyfully day and night.
mn-013-p02.core_idea: Check yourself honestly, then keep improving

mn-014-p01.plain: Feeling leads to perception, perception to thinking, and thinking to mental proliferation. That runaway proliferation is where the judgments that trouble a person come from.
mn-014-p01.core_idea: Runaway thinking breeds the judgments that trouble us.

mn-015-p01.plain: Whatever a mendicant keeps thinking about becomes the way their heart leans. Dwell often on sensual thoughts and you drop renunciation, and the mind bends toward sensuality.
mn-015-p01.core_idea: What you dwell on shapes your heart.

mn-015-p02.plain: The Buddha recalls that when a sensual thought arose in meditation, he saw that it harms oneself, others and both, blocks wisdom and leads away from freedom. Seeing this, the thought faded, and he let all such thoughts go.
mn-015-p02.core_idea: Seeing a thought's harm makes it fall away.

mn-015-p03.plain: When a mendicant's focus stirs up thoughts of desire, hate or delusion, they should switch to a wholesome subject. The bad thoughts end and the mind settles, like a mason knocking out a large peg with a finer one.
mn-015-p03.core_idea: Replace unwholesome thoughts with wholesome ones.

mn-016-p01.plain: Others may criticise you kindly or harshly, truly or falsely, lovingly or with hidden hate. However it comes, the Buddha tells mendicants to keep their minds steady, speak no bad words, and spread love to that person and the world.
mn-016-p01.core_idea: Meet any criticism with steady, boundless love.

judge.issue: Compresses training formula; drops sympathy, no secret hate, limitless love.

mn-016-p02.plain: A caretaker of a sal grove cuts out crooked saplings and tends the straight ones, and the grove grows. Likewise, mendicants should drop the unwholesome and devote themselves to the wholesome, and they will grow in this teaching.
mn-016-p02.core_idea: Remove the unwholesome and tend the wholesome to grow.

mn-017-p01.plain: Even if bandits were sawing you limb from limb, anyone who felt hatred because of it would not be following the Buddha's teaching. Instead, keep the mind steady and spread love to them and to the whole world.
mn-017-p01.core_idea: Hold love even toward those who torture you.

mn-018-p01.plain: Asked whether people can feel anxiety over what isn't outwardly there, the Buddha says yes: when someone mourns what was once theirs or what they can't get, they grieve, wail and fall into confusion.
mn-018-p01.core_idea: Grieving what's lost or unattained creates anxiety.

mn-018-p02.plain: When others abuse you, don't become resentful and bitter; when they honour you, don't become elated. If they praise you, simply think that it's for something already understood long ago.
mn-018-p02.core_idea: Stay unmoved by both abuse and praise.

mn-020-p01.plain: There are two quests, noble and ignoble. The ignoble quest is when someone who will be reborn, age, sicken, die and grieve goes looking for things that are subject to all the same.
mn-020-p01.core_idea: Seeking perishable things while perishable is the ignoble quest.

mn-021-p01.plain: Before his awakening, the Buddha says, he too chased things that age, sicken and die, as he did himself. Then he asked why he didn't instead seek what is free of all that: extinguishment, the supreme sanctuary.
mn-021-p01.core_idea: Seek what is beyond aging and death.

mn-025-p01.plain: The spiritual life isn't lived for possessions, honour, popularity, or even for ethics, meditation or insight. Its goal, core and final end is an unshakable freedom of heart.
mn-025-p01.core_idea: Unshakable freedom of heart is the spiritual life's goal.

mn-026-p01.plain: A monk tells the Buddha how lucky he feels to live with such companions. He treats them kindly in deed, word and thought, and sets aside his own ideas for theirs; though different in body, they are one in mind.
mn-026-p01.core_idea: Kindness and yielding make companions one in mind.

mn-029-p01.plain: A person developed in body and mind feels pleasure without craving it and pain without wailing or falling apart. Neither pleasant nor painful feelings take over their mind.
mn-029-p01.core_idea: A developed mind is not seized by pleasure or pain.

judge.issue: Loses which development (body vs mind) handles pleasant vs painful feeling.

mn-033-p01.plain: A mendicant is content with robes for the body and almsfood for the belly, taking only these wherever they go, like a bird whose only burden is its wings. Living ethically, they feel a blameless inner happiness.
mn-033-p01.core_idea: Travel light, like a bird with only wings.

mn-033-p02.plain: Mendicants might think that having conscience and prudence is enough and the work is done. The Buddha warns them: while there is still more to do, don't lose sight of the goal.
mn-033-p02.core_idea: Don't settle early while more remains to do.

mn-034-p01.plain: We won't overeat. We'll eat thoughtfully, not for fun or looks, but only to keep the body going, avoid harm and support practice, ending old discomfort without creating new.
mn-034-p01.core_idea: Eat mindfully, only to sustain body and practice.

judge.issue: Drops 'means to keep going, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding'.

mn-035-p02.plain: Anyone, from any direction, can quench their thirst at a cool lotus pond. Likewise, anyone of any class who comes to the Buddha's teaching and develops love, compassion, rejoicing and equanimity finds inner peace, which is true ascetic practice.
mn-035-p02.core_idea: Inner peace is open to anyone, whatever their origin.

mn-036-p01.plain: Asked what the body must lose before it lies discarded like a senseless log, the answer is three things: vitality, warmth and consciousness.
mn-036-p01.core_idea: Without life, warmth and consciousness, the body is a log.

mn-037-p01.plain: Pleasant feeling is pleasant while it lasts and painful when it ends; painful feeling is the reverse. Neutral feeling is pleasant when you understand it and painful when you don't.
mn-037-p01.core_idea: Every feeling turns into its opposite when it passes.

mn-038-p01.plain: There are four ways of taking up practices: pleasant now with future pain, painful now with future pain, painful now with future pleasure, and pleasant now with future pleasure.
mn-038-p01.core_idea: Practices differ in present and future pleasure or pain.

mn-038-p02.plain: Beings generally wish that unpleasant things would shrink and pleasant things grow. But exactly the opposite happens to them.
mn-038-p02.core_idea: We wish for more pleasure, yet get the opposite.

mn-039-p01.plain: The Buddha asks quarrelling mendicants whether wounding each other with barbed words is treating each other kindly. They admit it isn't, and he warns that such behaviour will bring them lasting harm and suffering.
mn-039-p01.core_idea: Quarrelling with cutting words brings lasting harm.

judge.issue: Softens the rebuke: drops 'you futile men' and 'what do you know and see'.
