tagore-gitanjali-001-p14.plain: Invited to the world's festival, I have been blessed by all I saw and heard, and played my part as best I could. Now I ask God whether it is time to see God's face and greet God silently.
tagore-gitanjali-001-p14.core_idea: Having played my part, I am ready to meet God.

tagore-gitanjali-001-p15.plain: I am only waiting to give myself up to love at last. Others try to bind me with laws and blame me as careless, perhaps rightly; the busy have gone home angry, but I still wait for love.
tagore-gitanjali-001-p15.core_idea: Waiting, above all else, to surrender to love.

tagore-gitanjali-001-p16.plain: As clouds darken, the poet asks love why he is left waiting alone. In busy hours he is with the crowd, but on this lonely day he hopes only for God and cannot bear the rainy hours without God.
tagore-gitanjali-001-p16.core_idea: Longing for God on a dark, lonely day.

tagore-gitanjali-001-p17.plain: If God does not speak, the poet will fill his heart with God's silence and endure it, waiting patiently like the night. Morning will surely come, the darkness will lift, and God's voice will pour down in golden streams.
tagore-gitanjali-001-p17.core_idea: Wait patiently through silence; morning will come.

tagore-gitanjali-001-p18.plain: When the lotus bloomed, my mind was wandering and I missed it. A faint fragrance stirred a longing in me, but I did not know then that this perfect sweetness had already blossomed deep within my own heart.
tagore-gitanjali-001-p18.core_idea: What we long for already blooms within us.

fix.display_text:
On the day when the lotus bloomed, alas, my mind was straying, and I knew it not. My basket was empty and the flower remained unheeded.

Only now and again a sadness fell upon me, and I started up from my dream and felt a sweet trace of a strange fragrance in the south wind.

That vague sweetness made my heart ache with longing and it seemed to me that it was the eager breath of the summer seeking for its completion.

I knew not then that it was so near, that it was mine, and that this perfect sweetness had blossomed in the depth of my own heart.

tagore-gitanjali-001-p19.plain: I must set out in my boat; idle hours pass on the shore. Spring is over and I linger with faded flowers. Why stare into emptiness? Can you not feel the thrill of a song from the far shore?
tagore-gitanjali-001-p19.core_idea: Stop lingering; answer the call from the far shore.

tagore-gitanjali-001-p20.plain: When the day is done, the poet asks God to cover him with darkness as gently as God puts the earth to sleep, and to lift the worn traveller's shame and renew his life like a flower overnight.
tagore-gitanjali-001-p20.core_idea: Ask God for rest and renewal when you are spent.

tagore-gitanjali-001-p21.plain: When I am weary, let me sleep without struggling, trusting God. Let me not force my tired spirit into a poor act of worship. It is God who brings night to tired eyes so they wake with fresh gladness.
tagore-gitanjali-001-p21.core_idea: Rest trustingly; tiredness is renewed by sleep.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p01.plain: Where is the light? Light it with the fire of desire! Thunder rolls, wind screams, and the night is black as stone. Do not let the hours pass in darkness; light the lamp of love with your life.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p01.core_idea: Light the lamp of love with your own life.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p02.plain: My chains are stubborn, yet breaking them hurts. I want freedom but feel ashamed to hope for it. I know God is my true wealth and friend, yet I cling to tinsel and fear my prayer might be granted.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p02.core_idea: We long for freedom yet cling to what binds us.

judge.issue: Drops the shroud hated yet hugged, and the heavy debts, failures and secret shame.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p03.plain: The self I wall in with my name weeps inside this prison. I keep building the wall higher, proud of it and sealing every gap, and in its shadow I lose sight of who I truly am.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p03.core_idea: Building up our name hides our true being.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p04.plain: On my way to meet God, someone follows me that I cannot escape. He stirs up dust and shouts over my every word. He is my own little self, and I am ashamed to come to God's door with him.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p04.core_idea: The ego shadows us even on the way to God.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p05.plain: A prisoner says he wanted to outdo everyone in wealth and power, hoarded his king's money, and woke a prisoner in his own treasure-house. He forged his chain himself to hold the world captive, and it holds him.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p05.core_idea: The chains of greed and power we forge bind us.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p06.plain: Those who love me here hold me tight and never leave me alone. God's greater love keeps me free and stays unseen; even if I forget to pray or keep God in my heart, God's love waits for mine.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p06.core_idea: God's love sets us free and patiently waits.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p07.plain: The poet asks that only enough of himself remain to call God his all, feel God everywhere and offer love every moment, with God's love as his only bond, carrying out God's purpose in his life.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p07.core_idea: Keep only enough self to love God fully.

judge.issue: Drops the plea that enough remain 'whereby I may never hide thee'.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p08.plain: The poet prays to God, his Father, that his country awake into a heaven of freedom: minds fearless, knowledge free, people undivided, words true, effort reaching for perfection, and reason not lost in dead habit.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p08.core_idea: A prayer for a nation free, truthful and fearless.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p09.plain: A prayer to God: root out the poverty in my heart; give me strength to bear joy and sorrow lightly, serve with love, stand by the poor, rise above trifles, and surrender my strength to your will.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p09.core_idea: Ask God for strength to serve and surrender

tagore-gitanjali-002-p10.plain: I thought my journey was over and my strength used up, but God's will in me has no end: when old words fail, new songs rise from the heart, and where old paths vanish, new country opens.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p10.core_idea: When old paths end, new ones open

tagore-gitanjali-002-p11.plain: My heart says to God again and again that it wants only Him; every other desire is empty. Even hidden deep inside me, even in my rebellion against His love, the cry is the same.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p11.core_idea: Beneath every desire, the soul wants only God

tagore-gitanjali-002-p12.plain: A prayer to God: when my heart is dry, come as mercy; when life loses grace, come as song; when work drowns me out, come as peace; when desire blinds me, come with light and thunder.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p12.core_idea: Asking God to come in every hard state

judge.issue: Drops the stanza asking the king to break open the crouching beggarly heart.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p13.plain: My heart has been dry for days, my God. Send a storm if you wish, even a deadly one, but take away this silent, burning despair, and let your grace bend down to me like a mother's tearful look.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p13.core_idea: Rather a storm than silent despair

tagore-gitanjali-002-p14.plain: Before I was ready, God, you entered my heart unnoticed and marked passing moments with eternity. You did not scorn my childish play; the steps I heard then echo now among the stars.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p14.core_idea: God was present in ordinary moments all along

judge.issue: Drops finding the marked moments scattered in the dust of forgotten days.

tagore-gitanjali-002-p15.plain: My joy is to wait by the roadside, watching the seasons and the passing messengers, sure that the happy moment of seeing will come. Meanwhile I smile and sing alone, and the air fills with promise.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p15.core_idea: Waiting with hope is itself a joy

tagore-gitanjali-002-p16.plain: Have you not heard him coming? God comes always, every moment and every season. In April and in stormy July nights he comes; in sorrow after sorrow his steps press on my heart, and his touch makes my joy shine.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p16.core_idea: God is always coming, in joy and sorrow

tagore-gitanjali-002-p17.plain: All around us the morning was full of birdsong, flowers and golden light, but we hurried on without noticing. We did not sing, play, speak or smile; we only walked faster as time went by.
tagore-gitanjali-002-p17.core_idea: Hurrying, we miss the beauty around us

tagore-gitanjali-003-p01.plain: My companions mocked me and hurried on into the distance, crossing many lands. Their scorn did not move me; I let myself be lost, in a humiliation that was glad and a quiet delight.
tagore-gitanjali-003-p01.core_idea: Letting others race ahead, content to rest

judge.issue: Drops the speaker's salute to the 'heroic host of the interminable path'.

tagore-gitanjali-003-p02.plain: I forgot what I was travelling for and gave myself up to the shade and songs. When I woke, God was standing beside me, smiling. I had feared the road to him was long and hard.
tagore-gitanjali-003-p02.core_idea: God is found by resting, not striving

tagore-gitanjali-003-p03.plain: A beggar hoped for riches from the passing King, but the King asked him for a gift. He gave one grain of corn. That night he found one grain of gold, and wept that he had not given everything.
tagore-gitanjali-003-p03.core_idea: What we give to God returns as gold

tagore-gitanjali-003-p04.plain: God's gift to me is pain, a burden that hurts and shames me, yet I will carry it as an honour. Now I fear nothing: death is my companion and God's sword cuts my bonds.
tagore-gitanjali-003-p04.core_idea: Pain accepted as God's gift ends fear

tagore-gitanjali-003-p05.plain: When you asked my name, God, I was ashamed; what had I done to be remembered? Yet the memory that I once gave you water for your thirst will stay sweet in my heart, as I sit and think.
tagore-gitanjali-003-p05.core_idea: A small kindness to God is treasured

tagore-gitanjali-003-p06.plain: Your heart is weary and your eyes still sleepy. Have you not heard that the flower is blooming in glory among the thorns? Wake up, and do not let the time go to waste.
tagore-gitanjali-003-p06.core_idea: Wake up; do not waste the time

tagore-gitanjali-003-p07.plain: Let my last song hold every kind of joy: the joy of wild grass, of life and death dancing together, of the storm that wakes everything, of tears sitting quietly with pain, and of giving everything away without a word.
tagore-gitanjali-003-p07.core_idea: Joy holds life, death, storm and pain

tagore-gitanjali-003-p08.plain: On the shore of endless worlds, children meet and play. Storms rage, ships sink and death is everywhere, yet the children play on.
tagore-gitanjali-003-p08.core_idea: Children play on amid storm and death

tagore-gitanjali-003-p09.plain: As a parent giving a child toys, songs, sweets and kisses, I understand why the world is full of colour, music, honey and morning delight: it is all a giving of love, like mine to my child.
tagore-gitanjali-003-p09.core_idea: Loving a child reveals why the world is beautiful

fix.display_text:
When I bring to you coloured toys, my child, I understand why there is such a play of colours on clouds, on water, and why flowers are painted in tints—when I give coloured toys to you, my child.

When I sing to make you dance I truly know why there is music in leaves, and why waves send their chorus of voices to the heart of the listening earth—when I sing to make you dance.

When I bring sweet things to your greedy hands I know why there is honey in the cup of the flowers and why fruits are secretly filled with sweet juice—when I bring sweet things to your greedy hands.

When I kiss your face to make you smile, my darling, I surely understand what pleasure streams from the sky in morning light, and what delight that is that is which the summer breeze brings to my body—when I kiss you to make you smile.

judge.issue: Adds the explicit conclusion 'it is all a giving of love'.

tagore-gitanjali-003-p10.plain: God, you have given me friends I did not know and homes not my own, and made strangers into brothers. Yet I fear leaving familiar shelter, forgetting that the old lives in the new and that you are there too.
tagore-gitanjali-003-p10.core_idea: God is present in the new and unfamiliar

tagore-gitanjali-004-p01.plain: Through birth and death, wherever God leads me, He is my one constant companion, tying my heart to the unfamiliar with joy. Whoever knows Him finds no one a stranger and no door shut.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p01.core_idea: Knowing God, no one is a stranger

judge.issue: Drops the closing prayer never to lose the touch of the one in the many.

tagore-gitanjali-004-p02.plain: The same life that flows in my veins flows through the whole world, in grass, leaves, flowers, and the tides of birth and death. Its touch makes me glorious; the pulse of ages dances in my blood.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p02.core_idea: One life flows through me and the world

tagore-gitanjali-004-p03.plain: Can you not rejoice in this rhythm, even be tossed and broken in its fearful joy? Everything rushes on without looking back; seasons, colours and scents pour past in a joy that gives itself away and dies every moment.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p03.core_idea: Rejoice in life's endless rushing flow

tagore-gitanjali-004-p04.plain: Freedom for me is not in renouncing the world but in a thousand bonds of delight. I will not close my senses: what I see, hear and touch will carry God's delight, and my desires will ripen into love.

tagore-gitanjali-004-p05.plain: Day after day, O God, I will stand before you face to face: in quiet solitude, in the crowded, toiling world, and, when my work is done, alone and silent.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p05.core_idea: Standing before God in every moment

tagore-gitanjali-004-p06.plain: I keep God at a respectful distance instead of holding Him close as my own. He is a brother among my brothers, yet I ignore them and do not share with them, and I shrink from plunging into life.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p06.core_idea: Distance from people is distance from God

judge.issue: Drops that sharing with his brothers would be sharing his all with God.

tagore-gitanjali-004-p07.plain: When the gods sang that creation was perfect, one cried that a star was lost, and they have searched for her in grief ever since. But at night the stars whisper that the search is vain: perfection is unbroken.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p07.core_idea: Nothing is truly lost; perfection remains whole

tagore-gitanjali-004-p08.plain: If I do not meet God in this life, let me never forget that I have missed Him. Amid profits, rest and celebration, let me carry the ache of that loss, waking and dreaming.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p08.core_idea: Keep the longing for God alive

tagore-gitanjali-004-p09.plain: I used to grieve over idle days, but no time is lost, my God; you hold every moment, ripening seeds into fruit. I slept thinking all work had stopped, and woke to find my garden full of flowers.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p09.core_idea: No time is lost in God's hands

tagore-gitanjali-004-p10.plain: God has endless time and waits centuries to perfect one wild flower. We, poor in time, scramble and give it to anyone who demands it. Yet hurrying to God's gate at day's end, I find there is still time.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p10.core_idea: God's patience means there is still time

judge.issue: Drops that God's altar is left empty of offerings.

tagore-gitanjali-004-p11.plain: Mother, I will make you a necklace of my tears. Wealth and fame are yours to give or withhold, but my sorrow is truly mine, and when I offer it to you, you reward me with grace.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p11.core_idea: Sorrow offered to God becomes grace

tagore-gitanjali-004-p12.plain: The ache of separation fills the world and gives birth to countless shapes in the sky. This sorrow watches silently from star to star, sings in rainy darkness, and deepens into human love, longing, suffering and joy.
tagore-gitanjali-004-p12.core_idea: Longing of separation shapes the world

extension.text:
It is the pang of separation that spreads throughout the world and gives birth to shapes innumerable in the infinite sky.

It is this sorrow of separation that gazes in silence all nights from star to star and becomes lyric among rustling leaves in rainy darkness of July.
It is this overspreading pain that deepens into loves and desires, into sufferings and joy in human homes; and this it is that ever melts and flows in songs through my poet’s heart.

judge.issue: Drops that this sorrow flows in songs through the poet's heart.

tagore-gitanjali-005-p01.plain: Death, God's servant, has come to my door with God's call. My heart is afraid, yet I will welcome him and honour him; when he leaves, only my lonely self will remain as my last offering to God.

tagore-gitanjali-005-p02.plain: I search my small house for the one I lost and cannot find her. But God's house is infinite, where nothing vanishes. Plunge my emptied life into that fullness, so I may feel her lost touch in the whole universe.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p02.core_idea: In God, nothing loved is truly lost

tagore-gitanjali-005-p03.plain: When death knocks at your door, what will you give him? I will give him my whole life, all its sweetness and all its earnings; I will not let him leave empty-handed.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p03.core_idea: Meet death with a life fully lived

tagore-gitanjali-005-p04.plain: Death, you are life's final fulfilment; come and speak to me. I have lived all my joys and pains for you, and everything I am has flowed toward you. One look from you and my life is yours forever.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p04.core_idea: Death as the fulfilment of life

tagore-gitanjali-005-p05.plain: One day I will die and the world will go on. Thinking of that end, I see even the world's lowliest lives as precious. Let what I wanted pass; let me truly hold what I overlooked.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p05.core_idea: Mortality reveals the worth of overlooked things

tagore-gitanjali-005-p06.plain: I am leaving; say goodbye to me, my brothers. I give back my keys and claims and ask only for kind words. We were neighbours long, and I received more than I gave. Now I am ready.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p06.core_idea: Parting with gratitude, ready for death

tagore-gitanjali-005-p07.plain: Wish me well as I leave, friends; the dawn is bright and my path beautiful. I go with empty hands and a hopeful heart, dressed for a wedding, not a journey, and unafraid of the dangers.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p07.core_idea: Facing death as a joyful journey

tagore-gitanjali-005-p08.plain: I did not notice entering this life, yet the nameless mystery received me as my mother. Death will be that same unknown, already known; loving life, I will love death too, like a child moved to the other breast.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p08.core_idea: Loving life, I shall love death too

tagore-gitanjali-005-p09.plain: When I leave, let my parting word be that what I have seen is unsurpassed. I have tasted hidden sweetness and glimpsed and felt the formless One in this world of forms; if the end comes now, let it come.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p09.core_idea: A parting word of gratitude for life

tagore-gitanjali-005-p10.plain: I will honour God with the trophies of my defeat; I can never escape being conquered by Him. My pride will fall, my life will break its bonds in pain, my empty heart will sing, and stone will weep.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p10.core_idea: Defeat by God breaks pride open

judge.issue: Softens 'sob out in music' to 'sing'.

tagore-gitanjali-005-p11.plain: When I let go of the helm, God takes it; my struggle is useless. So, my heart, accept defeat and sit still gladly. My lamps keep blowing out, so this time I will wait in the dark for God.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p11.core_idea: Let go and let God steer

judge.issue: Drops 'what there is to do will be instantly done' and God's coming at his pleasure.

tagore-gitanjali-005-p12.plain: In one bow to you, my God, let all my senses, my mind, my songs and my whole life bend toward you, like a heavy rain-cloud, or homesick cranes flying back to their mountain home.
tagore-gitanjali-005-p12.core_idea: My whole life as one bow to God

judge.issue: Drops 'sea of silence' and 'eternal home' images.

tagore-sadhana-001-p01.plain: You can see a road as an obstacle between you and what you want, every step won by force. Or you can see it as the way to your goal, already part of it, giving you something with every step.
tagore-sadhana-001-p01.core_idea: The road is already part of the goal

tagore-sadhana-001-p02.plain: A person who does not feel kinship with the world lives as if in a prison of strange walls. One who meets the eternal spirit in everything is set free, finding the world's full meaning and harmony with all.
tagore-sadhana-001-p02.core_idea: Kinship with the world sets us free

tagore-sadhana-001-p03.plain: When people cut themselves off from nature and walk the tightrope of humanity alone, they must strain at every step to keep their balance, and when tired, they rail against Providence and secretly enjoy feeling unfairly treated.
tagore-sadhana-001-p03.core_idea: Cut off from nature, we strain and complain

judge.issue: Drops 'either a dance or a fall'.

tagore-sadhana-002-p01.plain: When a person's awareness reaches no further than their own human self, their deeper roots find no lasting soil, their spirit is always close to starving, and they replace real strength with rounds of stimulation.
tagore-sadhana-002-p01.core_idea: A narrow self swaps strength for stimulation

tagore-sadhana-002-p02.plain: Human greatness lies not in getting and achieving but in a soul that embraces all; callous habit and frantic work kill it. We are lovers, not slaves; love unites us with the Spirit, and pushing past others cuts us off.
tagore-sadhana-002-p02.core_idea: Our greatness and freedom lie in love

judge.issue: Drops love as perfect comprehension and Spirit as breath of the soul.

tagore-sadhana-002-p03.plain: Someone set on piling up riches, with an ego always swelling, cannot pass into the spiritual world of harmony; he stays shut inside the narrow walls of what he owns.
tagore-sadhana-002-p03.core_idea: Greed walls us off from the spirit

tagore-sadhana-002-p04.plain: Someone bent on enlarging himself treats everything else as unreal. To see the reality of all, we must be free of personal desire, ready to share others' burdens. A larger life means gaining by giving and growing in unity.
tagore-sadhana-002-p04.core_idea: Gain a larger life by giving

judge.issue: Loses framing of discipline preparing for social duties.

tagore-sadhana-003-p01.plain: Our selfish desires and egoistic impulses cloud our view of the soul, because they show only our narrow self. When we are aware of our soul, we see the inner being beyond the ego, close to the All.

tagore-sadhana-003-p02.plain: Understanding finds something of ourselves in another, which gladdens us, but only partly. Love is complete: difference vanishes and the soul reaches into the infinite. So love is the highest bliss, showing we are one with the All.
tagore-sadhana-003-p02.core_idea: Love is complete union with the All

tagore-sadhana-003-p03.plain: It is ordinary, yet wonderful, that the joys and sorrows of those we love become ours, even more than ours. In them we have grown larger and touched the truth that holds the whole universe.

tagore-sadhana-003-p04.plain: We must know for certain that we are spirit, by mastering self and rising above pride, greed and fear; loss and death cannot touch the soul. Like a chick breaking its shell, we must burst the dead shell of ego.
tagore-sadhana-003-p04.core_idea: Break the shell of ego to be free

judge.issue: Compresses chick-and-shell image; loses shell never being part of its life.

tagore-sadhana-003-p05.plain: The Buddha tells Simha that he condemns only actions leading to evil, and preaches the ending only of pride, lust, evil thought and ignorance, never of forgiveness, love, charity and truth.
tagore-sadhana-003-p05.core_idea: The Buddha extinguishes vice, not love

tagore-sadhana-004-p01.plain: Until a person truly knows their soul, their poverty is bottomless, their wants endless, and the world a shifting illusion. Once the soul is realised, everything finds its place around a centre, and life becomes harmonious.
tagore-sadhana-004-p01.core_idea: Knowing the soul gives life a centre

fix.display_text: Man's poverty is abysmal, his wants are endless till he becomes truly conscious of his soul. Till then, the world to him is in a state of continual flux--a phantasm that is and is not. For a man who has realised his soul there is a determinate centre of the universe around which all else can find its proper place, and from thence only can he draw and enjoy the blessedness of a harmonious life.

tagore-sadhana-004-p02.plain: The early earth was scattered heat until a central force drew it into a beautiful whole. So with the soul: driven by blind passions we give nothing truly, but centred by self-restraint, our impressions become wisdom and impulses love.
tagore-sadhana-004-p02.core_idea: A centred soul turns impulse into love

judge.issue: Drops petty details revealing infinite purpose and inner harmony.

tagore-sadhana-004-p03.plain: We are miserable because we live as creatures of a narrow, blind self, loud with discord. Discontent, regret for the past and worry about the future trouble us because we have not found our souls.
tagore-sadhana-004-p03.core_idea: Misery comes from living only as self

judge.issue: Drops 'self-revealing spirit has not been manifest within us'.

tagore-sadhana-004-p04.plain: In sin, we crave pleasures only because passion makes them look desirable, and want things only because greed makes them look great. These distortions break our harmony and leave us without true values, pulled about by competing claims.
tagore-sadhana-004-p04.core_idea: Passion and greed distort what we value

tagore-sadhana-004-p05.plain: People long to express themselves fully, and that leads them to chase wealth and power. But piling things up is not fulfilment; it is the inner light that reveals who we are, not outward things.

tagore-sadhana-004-p06.plain: Our real misery is that we have not fully emerged; we are hidden from ourselves, lost in our own desires, unable to feel beyond our surroundings, our greater self blotted out.
tagore-sadhana-004-p06.core_idea: Lost in desire, our greater self is hidden

tagore-sadhana-005-p01.plain: A river has banks, but it is not just banks; the banks push its water forward. A towing rope binds a boat, yet it also pulls the boat ahead. Limits are not the whole meaning.

tagore-sadhana-005-p02.plain: What is remarkable is not that the world has obstacles and suffering, but that it has law and order, beauty and joy, goodness and love.
tagore-sadhana-005-p02.core_idea: The wonder is goodness, not suffering

tagore-sadhana-005-p03.plain: Pain is the feeling of our limits; it is not a permanent part of life or an end in itself, as joy is. To meet pain is to learn that it has no place in what truly lasts.

tagore-sadhana-005-p04.plain: Life as a whole does not take death seriously; it keeps playing, building and loving. Death frightens us only when isolated, like cloth seen under a microscope as holes. Death is not the final reality and does not stain existence.
tagore-sadhana-005-p04.core_idea: Death does not darken life as a whole

judge.issue: Drops sky-and-bird-wing image; death not blackening existence compressed.

tagore-sadhana-005-p05.plain: A child learning to walk fails over and over, which would look cruel if we watched only briefly. But a joy drives the child on, and it thinks less of its falls than of its moments of balance.
tagore-sadhana-005-p05.core_idea: Joy carries us through repeated failure

tagore-sadhana-005-p06.plain: Viewed narrowly, our failures loom large, but life leads us to a wider view. Within us is a hope, a faith in the infinite, that accepts no limitation as permanent, claims oneness with God, and keeps coming true.
tagore-sadhana-005-p06.core_idea: Hope in the infinite outruns our failures

tagore-sadhana-005-p07.plain: If existence were evil, no philosopher would be needed to prove it. Arguing it is like accusing a man of suicide while he stands alive in front of you; existence itself shows it is not evil.
tagore-sadhana-005-p07.core_idea: Existence itself proves it is not evil

tagore-sadhana-006-p01.plain: For one who lives for an idea or the good of all, pain matters less. Seen from goodness, pleasure may be shunned, pain sought, death welcomed, as martyrs show. As sea water weighs nothing when you dive in, on the moral plane pain lightens, giving near-superhuman patience under crushing persecution.

fix.display_text: To the man who lives for an idea, for his country, for the good of humanity, life has an extensive meaning, and to that extent pain becomes less important to him. To live the life of goodness is to live the life of all. Pleasure is for one's own self, but goodness is concerned with the happiness of all humanity and for all time. From the point of view of the good, pleasure and pain appear in a different meaning; so much so, that pleasure may be shunned, and pain be courted in its place, and death itself be made welcome as giving a higher value to life. From these higher standpoints of a man's life, the standpoints of the good, pleasure and pain lose their absolute value. Martyrs prove it in history, and we prove it every day in our life in our little martyrdoms. When we take a pitcherful of water from the sea it has its weight, but when we take a dip into the sea itself a thousand pitchersful of water flow above our head, and we do not feel their weight. We have to carry the pitcher of self with our strength; and so, while on the plane of selfishness pleasure and pain have their full weight, on the moral plane they are so much lightened that the man who has reached it appears to us almost superhuman in his patience under crushing trials, and his forbearance in the face of malignant persecution.

tagore-sadhana-006-p01.plain_v1: For those who live for others or an ideal, pain matters less; pleasure serves oneself, goodness serves all. A pitcher of seawater is heavy, yet in the sea you feel no weight: living for self makes pleasure and pain heavy.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the hard saying: pain courted, death welcomed, martyrs' patience under persecution.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the main point: on the moral plane pain lightens, as martyrs show.

tagore-sadhana-006-p02.plain: A strong imagination is closer to truth, and a strong individuality widens toward the universal. A personality's greatness lies in its universal content, just as a lake's depth is measured by its water, not the size of its hollow.
tagore-sadhana-006-p02.core_idea: Greatness lies in content, not size

tagore-sadhana-006-p03.plain: When my boat's mast stuck under a bridge, neither mast, bridge nor river gave way. That is exactly why I can rely on them. Things are what they are; we can know them because our wishes are not their law.
tagore-sadhana-006-p03.core_idea: Our wishes are not the world's law

tagore-sadhana-007-p01.plain: When the individual in us resists the universal, we shrink and suffer; success becomes failure and fulfilled desire leaves us poorer. Seeking special privilege, we live behind barricades and complain of unhappiness, though the universal spirit waits to give joy.
tagore-sadhana-007-p01.core_idea: Seeking special privilege makes us miserable

judge.issue: Drops that our individual spirit refuses the offered happiness.

tagore-sadhana-007-p02.plain: Life's key lesson is not that pain exists, but that we can use it well and even turn it into joy. No one would give up the right to suffer, for it is the right to be human.
tagore-sadhana-007-p02.core_idea: We can transform pain into joy

tagore-sadhana-007-p03.plain: A poor mother was hurt when a rich relative offered to take her son, for a mother's trouble is hers by right of love. Freedom is not being spared trouble, but taking it on and making it part of joy.
tagore-sadhana-007-p03.core_idea: Freedom is taking on trouble, not escaping it

tagore-sadhana-007-p04.plain: Ignorance makes us think the self is complete, so we live for it and are disappointed, like clutching road dust to reach a destination. The self passes on; living for its pleasure is a fire without bread, burning itself out.
tagore-sadhana-007-p04.core_idea: Living for the self alone ends in emptiness

judge.issue: Compresses; loses the thread-in-the-loom image of self passing on.

tagore-sadhana-007-p05.plain: We become free when we reach our truest nature, as an artist is freed from imitation and the need for applause by finding their ideal. Religion's role is not to destroy our nature but to fulfil it.
tagore-sadhana-007-p05.core_idea: Religion should fulfil our nature, not destroy it

tagore-sadhana-007-p06.plain: A seed is free when it fulfils its nature by becoming a tree; failing to do so is its prison. The sacrifice that brings fulfilment is not death but throwing off the bonds that hold us back.
tagore-sadhana-007-p06.core_idea: Freedom is fulfilling one's true nature

tagore-sadhana-008-p01.plain: A lamp clings to its oil, separate and miserly, but once lit it connects with everything and gladly spends its oil on the flame. Our self is like that lamp: hoarding keeps it dark; lit, it gives everything.
tagore-sadhana-008-p01.core_idea: The self, like a lamp, shines by giving

extension.text: The lamp contains its oil, which it holds securely in its close grasp and guards from the least loss. Thus is it separate from all other objects around it and is miserly. But when lighted it finds its meaning at once; its relation with all things far and near is established, and it freely sacrifices its fund of oil to feed the flame. Such a lamp is our self. So long as it hoards its possessions it keeps itself dark, its conduct contradicts its true purpose. When it finds illumination it forgets itself in a moment, holds the light high, and serves it with everything it has; for therein is its revelation.

tagore-sadhana-008-p02.plain: Love is its own end. Everything else makes us ask why and want a reason, but when we say we love, there is no room for why; love is its own final answer.

tagore-sadhana-008-p03.plain: A selfish person gives only under compulsion, like tearing unripe fruit from a branch. One who loves gives with joy, as a tree lets go of ripe fruit. Love loosens our grip on possessions, and giving them away fulfils us.

tagore-sadhana-008-p04.plain: The Gita says we must act, for action shows our nature, but only free action shows it fully; work driven by want or fear hides it. Like a mother serving her children, true freedom is freedom in action, through love.
tagore-sadhana-008-p04.core_idea: True freedom is acting out of love

tagore-sadhana-008-p05.plain: Repulsion only separates. Love both separates and unites, but the separation only seems real and the union is the final truth, as when a father tosses his child up: it looks like letting go, but is the opposite.
tagore-sadhana-008-p05.core_idea: In love, separation only seems real

tagore-sadhana-008-p06.plain: Work done only out of necessity is makeshift, abandoned once the need passes. Work that comes from joy takes on something immortal, because the immortal in us gives it permanence.

tagore-sadhana-008-p07.plain: To live, the self must keep changing and growing, dying and living at once. Refusing that change, fixing the self in place and treating its limits as final, is really choosing death.
tagore-sadhana-008-p07.core_idea: Refusing to change is a kind of death

tagore-sadhana-009-p01.plain: A tyrant crushes his slaves' will because his self-interest is not free and cannot bear freedom in others; he actually depends on them. A lover needs two free wills, for love is fulfilled in harmony between freedom and freedom.

tagore-sadhana-009-p02.plain: The self must be born again every moment, breaking through the illusions that crust it over, make it seem old and weigh it down with death.

tagore-sadhana-009-p03.plain: Our life, like a river, meets its banks not to be shut in but to discover again its endless opening to the sea. Like a poem keeping its metre, its limits express an inner freedom rather than silence it.

tagore-sadhana-009-p04.plain: It is said that the unrighteous prosper and defeat their enemies for a while, but in the end are cut off at the root. To grow into true greatness, our roots must reach deep into the universal.
tagore-sadhana-009-p04.core_idea: Greatness needs roots in the universal

tagore-sadhana-009-p05.plain: A child's play would be a horror if he could not return to his mother, and our pride in being someone will curse us if we cannot give it up in love.
tagore-sadhana-009-p05.core_idea: Pride must be surrendered in love

tagore-sadhana-010-p01.plain: Literature follows grammar yet is pure joy and freedom. A poem's laws are its wings, carrying it to freedom, not weighing it down. Law is the first step to freedom, and beauty, built on law, unites limit and liberty.
tagore-sadhana-010-p01.core_idea: Law is the first step to freedom

tagore-sadhana-010-p02.plain: Formless joy has to create and take shape: the singer's joy becomes a song, the poet's a poem. As creators, people keep making forms, and these flow from their overflowing joy.

tagore-sadhana-010-p03.plain: Our individual soul is separate from the supreme soul through the fullness of love, not estrangement. So falsehood, suffering and evil are not fixed: the soul can defy and overcome them, and turn them into new power and beauty.
tagore-sadhana-010-p03.core_idea: The soul can transform evil into beauty

tagore-sadhana-010-p04.plain: The soul travels from law to love, discipline to freedom, morality to spirit. The Buddha taught self-restraint and moral discipline, a full acceptance of law; but law is not the end, and mastering it lets us go beyond it.
tagore-sadhana-010-p04.core_idea: Master the law to go beyond it

tagore-sadhana-010-p05.plain: Lack of love is a kind of numbness, since love is consciousness made perfect. We fail to understand because we do not love. Love is not just a feeling; it is truth, the joy at the root of all creation.
tagore-sadhana-010-p05.core_idea: We do not understand because we do not love

tagore-sadhana-010-p06.plain: Love gives endlessly, but its gifts matter most when they lead us to the giver, and that needs love in us. Without love we value gifts only for their passing use; with love, even a small token has lasting worth.
tagore-sadhana-010-p06.core_idea: With love, a token outlasts any use

judge.issue: Drops that utility becomes a burden once the want is met.

tagore-sadhana-011-p01.plain: How do we receive this world, a perfect gift of joy? We rush to exploit it for power and riches. Using it only, we cheapen it and miss its truth, like a greedy child eating pages of a precious book.
tagore-sadhana-011-p01.core_idea: Using the world only, we miss its worth

judge.issue: Drops receiving the world in the heart among deathless things.

tagore-sadhana-011-p02.plain: People are useful to each other, but each is also a spirit, known truly only through love. Valued by market worth, a person is easily wronged. Seen as spirit, they are our own: cruelty to them is cruelty to ourselves.
tagore-sadhana-011-p02.core_idea: Seen as spirit, others are our own

judge.issue: Drops that exploiting others gains money at the cost of truth.

tagore-sadhana-011-p03.plain: Our desires limit our growth and give rise to sin, which separates us from God. Sin is not a single act but an attitude: that our goal is finite, our self the final truth, and we are not all one.
tagore-sadhana-011-p03.core_idea: Sin is believing we are separate

tagore-sadhana-011-p04.plain: A civilisation should be judged not by the power it has built, but by how far its laws and institutions express love of humanity. Its first and last test: does it see people more as spirits than machines?
tagore-sadhana-011-p04.core_idea: Judge a civilisation by its love of humanity

tagore-sadhana-011-p05.plain: Seen through our desires, the world looks small. It meets our needs, but our bond with it goes deeper: loving life is wishing to stay connected with it. That bond is love, with threads reaching from earth to stars.
tagore-sadhana-011-p05.core_idea: Our bond with the world is love

tagore-sadhana-011-p06.plain: The spirit finds its larger self in the whole world and knows it is immortal. Walled in by self it dies again and again, but one with all it cannot die. Feeling the world's soul within, a person is free.
tagore-sadhana-011-p06.core_idea: United with all, the spirit is free

tagore-sadhana-011-p07.plain: Only love is both movement and rest. The heart keeps moving until it finds love, then rests; yet that rest is intense activity, where perfect stillness and endless energy meet.
tagore-sadhana-011-p07.core_idea: Love is motion and rest at once

tagore-sadhana-011-p08.plain: In love, loss and gain are reconciled; giving counts as gaining. In creation, which is God's great self-giving, the lover keeps giving himself up to find himself in love. Love joins letting go and receiving into one.

tagore-sadhana-011-p09.plain: Hunger makes demands, but it is not the last word for a human being. Some have defied it to show the soul is not ruled by want or pain, and to live humanly we all resist it daily.
tagore-sadhana-011-p09.core_idea: Need is not the last word

tagore-sadhana-011-p10.plain: What finally moves us is joy, not compulsion. Joy is everywhere: in grass, sky, spring and winter, in the body, in living, learning and fighting evil. It is surplus, unnecessary, often defying the demands of necessity.

fix.display_text: Compulsion is not indeed the final appeal to man, but joy is. And joy is everywhere; it is in the earth's green covering of grass; in the blue serenity of the sky; in the reckless exuberance of spring; in the severe abstinence of grey winter; in the living flesh that animates our bodily frame; in the perfect poise of the human figure, noble and upright; in living; in the exercise of all our powers; in the acquisition of knowledge; in fighting evils; in dying for gains we never can share. Joy is there everywhere; it is superfluous, unnecessary; nay, it very often contradicts the most peremptory behests of necessity.

judge.issue: Drops 'dying for gains we never can share'.

tagore-sadhana-012-p01.plain: Only those who know that joy expresses itself through law can go beyond law. The bonds remain, but become the very shape of freedom. A freed soul gladly accepts bonds, feeling in each the infinite energy that delights in creating.
tagore-sadhana-012-p01.core_idea: For the free, bonds become freedom

tagore-sadhana-012-p02.plain: Without bonds, in reckless licence, the soul is not free but hurt and cut off from the infinite. Fallen into temptation, it cries like a child dropped from its mother's arms, begging God to bind it in His law.
tagore-sadhana-012-p02.core_idea: Without bonds, the soul loses its freedom

judge.issue: Compresses the soul's prayer; loses plea for protection from sin's laxity.

tagore-sadhana-012-p03.plain: Freedom is not in vagueness; obscurity is the worst bondage. Seeds sprout and ideas seek form to escape it, and the soul keeps creating new kinds of action, even unneeded ones, because it wants to see and realise itself.
tagore-sadhana-012-p03.core_idea: The soul seeks freedom through action

tagore-sadhana-012-p04.plain: When people turn a jungle into a garden or bring order to society, the beauty and goodness they free outside are their own soul's, which cannot otherwise be free within. The more they free in action, the greater they become.
tagore-sadhana-012-p04.core_idea: Freeing good outside frees the soul within

tagore-sadhana-012-p05.plain: Those who have realised the soul never lament life's sorrow or the bondage of work. They cling to life until the fruit is ripe, express themselves fully in work, and walk upright through joys and sorrows, undaunted by pain.
tagore-sadhana-012-p05.core_idea: The realised hold fast to life

tagore-sadhana-012-p06.plain: No creature works as hard as humans, building and tearing down, making laws, thinking, suffering, even taking on new troubles willingly. We have found that we are greater than our present, and that standing still destroys life's true purpose.
tagore-sadhana-012-p06.core_idea: We are greater than our present

fix.display_text: No creature has to work so hard as man; he has been impelled to contrive for himself a vast field of action in society; and in this field he is for ever building up and pulling down, making and unmaking laws, piling up heaps of material, and incessantly thinking, seeking and suffering. In this field he has fought his mightiest battles, gained continual new life, made death glorious, and, far from evading troubles, has willingly and continually taken up the burden of fresh trouble. He has discovered the truth that he is not complete in the cage of his immediate surroundings, that he is greater than his present, and that while to stand still in one place may be comforting, the arrest of life destroys his true function and the real purpose of his existence.

judge.issue: Drops mightiest battles and 'made death glorious'.

tagore-sadhana-012-p07.plain: We gain the joy of freedom only by fully submitting to truth, like a harp string. Only when tightly strung does it make music and find freedom; loosening it would not free it, only tuning it to true pitch.
tagore-sadhana-012-p07.core_idea: Like a tuned string, bonds make music

tagore-sadhana-013-p01.plain: Whoever tries to reach God by fleeing the world, where does he expect to meet Him? Flight leads only to nothing; the coward finds Him nowhere. We must dare to say we are reaching God right here, right now.
tagore-sadhana-013-p01.core_idea: Meet God here and now, not by fleeing

tagore-sadhana-013-p02.plain: We need holidays because we find no joy in work. A river's joy is in flowing, a fire's in blazing, a flower's in its scent. Work overwhelms us because we do not give ourselves to it fully and joyfully.
tagore-sadhana-013-p02.core_idea: Give yourself fully to work to find joy

tagore-sadhana-013-p03.plain: A prayer to God: give us the strength to love our whole life, its joys and sorrows, gains and losses, to see and hear your universe fully and work in it vigorously, to live fully, taking and giving bravely.
tagore-sadhana-013-p03.core_idea: Pray for strength to love all of life

tagore-sadhana-013-p04.plain: Things that give us no joy are burdens to shed, tools that weigh on us once used, or passers-by soon forgotten. Something is fully our own only when it is a joy to us.
tagore-sadhana-013-p04.core_idea: Only what brings joy is truly ours

tagore-sadhana-013-p05.plain: Truth is everywhere, so everything can be known. Beauty is everywhere, so everything can give us joy.

tagore-sadhana-014-p01.plain: Our sense of truth shows us the law in creation; our sense of beauty shows us its harmony. Knowing nature's laws gives us power; knowing the laws of our moral nature gives us mastery over ourselves and freedom.
tagore-sadhana-014-p01.core_idea: Knowing our moral law makes us free

tagore-sadhana-014-p02.plain: Alone in the silent night I heard the eternal singer. Falling asleep, I thought that even in sleep life's dance goes on in my body, heart and blood keeping time with the stars, every atom vibrating to the master's touch.
tagore-sadhana-014-p02.core_idea: Life's dance continues even in sleep

tagore-sadhana-014-p03.plain: When the soul longs for God, it does not want to add one more valuable thing to its belongings; endless adding is wearisome. Seeking God, the soul seeks its final escape from this endless gathering and heaping.
tagore-sadhana-014-p03.core_idea: Seeking God is escape from endless getting

tagore-sadhana-014-p04.plain: See everything in the universe as wrapped in God. Enjoy what He gives you, and do not let greed for wealth that is not yours take hold of your mind.
tagore-sadhana-014-p04.core_idea: Enjoy God's gifts; do not covet

tagore-sadhana-014-p05.plain: We do not have to buy morning light from a shop; we open our eyes and it is there. In the same way, we only need to give ourselves up to find that Brahma is everywhere.
tagore-sadhana-014-p05.core_idea: Brahma is everywhere, like morning light

tagore-sadhana-014-p06.plain: The Upanishads say: be lost in Brahma like an arrow buried in its target. Knowing Brahma surrounds us is not mere concentration but the aim of our whole life; in every act let us feel the infinite energy and rejoice.
tagore-sadhana-014-p06.core_idea: Live wholly conscious of the infinite

judge.issue: Drops that none could live without the all-pervading joy filling the sky.

tagore-sadhana-014-p07.plain: In deep love, having and not having always go together. A Vaishnava lover tells the beloved: I seem to have gazed at your face since birth, yet my eyes still hunger; held you for ages, yet am not satisfied.
tagore-sadhana-014-p07.core_idea: Deep love is never fully satisfied

tagore-sadhana-014-p08.plain: Our wish for wealth is not for a set sum but for something unlimited, and even fleeting pleasures are brief touches of the eternal. Our tragedy is trying to reach the infinite by endlessly adding rungs to a finite ladder.
tagore-sadhana-014-p08.core_idea: We cannot reach the infinite by adding more

tagore-sadhana-014-p09.plain: Renunciation is the soul's deepest truth. Saying it does not want something because it is above it, the soul speaks its highest truth, like a girl who outgrows her doll and throws it away. Bondage to lesser things is misery.
tagore-sadhana-014-p09.core_idea: We are greater than what we own

judge.issue: Drops that possession itself shows we are greater than things.

tagore-sadhana-015-p01.plain: A flying bird feels with every wingbeat that the sky is boundless, and that is its joy. A cage meets its needs but no more, and it cannot rejoice. It is glad only having far more than it needs.
tagore-sadhana-015-p01.core_idea: Joy needs more than the necessary

tagore-sadhana-015-p02.plain: Lasting happiness comes not from getting but from giving ourselves to something greater: country, humanity, God. Until an idea claims our all, life is mean. The great prophets offer such ideas, and in giving we find joy and freedom.
tagore-sadhana-015-p02.core_idea: Happiness lies in giving ourselves to something greater

fix.display_text: Man's abiding happiness is not in getting anything but in giving himself up to what is greater than himself, to ideas which are larger than his individual life, the idea of his country, of humanity, of God. They make it easier for him to part with all that he has, not excepting his life. His existence is miserable and sordid till he finds some great idea which can truly claim his all, which can release him from all attachment to his belongings. Buddha and Jesus, and all our great prophets, represent such great ideas. They hold before us opportunities for surrendering our all. When they bring forth their divine alms-bowl we feel we cannot help giving, and we find that in giving is our truest joy and liberation, for it is uniting ourselves to that extent with the infinite.

judge.issue: Drops parting with all 'not excepting his life'; prophets' alms-bowl.

tagore-sadhana-015-p03.plain: A human being is not finished but still becoming. What we are is small; stopping there forever would be hell. What we are yet to be is infinite: our heaven. Our present grasps; our becoming hungers for more.
tagore-sadhana-015-p03.core_idea: We are not finished; we are becoming

judge.issue: Loses that becoming hungers for what can never be lost.

tagore-sadhana-015-p04.plain: The rushing stream sings that it will become the sea; this is truth, not pride. It serves fields and towns along its way but stays separate; it can never become a forest or town. But it becomes the sea.
tagore-sadhana-015-p04.core_idea: The river's destiny is the sea

tagore-sadhana-015-p05.plain: A poem delights when the reader grasps the idea running through it; without that, endless images weary. The soul's progress is the same: grasp its infinite idea and every movement has meaning; lose it, and existence seems aimless and monstrous.
tagore-sadhana-015-p05.core_idea: Life has meaning when seen as a whole

tagore-sadhana-015-p06.plain: Words and the mind fall back, unable to reach Brahma, but whoever knows Him through His joy is free of all fear.
tagore-sadhana-015-p06.core_idea: Knowing Brahma's joy frees us from fear

tagore-sadhana-015-p07.plain: The intellect keeps us apart from what we know, but love knows by becoming one with it. This knowing is immediate and beyond doubt, like knowing ourselves, only more so.

tagore-sadhana-016-p01.plain: We feel we have not reached our goal; however hard we work, we never arrive. Like a child bored with its dolls, the heart keeps saying: not this, not this. But what is the other? Where is the farther shore?
tagore-sadhana-016-p01.core_idea: The heart keeps longing for something beyond

tagore-sadhana-016-p02.plain: My self toils for a home it calls its own, and suffers until it calls that home God's. Grasping what belongs to all, it hurts and is hurt. Once it calls its work God's, nothing changes, yet it crosses over.
tagore-sadhana-016-p02.core_idea: Offer your work to God and be carried across

judge.issue: Drops the ferryman cry and image of crossing within old walls.

tagore-sadhana-016-p03.plain: Where can I meet God except in my home made His and my work turned into His? Leaving home or work, I will not find Him. God lives in me and I in Him; apart, both are nothing.
tagore-sadhana-016-p03.core_idea: Meet God in your own home and work

tagore-stray-birds-001-p01.plain: The earth's tears are what keep her smiles blooming.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p02.plain: If you weep over missing the sun, you will also miss seeing the stars.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p02.core_idea: Grieving what's gone can blind you to what's here

tagore-stray-birds-001-p03.plain: We once dreamed we were strangers, and woke to find we were dear to each other.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p03.core_idea: We are closer than we think

tagore-stray-birds-001-p04.plain: The sorrow in my heart grows quiet and peaceful, like evening settling among still trees.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p05.plain: Do not place your love on a cliff edge just because it is high.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p05.core_idea: Do not love something for its height

tagore-stray-birds-001-p06.plain: You cannot see what you really are; what you see is only your shadow.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p06.core_idea: Our true self is unseen by us

tagore-stray-birds-001-p07.plain: I cannot pick the best; the best picks me.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p08.plain: People who carry their lamp behind them cast their own shadows ahead of them.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p08.core_idea: Light behind us darkens the path ahead

tagore-stray-birds-001-p09.plain: Life is the constant surprise that I exist at all.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p09.core_idea: Existing at all is a constant wonder

tagore-stray-birds-001-p10.plain: Rest belongs to work the way eyelids belong to eyes.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p11.plain: A human being is born a child, and our power is the power to grow.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p12.plain: Beauty, find yourself in love, not in your mirror's flattery.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p12.core_idea: Beauty is found in love, not vanity

tagore-stray-birds-001-p13.plain: Life gains its wealth from what the world asks of it, and its worth from what love asks of it.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p13.core_idea: Love, not the world, gives life worth

tagore-stray-birds-001-p14.plain: A dried-up riverbed gets no thanks for the water it once carried.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p15.plain: The bird wishes to be a cloud, and the cloud wishes to be a bird.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p15.core_idea: Everyone longs to be something else

tagore-stray-birds-001-p16.plain: The waterfall sings that it finds its song when it finds its freedom.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p17.plain: Do not blame the food when you are the one without appetite.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p17.core_idea: The fault may lie in us

tagore-stray-birds-001-p18.plain: You smiled and talked to me about nothing, and I felt this was what I had long been waiting for.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p18.core_idea: Simple closeness is what we wait for

tagore-stray-birds-001-p19.plain: He has turned his weapons into gods; when his weapons win, he himself is defeated.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p20.plain: The stars are not afraid of looking as small as fireflies.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p20.core_idea: True greatness does not fear seeming small

tagore-stray-birds-001-p21.plain: A mind that is sharp but narrow catches on every detail and never moves forward.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p22.plain: People do not show who they are in their history; they struggle upward through it.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p22.core_idea: We rise through history, not in it

tagore-stray-birds-001-p23.plain: We meet and draw close like seagulls and waves; then the gulls fly off, the waves roll away, and we part.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p23.core_idea: Meetings are brief, then we part

tagore-stray-birds-001-p24.plain: My day is over, and I am like a boat pulled up on the beach, listening to the tide's dance music in the evening.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p24.core_idea: Resting peacefully at the end of the day

tagore-stray-birds-001-p25.plain: Life is handed to us as a gift, but we make it truly ours by giving it away.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p25.core_idea: We earn life by giving it

tagore-stray-birds-001-p26.plain: We get closest to greatness when our humility is great.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p26.core_idea: Great humility brings us near greatness

tagore-stray-birds-001-p27.plain: The little sparrow feels sorry for the peacock, which has to carry its heavy, showy tail.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p28.plain: The eternal voice sings to us: do not be afraid of passing moments.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p28.core_idea: Do not fear the passing moments

tagore-stray-birds-001-p29.plain: Friend, take my wine in my own cup; poured into someone else's, it loses its crown of foam.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p29.core_idea: Take something in its own form, not recast

tagore-stray-birds-001-p30.plain: Be grateful to the flame for its light, but also remember the lampstand, patiently and faithfully holding it up out of sight in the shadow.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p30.core_idea: Remember the unseen supporters behind the visible

tagore-stray-birds-001-p31.plain: Little grass, your steps are tiny, yet the whole earth beneath you is yours.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p31.core_idea: The small still hold the earth

tagore-stray-birds-001-p32.plain: What is wrong cannot survive losing, but what is right can lose and still endure.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p32.core_idea: Right can survive defeat; wrong cannot

tagore-stray-birds-001-p33.plain: The waterfall sings that it gives all its water joyfully, even though the thirsty need only a little.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p33.core_idea: Give everything joyfully, beyond what is needed

tagore-stray-birds-001-p34.plain: The woodcutter's axe asked the tree for a handle, and the tree gave it.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p34.core_idea: The tree gives the means of its own cutting

tagore-stray-birds-001-p35.plain: We misread the world and then claim that it has fooled us.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p35.core_idea: We misread the world, then blame it

tagore-stray-birds-001-p36.plain: Grass looks for company down in the earth, while the tree looks for solitude up in the sky.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p36.core_idea: Some seek company, others seek solitude

tagore-stray-birds-001-p37.plain: May life be as beautiful as summer flowers, and death as beautiful as autumn leaves.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p37.core_idea: Life and death can both be beautiful

tagore-stray-birds-001-p38.plain: Someone who wants to do good has to knock at the gate; someone who loves finds it already open.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p38.core_idea: Love opens doors that good intentions knock on

tagore-stray-birds-001-p39.plain: The sheath is happy to be plain and dull, because it keeps the sword sharp.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p40.plain: Power claimed the world as its own, and the world made it a prisoner on her throne. Love gave itself to the world, and the world let it move freely in her home.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p40.core_idea: Power is confined; love is set free

tagore-stray-birds-001-p41.plain: I think of past ages that drifted through life, love and death and are now forgotten, and I feel how freeing it is to pass away.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p41.core_idea: Being forgotten by time can feel freeing

tagore-stray-birds-001-p42.plain: Death is like the stamp that gives a coin its value: because life ends, we can spend it on what really matters.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p43.plain: The cloud stayed modestly in a corner of the sky, and the morning crowned it with glory.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p44.plain: The dust is insulted, and in return it gives flowers.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p45.plain: Don't stop to pick and hoard flowers; keep walking, because flowers will go on blooming all along your way.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p45.core_idea: Don't cling to beauty; more will come

tagore-stray-birds-001-p46.plain: Don't insult your friend by crediting him with good qualities that are really your own.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p46.core_idea: Don't patronise friends with borrowed virtues

tagore-stray-birds-001-p47.plain: My own shadow falls across my path because the lamp I carry has never been lit.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p47.core_idea: Our unlit inner light darkens our way

tagore-stray-birds-001-p48.plain: People go into noisy crowds to drown out the loud silence inside themselves.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p48.core_idea: Crowds are used to escape inner silence

tagore-stray-birds-001-p49.plain: The road is lonely even though crowds walk it, because no one loves it.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p49.core_idea: Crowded but unloved is still lonely

tagore-stray-birds-001-p50.plain: Within my thriving world I carry all the worlds that failed.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p50.core_idea: Success carries past failures within it

tagore-stray-birds-001-p51.plain: It is not hammer blows but the water's dancing that sings the pebbles into perfect shape.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p52.plain: Bees drink nectar from flowers and hum their thanks as they leave, while the showy butterfly is sure the flowers should thank him.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p52.core_idea: The humble give thanks; the vain expect it

tagore-stray-birds-001-p53.plain: It is easy to speak bluntly when you don't wait until you can tell the whole truth.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p53.core_idea: Bluntness is easy without the whole truth

tagore-stray-birds-001-p54.plain: If you close your door to every mistake, you will close it to truth as well.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p54.core_idea: Shutting out all error shuts out truth

tagore-stray-birds-001-p55.plain: The roots underground ask no reward for making the branches bear fruit.

tagore-stray-birds-001-p56.plain: Time is the richness of change, but the clock mocks it, turning it into mere change with no richness at all.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p56.core_idea: Clocks reduce time to empty change

tagore-stray-birds-001-p57.plain: When you took me only from here to there, Road, I grew tired of you; now that you lead me everywhere, I love you as if married to you.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p57.core_idea: A road to everywhere becomes beloved

tagore-stray-birds-001-p58.plain: Let me believe that one of those stars is guiding my life through the dark unknown.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p58.core_idea: Hoping a star guides us through darkness

tagore-stray-birds-001-p59.plain: A sad voice lives among the ruins of the years, and at night it sings to me that it loved me.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p59.core_idea: Past love still sings in memory

tagore-stray-birds-001-p60.plain: I have stars in the sky, but oh, how I long for the little lamp in my house that is still unlit.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p60.core_idea: Distant splendour can't replace a near light

tagore-stray-birds-001-p61.plain: The dust of dead words clings to you. Wash your soul clean with silence.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p61.core_idea: Silence cleanses the soul of empty words

tagore-stray-birds-001-p62.plain: Life has gaps in it, and through them comes the sad music of death.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p62.core_idea: Death's sorrow enters through life's gaps

tagore-stray-birds-001-p63.plain: In the morning the world has opened its heart of light. My heart, come out with your love to meet it.
tagore-stray-birds-001-p63.core_idea: Meet the morning's light with love

tagore-stray-birds-002-p01.plain: God's great power is found in the gentle breeze, not in the storm.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p01.core_idea: God's power is in gentleness, not force

tagore-stray-birds-002-p02.plain: The setting sun asked who would take over its work, and the little clay lamp replied that it would do what it could.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p02.core_idea: Do what small part you can

judge.issue: Drops the lamp addressing the sun as 'my Master'.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p03.plain: Pulling off a flower's petals does not get you its beauty.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p03.core_idea: Taking apart beauty does not capture it

tagore-stray-birds-002-p04.plain: The truly great mix with the small without fear; it is those in the middle who hold themselves apart.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p04.core_idea: The great are not afraid of the small

tagore-stray-birds-002-p05.plain: When we delight in being full, we can give away what we produce with joy.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p06.plain: Love, when you come carrying the burning lamp of pain, I can see your face and recognise you as joy.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p06.core_idea: Pain reveals love's face as bliss

tagore-stray-birds-002-p07.plain: The world has touched my soul with pain and asks me to give it back as songs.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p07.core_idea: Turn the world's pain into song

tagore-stray-birds-002-p08.plain: Either you have real work or you don't. Trouble starts when you have to say, 'Let's do something.'

tagore-stray-birds-002-p09.plain: Asked what drives him on like fate, the answer is: his own self, striding on his back.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p09.core_idea: Our own self drives us like fate

tagore-stray-birds-002-p10.plain: As I walk I keep spilling water from my jar, so very little is left by the time I get home.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p10.core_idea: What we carry spills away on the road

tagore-stray-birds-002-p11.plain: Water in a jar sparkles while the sea is dark. A small truth can be said in clear words; a great truth is met with deep silence.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p11.core_idea: Great truths are held in silence

tagore-stray-birds-002-p12.plain: What I leave to the people I love are the little things; the great things belong to everyone.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p12.core_idea: Little things are our gifts to loved ones

tagore-stray-birds-002-p13.plain: My flower of the day lost its petals unnoticed, but by evening it ripens into a golden fruit of memory.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p13.core_idea: Lost moments ripen into precious memories

tagore-stray-birds-002-p14.plain: Someone too busy doing good has no time left to actually be good.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p14.core_idea: Busy doing good, too busy to be good

tagore-stray-birds-002-p15.plain: I am like the autumn cloud that has already poured out its rain; look for my fullness in the ripe rice fields.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p15.core_idea: What we gave shows where our fullness went

tagore-stray-birds-002-p16.plain: Darkness moves toward light, but blindness moves toward death.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p16.core_idea: Darkness can end in light; blindness cannot

tagore-stray-birds-002-p17.plain: Be still, my heart, and don't stir up dust. Let the world come to you.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p17.core_idea: Be still and let the world come

tagore-stray-birds-002-p18.plain: Before the arrow flies, the bow whispers to it that its freedom belongs to the bow.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p18.core_idea: Freedom depends on what launches it

judge.issue: 'Belongs to the bow' narrows 'your freedom is mine' to ownership.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p19.plain: A mind that is nothing but logic is like a knife that is all blade: it cuts the hand of whoever uses it.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p20.plain: Touching something can kill it, while keeping your distance may let you truly have it.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p21.plain: The wasp thinks the bees' honeycomb next door is too small, and the bees tell him to build an even smaller one.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p21.core_idea: Critics should try making something themselves

tagore-stray-birds-002-p22.plain: The riverbank tells the river that it cannot hold on to its waves, but asks to keep its footprints in its heart.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p22.core_idea: We can't keep what passes, only its traces

tagore-stray-birds-002-p23.plain: May I not present myself wrongly to the world and so turn it against me.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p23.core_idea: Don't turn the world against yourself

tagore-stray-birds-002-p24.plain: Praise makes me ashamed, because secretly I beg for it.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p25.plain: When I have nothing to do, may my idleness be deeply peaceful and untroubled, like evening on the shore when the water is still.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p25.core_idea: Let idle time be deeply peaceful

tagore-stray-birds-002-p26.plain: Our desires paint rainbow colours onto what are only mists and vapours in life.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p27.plain: My sad thoughts tease me by asking me what they are called.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p28.plain: The fruit's service is precious and the flower's is sweet, but may my service be like the leaves, giving shade in humble devotion.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p28.core_idea: Choose humble, devoted service like leaves

tagore-stray-birds-002-p29.plain: People as individuals can be cruel, but humanity as a whole is kind.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p29.core_idea: Men are cruel, humanity is kind

tagore-stray-birds-002-p30.plain: Nothing drains out of the world when someone dies, because death is not a crack in it.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p30.core_idea: Death is not a hole in the world

tagore-stray-birds-002-p31.plain: Love that has been lost has made life richer.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p32.plain: Kicking the ground only raises dust; it never grows crops.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p33.plain: Our names are like light glowing on night waves at sea, which fades without leaving a trace.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p33.core_idea: Our names fade without a trace

tagore-stray-birds-002-p34.plain: Only someone who can see the rose should be allowed to see the thorns.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p34.core_idea: Only see faults if you see beauty too

tagore-stray-birds-002-p35.plain: Cover a bird's wings in gold and it will never fly in the sky again.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p35.core_idea: Riches can ground the free spirit

tagore-stray-birds-002-p36.plain: To the heart, distance seems much larger than it is.

judge.issue: Adds 'than it is', a slight claim beyond 'looms large'.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p37.plain: The moon spreads her light across the whole sky and keeps her dark spots to herself.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p37.core_idea: Share your light, keep your flaws private

tagore-stray-birds-002-p38.plain: Don't just say 'It's morning' and brush it off with yesterday's label. See it for the first time, like a newborn child without a name.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p38.core_idea: See each morning as completely new

tagore-stray-birds-002-p39.plain: The raindrop asked the jasmine to keep it in her heart forever; the jasmine sighed 'Alas' and fell to the ground.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p39.core_idea: Nothing can promise to keep us forever

tagore-stray-birds-002-p40.plain: Shy thoughts, don't be afraid of me; I am a poet.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p41.plain: You have led me through the busy journeys of the day to the loneliness of evening, and I wait through the quiet night to learn what it means.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p41.core_idea: Waiting in stillness for life's meaning

tagore-stray-birds-002-p42.plain: Life is like crossing a sea together in one small boat; at death we reach the shore and each go off to our own world.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p42.core_idea: We share life's voyage, part at death

tagore-stray-birds-002-p43.plain: Truth flows like a stream, and the channels it runs through are our mistakes.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p44.plain: Today my heart longs, like someone homesick, for one sweet hour far back across the sea of time.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p44.core_idea: Longing for one sweet hour long past

tagore-stray-birds-002-p45.plain: The sharp blade should not sneer at its handle for being blunt.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p45.core_idea: Don't scorn the plain parts that support you

tagore-stray-birds-002-p46.plain: When what is real is misunderstood and the stress is put in the wrong place, it becomes unreal.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p47.plain: My heart, find your beauty in the movement of the world, as a boat takes its grace from the wind and the water.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p47.core_idea: Find beauty by moving with the world

tagore-stray-birds-002-p48.plain: I live in my own little world and fear losing even the smallest part of it. Lift me into your world, and let me be free to gladly lose everything.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p48.core_idea: Freedom in gladly losing everything to God

tagore-stray-birds-002-p49.plain: Something false can never become true just by becoming more powerful.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p50.plain: The little flower lies in the dust because it tried to follow the butterfly's path.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p50.core_idea: Trying to be what you're not brings a fall

tagore-stray-birds-002-p51.plain: I have sung the songs of your day; in the evening, let me carry your lamp along the stormy path.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p51.core_idea: Serving God through day and stormy night

tagore-stray-birds-002-p52.plain: I don't invite you into my house; I ask you, my Lover, to come into my endless loneliness.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p52.core_idea: Inviting the beloved into one's loneliness

tagore-stray-birds-002-p53.plain: Death is as much a part of life as birth, just as walking is lifting your foot as well as putting it down.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p53.core_idea: Death belongs to life like birth

tagore-stray-birds-002-p54.plain: I have understood what you whisper through flowers and sunshine; now teach me to understand what you say through pain and death.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p54.core_idea: Learning God's meaning in pain and death

judge.issue: Drops 'simple' from 'the simple meaning of thy whispers'.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p55.plain: Beneath the sadness of everything, I hear the Eternal Mother softly singing.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p55.core_idea: The Eternal Mother sings through all sadness

tagore-stray-birds-002-p56.plain: My earth, I arrived on your shore a stranger, lived in your home as a guest, and leave your door as a friend.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p56.core_idea: Arriving a stranger, leaving the earth a friend

tagore-stray-birds-002-p57.plain: When I am gone, may my thoughts reach you like the lingering glow after sunset at the edge of the silent, starry night.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p57.core_idea: Being remembered like a sunset's afterglow

tagore-stray-birds-002-p58.plain: The day's work is over. Mother, let me hide my face in your arms and dream.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p58.core_idea: Resting in the Mother's arms after work

tagore-stray-birds-002-p59.plain: The lamp of being together burns a long time, but at parting it goes out in an instant.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p59.core_idea: Togetherness lasts long, parting is instant

tagore-stray-birds-002-p60.plain: World, when I am dead, keep just one phrase for me in your silence: 'I have loved.'
tagore-stray-birds-002-p60.core_idea: Be remembered only for having loved

tagore-stray-birds-002-p61.plain: We truly live in this world only when we love it.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p61.core_idea: Loving the world is truly living

tagore-stray-birds-002-p62.plain: Let the dead live on through fame, but let the living live on through love.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p62.core_idea: Fame for the dead, love for the living

tagore-stray-birds-002-p63.plain: I will die over and over to learn that life never runs out.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p63.core_idea: Repeated deaths show life is endless

tagore-stray-birds-002-p64.plain: Walking in the crowded road, I saw your smile from the balcony, and I sang and forgot all the noise.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p64.core_idea: One smile can silence the world's noise

tagore-stray-birds-002-p65.plain: Love is life at its fullest, like a cup filled with wine.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p65.core_idea: Love is life filled to the brim

tagore-stray-birds-002-p66.plain: The pain of love surrounded my life like a bottomless sea, and the joy of love sang like birds in its blossoming woods.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p66.core_idea: Love brings both deep pain and joy

tagore-stray-birds-002-p67.plain: Put out the lamp whenever you wish; I will come to know your darkness and love it.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p67.core_idea: Loving God's darkness as well as light

tagore-stray-birds-002-p68.plain: When I stand before you at the end of the day, you will see my scars and know I was wounded and also healed.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p68.core_idea: Scars show both wounds and healing

tagore-stray-birds-002-p69.plain: Clouds from past days drift into my life, no longer bringing rain or storms, only colour for my sunset sky.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p69.core_idea: Old troubles become colour in later life

tagore-stray-birds-002-p70.plain: Truth stirs up a storm against itself, and that storm spreads its seeds far and wide.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p71.plain: Last night's storm has left this morning crowned with a golden calm.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p72.plain: Blessed is the person whose fame does not shine brighter than their truth.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p72.core_idea: Let your truth outshine your fame

tagore-stray-birds-002-p73.plain: The world loved people when they smiled, and grew afraid of them when they laughed.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p73.core_idea: Smiles are loved, laughter can be feared

tagore-stray-birds-002-p74.plain: Your sunshine smiles on the winter days of my heart, never doubting that spring flowers will come.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p74.core_idea: God's light trusts the heart's coming spring

tagore-stray-birds-002-p75.plain: You cross deserts of empty years to reach the moment when everything is fulfilled.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p76.plain: The day is gloomy: the light under the dark clouds looks like a punished, tear-stained child, and the wind cries like a wounded world. Yet I know I am travelling to meet my Friend.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p76.core_idea: Through gloom, journeying toward the divine Friend

tagore-stray-birds-002-p77.plain: We cannot accept as true the fact that love can ever lose.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p77.core_idea: We refuse to believe love can lose
