tagore-stray-birds-002-p78.plain: One day we will know that death can never take what the soul has gained, because those gains have become part of the soul itself.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p78.core_idea: Death cannot take the soul's gains

tagore-stray-birds-002-p79.plain: In the evening of my life, God comes to me carrying the flowers of my past, still fresh in his basket.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p79.core_idea: God keeps our past fresh for us

tagore-stray-birds-002-p80.plain: My Lord, let me live truthfully, so that my death will be true as well.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p80.core_idea: Live truly so death is true

tagore-stray-birds-002-p81.plain: Human history waits patiently for the day the insulted and humiliated triumph.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p81.core_idea: History awaits the triumph of the humiliated

tagore-stray-birds-002-p82.plain: I climbed to the summit and found no shelter on fame's cold, empty heights. Guide me, before the light goes, down to the quiet valley where life's harvest ripens into wisdom.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p82.core_idea: Fame's heights are empty; wisdom grows in quiet

tagore-stray-birds-002-p83.plain: I have suffered, despaired and known death, and I am glad to be in this great world.

tagore-stray-birds-002-p84.plain: Some stretches of my life are bare and silent; they are the open spaces that gave my busy days light and air.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p84.core_idea: Empty times give busy life room to breathe

tagore-stray-birds-002-p85.plain: Free me from the unfinished past that clings to me from behind and makes dying hard.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p85.core_idea: An unfulfilled past makes death hard

tagore-stray-birds-002-p86.plain: May my final word be this: that I trust in your love.
tagore-stray-birds-002-p86.core_idea: Ending with trust in God's love

tao-001-p01.plain: The highest goodness is like water: it benefits everything and, without struggling, settles in the low places everyone avoids. That is why it comes close to the Tao.
tao-001-p01.core_idea: Highest goodness is humble and helpful like water

tao-001-p02.plain: Better not to fill a vessel than carry it full. A point you keep fingering won't stay sharp. A hall full of gold and jade can't be kept safe. Wealth and honour turned to arrogance bring their own ruin. When work is done and fame grows, withdrawing is Heaven's way.
tao-001-p02.core_idea: Stop before excess; withdraw when work is done
tao-001-p02.plain_v1: Better not to fill a vessel than carry it brimming. Sharpened points dull; hoarded treasure can't be guarded; wealth that breeds arrogance brings ruin. When the work is done and fame grows, withdrawing is Heaven's way.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the condition of repeatedly feeling the point; says sharpened points simply dull.

tao-001-p03.plain: Too many colours blind the eyes, too much music deafens the ears, too many flavours dull the taste; racing and hunting drive the mind wild, and chasing rare things leads people to do wrong.
tao-001-p03.core_idea: Overindulging the senses dulls and corrupts us

judge.issue: Renders 'five' hues, notes, flavours as 'too many', an interpretive shift.

tao-001-p04.plain: Favour and disgrace are both to be feared, and honour and great calamity are alike personal conditions. Disgrace means falling low after favour: gaining favour brings fear of losing it, and losing it brings fear of worse disaster. That is why favour and disgrace are equally feared.
tao-001-p04.core_idea: Favour and disgrace both bring fear
tao-001-p04.plain_v1: Favour and disgrace are equally to be feared. Gaining favour makes you anxious about losing it, and losing it makes you dread worse misfortune; so both bring fear.

judge_v1.issue: Drops honour and calamity as personal conditions, and the definition of disgrace.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops honour and calamity regarded as personal conditions.

tao-001-p05.plain: Who can clear muddy water? Leave it still, and it slowly clears. Who can reach rest? Let movement continue, and rest gradually comes.
tao-001-p05.core_idea: Stillness clears; rest arises in its own time

tao-001-p06.plain: Everyone else looks content, as if feasting. I alone seem flat and still, like a baby not yet smiling, forlorn and homeless. Others have plenty; I seem to have lost everything, my mind foolish and in chaos.
tao-001-p06.core_idea: The sage feels alone and lost among content crowds

judge.issue: Drops the speaker's desires not yet showing themselves, a key nuance.

tao-002-p01.plain: What is partial becomes whole, the crooked straight, the empty full, the worn-out new. Those who want little get it; those who want much lose their way.
tao-002-p01.core_idea: Want little and you will have enough

tao-002-p02.plain: A gale doesn't last the whole morning, and a downpour doesn't last all day. These come from Heaven and Earth, and if even they can't make such bursts last, how much less can a person.

tao-002-p03.plain: On tiptoe you can't stand firm; taking huge strides you can't walk well. In the same way, showing off doesn't make you shine, pushing your views doesn't earn respect, and boasting or conceit wins no recognition.

tao-002-p04.plain: Things naturally turn around: what was ahead falls behind, what was warm grows cold, strength often falls to weakness, and stored wealth crumbles, mocking our effort.

tao-002-p05.plain: Knowing others is shrewd; knowing yourself is wise. Defeating others is strength; mastering yourself is real power. Being content is wealth; persevering shows a firm will.
tao-002-p05.core_idea: Self-knowledge and self-mastery are true strength

tao-002-p06.plain: The soft overcomes the hard, and the weak overcomes the strong.

tao-003-p01.plain: Which matters more to you, fame or life? Life or wealth? If you keep your life and lose the rest, or keep the rest and lose your life, which brings sorrow nearer?
tao-003-p01.core_idea: Life matters more than fame or wealth

tao-003-p02.plain: No wrong is greater than approving ambition, no disaster greater than discontent, no fault greater than always wanting more. So the enough that comes from contentment is an enough that lasts.

tao-003-p03.plain: I am good to those who are good to me and also to those who are not, and so everyone becomes good. I am sincere with the sincere and also with the insincere, and so everyone becomes sincere.
tao-003-p03.core_idea: Return goodness to all, and goodness spreads

tao-003-p04.plain: Happiness sits right beside misery, and misery hides beneath happiness. Who knows how either will turn out in the end?

tao-004-p01.plain: People who promise easily rarely keep their word, and those who assume everything is easy find it hard. So the sage treats even easy-looking things as difficult, and so meets no difficulties.
tao-004-p01.core_idea: Treat easy things seriously to avoid trouble

tao-004-p02.plain: A tree too wide to hug grew from a tiny sprout; a nine-storey tower began as a small pile of earth; a thousand-mile journey starts with one step.

tao-004-p03.plain: Knowing, yet thinking you don't know, is the highest state; not knowing, yet thinking you do, is a sickness.
tao-004-p03.core_idea: Thinking you know when you don't is sickness

tao-004-p04.plain: At birth people are soft and weak; at death, stiff and hard. Plants are tender when young and dry and brittle when dead. So hardness and rigidity go with death, softness and weakness with life.
tao-004-p04.core_idea: Softness belongs to life, rigidity to death

tao-004-p05.plain: After a bitter quarrel is patched up, some resentment always remains, and how can that be good?

judge.issue: Drops that the grudge stays with the one who was wrong.

tao-004-p06.plain: True words aren't fancy, and fancy words aren't true. Those skilled in the Tao don't argue; those who argue aren't skilled. Those who know it aren't widely learned; the widely learned don't know it.
tao-004-p06.core_idea: Truth is plain; wisdom needs no argument

tao-004-p07.plain: The sage doesn't hoard. The more he spends on others, the more he has; the more he gives, the richer he becomes.
tao-004-p07.core_idea: Giving to others enriches the giver

teresa-interior-castle-001-p01.plain: I pictured the soul as a castle of diamond or clear crystal with many rooms, like heaven's many mansions. The soul of the just person is a paradise where God delights. Its beauty and powers are beyond our understanding, as God is, for he made us in his image.
teresa-interior-castle-001-p01.core_idea: The soul is a crystal castle where God dwells
teresa-interior-castle-001-p01.plain_v1: The soul is like a castle of clear crystal with many rooms, a paradise where God delights to dwell. Its beauty and powers are beyond our understanding, just as God is, because he made us in his image.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the condition 'soul of the just man'; says any soul is God's paradise.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops 'of the just man'; implies every soul is God's paradise.

teresa-interior-castle-001-p02.plain: It is our own shameful fault that we don't understand our nature or origin. Worse than not knowing your own name, we think only of our bodies and rarely consider the soul's gifts, worth, and who dwells in it.
teresa-interior-castle-001-p02.core_idea: We neglect to know our own souls

judge.issue: Drops knowing of the soul only vaguely, from hearsay and doctrine.

teresa-interior-castle-001-p03.plain: Resenting God's graces to others shows a lack of humility and love. Why not be glad when someone receives favours that take nothing from us, and rejoice that God shows his greatness wherever he chooses?

teresa-interior-castle-001-p04.plain: If someone doesn't consider who they are speaking to, what they are asking, or who they are to speak to God, then however many words they say, it isn't prayer.
teresa-interior-castle-001-p04.core_idea: Prayer needs awareness of whom we address

teresa-interior-castle-002-p01.plain: A soul in that state is like a crystal in sunlight covered with a thick black cloth: however bright the sun, the crystal cannot reflect it.
teresa-interior-castle-002-p01.core_idea: A darkened soul cannot reflect God's light

teresa-interior-castle-002-p02.plain: Humility must always be at work, like a bee making honey, or all is lost. Yet the bee leaves its hive for flowers, and the soul should sometimes stop thinking of itself and rise to contemplate God's greatness.

teresa-interior-castle-002-p03.plain: We will never know ourselves except by trying to know God: his greatness shows our lowliness, his purity our impurity, and his humility how far we are from being humble.
teresa-interior-castle-002-p03.core_idea: Knowing God is how we know ourselves

teresa-interior-castle-002-p04.plain: My daughters, don't burden yourselves with worries that are not your concern.
teresa-interior-castle-002-p04.core_idea: Don't worry about what isn't yours

teresa-interior-castle-003-p01.plain: My daughters, true perfection lies in loving God and our neighbour; the better we keep these two commandments, the more perfect we become.
teresa-interior-castle-003-p01.core_idea: Perfection is loving God and neighbour

teresa-interior-castle-003-p02.plain: We can lose our own peace, and disturb others', by constantly criticising small actions that often aren't faults at all, but which we misjudge because we don't know the reasons behind them.

teresa-interior-castle-003-p03.plain: Sisters, don't undervalue this first grace or lose heart if you didn't answer the Lord's call at once; he will wait days and even years, especially when he sees perseverance and good desire. Perseverance is what matters most.
teresa-interior-castle-003-p03.core_idea: God waits patiently; perseverance is essential

judge.issue: Drops the assurance that perseverance brings great profit.

teresa-interior-castle-003-p04.plain: How absurd! We are full of obstacles and faults, our virtues barely born, if they exist at all, and yet we shamelessly expect sweetness in prayer and complain when it feels dry.
teresa-interior-castle-003-p04.core_idea: Don't demand sweetness in prayer while imperfect

teresa-interior-castle-003-p05.plain: You may think you could bear outward troubles if God gave you inner comfort, but God knows what is good for us; it is not our place to advise Him, since we do not know what we ask.
teresa-interior-castle-003-p05.core_idea: God knows our good better than we do.

teresa-interior-castle-004-p01.plain: If you sometimes fall into sin, do not lose heart or stop trying to move forward, because God can bring good even out of our falls.
teresa-interior-castle-004-p01.core_idea: God draws good even from our failures.

judge.issue: Drops the theriac merchant simile.

teresa-interior-castle-004-p02.plain: What trouble is worse than the trouble inside us? If we have no peace within, where else could we expect to find it?
teresa-interior-castle-004-p02.core_idea: Peace must be found within, not elsewhere.

teresa-interior-castle-004-p03.plain: If you have let go of the habit of inward prayer, the only cure is to start again; otherwise the soul loses it a little more each day.
teresa-interior-castle-004-p03.core_idea: A lapsed spiritual habit is cured by restarting.

judge.issue: Drops the closing prayer that the soul may realise its danger.

teresa-interior-castle-004-p04.plain: Life in this world is miserable: we are like people with enemies at the door, who can never put down their weapons, even to sleep or eat, always afraid of a breach.
teresa-interior-castle-004-p04.core_idea: Life is constant watchfulness against inner enemies.

teresa-interior-castle-004-p05.plain: God knows I can rely on nothing but His mercy. Since I cannot undo the past, my only remedy is to run to Him and trust in His Son and the Virgin Mary.
teresa-interior-castle-004-p05.core_idea: The past cannot be undone; only mercy remains.

judge.issue: Drops the merits of the Son and the Virgin's habit she wears.

teresa-interior-castle-005-p01.plain: Where there is real humility, even if God never gives feelings of comfort in prayer, He gives a peace and acceptance that make the soul happier than those who have such feelings.
teresa-interior-castle-005-p01.core_idea: Humility brings peace beyond felt consolation.

teresa-interior-castle-005-p02.plain: A rich man with no heirs loses part of his wealth yet still has plenty. If he grieves as though he were reduced to begging, how could God ask him to give up everything?
teresa-interior-castle-005-p02.core_idea: Clinging to small losses shows how attached we are.

teresa-interior-castle-005-p03.plain: What matters is not whether we wear religious dress but whether we live the virtues and give our will over to God's in everything. Our aim should be to do His will, not ask for ours.
teresa-interior-castle-005-p03.core_idea: Virtue and surrender matter, not outward religious signs.

teresa-interior-castle-005-p04.plain: Humility is the balm for our wounds. If we have it, God, our doctor, will come and heal us, even if He delays for a while.
teresa-interior-castle-005-p04.core_idea: Humility lets God heal our wounds.

teresa-interior-castle-005-p05.plain: When caution rules everything we do, everything holds us back; fear stops our progress, as if someone else could make the inner journey for us. So let us push ourselves, leaving our reasoning and fears with God.

judge.issue: Drops 'for the love of God' and ignoring nature's weaknesses.

teresa-interior-castle-005-p06.plain: Those who do not feel comfort in prayer need not be discouraged, because perfection is not about comfort but about greater love; our reward will match that love and the honesty of our actions.
teresa-interior-castle-005-p06.core_idea: Perfection lies in love, not in consolation.

teresa-interior-castle-005-p07.plain: It does matter whether you seek these graces. But if you are not at fault, God is fair: what He withholds one way He will give another, in His mysterious ways, doing what is best for you.
teresa-interior-castle-005-p07.core_idea: What God withholds one way, He gives another.

teresa-interior-castle-006-p01.plain: It is encouraging to see others bear gently the trials we thought impossible. Their flight makes us try to fly, like young birds who learn bit by bit by copying their parents.
teresa-interior-castle-006-p01.core_idea: Others' endurance teaches us to endure.

teresa-interior-castle-006-p02.plain: Look at your own faults, not other people's. Very proper people are often shocked by everything, yet we can learn a great deal from the very people we criticise.
teresa-interior-castle-006-p02.core_idea: Mind your own faults; learn from those you judge.

fix.display_text: Let us look at our own faults, and not at other persons'. People who are extremely correct themselves are often shocked at everything they see; however, we might often learn a great deal that is essential from the very persons whom we censure.

judge.issue: Shifts 'let us' to a direct command to the reader.

teresa-interior-castle-006-p03.plain: To make fast progress toward the inner rooms of the soul, thinking much matters less than loving much, so do whatever most stirs you to love.
teresa-interior-castle-006-p03.core_idea: Progress comes from loving much, not thinking much.

teresa-interior-castle-006-p04.plain: Love is not sweet feelings in devotion but a firm resolve to please God in everything, avoid offending Him, and pray for His glory and the Church. It is not lost because your thoughts wander.
teresa-interior-castle-006-p04.core_idea: Love is determination, not sweet feelings.

judge.issue: Drops 'Catholic' and the error of thinking only of God.

teresa-interior-castle-006-p05.plain: Many suffer, grow gloomy or even give up prayer because they mistake a wandering imagination for a grave fault. We cannot control our imagination any more than the turning heavens, so its wandering does not mean prayer is wasted.
teresa-interior-castle-006-p05.core_idea: A wandering mind does not ruin prayer.

judge.issue: Drops the 'interior world' idea and taking good things for faults.

teresa-interior-castle-007-p01.plain: We shouldn't be troubled by our thoughts: if from the devil, he leaves us alone when ignored; if frailties from Adam's sin, let us bear them patiently for love of God. Since we must eat and sleep, let us admit we are human and long for where none despise us.
teresa-interior-castle-007-p01.core_idea: Bear troubling thoughts patiently; we are human.
teresa-interior-castle-007-p01.plain_v1: Do not be distressed or worried by your thoughts: if they come from the devil, ignoring them makes him leave; if they are human weakness, bear them patiently for God's love, accepting that we are human.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the eating and sleeping point and longing for where none despise us.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the longing to be where no one may despise us.

teresa-interior-castle-007-p02.plain: Any trouble or conflict can be borne while we have peace inside; but when we seek rest from the world's trials and the obstacle is in ourselves, the pain is almost unbearable.
teresa-interior-castle-007-p02.core_idea: Outer trials are bearable; inner conflict is not.

judge.issue: Drops 'knowing that God has prepared this rest for us'.

teresa-interior-castle-007-p03.plain: God, so great and wise, has hidden secrets in everything He made. Even the smallest creature, even a tiny ant, holds more wonders than we can understand.
teresa-interior-castle-007-p03.core_idea: Even the smallest creature holds countless wonders.

judge.issue: Drops that knowing these hidden secrets would greatly benefit us.

teresa-interior-castle-007-p04.plain: We belong to God; let Him do what He wants with us and lead us wherever He wants.
teresa-interior-castle-007-p04.core_idea: We belong to God; let Him lead.

teresa-interior-castle-008-p01.plain: Looking for God within ourselves helps far more than looking for Him among created things; Saint Augustine found God in his own soul after long searching elsewhere.

teresa-interior-castle-008-p02.plain: We should ask God for things like beggars before a rich and powerful emperor, and then wait humbly with lowered eyes.

teresa-interior-castle-008-p03.plain: We should rather give our souls into God's hands, letting Him do as He chooses with us, forgetting our own interests as far as we can and surrendering fully to His will.
teresa-interior-castle-008-p03.core_idea: Surrender yourself completely to God's will.

teresa-interior-castle-008-p04.plain: God gave us our mental powers to use, and each will be rewarded. So we should not try to lull them to sleep but let them work until God calls us to something higher.
teresa-interior-castle-008-p04.core_idea: Use your God-given faculties; do not suppress them.

teresa-interior-castle-009-p01.plain: Wake up, sisters: since some taste of heaven can be had on earth, ask God for the grace not to miss it through our own fault, and for the strength to dig for the treasure hidden in our hearts.
teresa-interior-castle-009-p01.core_idea: A hidden treasure lies buried within our hearts.

teresa-interior-castle-010-p01.plain: One way or another, we have to carry the cross our whole lives.
teresa-interior-castle-010-p01.core_idea: Suffering accompanies us all our lives.

teresa-interior-castle-011-p01.plain: People who avoid offending God and enter religious life may think nothing more is needed. But hidden pests like self-love, pride, quick judgment of others and lack of love for neighbours quietly eat away their virtues.
teresa-interior-castle-011-p01.core_idea: Hidden self-love and judgment quietly destroy virtue.

judge.issue: Drops the simile of the worm gnawing Jonas's ivy.

teresa-interior-castle-011-p02.plain: God asks only two things of us: love for Him and love for our neighbour. If we practise both perfectly, we are doing His will and are united with Him.
teresa-interior-castle-011-p02.core_idea: God asks only love of Him and neighbour.

teresa-interior-castle-011-p03.plain: We cannot be sure whether we love God, but we can be sure whether we love our neighbour. As you grow in love for others, you grow in love for God, and He repays it many times over.
teresa-interior-castle-011-p03.core_idea: Love of neighbour is the sure measure of loving God.

judge.issue: Loses that God repays by increasing our love for Him.

teresa-interior-castle-011-p04.plain: It is funny to see people who, at prayer, imagine they would gladly be insulted for God's sake, yet afterward hide their small faults and cry out loudly when someone wrongly accuses them.
teresa-interior-castle-011-p04.core_idea: Humility imagined in prayer often fails in practice.

teresa-interior-castle-012-p01.plain: Anxiously guarding feelings of devotion in prayer misunderstands union with God. The Lord wants works: care for a sick sister, feel her pain, fast so she may eat, because the Lord asks it. That is true union of wills. Rejoice when others are praised, and hide their faults.
teresa-interior-castle-012-p01.core_idea: Union with God shows in deeds of love.
teresa-interior-castle-012-p01.plain_v1: Union with God is not guarding pious feelings in prayer; God wants deeds. Help a sick sister, feel her pain as your own, rejoice when others are praised, and grieve over their faults as if they were yours, hiding them.

judge_v1.issue: Drops motive 'because the Lord asks it', union of wills, and humility vexed by praise.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops fasting for her because the Lord asks it, the true union of wills.

teresa-interior-castle-012-p02.plain: Ask God for perfect love of your neighbour and leave the rest to Him. Push yourself to give way to others' wishes, put their interests before yours however much you resist, and take burdens off them.
teresa-interior-castle-012-p02.core_idea: Love your neighbour by putting their needs first.

fix.display_text: Beg our Lord to grant you perfect love for your neighbour, and leave the rest to Him. He will give you more than you know how to desire if you constrain yourselves and strive with all your power to gain it, forcing your will as far as possible to comply in all things with your sisters' wishes although you may sometimes forfeit your own rights by so doing. Forget your self-interests for theirs, however much nature may rebel; when opportunity occurs take some burden upon yourself to ease your neighbour of it.

judge.issue: Drops promise that God gives more than we know to desire.

teresa-interior-castle-012-p03.plain: We must keep asking God to hold us up, since without Him we would fall at once. Then we should watch whether we grow or slip in virtue, especially in love of neighbour, humility and daily duties.
teresa-interior-castle-012-p03.core_idea: Rely on God and watch your progress in virtue.

judge.issue: Drops begging the Lord for light to perceive gain or loss.

teresa-interior-castle-013-p01.plain: God often sends severe illness, perhaps the hardest earthly trial, reaching body and spirit until death seems preferable. But these attacks pass quickly, for God never sends more than we can bear and gives patience first.
teresa-interior-castle-013-p01.core_idea: God never sends more than we can bear.

judge.issue: Drops preferring quick martyrdom; generalises 'now usually sends' to 'often'.

teresa-interior-castle-013-p02.plain: In such a storm the only remedy is to wait for God's mercy, which suddenly clears every sorrow and leaves the mind brighter. The soul knows the victory was God's and sees how weak it is alone.
teresa-interior-castle-013-p02.core_idea: Wait for God's mercy to end the storm.

judge.issue: Drops the soul praising God like a victor after battle.

teresa-interior-castle-013-p03.plain: When such inner suffering lasts for days, prayer brings no comfort, solitude hurts, company torments, and the pain cannot be described. The best way to bear it is outward charity and trust in God's unfailing mercy.
teresa-interior-castle-013-p03.core_idea: Bear inner anguish through charity and trust in God.

teresa-interior-castle-014-p01.plain: God is like a burning furnace sending a small spark into the soul, which feels its heat without being consumed. The feeling is so delightful that the spirit lingers in the pain it causes.
teresa-interior-castle-014-p01.core_idea: God's touch is a delightful, burning pain.

teresa-interior-castle-015-p01.plain: If the soul receives signs of God's love, it should check whether it now thinks more of itself. Truly divine favours always make the soul humbler and more aware of its sins.
teresa-interior-castle-015-p01.core_idea: True divine favours make the soul humbler.

judge.issue: Drops explicit test that favours without humility are not from the Holy Spirit.

teresa-interior-castle-016-p01.plain: We are so blind. Even small specks of fault, left to spread, can harm us greatly. Let our faults show us how poor we are and clear our sight, so we ask God more earnestly to help us please Him.
teresa-interior-castle-016-p01.core_idea: Small faults, seen honestly, can clear our sight.

fix.display_text: Oh, human blindness! When, oh, when shall this dust be taken from our eyes? Although we think it insufficient to blind us, yet I see some little motes or grains of dust which, if left to spread, will suffice to harm us greatly. At least, for the love of God, my sisters, let these faults convince us of our misery, serving to clear our sight as did the clay the eyes of the blind man who was cured by the Spouse. Then, realizing our imperfections, we shall beg Him more fervently to let us benefit by our defects so as to please Him in all things.

judge.issue: Drops the clay and the blind man healed by the Spouse.

teresa-interior-castle-016-p02.plain: God gives such favours to whom He chooses, yet if we sought Him as He seeks us, He would give them to everyone. He longs for souls to give them to, since giving costs Him nothing.
teresa-interior-castle-016-p02.core_idea: God longs to give; we need only seek Him.

teresa-interior-castle-016-p03.plain: The Lord once told a troubled person not to be disturbed: people will either praise Him or condemn you, and either way you will gain.
teresa-interior-castle-016-p03.core_idea: Praise or blame, you gain either way.

fix.display_text: Our Lord once said to some one who was troubled by such thoughts: 'Do not be disturbed; people will either praise Me or condemn thee; in either case thou wilt be the gainer.'

teresa-interior-castle-018-p01.plain: Tears are not enough; what matters is hard work and virtue, letting tears come when God sends them, for they water the soul as no digging can. So we should stand before God, weigh His mercy and our vileness, and accept water or drought; then we have peace.
teresa-interior-castle-018-p01.core_idea: Practise virtue; leave tears and comfort to God.
teresa-interior-castle-018-p01.plain_v1: Crying a lot is not enough; what matters is working at the virtues and letting tears come when God sends them. Rest in God's presence and let Him give water or drought, since He knows best.

judge_v1.issue: Drops heavenly water versus digging, contemplating our vileness, and the devil.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops tears watering the soul and the resulting peace from the devil.

teresa-interior-castle-018-p02.plain: However much God has favoured a soul, it is dangerous to forget the unhappy state it was once in; remembering may hurt, but it does great good.
teresa-interior-castle-018-p02.core_idea: Remembering past misery keeps us humble.

teresa-interior-castle-019-p01.plain: Life is long and full of crosses, so to bear our trials well we need to look at how Christ bore His, and learn from His apostles and saints too.
teresa-interior-castle-019-p01.core_idea: Look to Christ to learn how to bear trials.

teresa-interior-castle-020-p01.plain: Look at the virtues: the one who is most self-denying, humble and wholehearted in serving God is the holiest.
teresa-interior-castle-020-p01.core_idea: Holiness is humility and wholehearted service.

teresa-interior-castle-021-p01.plain: Let us put ourselves wholly in God's hands so that His will is done in us; if our will stays fixed on this, we can never go wrong.
teresa-interior-castle-021-p01.core_idea: A will fixed on God's never goes astray.

teresa-interior-castle-022-p01.plain: Bearing injuries patiently is no great achievement; we should bear them gladly and love our enemies, since God has never stopped loving us despite our many sins. That is the main reason to forgive any harm done to us.
teresa-interior-castle-022-p01.core_idea: Forgive others because God keeps loving us.

teresa-interior-castle-022-p02.plain: God loves humility because He is the supreme Truth and humility is truth: we have nothing good of ourselves. Whoever ignores this lives a lie; those who grasp it most deeply please God most, for they walk in truth.
teresa-interior-castle-022-p02.core_idea: Humility is simply living in the truth.

judge.issue: Softens 'only misery and nothingness' to 'nothing good of ourselves'.

teresa-interior-castle-022-p03.plain: Lord, what suffering You bring to those who love You! Yet it is nothing next to the reward You will give. It is right that great riches cost a great deal.
teresa-interior-castle-022-p03.core_idea: Great riches are rightly bought at great cost.

teresa-interior-castle-023-p01.plain: We each have a soul, but we do not grasp its worth as made in God's image, so we miss the great secrets it holds.
teresa-interior-castle-023-p01.core_idea: The soul, made in God's image, holds hidden secrets.

teresa-interior-castle-024-p01.plain: If we empty ourselves of everything created, giving it up for love of God, the Lord will surely fill us with Himself.
teresa-interior-castle-024-p01.core_idea: Empty yourself, and God fills you.

teresa-interior-castle-024-p02.plain: Like a king who stays on his throne while wars rage in his kingdom, the soul in the innermost mansion keeps its peace; it regrets the turmoil outside, but the passions cannot enter or disturb it there.
teresa-interior-castle-024-p02.core_idea: The innermost soul keeps peace amid turmoil.

teresa-interior-castle-025-p01.plain: Those closest to Christ always carry the heaviest cross; think of what His mother and the apostles endured.
teresa-interior-castle-025-p01.core_idea: Those nearest Christ bear the heaviest cross.

teresa-interior-castle-026-p01.plain: It does me little good to pray deeply alone, making acts of virtue and promising great things for God, if later, when the chance comes, I do the opposite.
teresa-interior-castle-026-p01.core_idea: Good resolutions mean little without matching deeds.

teresa-interior-castle-026-p02.plain: The devil often fills our minds with grand plans so we settle for wishing the impossible instead of doing the work we can. Pray, and rather than trying to help the whole world, help those closest to you.
teresa-interior-castle-026-p02.core_idea: Help those near you instead of dreaming grandly.

judge.issue: Drops that helping companions is better because we are more bound to it.

teresa-interior-castle-026-p03.plain: Do not build towers without foundations: the Lord cares less about how great our works are than about the love behind them. When we do all we can, He helps us do more each day.
teresa-interior-castle-026-p03.core_idea: God values the love in our works, not their size.

upanishads-paramananda-001-p01.plain: Everything that exists in the universe should be seen as pervaded by the Lord. Let go of the unreal and enjoy the Real. Do not covet anyone's wealth.
upanishads-paramananda-001-p01.core_idea: See the Lord in all; covet nothing.

upanishads-paramananda-001-p02.plain: Whoever sees all beings in the Self and the Self in all beings never turns away from it. For one who sees all beings as the Self, seeing this oneness everywhere, how can there be delusion or grief?
upanishads-paramananda-001-p02.core_idea: Seeing oneness in all ends delusion and grief.

upanishads-paramananda-001-p03.plain: Look at those who lived before and those living now: mortals decay like grain and, like grain, spring up again in rebirth.
upanishads-paramananda-001-p03.core_idea: Mortals die and are reborn like grain.

upanishads-paramananda-001-p04.plain: Nachiketas tells Death that these pleasures are fleeting and wear out the senses; even the longest life is short. Death can keep his chariots, dancing and music, for wealth never satisfies anyone.

upanishads-paramananda-001-p05.plain: Yama says the good and the pleasant differ and lead to different ends. All is well for whoever chooses the good; whoever chooses the pleasant misses the true goal. The wise prefer the good; fools choose pleasure.
upanishads-paramananda-001-p05.core_idea: Choose the good over the merely pleasant.

upanishads-paramananda-001-p06.plain: Fools living in ignorance, yet thinking themselves wise and learned, wander round and round on crooked paths, like the blind led by the blind.
upanishads-paramananda-001-p06.core_idea: The ignorant who think themselves wise go astray.

upanishads-paramananda-001-p07.plain: The Self is never born and never dies; it came from nothing and nothing came from it. Unborn and eternal, it is not killed when the body is killed. Whoever thinks they kill or are killed does not understand.
upanishads-paramananda-001-p07.core_idea: The Self is unborn, undying and cannot be slain.

upanishads-paramananda-001-p08.plain: The Self is finer than the finest and greater than the greatest, living in the heart of every being. Whoever is free from desire and grief, with a calm mind and senses, sees the glory of the Atman.
upanishads-paramananda-001-p08.core_idea: A calm, desireless mind sees the Self within.

upanishads-paramananda-002-p01.plain: The Atman is the chariot's owner, the body the chariot, the intellect the driver, the mind the reins, the senses the horses. Without discernment and a controlled mind the senses run wild; with them, they obey like good horses.
upanishads-paramananda-002-p01.core_idea: A disciplined mind steers the senses well.

judge.issue: Drops the Atman as enjoyer when united with body, senses and mind.

upanishads-paramananda-002-p02.plain: Arise, awake! Seek out the great teachers and gain understanding. The wise say the path is as sharp as a razor's edge, hard to cross and hard to travel.
upanishads-paramananda-002-p02.core_idea: Wake up; the path is hard but walk it.

upanishads-paramananda-002-p03.plain: The senses face outward, so we see the outer world, not the inner Atman. A wise person seeking immortality turns inward and sees the Self. The ignorant chase pleasures into death's snare; the wise seek nothing lasting in fleeting things.
upanishads-paramananda-002-p03.core_idea: Turn inward to find the lasting Self.

fix.display_text: The Self-existent created the senses out-going; for this reason man sees the external, but not the inner Atman (Self). Some wise man, however, desiring immortality, with eyes turned away (from the external) sees the Atman within. Children (the ignorant) pursue external pleasures; (thus) they fall into the widespread snare of death. But the wise, knowing the nature of immortality, do not seek the permanent among fleeting things.
fix.reason: Word broken by hyphen and space

judge.issue: Drops the Self-existent as the one who made the senses outgoing.

upanishads-paramananda-002-p04.plain: Just as the sun, the eye of the world, is not stained by the impurities it lights up, the one inner Self of all beings is not stained by the world's misery, being beyond it.
upanishads-paramananda-002-p04.core_idea: The inner Self is untouched by the world's misery.

upanishads-paramananda-002-p05.plain: When the five senses and the mind fall still and the intellect stops working, that is the highest state. This steady restraint of the senses is Yoga. Then stay watchful, because Yoga comes and goes.
upanishads-paramananda-002-p05.core_idea: Stilling the senses is Yoga; stay watchful.

upanishads-paramananda-002-p06.plain: When all the desires in the heart fall away, the mortal becomes immortal and reaches Brahman here and now. When all the heart's knots are cut, the mortal becomes immortal. That is the teaching.

upanishads-paramananda-002-p07.plain: Whoever thinks they do not know Brahman knows it; whoever thinks they know it does not. True knowers feel they can never know it, being infinite, while the ignorant think they do.
upanishads-paramananda-002-p07.core_idea: Those who know the Infinite admit they cannot know it.

viv01-001-p01.plain: Just as streams rising in different places all mix their waters in the sea, so, Lord, the different paths people take, crooked or straight, all lead to You.
viv01-001-p01.core_idea: All paths lead to God, like streams to the sea.

viv01-001-p02.plain: When I close my eyes and think of 'I', I picture a body. Am I only matter? The Vedas say no: I am a spirit living in a body. The body will die, but I will go on living.
viv01-001-p02.core_idea: I am a spirit, not the body.

viv01-002-p01.plain: You are children of God, sharers in immortal bliss, holy and perfect; calling people sinners slanders human nature. Rise up, lions, and shake off the delusion that you are sheep; you are free, eternal souls, and matter serves you.
viv01-002-p01.core_idea: You are divine, free souls, not sinners.

viv01-002-p02.plain: Loving God for a reward is good, but loving God for love's sake is better, as in the prayer that asks not for wealth, children or learning, only to love God without hope of reward, even through many births.
viv01-002-p02.core_idea: Love God for love's sake, not reward.

viv01-002-p03.plain: For the Hindu, people move not from error to truth but from lower to higher truth. Every religion is the soul's attempt to grasp the Infinite, and every soul is a young eagle rising toward the Sun.
viv01-002-p03.core_idea: We move from lower truth to higher truth.

judge.issue: Drops each religion being shaped by its conditions and marking a stage of progress.

viv01-003-p01.plain: Offering religion to starving people is an insult, just as teaching philosophy to a starving man is.
viv01-003-p01.core_idea: Feed the hungry before preaching to them.

viv01-003-p02.plain: Whatever philosophy says, as long as there is death, weakness in the human heart, and a cry rising from that weakness, people will have faith in God.
viv01-003-p02.core_idea: Human weakness and death keep faith alive.

viv01-003-p03.plain: A seed does not become earth, air or water; it absorbs them and grows into a plant by its own law. So with religion: no one need convert, but each should absorb others' spirit while growing in their own way.
viv01-003-p03.core_idea: Learn from other faiths while staying true to yours.

judge.issue: 'No one need convert' softens 'is not to become'; drops preserving individuality.

viv02-001-p01.plain: Good and bad both shape character, and misery can teach more than happiness. In most great people, it was suffering, poverty and blows, more than happiness, wealth and praise, that brought out their inner fire.
viv02-001-p01.core_idea: Suffering often teaches more than happiness.

viv02-001-p02.plain: To judge someone's character, do not look at their great deeds; any fool can be a hero once. Watch their most ordinary actions. Great moments rouse anyone, but the truly great person is great always, wherever they are.
viv02-001-p02.core_idea: Character shows in ordinary actions, not great deeds.

viv02-001-p03.plain: We are responsible for who we are, and we can make ourselves whatever we wish. Since what we are now comes from past actions, what we become depends on how we act now.
viv02-001-p03.core_idea: Present actions shape who we become.

viv02-001-p04.plain: Love, truth and unselfishness are our highest ideal because they hold real power. Working even briefly with no selfish motive makes a person morally strong; holding back is greater power than any outward action.
viv02-001-p04.core_idea: Self-restraint is the greatest form of power.

judge.issue: Drops working without thought of heaven or punishment; 'moral giant' softened.

viv02-002-p01.plain: You have a right to work, not to its results, so leave the results alone. When you help someone, don't think about how they should treat you; when doing good work, don't worry about the outcome.
viv02-002-p01.core_idea: Do the work; let go of the results.

viv02-002-p02.plain: The ideal person finds intense activity in deep silence, and the calm of the desert in intense activity. Having mastered himself, he walks busy city streets with a mind as quiet as a cave, working hard all the while.
viv02-002-p02.core_idea: Stay inwardly calm while working intensely.

viv02-002-p03.plain: We must work and watch what drives us. At first we will find our motives almost always selfish, but with persistence that selfishness slowly melts until we can do truly unselfish work.
viv02-002-p03.core_idea: Persistent work slowly melts away selfishness.

viv02-002-p04.plain: Once someone starts to hate himself, decline has begun, and the same is true of a nation. Our first duty is not to hate ourselves, because without faith in yourself you can never have faith in God.
viv02-002-p04.core_idea: Faith in yourself comes before faith in God.

viv02-002-p05.plain: Each person should pursue their own ideal, not someone else's they can never reach. People differ, so mock no ideal and judge no one by another's standard; an apple tree isn't judged as an oak.
viv02-002-p05.core_idea: Judge each person by their own ideal.

viv02-003-p01.plain: The married householder is as great as the monk, and the street sweeper as great as the king. It is far harder to live in the world and worship God than to give it up for an easy life apart.
viv02-003-p01.core_idea: Living in the world and worshipping God is harder.

viv02-003-p02.plain: The hardest thing is to work without caring for results, help without expecting thanks, and do good without looking for fame. Anyone can be brave when praised; doing good steadily without anyone's approval is the highest sacrifice.
viv02-003-p02.core_idea: Doing good without seeking approval is the highest sacrifice.

viv02-003-p03.plain: The Vedas keep repeating one word: fearlessness, fear nothing. Fear is a sign of weakness. A person must go about their duties ignoring the world's sneers and ridicule.
viv02-003-p03.core_idea: Fear is weakness; do your duty fearlessly.

viv02-004-p01.plain: Giving knowledge is a greater gift than food, clothes or even life itself, because real life is knowledge. Ignorance is death and knowledge is life; a life spent groping in the dark is worth little.
viv02-004-p01.core_idea: Knowledge is the greatest gift; ignorance is death.

viv02-004-p02.plain: What we repeatedly hear, think and do leaves impressions that drive us without our knowing. Bad impressions push a person toward evil; enough good thoughts and deeds make goodness irresistible, and then good character is established.
viv02-004-p02.core_idea: Repeated thoughts and deeds form our character.

judge.issue: Softens 'he cannot help it' and being forced like a machine to 'push toward'.

viv02-005-p01.plain: Work tirelessly, but like a traveller passing through a foreign land, without tying yourself down, because bondage is terrible. This world is not our home, only one of many stages we pass through.
viv02-005-p01.core_idea: Work hard but unattached; this world is a passing stage.

viv02-005-p02.plain: A man who wants a woman all to himself, jealous of her every move, is a slave who wants her as his slave. That is not love, because it brings pain; real love brings only joy.
viv02-005-p02.core_idea: Possessive jealousy is not love; love brings only joy.

viv02-005-p03.plain: You expect nothing back from your children. Treat all your work that way: give freely, without thought of return, and your work won't bind you, because attachment comes from expecting returns.
viv02-005-p03.core_idea: Give freely, expecting nothing, and attachment disappears.

viv02-005-p04.plain: Two forces guide people: power and mercy. Using power is always selfish, since people exploit whatever advantage they have. Mercy is heaven itself; to be good we must be merciful, and even justice should rest on mercy.
viv02-005-p04.core_idea: Even justice should rest on mercy.

viv02-006-p01.plain: Never boast about what you give the poor or expect their thanks; instead be grateful to them for the chance to be charitable.
viv02-006-p01.core_idea: Thank those you help for the chance to give.

viv02-006-p02.plain: Only one idea of duty has been accepted by all people everywhere, summed up in a Sanskrit saying: do not harm any being; not harming is virtue and harming is sin.
viv02-006-p02.core_idea: Not harming any being is the universal duty.

viv02-006-p03.plain: I am not the measure of the universe. I have to adapt myself to the world, not the world to me.
viv02-006-p03.core_idea: Adapt yourself to the world, not the reverse.

viv02-006-p04.plain: When we start working seriously, life's knocks soon show us where we belong, and no one stays long in a role they don't suit. Lower work doesn't make a lower person; judge people by the spirit in which they work.
viv02-006-p04.core_idea: Judge people by how they work, not what work.

judge.issue: 'Nature's adjustment' becomes 'life's knocks'; drops 'no use grumbling'.

viv02-006-p05.plain: Duty is rarely sweet; only love makes it run smoothly. Love thrives in freedom, yet being ruled by anger and jealousy is not freedom. Amid life's small irritations, the highest freedom is to hold back.
viv02-006-p05.core_idea: Duty is sweet only through love; forbearance is freedom.

viv02-007-p01.plain: The only way to rise is to do the duty right in front of you, gaining strength from it, and keep going until you reach the highest state.
viv02-007-p01.core_idea: Rise by doing the duty in front of you.

viv02-007-p02.plain: When you do any work, don't think of anything beyond it. Do it as worship, the highest worship, and give your whole life to it while you are doing it.
viv02-007-p02.core_idea: Do each task wholeheartedly, as worship.

viv02-007-p03.plain: Only workers attached to results grumble about their duties; to the unattached, every duty helps kill selfishness and free the soul. The grumbler is never satisfied. Keep doing your duty and you will see the Light.
viv02-007-p03.core_idea: Stop grumbling, do your duty, and find the Light.

judge.issue: Drops that competition kills kindliness and that desires shape our duties.

viv02-007-p04.plain: In our busy, material lives our nerves harden and we grow callous with age, ignoring what happens around us. Yet sometimes human nature stirs and we wonder at ordinary things, and that wonder is the first step toward understanding.
viv02-007-p04.core_idea: Wondering at ordinary things begins understanding.

viv02-007-p05.plain: Call a man a fool and he punches you; speak a few gentle words to a weeping woman and her sorrow lifts and she begins to smile. Words have great power.
viv02-007-p05.core_idea: Words have great power to hurt or heal.

viv02-008-p01.plain: Life is good or bad according to how we look at it; in itself it is neither. Fire warms us and we praise it, burns us and we blame it, yet it is neutral, and so is the world.
viv02-008-p01.core_idea: The mind makes life good or evil.

viv02-008-p02.plain: We help someone, expect thanks, and are hurt when none comes. Why expect anything? Be grateful to the one you help and see him as God; without attachment we escape the pain of expectation.
viv02-008-p02.core_idea: Help others as worship, expecting no thanks.

judge.issue: Drops helping others as a privilege of worshipping God.

viv02-008-p03.plain: Don't lose sleep worrying about the world; it will go on without you. Only once you avoid fanaticism will you work well. The calm, level-headed, sympathetic and loving person does good work and so does good to himself.
viv02-008-p03.core_idea: The calm, unfanatical worker does the most good.

viv02-008-p04.plain: The world will always mix good and evil. Our duty is to sympathise with the weak and love even the wrongdoer. The world is a great moral gym where we all train to grow spiritually stronger.
viv02-008-p04.core_idea: The world is a gym for spiritual strength.

viv02-009-p01.plain: Whoever sees some evil in good actions, and some good somewhere in evil, has understood the secret of work.
viv02-009-p01.core_idea: Every action mixes good and evil.

viv02-009-p02.plain: Working for others mainly purifies us, teaching us to forget ourselves, the great lesson of life. True happiness comes from killing selfishness, and only you can make yourself happy. Every kind act shrinks our self-importance, and that is good.
viv02-009-p02.core_idea: Serving others purifies us by shrinking the self.

judge.issue: Drops thinking of ourselves as the lowest and the least.

viv02-009-p03.plain: Unselfishness is God. Someone can live in a golden palace and be wholly unselfish, and so be in God; another can live in rags with nothing, yet if selfish, be sunk deep in the world.
viv02-009-p03.core_idea: Unselfishness, not wealth or poverty, places us in God.

viv02-010-p01.plain: Our greatest weakness often passes for our greatest strength: believing others depend on me and that I can do them good. That belief is the root of all attachment, and attachment brings all our pain.
viv02-010-p01.core_idea: Thinking others depend on us breeds attachment and pain.

viv02-010-p02.plain: Some of your friends may have died this year. Has the world stopped and waited for them to return? No, it goes on.
viv02-010-p02.core_idea: The world goes on without any of us.

viv02-010-p03.plain: When you give and expect nothing, not even thanks, the person's ingratitude won't hurt you, because you never thought you had a right to anything in return.
viv02-010-p03.core_idea: Expect nothing and ingratitude cannot hurt you.

viv02-010-p04.plain: Hard as it is to grasp, in time you will learn that nothing in the universe has power over you unless you allow it. Nothing can touch the Self until the Self foolishly gives up its independence.
viv02-010-p04.core_idea: Nothing has power over you unless you allow it.

viv02-010-p05.plain: To those who haven't mastered their minds, the world seems evil or mixed. Master the mind and it becomes harmonious; some who begin calling it hell end, through self-control, by calling it heaven.
viv02-010-p05.core_idea: Master your mind and the world becomes harmonious.

viv02-010-p06.plain: No one is ever really taught by another; we each teach ourselves. The explanation of everything lies within you, and an outside teacher only offers a hint that wakes up the teacher inside.
viv02-010-p06.core_idea: The real teacher is within you.

viv02-010-p07.plain: Are you unselfish? That is the real question. If you are, you will be perfect without reading any religious book or entering any church or temple.

viv02-011-p01.plain: A river swirls in a whirlpool, then flows on free. Each life is like that: caught in the world, crying 'my family, my name, my fame', then finally breaking out to regain its freedom.
viv02-011-p01.core_idea: Every life passes through the world's whirlpool toward freedom.

judge.issue: Drops the whole universe working to escape the dream of the world.

viv02-012-p01.plain: Pain, misery, poverty, wealth and happiness are just passing conditions of this world and are not our real nature, which lies beyond all of them and beyond the senses. Still, we must keep working all the time.
viv02-012-p01.core_idea: Our true nature is beyond pleasure and pain.

viv02-012-p02.plain: Misery comes from attachment, not from work. If someone else's beautiful painting burns, we barely care; if our own burns, we are heartbroken. The difference is that we identify with one. Thinking 'I and mine' causes all misery.
viv02-012-p02.core_idea: 'I and mine' is the source of misery.

viv02-012-p03.plain: Someone who gives up home and comforts for the desert can still be deeply attached, even to his body. Non-attachment is in the mind: one person on a throne can be free, another in rags bound.
viv02-012-p03.core_idea: Non-attachment is in the mind, not outward circumstances.

viv02-012-p04.plain: Look at people enslaved by duty: no time to pray or bathe, working all day and planning tomorrow's work at night. It is a slave's life, ending in dropping dead in harness like a horse.
viv02-012-p04.core_idea: Being enslaved by duty is a slave's life.

viv02-012-p05.plain: Give whatever you have to give the world, but not out of duty or compulsion. Don't dwell on it. Everything done under compulsion builds attachment.

viv02-012-p06.plain: Seek no praise or reward for anything. The moment we do good we want credit; give to charity and we want our names in the papers. Such desires bring misery. The greatest people died unknown.
viv02-012-p06.core_idea: Seek no credit; the greatest died unknown.

viv02-013-p01.plain: The highest people are calm, quiet and unknown. They know the power of thought: even five true thoughts thought alone in a cave will live forever, travel the world, enter human hearts and inspire people to live them out.
viv02-013-p01.core_idea: True thoughts, even unspoken, outlive us and spread.

viv02-013-p02.plain: Millions of us think we are important in the world, but we all die, and within five minutes the world forgets us.
viv02-013-p02.core_idea: The world quickly forgets us all.

viv02-014-p01.plain: A lamp lives by constantly burning out; to live, you must die every moment. Life and death are the falling and rising of one wave. The pessimist looks only at the fall, the optimist only at the rise.
viv02-014-p01.core_idea: Life and death are one wave rising and falling.

fix.display_text: The lamp is constantly burning out, and that is its life. If you want to have life, you have to die every moment for it. Life and death are only different expressions of the same thing looked at from different standpoints; they are the falling and the rising of the same wave, and the two form one whole. One looks at the “fall” side and becomes a pessimist; another looks at the “rise” side and becomes an optimist.

viv02-014-p02.plain: A schoolboy cared for by his parents finds everything wonderful; his needs are simple and he is full of optimism. An old man, after much experience, grows calmer and his warmth cools a great deal.
viv02-014-p02.core_idea: Youth is hopeful; experience cools our enthusiasm.

viv02-014-p03.plain: The world is a terrible machine of wheels within wheels; once caught in it, we are lost. We think we will rest after finishing one duty, but another is already waiting. We are all dragged along by it.
viv02-014-p03.core_idea: The world's demands never let us rest.

viv02-014-p04.plain: Do good because doing good is good. Even doing good to reach heaven binds you. Any work done with the slightest selfish motive adds another chain instead of freeing you.
viv02-014-p04.core_idea: Do good for its own sake, or it binds you.

judge.issue: Drops attribution to the Karma-Yogi, stating it as a direct claim.

viv02-014-p05.plain: Every good act done without ulterior motive breaks a link in the chains that bind us. Every good thought sent out without expecting return breaks another, making us purer until we are purest of all.
viv02-014-p05.core_idea: Selfless good deeds break our chains.

viv02-014-p06.plain: The best worker works with no motive at all, not for money, fame or anything else. Whoever can do that becomes a Buddha, and from him comes the power to work in a way that transforms the world.
viv02-014-p06.core_idea: Working without motive transforms the world.

viv03-001-p01.plain: Every soul is divine at heart; the goal is to bring out that divinity by mastering nature outside and within, through work, worship, mind control or philosophy, and be free. Doctrines, rituals and temples are secondary.
viv03-001-p01.core_idea: Religion is manifesting the divinity within the soul.

judge.issue: 'Potentially divine' becomes 'divine at heart'; drops 'this is the whole of religion'.

viv03-001-p02.plain: What right has anyone to claim a soul or God without feeling or seeing them? If they exist we must experience them; otherwise better not to believe. An honest atheist is better than a hypocrite.
viv03-001-p02.core_idea: An honest atheist beats a hypocritical believer.

viv03-002-p01.plain: Looking deep into his mind, a person can find something eternally pure and perfect. Misery comes from fear and unmet desire; knowing he never dies and is already perfect, he loses both and finds bliss.
viv03-002-p01.core_idea: Knowing your undying, perfect nature ends misery.

judge.issue: Drops 'even while in this body'.

viv03-002-p02.plain: The world will give up its secrets if we knock hard enough, and that force comes from concentration. The mind's power has no limit; the more it focuses on one point, the more power it has.
viv03-002-p02.core_idea: Concentration is the secret of the mind's power.

viv03-002-p03.plain: Being human is enough. Every person has the right and the power to seek religion, to ask why, and to find the answer for themselves if they take the trouble.
viv03-002-p03.core_idea: Everyone has the right to seek truth themselves.

viv03-002-p04.plain: When the body is sick the mind gets sick too, and when the body is healthy the mind stays strong. Anger disturbs the mind, and a disturbed mind disturbs the body.
viv03-002-p04.core_idea: Body and mind affect each other.

viv03-002-p05.plain: Strength is the best guide in life. In religion as in everything, reject whatever makes you weak and have nothing to do with it.

viv03-003-p01.plain: A young plant needs a fence around it so it isn't damaged; once it becomes a tree, the fence is removed, because it can withstand anything.
viv03-003-p01.core_idea: Protect what is young until it grows strong.

viv03-003-p02.plain: Practice is essential. You can listen to me for hours every day, but without practice you won't move a step. We only understand these things by experiencing and feeling them ourselves; theories are not enough.
viv03-003-p02.core_idea: Only practice and experience bring understanding.

viv03-003-p03.plain: No one can stop the body changing even for a moment; it is a flow, like a river whose water is always new yet looks the same. Still, keep it strong and healthy: it is our best instrument.
viv03-003-p03.core_idea: The ever-changing body is still our best instrument.

viv03-004-p01.plain: Sit upright and silently wish all beings, in every direction, to be happy, peaceful and blissful. The more you do it, the better you feel; making others happy and healthy is the easiest way to be so yourself.
viv03-004-p01.core_idea: Wishing others happiness makes us happy.

viv03-004-p02.plain: The weak never reach freedom. Throw off all weakness: tell your body and your mind that they are strong, and have boundless faith and hope in yourself.
viv03-004-p02.core_idea: Throw off weakness and believe in yourself.

viv03-004-p03.plain: Everyone has to start where they are and learn to control what is closest to them. The body is closer than anything in the outside world, and the mind is closest of all.
viv03-004-p03.core_idea: Begin by mastering what is nearest: body and mind.

viv03-005-p01.plain: Everything in this world is catching, good or bad. If you are tense, strong or sick, those near you tend to become the same.
viv03-005-p01.core_idea: Strength and weakness are both contagious.

viv03-006-p01.plain: The ocean has mountainous waves, small waves and tiny bubbles, but behind them all is the infinite ocean. Likewise, great or small, every living being is connected to the same infinite store of energy behind all life.
viv03-006-p01.core_idea: Every life draws on the same infinite energy.

viv03-007-p01.plain: Begin by breathing evenly in and out to bring the body into harmony. Later let a sacred word like 'Om' flow with the breath. Then you will know real rest, deeper than sleep, calming even the most tired nerves.
viv03-007-p01.core_idea: Rhythmic breathing with a sacred word brings deep rest.

viv03-008-p01.plain: Every child is told 'be good', 'don't steal', 'don't lie', but no one teaches them how to avoid doing these things. Telling is not enough; only teaching them to control their mind really helps.
viv03-008-p01.core_idea: Teaching mind control helps more than moral rules.

viv03-008-p02.plain: The mind is hard to control, like a restless monkey made drunk, stung by a scorpion and then possessed by a demon. It is restless by nature, drunk with desire, stung by jealousy of others' success, and possessed by pride.
viv03-008-p02.core_idea: The mind is a drunk, stung, possessed monkey.

viv03-008-p03.plain: Knowledge is power: you can't control the mind until you know what it is doing. Let it run; ugly thoughts may surprise you. But with patient daily practice its wanderings calm, month by month, until it is under full control.
viv03-008-p03.core_idea: Watch the mind patiently and it calms down.

viv03-009-p01.plain: Be like the pearl oyster of the Indian fable, which catches a special raindrop, closes its shell, dives deep and patiently turns it into a pearl. First hear and understand, then shut out distractions and develop the truth within you.
viv03-009-p01.core_idea: Take in truth, then develop it quietly within.

viv03-009-p02.plain: Don't waste your energy chasing ideas for their novelty and dropping them for newer ones. Take up one thing and see it through to the end. Only someone who becomes mad about an idea sees light; nibblers achieve nothing.
viv03-009-p02.core_idea: Commit to one thing and see it through.

viv03-009-p03.plain: Success needs enormous perseverance and will. The persevering soul says it will drink the ocean and crumble mountains at will. Have that kind of energy and will, work hard, and you will reach the goal.
viv03-009-p03.core_idea: Tremendous perseverance and will reach the goal.

viv03-010-p01.plain: Experience is our only teacher. We can reason all our lives without grasping truth until we experience it. Books don't make a surgeon, and a map only makes you curious to see the country.
viv03-010-p01.core_idea: Experience is the only real teacher.

viv03-010-p02.plain: While there is desire there is no real happiness; real joy comes from looking on as a calm witness. Animals find happiness in the senses, people in the intellect, gods in contemplation; to the desireless, nature is all beauty.
viv03-010-p02.core_idea: Desireless contemplation makes the world beautiful.

viv03-010-p03.plain: Non-injury, or Ahimsa, means never causing pain to any living being by thought, word or deed. There is no higher virtue, and no greater happiness than having this harmless attitude toward all creation.
viv03-010-p03.core_idea: Non-injury is the highest virtue and happiness.

viv03-011-p01.plain: God describes his beloved devotee: one who hates no one, is a friend to all, merciful, selfless, calm in pain and pleasure, content and given to God; unafraid, unmoved by praise or blame, at home everywhere.
viv03-011-p01.core_idea: God's beloved devotee is calm, selfless and content.

judge.issue: Heavy compression drops several marks: no possessions, free from joy, unperturbing, homeless.

viv03-011-p02.plain: It is certain that every bit of hatred sent out from someone's heart returns to them in full force, and nothing can stop it; likewise every impulse of love comes back.
viv03-011-p02.core_idea: Hatred and love both return to the sender.

viv03-012-p01.plain: Staying calm is the greatest show of power. Activity is easy, like letting horses bolt; stopping them takes strength. Calm is not dullness: the calm person controls the waves of the mind. Calm is the greater strength.
viv03-012-p01.core_idea: Calm is greater strength than activity.

viv03-012-p02.plain: When the waves stop and a lake goes still, you can see its bottom. Likewise, when the mind is calm, we see our own true nature and remain ourselves instead of getting mixed up with our thoughts.
viv03-012-p02.core_idea: A calm mind reveals our true nature.

viv03-013-p01.plain: The only cure for bad habits is good counter-habits. Keep doing good and thinking holy thoughts to suppress bad impressions. Never call anyone hopeless: a person's character is a bundle of habits that new, better ones can check. Character is repeated habit, and only repeated habit can reform it.
viv03-013-p01.core_idea: Only good habits can reform bad ones.
viv03-013-p01.plain_v1: The highest people are calm, quiet and unknown. They know that even five true thoughts, thought alone in a cave, will live forever, travel the world, and inspire people to live them out.

judge_v1.issue: Plain version belongs to a different passage (calm unknown men); says nothing about habits.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Plain version belongs to a different passage; says nothing about habits.

viv03-014-p01.plain: All knowledge is within us, but it must be drawn out by another knowing being; lifeless matter cannot do it. That is why teachers have always been needed.
viv03-014-p01.core_idea: Knowledge within us needs a living teacher to awaken.

judge.issue: Drops attribution to a Yogi; states it as plain fact.

viv03-015-p01.plain: Avoid bad company, because old scars are in you and bad company reopens them. Good company brings out the hidden good impressions in you. Nothing is holier than keeping good company.
viv03-015-p01.core_idea: Good company brings out the good in you.

viv03-015-p02.plain: Sometimes for days or weeks practice goes well, the mind is calm and you progress fast. Then suddenly progress stops and you feel stuck. Keep going: all progress moves through such ups and downs.
viv03-015-p02.core_idea: Persevere; all progress rises and falls.

viv03-015-p03.plain: Every reaction of hatred is a loss to the mind, but every one controlled counts in our favour. Restraint is not loss: each time we suppress hatred or anger, good energy is stored and turned into higher powers.
viv03-015-p03.core_idea: Restraining anger stores up good energy.

viv03-016-p01.plain: Realisation is real religion; everything else, like hearing lectures, reading books or reasoning, only prepares the ground. Agreeing or disagreeing with ideas is not religion.
viv03-016-p01.core_idea: Realisation, not belief or study, is religion.

viv03-016-p02.plain: The ignorant think the body is the Soul, the learned the mind; both are wrong. Waves in the mind cover the Soul and we see it reflected in them, so we say 'I am angry', 'loving' or 'weak'.
viv03-016-p02.core_idea: We mistake the mind's passing waves for the Soul.

viv03-017-p01.plain: The senses are the horses, the mind the reins, the intellect the driver, the body the chariot, the Self the rider. If the driver can't control the horses, the chariot crashes; well controlled, it reaches the goal.
viv03-017-p01.core_idea: Control the senses through mind and intellect.

viv03-017-p02.plain: There are endless books and little time, so the secret of knowledge is to take what is essential and try to live by it.
viv03-017-p02.core_idea: Take the essential and live by it.

viv03-017-p03.plain: Surrendering the results of work to God means taking neither credit nor blame for yourself, giving both to the Lord, and being at peace.
viv03-017-p03.core_idea: Give credit and blame to God and be at peace.

viv03-017-p04.plain: When I am angry my mind becomes a huge wave of anger. At first anger and I are separate; then I become it. To truly win, such feelings must be controlled at the root, before we even notice them.
viv03-017-p04.core_idea: Control anger at its root, before it takes over.

viv03-018-p01.plain: All happiness from the senses eventually brings pain. Every pleasure makes us want more, and human desire has no limit; when desire can't be satisfied, pain follows.
viv03-018-p01.core_idea: Sense pleasures breed endless desire and pain.

viv03-018-p02.plain: King Yudhishthira said the greatest wonder is that we see people dying every moment yet think we will never die. Amid fools we think ourselves wise; amid fickleness we think our love alone will last.
viv03-018-p02.core_idea: We see death everywhere yet think we won't die.

viv03-018-p03.plain: Experience of pleasure and pain is the one great teacher, but remember that it is only experience.
viv03-018-p03.core_idea: Experience teaches, but it is only experience.

viv03-019-p01.plain: It is the people, not the building, that make a church, and we always forget that.
viv03-019-p01.core_idea: People, not buildings, make a church.

viv03-019-p02.plain: Two opposite ideas come together: that we are bound and that we are free. A wall shows our limits, yet our will feels boundless. We must believe we are free, yet at every moment find we are not.
viv03-019-p02.core_idea: We feel both bound and free at once.

viv03-020-p02.plain: Hungry for knowledge, we search everywhere, and failing, grow dissatisfied and look elsewhere. All searching is useless until we see that knowledge is within us, that no one else can help us, and that we must help ourselves.
viv03-020-p02.core_idea: Knowledge is within; we must help ourselves.

viv03-020-p03.plain: To control a big wave of anger, raise an opposite wave: think of love. An angry mother who kisses her baby finds the anger fading as love for the child rises. Love is the opposite of anger.

viv03-020-p04.plain: Every hateful thought, even one thought alone in a cave, is stored up and will return to you as misery. Hatred and jealousy come back with compound interest; once set in motion, you must bear them.
viv03-020-p04.core_idea: Hateful thoughts return to us with interest.

viv03-020-p05.plain: The first sign you are becoming religious is that you are becoming cheerful. Gloominess may be indigestion, but it is not religion.
viv03-020-p05.core_idea: Cheerfulness is the first sign of real religion.

viv03-021-p01.plain: The more time slips by unnoticed, the more concentrated we are. Absorbed in a book, we lose track of time and are surprised how many hours have passed.
viv03-021-p01.core_idea: Losing track of time shows deep concentration.

viv03-022-p01.plain: Our misery comes from ignorance, from failing to tell the real from the unreal. We mistake bad for good and the dream for reality. The Soul is the only reality, and we have forgotten it.
viv03-022-p01.core_idea: Misery comes from forgetting the Soul, the only reality.

viv03-023-p01.plain: We live surrounded by so many miracles, day and night, that we think nothing of them.
viv03-023-p01.core_idea: We ignore the miracles all around us.

viv03-023-p02.plain: Irrigation water waits in the canal behind gates; open them and it flows in by itself. Likewise all progress and power are already in everyone; perfection is our nature, and once the barrier is removed it rushes in.
viv03-023-p02.core_idea: Perfection is already within; remove the barrier.

viv03-023-p03.plain: Nothing you do can ever destroy your own glory or true nature, because nothing can touch the soul; a veil is only drawn over it, hiding its perfection.
viv03-023-p03.core_idea: Nothing you do can destroy the soul's glory.

viv03-024-p01.plain: Nature, like a kind nurse, leads the forgetful soul through every experience and many bodies until it remembers its glory, then returns for others who are lost. Through pleasure and pain, souls flow into perfection.
viv03-024-p01.core_idea: Nature guides every soul back to its own perfection.

judge.issue: Drops nature working without beginning or end and the river of souls image.

viv03-024-p02.plain: A hawk is miserable if its food is taken away but happy if it gives the food up itself; so whoever gives everything up willingly is happy.

viv03-024-p03.plain: Though you may be devoted to many institutions and teachers, take the essence from them all, as a bee takes nectar from many flowers.
viv03-024-p03.core_idea: Take the essence from every teacher.

viv04-001-p01.plain: Everyone seeks infinite power and infinite pleasure, and most human activity is that struggle. A few soon discover these cannot be reached through the senses, because the senses and body are too limited to express the Infinite.
viv04-001-p01.core_idea: The senses are too limited to reach the Infinite.

viv04-001-p02.plain: Ethics says 'not I, but you'. It asks us to drop the vain individualism we cling to while seeking the Infinite through the senses. The senses say 'me first'; ethics says 'I must put myself last'.

viv04-002-p01.plain: Conquering outer nature is grand, but conquering our inner nature is grander. Knowing the laws of the stars and planets is good; knowing the laws of human passions, feelings and will is far better.
viv04-002-p01.core_idea: Mastering inner nature is greater than outer.

viv04-002-p02.plain: As long as there is death, we must ask whether it ends everything we cling to as real. Facing that abyss, every mind asks: is this real? A lifetime's hopes vanish in a second. Time only sharpens the question.
viv04-002-p02.core_idea: Death forces us to ask what is real.

viv04-003-p01.plain: We chase the senses to be happy. The successful young man calls life real; old and unfulfilled, he calls it fate, facing a wall he cannot pass. Pleasure, wealth, power, even life itself, all pass away.
viv04-003-p01.core_idea: Everything we chase for happiness passes away.

viv04-004-p01.plain: Only someone whose life is in the whole universe truly lives; narrowing life to small things brings death and its fear. That fear ends only when you can say: I am in everything, in all lives; I am the universe.
viv04-004-p01.core_idea: Seeing yourself in all life ends fear of death.

viv04-004-p02.plain: After searching temples, churches, earth and heaven, you come back to your own soul and find that the God you sought and wept for is nearest of all, your own Self. You are already pure and perfect.
viv04-004-p02.core_idea: God is your own Self; you are already perfect.

judge.issue: Drops the call to assert and manifest your own nature.

viv04-004-p03.plain: Everyone seeks happiness, but most look for it in passing, unreal things. No one has ever found happiness in the senses or sense pleasures. Happiness is found only in the Spirit.
viv04-004-p03.core_idea: Happiness is found only in the Spirit.

viv04-004-p04.plain: As soon as I think I am just a small body, I want to protect and pamper it at others' expense, and you and I become separate. That idea of separation opens the door to all wrongdoing and all misery.
viv04-004-p04.core_idea: Feeling separate from others causes all misery.

viv04-005-p01.plain: People today praise doing and look down on thinking, but all work comes from thought. So fill your mind with the highest thoughts and ideals, keep them before you day and night, and great work will follow.
viv04-005-p01.core_idea: Great work grows from high thoughts.

viv04-005-p02.plain: Why are you crying, friend? For you there is no birth or death, no disease or misery. You are like the endless sky: coloured clouds pass over it and vanish, but the sky stays the same eternal blue.
viv04-005-p02.core_idea: You are the unchanging sky; troubles are passing clouds.

viv04-005-p03.plain: In the dark, a thief took a tree stump for a policeman, a lover for his sweetheart, a child for a ghost. It was only a stump. We see the world as we are.
viv04-005-p03.core_idea: We see the world as we are.

viv04-005-p04.plain: Don't talk about the world's wickedness and sin; grieve that you still see wickedness and sin everywhere. If you want to help the world, don't condemn it and make it weaker still.
viv04-005-p04.core_idea: Help the world by not condemning it.

viv04-005-p05.plain: Let us be brave. Know the Truth and live it. The goal may be far away, but wake up, get up, and don't stop until you reach it.
viv04-005-p05.core_idea: Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal.

viv04-006-p01.plain: Children are born optimists, and youth hardly believes in death or defeat. Then old age comes, dreams vanish, and the person turns pessimist. Pushed by nature, we swing between extremes without knowing where we go.
viv04-006-p01.core_idea: We swing from youthful hope to old despair.

viv04-006-p02.plain: Death roams the earth day and night, yet we think we will live forever. Asked what the most wonderful thing on earth was, King Yudhishthira replied that people die around us every day, yet everyone thinks they will never die.
viv04-006-p02.core_idea: We see death daily yet think we won't die.

viv04-006-p03.plain: Hiding from facts is no remedy. A hare chased by dogs puts its head down and thinks it is safe; when we escape into optimism we do the same, but it solves nothing.
viv04-006-p03.core_idea: Blind optimism is hiding, not a remedy.

viv04-007-p01.plain: As our capacity for happiness grows, so does our capacity for suffering, perhaps even faster. The more we progress, the more doors open to pain as well as pleasure.
viv04-007-p01.core_idea: Greater capacity for joy brings greater capacity for pain.

viv04-007-p02.plain: We may imagine a place of only good and no evil, only smiles and no tears, but that is impossible. Whatever can make us smile or happy can also make us cry or miserable.
viv04-007-p02.core_idea: Whatever brings joy can also bring sorrow.

viv04-007-p03.plain: What I thought good yesterday I no longer think good. Over my life my ideals changed: a fine pair of horses, a certain sweet, then a wife, children and money. Today I laugh at them all as childish nonsense.
viv04-007-p03.core_idea: Our ideals keep changing as we grow.

fix.display_text: What I thought to be good yesterday, I do not think to be good now. When I look back upon my life and see what were my ideals at different times, I find this to be so.
