At one time my ideal was to drive a strong pair of horses; at another time I thought, if I could make a certain kind of sweetmeat, I should be perfectly happy; later I imagined that I should be entirely satisfied if I had a wife and children and plenty of money. Today I laugh at all these ideals as mere childish nonsense.

viv04-007-p04.plain: A time comes when the mind wakes from its long, dreary dream, like a child leaving play to go back to its mother. It learns that indulging desire only feeds it, as butter feeds a fire.
viv04-007-p04.core_idea: Indulging desire only feeds it, like fire.

viv04-007-p05.plain: Fanatics can't really work; they waste three-quarters of their energy. It is the calm, level-headed, practical person who gets work done.
viv04-007-p05.core_idea: Calm, practical people work; fanatics waste energy.

viv04-008-p01.plain: Someone who says he will work and be happy once the world becomes entirely good is like a man sitting by the Ganges saying he will cross once all the water has flowed into the sea.
viv04-008-p01.core_idea: Waiting for a perfect world means never acting.

viv04-008-p02.plain: We judge others by our own ideals, but everyone should be judged by theirs. Most quarrels come from judging others' gods, ideals and motives by our own. Someone may do what I would do for an entirely different reason.
viv04-008-p02.core_idea: Judge others by their ideals, not yours.

viv04-008-p03.plain: One impulse in the mind says 'do', and behind it another voice says 'don't'. Our ideas constantly push outward through the senses, but behind them a tiny, faint voice says 'don't go outside'.
viv04-008-p03.core_idea: A quiet inner voice pulls us back from the senses.

viv04-009-p01.plain: We cannot live together without putting up with each other and holding ourselves back. All society rests on restraint, and anyone who hasn't learned to bear and forbear lives a very miserable life.
viv04-009-p01.core_idea: Living together requires bearing and forbearing.

viv04-009-p02.plain: We have strong cravings we can't satisfy; every step forward brings a blow, like Tantalus. Our high ideals can't find expression and the crowd crushes us. Yet giving up ideals to just survive makes us brutish. Neither way brings happiness.
viv04-009-p02.core_idea: Neither chasing nor abandoning ideals brings happiness.

viv04-010-p01.plain: What you don't set free will never grow. Thinking you can guide others' growth while keeping all freedom for yourself is a dangerous lie that has held back millions. Liberty is the only condition of growth.
viv04-010-p01.core_idea: Freedom is the only condition of growth.

viv04-010-p02.plain: Denouncing an evil won't remove it. Go to the root: find the cause and remove it, and the effect will go too.
viv04-010-p02.core_idea: Remove the cause, not just denounce the evil.

viv04-010-p03.plain: Whoever sees the One running through this world of many things, finds the One Infinite Life in this world of death, and the One Light in this world of ignorance, has eternal peace, and no one else.
viv04-010-p03.core_idea: Eternal peace belongs to those who see the One.

viv04-010-p04.plain: We arrive crying and fight our way through life's endless ocean as best we can, with ages behind us and vast stretches ahead, until death takes us off the field, and we don't know whether we won or lost.
viv04-010-p04.core_idea: We struggle through life not knowing if we win.

viv04-010-p05.plain: We seek happiness where it can't be found. Though told for ages it is futile, we learn only by experience, and not even then. Like moths into a flame we keep hurling ourselves at sense pleasures until we die cheated.
viv04-010-p05.core_idea: Like moths, we keep chasing pleasures that burn us.

viv04-011-p01.plain: You can't hide rotting flesh under roses for long; the roses fade and it is worse than before. So with our lives: we may cover festering sores with gold cloth, but one day it is removed.
viv04-011-p01.core_idea: You cannot hide decay for long.

viv04-011-p02.plain: Today's beautiful, hopeful young person is tomorrow's old veteran. Hopes, joys and pleasures will die like blossoms in tomorrow's frost.
viv04-011-p02.core_idea: Youth and its joys fade like blossoms.

viv04-011-p03.plain: One person stumbles more than another; we call the one who stumbles more bad and the one who stumbles less good. Good and bad are not different things but the same, differing only in degree.
viv04-011-p03.core_idea: Good and bad differ in degree, not kind.

viv04-013-p01.plain: A small fish fleeing enemies in the water escaped by growing wings and becoming a bird. It didn't change the water or the air; it changed itself. Change always happens within.

viv04-014-p01.plain: Life's great inspirations come through the heart. Better a little heart and no brain than all brain and no heart, which withers. Yet heart alone falls into pitfalls; we need heart and head together.
viv04-014-p01.core_idea: We need heart and head together.

viv04-014-p02.plain: The Lord is equally present in life and death, in happiness and misery. The whole world is full of the Lord. Open your eyes and see Him.
viv04-014-p02.core_idea: The Lord is present everywhere; open your eyes.

viv04-015-p01.plain: What makes us miserable? Desire causes all our suffering. You want something, don't get it, and you are distressed. Without desire there is no suffering.
viv04-015-p01.core_idea: Desire is the cause of all suffering.

viv04-015-p02.plain: We've done many things we wish we hadn't, yet they taught us much. I'm glad of my good deeds and my many mistakes, since each was a lesson. I am the result of all I have done and thought.
viv04-015-p02.core_idea: Our mistakes are lessons; we are their sum.

viv04-015-p03.plain: Jesus said the kingdom of heaven is within you, and so do the Vedanta and every great teacher. In ignorance we roamed the world weeping for the truth, while it lived all along in our own hearts.
viv04-015-p03.core_idea: The truth we seek is within our hearts.

judge.issue: Drops 'there alone can we find it' and the eyes-to-see saying.

viv04-015-p04.plain: Who enjoys a painting, the seller or the viewer? The seller is busy counting his profit and watching the bids. The one who enjoys it is the person who came with no intention of buying or selling and simply looks.
viv04-015-p04.core_idea: Only those who want nothing truly enjoy.

viv04-015-p05.plain: Plunging into foolish luxury without knowing the truth misses the goal. So does cursing the world, fleeing to a forest and starving body and feeling until you are harsh and dried up. Both extremes lose the way.
viv04-015-p05.core_idea: Both indulgence and harsh self-denial miss the goal.

viv04-015-p06.plain: We are dying of thirst beside the mightiest river and of hunger beside heaps of food. The universe is full of bliss, yet we are in it all the time and keep mistaking it.
viv04-015-p06.core_idea: Bliss surrounds us, yet we fail to see it.

viv04-015-p07.plain: It's easy to talk about seeing God in everyone. But when a strong man shoves me onto the pavement, I jump up with clenched fists, the thought gone. Instead of meeting God, I see the devil.
viv04-015-p07.core_idea: Seeing God in everyone vanishes at the first shove.

viv04-015-p08.plain: In Aesop's fable, a stag boasts of his strength, then flees when dogs bark; his confidence vanishes at the sound. We are the same: bold in our resolutions, but we run when trial and temptation bark.
viv04-015-p08.core_idea: Our confidence vanishes when trials come.

fix.display_text: You all remember how in Æsop’s Fables a fine stag is looking at his form reflected in a lake and is saying to his young one, “How powerful I am, look at my splendid head, look at my limbs, how strong and muscular they are; and how swiftly I can run.” In the meantime he hears the barking of dogs in the distance, and immediately takes to his heels, and after he has run several miles, he comes back panting. The young one says, “You just told me how strong you were, how was it that when the dog barked, you ran away?” “Yes, my son; but when the dogs bark all my confidence vanishes.” Such is the case with us. We think highly of humanity, we feel ourselves strong and valiant, we make grand resolves; but when the “dogs” of trial and temptation bark, we are like the stag in the fable.

viv04-015-p09.plain: Most people grope through life with no ideal at all. If someone with an ideal makes a thousand mistakes, someone without one makes fifty thousand. So it is better to have an ideal.
viv04-015-p09.core_idea: Better to have an ideal, even with mistakes.

viv04-015-p10.plain: Don't mind failures; they are natural, the beauty and poetry of life, which would be worthless without struggle. Only a cow never lies. Hold to your ideal, and if you fail a thousand times, try once more.
viv04-015-p10.core_idea: Fail a thousand times, then try once more.

judge.issue: 'Only a cow never lies' loses the point that only a cow, never a man, is faultless.

viv04-017-p01.plain: Nachiketas told Death: these pleasures last a day and wear out the senses, and even the longest life is short. Keep your horses, chariots, dances and songs. Wealth cannot satisfy a person, nor can we keep it when we face you; we live only as long as you wish.
viv04-017-p01.core_idea: Wealth and pleasure cannot satisfy a human being

extension.text: Nachiketas said, “These are merely things of a day, O Death, they wear away the energy of all the sense-organs. Even the longest life is very short. These horses and chariots, dances and songs, may remain with Thee. Man cannot be satisfied by wealth. Can we retain wealth when we behold Thee? We shall live only so long as Thou desires”.

viv04-017-p01.plain_v1: Nachiketas tells Death that riches, pleasures and even a long life are short-lived and drain the senses; Death can keep them, because wealth can never satisfy a person.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the closing point that life lasts only as long as Death wills, and wealth is futile before him.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops that wealth cannot be kept before Death and we live as long as Death wills.

viv04-017-p02.plain: Once you see religion and God more vividly than you see the outside world, nothing can shake your belief, just as no one can make you doubt a country you have visited. That is real faith.
viv04-017-p02.core_idea: Real faith comes from direct experience of God

viv04-017-p03.plain: Joy and sorrow keep vanishing: as a child he thought driving a cab would be perfect happiness, and now he does not. So which joy will you cling to?
viv04-017-p03.core_idea: Every joy we chase keeps changing and vanishing

viv04-018-p01.plain: What feels like pleasure today may feel like pain tomorrow. The same fire that warms us can burn us, and that is not the fire's fault.
viv04-018-p01.core_idea: The same thing can bring pleasure or pain

judge.issue: Drops 'under better circumstances', a small loss of nuance.

viv04-018-p02.plain: Picture the Self as the rider, the body as the chariot, the intellect as driver, the mind as reins and the senses as horses. Keep senses and mind in control and you reach God; lose control and you are destroyed.
viv04-018-p02.core_idea: Control the senses and mind to reach the goal

judge.issue: Simplifies the intellect's role and 'the state of the Omnipresent' to 'reach God'.

viv04-018-p03.plain: The path is like walking on a razor's edge, long and dangerous, but keep going and do not lose heart. Wake up, get up, and do not stop until you reach the goal.
viv04-018-p03.core_idea: Keep striving on the hard path until the goal

viv04-018-p04.plain: Desire causes all misery: it keeps you like a beggar, always wanting more. As your power to satisfy desires grows steadily, the desires themselves multiply far faster.
viv04-018-p04.core_idea: Desire always outgrows our power to satisfy it

viv04-019-p01.plain: Giving up the self is the basis of true life; every good and truly alive moment comes when we are not thinking of ourselves. The small, separate self has to die.
viv04-019-p01.core_idea: True life comes from forgetting the separate self

judge.issue: 'Renunciation' narrowed to 'giving up the self'; slight loss of breadth.

viv04-019-p02.plain: In this world, misery follows every happiness like a shadow, and death follows life. They belong together because they are not opposites but two sides of one thing, as are sorrow and joy, good and evil.
viv04-019-p02.core_idea: Happiness and misery are two sides of one thing

viv04-020-p01.plain: A young man left poor after his father died was told by a clergyman that everything happens for our good. Such comfort is like gold leaf over an old sore: an admission of weakness and absurdity.
viv04-020-p01.core_idea: Saying all suffering is good is empty comfort

fix.display_text: I remember when I was young, a young man’s father died and left him poorly off, with a large family to support, and he found that his father’s friends were unwilling to help him. He had a conversation with a clergyman who offered this consolation, “Oh, it is all good, all is sent for our good.” That is the old method of trying to put a piece of gold leaf on an old sore. It is a confession of weakness, of absurdity.

viv04-020-p02.plain: Be good and show mercy to those who suffer. But do not try to patch the world up, because nothing will cure it; go beyond it.
viv04-020-p02.core_idea: Be kind, but seek to go beyond the world

viv04-020-p03.plain: Life is hard and real; push through it bravely, however unyielding it seems. It does not matter, because the soul is stronger.
viv04-020-p03.core_idea: The soul is stronger than life's hardships

viv04-020-p04.plain: You cause your own suffering and make good and evil; you cover your eyes and complain it is dark. Take your hands away and see the light: you are radiant and already perfect, and always were.
viv04-020-p04.core_idea: You are already perfect; stop covering your eyes

viv04-020-p05.plain: Moving to a cave, a forest or Varanasi did not bring him clarity, because the same trouble followed him everywhere. We make our own worlds: if I am evil, the whole world looks evil to me.
viv04-020-p05.core_idea: We carry our own world wherever we go

viv04-021-p01.plain: He wants to know the heart of life itself, what it truly is, not just how it works or what it looks like. He wants the why of everything and leaves the how to children.
viv04-021-p01.core_idea: Seek the why of life, not just how

viv04-021-p02.plain: A huge river is carrying all of us toward the ocean. Though we sometimes drift aimlessly like bits of straw and paper, in the end we will surely reach the Ocean of Life and Bliss.
viv04-021-p02.core_idea: All of us will reach the ocean of bliss

viv04-022-p01.plain: One bright idea shines through the superstition of every country and religion: human beings are divine, and divinity is our true nature.
viv04-022-p01.core_idea: Human beings are divine by nature

viv04-022-p02.plain: Fire lies hidden in flint and dry wood until friction draws it out. In the same way freedom and purity are the very nature of every soul, not qualities, since qualities can be gained and lost.
viv04-022-p02.core_idea: Freedom and purity are the soul's very nature

viv04-022-p03.plain: Why search for something you never lost, when you are already pure and free? If you think you are free, you are free right now; if you think you are bound, bound you will be.
viv04-022-p03.core_idea: You are free if you think you are

viv04-022-p04.plain: The moment you say you are bound, weak or helpless, you bring trouble on yourself and add another chain. Do not say it, and do not think it.
viv04-022-p04.core_idea: Calling yourself weak binds you further

viv04-022-p05.plain: Vedanta says weakness is the one cause of misery: we lie, steal, kill, suffer and even die because we are weak. Where nothing weakens us, there is neither death nor sorrow.
viv04-022-p05.core_idea: Weakness is the one cause of suffering

viv04-023-p01.plain: However frightening it seems now, one day we will each look back and smile at the superstitions that hid the pure, eternal soul, and say gladly and truly: I am free, always was and always will be.
viv04-023-p01.core_idea: One day we will know we were always free

viv04-023-p02.plain: Living up to the ideal of being pure is hard, but a child still looks up at the distant sky. Failing to reach truth at once is no reason to drink poison by turning to weakness and superstition.
viv04-023-p02.core_idea: A hard ideal is no reason to choose weakness

judge.issue: Compresses the nectar/poison and darkness questions; loses some nuance.

viv04-023-p03.plain: We are at our best when all responsibility is ours, as anyone handed a baby turns selfless. With no devil to blame and no personal God to carry our burdens, I alone make my fate, good or bad.
viv04-023-p03.core_idea: Full responsibility brings out our best

judge.issue: Compresses; loses the point that responsibility transforms character.

viv04-024-p01.plain: Water runs down mountains to the ocean, rises as vapour and returns, over and over. All life and everything we know moves this way, like breathing in and out: each wave has its hollow, each hollow its wave.
viv04-024-p01.core_idea: All existence moves in cycles of rising and falling

viv04-024-p02.plain: A seed does not become a tree at once. It rests and works unseen beneath the soil, breaks apart and seems to decay, and new life grows out of that decay.
viv04-024-p02.core_idea: New life grows out of apparent decay

viv04-024-p03.plain: O Lord, you are the man and the woman, the strong youth and the old man on crutches; you are in everything, and you are everything.
viv04-024-p03.core_idea: God is in and is everything

viv04-025-p01.plain: People have always asked whether anything in this fleeting life is lasting: does something survive when the body dies and burns to ash, and if so, where does it come from and where does it go?
viv04-025-p01.core_idea: Does anything in us survive death?

viv04-025-p02.plain: The soul does not have knowledge, existence or happiness; it is knowledge, existence and happiness itself. Anything that merely has these has borrowed them and reflects them.
viv04-025-p02.core_idea: The soul is knowledge, existence and happiness itself

viv04-025-p03.plain: None of us came from nothing or will return to nothing. We have always existed and always will, and no power anywhere can undo our existence.
viv04-025-p03.core_idea: We have always existed and always will

viv04-026-p01.plain: A child learning piano must first watch every key, but after months and years the playing becomes almost automatic. What first took conscious effort later needs no effort of will.
viv04-026-p01.core_idea: Practice turns conscious effort into instinct

viv04-026-p02.plain: Like eyes that see others but not themselves, we miss our own faults and blame people, God or fate. But we reap what we sow: we make our own fate, and no one else earns blame or praise.

viv04-026-p03.plain: The wind fills only ships with sails raised; God's mercy blows day and night for saint and sinner alike, so it is not His fault that some are happy and some not. We make our own destiny.
viv04-026-p03.core_idea: God's mercy is for all; we make our destiny

viv04-026-p04.plain: God's endless mercy is open to everyone, always, and how we use it is up to us. Blame neither people nor God; when you suffer, blame yourself and try to do better.
viv04-026-p04.core_idea: When you suffer, blame no one but yourself

viv04-027-p01.plain: Admit your suffering is your own doing, so you alone can undo it. Stand up, be brave and strong, take full responsibility for your destiny, and know all the strength you need is within you.
viv04-027-p01.core_idea: You made your misery, so you can undo it

judge.issue: Drops the reasoning that what others create one cannot destroy.

viv04-027-p02.plain: Let the past go. The whole future lies ahead, and every word, thought and act builds up for you: bad ones lie in wait like tigers, while good ones stand ready like a hundred thousand angels to defend you forever.
viv04-027-p02.core_idea: Every thought and deed shapes your future

viv04-027-p03.plain: In the rush of life we forget, but when someone we love dies suddenly, the noise stops for a moment and the soul asks the old questions: what comes after this, and what becomes of the soul?
viv04-027-p03.core_idea: A loved one's death stirs questions about the soul

viv04-027-p04.plain: Nothing moves in a straight line; everything moves in a circle. So no soul can go downhill forever: everything must complete the circle and return to its source.
viv04-027-p04.core_idea: Every soul must return to its source

viv04-028-p01.plain: A cloud passing the moon makes the moon seem to move, and from a train the land seems to fly. Likewise you are not really coming or going, born or reborn; you are infinite, ever-present, beyond cause and ever free.
viv04-028-p01.core_idea: You are not born or reborn; you are infinite

viv04-028-p02.plain: Wherever there are two, there is fear, danger and conflict. When everything is One, when everything is God, who is there to hate or fight?
viv04-028-p02.core_idea: Where all is One, there is no one to fight

viv04-028-p03.plain: You are the One Being in the universe, so what can make you weak or afraid? Stand up and be free; whatever thought or word makes you weak and fearful is the only evil, and must be avoided.
viv04-028-p03.core_idea: Whatever makes you weak and afraid is evil

viv04-028-p04.plain: Even if suns fall, moons crumble and whole star systems are destroyed, what is that to you? Stand firm like a rock; you cannot be destroyed.
viv04-028-p04.core_idea: You are indestructible; nothing can frighten you

viv04-028-p05.plain: Foolish people call you sinners and you sit in a corner weeping, but calling you sinners is foolish and wicked. You are all God; how can you see God and call Him a mere man?
viv04-028-p05.core_idea: You are not sinners; you are God

viv04-028-p06.plain: When you help a poor person, do not feel the slightest pride. Helping is your worship, not something to be proud of.
viv04-028-p06.core_idea: Helping the poor is worship, not pride

viv04-029-p01.plain: In life we can see that each of us shapes our future every day: today we decide what tomorrow will be, tomorrow we decide the day after, and so on.
viv04-029-p01.core_idea: Each day we shape the next

viv04-029-p02.plain: The sense of me and mine is the root of all evil in the world. A dualist says his child and property belong not to him but to God, and everything should be held that way.
viv04-029-p02.core_idea: Me and mine is the root of evil

viv04-030-p01.plain: God draws every soul as a magnet draws a needle. The dualist says a needle caked in clay will not move toward the magnet until the clay is washed off; the soul's evil deeds are that dirt.
viv04-030-p01.core_idea: Evil deeds cover the soul's pull toward God

viv04-030-p02.plain: We have made ourselves weak, always wanting something to lean on like small plants needing a stake. Many want a comfortable religion; very few ask for truth, fewer dare to learn it, and fewest dare to live it.
viv04-030-p02.core_idea: Few dare to seek and live the truth

viv04-030-p03.plain: A sick man keeps answering a knock and finding no one, until he realises it was his own heartbeat. So, after seeking God in temples, rivers and heavens, a person finds God is his own Self.
viv04-030-p03.core_idea: The God we seek outside is our own Self

viv04-031-p01.plain: You are never inside illusion; illusion passes before you. As clouds of every colour come and go across the blue sky and leave it unchanged, you remain forever pure and perfect.
viv04-031-p01.core_idea: Like the sky, you stay pure as illusions pass

viv04-031-p02.plain: When a person sees himself as one with the Infinite and all separateness melts away, fear, sorrow, jealousy and ill will vanish. Who is left to fear or resent, when there is no one in the universe but I?
viv04-031-p02.core_idea: In oneness, fear, sorrow and jealousy vanish

viv04-031-p03.plain: Harm no one and dismiss no one's view; meet people where they are and, if you can, help them higher, but never hurt or tear down. Everyone will reach truth in the end.
viv04-031-p03.core_idea: Meet people where they are; harm no one

viv04-032-p01.plain: Every act and thought leaves an impression on the mind, called samskara in Sanskrit, and all these together form the powerful force we call character. Your character is what you have made of yourself through your actions.
viv04-032-p01.core_idea: Character is built from every act and thought

viv04-032-p02.plain: Like a caterpillar trapped in the cocoon it spun from its own thread, we have tied ourselves up in our own actions. We set the wheel of cause and effect turning, and now it crushes us.
viv04-032-p02.core_idea: We are trapped by our own actions

viv04-033-p01.plain: The mind is like a lake and each thought a wave on it. Thought-waves rise and seem to vanish, but they never disappear completely; they become subtler and wait, ready to rise again when called.
viv04-033-p01.core_idea: Thoughts never vanish; they wait to rise again

viv04-034-p01.plain: To most people nature looks like nothing but a whirling, shifting mass of change. Few ever glimpse the calm sea underneath; to us the universe seems only tossing waves.
viv04-034-p01.core_idea: Few glimpse the calm beneath constant change

viv04-034-p02.plain: A wave is not truly different from the sea; only its shape and the name we give it set it apart. Take away name and form, and it is the same sea.
viv04-034-p02.core_idea: Only name and form separate wave from sea

viv04-035-p01.plain: When I read a book, the pages turn, not I; nature is such a book before the soul, scene after scene, while the soul stays the same forever. Birth and death belong to nature, not to you.
viv04-035-p01.core_idea: Nature changes; the soul stays the same

viv04-035-p02.plain: The worst lie you can tell yourself is that you were born a sinner or wicked. Only the person who sees a sinner in someone else is a sinner.
viv04-035-p02.core_idea: Only one who sees sinners is a sinner

viv04-036-p01.plain: Crossing a desert, he saw lovely lakes daily until one vanished as he went to drink: a mirage, which he then kept seeing but knew was false. We all travel through the world's mirage without knowing it.
viv04-036-p01.core_idea: The world is a mirage we do not recognise

viv04-036-p02.plain: Realising truth and merely talking about it are worlds apart; anyone can talk, even parrots. Philosophies, books and churches help in their way, but they fall away once realisation comes, as maps do when you see the country itself.
viv04-036-p02.core_idea: Talking about truth is not realising it

viv04-036-p03.plain: How can you see evil, a thief or a murderer, unless it is already sitting in your own heart? Be good, and evil will disappear for you.
viv04-036-p03.core_idea: Be good and evil disappears for you

viv05-001-p01.plain: Bhakti-Yoga is a sincere search for the Lord that begins, goes on and ends in love. A single moment of wildly intense love for God brings eternal freedom.
viv05-001-p01.core_idea: One moment of intense love for God frees us

viv05-001-p02.plain: In every religion and country, weak and immature minds can love their own ideal only by hating every other one.
viv05-001-p02.core_idea: Weak minds love their ideal by hating others

viv05-001-p03.plain: A bird needs two wings and a tail to fly. Knowledge is one wing, love of God the other, and yoga is the tail that keeps the balance.
viv05-001-p03.core_idea: Knowledge, love and yoga must work together

viv05-001-p04.plain: A prayer: as I keep meditating on You, may I never lose the same unfailing love that ignorant people feel for passing pleasures of the senses.
viv05-001-p04.core_idea: Love God as fiercely as others love pleasure

judge.issue: Wording is ambiguous: could read as wanting love of sense objects rather than that intensity turned to God.

viv05-002-p01.plain: A little practice of right living and spiritual self-realisation is worth more than tons of empty talk and silly sentiment.
viv05-002-p01.core_idea: A little practice outweighs much empty talk

viv05-002-p02.plain: Every soul will be perfect in the end; what we are comes from past thoughts and acts, and what we will be from what we do now. Yet we mostly need outside help to awaken the soul's higher powers.
viv05-002-p02.core_idea: We shape our destiny, but need outside help

fix.display_text: Every soul is destined to be perfect, and every being, in the end, will attain the state of perfection. Whatever we are now is the result of our acts and thoughts in the past; and whatever we shall be in the future will be the result of what we think and do now. But this, the shaping of our own destinies, does not preclude our receiving help from outside; nay, in the vast majority of cases such help is absolutely necessary. When it comes, the higher powers and possibilities of the soul are quickened, spiritual life is awakened, growth is animated, and man becomes holy and perfect in the end.

judge.issue: Softens 'absolutely necessary' help to 'mostly need'; drops becoming holy and perfect.

viv05-003-p01.plain: We can study books our whole lives and become very clever, yet find we have not grown spiritually at all. Great intellect does not always bring equal spiritual growth.
viv05-003-p01.core_idea: Intellect does not bring spiritual growth

viv05-003-p02.plain: Often when someone we love dies, we feel the world slipping away and resolve to seek something higher and become religious. In a few days the feeling passes, and we are left just where we were.
viv05-003-p02.core_idea: Grief's urge toward religion soon fades

viv05-003-p03.plain: Truly longing for religion is hard; talks and books do not prove it, only a constant fight with your lower nature until the longing is real. It may take many lifetimes, but whoever perseveres will succeed.
viv05-003-p03.core_idea: Real spiritual longing takes endless persistent struggle

judge.issue: Drops that success may come at once and the call to wait patiently.

viv05-003-p04.plain: Ramakrishna told of men in a mango orchard who counted and debated leaves, twigs and branches, while one sensible man simply ate the mangoes. Was he not the wise one?
viv05-003-p04.core_idea: Taste the fruit instead of counting leaves

fix.display_text: Bhagavân Ramakrishna used to tell a story of some men who went into a mango orchard and busied themselves in counting the leaves, the twigs, and the branches, examining their colour, comparing their size, and noting down everything most carefully, and then got up a learned discussion on each of these topics, which were undoubtedly highly interesting to them. But one of them, more sensible than the others, did not care for all these things, and instead thereof, began to eat the mango fruit. And was he not wise?

viv05-004-p01.plain: Religion, the highest wisdom, cannot be bought or learned from books. Search the Himalayas, the seabed or Tibet and you will not find it until your heart is ready and your teacher has come.
viv05-004-p01.core_idea: Wisdom comes when the heart is ready

viv05-005-p01.plain: Very few combine wide sympathy with intense love: liberal groups lose their fervour and become social clubs, while narrow sects love their ideal by hating everyone else. If only more people were both intense and broad.
viv05-005-p01.core_idea: Few combine intense love with wide sympathy

viv05-005-p02.plain: The young plant of spirituality dies if exposed too early to constantly changing ideas. Some, calling it open-mindedness, chase new ideals for the thrill like a craving for drink, and religion becomes a mental drug.
viv05-005-p02.core_idea: Chasing endless new ideals kills spiritual growth

viv05-006-p01.plain: At first it is very hard to make the mind think of the Lord all the time, but each effort makes the power stronger. As Krishna says in the Gita, it comes through practice and non-attachment.

viv05-006-p02.plain: Anyone can do a good deed on impulse or out of superstition, but the true lover of humanity envies no one. The world's so-called great people grow jealous of one another over a little name, fame or gold.
viv05-006-p02.core_idea: True love of humanity is free of jealousy

viv05-006-p03.plain: Inner purity alone is better when outward rituals are impractical, but woe to anyone or any nation that forgets the inner essentials and clings to forms. Forms matter only while they express inner life; otherwise destroy them.
viv05-006-p03.core_idea: Forms matter only while they express inner life

judge.issue: 'Crush them out without mercy' softened to 'destroy them'.

viv05-006-p04.plain: In the West a religious person is pictured gloomy and long-faced, but such people need a doctor; they are not yogis. It is the cheerful mind that perseveres and the strong mind that cuts through a thousand difficulties.

viv05-006-p05.plain: Too much laughter unfits the mind for serious thought and wastes its energy, just as too much gloom does. A strong will yields less to emotion, and spiritual realisation comes only when the mind is steady, peaceful and balanced.
viv05-006-p05.core_idea: Realisation needs a steady, balanced mind

viv06-001-p01.plain: When the moon shines, the stars fade, and when the sun shines, the moon fades. The renunciation that devotion needs comes not by killing desire but naturally, as weaker lights fade before a growing brighter one.
viv06-001-p01.core_idea: Love of God makes lesser desires fade naturally

viv06-001-p02.plain: When a ship nears a magnetic rock, its iron bolts are pulled out and its planks float free. In the same way God's grace loosens what binds the soul, and the soul becomes free.
viv06-001-p02.core_idea: God's grace loosens what binds the soul

viv06-001-p03.plain: The same love, rightly or wrongly directed, makes one person give everything to the poor and another kill and rob. Like fire that can cook a meal or burn a child, the difference lies in how it is used.
viv06-001-p03.core_idea: Love's direction makes it good or harmful

judge.issue: Drops that the giver loves others as much as the robber loves himself.

viv06-001-p04.plain: Pull away from the world's petty selfish clingings and don't make humanity the centre of your interests. Stand apart as a witness and student, unattached to people, and watch love work itself out. Frictions and falls are passing; outside the world's current you see God showing Himself as Love everywhere.
viv06-001-p04.core_idea: As a witness, see God as Love everywhere
viv06-001-p04.plain_v1: Step back from the world's petty selfish attachments and watch life as a witness and a student. Inside the current you feel the friction, falls and fights; standing outside it, you see God showing Himself as Love through countless channels.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the hard saying not to make humanity the centre, and non-attachment toward people.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops not making humanity the centre and non-attachment to people.

viv06-001-p05.plain: The Lord is a great magnet and we are iron filings, always drawn toward Him. All our struggle in life, even when people do not know it, is meant to bring us to Him and make us one with Him.
viv06-001-p05.core_idea: All life's struggle draws us toward God

judge.issue: 'Fools do not know' softened to 'even when people do not know it'.

viv06-002-p01.plain: Pain at lacking money and joy at a handful of coins are feelings aimed wrongly. Pain at not yet reaching God leads to salvation, and joy should serve the highest ideal; the same goes for every feeling.
viv06-002-p01.core_idea: Turn every feeling toward the highest ideal

fix.display_text: We find that pleasures and pains are very common and oft-recurring feelings in our lives. When a man feels pain because he has not wealth or some such worldly thing, he is giving a wrong direction to the feeling. Still pain has its uses. Let a man feel pain that he has not reached the Highest, that he has not reached God, and that pain will be to his salvation. When you become glad that you have a handful of coins, it is a wrong direction given to the faculty of joy; it should be given a higher direction, it must be made to serve the Highest Ideal. Pleasure in that kind of ideal must surely be our highest joy. This same thing is true of all our other feelings.

viv06-002-p02.plain: Love of God surely brings love of everyone in the universe. The closer we come to God, the more we see all things in Him, and the heart becomes an endless fountain of love.
viv06-002-p02.core_idea: Loving God brings love for everyone

viv06-002-p03.plain: Intense love for God brings total surrender, the sense that nothing that happens is against us, so the devotee welcomes pain, misery, even death as from the Beloved. Such uncomplaining acceptance is worth more than heroic deeds.
viv06-002-p03.core_idea: Loving surrender welcomes even pain as God's gift

judge.issue: Loses explicit resignation to the will of God and ceasing to distinguish pleasure and pain.

viv06-002-p04.plain: We can care for our bodies for a while, but they must go. Since death is the one certainty, blessed are those whose bodies are spent serving others; better to die in a good cause than a bad one.
viv06-002-p04.core_idea: Spend your body in service of others

viv06-003-p01.plain: The delusion that we are only our body, and must protect and please it at all costs, breeds all the world's selfishness. Once you know you are other than your body, there is nothing to fight for and selfishness dies.
viv06-003-p01.core_idea: Believing we are the body breeds selfishness

viv06-003-p02.plain: Let things come as they will; that is what Thy will be done means, not struggling while assuming God wants our weaknesses and ambitions. If good comes even from our selfish efforts, that is God's business.
viv06-003-p02.core_idea: Thy will be done means letting things come

viv06-003-p03.plain: Human love usually thrives only when returned, but rarely it goes on without return, like the moth that loves the flame and dies in it. Loving simply because love's nature is to love is the highest, most unselfish love.
viv06-003-p03.core_idea: The highest love asks nothing in return

fix.display_text: Ordinarily human love is seen to flourish only in places where it is returned; where love is not returned for love, cold indifference is the natural result. There are, however, rare instances in which we may notice love exhibiting itself even where there is no return of love. We may compare this kind of love, for purposes of illustration, to the love of the moth for the fire; the insect loves the fire, falls into it, and dies. It is indeed in the nature of this insect to love so. To love because it is the nature of love to love is undeniably the highest and the most unselfish manifestation of love that may be seen in the world.

viv06-003-p04.plain: Where something is wanted in return, there is no real love, only shopkeeping. While we expect favours from God for our worship, true love cannot grow; those who worship for favours will stop when the favours do not come.
viv06-003-p04.core_idea: Love that seeks a reward is shopkeeping

fix.display_text: Wherever there is any seeking for something in return, there can be no real love; it becomes a mere matter of shop-keeping. As long as there is in us any idea of deriving this or that favour from God in return for our respect and allegiance to Him, so long there can be no true love growing in our hearts. Those who worship God because they wish Him to bestow favours on them are sure not to worship Him if those favours are not forthcoming.

viv06-003-p05.plain: Begging is not love's language, and worshipping God even for salvation is just as low; love is for love's sake. As a beautiful landscape asks nothing yet fills you with calm and bliss, the devotee simply loves.
viv06-003-p05.core_idea: Love is for love's sake, seeking no reward

viv06-003-p06.plain: Love conquers fear: a mother who flees a barking dog will leap into a lion's mouth to save her child. Fear comes from making ourselves small and separate; the less we think ourselves insignificant, the less we fear.

viv06-004-p01.plain: Some say selfishness drives all human action, but selfishness is just love narrowed. When I see myself as including the whole universe, there is no selfishness; when I mistake myself for something small, my love shrinks.

viv06-004-p02.plain: As you open your heart to a friend who never scolds but always helps, equal love can flow between you and a friendly God. Then God is a near friend to whom you can safely tell your deepest secrets.
viv06-004-p02.core_idea: God can be a close, trusted friend

viv06-004-p03.plain: The world is a playground and God is our eternal playmate. Misery comes only when we forget it is play and take life's passing events too seriously; see it as a stage where we help Him play, and misery ends.
viv06-004-p03.core_idea: See life as God's play and misery ends

fix.display_text: The world is just a playground, and we are here having good fun, having a game; and God is with us playing all the while, and we are with Him playing. God is our eternal playmate. How beautifully He is playing! The play is finished when the cycle comes to an end. There is rest for a shorter or longer time; again all come out and play. It is only when you forget that it is all play and that you are also helping in the play, it is only then that misery and sorrows come. Then the heart becomes heavy, then the world weighs upon you with tremendous power. But as soon as you give up the serious idea of reality as the characteristic of the changing incidents of the three minutes of life and know it to be but a stage on which we are playing, helping Him to play, at once misery ceases for you.

viv06-005-p01.plain: The great love we feel for a child, given blindly to any human being, sooner or later brings pain. That pain wakes us up to give our love to the Highest One, who never dies or changes.
viv06-005-p01.core_idea: Give your love to the unchanging God

viv06-005-p02.plain: God is the goal of all our feelings, so if you must be angry, be angry with Him, your Beloved and Friend. People will react to your anger, but you can safely ask Him why He leaves you alone.
viv06-005-p02.core_idea: Bring even your anger to God

viv06-005-p03.plain: A man the world called mad answered that the world is a madhouse: some are mad for love, fame, money or heaven, and he is mad for God. Everyone is mad, he said, but his madness is the best.
viv06-005-p03.core_idea: Everyone is mad for something; choose God

viv06-005-p04.plain: We all start by loving ourselves, and the little self makes love selfish. But at last a blaze of light shows the little self joined with the Infinite, and we realise that Love, the Lover and the Beloved are One.
viv06-005-p04.core_idea: Love, Lover and Beloved are One

viv07-001-p01.plain: Doing nothing cannot be the goal, or walls and tree stumps would be the wisest of all, and passion is not true activity either. Real activity, as Vedanta sees it, goes with unshakeable calm, the best state for work.
viv07-001-p01.core_idea: True action is combined with unshakeable calm

viv07-001-p02.plain: He once thought, as many ask, that work needs passion, but experience shows the less passion and the more calm, the better and more we work. Letting feelings loose wastes energy, frays the nerves and achieves little.
viv07-001-p02.core_idea: The calmer we are, the better we work

viv07-001-p03.plain: The world's great workers were remarkably calm; nothing threw them off balance. Someone who gives way to anger or hatred breaks himself apart and achieves nothing; the calm, forgiving, balanced mind does the most work.
viv07-001-p03.core_idea: A calm, forgiving mind does the most work

viv07-001-p04.plain: The soul was never born and will never die; fear of death and beliefs about what we cannot do are superstitions, for we can do everything. Vedanta says whoever does not believe in himself is the real atheist.
viv07-001-p04.core_idea: Not believing in yourself is the real atheism

viv07-001-p05.plain: All the powers of the universe are already ours; we cover our eyes and cry that it is dark, but remove the hands and the light is there. Darkness and weakness never existed; only fools call themselves weak and impure.
viv07-001-p05.core_idea: All power is already ours; darkness never existed

viv07-001-p06.plain: Vedanta knows no sin, only error, and the worst error is calling yourself weak, sinful or powerless. Each such thought adds a link to your chain and sends a bad thought into the world.
viv07-001-p06.core_idea: Calling yourself weak or sinful is the greatest error

judge.issue: Drops the explicit verdict that whoever thinks himself weak or impure is wrong.

viv07-002-p01.plain: Human nature resists moving even one step forward. We are like people freezing in snow who beg to keep sleeping because it feels pleasant, and die there; all our lives we freeze from the feet up and still want sleep.
viv07-002-p01.core_idea: We resist growth like the freezing who want sleep

viv07-002-p02.plain: Condemn no one: help if you can, and if not, bless others and let them go their way. Criticism wastes energy, because in the end we see everyone is nearing the same ideal and our differences are mostly of expression.
viv07-002-p02.core_idea: Help or bless others, but never condemn

viv07-002-p03.plain: We all know our weaknesses, and dwelling on a disease does not cure it; medicine does. The cure for weakness is not brooding over it but thinking of strength, so teach people the strength already in them.
viv07-002-p03.core_idea: Cure weakness by thinking of strength

viv07-002-p04.plain: The strongest force in the lives of great people has been faith in themselves, and even someone who sinks very low will one day learn it. Why wait for bitter experience, when faith in ourselves will do everything?
viv07-002-p04.core_idea: Faith in yourself will do everything

judge.issue: Drops that great people became great through consciousness of greatness, and faith marks difference between people.

viv07-002-p05.plain: No one knows how much power lies hidden in you; humanity has shown only a tiny part of it in millions of years. So do not call yourself weak, for behind you lies an ocean of infinite power and blessedness.
viv07-002-p05.core_idea: Infinite power lies hidden within you

viv07-003-p01.plain: You are the Pure One: wake up and rise, mighty one, for this sleep does not suit you. Do not think yourself weak, miserable or a sinner, but show your true, almighty nature.
viv07-003-p01.core_idea: Wake up to your pure, mighty nature

viv07-003-p02.plain: Whatever leads to oneness is truth. Love is true and hatred false, because hatred divides people and destroys, while love binds and unites.
viv07-003-p02.core_idea: Love unites and is true; hatred divides

viv07-003-p03.plain: If you feel for others, you are growing toward oneness; without that feeling, even the greatest intellect is dry and worth nothing. If you feel, even unable to read, you are on the right path and the Lord is yours.
viv07-003-p03.core_idea: Feeling for others matters more than intellect

viv07-004-p01.plain: Vedanta's theme is to see the Lord in everything, and to see things as they really are, not as they seem.

viv07-004-p02.plain: You can make an image to worship God, but a better one already exists: the living person. You can build a temple, but a far higher one already exists: the human body.
viv07-004-p02.core_idea: The living person is God's best temple

viv07-004-p03.plain: Some truths are uncomfortable until we follow them all the way. Human nature is conservative: once we do something, we find it hard to stop, and the mind resists new ideas because they bring discomfort.
viv07-004-p03.core_idea: The mind resists new truths because they discomfort

fix.display_text: There are cases where truth is not comfortable until we reach its climax. Human nature is very conservative. It does something, and having once done that, finds it hard to get out of it. The mind will not receive new thoughts, because they bring discomfort.

viv07-005-p01.plain: Religion is always a practical science; there never was and never will be a purely theological religion. Practice comes first, knowledge after.
viv07-005-p01.core_idea: In religion, practice comes before knowledge

viv07-005-p02.plain: The moment I see God living in every human body and stand in reverence before every person, seeing God in them, everything that binds me falls away and I am free.
viv07-005-p02.core_idea: Seeing God in everyone sets you free

viv07-005-p03.plain: Vedanta does say each person must have their own path, but the path is not the goal.
viv07-005-p03.core_idea: The path is not the goal

viv07-005-p04.plain: Love cannot grow out of fear; it rests on freedom. Only when we truly begin to love the world do we understand what the brotherhood of humanity means.
viv07-005-p04.core_idea: Love rests on freedom, not fear

viv07-005-p05.plain: Come out of narrow ruts into the open light, for an infinite soul cannot be content in small grooves. Everything is yours, so embrace it with love; if you have ever wanted to, you have felt God.
viv07-005-p05.core_idea: Embracing the universe with love is feeling God

viv07-006-p01.plain: Until we know our real nature, we are beggars pushed around and enslaved by every force in nature. We cry for help, even to imaginary beings, and it never comes, yet we keep hoping while a whole life passes.
viv07-006-p01.core_idea: Not knowing our nature, we beg for help in vain

viv07-006-p02.plain: Be free and expect nothing from anyone; looking back, you will see that the help you hoped for from others never came. All real help came from within, from what you yourself worked for.
viv07-006-p02.core_idea: All real help comes from within

viv07-006-p03.plain: As the Bible says, if you can't love the brother you see, how can you love the unseen God? If you can't see God in a human face, you won't find him in clouds, images or stories. Seeing God in people makes you religious, and explains turning the other cheek.
viv07-006-p03.core_idea: Religion begins when you see God in people
viv07-006-p03.plain_v1: As the Bible says, if you cannot love the brother you see, how can you love the God you do not? If you cannot see God in a human face, you cannot see Him in clouds or idols.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the closing point: religion begins when you see God in people, and turning the other cheek.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the conclusion: true religion begins in seeing God in people.

viv07-006-p04.plain: Always look at others with love and sympathy, knowing they are walking the same path we have already walked.
viv07-006-p04.core_idea: See others with love; they walk our path

viv07-006-p05.plain: If you are truly pure, how can you see impurity? What is inside shows outside, so we see impurity only when it is in us.
viv07-006-p05.core_idea: We see impurity only if it is within us

viv07-007-p01.plain: As individuals we seem separate, but in reality we are one. The less we think of ourselves as separate from that One, the better; the more separate we feel from the Whole, the more miserable we become.
viv07-007-p01.core_idea: Feeling separate from the Whole brings misery

viv07-007-p02.plain: What we need is growth and realisation; no theory ever raised anyone higher and no books can make us purer. The only power is realisation, which lies within us and comes from thinking, so let people think.
viv07-007-p02.core_idea: Realisation comes from within, through thinking

viv07-008-p01.plain: Infinite power, existence and bliss are already ours. We do not need to gain them; we only need to bring them out.
viv07-008-p01.core_idea: Infinite power is already ours to bring out

viv07-008-p02.plain: Since childhood everyone around him taught weakness and told him he was weak. It is hard now to realise his own strength, but through analysis and reasoning he comes to know it and realise it.
viv07-008-p02.core_idea: Reason can undo a lifetime of being taught weakness

viv07-009-p01.plain: When someone gains a better idea, he calls his old ideas harmful and useless, forgetting they were needed to bring him where he is. We all grow by living on crude ideas first and then rising higher.
viv07-009-p01.core_idea: Old ideas were steps to where we are

viv07-009-p02.plain: We are bound only by laws we make ourselves: our thoughts, words and deeds are the threads of the net we throw around ourselves. Once we set a force in motion, we must take its full consequences.
viv07-009-p02.core_idea: Our own deeds weave the net that binds us

viv07-010-p01.plain: If you dare to declare that you are free, you are free this moment. If you say you are bound, bound you will stay.
viv07-010-p01.core_idea: Declare yourself free and you are free

viv07-010-p02.plain: You may dread losing a hundred pounds, while others would not blink at losing everything they own; such people have existed and still do. Why judge them by your own standard?
viv07-010-p02.core_idea: Do not judge others by your own limits

viv07-010-p03.plain: History shows that those who never thought of their own little selves did the most good for humanity, and the more people think of themselves, the less they can do for others.

viv07-010-p04.plain: The key to all goodness is not I but you; never mind heaven, hell or the soul. The world is full of misery, so go into it as the Buddha did and work to lessen it, or die trying.
viv07-010-p04.core_idea: Go out and lessen the world's misery

viv07-010-p05.plain: Like silkworms, we spin a cocoon from our own substance and end up trapped inside. But not forever: inside it we will grow spiritually and, like the butterfly, come out free.
viv07-010-p05.core_idea: We will emerge free from our self-made cocoon

viv07-010-p06.plain: He is glad of his many mistakes, since each made him who he is; that is no reason to err on purpose, but do not mope over them. All will come right, because goodness and purity are our indestructible nature.
viv07-010-p06.core_idea: Do not mope over mistakes; your goodness remains

viv07-011-p01.plain: We make what we call mistakes, rather than sins, because we are weak, and we are weak because we are ignorant. We cover our own eyes and cry that it is dark; remove the hands and the soul's light shines.
viv07-011-p01.core_idea: Mistakes come from weakness, weakness from ignorance

judge.issue: Drops 'who makes us ignorant? We ourselves', the self-responsibility point.

viv07-011-p02.plain: Wailing about a room that has been dark for thousands of years will not end the darkness, but striking a match will. Brooding over your wrongs does no good; bring in the light and evil goes at once.
viv07-011-p02.core_idea: Bring in light instead of lamenting the dark

viv07-011-p03.plain: Someone who wants nothing for himself has nothing to fear. What can frighten him, and what fear can death or evil hold for him?

viv07-011-p04.plain: However busy we are with work, ambitions and struggles, sometimes a pause comes and the mind wants to know what lies beyond this world. At times it glimpses a realm beyond the senses and begins to strive toward it.
viv07-011-p04.core_idea: In quiet pauses the mind seeks the beyond

viv07-012-p01.plain: Why should everyone think as we do? A rational person should be glad they do not, for he wants to live among thinking people, not in a land like a grave; difference is the first sign of thought.
viv07-012-p01.core_idea: Difference is the first sign of thought

viv07-012-p02.plain: People never move from error to truth, only from lesser truth to higher truth. What you knew as a child was not foolish; what you know now is that knowledge plus something more.
viv07-012-p02.core_idea: We grow from lesser truth to higher truth

viv07-012-p03.plain: Photos of the sun taken at each stage of a journey toward it all differ yet show one sun. So each of us sees truth from a standpoint shaped by birth, education and surroundings, yet all share one universal truth.
viv07-012-p03.core_idea: We all see one truth from different standpoints

judge.issue: Drops that we know only as much truth as we can receive, causing contradictory views.

viv07-012-p04.plain: Spiritual ideas satisfy only when they come in your own way and speak your soul's language. When someone gives truth in my language, I understand it at once and keep it forever.
viv07-012-p04.core_idea: Truth must speak your own soul's language

viv07-013-p01.plain: When we start out in life we believe our fate will be extraordinary, and nothing can shake that belief. When we grow old, we think differently.
viv07-013-p01.core_idea: Youth expects greatness; age thinks differently

viv07-013-p02.plain: Money may come and go and troubles pile up, but if you keep your ideal whole, nothing can kill you, even at a hundred. Once that ideal and mission are lost, all the world's wealth and power cannot save you.
viv07-013-p02.core_idea: Keep your ideal alive and nothing can kill you

viv07-013-p03.plain: An ideal comes to mind that may only be a dream and may never come true. But sometimes it is better to dream great truths than to die on bad, hard facts, so let us dream.
viv07-013-p03.core_idea: Better to dream great truths than die on facts

viv07-013-p04.plain: He believes in acceptance, not tolerance, since to tolerate is to think others wrong and merely allow them to live. Is it not blasphemy to think we are allowing others to live?

viv07-013-p05.plain: We stand in the present yet open ourselves to the endless future. We take in all of the past, enjoy the light of today, and open every window of the heart to whatever is to come.
viv07-013-p05.core_idea: Embrace past, present and future with an open heart

viv07-014-p01.plain: Fanaticism is one of the most dangerous diseases. It stirs up all the wickedness in human nature: anger rises, nerves tighten, and people become like tigers.

viv07-014-p02.plain: Winter thunderclouds roar without rain, while monsoon clouds silently flood the world; so those who truly feel the brotherhood of humanity show it in their lives, not in talk or little sects. We need more work, less talk.
viv07-014-p02.core_idea: Real love shows in deeds, not talk

viv07-014-p03.plain: Our faces all differ, yet we are all human. He cannot grasp this shared humanity with the senses, but if he is sure of anything, it is that it is there, common to us all.
viv07-014-p03.core_idea: A shared humanity lies beneath all our differences

viv07-015-p01.plain: We should not wish everyone thought alike, or there would be nothing to think and we would stare at each other like museum mummies. Our differences are the very soul of progress and of all thought.
viv07-015-p01.core_idea: Differences are the soul of progress

viv07-015-p02.plain: People fetch water from a lake in cups, jars and buckets, and the water takes each vessel's shape, yet it is all water. Our minds are such vessels: God fills each and appears in its shape, yet He is One.
viv07-015-p02.core_idea: God is one, though each mind shapes Him

viv07-015-p03.plain: Do not tear anything down; build, and help if you can, or else fold your hands and stand by. If you cannot help, at least do no harm, and never speak against anyone's sincere beliefs.
viv07-015-p03.core_idea: Build and help, or at least do no harm

viv07-015-p04.plain: Just as a plant grows by itself while you only protect it, spiritual growth comes from within. Nobody can make you spiritual; you must teach yourself.
viv07-015-p04.core_idea: Spiritual growth comes from inside; no one can impose it.

viv07-016-p01.plain: The ideal person has philosophy, mysticism, feeling and work all fully present. Most people are one-sided and fear other paths; being balanced in all four is the ideal of religion.
viv07-016-p01.core_idea: True religion balances thought, mysticism, feeling and work.

viv07-016-p02.plain: Inspiration grows out of reason, so it completes reason rather than opposing it, just as an old man completes rather than contradicts the child he was.
viv07-016-p02.core_idea: Inspiration fulfils reason instead of contradicting it.

judge.issue: Drops that inspiration reveals what reason cannot reach.

viv07-017-p01.plain: Whatever you do, from blacking shoes to worshipping God, concentration makes you do it better. Concentration is the one key that opens nature and the treasure-house of knowledge.
viv07-017-p01.core_idea: Concentration is the key to all knowledge and skill.

viv07-017-p02.plain: Our minds are scattered over a hundred things. The moment I try to calm my thoughts and focus on one thing, thousands of unwanted impulses and thoughts rush in and disturb me.
viv07-017-p02.core_idea: The mind scatters the moment we try to focus.

viv07-017-p03.plain: All misery comes from attachment: we help people, they turn ungrateful, and we suffer. Karma-Yoga teaches working for its own sake, giving without wanting anything back, and so escaping misery.
viv07-017-p03.core_idea: Work without attachment, give without expecting return.

viv07-017-p04.plain: Wherever there is love, the Lord is there: in a husband's kiss, a mother's kiss, friends clasping hands, a great person helping humanity. Wherever the heart opens, God shows himself.
viv07-017-p04.core_idea: God is present wherever there is love.

viv07-017-p05.plain: A lower bird, happy and miserable by turns among sweet and bitter fruits, keeps nearing a calm golden bird above until it finds it was that bird all along. The upper bird is God; the lower, the soul.
viv07-017-p05.core_idea: The suffering self is really the calm divine Self.

extension.text: Upon the same tree there are two birds, one on the top, the other below. The one on the top is calm, silent, and majestic, immersed in his own glory; the one on the lower branches, eating sweet and bitter fruits by turns, hopping from branch to branch, is becoming happy and miserable by turns. After a time the lower bird eats an exceptionally bitter fruit and gets disgustful and looks up and sees the other bird, that wondrous one of golden plumage, who eats neither sweet nor bitter fruit, who is neither happy nor miserable, but calm, Selfcentred, and sees nothing beyond his Self. The lower bird longs for this condition but soon forgets it, and again begins to eat the fruits. In a little while, he eats another exceptionally bitter fruit, which makes him feel miserable, and he again looks up, and tries to get nearer to the upper bird. Once more he forgets and after a time he looks up, and so on he goes again and again, until he comes very near to the beautiful bird and sees the reflection of light from his plumage playing around his own body, and he feels a change and seems to melt away; still nearer he comes, and everything about him melts away, and at last he understands this wonderful change. The lower bird was, as it were, only the substantial-looking shadow, the reflection of the higher; he himself was in essence the upper bird all the time. This eating of fruits, sweet and bitter, this lower, little bird, weeping and happy by turns, was a vain chimera, a dream: all along, the real bird was there above, calm and silent, glorious and majestic, beyond grief, beyond sorrow. The upper bird is God, the Lord of this universe; and the lower bird is the human soul, eating the sweet and bitter fruits of this world.

judge.issue: Heavily compressed; loses the lower bird as mere shadow or dream of the upper.

viv07-017-p06.plain: We can agree with foolish ideas today and drop them tomorrow, but true religion does not change. Religion is realisation: not talk or theory, but your whole soul becoming what it believes.
viv07-017-p06.core_idea: Religion is realisation and becoming, not doctrine.

viv07-018-p01.plain: In action we are so powerless; our will is blocked at every turn. We can want anything, even to reach a distant star, yet the body lets us achieve very few of our desires.
viv07-018-p01.core_idea: Our desires are boundless but our power is small.

viv07-018-p02.plain: Small things hurt us because we think we are small, finite beings. Though it is hard, amid misery I must believe I am infinite; and we really are, always seeking something infinite and free.
viv07-018-p02.core_idea: Misery comes from believing we are finite.

viv07-018-p03.plain: Even in the deepest misery the Soul sends a ray of light, and we wake to find we can never lose what is truly ours. Our existence comes first, before good or bad; it is never lost.
viv07-018-p03.core_idea: Our true existence can never be lost.

viv07-018-p04.plain: No one can die or be degraded forever; life is a playground, however rough the game. However hard the blows, the Soul is never harmed, for we are that Infinite.
viv07-018-p04.core_idea: The Soul is never injured by life's blows.

viv07-018-p05.plain: Often near death from hunger and exhaustion, collapsing under a tree, his mind turned to the thought that he was It, beyond fear, death and hunger, and nature could not crush him. Then he would rise renewed.
viv07-018-p05.core_idea: Asserting the inner Self gives strength in extremity.

judge.issue: Drops the self-address 'Lord of lords and God of gods' and command to arise.

viv07-018-p06.plain: Do not be afraid, and do not count how many times you fail, for time is endless. Keep going, assert yourself again and again, and light will come.
viv07-018-p06.core_idea: Keep going despite failures; light will come.

viv07-018-p07.plain: Only you can lift yourself up; you are your own worst enemy and best friend. So hold on to the Self, stand up, do not fear, and let the Self emerge amid all weakness, however faint at first.
viv07-018-p07.core_idea: You alone are your enemy and your friend.

viv07-019-p01.plain: I am like the unchanging blue sky with clouds passing over it. Happiness and misery, good and evil, may hide the Self for a moment, but they are finite and pass, while I remain.
viv07-019-p01.core_idea: Joys and sorrows pass; the Self stays unchanged.

viv07-019-p02.plain: Do not be afraid, and do not believe that we are evil, limited, or that we can ever die. None of that is true.
viv07-019-p02.core_idea: We are not evil, finite or mortal.

fix.display_text: Fear not. Believe not that we are evil, that we are finite, that we can ever die. It is not true.
fix.reason: Removed stray full stop after comma.

viv07-019-p03.plain: There are two paths, enjoyment and blessedness, and both pull at people. Whoever chooses blessedness becomes wise; whoever chooses enjoyment declines.
viv07-019-p03.core_idea: Choosing blessedness over enjoyment makes a sage.

viv07-019-p04.plain: The Self you ask about is never born and never dies, and it is not destroyed when the body is. Neither killer nor killed is right, since the Self cannot kill or be killed.
viv07-019-p04.core_idea: The Self is unborn, undying and cannot be killed.

viv07-019-p05.plain: The body is a chariot, the senses horses, the mind the reins, the intellect the driver and the soul the rider. Without control and discernment the senses run wild; with them they are like well-trained horses.
viv07-019-p05.core_idea: A controlled mind keeps the senses in check.

judge.issue: Drops the soul becoming the enjoyer when joined with intellect, mind and senses.

viv07-019-p06.plain: Wake up and act. Do not stop until you reach the goal, for the sages say the path is as hard as walking a razor's edge.
viv07-019-p06.core_idea: Persist to the goal though the path is hard.

viv07-020-p01.plain: As street noise drowns out the person beside you, the world's noise pulls the mind outward. To see the Self, that outward pull must stop; turn your eyes inward and you will see the Lord's glory within.
viv07-020-p01.core_idea: Turn inward from the world's noise to see the Self.

viv07-020-p02.plain: When every desire troubling the heart ends, the mortal becomes immortal and reaches Brahman here. Only when the heart's crookedness goes and its knots are cut does one become immortal.
viv07-020-p02.core_idea: Freedom from desire makes the mortal immortal.

viv07-020-p03.plain: People hurt each other out of fear of not having enough. A man afraid he will lack money is driven by that fear to harm and rob others.
viv07-020-p03.core_idea: Fear of scarcity drives people to harm others.

viv07-020-p04.plain: I should love everyone, my brother included, because we are one. The whole universe is bound together in that oneness.
viv07-020-p04.core_idea: Love everyone because all are one.

viv07-021-p01.plain: When Yajnavalkya offered his wife all his wealth before leaving, she asked whether a world full of riches could make her immortal. He said no: wealth makes you rich, nothing more.

viv07-022-p01.plain: Look at our own lives: as children we think bad things good and good things bad. Our ideas keep changing and rising; what once seemed very good no longer seems so.
viv07-022-p01.core_idea: Our ideas of good and evil change as we grow.

viv07-022-p02.plain: Our hatred of others comes from foolish ideas of good and evil absorbed since childhood. They distort our judgment and turn the earth into hell; give them up and it becomes heaven.
viv07-022-p02.core_idea: Ideas of good and evil breed hatred.

viv07-023-p01.plain: Rain rises from the ocean and flows back to it; trees end in seeds that become trees; birds leave eggs. Everything starts from fine seeds, grows grosser, and returns to that fine form.
viv07-023-p01.core_idea: All things arise from seeds and return to them.

fix.display_text: The raindrop is drawn from the ocean in the form of vapour, and drifts away through the air to the mountains; there it changes again into water and flows back through hundreds of miles down to the mother ocean. The seed produces the tree. The tree dies, leaving only the seed. Again it comes up as another tree, which again ends in the seed, and so on. Look at a bird, how from the egg it springs, becomes a beautiful bird, lives its life and then dies, leaving only other eggs, containing germs of future birds. So with the animals; so with men. Everything begins, as it were, from certain seeds, certain rudiments, certain fine forms, and becomes grosser and grosser as it develops; and then again it goes back to that fine form and subsides.

viv07-024-p01.plain: Man watches all these changes and is never impure himself; he only seems so by reflection, as a clear crystal looks red or blue beside a coloured flower while staying pure.
viv07-024-p01.core_idea: The self only appears impure, like coloured crystal.

viv07-025-p01.plain: Nature is always changing but the soul never changes, and because nature changes, the soul can come out of its bondage.
viv07-025-p01.core_idea: Changing nature lets the unchanging soul become free.

viv07-026-p01.plain: Someone who calls himself a sinner says something untrue, because he does not know himself. He is deeply ignorant, knowing only a small part of what he is.
viv07-026-p01.core_idea: Calling yourself a sinner shows self-ignorance.

viv07-027-p01.plain: The soul feels neither pleasure nor pain; it is the eternal witness of all action and takes no fruit from it. Like the sun or a crystal, it is untouched, beyond both passive and active.
viv07-027-p01.core_idea: The soul is the untouched witness of all action.

judge.issue: Compresses the sun analogy; loses that the soul is unaffected by the eye's defects.

viv07-027-p02.plain: Every person exists, every person must know, and every person is mad for love and cannot help loving. All beings, lowest to highest, must love.
viv07-027-p02.core_idea: Every being exists, knows and loves.

viv07-027-p03.plain: The soul's true nature is unlimited bliss, but whatever shows itself is limited. So love as we know it shifts: I love you one day, hate you the next, because it is only a manifestation.
viv07-027-p03.core_idea: Expressed love is limited; the soul's bliss is not.

viv07-028-p01.plain: If you think you are bound, you stay bound, making your own chains; if you know you are free, you are free right now. Freedom is the goal of all nature.
viv07-028-p01.core_idea: Believing yourself bound keeps you bound.

viv07-028-p02.plain: Cut yourself off and everything hurts you; reach out and feel for others and you are helped. The selfish man is the most miserable; the happiest has no selfishness at all.
viv07-028-p02.core_idea: Selfishness brings misery; caring for others brings help.

viv07-028-p03.plain: Which version of me is my real individuality: the baby sucking its thumb? In fifty years I will laugh at who I am now, as I now laugh at that baby.
viv07-028-p03.core_idea: Our individuality keeps changing; which one is real?

viv07-029-p01.plain: If your pleasure depends on something outside you, you suffer when it goes; nothing in the universe is reliable. If all my joy is in myself, I always have it, because I can never lose my Self.
viv07-029-p01.core_idea: Joy found in the Self cannot be lost.

viv07-029-p02.plain: We make mistakes, so what; it is all play, so do not weep and repent over past sins. Keep going and do not look back, for there is nothing to gain from it.
viv07-029-p02.core_idea: Don't dwell on past mistakes; keep moving forward.

judge.issue: Drops 'after work, do not think of it' and 'you lose nothing'.

viv07-029-p03.plain: Know for certain that you are in everything. That is why you should hurt no one: hurting them, you hurt yourself.

viv07-029-p04.plain: Whoever sees the One amid the many, the one life amid endless death, and the changeless within their own soul, to that person belongs eternal peace.
viv07-029-p04.core_idea: Seeing the changeless One brings eternal peace.

viv08-001-p01.plain: Evil is an iron chain and good a golden one, but both bind. Use the golden chain to loosen the iron one, as you use one thorn to remove another, then throw both away and be free.
viv08-001-p01.core_idea: Good and evil both bind; go beyond both.

judge.issue: Drops 'know once for all that there is no chain for you'.

viv08-001-p02.plain: Always be the giver: give love, help, service, any little thing, with no bargaining, no conditions and nothing expected back. Give freely from your own abundance, as God gives to us.
viv08-001-p02.core_idea: Give freely and expect nothing in return.

judge.issue: Drops 'and none will be imposed', the reciprocal half of the condition.

viv08-001-p03.plain: In our struggles the world seems dreadful, but as we watch puppies nip each other in play without worry, our struggles are only play to God. The world amuses God, and nothing in it angers God.
viv08-001-p03.core_idea: Our struggles are only play in God's eyes.

viv08-001-p04.plain: A cry to the divine Mother: my boat is sinking in life's sea, illusion and attachment are raging, my senses are foolish and my mind weak, and I am lost. Mother, save me!
viv08-001-p04.core_idea: A desperate plea to the Mother to be saved.

viv08-001-p05.plain: Be brave and sincere, follow any path with devotion, and you will reach the Whole. Grasp one link and the whole chain follows; water the roots, reach the Lord, and you have everything.
viv08-001-p05.core_idea: Sincere devotion on any path leads to God.

viv08-001-p06.plain: His Master called the world a madhouse where people chase money, sex or fame and a few chase God, which he preferred. God turns us to gold at once: we look the same but can no longer hurt or sin.
viv08-001-p06.core_idea: Better to be mad after God than worldly things.

judge.issue: Loses the philosophers' stone image; 'women' rendered as 'sex'.

viv08-001-p07.plain: Follow the scriptures until you can go beyond them, since books are not the goal and each person must verify religious truth. Trust only the teacher who says you can see it too.
viv08-001-p07.core_idea: Verify religious truth yourself; books aren't the end.

judge.issue: 'Obey' softened to 'follow'; warning against the 'you cannot' teacher only implied.

viv08-001-p08.plain: There are three kinds of love: one takes and gives nothing, one is a trade, and one gives with no thought of return, like a moth drawn to a flame.
viv08-001-p08.core_idea: The highest love seeks nothing in return.

judge.issue: Moth 'for the light' becomes 'drawn to a flame', adding a self-destruction connotation.

viv08-002-p01.plain: Misery always follows happiness, and both are chains that hide our true nature. Behind them is the Atman, whose nature is unchanging bliss and peace; we already have it and need only wash away the dross.
viv08-002-p01.core_idea: Beyond happiness and misery lies the Self's bliss.

judge.issue: Drops that misery follows faster for the advanced soul.

viv08-002-p02.plain: A mind pleased by praise will be hurt by blame. Pleasures of the senses and mind are fleeting, but within us is one true joy that depends on nothing; it is free, it is bliss.
viv08-002-p02.core_idea: True joy lies within, independent of praise.

viv08-002-p03.plain: Neither chase nor avoid; accept what comes, for freedom is being unaffected, not merely enduring. Be like the bull who told an apologetic mosquito to bring its whole family to live on his horn.
viv08-002-p03.core_idea: Freedom is being untouched by what comes.

viv08-002-p04.plain: We do our best work and have our greatest influence when we are not thinking of ourselves. All great geniuses know this.
viv08-002-p04.core_idea: Our best work comes without thought of self.

viv08-002-p05.plain: Our thoughts have made us what we are, so be careful what you think. Words matter less; thoughts live on and travel far.

viv08-002-p06.plain: Bless people when they insult you. Think how much good they do you; they can only harm themselves.

viv08-002-p07.plain: We give things up and press on, find nothing and fall into despair; but hold on, keep holding on.
viv08-002-p07.core_idea: Hold on through the despair of renunciation.

viv08-002-p08.plain: Be like a lily: stay where you are and open your petals, and the bees will come on their own.
viv08-002-p08.core_idea: Unfold where you are and others will come.

viv08-003-p01.plain: Seek truth only for its own sake, not for bliss, which may come but must not be your motive; have no motive except God. Dare to reach Truth even if it means going through hell.
viv08-003-p01.core_idea: Seek truth for its own sake.

viv08-003-p02.plain: The whole universe is the one Self with variations, like one tune made bearable by variety. Its discords only make the harmony that follows more perfect.
viv08-003-p02.core_idea: The universe is one Self in many variations.

viv08-003-p03.plain: Every thought is a small hammer blow on the iron of our bodies, shaping them into what we want them to be.
viv08-003-p03.core_idea: Each thought shapes who we become.

viv08-003-p04.plain: The source of all knowledge is in everyone, ant or angel, and true religion is one; we only quarrel over forms and symbols. Paradise exists for those who find it; we lose ourselves and think the world is lost.
viv08-003-p04.core_idea: All knowledge is within; true religion is one.

judge.issue: 'Millennium' rendered as 'Paradise'; slight shift.

viv08-003-p05.plain: The divine light in most people is hidden like a lamp in an iron cask, but purity and unselfishness thin the cask until it is clear as glass, as in Ramakrishna. The impatient never succeed.
viv08-003-p05.core_idea: Purity makes the hidden inner light visible.

judge.issue: Drops 'we are all on the way' and thinking through material means.
