viv12-006-p01.plain: Everyone knows not to steal or hurt others, but that knowledge means little. Only those who have actually lived by it truly know it and have built their character on it.
viv12-006-p01.core_idea: Knowing a rule means living it, not reciting it

viv12-006-p02.plain: My religion cannot be yours, nor yours mine. The goal is the same, but each person must take a different road suited to their mind, and all these roads are true because they lead to the same goal.
viv12-006-p02.core_idea: Different paths, suited to each mind, reach one goal

viv12-006-p03.plain: The body will die anyway, so why keep praying for health and wealth? No one can have everything, and it does not matter. Welcome good things when they come and let them go when they leave; both are blessed.
viv12-006-p03.core_idea: Welcome good things and let them go freely

viv12-006-p04.plain: Always guarding a fragile body, we live in constant fear, worse off than a frightened deer. The deer rests once fed, but we keep multiplying our wants until nothing natural satisfies us.
viv12-006-p04.core_idea: Endless wants and fear leave us no rest

viv12-006-p05.plain: A poor man wants money; once he has it he wants company, then something else. He is never at rest.
viv12-006-p05.core_idea: Desire never rests once it is satisfied

viv12-007-p01.plain: Being born into a church or sect is good, because its training brings out our best; but dying there is bad, since most of us never grow beyond that small group.
viv12-007-p01.core_idea: Begin in a tradition, but outgrow its limits

viv12-007-p02.plain: Think for yourself. Honour the holy teachers, but treat religion as your own independent search; you must find your own light as they found theirs, because their light will not satisfy you.
viv12-007-p02.core_idea: Find your own light; others' cannot satisfy you

viv12-008-p01.plain: We all want to escape misery and become free in body, mind and spirit. The goal is the same for everyone, but there are many ways to reach it, shaped by each person's nature.
viv12-008-p01.core_idea: One goal of freedom, many paths by nature

fix.display_text: All of us want to get rid of misery; we are struggling to attain to liberty — physical, mental, spiritual. This is the whole idea upon which the world is working. Though the goal is one and the same, there may be many ways to reach it, and these ways are determined by the peculiarities of our nature.

viv12-009-p01.plain: A teaching may seem perfect to you and terrible to your friend. He is not wrong and there is no point arguing; the teaching was fine, it just did not fit him.
viv12-009-p01.core_idea: A good teaching may not fit everyone

viv12-009-p02.plain: There is one sun, yet everyone sees it differently from where they stand. Likewise truth looks different from different viewpoints, though Absolute Truth is one, so we need not fight when others see religion differently; both may be true.
viv12-009-p02.core_idea: One truth appears differently from different standpoints

fix.display_text: The sun is one; but when you and I and a hundred other people stand at different places and look at it, each one of us sees a different sun. We cannot help it. A very little change of place will change a man’s whole vision of the sun. A slight change in the atmosphere will make again a different vision. So, in relative perception, truth always appears various. But the Absolute Truth is only one. Therefore we need not fight with others when we find they are telling something about religion which is not exactly according to our view of it. We ought to remember that both of us may be true, though apparently contradictors.

viv12-009-p03.plain: You cannot force a plant to grow, and a child teaches itself. All you can do is remove obstacles, loosen the soil and protect it; the knowledge comes from within, and there your work ends.
viv12-009-p03.core_idea: Growth comes from within; we only remove obstacles

judge.issue: 'Cannot force a plant to grow' loosens 'cannot grow in unsuited soil'.

viv12-009-p04.plain: I have no right to force an ideal on you. My job is to show you all the ideals I know so you can see which suits your nature best; then take that one up and stick with it.
viv12-009-p04.core_idea: Choose the ideal that suits you and persevere

viv12-009-p05.plain: Be strong, stand up and seek the God of Love; that is the highest strength. No power is greater than purity, and love and purity rule the world.
viv12-009-p05.core_idea: Love and purity are the highest power

viv13-002-p01.plain: The Buddha said that hurting someone back does not heal the first hurt; it only adds one more wrong to the world.
viv13-002-p01.core_idea: Revenge only adds another wrong to the world

viv13-005-p01.plain: Every moment we see people around us dying, yet those still living think they will never die. Strangest of all, facing death everywhere, no one believes it will come to them.
viv13-005-p01.core_idea: Surrounded by death, no one believes they'll die

viv13-005-p02.plain: Argument settles nothing; doctrines and scriptures are many and contradict each other, and no two sages agree. The secret of religion lies hidden deep, so follow the path the great ones have walked.
viv13-005-p02.core_idea: When arguments fail, follow the path of the great

viv13-005-p03.plain: Whoever finds peace amid great activity, and activity amid great calm, knows life's secret. Krishna teaches non-attachment: you are the free soul, the Witness; work, earn, love your family, but do not get attached, for attachment brings misery.
viv13-005-p03.core_idea: Work fully, but stay unattached; attachment brings misery

viv13-007-p01.plain: The only real sin is fear. Any work that brings out your hidden strength is virtue, and whatever weakens your body and mind is sin. Shake off this weakness and faintheartedness.
viv13-007-p01.core_idea: Fear and weakness are the only sin

viv13-007-p02.plain: Do not hate even the worst sinner or judge his outside; look within, where the Supreme Self lives. Tell the world: you have no sin or misery, you hold limitless power; rise and show the divine within.
viv13-007-p02.core_idea: Every person holds the divine within

viv13-007-p03.plain: Our duty is to believe only what is true. Superstition, blind faith in tradition, binds people so tightly that even Jesus, Mohammed and other great men could not shake some off. Keep your eye on truth and reject all superstition.
viv13-007-p03.core_idea: Believe only the truth; reject blind tradition

viv13-008-p01.plain: A prayer to God: may I love you with the same intensity that the ignorant feel for worldly things, but only for the sake of love itself.
viv13-008-p01.core_idea: Love God as intensely as others love things

viv13-008-p02.plain: Hindus see the universe moving in waves: rising, peaking, falling, resting low, then rising again. What holds for the whole holds for every part, and human affairs move the same way.
viv13-008-p02.core_idea: Everything, including human life, rises and falls in waves

viv13-009-p01.plain: We arrive like orphans who are lost without knowing it. We do not know what our lives mean; we do one thing today and another tomorrow, tossed about like straws on water or feathers in a storm.
viv13-009-p01.core_idea: Without purpose we drift like straws on water

viv13-009-p02.plain: How can someone who cannot believe in himself believe in anything else? One moment I feel immortal and moral, the next terrified or knocked flat, because I have lost faith in myself and my moral backbone is broken.
viv13-009-p02.core_idea: Without faith in yourself, everything else collapses

viv13-009-p03.plain: It does not matter what language you use, or whether your grammar and style are fine. What matters is whether you have something to give. That is the first question; if you have, give it.
viv13-009-p03.core_idea: What matters is having something real to give

viv13-009-p04.plain: Some fools drink salty water even with sweet water nearby, simply because their father dug the salty well.
viv13-009-p04.core_idea: Clinging to inherited ways even when better exists

viv13-009-p05.plain: Religion is not talk, theory or agreement of the mind. It is realisation deep in the heart: touching God, feeling that I am a spirit connected with the Universal Spirit and all its forms.
viv13-009-p05.core_idea: Religion is felt union with the Universal Spirit

viv13-010-p01.plain: Let us think something new, even if it turns out wrong; that is better. Why not try to hit the mark? We grow wiser through failure, and there is endless time.
viv13-010-p01.core_idea: Try new things; failure makes us wiser

viv13-010-p02.plain: If someone fed me daily, I would lose the use of my hands. Following others like sheep kills the spirit; inaction is death. Be active; activity brings difference, the beauty and sign of life, so why fear it?
viv13-010-p02.core_idea: Activity and difference are the signs of life

viv13-010-p03.plain: Do not give your heart to anything that changes, because that brings misery. A loved one may die, a friend may turn enemy, a husband may quarrel, a wife may die; that is how the world goes.
viv13-010-p03.core_idea: Giving your heart to changing things brings misery

viv13-010-p04.plain: How could God be angry with us? You are not angry with your mischievous baby. God knows we will all become perfect sooner or later, and he has infinite patience.
viv13-010-p04.core_idea: God is infinitely patient, never angry with us

viv13-010-p05.plain: Whoever lives and works in the world and gives all the results of their work to the Lord is never stained by the world's evils, just as a lotus grows under water yet blooms above it.
viv13-010-p05.core_idea: Offer your work to God, untouched like the lotus

viv13-010-p06.plain: The Gita says work day and night. Asked where peace lies in endless toil, Krishna says you will find it, but never by fleeing work; even on a mountaintop the mind keeps whirling.
viv13-010-p06.core_idea: Peace is not found by fleeing from work

viv13-010-p07.plain: Go ahead without worrying about what kind of work it is; just ask if you are unselfish. If so, nothing can stop you; plunge into the duty at hand. In time you find peace within activity and activity within peace.
viv13-010-p07.core_idea: Unselfish work leads to peace within activity

judge.issue: Drops that such a person is a Yogi who has reached perfection.

viv13-010-p08.plain: No duty in the world can rightly be called lowly; everyone's work is as good as an emperor's on his throne.
viv13-010-p08.core_idea: No work is lowly; all duty is equal

viv13-010-p09.plain: Do not fear that your work contains some evil, because all work does. Leave it to the Lord and do not look for results.
viv13-010-p09.core_idea: All work has flaws; leave results to God

viv13-010-p10.plain: Only the good lasts, because only the good is strong. Even in this life, the impure live shorter lives than the pure, for purity and goodness are strength.
viv13-010-p10.core_idea: Goodness and purity are strength, and they endure

viv13-011-p01.plain: As he was dying the Buddha said that no one can help you; you must help yourself and work out your own salvation. He said Buddha means infinite knowledge, which he had reached and which everyone can reach by striving.
viv13-011-p01.core_idea: Work out your own salvation; anyone can awaken

viv13-011-p02.plain: Perfection does not come from belief or faith, and talk counts for nothing; parrots can talk. Perfection comes from doing your work without self-interest.
viv13-011-p02.core_idea: Perfection comes from selfless action, not belief

viv13-011-p03.plain: Like ocean waves, events rise and fall again and again. We notice the rises and forget the falls, but both are necessary and great. The same rhythm runs through our thoughts, society and spiritual life.
viv13-011-p03.core_idea: Rises and falls are both necessary and great

viv13-012-p01.plain: The ideal may be far beyond us, but hold on to it anyway. Admit that it is our ideal even though we cannot reach it yet.
viv13-012-p01.core_idea: Keep your ideal even when it seems unreachable

viv13-012-p02.plain: Do not think of yourselves as trampled slaves, because within you is something that can never be oppressed, troubled or killed. You are all Sons of God, immortal spirit.
viv13-012-p02.core_idea: Within you is an immortal spirit no one can crush

viv13-012-p03.plain: Humanity does not move from error to truth, but from truth to truth, or from lower truth to higher truth.
viv13-012-p03.core_idea: We move from lower truth to higher truth

viv13-013-p01.plain: Jesus said the pure in heart will see God and the Kingdom of Heaven is within you. Why search elsewhere? Purify your spirit and it is there, already yours; you are heirs of immortality, children of the Eternal Father.
viv13-013-p01.core_idea: God's kingdom is already within a pure heart

viv13-013-p02.plain: Everyone quietly bears a burden; the Prophets carried the world, we carry small crosses at home. Yet however low we fall, a small circle of light in the heart always stays in touch with the divine.
viv13-013-p02.core_idea: Everyone carries a burden and a light divine

judge.issue: Drops the reasoning that losing touch with the divine would mean annihilation.

viv13-014-p01.plain: What good is power over the whole world and every atom in it? It will not make you happy unless you have the power of happiness within you and have conquered yourself.
viv13-014-p01.core_idea: Happiness needs self-mastery, not power over the world

viv13-014-p02.plain: Check your motive. Are you free of greed, fame and power? Can you hold to your ideals if the whole world tries to crush you, do your duty at the cost of your life, and persist to your last heartbeat?
viv13-014-p02.core_idea: Test whether your motives and resolve are pure

viv13-014-p03.plain: Krishna says you have a right to your work but not to its results. Why cling to outcomes? Our part is the duty; let the results take care of themselves.
viv13-014-p03.core_idea: Do your duty; let results take care of themselves

viv13-015-p01.plain: Life is brief whether you are wise or ignorant, poor or rich, oppressed or an emperor, healthy or ill, gentle and poetic or cruel.
viv13-015-p01.core_idea: Life is brief for everyone, whatever their lot

viv13-015-p02.plain: Facts must be perceived, and so must religion. We have to sense God to be sure God exists; no amount of reasoning, only our own direct perception, can make these things real and our belief rock-solid.
viv13-015-p02.core_idea: Only direct experience makes faith in God firm

viv13-016-p01.plain: At times, tired of dead logic and useless books, the heart cries to God: if you exist, show me the light, speak to me yourself, tell me whom to follow. Such thoughts come in deep depression, then we forget.
viv13-016-p01.core_idea: In despair we cry for God, then forget

viv13-016-p02.plain: People call a man mad when he throws away worldly vanities, but such people are the salt of the earth. That kind of madness produced the forces that moved the world, and only it will move the world in future.
viv13-016-p02.core_idea: Those called mad for renouncing vanity move the world

viv13-016-p03.plain: The whole world is mad: for money, pleasure, fame, a spouse, trifles, power over others, for every foolish thing except God. And people can only understand their own kind of madness.
viv13-016-p03.core_idea: Everyone is mad for something except God

viv13-016-p04.plain: The smaller a person's little ego, the more of God there is in them.
viv13-016-p04.core_idea: Less ego means more God within

viv13-017-p01.plain: Few grasp the power of thought. One great thought, thought alone in a sealed cave, will spread through space until it reaches all humanity. So do not rush to share your thoughts; first have something worth giving.
viv13-017-p01.core_idea: Thought is powerful; have something worth giving first

viv13-017-p02.plain: We hear brilliant speeches and forget them all by the time we get home, while at other times a few simple words enter our lives, become part of us and change us for good.
viv13-017-p02.core_idea: Simple words can change us more than grand speeches

viv13-017-p03.plain: Religion is not temples, churches, public worship, books, lectures or organisations; it is realisation. Nothing satisfies us until we know the truth for ourselves, and that experience is possible for every one of us if we try.
viv13-017-p03.core_idea: Only knowing truth for yourself truly satisfies

viv13-018-p01.plain: Do not shake anyone's faith. If you can, give them something better, or meet them where they are and help them upward, but do not destroy what they have.
viv13-018-p01.core_idea: Never destroy someone's faith; help them upward

viv13-018-p02.plain: Doctrines, sects and temples matter little next to the spirituality in each person, which makes them powerful for good. Develop that, criticise no one, for every creed has some good, and show by your life that religion is realisation.
viv13-018-p02.core_idea: Live spirituality; don't fight over doctrines

viv13-019-p01.plain: Death is only a change of condition; we stay in the same universe under the same laws. Those who have gone ahead and grown in beauty and wisdom are just the front line of a universal army following behind them.
viv13-019-p01.core_idea: Death is a change of state, not an end

viv13-019-p02.plain: We should cultivate optimism and try to see the good in everything. Lamenting the flaws of our bodies and minds gets us nowhere; it is the heroic effort to overcome hard circumstances that lifts the spirit.
viv13-019-p02.core_idea: Heroic effort, not lament, lifts the spirit

viv13-019-p03.plain: Teach your children that true religion is positive: not just avoiding evil but steadily doing noble deeds. It does not come from people's teachings or from books; it is the awakening of the spirit within that follows pure, heroic action.
viv13-019-p03.core_idea: True religion is doing good, not just avoiding evil

viv13-019-p04.plain: Love God for love's sake, do your duty for duty's sake and honour beauty for beauty's sake, never for reward. With hearts made pure this way, we will see God.
viv13-019-p04.core_idea: Love, duty and beauty for their own sake

viv13-019-p05.plain: What use is calling God the Father of all in prayer if we do not treat everyone as a brother? Books only point to a higher life; nothing comes of it unless we walk the path unflinchingly.
viv13-019-p05.core_idea: Live what you pray; walk the path, don't just read

viv13-019-p06.plain: Each person is like a glass globe holding the same pure divine light; the glass varies in colour and thickness, so the light looks different. The flame is equally beautiful in all, and the glass clears as we rise.
viv13-019-p06.core_idea: The same divine light shines in every person

viv13-020-p01.plain: A nation can master the seas and the elements and solve every practical problem, yet miss that the highest civilisation in a person belongs to one who has learned to conquer himself.
viv13-020-p01.core_idea: Highest civilisation is conquering the self

viv13-020-p02.plain: As children we thrilled at sunrise, and we gaze at sunsets trying to see beyond. The universe works like that: rising out of the unknown and returning to it, a child from darkness, an old man back into it.
viv13-020-p02.core_idea: Life rises from and returns to the unknown

viv13-021-p01.plain: It is unreasonable to expect happiness without misery. Adding more comforts only increases wants, and endless wants are a thirst never quenched; while that thirst remains, misery is certain. Life by nature brings happiness and misery in turn.
viv13-021-p01.core_idea: Happiness and misery come in turns

viv13-021-p02.plain: Pessimism and optimism are both wrong because both are extremes. A man with plenty to eat and wear becomes a great optimist, and the same man, losing everything, becomes a great pessimist.
viv13-021-p02.core_idea: Optimism and pessimism depend on circumstance

viv13-021-p03.plain: The world is neither good nor evil; it is the Lord's world, beyond both, perfect, his will playing out without beginning or end. It is a great gymnasium where countless souls exercise and grow strong and perfect.
viv13-021-p03.core_idea: The world is a gymnasium for souls to grow strong

viv13-021-p04.plain: Kitchen fire is neither good nor bad: we bless it when it cooks and curse it when it burns. The universe is the same; we call it good when it helps us and evil when it hurts us.
viv13-021-p04.core_idea: The world is neutral; our stance makes it good

viv13-022-p01.plain: Many of us get, or think we get, inner messages. If one concerns only yourself, do as you please; but if it concerns how you treat others, think a hundred times before acting on it, and you will be safe.
viv13-022-p01.core_idea: Think hard before acting on 'messages' affecting others

viv13-022-p02.plain: Have you seen God or the soul? If not, are you striving for it? It is here and now; the future is only the endless present, all time one second repeated. Religion belongs to this present life.
viv13-022-p02.core_idea: Religion is here and now, not in the future

viv13-023-p01.plain: The Buddha said not to believe something just because you heard it, it is traditional or popular, a sage said it, or habit or elders taught it. Examine it; if it fits reason and helps all, live by it.
viv13-023-p01.core_idea: Accept only what reason shows is good for all

viv13-023-p02.plain: All great people show tremendous power of concentration. We call them geniuses, but Yoga says we can all be geniuses if we try hard; some start better equipped and move faster, but the same power is in everyone.
viv13-023-p02.core_idea: Everyone has the power of concentration genius needs

viv13-023-p03.plain: It is not our business to look at others' faults; it does no good, and we should not even think of them. Our concern is with the good. Our business is to be good.
viv13-023-p03.core_idea: Don't dwell on others' faults; be good yourself

fix.display_text: We have no business to look at the faults of others: it does no good. We must not even think of them. Our business is with the good. We are not here to deal with faults. Our business is to be good.

viv13-024-p01.plain: Whenever I feel pain or pleasure, I have identified myself with the body. In the high state, pleasure and pain are both met with the same bliss.
viv13-024-p01.core_idea: The high state meets pain and pleasure alike

viv13-024-p02.plain: We have taken on the colour of the body and forgotten what we are. All our fears, worries, troubles, mistakes, weakness and evil come from one great blunder: believing that we are bodies.
viv13-024-p02.core_idea: Our troubles come from thinking we are bodies

fix.display_text: We have taken the colour of the body and have forgotten what we are. All the difficulties that follow come from that one dead body. All our fears, all worries, anxieties, troubles, mistakes, weakness, evil, are from that one great blunder — that we are bodies.

viv13-024-p03.plain: In English people greet with 'How do you do?'; the Indian greeting asks 'Are you upon yourself?' The moment you rest on something else, you risk misery. Meditation is the soul trying to stand on itself.
viv13-024-p03.core_idea: Meditation is the soul standing on itself

viv13-025-p01.plain: You cannot convince a young man that life has difficulties, nor an old man that life is smooth, because he has lived through a great deal. That is the difference.
viv13-025-p01.core_idea: Experience teaches what youth cannot believe

viv13-025-p02.plain: We all struggle. Even if we cannot reach the Absolute, we will get somewhere better than where we are now.
viv13-025-p02.core_idea: Striving always takes us somewhere better

viv13-025-p03.plain: Work at it harder and meditation comes; you no longer feel the body. Afterwards you have had the deepest rest of your life, deeper than any sleep, because even in the deepest sleep the mind keeps jumping.
viv13-025-p03.core_idea: Meditation gives deeper rest than sleep

viv13-025-p04.plain: Looking at a tree stump, a thief sees a policeman, a child sees a ghost, and a young man waiting for his sweetheart sees her. Yet the stump never changed.
viv13-025-p04.core_idea: We see what our minds bring to things

viv13-025-p05.plain: What is the goal of life? Is it just this world and nothing more? Are we only to stay as we are, smooth-running machines? Are today's sufferings all there is, and do we want nothing more?
viv13-025-p05.core_idea: Life must have a goal beyond this world

viv13-026-p01.plain: Poverty deceives us, then wealth deceives us; ignorance deceives us, then knowledge does. No one is ever satisfied. That is the cause of misery, but also the source of every blessing.
viv13-026-p01.core_idea: Never being satisfied brings both misery and blessing

viv13-026-p02.plain: A century ago people walked or bought horses. Now they are happy to ride trains but unhappy because they must work and earn more. Every labour-saving machine puts more strain on labour.

viv13-026-p03.plain: Whoever is on top of the wave thinks all is good; whoever is at the bottom thinks all is evil. Whoever stands aside sees the divine play: some weep, some laugh, and in turn they trade places.
viv13-026-p03.core_idea: Joy and sorrow take turns in the divine play

viv13-026-p04.plain: You always give up a lesser joy for a greater one. That is practical religion: freedom through renunciation. Give up the lower so that you may gain the higher.
viv13-026-p04.core_idea: Give up the lower to gain the higher

viv13-026-p05.plain: The great, the weak, even gods have died; the world is a graveyard of the past, yet we cling to life. There is meaning in that, but the mistake is clinging to the body when only the spirit is immortal.
viv13-026-p05.core_idea: Cling to the immortal spirit, not the body

viv13-026-p06.plain: My Master said a parrot can repeat 'Lord, Lord', but forgets when the cat grabs its neck. You may pray, read every scripture, worship every god, yet without realising the soul there is no freedom. Realisation is practical religion.
viv13-026-p06.core_idea: Without realising the soul, worship brings no freedom

viv13-027-p01.plain: Serve the poor, the miserable and the weak as worship of the Lord himself in them. Once that is done, the result does not matter; work like this, done without thought of gain, benefits the soul.
viv13-027-p01.core_idea: Serving the weak is worshipping God in them

viv13-027-p02.plain: Is it practical to spend life getting things that death takes away? A great conqueror, dying, had his treasures laid out, pressed his biggest diamond to his chest, wept, and died just as a dog dies.
viv13-027-p02.core_idea: All our possessions are left behind at death

viv13-027-p03.plain: The mind is like a lake: every stone dropped in makes waves that hide what we are, as ripples blur the moon's reflection. Let it grow calm and still; then nature lets go, and we know what we are.
viv13-027-p03.core_idea: A calm mind reveals our true self

viv13-027-p04.plain: We must train ourselves slowly. It is serious work that may take days, years or even lifetimes, but never mind; keep pulling, knowingly and willingly, and inch by inch we will gain ground.
viv13-027-p04.core_idea: Keep pulling; inch by inch we gain ground

viv13-027-p05.plain: How foolish to depend on other people for happiness; every separation is misery. Wealth rises and falls. Depending on health, or anything but the unchanging spirit, must bring misery sooner or later.
viv13-027-p05.core_idea: Only the unchanging spirit is a safe foundation

viv13-027-p06.plain: Everything except the infinite spirit keeps changing. Permanence is found only within yourself, where there is infinite, unchanging joy, and meditation is the gate that opens it.
viv13-027-p06.core_idea: Lasting joy lies within; meditation opens it

viv14-001-p01.plain: A farewell to a departed soul: go freely on your starry path beyond time and space, your service complete, your bonds broken, one with what comes as death and life; keep helping this troubled world with love.
viv14-001-p01.core_idea: Blessing a freed soul to keep helping with love

judge.issue: Drops the blessing of eternal peace and finding home in transcendent love.

viv14-001-p02.plain: If clouds hide the sun and the sky looks only gloomy, hold on a little longer, brave heart; victory will come. Summer always follows winter, every trough rises into a wave, so stay steady and brave.
viv14-001-p02.core_idea: Hold on; summer always follows winter

viv14-001-p03.plain: Life's duties are painful, its pleasures brief and empty, the goal dim; yet keep going through the dark with all your strength, brave heart. No work or struggle is wasted, even when hopes die; no good is ever undone.
viv14-001-p03.core_idea: No good work or struggle is ever wasted

judge.issue: Drops the promise that heirs to all shall come of thy loins.

viv14-001-p04.plain: Neither this world nor the next can give you freedom, and searching books and temples is useless. Your own hand holds the rope that drags you on, so stop lamenting and let go, bold renouncer, saying 'Om Tat Sat, Om!'
viv14-001-p04.core_idea: You hold the rope that binds you; let go

viv14-001-p05.plain: Few know the truth; the rest will hate and mock you, but ignore them. Go freely from place to place helping people out of the darkness of illusion, fearing no pain and seeking no pleasure, beyond both, bold renouncer.
viv14-001-p05.core_idea: Help others freely, ignoring mockery, beyond pain and pleasure

viv14-001-p06.plain: Peace is neither joy nor sorrow but what lies between, neither night nor morning but what joins them: the rest in music, the pause in sacred art, the silence between words and passions, the calm of the heart.
viv14-001-p06.core_idea: Peace is the calm between opposites

walden-thoreau-001-p01.plain: I have met so many immortal souls nearly crushed under their load, creeping through life pushing a huge barn with stables never cleaned and a hundred acres of farmland ahead of them.
walden-thoreau-001-p01.core_idea: Possessions can crush the soul that owns them

walden-thoreau-001-p02.plain: Our finest qualities, like the bloom on fruit, survive only with the gentlest handling, yet we do not treat ourselves or each other that tenderly.
walden-thoreau-001-p02.core_idea: Our best qualities need tender handling

walden-thoreau-001-p03.plain: Public opinion is a weak tyrant next to our own opinion of ourselves. What a person thinks of himself determines, or at least shows, his fate.
walden-thoreau-001-p03.core_idea: Your opinion of yourself shapes your fate

walden-thoreau-001-p04.plain: Most people live lives of quiet desperation, and what they call resignation is confirmed despair. Even their games and amusements hide an unconscious despair, with no real play in them. But it is wise not to do desperate things.
walden-thoreau-001-p04.core_idea: Most people live in quiet desperation

walden-thoreau-001-p05.plain: It is never too late to drop our prejudices. No old way of thinking should be trusted without proof; what everyone accepts today may be false tomorrow. Try what the old say you cannot do; you may find you can.
walden-thoreau-001-p05.core_idea: Never too late to test and drop old beliefs

judge.issue: Drops 'old deeds for old people, and new deeds for new'.

walden-thoreau-001-p06.plain: Boredom that claims life has nothing new is as old as Adam. But human abilities have never been measured, and little has been tried. Whatever your failures, do not despair: no one can say what you have left to do.
walden-thoreau-001-p06.core_idea: Past failures don't measure what you can still do

walden-thoreau-002-p01.plain: Nature and life are as varied as people are. Who can say what life looks like to someone else? What greater miracle could there be than to see through each other's eyes for a moment?
walden-thoreau-002-p01.core_idea: Seeing through another's eyes would be a miracle

walden-thoreau-002-p02.plain: We can safely trust far more than we do, setting aside as much care for ourselves as we honestly give elsewhere. Nature fits our weakness as well as our strength. Constant anxiety and strain is an almost incurable disease.
walden-thoreau-002-p02.core_idea: Trust more; constant anxiety is a disease
walden-thoreau-002-p02.plain_v1: We could safely trust far more than we do, and worry about ourselves less. Nature suits our weakness as well as our strength; the constant anxiety and strain some people live with is an almost incurable disease.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the condition: waive only as much self-care as we honestly give elsewhere.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops the condition: only as much self-care as we bestow elsewhere.

walden-thoreau-002-p03.plain: We say ours is the only way, but there are as many ways as lines drawn from a centre. Every change is a miracle to think about, and it is happening every moment.
walden-thoreau-002-p03.core_idea: Many ways exist; change is a constant miracle

walden-thoreau-002-p04.plain: Being a philosopher is not just having clever thoughts or founding a school, but loving wisdom enough to live by it: simply, independently, generously and trustingly, solving some of life's problems in practice, not only in theory.
walden-thoreau-002-p04.core_idea: Philosophy means living wisely, not just thinking

walden-thoreau-002-p05.plain: In all weather and at all hours I have tried to make the most of the moment and mark it, to stand where past and future meet, which is exactly the present, and keep to that line.
walden-thoreau-002-p05.core_idea: Live fully at the meeting point of now

walden-thoreau-002-p06.plain: Long ago I lost a hound, a bay horse and a turtle dove, and I am still searching. A few travellers had heard or glimpsed them, and seemed as eager to find them as if they were their own.
walden-thoreau-002-p06.core_idea: We all seek something precious we have lost

judge.issue: Drops his describing the lost creatures to many travellers.

walden-thoreau-003-p01.plain: The life people praise as successful is only one kind of life. Why should we exalt one kind above all the others?
walden-thoreau-003-p01.core_idea: Conventional success is just one kind of life

walden-thoreau-003-p02.plain: I have never thought less of anyone for a patch on their clothes, yet people usually worry more about having fashionable, clean, unpatched clothes than about having a clear conscience.
walden-thoreau-003-p02.core_idea: We care more about appearance than conscience

walden-thoreau-003-p03.plain: Beware of ventures that need new clothes rather than a new person wearing them; without a new person, how will new clothes fit? Try any venture in your old clothes. People want not something to use but something to be.
walden-thoreau-003-p03.core_idea: Change yourself, not your outward trappings

judge.issue: Drops 'something to do'; compresses the closing contrast.

walden-thoreau-003-p04.plain: Like birds moulting, our times of renewal must be crises. The loon goes off to lonely ponds for it; the snake sheds its skin and the caterpillar its coat by growth from within, for clothes are just our outermost skin.
walden-thoreau-003-p04.core_idea: Real renewal comes from growth within

walden-thoreau-003-p05.plain: It is good to dress so simply you can find yourself in the dark, and to live so compactly that if an enemy took the town, you could walk out empty-handed without worry, like the old philosopher.
walden-thoreau-003-p05.core_idea: Live so simply you can leave without worry

walden-thoreau-004-p01.plain: In the long run people hit only what they aim at, so even if they fail at first, they had better aim high.
walden-thoreau-004-p01.core_idea: Aim high; we only hit what we aim at

walden-thoreau-004-p02.plain: We have forgotten how to live outdoors; our lives are more housebound than we think. It might be good to spend more days and nights with nothing between us and the stars. Birds do not sing in caves.
walden-thoreau-004-p02.core_idea: We need open sky, not just shelter

judge.issue: Drops the poet and saint under a roof and the doves.

walden-thoreau-004-p03.plain: If civilisation is real progress, and I think it is though only the wise use it well, it must give better homes without costing more; and a thing's cost is how much of your life you trade for it.
walden-thoreau-004-p03.core_idea: The real cost of a thing is life traded

judge.issue: Drops 'immediately or in the long run' from the cost of life.

walden-thoreau-005-p01.plain: Most people never consider what a house is for, and stay needlessly poor all their lives because they think they need one like their neighbours'. Should we always strive to get more, and never learn to be content with less?
walden-thoreau-005-p01.core_idea: Keeping up with neighbours keeps us poor

judge.issue: Drops the tailor and crown analogy and the unaffordable house.

walden-thoreau-005-p02.plain: I had three pieces of limestone on my desk, but was horrified to find they needed dusting every day while the furniture of my mind was still undusted, so I threw them out the window in disgust.
walden-thoreau-005-p02.core_idea: Possessions demand care better spent on the mind

walden-thoreau-005-p03.plain: People have become tools of their tools. The one who picked fruit when hungry became a farmer; the one sheltering under a tree, a housekeeper. We no longer camp for a night, but have settled on earth and forgotten heaven.
walden-thoreau-005-p03.core_idea: We've become tools of our tools

walden-thoreau-006-p01.plain: It is hard to start without borrowing, but perhaps that is the most generous way, since it lets others share an interest in what you are doing.
walden-thoreau-006-p01.core_idea: Borrowing lets others share in your venture

walden-thoreau-006-p02.plain: Those were pleasant spring days, when people's winter of discontent thawed along with the earth, and life that had been dormant began to stretch.
walden-thoreau-006-p02.core_idea: Spring thaws our discontent along with the earth

walden-thoreau-006-p03.plain: People claim to know many things, but their arts, sciences and countless devices have flown away; the blowing wind is all anyone really knows.
walden-thoreau-006-p03.core_idea: Human knowledge is fleeting; little is truly known

walden-thoreau-007-p01.plain: Someone else may think for me, but that does not mean they should do it so that I stop thinking for myself.
walden-thoreau-007-p01.core_idea: Don't let others' thinking replace your own

walden-thoreau-007-p02.plain: A student who wins leisure by dodging all necessary work gets only a shameful, empty leisure, cheating himself of the experience that alone makes leisure fruitful.
walden-thoreau-007-p02.core_idea: Leisure without real work is empty

walden-thoreau-007-p03.plain: How could young people learn to live better than by trying the experiment of living right away?

walden-thoreau-007-p04.plain: Our inventions are usually pretty toys that distract us from serious things, better means to an unimproved end. We rush to build a telegraph from Maine to Texas, but they may have nothing important to say.
walden-thoreau-007-p04.core_idea: Better tools don't give us better purposes

judge.issue: Drops that the end was already too easy to reach.

walden-thoreau-008-p01.plain: Spending the best part of life earning money to enjoy a doubtful freedom in its worst part is like the Englishman who made a fortune in India so he could later be a poet. He should have started at once.
walden-thoreau-008-p01.core_idea: Don't postpone the life you want

judge.issue: 'Gone up garret' (live as a poor poet now) flattened to 'started at once'.

walden-thoreau-008-p02.plain: Nations are crazily ambitious to be remembered by the stone they leave behind. What if they worked as hard on refining their manners? One piece of good sense would be more memorable than a monument as high as the moon.

walden-thoreau-009-p01.plain: More than any other animal, humans can adapt to every climate and circumstance.

walden-thoreau-009-p02.plain: When I met an immigrant staggering under a bundle holding everything he owned, I pitied him, not because that was all he had, but because he had all that to carry.

walden-thoreau-010-p01.plain: Faith and experience convince me that supporting yourself is not a hardship but a pastime, if you live simply and wisely. No one need earn a living by the sweat of his brow, unless he sweats more easily than I.
walden-thoreau-010-p01.core_idea: Living simply makes earning a living easy

walden-thoreau-010-p02.plain: I would not want anyone to copy my way of life; I may have found another by then, and I want many different people in the world. Each should carefully find and follow his own way, not his parents'.
walden-thoreau-010-p02.core_idea: Find and follow your own way

judge.issue: Drops 'neighbor's' from the ways not to follow.

walden-thoreau-010-p03.plain: Our wisdom is only a single point, like the pole star a sailor or escaping slave steers by, but that is enough guidance for life. We may not reach port on time, but we can keep the true course.
walden-thoreau-010-p03.core_idea: Keep your guiding star and true course

judge.issue: 'Within a calculable period' loosened to 'on time'.

walden-thoreau-010-p04.plain: People say, in effect: start where and as you are, without trying mainly to become better, and set out kindly to do good. If I preached at all, I would say instead: set about being good.
walden-thoreau-010-p04.core_idea: Be good, rather than just doing good

walden-thoreau-011-p01.plain: For every one striking at the root of evil, a thousand hack at its branches. Whoever gives most to the needy may, by the way he lives, be doing most to cause the misery he vainly tries to relieve.
walden-thoreau-011-p01.core_idea: Strike at the root of evil, not branches

walden-thoreau-011-p02.plain: We should pass on our courage, not our despair, our health and ease, not our sickness, and be careful that the sickness does not spread.
walden-thoreau-011-p02.core_idea: Share courage and health, not despair

walden-thoreau-011-p03.plain: All health and success does me good, however distant; all sickness and failure makes me sad and harms me. To truly help humanity, first be simple and well like Nature, clear your own gloom, and become a person of worth.
walden-thoreau-011-p03.core_idea: Heal yourself first to truly help others

judge.issue: Drops the closing contrast: not an overseer of the poor but one of the worthies.

walden-thoreau-011-p04.plain: Do not fix your heart on what passes; the Tigris will flow through Baghdad after the caliphs are gone. If you have plenty, give freely like the date tree; if you have nothing to give, be free like the cypress.
walden-thoreau-011-p04.core_idea: Don't cling to the passing; give freely or stay free

walden-thoreau-012-p01.plain: I would tell everyone, once and for all: stay free and uncommitted for as long as you can. It makes little difference whether you are tied to a farm or to the county jail.
walden-thoreau-012-p01.core_idea: Stay free and uncommitted as long as possible

walden-thoreau-012-p02.plain: The morning wind always blows and the poem of creation never stops, but few ears hear it.
walden-thoreau-012-p02.core_idea: Creation's poem goes on; few listen

walden-thoreau-012-p03.plain: Whoever does not believe each day holds an earlier, holier dawn hour than he has yet spoiled has given up on life and is heading into darkness. Each day the rested soul tries again to make a noble life.
walden-thoreau-012-p03.core_idea: Each day offers a fresh, sacred start

judge.issue: 'His Genius' rendered as 'rested soul'; slight loss.

walden-thoreau-012-p04.plain: For someone whose lively thought keeps pace with the sun, every day is morning, whatever the clocks say. Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me. Moral reform is the effort to shake off sleep.
walden-thoreau-012-p04.core_idea: Morning is when you are awake inside

walden-thoreau-012-p05.plain: Millions are awake enough for physical work, one in a million for real intellectual effort, one in a hundred million for a poetic or divine life. To be awake is to be alive. I have never met anyone fully awake.
walden-thoreau-012-p05.core_idea: To be truly awake is to be alive

judge.issue: Drops 'How could I have looked him in the face?'

walden-thoreau-013-p01.plain: We must stay awake to life through hope, not gadgets. People can raise their lives by deliberate effort, and the highest art is to shape the quality of each day so your whole life is worthy of your best moments.
walden-thoreau-013-p01.core_idea: The highest art is shaping the quality of the day.

judge.issue: Heavy compression; drops the painting-the-atmosphere image; 'critical hour' softened to 'best moments'.

walden-thoreau-013-p02.plain: I went to the woods to live deliberately, facing only life's essentials, to learn what it could teach and not find at death that I had never lived. I didn't want to live what wasn't life, life being so precious, nor to resign myself unless truly necessary.
walden-thoreau-013-p02.core_idea: Live deliberately so you do not miss life itself.
walden-thoreau-013-p02.plain_v1: I went to live in the woods to face only what truly matters in life, so that when I died I would not find I had never really lived.

judge_v1.issue: Drops 'live deliberately', learning what life teaches, and refusing resignation unless necessary.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops learning what life had to teach and not practising resignation.

walden-thoreau-013-p03.plain: Our lives are wasted on endless small details. Keep things simple: reduce your concerns to a few instead of hundreds or thousands.
walden-thoreau-013-p03.core_idea: Simplify your life; too many details fritter it away.

judge.issue: Drops the counting imagery; compressed.

walden-thoreau-013-p04.plain: Why live in such a rush and waste our lives? We worry about need before it arrives, doing a huge amount of work today to save a little tomorrow.
walden-thoreau-013-p04.core_idea: Hurrying to prevent future trouble wastes life now.

judge.issue: Drops the stitch-in-time proverb; compressed.

walden-thoreau-013-p05.plain: When we slow down and think wisely, we see that only great and worthy things truly last, and small fears and small pleasures are mere shadows. Seeing this is thrilling.
walden-thoreau-013-p05.core_idea: Only worthy things are real; petty fears are shadows.

walden-thoreau-013-p06.plain: A Hindu text tells of a prince raised by a forester who thought himself a commoner until told the truth. Likewise the soul mistakes its nature until a holy teacher reveals it is Brahman.
walden-thoreau-013-p06.core_idea: The soul forgets it is divine until taught otherwise.

walden-thoreau-013-p07.plain: People think truth lies far away in distant times and places. But every time and place is here and now; God is most fully present in this very moment and will never be more divine.
walden-thoreau-013-p07.core_idea: Truth and God are found in the present moment.

judge.issue: Drops the concession that eternity holds something true and sublime.

walden-thoreau-014-p01.plain: Let us spend one day as calmly as nature does, not knocked off course by every small disturbance. Let visitors and noise come and go while we hold steady. Why give in and simply drift with the crowd?
walden-thoreau-014-p01.core_idea: Live one day calmly, undisturbed by small distractions.

judge.issue: Drops rising early and fasting; compressed.

walden-thoreau-014-p02.plain: Whether we face life or death, we want only what is real. If we are dying, let us feel it fully; if we are alive, let us get on with living.
walden-thoreau-014-p02.core_idea: Face reality fully, whether in dying or living.

judge.issue: Death-rattle image softened to 'feel it fully'.

walden-thoreau-014-p03.plain: Time is like a shallow stream I fish in; its current slips away but eternity remains. I want to drink more deeply and fish in the sky, where the bottom is stars.
walden-thoreau-014-p03.core_idea: Time is shallow; I long for eternity beneath it.

judge.issue: Drops drinking and seeing the sandy bottom; compressed.

walden-thoreau-014-p04.plain: When we pile up property, build families or states, or chase fame, we are mortal. But when we deal with truth we are immortal and need fear neither change nor accident.
walden-thoreau-014-p04.core_idea: Pursuing truth makes us immortal; possessions do not.

walden-thoreau-015-p01.plain: Somewhere there are words written for exactly our condition that could renew our lives; many have begun anew from a book. The questions troubling us troubled every wise person, and each answered them in words and life.
walden-thoreau-015-p01.core_idea: The right book can answer the questions that trouble us.

judge.issue: Drops the book explaining our miracles and the unutterable found uttered.

walden-thoreau-015-p02.plain: No method replaces staying always alert. No study, company or routine compares with really looking at what is before you. Will you merely read, or will you see? Look at what lies ahead and walk on.
walden-thoreau-015-p02.core_idea: Seeing what is before you beats any study.

judge.issue: Drops 'Read your fate' and the reader/student/seer triad; compressed.

walden-thoreau-015-p03.plain: Sometimes the present moment was too lovely to give up for work; I like a wide margin to my life. I sat whole mornings in the sun, daydreaming, and grew in those hours. They were time added, not lost.
walden-thoreau-015-p03.core_idea: Unhurried idle hours can be growth, not waste.

judge.issue: Heavy compression; drops the scene and 'over and above my usual allowance' nuance.

walden-thoreau-016-p01.plain: If we were always living by the best way we had learned so far, we would never be bored. Follow your own genius closely and it will show you something fresh every hour.
walden-thoreau-016-p01.core_idea: Following your genius keeps life fresh and free of boredom.

walden-thoreau-017-p01.plain: I admit that once I know a person's real nature, I have no hope of changing it in this life. As an Eastern saying goes, a dog's tail can be bound straight for twelve years and still curl back.
walden-thoreau-017-p01.core_idea: A person's true nature rarely changes.

walden-thoreau-017-p02.plain: I am glad there are owls to do the wild, mad hooting for us. Their cry suits swamps and dusky woods and speaks of a vast untamed nature, and of the dim, unsatisfied thoughts everyone has.
walden-thoreau-017-p02.core_idea: Owls voice the dark, restless thoughts we all share.

walden-thoreau-018-p01.plain: Feeling at one with the trembling leaves almost takes my breath away, yet like the lake my calm is rippled but not disturbed. These small waves from the evening wind are far from a storm.
walden-thoreau-018-p01.core_idea: Calm can be rippled without being broken.

walden-thoreau-018-p02.plain: No deep gloom can hold someone who lives close to nature with senses alive. To a healthy ear every storm is music. While I have the friendship of the seasons, I trust nothing can make life a burden.
walden-thoreau-018-p02.core_idea: Living close to nature guards against deep gloom.

judge.issue: Drops 'nothing can compel a simple and brave man to a vulgar sadness'.

walden-thoreau-018-p03.plain: I felt lonely only once in the woods, wondering if I needed people nearby. Then, in a gentle rain, I felt nature itself as warm, friendly company, and since then no place has seemed strange.
walden-thoreau-018-p03.core_idea: Nature itself can be companionship in loneliness.

judge.issue: Heavy compression; drops the slight insanity of the mood and nature as nearest kin.

walden-thoreau-018-p04.plain: What kind of distance makes a person lonely? I have found that walking closer to someone does little to bring two minds nearer together.
walden-thoreau-018-p04.core_idea: Physical nearness does not bring minds closer.

walden-thoreau-018-p05.plain: We let passing events shape our days, and they only distract us. Nearest to everything is the power that makes it; the grandest laws work beside us, and nearest of all is the maker whose work we are.
walden-thoreau-018-p05.core_idea: The power that made us is nearer than any distraction.

judge.issue: Drops the contrast with the hired workman we love to talk to.

walden-thoreau-018-p06.plain: Confucius rightly says that goodness is never left alone like an orphan; it always draws neighbors to it.
walden-thoreau-018-p06.core_idea: Virtue never stays alone; it attracts companions.

walden-thoreau-019-p01.plain: By thinking, we can step back and watch events flow past like a stream. However intense my experience, part of me watches as a spectator, noting it without sharing it, as distant from me as from you.
walden-thoreau-019-p01.core_idea: Part of us can watch our life as a spectator.

judge.issue: Drops Indra/driftwood image and the theatre example; compressed.

walden-thoreau-019-p02.plain: Being alone most of the time is good for me; even the best company soon tires me. No companion is as good as solitude. We are often lonelier among people than alone; solitude is not measured in miles.
walden-thoreau-019-p02.core_idea: Solitude is the best companion; loneliness is not distance.

judge.issue: Drops 'a man thinking or working is always alone'.

walden-thoreau-019-p03.plain: We meet too often to have anything new to offer, so we need politeness just to avoid conflict. Crowded together, we lose respect for one another; meeting less often would serve everything that truly matters.
walden-thoreau-019-p03.core_idea: Too much company cheapens it; meet less, value more.

judge.issue: Drops the opening claim 'society is commonly too cheap' and the musty-cheese image.

walden-thoreau-019-p04.plain: Nature, in sun, wind, rain and seasons, is innocent, kind and cheering, and feels so deeply with us it would mourn anyone's just grief. Can I not commune with the earth? I am partly leaves and soil myself.
walden-thoreau-019-p04.core_idea: We are part of a kind, sympathetic nature.

judge.issue: Compresses nature's mourning imagery; loses some intensity.

walden-thoreau-019-p05.plain: People, like nations, need wide and natural boundaries between them, even a good stretch of neutral ground.
walden-thoreau-019-p05.core_idea: People need generous space between them.

walden-thoreau-021-p01.plain: In short, anyone who is alive is always at risk of dying, though the risk is smaller for someone who is half-dead already. Sitting still carries as many risks as running.
walden-thoreau-021-p01.core_idea: Avoiding risk is its own risk; being alive is risky.

walden-thoreau-021-p02.plain: At four I was brought through these woods to this pond, one of my oldest memories. Tonight my flute echoes over the same water. The pines still stand, and new growth rises for new young eyes.
walden-thoreau-021-p02.core_idea: Places endure and renew across a lifetime.

judge.issue: Drops fallen pines used for supper; minor loss.

walden-thoreau-021-p03.plain: Working with your hands, even to the point of drudgery, is probably never the worst way to waste time. It always carries a lasting lesson, and for a thinker it bears fine results.
walden-thoreau-021-p03.core_idea: Manual labor always teaches something lasting.

walden-thoreau-022-p01.plain: I resolved that next summer I would plant virtues like sincerity, truth, simplicity, faith and innocence instead of beans, and see if they grew. Summers have passed, and I must admit to you, Reader, that those seeds never came up.
walden-thoreau-022-p01.core_idea: Resolving to grow virtues is easier than growing them.

judge.issue: Drops his doubt whether the seeds were truly those virtues, worm-eaten or dead.

walden-thoreau-022-p02.plain: Sincere people should never stand on ceremony with each other. If real worth and friendliness were there, we would not cheat, insult and shut each other out through meanness. We should not meet in such a hurry.
walden-thoreau-022-p02.core_idea: Real friendliness drops ceremony and haste.

judge.issue: 'Never stand upon ceremony with sincerity' narrowed to sincere people with each other.

walden-thoreau-023-p01.plain: It matters little whether the harvest fills the barn. The true farmer stops worrying, like squirrels that do not fret about the chestnut crop, finishes each day's work, and gives up all claim to what his fields produce.
walden-thoreau-023-p01.core_idea: Do the work daily and let go of the outcome.

judge.issue: Drops sacrificing first and last fruits in his mind.

walden-thoreau-023-p02.plain: Getting lost, even on a familiar road in a snowstorm, is valuable. We steer by habit; only when completely lost do we feel nature's vastness. Not until we have lost the world do we begin to find ourselves.
walden-thoreau-023-p02.core_idea: Only when lost do we begin to find ourselves.

judge.issue: Heavy compression; drops relearning the compass on waking and infinite extent of relations.

walden-thoreau-023-p03.plain: Rulers have no need of punishment. Love goodness and the people will be good. A leader's virtue is like the wind and the people's like grass: when the wind passes over, the grass bends.
walden-thoreau-023-p03.core_idea: Leaders who love virtue make the people virtuous.

judge.issue: Direct address to those who govern made general; 'superior man' becomes 'leader'.

walden-thoreau-024-p01.plain: An old, deaf fisherman sometimes sat with me in my boat. We hardly spoke, though he hummed a psalm now and then, and our time together was perfect harmony, sweeter to remember than talk.
walden-thoreau-024-p01.core_idea: Quiet companionship can be deeper than conversation.

walden-thoreau-025-p01.plain: A lake is the most beautiful and expressive part of a landscape. It is the earth's eye, and looking into it, you measure the depth of your own nature.
walden-thoreau-025-p01.core_idea: Looking into a lake, we see our own depth.

walden-thoreau-026-p01.plain: When younger, I spent many summer mornings drifting on the pond, daydreaming; idleness was then my most fruitful work. I was rich in sunny hours, spent them freely, and do not regret missing more work.
walden-thoreau-026-p01.core_idea: Sunny idle hours can be the richest wealth.

walden-thoreau-027-p01.plain: Let me be poor in a way that enjoys what is truly valuable.
walden-thoreau-027-p01.core_idea: Better to be poor and enjoy real wealth.

walden-thoreau-028-p01.plain: Get up before dawn, free of worry, and go looking for adventure. Let midday find you at other lakes, and let night catch you anywhere, feeling at home wherever you are.
walden-thoreau-028-p01.core_idea: Roam freely and be at home everywhere.

walden-thoreau-028-p02.plain: Do not make earning a living your job; make it your play. Enjoy the land without owning it. People stay stuck buying and selling, living like serfs, because they lack daring and faith.
walden-thoreau-028-p02.core_idea: Make earning a living play, not bondage.

walden-thoreau-028-p03.plain: Most people come home each night from just next door, and their lives stagnate in the same stale air. We should come home every day from far off, from adventures, risks and discoveries, with new experience and character.
walden-thoreau-028-p03.core_idea: Come home each day changed by new experience.

judge.issue: Drops shadows reaching farther than daily steps; compressed.

walden-thoreau-029-p01.plain: Like most people, I find in myself both a pull toward a higher, spiritual life and a pull toward a raw, wild one, and I honor both. I love wildness as much as goodness.
walden-thoreau-029-p01.core_idea: Honor both the spiritual and the wild in yourself.

walden-thoreau-029-p02.plain: Lately, whenever I fish, I lose a little self-respect. I am good at it and the urge returns, but afterward I feel I should not have. It is a faint hint, but so is the first light of morning.
walden-thoreau-029-p02.core_idea: A faint inner unease can signal a new dawn.

walden-thoreau-029-p03.plain: Whoever follows the faint, steady promptings of his genius may not see what extremes, even madness, they lead to, yet his road lies there. No one was ever misled by his genius; even bodily weakness wouldn't be regretted. If you greet each day and night with joy, that is success.
walden-thoreau-029-p03.core_idea: Following your genius never misleads; joy is success.

judge.issue: Drops the healthy objection prevailing and life's fragrance as the measure of success.

walden-thoreau-029-p03.plain_v1: Follow the faint but steady promptings of your genius, though you cannot see where they lead; no one ever followed their genius until it misled them. If you greet each day with joy, that is success.

judge_v1.issue: Softens 'extremes, or even insanity' and bodily weakness; conditional made a command.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Turns a conditional description into a command; drops the risk of extremes or insanity.

walden-thoreau-029-p04.plain: The greatest things in life are the least noticed; we doubt and forget them, yet they are most real. The true harvest of my days is indescribable: a little stardust caught, a piece of rainbow held.
walden-thoreau-029-p04.core_idea: Life's truest gains are intangible and easily overlooked.

judge.issue: Drops 'most astounding facts are never communicated man to man'.

walden-thoreau-030-p01.plain: A Chinese sage says that when the soul is not its own master, we look without seeing, listen without hearing, eat without tasting. Whoever truly tastes food cannot be a glutton; whoever does not must be one.
walden-thoreau-030-p01.core_idea: Attention to what you taste prevents gluttony.

walden-thoreau-030-p02.plain: Our whole life is surprisingly a moral matter. Virtue and vice never stop struggling for a moment. Goodness is the only investment that never fails.
walden-thoreau-030-p02.core_idea: Goodness is the only investment that never fails.

walden-thoreau-030-p03.plain: We sense an animal within us that wakes as our higher nature sleeps. It is crude and sensual and may never be fully driven out; we may draw back from it, but we cannot change what it is.
walden-thoreau-030-p03.core_idea: Our animal nature wakes when our higher nature sleeps.

judge.issue: Drops 'reptile' and the worm analogy.

walden-thoreau-030-p04.plain: Effort brings wisdom and purity; laziness brings ignorance and sensuality. To avoid impurity and every sin, work hard, even cleaning a stable. Our nature is hard to master, but it must be mastered.
walden-thoreau-030-p04.core_idea: Earnest work guards against laziness and impurity.

judge.issue: Drops the description of the slothful, unclean person and the student.

walden-thoreau-030-p05.plain: Each person builds a temple, their body, to the god they worship, in their own style, and cannot substitute marble. We sculpt our own flesh: any nobility starts to refine our features, and any meanness or sensuality makes them brutish.
walden-thoreau-030-p05.core_idea: How we live shapes our very body and face.

walden-thoreau-031-p01.plain: If you just sit still long enough in a lovely spot in the woods, all its creatures will show themselves to you one by one.
walden-thoreau-031-p01.core_idea: Sit still long enough and nature reveals itself.

walden-thoreau-033-p01.plain: I was glad to see my work rising square and solid bit by bit, and thought that if it was going slowly, it was built to last a long time.
walden-thoreau-033-p01.core_idea: Slow work is built to last.

walden-thoreau-034-p01.plain: Snow had covered the ground since late November and suddenly winter surrounded me. I withdrew further into my shell and tried to keep a bright fire burning both in my house and in my heart.
walden-thoreau-034-p01.core_idea: In winter, keep a fire burning in your heart.

walden-thoreau-035-p01.plain: There is always a face to be seen in a fire. A worker gazing into it in the evening clears away the grime and heaviness his thoughts gathered during the day.
walden-thoreau-035-p01.core_idea: Gazing at a fire cleanses the day's thoughts.

walden-thoreau-036-p01.plain: Long after a house has vanished, the lilac its children planted still blooms each spring. They never imagined that small cutting would outlive them and, fifty years on, quietly tell their story to a wanderer.
walden-thoreau-036-p01.core_idea: What we plant can outlive us and tell our story.

judge.issue: Heavy compression; loses the lilac outliving the family as sole survivor.

walden-thoreau-037-p01.plain: There, as everywhere, I sometimes waited for the Visitor who never comes. A Hindu text says a householder should wait in his courtyard at evening for a guest. I often waited long, but no one came from town.
walden-thoreau-037-p01.core_idea: Waiting hospitably for a visitor who never comes.

judge.issue: Drops the milking-time measure and the waiting-for-a-herd humour.

walden-thoreau-037-p02.plain: Once a sparrow landed on my shoulder for a moment while I was hoeing, and I felt more honored by that than I would have by any military badge.
walden-thoreau-037-p02.core_idea: Nature's small graces honor us more than rank.

walden-thoreau-038-p01.plain: After a still winter night I woke feeling a question had been put to me. But dawn looked in calmly, asking nothing, and the snowy hill seemed to say: Forward! Nature asks no questions and answers none of ours.
walden-thoreau-038-p01.core_idea: Nature answers our questions by simply going forward.

judge.issue: Drops 'I awoke to an answered question' and Nature's settled resolution.

walden-thoreau-038-p02.plain: Heaven is below us, right where we stand, as much as it is above us.
walden-thoreau-038-p02.core_idea: Heaven is here on earth as well as above.

walden-thoreau-039-p01.plain: If we knew all of Nature's laws, one fact would reveal everything. We know few, so our results fail through our ignorance, not Nature's disorder. Unseen concurring laws make a harmony more wonderful still. Laws are like viewpoints on a mountain: endless profiles, but one true form, never grasped whole.
walden-thoreau-039-p01.core_idea: Nature's harmony exceeds the few laws we know.
walden-thoreau-039-p01.plain_v1: If we knew all nature's laws, one fact would reveal everything. We know few, so our conclusions fail through our ignorance, not nature's disorder. The hidden harmony is greater still; like a mountain, truth changes with every viewpoint.

judge_v1.issue: 'Truth changes with every viewpoint' loses the mountain's one absolute form behind many profiles.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Says truth changes with viewpoint; the passage says one form, many profiles.

walden-thoreau-042-p01.plain: A gentle thaw is more powerful than the god Thor with his hammer: the thaw melts things, while the hammer only smashes them.
walden-thoreau-042-p01.core_idea: Gentleness melts what force can only break.

walden-thoreau-042-p02.plain: The first sparrow of spring! The year begins with fresher hope than ever, with soft birdsong over the thawing fields. At such a moment, what do histories, traditions and written revelations matter?
walden-thoreau-042-p02.core_idea: Spring's first birdsong outweighs all written wisdom.

walden-thoreau-042-p03.plain: In spring the grass flames up green on the hills, a sign of endless youth; checked by frost, it keeps pushing on. So human life dies back to its root and still sends up its green blade toward eternity.
walden-thoreau-042-p03.core_idea: Life dies to its root and grows again forever.

judge.issue: Compresses the grass-as-green-stream imagery.

walden-thoreau-042-p04.plain: The shift from storm and winter to calm, mild weather, from dark sluggish hours to bright lively ones, is a turning point that everything announces. When it finally comes, it seems to happen in an instant.
walden-thoreau-042-p04.core_idea: The turn from winter to spring comes suddenly.

walden-thoreau-043-p01.plain: One gentle rain greens the grass, as better thoughts brighten our outlook. We would be blessed to live always in the present, using every chance, not atoning for past neglect. We linger in winter when it is already spring.
walden-thoreau-043-p01.core_idea: Live in the present; it is already spring.

judge.issue: Drops the irony that atoning for past neglect is 'what we call doing our duty'.

walden-thoreau-043-p02.plain: On a pleasant spring morning everyone's sins are forgiven; such a day is a pause from wrongdoing, and even the worst sinner may turn back. When our own innocence returns, we can see the innocence in our neighbors.
walden-thoreau-043-p02.core_idea: Renewed innocence lets us see others' innocence.

walden-thoreau-043-p03.plain: Village life would stagnate without the wild land around it; we need the tonic of wildness. We long to explore everything, yet need the world to stay mysterious. We can never have enough of nature's untamed vastness.
walden-thoreau-043-p03.core_idea: We need wildness and mystery beyond our reach.

judge.issue: Drops needing to see our own limits transgressed and wild life beyond us.

walden-thoreau-043-p04.plain: Doctors wisely prescribe a change of scene. This place is not the whole world; wild geese and bison range far. Yet we think our fences and duties fix our fates. The universe is wider than our view of it.
walden-thoreau-043-p04.core_idea: The universe is wider than our views of it.

judge.issue: Drops the town clerk and Tierra del Fuego / infernal fire turn.

walden-thoreau-043-p05.plain: Look inward and you will find a thousand unexplored regions in your mind. Travel through them and become an expert in mapping your own inner world.
walden-thoreau-043-p05.core_idea: Explore the undiscovered regions within your own mind.

walden-thoreau-044-p01.plain: I left the woods for as good a reason as I went: I had other lives to live. Within a week my feet wore a path to the pond. The mind wears paths too; tradition and conformity cut deep ruts.
walden-thoreau-044-p01.core_idea: We easily wear ruts of habit and conformity.

judge.issue: Drops others keeping his path open; compressed.

walden-thoreau-044-p02.plain: Advance confidently toward your dreams and live the life you imagined, and you'll meet unexpected success, and freer laws will form around you. The more you simplify, the simpler the universe seems; solitude, poverty and weakness cease to be such. Build castles in the air, then put foundations under them.
walden-thoreau-044-p02.core_idea: Pursue your dreams boldly, then build their foundations.

judge.issue: Turns 'if you have built castles' into an instruction to build them.

walden-thoreau-044-p02.plain_v1: My experiment taught me that if you move confidently toward your dreams and live the life you imagined, you will meet unexpected success. If you built castles in the air, they belong there; now build foundations under them.

judge_v1.issue: Drops simplicity making laws less complex and solitude, poverty, weakness ceasing to be such.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops passing boundaries, freer laws, and simplicity making solitude not solitude.

walden-thoreau-044-p03.plain: People call moderns intellectual dwarfs beside the ancients. So what? A living dog beats a dead lion. Rather than despair at being small, be the biggest small person you can. Mind your business; be what you were made to be.
walden-thoreau-044-p03.core_idea: Be fully what you are, not what others were.

judge.issue: 'Shall a man go hang himself' softened to 'rather than despair'.

walden-thoreau-044-p04.plain: Why rush so desperately to succeed? If someone falls out of step, perhaps they hear a different drummer; let them step to their own music, however slow. If the life we were made for has not come, nothing substitutes.
walden-thoreau-044-p04.core_idea: Step to the music you hear, at your own pace.

judge.issue: Drops the heaven of blue glass and not being shipwrecked on a vain reality.

walden-thoreau-044-p05.plain: An artist of Kouroo resolved to make a perfect staff, believing time does not enter perfect work. He searched for the right wood while his friends grew old and died, but he did not age; his singleness of purpose and piety kept him young, and Time could not overcome him.
walden-thoreau-044-p05.core_idea: Single-minded devotion to perfection is untouched by time.
walden-thoreau-044-p05.plain_v1: An artist set out to make a perfect staff, since time has no part in perfect work. While he searched for wood, his friends aged and died, but he did not. He never compromised with Time, so Time spared him.

judge_v1.issue: Drops singleness of purpose and elevated piety as the source of his perennial youth.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops singleness of purpose and piety as the cause of his youth.

walden-thoreau-044-p06.plain: In the end nothing serves us like the truth; it alone wears well. We often live in a false position, imagining a situation and stepping into it. Say what you have to say, not what you ought; truth beats pretending.
walden-thoreau-044-p06.core_idea: Any truth is better than make-believe.

judge.issue: Drops being in two cases at once and regarding only facts in sane moments.

walden-thoreau-045-p01.plain: However poor your life is, face it and live it; do not avoid it or curse it. It is not as bad as you are. Love your life, poor as it is; sunset shines on the poorhouse as brightly too.
walden-thoreau-045-p01.core_idea: Love your life, however poor it is.

judge.issue: Drops 'it looks poorest when you are richest' and the fault-finder in paradise.

walden-thoreau-045-p02.plain: Grow your poverty like a garden herb. Do not chase new things, clothes or friends; return to the old. Things do not change; we do. Sell your clothes and keep your thoughts. God will see you do not lack company.
walden-thoreau-045-p02.core_idea: Things do not change; we change.

walden-thoreau-045-p03.plain: Even confined to an attic corner, I would find the world as large while I had my thoughts, which no one can take. Do not anxiously chase many influences; it scatters you. Humility, like darkness, reveals the heavenly lights.
walden-thoreau-045-p03.core_idea: Humility, like darkness, reveals the heavenly lights.

judge.issue: Drops the philosopher's army saying and 'do not seek to be developed'.

walden-thoreau-045-p04.plain: Life is sweetest lived close to the bone, and it keeps you from trifling. Being generous in higher things never costs you in lower ones. Extra wealth buys only extras; money cannot buy a single thing the soul needs.
walden-thoreau-045-p04.core_idea: Money cannot buy anything the soul needs.

walden-thoreau-045-p05.plain: I love to find my true bearings: not to march in showy parades, but to walk alongside the Builder of the universe if I can, and to sit thoughtfully while this restless, trivial century rushes past.
walden-thoreau-045-p05.core_idea: Walk with the Creator while the busy age rushes by.

walden-thoreau-045-p06.plain: Do not drive a nail into flimsy plaster; find solid wood and drive it home so well you can recall your work at night with satisfaction. Only so will God help you. Each nail is a rivet in the universe.
walden-thoreau-045-p06.core_idea: Do every task so well you can rest easy.

judge.issue: Drops the Muse and 'you carrying on the work' of the universe.

walden-thoreau-045-p07.plain: I would choose truth over love, money or fame. I once sat at a table with rich food, wine and eager servants but no sincerity or truth, and I left hungry.
walden-thoreau-045-p07.core_idea: Without sincerity and truth, abundance leaves us hungry.

walden-thoreau-045-p08.plain: The life within us is like a river. This year it may rise higher than ever known and flood the dry uplands; this may be the momentous year that sweeps away all our old ways.
walden-thoreau-045-p08.core_idea: The life in us can rise beyond anything known.

judge.issue: 'Drown out all our muskrats' interpreted as 'sweeps away all our old ways'.

walden-thoreau-045-p09.plain: A light too bright for our eyes is darkness to us. Only the day we are awake to truly dawns. There is more day yet to come; the sun is only a morning star.
walden-thoreau-045-p09.core_idea: Only the day we are awake to dawns.

walden-thoreau-046-p01.plain: Should a citizen ever hand their conscience to lawmakers? Then why have one? We should be people first, subjects second. Respect for right matters more than respect for law. My only real duty is to do what I think right.
walden-thoreau-046-p01.core_idea: Conscience and right come before obedience to law.

walden-thoreau-046-p02.plain: Someone who gives themselves entirely to others seems useless and selfish to them, while someone who gives only partly is called a benefactor and philanthropist.
walden-thoreau-046-p02.core_idea: Total self-giving is often misjudged; partial giving praised.

walden-thoreau-046-p03.plain: It matters less that many people are as good as you than that there is some perfect goodness somewhere, because that will spread through and transform the whole.
walden-thoreau-046-p03.core_idea: A little true goodness transforms the whole.

walden-thoreau-046-p04.plain: You are not bound to devote yourself to ending even the greatest wrong; you may have other concerns. But you must not support it in practice. Before pursuing your own aims, get off the shoulders you are standing on.
walden-thoreau-046-p04.core_idea: You need not fight every wrong, but never support it.

judge.issue: Drops 'wash his hands of it' and that the other man may pursue his contemplations too.

walden-thoreau-047-p01.plain: How can anyone be content merely to hold an opinion that they are wronged? Cheated of a dollar, you would act. Acting on principle is revolutionary: it divides states, churches, families, even the self, separating the devilish from the divine.
walden-thoreau-047-p01.core_idea: Acting on principle, not just opinion, changes things.

judge.issue: Drops taking effectual steps to recover the full amount and never be cheated again.

walden-thoreau-047-p02.plain: Whatever else happens, my task is to make sure I do not lend myself to the wrong that I condemn.
walden-thoreau-047-p02.core_idea: Never take part in the wrong you condemn.

walden-thoreau-047-p03.plain: I was not born mainly to make the world a good place, but to live in it, good or bad. No one must do everything, only something; and being unable to do everything is no reason to do wrong.
walden-thoreau-047-p03.core_idea: You cannot do everything, but must not do wrong.

walden-thoreau-047-p04.plain: However small a beginning looks, whatever is done well once is done for good.
walden-thoreau-047-p04.core_idea: What is well done is done forever.

walden-thoreau-047-p05.plain: Is there not a kind of bloodshed when conscience is wounded? Through that wound a person's true humanity and immortality drain away until they bleed to an everlasting death.
walden-thoreau-047-p05.core_idea: Wounding your conscience drains away your true self.

walden-thoreau-047-p06.plain: The rich are always bound to what made them rich. The more money, the less virtue: money gets things for us and spares us hard questions. As means grow, real living shrinks. When rich, pursue your plans from poorer days.
walden-thoreau-047-p06.core_idea: Wealth erodes virtue and narrows real living.

judge.issue: Drops money removing his moral ground and the hard question of how to spend it.

walden-thoreau-048-p01.plain: When an acorn and a chestnut fall side by side, neither holds back for the other; each grows by its own laws until one perhaps overshadows and destroys the other. A plant that cannot live by its nature dies, and so does a man.
walden-thoreau-048-p01.core_idea: Like a plant, a person must live by their nature.
walden-thoreau-048-p01.plain_v1: When an acorn and a chestnut fall side by side, neither holds back for the other; each follows its nature and grows as best it can. A plant that cannot live by its nature dies, and so does a person.

judge_v1.issue: Drops the hard ending: one may overshadow and destroy the other.

judge_v1_rejudged.issue: Drops that one may overshadow and destroy the other.

walden-thoreau-049-p01.plain: I do not want to quarrel with anyone, person or nation. I do not want to split hairs or set myself up as better than my neighbors.
walden-thoreau-049-p01.core_idea: No wish to quarrel or feel superior to others.

walden-thoreau-049-p02.plain: I spend few moments actually living under a government. If a person's thought and imagination are free, and illusions do not hold them long, foolish rulers or reformers cannot seriously disrupt their life.
walden-thoreau-049-p02.core_idea: A free mind cannot be ruled by unwise rulers.

walden-thoreau-049-p03.plain: Those who know no purer source of truth sensibly stand by the Bible and the Constitution and drink there reverently. But those who see truth trickling in from higher up set out again on their pilgrimage toward its source.
walden-thoreau-049-p03.core_idea: Seek truth beyond its familiar sources, toward its fountainhead.
